children.translated_text: There is a city called <s>Ujjayinī</s>, with great moats and great halls,
like the great earth itself, girdled by the great ocean and great mountains.
There, seeing the uninterrupted palaces made of gold and silver,
the citizens do not long for the peaks of <s>Meru</s> or <s>Kailāsa</s>.
The sounds of Vedic recitation, bowstrings, and lutes in every house
meet together there, yet do not obstruct one another.

children.text: kṛtaṃ varṇanayā tasyā yasyāṃ satatam āsate
children.translated_text: Enough with describing that city, in which, constantly,
<s>Mahākāla</s> and the other gaṇas dwell, having left the city of <s>Śiva</s>.
In that city there was a king, <s>Mahāsena</s>, a lord of the earth,
who had sixteen thousand queens, like <s>Śrīpati</s>.
As he long protected his subjects, who acted according to śāstra (authoritative teaching),

children.text: gopālaḥ pālakaś ceti sutau jātau guṇāmbudhī ||
children.translated_text: two sons were born to him, <s>Gopāla</s> and <s>Pālaka</s>, oceans of virtues.
His minister <s>Bharatarohaka</s> was equal to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: rohantakaḥ surohaś ca tasyāstāṃ tatsamau sutau ||
children.translated_text: and his two sons, <s>Rohantaka</s> and <s>Suroha</s>, were equal to him.
The sons of the king and the minister knew the meanings of the four sciences,

children.text: prayogeṣu ca daṣāṇāṃ yānti sma divasāḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: and their days passed happily in the practice of the ten disciplines.
Then <s>Gopāla</s> ruled the earth that had been ruled by his father,
while <s>Pālaka</s>, being younger, administered the office of heir-apparent.

children.text: mantriputrau tu mantritvam atha bhūmir naveśvarā
children.translated_text: The minister's two sons then took up the ministry; and the land, with a new lord,
guarded by new ministers, became renewed once again.
Then the king mounted his lordly elephant, shining with streams of rut-fluid,
the very essence of the world, and went outside the city.
A great crowd of people had come, desiring to see him,

children.text: bibhyad vyāḍād gajāt tasmād itaś cetaś ca vidrutam ||
children.translated_text: but, afraid of that fierce elephant, they fled this way and that.
There a certain maiden, as she was being seized by the elephant,
went from the lofty rampart into a deep moat that was hard to reach.
For a moment she lost consciousness from the pain caused by falling into the moat;
then, standing on the bank, she angrily addressed the king seated on the elephant.

children.text: avadhyam avadhīr yas tvaṃ pitaraṃ tasya kiṃ mayā
children.translated_text: 'You are one who killed a father who should never be killed; what am I to such a man?

children.text: adhītavedaṃ yo hanti brāhmaṇaṃ tasya ke mṛgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: What are mere animals to one who kills a Brāhmaṇa learned in the Veda?'

children.text: iti kanyāvacaḥ śrutvā duḥśravaṃ śvapacair api
children.translated_text: Hearing the maiden's words, painful to hear even for outcastes,
he entered his residence, his heart pierced by the arrows of thought.
With grief he passed the remainder of the day as though it were a year,
and at nightfall he went out from the house to learn the talk of the people.
Wrapped in a black blanket, carrying sword, shield, and dagger,
and equipped with spells, antidotes, and armor, he wandered slowly about.
Then, in a certain temple, he heard the sound
of a lover speaking with a woman going to a secret rendezvous.

children.text: hataṃ muṣṭibhir ākāśaṃ tuṣāṇāṃ kaṇḍanaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: 'I have beaten the empty air with my fists and pounded husks,

children.text: mayā yena tvayā sārdhaṃ baddhā prītir abuddhinā ||
children.translated_text: fool that I was, because I formed an attachment together with you.
So long a time has been passed by me in distress,

children.text: mayā tvaṃ tu gṛhād eva na niryāsi pativratā ||
children.translated_text: but you, faithful wife that you are, do not even leave your house.

children.text: kaumāraḥ subhāgo bhartā yadi nāma priyas tava
children.translated_text: If your young, handsome husband is truly dear to you,
why have you uselessly made fools of us, men of good family?'
After hearing such words, that bold woman of the rendezvous

children.text: vihasya viṭam āha sma tvādṛśā hi hatatrapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: laughed and said to the libertine, 'Men like you are indeed shameless.

children.text: nanu cittaṃ mayārādhyaṃ tasyāpi bhavataḥ kṛte
children.translated_text: For your sake I must also win over his mind,

children.text: na hi bhartṝn aviśvāsya ramante kulaṭā viṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for unchaste women do not sport with libertines without making their husbands trust them.

children.text: atha nirmakṣikaṃ bhadra madhu pātuṃ manorathaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, good sir, if your desire is to drink honey free from flies,

children.text: jahi ghātaya bālaṃ me patiṃ nityapramādinam ||
children.translated_text: kill, or have killed, my young husband, who is always careless.

children.text: atha pāpād asi trastaḥ sphuṭaṃ nāhaṃ tava priyā
children.translated_text: But if you are afraid of sin, then clearly I am not dear to you.
Surely <s>Prajāpati</s>, blinded by irresistible passion, goes even to his daughter.

children.text: athavālaṃ vivādena vaidharmyaṃ kiṃ na paśyasi
children.translated_text: Or enough of argument. Do you not see the breach of dharma (righteous conduct),
by which the protector of subjects killed his father, blinded by the pleasures of kingship?'

children.text: suduḥśravam idaṃ śrutvā gopālo durvacaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this extremely painful and harsh speech, <s>Gopāla</s>

children.text: gacchann anyatra śuśrāva dhvaniṃ viprasya jalpataḥ ||
children.translated_text: went elsewhere and heard the sound of a Brāhmaṇa speaking.

children.text: ayi brāhmaṇi jāgarṣi nandini krandate śiśuḥ
children.translated_text: 'O Brāhmaṇa woman, are you awake? <s>Nandinī</s>, the child is crying.

children.text: tvaritaṃ yājate dehi stanyaṃ kaṇṭho 'sya mā śuṣat ||
children.translated_text: Quickly give him milk to suck; let his throat not dry up.'

children.text: iti śrutvā giraṃ bhartur vinidrā brāhmaṇī sutam
children.translated_text: Hearing her husband's words, the Brāhmaṇa woman, now awake,
cruelly rebuked her son: 'Die, patricide!'

children.text: āḥ pāpe kim asaṃbaddhaṃ pitṛghātinn iti tvayā
children.translated_text: 'Ah, wicked woman, what senseless thing have you said,
calling this boy a patricide?' the angry Brāhmaṇa said to her.

children.text: kim āryaputra putreṇa yadā rājñā pitā hataḥ
children.translated_text: 'What is there about a son, noble husband, when the king,

children.text: śrutismṛtivid ity etad uvāca brāhmaṇī patim ||
children.translated_text: a knower of śruti (revealed scripture) and smṛti (remembered tradition), has killed his father?' the Brāhmaṇa woman said to her husband.
Having heard such scandalous talk, the king entered the inner apartments
and passed the rest of the night without closing his eyes.
Then, at a time of dense darkness, he privately asked his two ministers,

children.text: apṛcchat ko 'yam asmāsu pravādaḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'What is this rumor about us? Tell me.'

children.text: tatas tāv ūcatus trastau satrāsaṃ nṛpacoditau
children.translated_text: Then the two, frightened and pressed by the king, spoke with fear:
'Let Your Majesty's mind attend to hearing the cause of the scandal.
When your father <s>Pradyota</s>, of well-chosen name,
was near death, there were eight unfailing omens.

children.text: uddhārye dhavale keśe pramādāt kṛṣṇa uddhṛte
children.translated_text: When a white hair was to be plucked out, but by mistake a black one was plucked,
the king had the barber who plucked it cut down.
And while he was eating, when a stone was broken by the tip of his tooth,
the old cook, inherited through the family line, was put to death.
Even though he knew from such signs that his nature had turned contrary...

children.text: prabho vidher vidheyatvād brāhmaṇān apy abādhata ||
children.translated_text: My lord, because fate had to be obeyed, he oppressed even the brahmins.

children.text: bhartur īdṛśi vṛttānte mantrī tasyāvayoḥ pitā
children.translated_text: At such a turn in his master's affairs, the minister, the father of us two,
before he saw his lord's calamity, had already gone to heaven.
But that king, hearing of the minister's death, was at once overcome
by royal consumption, with heavy grief as its ally.

children.text: tatas tāte divaṃ yāte yātukāme ca bhūpatau
children.translated_text: Then, when our father had gone to heaven, when the king wished to depart,

children.text: prajāsu ca viraktāsu jātau svaḥ kiṃkriyākulau ||
children.translated_text: and when the subjects were alienated, the two of us were thrown into anxious uncertainty over what should be done.

children.text: prāptakālam idaṃ śreya iti buddhvā prasāritam
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'This useful moment has arrived,'
we spread this rumor through <s>Avanti</s> and its surrounding districts.
Because his judgment was impaired by anger, he was oppressing his own subjects;
so the prince, beloved of the people, had the king put in bonds.
With his feet controlled by chains, fallen from his independent station,

children.text: sukhasya mahato dadhyau sa rājendro gajendravat ||
children.translated_text: that lord of kings brooded, like a lordly elephant, on his former great happiness.
Since anxiety had stolen his sleep, and because he was without food,
he wasted away while passing nights that seemed a hundred years long.
Although he had been brought to such a state by his own son, who wished to win the people's affection,

children.text: na mukta eva muktaś ca yāvat prāṇaiḥ priyair iti ||
children.translated_text: he was never released, except when he was released from his dear life-breaths.
This is the blameworthy source of that rumor;

children.text: itarad vādhunā devaḥ prabhur ity atha bhūpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: as for the rest, Majesty, you are now the master. Then the king,
standing for a moment with downcast face and striking the ground with his palm,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca sāsram ākāśam anātha idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: looked tearfully toward the sky and, helpless, said this:
Apart from you two, best of friends, equal to <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
who could put into effect such an unfailing plan?

children.text: kiṃ tu sattvavatām eṣa śaṅkāśūnyadhiyāṃ kramaḥ
children.translated_text: But this is the way of men of courage, whose minds are free from suspicion,
not of men like me, whose minds are seized by fear of seen and unseen dangers.

children.text: tasmāt pālayataṃ bhadrau pālakaṃ pālakaṃ buvaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, good sirs, protect <s>Pālaka</s>, the protector of the earth;
but I am unable to disregard this false rumor.
As he was speaking thus, while the ministers' faces were lowered in shame,
the copper-crested rooster, crowing, announced that the night had waned.
Then the voices of the sūtas, māgadhas, and court bards were heard,
saying, 'Awake, while the endless quarters are whitened by your fame.'
Hearing that pitiful, piercing, unpleasant sound,
the king covered his ears and shook his head.

children.text: sa cāvocat pratīhārī nivāryantām amī mama
children.translated_text: And he said to the doorkeeper, 'Stop these men of mine;

children.text: kṣate kṣārāvadekena kiṃ phalaṃ bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: what profit is there for you in pouring alkali upon a wound?'

children.text: āsīc cāsyātha vā dhiṅ mām evam ātmāpavādinam
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to him: 'Or rather, shame on me, who blame myself in this way.

children.text: nanu praśasyam ātmānaṃ nāham arhāmi ninditum ||
children.translated_text: Surely I do not deserve to censure myself, who am worthy of praise.
While the king lived long in unrestricted enjoyment,
by what other prince was he cherished as he was by me?
Having cut off enemies hard to uproot, both external and internal,

children.text: varṇāśramāḥ svadharmebhyaḥ kiṃ vā vicalitā mayā ||
children.translated_text: did I make the <s>varṇāśramas</s> (social and religious orders) stray from their own duties?
Who else has, as I do, a son like <s>Avantivardhana</s>, a mine of innate and acquired virtues,

children.text: putraḥ punnarakāt trātā kasyānyasya yathā mama ||
children.translated_text: who rescues him from the hell called <s>Punnaraka</s>?
Or let all this be. By one thing alone I have been exalted:
by my son-in-law, the emperor <s>Naravāhanadeva</s>.

children.text: eka eva tu me nāsīd guṇaḥ so 'py ayam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Only one virtue had not been mine; now that too has arrived,
through the favor of the two excellent ministers: service of a hermitage grove.'
With resolve unshaken, he urged the two ministers:
'Let the audience hall, together with the throne, be set in the pavilion.'

children.text: tayos tu gatayoḥ keśān vāpayitvā savalkalaḥ
children.translated_text: When the two had gone, the king had his hair shaved, put on bark garments,
took up a water-pot as his companion, and left the palace.
Seen by the women of the inner apartments, whose eyes were flooded with grief
and whose hands were laid upon their breasts, he entered the audience pavilion.
He was seen by <s>Pālaka</s>, whose cheeks had grown pale with terror and whose eyes were wide;

children.text: pālakenābravīt taṃ ca sthita eva sthitaṃ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: and, while still standing, he spoke to him as he stood there.

children.text: prasādāt tāta tātasya vatsarājasya ca tvayā
children.translated_text: 'Dear son, by the favor of your father and of <s>Vatsarāja</s>,

children.text: buddheḥ svasyāś ca śuddhāyāḥ kiṃ nāma na parīkṣitam ||
children.translated_text: and by your own pure intelligence, what indeed has not been examined by you?
Therefore foolish men instruct you, who are yourself an instructor;

children.text: yena loke ta ucyante viyātāḥ pitṛśikṣakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for that reason they are called in the world famous teachers of their fathers.

children.text: etāvat tu mayā vācyaṃ pitryaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Only this much must be said by me: this paternal throne
should be occupied by you for the protection of the <s>varṇāśramas</s>.

children.text: tac cāvaśyam anuṣṭheyam asmākīnaṃ vacas tvayā
children.translated_text: And this word of ours must necessarily be carried out by you,

children.text: mādṛśāṃ hi na vākyāni vimṛśanti bhavādṛśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for men such as you do not deliberate over the words of men such as me.'

children.text: itīdaṃ pālakaḥ śrutvā sthitvā cādhomukhaḥ kṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Pālaka</s> stood for a moment with face cast down;
with his eyes fixed on the tip of his nose, he pondered a reply.
But the king, making a deliberately feigned anger, said to <s>Pālaka</s>,
'Sir, mount the throne. What need have you to think of a reply?
Even with a hundred well-reasoned replies from you,
I am hard to restrain, like the torrent of the <s>Śoṇa</s> in the rains by a foot.'
Hearing this, the brahmins, led by the household priest,
wiped away their tears and spoke with voices choked by grief:

children.text: pālakas te niyojyatvād ājñāṃ mā sma vicārayat
children.translated_text: 'Since <s>Pālaka</s> is subject to your command, let him not examine your order.
But since we are empowered by your command, why should we hold back?
While the protector of the subjects, his elder brother, is still alive,
<s>Pālaka</s>, mounting the lion-throne, would surely be as one mounted on a cot.
Or, while you are alive for a hundred years, if he were to kindle the fire of kingship,
he would regard himself as a censured <s>parivettṛ</s> (one who improperly precedes an elder).
Therefore turn away, for our sake, from this exceedingly dreadful resolve.'
May our waters of tears, born of grief, become tears born of joy.
Then, with hands joined, his neck somewhat bowed,

children.text: alaṃ vaḥ pīḍayitvā māṃ vacobhir iti pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king said, "Enough of tormenting me with your words."

children.text: mayāyam abhyanujñāto rakṣaṇe ca kṣamaḥ kṣiteḥ
children.translated_text: "This man has my authorization, and he is capable of protecting the earth.
When raised to the couch of rule, he will not be a condemned <s>khaṭvārūḍha</s> in the eyes of those versed in terminology.

children.text: asamarthe ca rājyāgneḥ pālane patite mayi
children.translated_text: And when I have fallen, unable to tend the fire of kingship,
this lord of men will not become a <s>parivettā</s> (one who improperly supersedes an elder) either.

children.text: yac cāpi pihitāḥ karṇā ākarṇya patitadhvanim
children.translated_text: And as for the fact that your ears were covered when you heard the word 'fallen,'

children.text: prajābhis tac ca na mṛṣā mayā hi nihataḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: that too is not false, for I did indeed kill my father.
Therefore, having committed this sin, in order to quiet the distress I have caused you,

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ vrajan kartuṃ na nivāryo 'smi kenacit ||
children.translated_text: I am going to perform expiation, and I am not to be restrained by anyone.

children.text: mayā cātyaktadharmeṇa yat prajānāṃ kṛte kṛtam
children.translated_text: And what I have done for the sake of the subjects, without abandoning <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty),
in return for that, let this <s>Pālaka</s> be guarded as your protector."

children.text: itīdaṃ prakṛtīr uktvā pālakaṃ punar abravīt
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the ministers and citizens, he again addressed <s>Pālaka</s>:
"For love of me, protect my son <s>Avantivardhana</s>."
With an embarrassed smile, <s>Pālaka</s> said to <s>Gopāla</s>,

children.text: avantivardhano rājā rājan kasmān na jāyatām ||
children.translated_text: "O king, why should <s>Avantivardhana</s> not become king?"

children.text: satsu bhartṛṣu bhūpāla guṇavatsv api bhūbhujaḥ
children.translated_text: "Even when there are capable husbands of the earth, O ruler, though endowed with virtues,

children.text: nikṣiptavantaḥ śrūyante putreṣv eva guruṃ dhuram ||
children.translated_text: kings are heard to have placed the heavy burden upon their sons alone."

children.text: gopālas tam athovāca bhaviṣyati yuvā yadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gopāla</s> said to him, "When he becomes a young man,

children.text: tvaṃ ca vṛddhas tadā yuktaṃ svayam eva kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: and you are old, then you yourself will properly do this."

children.text: evaṃ niruttarāḥ kṛtvā prakṛtīs tāḥ sapālakāḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus left those ministers and citizens, together with <s>Pālaka</s>, without an answer,
he consecrated <s>Pālaka</s> with jars of water from all the sacred fords.
And, quickly setting him upon the throne, facing north,
he went out from his own city as if he had stayed there for only one night.
Then, when the king had disappeared into the forest,
<s>Pālaka</s> entered the city, its people's eyes unmoving, its low sound like labored breathing, as though it were dead.
Then <s>Pālaka</s>, bearing grief hard to cut away, born from separation from his brother,
cast aside concern for the earth and let time pass.
At some point the subjects, beginning with the royal priest, said to him,

children.text: utsīdantīḥ prajā rājan nārhasi tvam upekṣitum ||
children.translated_text: "O king, you ought not to neglect the subjects as they sink into ruin.

children.text: bhrātuḥ puraḥ pratijñāya dūrakṣāṃ rakṣituṃ kṣitim
children.translated_text: Having promised before your brother to protect the earth, hard though it is to protect,

children.text: kiṃ śocasi na śoko 'yam upāyaḥ kṣitirakṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: why do you grieve? This grief is no means for protecting the earth.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhaṃ pāpāṃśam ādatte rakṣann api nṛpaḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: A king takes a sixth share of sin even while protecting his subjects;

children.text: nikṣiptakṣitirakṣas tu sarvam eva na muñcati ||
children.translated_text: but one who has abandoned the protection of the earth does not escape any of it at all.
Therefore, O king, if you wish to destroy sin and to increase merit,

children.text: rājan dhanyāḥ prajāḥ kāryāḥ sukhaṃ cānububhūṣatā ||
children.translated_text: and if you wish to enjoy happiness, you must make your subjects prosperous.

children.text: na ced arthayamānānāṃ vacanaṃ naḥ kariṣyasi
children.translated_text: If you will not do what we ask,

children.text: dhruvaṃ drakṣyasi saṃkrāntā deśān rājanvataḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: you will surely see your subjects, O king, having gone over to countries that have rulers.
While you remain indifferent, we have heard of something never before seen among us:

children.text: balād agnigṛhān nītaḥ puroḍāśaḥ śunā kila ||
children.translated_text: a dog, they say, forcibly carried off the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) from the fire-hall.

children.text: baṭoś ca bhrāmyato bhikṣāṃ bhikṣāpātrād anāvṛtāt
children.translated_text: And from the uncovered alms-bowl of a wandering novice seeking alms,
a crow snatched a sweet-cake while his mind was distracted by his boyishness."
Hearing this, the king, filled with alarm and with drums beaten,
sat upon the lion-seat like <s>Maghavan</s> upon <s>Sumeru</s>.

children.text: tasmin nārūḍhamātre ca samaṃ vikasitāḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: And as soon as he had mounted it, the subjects blossomed all at once,
like lotuses when the sun stands on the peak of the mountain of sunrise.

children.text: athātīte kvacit kāle viprān papraccha pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when some time had passed, the king asked the Brahmins,

children.text: dharmam ācakṣatāṃ pūjyāḥ śuddham ity atha te 'bruvan ||
children.translated_text: "Let the venerable ones declare pure <s>dharma</s>." Then they said:
"What <s>dharma</s> has not been examined by you, who know every branch of knowledge?

children.text: ācāro 'yam iti vyaktam anuyuktās tvayā vayam ||
children.translated_text: It is plainly this matter of conduct about which you have questioned us.

children.text: rāgādimantaḥ puruṣās tair uktā hy apramāṇatā
children.translated_text: Men possess passion and the other faults; therefore what is said by them lacks authority.
Because systems such as <s>Sāṃkhya</s> are not binding for action, the Veda alone has authority.

children.text: tasmād vedeṣu vihitaṃ yat tad āsevyatām iti
children.translated_text: Therefore what is prescribed in the Vedas should be practiced."
Having heard this, the king worshiped with sacrifices accompanied by countless gifts.
Then, because he had abandoned the affairs of his subjects through devotion to a succession of consecrations,
his two ministers, alarmed, once addressed him:
"You have been lifted out of the mud of grief by powerful bull-like Brahmins;
but by whom are you now to be lifted out of the mud of consecration, so hard to cross?

children.text: kāmārthau yady api tyaktau sevyāv eva tathāpi tau
children.translated_text: Even if pleasure and wealth have been renounced, still they too must be attended to,

children.text: durlabho hi vinā tābhyāṃ dharmaḥ śuddho nṛpair iti ||
children.translated_text: for pure <s>dharma</s> is hard for kings to attain without those two."

children.text: upapannam idaṃ śrutvā pratiśrutya tatheti ca
children.translated_text: Hearing this as reasonable, and promising, "So be it,"
he went to the women's quarters, where the women were busy praying to the deities.
Honored with gifts of drink, ornaments, garments, garlands, and affectionate speech,
he moved about, gratifying the maidservants of the inner apartments.
Immediately afterward, the king honored his queens in order, from younger to elder,
and passed the night with the chief queen <s>Vāsukinī</s>.
Awakened by bands of bards along with the cries of roosters,
he attended upon the early dawn until the sight of the sun.
Then, with white garments, garlands, ornaments, and unguents,
praised with blessings of victory, he came to the audience hall.
There, being dear to his officials, he honored the officials beginning with the royal priest
as each deserved, with due ceremony, and dismissed them.

children.text: smayamānas tato rājā mantriṇāv idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then, smiling, the king said this to his two ministers:
"Let a delightful drinking-ground be prepared in the garden.
For who, having friends like you who have provided a remedy for misfortune...
One should not indulge in objects of enjoyment that conflict with what is seen and unseen.
Therefore I, for the townspeople, the servants, and those who move within the inner palace,

children.text: ātmānaṃ ca bhavannāthaṃ yojayāmi sukhair iti ||
children.translated_text: and for myself, whose lord is you, arrange pleasures, so I think.
Then those two, their heads bent low and knowing their master's intention,
said, 'All the equipment for drinking is already prepared.'

children.text: vyāhārya sa tatas tatra sabālasthavirāṃ purīm
children.translated_text: Then, having summoned the city there, including children and elders,
he made it delighted with gifts of clothing, ornaments, garlands, and food.
Then wine, set in cups of ruby and the like, perfumed with blue lotuses and other flowers,

children.text: kṛtajotkāram anyonyaṃ pīyate sma tato madhu ||
children.translated_text: was drunk with mutual shouts of delight.
In the intervals between drinking wine, again and again, to the sound of the vīṇā,

children.text: gīyate sma manohāri naṭādyair nṛtyate sma ca ||
children.translated_text: charming songs were sung, and dancers and others danced.

children.text: vihṛtya dinam evaṃ ca śītaraśmau divākare
children.translated_text: Having passed the day in sport in this way, when the sun was cool-rayed,
the king dismissed his subjects and then entered the inner palace.
There too he heard music and watched a drama performed by women as the actors,
and after making all his wives drink, he afterwards took to sleep.
As he thus enjoyed the objects of sense according to the seasons,
many days passed for him, while his attachment to pleasure increased.
At one time, distressed, he reported to the Brahmins and others:

children.text: svapno mayādya yo dṛṣṭaḥ praśasyaiḥ śrūyatām asau ||
children.translated_text: 'Listen, venerable ones, to this dream that I saw today.
I had gone out to inspect the outer grounds, and there I saw
a great rutting elephant, a forest-roamer, approaching.
Smelling the scent of its rut, even my own royal elephant,
in anger, uprooted its tying post and went toward the forest elephant.

children.text: vanyas tu hastam utkṣipya kiṃcid ākuñcitāṅguliḥ
children.translated_text: But the wild elephant raised its trunk, with its fingers somewhat bent,
and seemed to challenge it to battle with proud roars from its throat.
Then my elephant rushed from afar with speed,
and delivered a great impact against the tusks of the forest elephant.
With its two tusks, white as crystal pillars, that elephant

children.text: dūram utkṣipya nikṣiptas tato yātaḥ parāṅmukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: tossed mine far away, threw it down, and then turned its face away and went off.
Then, seeing my own royal elephant defeated by the other,
I wished to turn it back and said this to those standing near:
I shall turn back the royal elephant; quickly bring the goad.
Surely I was trained in elephant-training by <s>Vatsarāja</s>.
While I was saying this, not obtaining the goad I wanted,

children.text: pratibuddhaḥ sasaṃtrāsaḥ kim etad iti cintayan ||
children.translated_text: I woke up in terror, wondering, What is this?

children.text: iti svapno mayā dṛṣṭaḥ kṣaṇadāyāḥ parikṣaye
children.translated_text: This is the dream I saw at the close of the night.

children.text: phalam iṣṭam aniṣṭaṃ vā pūjyair atrocyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Let the venerable ones say whether its result here is favorable or unfavorable.'
Then the twice-born men, though they knew the dream had an unfavorable result,
being skilled in courtly service to kings, explained it otherwise.

children.text: yau 'sau rājan gajo vanyas taṃ budhyasva vināyakam
children.translated_text: 'That wild elephant, O king, understand to be <s>Vināyaka</s>,
and the consecration elephant to be an embodied obstacle to the kingdom.

children.text: tat te gaṇapatiḥ prītaḥ prasahyoddharati prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the powerful <s>Gaṇapati</s>, pleased with you, forcibly uproots

children.text: tvam apy unmūlitānarthaś ciraṃ pāhi mahīm iti ||
children.translated_text: your misfortune; you too, with calamities uprooted, rule the earth for a long time.'

children.text: iti duḥśliṣṭam ākarṇya phalaṃ svapnasya kalpitam
children.translated_text: Hearing this badly fitted, fabricated fruit of the dream,
he found no comfort. Then his two ministers said this to him:

children.text: śrūyatāṃ deva yad vṛttaṃ vṛddhasya jagatīpateḥ
children.translated_text: 'Listen, Your Majesty, to what happened to an aged lord of the earth.

children.text: āvābhyāṃ śrutam etac ca gṛhe kathayataḥ pituḥ ||
children.translated_text: We heard this from our father as he was telling it at home.
When <s>Pradyota</s>, so the story goes, wished to mount the lion-seat,
the principal twice-born men who had assembled as was fitting were asked about a dream.
While I was seated on the throne, a bird stood on my head,

children.text: vicitraiḥ saptabhiḥ pakṣaiḥ ko 'sau vyākriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: with seven variegated wings. What is that? Explain it.
Among those explanations one Brahmin named <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>,
his speech trembling, spoke in a low voice, nervous and fearful:

children.text: rājñā svapnaphalaṃ pṛṣṭāḥ kiṃ tūṣṇīm āstha kathyatām
children.translated_text: When asked by the king about the fruit of the dream, why do you sit silent? Let it be told.

children.text: trasyadbhiḥ paruṣād vāpi mādṛk kasmān na yujyatām ||
children.translated_text: If you are frightened by harsh consequences, how is one like me not fit to speak?
Even an unwelcome thing should be stated, when its remedy can be accomplished by proper action;
but where a remedy is difficult to make, it is fitting to remain thus indifferent.
Hearing this, <s>Mahāsena</s>, his mind touched by doubt,
asked <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, who wished to speak and whose lips were quivering:

children.text: brahman kathaya viśrabdham anujñāto dvijair api
children.translated_text: Brahmin, speak confidently; you have been permitted even by the Brahmins,

children.text: yasmāt vyāhartum ārabdhaḥ pratiṣiddho na kenacit ||
children.translated_text: since, when you began to speak out, you were not forbidden by anyone.
Thus addressed by the protector of the earth, he began to speak:

children.text: ahitādi hitāntaṃ ca śrūyatāṃ deva mā kupaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Listen, Your Majesty, without anger, to what begins in harm and ends in benefit.
That seven-winged bird is a thunderbolt, dreadful in sound;

children.text: sapta pakṣās tu ye tasya sapta pakṣān nibodha tān ||
children.translated_text: and the seven wings that it has, know them to be seven fortnights.
Enough of speaking at length in every way; enough of that throne for you.

children.text: kaścid āropyatām etad yasya necchasi jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: Let someone be placed upon it whose life you do not desire.
Whoever mounts this today, when seven half-months have passed,

children.text: atīteṣv aśanir hanti patitvā mūrdhani dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: a thunderbolt will surely fall upon his head and kill him.
Hearing this, the lord, his anger throbbing, ordered <s>Bharatarohaka</s>:
Let the eyes of this loud-mouthed fellow be gouged out.
Saying, As you command, and fastening his belt, the minister
with a secret wink made known to the Brahmins the words they should seize upon as testimony.
Then the Brahmins, beginning gently, instructed the king:
Your Majesty, the words of madmen are not accepted by the keen-witted.

children.text: na ca kevalam unmatto brāhmaṇaś caiṣa mūḍhakaḥ
children.translated_text: And this foolish Brahmin is not merely mad
Even for that reason he certainly does not deserve the punishment of having his eyes torn out.

children.text: kiṃ tu tāvad ayaṃ baddhaḥ sthāpyatāṃ vidhavāsutaḥ
children.translated_text: But let this son of a widow be bound and kept for so long

children.text: pakṣāḥ sapta gatā yāvat tataḥ prāpsyati nigraham ||
children.translated_text: until seven fortnights have passed; then he will receive punishment.
Let a golden image of the king quickly mount the throne
at this very auspicious moment, in order to test the twice-born man.

children.text: yadi satyaiva vāg asya tataḥ satkāram āpsyati
children.translated_text: If his speech is in fact true, then he will receive honor;
if the opposite occurs, he will receive the disgrace prescribed by <s>Manu</s> and the others.

children.text: devo 'pi divasān etān vidbhiḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: And Your Majesty, during these days, together with learned Brahmins
who perform rites of pacification, should attend upon <s>Mahākāla</s>.

children.text: iti śrutvā dvijātibhyo yuktam ity avadhārya ca
children.translated_text: Hearing this from the twice-born men and deciding that it was proper,

children.text: bandhayitvā ca śāṇḍilyaṃ mahākālaṃ yayau nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king had <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> bound and went to <s>Mahākāla</s>.

children.text: tatra sapta sthitaḥ pakṣān apaśyad divase 'ntime
children.translated_text: After remaining there for seven fortnights, on the last day
at midday he saw a mass of clouds rising toward the sun.
Then, in a mere moment, it filled the endless quarters of space,
dark as the throat of <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, and rained down a shower of stones.
A fierce thunderbolt, making a harsh crackling roar,
crushed the royal likeness and then disappeared there itself.
Then he summoned <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, had his bonds removed,
asked his forgiveness, and satisfied him with abundant gifts.

children.text: rājñā cāsya kṛtaṃ nāma tac ca loke pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: The king gave him that name, and it became established in the world:
'This is <s>Mukharaśāṇḍilya</s>, whose command has proved true; let him be questioned.'
When he was summoned and questioned by him, he reported without hesitation:

children.text: śṛṇu rājan na kopaṃ ca pitṛvat kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: 'Listen, O king, and you should not become angry, but act like a father.

children.text: yo 'sau vanyo gajaḥ so 'nyo rājā rājann upāgataḥ
children.translated_text: That wild elephant is another king who has come, O king;

children.text: bhavadīyo bhavān eva sarvathā śrūyatām idam ||
children.translated_text: your own elephant is none other than you yourself. Hear this completely.
You, O protector of the earth, have been driven from the kingdom

children.text: svataḥ pracyāvitas tasmād yuktam āsthīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: by another protector of the earth; therefore adopt what is fitting.'
When the lord of the earth heard this, his head bowed down with despondency,
the Brahmins, headed by <s>Mukharaśāṇḍilya</s>, slowly went out.
But the king, with only his minister as helper, put on a covering

children.text: kaḥ syād rājeti cintāvān niṣasāda nṛpāsane ||
children.translated_text: and sat down on the royal seat, thinking, 'Who could be the king?'
Then <s>Surohaka</s>, trusting the words of the one whose command had proved true,
spoke to the lord of the earth in a pitiable voice born of grief:

children.text: mahāsenena duḥsvapnaḥ sa yathā vañcitas tathā
children.translated_text: 'Just as the bad dream was deceived by <s>Mahāsena</s>,

children.text: vañcaya tvam api kṣipram atyāsannaphalo hy asau ||
children.translated_text: so deceive it quickly yourself, for its result is very near.
Let some being born in an animal womb occupy the royal seat,

children.text: devo 'pi divasān kāṃścid vanavāsī bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: and let Your Majesty for a few days become a forest-dweller.'

children.text: tuṣṇībhūtaṃ tu rājānam eva bruvati mantriṇi
children.translated_text: But while the minister was speaking in this way to the silent king,
<s>Avantivardhana</s>, the son of a cowherd, entered there.
As he was playing, his ball flew far away,
fell down, bounced up again, and went beneath the throne.
His sister <s>Avantivardhanayaśā</s>, urged on by him,
was told, 'Pull the ball out from under the throne.'

children.text: tayoktaṃ svayam eva tvaṃ kiṃ na karṣasi kandukam
children.translated_text: She said, 'Why do you not pull the ball out yourself?

children.text: kiṃ cāhaṃ bhavataḥ praiṣyā yenādiśasi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: And am I your servant, that you order me?'

children.text: tataḥ paśyeti tām uktvā tad utkṣipya nṛpāsanam
children.translated_text: Then, saying to her, 'Watch,' <s>Avantivardhana</s>
lifted that royal seat and set it down elsewhere without strain.

children.text: sa tu kandukam ādātum ārabdhaś ca nṛpeṇa tu
children.translated_text: And when he began to take the ball, the king
leapt down from the throne and embraced him, his head bowed with shame.
Immediately afterward the king summoned the circle of his subjects and officials
and said, 'Let this prince be consecrated to the kingdom today.
In your presence, when my elder brother was departing, I was told by him:
"Out of love for me, protect my son <s>Avantivardhana</s>."
Because of that command, and because he is a son, he has now been brought up;

children.text: pitryam āsanam adhyāstāṃ nyāsaṃ pratyarpitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: let him occupy his father's seat. The trust has been restored by me.'
Then, when this difficult matter had been presented by <s>Pālaka</s>,

children.text: sabhāyām ānatāṅgāyāṃ na kaścid kiṃcid uktavān ||
children.translated_text: and the assembly had bowed its limbs, no one said anything.
Then <s>Pālaka</s>, explaining the proper measure of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>,
installed his son upon the throne of <s>Avanti</s>.
The old king, wearing a black-antelope skin as his garment, his hair shorn, a water-pot hanging from his shoulder,

children.text: adhyāsita munivaraiḥ saha kāśyapena mandaspṛho 'sitagiriṃ tapase jagāma ||
children.translated_text: with little desire left, went to <s>Asitagiri</s>, inhabited by eminent sages together with <s>Kāśyapa</s>, for austerity.
Then, while <s>Avantivardhana</s> was king in <s>Avanti</s>,
distress was not caused by anyone even to the smallest creatures.
When many days had passed in this way, the king
once returned after exercising his horses and saw, somewhere,
a maiden shining within a swing hanging from a tamāla tree,
like a trembling crescent moon reflected in a pool of the <s>Kālindī</s>.
She was drawing out a little peacock-feather ornament caught in the end of her upper garment,
like a serpent-woman drawing out a coil from which its slough was being shed.

children.text: dṛśyamānas tayā rājā tāṃ ca paśyan punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Seen by her, and looking at her again and again, the king
entered his own residence, attended by the horse-stable servants.
There, after briefly performing bathing and the rest, he went into seclusion,
and, with his heart swinging, thought only of the swing.
For the king, whose desire for food was slight, whose sleep was slight,
and whose thought of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> was slight, a few days passed.
Then, one day, at an hour when the sun's rays were gentle,
He heard a roar like that of oceans thrown into turmoil.
Wishing to see its cause, with curiosity arisen in him,
he climbed to the palace roof, surrounded by the attendants of the inner apartments.
He saw the elephant <s>Saṃghamardana</s> crushing men, elephants, horses, camels, cows, goats, sheep, and donkeys,
trampling them down in a mass.
With great trees uprooted and lofty houses reduced to powder,
and with rows of bees attending him, he moved on at every moment.
Then the Mātaṅga chieftain, his eyes turned toward the circle of rut-maddened elephants,
saw the king of elephants.
He at once ordered a maiden who stood nearby:
'This elephant-worm is violent and hard to tame; let it be tamed.'
Then, with water made lovely by the touch of her lotus-hand,
she sprinkled the elephant from afar on his trunk, whose tip was curled.
Then, abandoning his rage, the elephant curled up his trunk,

children.text: vavande caraṇau tasyāḥ saṃspṛśya śirasā mahīm ||
children.translated_text: and bowed at her feet, touching the earth with his head.
The lord of <s>Avanti</s>, seeing her, as though she had been seen before, and seeing her come in that way,
wondering in his heart, reflected in his mind:

children.text: kiṃ citraṃ yad ayaṃ nāgaḥ saharāgaḥ sacetanaḥ
children.translated_text: 'What wonder is it that this elephant, passionate and conscious as he is,
has been brought under control by an embodied science of enchantment?

children.text: iyaṃ hi vītarāgādīn munīn api nirīkṣitā
children.translated_text: For she, merely beheld, would bring under her power even sages whose passion has departed,

children.text: vaśīkuryād viśantī ca calayed acalān api ||
children.translated_text: and, entering them, would make even the immovable move.'
Then, with an upper garment colored like a rainbow,

children.text: baddhāṃ dolām adhiṣṭhāya nāgaṃ yāhīty acodayat ||
children.translated_text: he fastened a swing to the tusks and urged her, 'Mount it and drive the elephant.'
Then <s>Saṃghamardana</s>, with very slow, well-practiced steps,
went to the post, surrounded by citizens whose fear had gone.

children.text: tayoktam ātapaś caṇḍaḥ saṃtāpayati mām iti
children.translated_text: When she said, 'The sun is fierce and burns me,'

children.text: aśokapallavaiś chāyām atha tasyāś cakāra saḥ ||
children.translated_text: he then made shade for her with aśoka leaves.
After tying the elephant to a post on the palace roof,

children.text: vanditvā ca mahīpālaṃ mātaṅgī pakṣaṇaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: and after saluting the king, the Mātaṅgī went to the quarter.
Seeing himself purified by the Mātaṅgī's salutation, the king

children.text: keyaṃ kasya kuto veti pṛcchati sma surohakam ||
children.translated_text: asked <s>Surohaka</s>, 'Who is she? Whose daughter is she? From where has she come?'

children.text: sa tasmai kathayāmāsa deva na jñāyate kutaḥ
children.translated_text: He told him, 'Your Majesty, it is not known from where
this Mātaṅga quarter suddenly came here recently.
There are powerful Mātaṅgas there. <s>Utpalahastaka</s> is their chieftain;
this maiden is his daughter, <s>Surasamañjarī</s>.'
Hearing this, he went inside, meditating on <s>Surasamañjarī</s>,
and kept his body alive with treatments for a bilious fever.
But <s>Surohaka</s>, seeing that his mind had been affected by the Mātaṅgī,

children.text: ākhyad aṅgāravatyai sa tannaptur vṛttam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: reported this condition of her grandson to <s>Aṅgāravatī</s>.

children.text: sā tu sthitvā kṣaṇaṃ tūṣṇīṃ vicārastimitekṣaṇā
children.translated_text: She remained silent for a moment, her eyes motionless in thought,
and then, with a smile that removed his fear, addressed <s>Surohaka</s>:
'Just as other divine women take on the form of Mātaṅgīs,
so too she has come to earth for some reason.

children.text: kva saṃghamardano vyālaḥ kva ca taddantalambanam
children.translated_text: Where is the savage <s>Saṃghamardana</s>, and where is hanging from his tusks?
Who has ever seen such an action performed by anyone not divine?
Or rather, enough deliberation. I myself shall go to her kinsman's house
to ask for the maiden; there is no go-between equal to oneself.'
Then, mounted on a carriage and preceded by aged Brahmins,
she went and saw <s>Utpalahastaka</s> standing in the middle of the settlement.

children.text: dūrād eva sa dṛṣṭvā tām āttakarkaraveṇukaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing her from afar, he took up his karkara and flute,
and, together with the Mātaṅga assembly, bowed while withdrawing far away.
Then <s>Aṅgāravatī</s>, descending from the vehicle, said to him,

children.text: ahaṃ tvāṃ draṣṭum āyātā tvam apy eṣa palāyase ||
children.translated_text: 'I have come to see you, and here you are running away.

children.text: kāryaṃ me mahad āsannam ādhīnaṃ cāpi tat tvayi
children.translated_text: A great matter of mine is at hand, and it depends on you;

children.text: dūrotsaraṇam utsṛjya tena ḍhaukasva mām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore stop moving away at a distance and approach me.'
When he had sent the Mātaṅgas away and sat near her, she said to him,
'Let <s>Surasamañjarī</s> be given as queen to my grandson, the king.
You should not obstruct me with rustic talk such as,

children.text: na ca grāmeyakālāpais tvaṃ māṃ bādhitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: "A king should not touch a Caṇḍālī," and the like.

children.text: yaś ca divyābhimānas te tatrāpīdaṃ mamottaram
children.translated_text: And as for your pride in being divine, this too is my answer:
good sir, my grandson is a cakravartin for such people as you.'
Hearing <s>Aṅgāravatī</s>'s words, <s>Utpalahastaka</s>
accepted her request with 'So be it,' without uttering any reply.
Then, secretly placing <s>Surasamañjarī</s> in a carriage,
she brought that life-restoring herb for her grandson.

children.text: pariṇīya tu mātaṅgīm antar antaḥpurād bahiḥ
children.translated_text: Having married the Mātaṅgī, whether inside the inner apartments or outside,

children.text: sa buddhyāpi na yāti sma pratyakṣam api tāṃ smaran ||
children.translated_text: he did not go elsewhere even in thought, remembering her though she was before his eyes.

children.text: iyam evāsti tattvena mithyānyad iti cintayan
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'She alone truly exists; everything else is false,'
he regarded saṃsāra as having the form of a city of Gandharvas.

children.text: gamayan divasān evam ekadā saha kāntayā
children.translated_text: Passing his days in this way, one day, together with his beloved,
he went up to the palace and saw the settlement empty of people.

children.text: taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā triyāmānte mandaṃ surasamañjarī
children.translated_text: Seeing it at the end of the night, <s>Surasamañjarī</s>, softly
weeping and wiping away her tears, was questioned by the king:

children.text: kiṃ śūnyaṃ pakkaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā rudyate sundari tvayā
children.translated_text: 'Why do you weep, beautiful one, after seeing the settlement empty?

children.text: utānyad asti duḥkhasya kāraṇaṃ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Or is there some other cause of sorrow? Tell me.'
She said, 'What have I to do with the settlement now, when I have come to you?

children.text: kiṃ tu kāraṇam asty anyad bhīṣaṇaṃ tan niśāmyatām ||
children.translated_text: But there is another dreadful cause; listen to it.
This father of mine is accomplished in Mātaṅga magic and possesses great supernatural power.
Formerly, in <s>Saptavarṇapura</s>, in the city called <s>Vāyumukta</s>, there lived
a śvapāka named <s>Kāla</s>, the lowest of the hosts of <s>Vidyādharas</s>.

children.text: ipphako nāma tasyaiva pitrāhaṃ ca pratiśrutā ||
children.translated_text: He was called <s>Ipphaka</s>, and I was promised to that very one by my father.
Then once, when the wind had come through the sky to my father's house,
it carried off a flower garland, tawny with dust and with a line of bees upon it.

children.text: sā tu saṃdhyām upāsīnaṃ gaṅgārodhasi nāradam
children.translated_text: But that garland, while <s>Nārada</s> was performing his twilight worship on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
wrapped itself around him, wavering like a female serpent, as he stood with his arm steady as a post.

children.text: vyutthitaś ca samādhes taṃ dṛṣṭvā lohitalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: And rising from his meditation and seeing it, his eyes red,
<s>Nārada</s>, because of his fierce anger, spoke these words aloud:
'The garland touched by a body, which has been thrown at me by this garland-bearer,

children.text: kṣiptā mayi manuṣyeṣu caṇḍālaḥ sa bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: whoever he is, let him become a caṇḍāla among human beings.'
Then my father, scorched by the curse, petitioned him,
saying, 'Let there be some remedy for this terrible curse of a Brahmin.'
Then the fire of <s>Nārada</s>, its mass of flames of anger quenched by the water of compassion,
said this to the downcast lotus-handed one:

children.text: na śakyaḥ pratisaṃhartuṃ śāpavahnir mayāpy ayam
children.translated_text: 'This fire of a curse, once released even by me, cannot be drawn back,
like an arrow shot by an archer who has set the feathers in place.

children.text: kiṃtv anicchāśamāḥ śāpāḥ prājñair abhimukhā gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Yet curses that have gone forth against one's will and have been faced by the wise

children.text: svalpenāpi hi vañcyante tena tvam api vañcaya ||
children.translated_text: are cheated even by a little means; therefore you too must cheat this one.
When <s>Gaupāli</s> marries your daughter,

children.text: tadā tvaṃ dāruṇād asmād asmacchāpād vimokṣyase ||
children.translated_text: then you will be released from this dreadful curse of mine.'

children.text: iti śāpe varaṃ labdhvā vayaṃ tvatpādapālitāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, having obtained a boon within the curse, we, protected at your feet,
lived free from sorrow through a year equal to day and night.
By the sage's grace I became the guardian of your feet,
and, once his curse too had been pacified, I was driven away from heaven to you.

children.text: sa kadācid ito dṛṣṭvā gatam utpalahastakam
children.translated_text: But once, seeing <s>Utpalahastaka</s> gone away from here,

children.text: matkṛte tvām api krūra ipphakaḥ pīḍayed iti ||
children.translated_text: cruel <s>Ipphaka</s>, on my account, might torment you as well.
Seeing this dwelling of my father free of mātaṅgas,
and suspecting danger from the caṇḍāla, I wept, helpless and without support.

children.text: asti cātrāpi sukara upāyaḥ sa tu duṣkaraḥ
children.translated_text: There is, even here, a remedy that is easy, yet it is also difficult,
because it must be accomplished through the great king; for the king is hostile.

children.text: yadi vijñāpayantīṃ māṃ nānyathā vaktum iṣyasi
children.translated_text: If, when I am making my request, you will not wish to answer me otherwise,

children.text: tato vijñāpayiṣyāmi kartavye tu bhavān prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: then I shall make it known; but in what is to be done, you are the master.

children.text: athoktaṃ janarājena yad icchasi tad ucyatām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Janarāja</s> said, 'Say whatever you wish.
Apart from talk of another woman, timid one, I shall accomplish everything for you.'
Then <s>Surasamañjarī</s>, her face and breasts sprinkled with tears of joy,
said, 'This is very great favor,' and spoke:
'As the ordinance has been established by the overlord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>,
a king who has entered the inner apartments is not to be harmed, even if he is guilty.'

children.text: itīdaṃ nṛpatiḥ śrutvā tām uvāca kṛtasmitaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the king said to her with a smile,

children.text: anugrahe 'pi yācñeti yad idaṃ tad idaṃ nanu ||
children.translated_text: 'So this, then, is your request even in the matter of favor.'
And from that day onward, day and night, the lord of <s>Avanti</s>,
like the moon on the night of new moon, became hard for people to see.
Then once, hearing that the city was going out for a water-giving festival,
the king too became eager, with the whole row of palace buildings remaining behind.
Because he had gained the kingdom in childhood, his mind was led away by the senses,

children.text: tadālpadarśī samayaṃ visasmāra sa taṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, being shortsighted then, he forgot that arrangement.

children.text: prasuptām eva dayitām āropya śibikāṃ niśi
children.translated_text: At night he placed his beloved, still sleeping, in a palanquin
and brought her to the bank of <s>Śivataḍāga</s>, a place of wondrous happenings.
Then, on a raft as on a boat, over that tank crowded with makaras like a great ocean,
he roamed with his wife, who had shaken off sleep.
As he watched the boys of the city, who had been permitted to plunge in,

children.text: so 'paśyad dayitāṃ bhītāṃ mā bhaiṣīr iti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: he saw his beloved afraid and said, 'Do not be frightened.'

children.text: sāvadat pālitā yena prajāḥ sarvā na bibhyati
children.translated_text: She said, 'All the subjects feel no fear because they are protected by you;
therefore, while I stand upon your very breast, it is not fitting for me to say, "I am afraid."
But this excursion has now been experienced;

children.text: ihāsitam ahaṃ manye tasmād āvartyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: I think staying here is pointless, so let us turn back.'
Since his mind had been carried away by the excursion, he did not listen to her words,
and <s>Avantivardhana</s> saw himself bound together with his wife.
Then, while the citizens cried out and watched with eyes raised upward,
<s>Ipphaka</s>, his anger throbbing, lifted him up and carried him away.
Then, when <s>Aṅgāravatī</s> was bewildered on hearing of her grandson's abduction,
the two ministers cooled her with words like moist winds.

children.text: sā tāv uvāca saṃbhrāntā gatvāsitagiriṃ laghu
children.translated_text: Alarmed, she said to them, 'Go quickly to <s>Asitagiri</s>;

children.text: pālakaḥ śrāvyatāṃ sūnor vṛttāntam iti tau gatau ||
children.translated_text: let <s>Pālaka</s> be told the account of his son.' So the two went.
There they bowed to the ascetics headed by <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
and, after being received, they told <s>Pālaka</s> that his son had been taken.
Then <s>Kāśyapa</s> revived him, whose life-breath had risen to his throat,

children.text: svantaḥ khalv eṣa vṛttānta iti vākyāmṛtena tam ||
children.translated_text: with the nectar of his words: 'Surely this affair has a happy ending.
If there is doubt, look, with your eyes set toward the sky;

children.text: āyāntīm eva jānīhi putravārttāṃ śivām iti ||
children.translated_text: know that auspicious news of your son is arriving even now.'
Then, sending their gaze into the sky,
the ascetics saw a divine being coming through the air, shining with sword and shield.
Descending from the path of the wind, with <s>Ipphaka</s> brought under his control,
he bowed to <s>Kāśyapa</s> and the others together with the lord of <s>Avanti</s>.
And when <s>Pālaka</s> had regained consciousness and the daughter-in-law had bowed at his feet,
the <s>Vidyādhara</s> told the story in the presence of the sages,
a matter dear to <s>Naravāhanadatta</s>, lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>.
Know me as the attendant named <s>Divākaradeva</s>.
As I was going through the sky from <s>Himavat</s> to <s>Malaya</s>,
above the land of the <s>Avantīs</s> I saw this <s>Caṇḍāla</s>,
carrying off the lord of the earth together with his wife and departing,
the low-born member of a <s>Vidyādhara</s> clan, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> named <s>Ipphaka</s>.

children.text: muñceti ca mayoktaḥ san yadāyaṃ na vimuktavān
children.translated_text: When, though I had told him, 'Release him,' he did not release him,
then, after defeating him in battle, I brought him to the Cakravartin.

children.text: anuyuktaś ca tenāyam ayaṃ rājā hṛtas tvayā
children.translated_text: And when he was questioned by him, 'Was this king carried off by you?

children.text: kim ity avocad etena yan me dārā hṛtā iti ||
children.translated_text: Why?' he said, 'Because my wives were carried off by him.'

children.text: atha bhartrāham ādiṣṭaḥ saṃyamya prāpyatām ayam
children.translated_text: Then I was ordered by my lord, 'Bind this man and bring him
to the good assembly presided over by good members of the assembly, beginning with <s>Kāśyapa</s>.
When he has been defeated in the lawsuit, whether he has gained <s>Surasamañjarī</s>
or <s>Vardhamānakamālā</s>, this man has been defeated before the whole assembly.'

children.text: aham apy āryuṣaṃ draṣṭuṃ kāśyapaṃ svaṃ ca mātulam
children.translated_text: I too will come tomorrow to see the venerable <s>Kāśyapa</s>

children.text: āgantā svaḥ pratijñātaṃ teṣām āgamanaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: and my own maternal uncle; their coming has been promised by me.
Then, honoring the king with divine garments and ornaments,

children.text: āliṅgya ca sasauhārdaṃ mayā saha visṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: and embracing him with affection, he sent him off with me.

children.text: sa cāyam ipphako baddhaḥ sadāraś caiṣa bhūpatiḥ
children.translated_text: And this <s>Ipphaka</s> is bound; and here is the king together with his wife.

children.text: cakravartī ca vo draṣṭum āgantā sāvarodhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Cakravartin too, with his inner apartments, will come to see you.
When the seers heard these words of <s>Divākaradeva</s>,
their bodies wet with tears of joy, they passed the night with difficulty.

children.text: atha prātar nabhovyāpi nirabhre vyomni garjitam
children.translated_text: Then in the morning, hearing a roar spreading through the sky

children.text: ākarṇya munayo 'pṛcchan kim etad iti khecaram ||
children.translated_text: in the cloudless firmament, the sages asked the sky-goer, 'What is this?'
He said, 'This is the sound of the drums of those who travel in aerial cars.
Because they are inside the aerial cars, it is heard in the form of thunder.
Here comes our master, the sovereign lord of the <s>Vidyādhara</s> chiefs.
Look at him in the sky, like a cloud with thundering drums.'
Then from afar the ascetics saw a host of aerial cars in the sky,
covering the sky in all directions like clouds, tawny with red rainbows, lightning, and crane-like brightness,
formidable with masses of radiance from many jewels,
as it approached from the heavens.
The Cakravartin's aerial car descended at the gate of the hermitage,
while the others stood on the cave-mouths and summits of the mountain.
The aerial car of the overlord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> was lotus-shaped,
adorned with twenty-six petals made of ruby.
He himself sat in the middle, on a pericarp made of garuḍa-stone,
and his wives, beautifully adorned, stood on its petals.
That elephant among <s>Vidyādharas</s>, with his herd of wife-elephants,
entered the lotus-pond of the assembly, whose face-lotuses were blooming.
Then, after saluting the sages there, headed by <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
he bowed to his maternal uncle, who was motionless from excess of joy.
Thereafter, by the queens who followed their husband,
his fathers-in-law, the ascetics in order from younger to elder, were saluted.
When the Cakravartin had sat down on the seat permitted to him, <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
with the water of joy pouring from his eyes, spoke in choked syllables:
'A blessing is uttered as a wish for the attainment of a desired object not yet gained;

children.text: āyuṣmatā tu tat prāptam āśiṣāṃ yad agocaram ||
children.translated_text: but you, long-lived one, have gained what lies beyond the reach of blessings.
Yet, since conversation requires a reply in return,
we, following custom, say this:
May this blameless sovereignty of yours, together with your wives and friends,
remain unshaken even at the end of a great kalpa.'
When <s>Pālaka</s> asked about the lineages and names of the brides,
<s>Gomukha</s>, prompted by the Cakravartin, related them.
And at the end of such stories, the Cakravartin said to the ascetics,
'Venerable ones, let <s>Ipphaka</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s>, be questioned.
On account of what offense did this man carry off the king,
whose mind was occupied with his journey, together with <s>Surasamañjarī</s>?'
When questioned, he replied, 'After giving his daughter to me,

children.text: dattvā duhitaraṃ paścād etasmai dattavān iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Utpalahastaka</s> later gave her to this man.'
Then, when asked, 'Speak,' <s>Avantivardhana</s> said,

children.text: dattvā na dattavān yo 'smai nanv asau pṛcchyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Surely the one who, having given her, did not give her to him, should be questioned.'
Then <s>Utpalahastaka</s>, leaving his seat, said to the assembly,
'It is just as this man says; but hear the special circumstance.

children.text: nāradena purā śaptaḥ kruddhenāhaṃ yathā tathā
children.translated_text: Long ago I was cursed by the angry <s>Nārada</s>,
as was directly seen by the venerable ones with divine sight.
At that time this long-lived man was instructed by me many times:

children.text: sutā dattā mayā tubhyam upayacchasva tām iti ||
children.translated_text: "My daughter has been given by me to you; marry her."

children.text: uktaś caivam uvācāyaṃ ninditāṃ kaḥ sacetanaḥ
children.translated_text: And when addressed in this way, he said, "What sensible man
would marry a censured maiden from a family burnt by a curse?"
When she had been rejected by him in the presence of <s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s> and others,
then <s>Surasamañjarī</s> was given to the lord of <s>Avantī</s>.
If there is any doubt, let all these lords of the <s>Vidyādhara</s> hosts

children.text: pṛcchyantām iti pṛṣṭaiś ca tat tatheti niveditam ||
children.translated_text: be asked'; and when they were asked, they reported, 'That is so.'
Then <s>Kāśyapa</s> said to him, 'You are cast down, sky-goer,
since the matter has been established by witnesses such as <s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s> and the others.
Now perform this penance for your insolence:
in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, immerse dead bodies in the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
making your dwelling in a charnel ground and wearing a corpse-shroud,
And living on alms for food, at the end of the rainy season you will be freed from the curse.
Then, from <s>Ujjayinī</s>, even old men blind from age, men blind from birth, dull-witted children, and others somehow arrived,
desiring to see the son of the king of the <s>Vatsas</s>; the ascetic grove was then surrounded by them together with the women.
Then the lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>, in front of <s>Kāśyapa</s> and <s>Āryuṣa</s>,
was questioned by his maternal uncle the seer, by his friends, and by the whole company of his wives:

children.text: āyuṣman vayam ete ca tapovittāḥ sapālakāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Long-lived one, we and these ascetics rich in austerity, together with <s>Pālaka</s>,
stand here with minds motionless through longing to hear your story.

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ durlabhaṃ labdham idam āyuṣmatā yathā
children.translated_text: Tell us how this hard-to-obtain sovereignty was obtained by you, long-lived one,

children.text: svīkṛtāś ca yathā vadhvas tathā naḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and how your brides were accepted by you.'
Then, when the lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> had been asked thus by the ascetic,
his face, with its great eyes widened from fear, became pale.

children.text: acintayac ca kaṣṭeyam āpad āpatitā yataḥ
children.translated_text: And he thought, 'This harsh calamity has befallen me, since
who would not be burned by a fire that is very near and very fickle?

children.text: iyam api bhṛśaṃ raktā prītyāham anayāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: She too is deeply attached, and I was brought away by her through love;

children.text: idaṃ sacetanaḥ ko nu kathayed gurusaṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: what conscious man could tell this in the presence of his elders?

children.text: śūro mayā hataḥ śatrur māṃ śūraḥ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: A brave man might say, "A brave enemy was killed by me, and a brave man came to me for refuge";

children.text: iti śūrakathāṃ śūraḥ kuryāt kaḥ śūrasaṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: but what brave man would tell a story of bravery in the presence of brave men?
If I do not tell it, there will be the sage's curse; otherwise, a great sin.

children.text: sulabhānto varaṃ śāpo dustaraṃ na tu pātakam ||
children.translated_text: Better a curse, whose end is easily reached, not a sin that is hard to cross.

children.text: kṛta eva tu gauryā me prasādaḥ saṃkaṭeṣu mām
children.translated_text: But <s>Gaurī</s> has indeed granted me a favor: "Remember me in emergencies."

children.text: smarer iti na ca nyāyyaṃ tām api smartum īdṛśi ||
children.translated_text: Yet in such a case it is not proper to remember even her.'
As soon as he had merely thought this, before the universal emperor
great <s>Gaurī</s>, whose radiance had eclipsed the sun, spoke:
'Of the seer, the maternal uncle, the wives, the friends, and the kings,

children.text: śrotuṃ yad ucitaṃ yasya sa tac chroṣyati netaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: each will hear what is proper for him to hear, and no other thing.'

children.text: ity uktvā vadane tasya paṭūbhūtvā sarasvatī
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, becoming skilled upon his mouth,
told that wondrous life-story of the universal emperor.
Let the sage, the maternal uncle, the friends, the kings, and the beloved women
hear, with steady minds, the life-story as it is being narrated.

children.text: asti vatseṣu nagarī kauśāmbī hṛdayaṃ bhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: In the land of the <s>Vatsas</s> there is a city, <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, the heart of the earth;
in it King <s>Udayana</s> dwelt, near the <s>Kālindī</s>.
If I were to tell even a little of the virtues of this country, this city,

children.text: kathayeyaṃ yadi guṇān na kathā kathitā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and this king, the story itself would not be told.

children.text: yo hi saptārṇavadvīpāṃ draṣṭum uccalitaḥ kṣitim
children.translated_text: For if a man sets out to see the earth with its seven oceans and islands,

children.text: ratnāni gaṇayen meroḥ kadā draṣṭā sa medinīm ||
children.translated_text: but counts the jewels of <s>Meru</s>, when will he see the earth?
Therefore enough of this digression, which obstructs attachment to the tale.

children.text: kathyamānāṃ kathām eva śṛṇuta prakṛtāṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: Listen to the present story itself as it is told by me.
Although the king had a great inner palace, his thought of wives rested on two:
on <s>Vāsavadattā</s> and on <s>Padmāvatī</s>.
Like the arms of <s>Śārṅgapāṇi</s>, mighty in power for the king,
and like the expedients embodied, there were four friends and ministers:

children.text: ṛṣabhaś ca rumaṇvāṃś ca tathā yaugandharāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Rumaṇvān</s>, <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: vasantakaś ceti sa taiḥ saha kālam ayāpayat ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vasantaka</s>. With them he passed his time.
One day, when the king was in the audience hall, two merchant youths,
their knees touching the ground, made this petition after being questioned:
'Your Majesty, our father went with fear upon the abode of makaras, the sea;

children.text: saha tena sa potena nāgalokaṃ praveśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with that ship he was made to enter the world of the <s>Nāgas</s>.

children.text: jyeṣṭhaś ca tanayas tasya pitṛbhaktyaiva sāgaram
children.translated_text: And his eldest son, out of devotion to his father, went to the ocean,

children.text: gatas tatraiva ca gataḥ so 'pi tātagatāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: and there he too met the same fate that his father had met.

children.text: yac ca no draviṇaṃ sāraṃ tad gṛhītvā prajāvatī
children.translated_text: Taking what was the substantial part of our wealth, his wife <s>Prajāvatī</s>
keeps it and, though repeatedly sought out, does not give it back.

children.text: tena deva yadi nyāyyaṃ pitṛdraviṇam āvayoḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, Your Majesty, if it is proper, let our father’s property

children.text: bhrātṛjāyā tataḥ sā nau vyutthitā dāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: be made to be delivered to us by that sister-in-law, who has risen against us.'
Then the king spoke to the bowing door-keeper <s>Yaśodharā</s>:
'It is difficult for women of good family to enter the royal audience hall.

children.text: tena gatvā gṛhaṃ tasyās tvayā vāṇijayoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore go yourself to the house of that merchant’s wife,

children.text: sā yadāha sabhāyās tat samakṣaṃ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and what she says there should be reported in the presence of the assembly.'
Then <s>Yaśodharā</s>, having gone and returned, made this report:

children.text: vijñāpayati sā yat tad ākarṇayitum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: 'What she reports, you ought to hear.

children.text: sā dūrād eva māṃ dṛṣṭvā pratyudgamya sasaṃbhramā
children.translated_text: Seeing me from afar, she rose to meet me in agitation,
and, with a smile, said, "Welcome, tongue of the king."
Then, when I had sat on a cane seat and she had performed the courtesies of water for the feet and so on,

children.text: sā mām āhāgame kāryam āryayā jñāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: she said to me, "Let the noble lady make known the business of her coming."
But when the command of His Majesty had been told, she said with keen modesty:

children.text: ārye sarvam idaṃ satyaṃ devarau me yad āhatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Noble lady, all this is true that my two brothers-in-law have said.

children.text: kiṃtu tasyānayor bhrātur vipannaṃ vahanaṃ śrutam
children.translated_text: But it has been heard that the ship of the brother of these two was lost;

children.text: vahanasya punaḥ svāmī vipanna iti na śrutam ||
children.translated_text: it has not, however, been heard that the master of the ship was lost.
Many travelers by sea, whose ships have been heard to be destroyed,

children.text: avipannā gṛhān eva śrūyante punar āgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are heard to have come back again to their homes, unharmed.

children.text: tathā kadācid anayoḥ sa bhrātā vahanāpadaḥ
children.translated_text: So perhaps that brother of these two, freed from the danger to the ship,
may come back again, in accordance with the signs that I am not widowed.
And another thing: for me, being pregnant, this is the tenth month
that is passing; perhaps a brother's son may be born for these two.

children.text: putro me yadi jāyeta jīvan vā patir āpatet
children.translated_text: If a son is born to me, or if my living husband comes in distress,

children.text: tataḥ svīkṛtasarvasvau devarau me kva yāsyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then where will my brothers-in-law go, after having taken possession of all the property?

children.text: etan manasi kṛtvārthaṃ dravyaṃ devarayor aham
children.translated_text: Keeping this matter in mind, I have not deposited the property of my brothers-in-law.

children.text: na nikṣiptavatī śeṣam āryayā jñāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Let the noble lady report the rest."'

children.text: iti śrutvā mahīpālo vāṇijāv idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Having heard this, the king said this to the two merchants:
"The housewife, skilled in family custom, has spoken what is proper.
When a brother's son has been born to you two, or else when your brother returns,
then, whether it concerns both of you or neither of you, we shall deal with it as is proper."
Then, while this conversation was still unfinished,
a loud tumult arose, filling the sky and mingled with the roar of musical instruments.
And suddenly, with a smile, holding garments and the like in her hands,
a merchant's female attendant who had come in haste informed the king:

children.text: vardhatāṃ naś ciraṃ devo diṣṭyā prakṛtisaṃpadā
children.translated_text: "May Your Majesty prosper for us for a long time! By good fortune, with prosperity restored to the realm,
a son has been born to the wife of the brother of these two merchants."
And with his mind filled with wonder, the lord of the earth thought:
"Ah, the greatness of a son is being experienced directly.
When, for a householder, a little drop of blood called 'son' has been born,
look at the display of these merchants, whose minds are bewildered by joy.

children.text: vaṇijo draviṇasyāyam ataḥ pālaka ity amī
children.translated_text: Since this child is now the guardian of the merchant's wealth,
these men have become like friends and enemies together, equal in joy and sorrow.
But for this wealth of ours, and for the circle of the earth,

children.text: avasāne vinā putrāt pālakaḥ ko bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: who will be the protector at the end, apart from a son?"
As the king sat absorbed in this thought concerning a son,
with long sighs as his companions, several days passed.
One day, while he was sitting comfortably, the commander of the army addressed him:
"Let an excursion to the <s>Mṛgājina</s> garden be graced by your sight."

children.text: gataś ca dṛṣṭavāṃs tatra tatra tatra niveśitāḥ
children.translated_text: He went, and there he saw, set up here and there,
large picture galleries, with kings painted in the pictures.

children.text: apṛcchac ca rumaṇvantam ayaṃ kaḥ kaḥ kṣitīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: And he asked <s>Rumaṇvān</s>, "Who is this, and which king is that?

children.text: ye caitān anutiṣṭhanti te ke ke puruṣā iti ||
children.translated_text: And who are the men who attend upon them?"
He said, "This is <s>Sagara</s>, whose fame crossed the ocean,
surrounded by sixty thousand heroic sons.

children.text: ayaṃ daśaratho rājā vṛto rāmādibhiḥ sutaiḥ
children.translated_text: This is King <s>Daśaratha</s>, attended by sons beginning with <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ pāṇḍur amī cāsya tanayāḥ pañca pāṇḍavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, and these are his five sons, the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>."

children.text: evamādīn asau dṛṣṭvā svargiṇaḥ putriṇo nṛpān
children.translated_text: Seeing such kings, departed to heaven and possessed of sons,
he became anxious and reflected, no longer thinking of the painted tour:

children.text: puṇyavanta ime bhūpāḥ putravanto divaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: "These fortunate kings, having sons, went to heaven;
but I, of little merit, must go, I think, to the hell for the sonless."
Overcome by concern for a son, he returned from the <s>Mṛgājina</s> excursion
and saw the Avanti princess frequenting the palace garden,
standing while she leaned upon the end of a coppery <s>aśoka</s> creeper,
whose young shoots were reddened by the shade of the lotus of her own hand.
Through neglect, her garlands, sandal paste, and ornaments were carelessly arranged,
and her faded lotus-face seemed to announce distress.
Approaching her, he said, "Why should an <s>aśoka</s>, a 'sorrowless' tree, be honored by one full of sorrow?
Why is a red young shoot attended as though it had won a victory?"
She, flustered by the sudden arrival of her husband, replied:

children.text: mahārāja kutaḥ śoko nāmāpi tava gṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: "Great king, how could even the name of sorrow be uttered in regard to you?

children.text: kiṃtu pārāvatīm enāṃ cañcvā cañcuṣu taṇḍulān
children.translated_text: But I am watching this pigeon, putting grains of rice with its beak
into the beaks of its own chicks, as a creature blessed with offspring."
And the king had this thought: "Just as I am distressed by concern for a son,
endless and continuous, so too is she afflicted."

children.text: atha tatra kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā gatvā padmāvatīgṛham
children.translated_text: Then, after staying there a moment, he went to <s>Padmāvatī</s>'s house;

children.text: adṛṣṭvā tatra tāṃ tasyāḥ pṛṣṭavān paricārikām ||
children.translated_text: not seeing her there, he asked her maidservant:

children.text: kva devīty uktayākhyātam udyāne putrakasya sā
children.translated_text: "Where is the queen?" When asked, the servant reported, "She is in the garden,
celebrating the marriage of her child, the <s>Mādhavī</s> creeper, with the <s>Sahakāra</s> mango."

children.text: śrutveti vatsarājasya buddhir āsīd aho mama
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the king of the <s>Vatsas</s> thought, "Ah, for my wives,
the days pass together with wishes for a son.
For people who do not want sons, there is no room left in their houses
because of children whose hands scatter things through the home and whose crying fills the cradles.
But for us, who long for one, not even a single son, the cause of a family's life,

children.text: na labhyate sutaḥ paśya vaiparītyaṃ vidher iti ||
children.translated_text: is obtained. See the perversity of fate!"
Departing from there, he sat in his own pavilion
in the palace garden, surrounded by friends who had come without summons.
There he asked his friends, "That medicine for life,

children.text: mūlaṃ kulataroḥ kasya kiyantaḥ putrakā iti ||
children.translated_text: the root of the family tree: how many sons does each of you have?"
When they had no answer and had bent their heads a little,
<s>Vasantaka</s>, joking out of affection, spoke:
"Your Majesty, we are devoted to our master and follow our master's condition.

children.text: yāvantaḥ svāminaḥ putrās tāvanto 'smākam apy ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, as many sons as our master has, so many do we also have."
<s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>, who was standing nearby, said to him softly:
"Even when there is no occasion, this mouth of yours is uncovered.
By striking the thorn in one tormented by the sickness of concern for a son,
surely you produce many times more pain for your lord.
Therefore, at such a time, since you know the conduct proper to a servant,
you should adopt only behavior that accords with your master's mind."
He replied, "If concern for a son truly oppresses him,
then this very <s>Piṅgalikā</s> should propitiate Your Majesty."

children.text: athedaṃ nīyakair uktaṃ yuktaṃ śrutvā mahībhujā
children.translated_text: Then the king, hearing this statement of the attendants and judging it proper, said,

children.text: yāsau piṅgalikā sā naḥ putriṇī kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let that <s>Piṅgalikā</s>, who has sons, be described to us."
Immediately, approaching with cries of victory preceding her,

children.text: putravān bhava deveti brāhmaṇī tam avardhayat ||
children.translated_text: the Brahmin woman blessed him, saying, "May you have a son, Your Majesty!"
Having saluted her, the king then asked that noble woman...

children.text: āgamyate kutaḥ ke vā tavāmī bālakā iti ||
children.translated_text: 'From where do you come, and who are these boys of yours?'
'From the house of <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, O king, I have come,

children.text: bālakāś ca sutā ete mameti kathitaṃ tayā ||
children.translated_text: and these boys are my sons'; so she told him.

children.text: atha tām abravīd rājā citram etat tvayoditam
children.translated_text: Then the king said to her, 'This that you have said is astonishing.

children.text: na hi bhartrā na ca sutair bhavitavyaṃ tavedṛśaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For neither a husband nor sons of such a kind ought to be yours.
You are wholly darkened by marks that destroy husbands,
like the house-wall of a woman whose beloved has long been away.

children.text: na ca patyā vinā putrair bhavitavyaṃ yataḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: And since women cannot have sons without a husband,

children.text: tasmād idaṃ mahac citraṃ sphuṭaṃ naḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: this is therefore a great marvel. Tell it to us plainly.'

children.text: athāvocad asau deva yathāttha na tad anyathā
children.translated_text: Then she said, 'Your Majesty, it is not otherwise than you have said.

children.text: mahatī tu kathā śrotum icchā cec chrūyatām iyam ||
children.translated_text: But the story is a long one; if you wish to hear it, let it be heard.
In <s>Avanti</s> there is a settlement of Brahmins called <s>Kapiṣṭhala</s>,
