its boundary marked by piled fire-altars, rich in wheat and herds of cattle.
There lived a Brahmin, <s>Somadatta</s>, whose wealth was the three Vedas,
and the earth was filled with his pupils, knowers of the Veda.
His virtuous wife was <s>Vāsiṣṭhī</s>, wife of that man who was like <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>;
by her good conduct she put even <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s wife to shame.

children.text: tasya tasyām aputrasya kāle mahati gacchati
children.translated_text: As a long time passed for him without a son, by her
a daughter was born, like a meteor at twilight, ill-favored to the eyes.
But <s>Somadatta</s>, seeing her and being skilled in the marks of women,
declared that she would be bereft of husband, sons, and wealth.
And because calamities were very strong, before long the unlucky girl
grew tall and harsh, like the high flame of a comet.
Snatching alms from the pupils, with shame worn away by hunger,
she would eat it in their presence without even washing her hands.
Because of her ill fortune, ugliness, and quarrelsome nature,

children.text: na kaścid varayāmāsa varaḥ prāptavarām api ||
children.translated_text: no suitor sought her, though she had reached the age for obtaining a husband.

children.text: na ca tāṃ somadatto 'pi kasmaicid aśubhām adāt
children.translated_text: Nor did <s>Somadatta</s> give that inauspicious girl to anyone,

children.text: mā sma yujyata duḥkhena prāpyaināṃ ninditām iti ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'Let no man, having obtained this censured girl, be joined with misery.'
She too was burned by the powerful bodily-born passion, whose force consumes everything,
like a little heap of refuse by a village fire.

children.text: kadācit kaścid āgatya vācāṭo baṭur uccakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Once a certain talkative young student came and, speaking loudly,
with danger hanging over his head, addressed <s>Somadatta</s>:
'The teacher's daughter, angry at me though I am innocent,
strikes me with bricks and clods; therefore let her be restrained.'

children.text: somadattas tataḥ kruddhaḥ sutāṃ caṇḍam abhartsayat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Somadatta</s>, enraged, fiercely rebuked his daughter:

children.text: ulke piśācike gaccha śīghraṃ mama gṛhād iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Meteor! Demoness! Go quickly from my house.'

children.text: sā tu tat paruṣaṃ śrutvā manasvijanaduḥśravam
children.translated_text: But hearing that harsh speech, unbearable for a proud person,
and because she could not endure the torment of Love, she set her mind on death.
Then, going to the forest in search of a means of dying,
she saw, in a certain place, a temple of the Slayer of the Daityas.
Near it was a lake, noisy with crying ospreys and cranes,
its bank to be inferred from rows of humming bees.

children.text: āsīccāsyā mayā tāvan martavyam iti niścitam
children.translated_text: And she thought, 'It is settled that I must die;
but there is doubt about the means. Here this means is best.
Worshipping the god <s>Mādhava</s> with lotuses, blue lotuses, and the like,
and wasting away on a diet of lotus parts, I shall abandon life.
Having gained merit, when dead I shall go to heaven without trouble,
and I shall not go to hell, crowded with those dead by a woman's death.'
Having resolved this, she acted attentively according to her intention,

children.text: rātrau ca baddhaparyaṅkā devaṃ mādhavam asmarat ||
children.translated_text: and at night, sitting cross-legged, she remembered the god <s>Mādhava</s>.
When only a month had passed, at the end of a dream she saw <s>Madhusūdana</s>,
joyfully saying, 'Choose a boon, daughter.'
Then she, bowed down and with folded hands, petitioned the god:

children.text: maraṇaṃ me jagannātha prasādaḥ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Lord of the world, let death be granted to me as your favor.'

children.text: devas tām avadan nedaṃ devatārādhanāt phalam
children.translated_text: The god said to her, 'This is not the fruit of propitiating a deity.
That is the result of killing living beings, and suicide is condemned.
Therefore name another boon, greater than husband, sons, and wealth,

children.text: yena hīnāsi vairāgyān niryātā svagṛhād iti ||
children.translated_text: for lack of which you left your own home in despondency.'
She said, 'A husband and the rest are obtained by women who have done merit;

children.text: ahaṃ tv ācaritāpuṇyā duḥkhair eva vibhāvitā ||
children.translated_text: but I, having done no merit, have been made manifest only by sufferings.
Therefore enough of fruitless thought about husband, sons, and the like.

children.text: mṛtyunā śāntim icchāmi sā me saṃpādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: I desire peace through death; let that be accomplished for me.'

children.text: so 'bravīt satyam evedaṃ kiṃtu janmāntare tvayā
children.translated_text: He said, 'This is indeed true. But in a former birth
an āḍhaka measure of barley was given by you, in your father's house, to a Brahmin.

children.text: sa ca jātaś caturvedaḥ svapuṇyair iha janmani
children.translated_text: He, through his own merits, has been born in this life as one who knows the four Vedas,

children.text: surūpaḥ sādhuvṛttaś ca sa te bhartā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: handsome and virtuous, and he will be your husband.

children.text: sa ca tvām urvaśīrūpām eko drakṣyati nāparaḥ
children.translated_text: He alone, and no one else, will see you as having the beauty of <s>Urvaśī</s>,

children.text: krīto yavāḍhakena tvam iti yāvan na vakṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: so long as you do not say, "I was bought for an āḍhaka of barley."

children.text: janmāntare ca pūrvasmin bhakṣayantyās tilās tava
children.translated_text: And in a previous former birth, while you were eating sesame seeds,
eight fell into the fire from your handful, through your loosely spread fingers.

children.text: te te putrā bhaviṣyanti putri candranibhānanāḥ
children.translated_text: Those will become your sons, daughter, with faces like the moon.

children.text: maraṇād dāruṇāt tena cittam āvartyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore turn your mind away from this terrible death.'

children.text: ity uktvāntarhite deve pratibuddhā dadarśa sā
children.translated_text: When the god had spoken thus and disappeared, she awoke and saw
her father, come with his group of pupils, searching for her.
Her father, full of pity for her, emaciated by ascetic practice, caused her to break her fast,

children.text: śrāmyantīm anayad gehaṃ viśrāmyantīṃ tarau tarau ||
children.translated_text: and led her home as she grew weary and rested at every tree.

children.text: yā sā piṅgalikā deva devam ārādhya keśavam
children.translated_text: That <s>Piṅgalikā</s>, O king, having propitiated lord <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: varaṃ labdhavatī tasmāt tāṃ mām eva nibodha tām ||
children.translated_text: received a boon from him; therefore understand that she is I myself.
Once, however, a man versed in the four Vedas, together with his pupils, by chance

children.text: gṛham asmākam āyātaḥ kṛtātithyo dadarśa mām ||
children.translated_text: came to our house; after being treated as a guest, he saw me.

children.text: mama tātaṃ tu so 'pṛcchad brahman kasyeyam ātmajā
children.translated_text: He asked my father, 'Brahmin, whose daughter is this,
whose beauty puts moonlight to shame? If it is proper, tell me.'

children.text: mameti kathite pitrā māṃ prārthayata sa dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: When my father said, 'She is mine,' that twice-born man asked for me,

children.text: pitrā dattaṃ ca vidhivan muditaḥ pariṇītavān ||
children.translated_text: and, when I had been given by my father according to rule, he joyfully married me.

children.text: tataś cārabhya divasāt sa siddha iva kiṃkaraḥ
children.translated_text: From that day onward, like an accomplished servant,

children.text: na kāṃcin na karoti sma mamājñāṃ ninditām api ||
children.translated_text: he failed to carry out no command of mine, even one worthy of blame.

children.text: amī cāṣṭau sutās tasmād acireṇaiva durlabhāḥ
children.translated_text: And these eight sons, hard to obtain, were soon

children.text: labdhā mayā sutā ye 'sya prasādāl lokadhāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: obtained by me from him, sons gained by the favor of this sustainer of the world.

children.text: iti kāle gate bhartā māṃ kadācid abhāṣata
children.translated_text: When some time had passed, my husband once said to me,

children.text: pṛṣṭhaṃ duḥkhāyamānaṃ me caṇḍi saṃvāhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'My back is hurting, fierce one; please massage it.'
Then I said to him, who had uttered words he had never spoken before,

children.text: kim ahaṃ bhavatā krītā pṛṣṭhasaṃvāhiketi tam ||
children.translated_text: 'Have I been bought by you as a back-massaging servant-woman?'

children.text: so 'bravīn nīcakais trāsād aṅguṣṭhāgreṇa gāṃ likhan
children.translated_text: He said softly, out of fear, tracing the ground with the tip of his big toe,

children.text: ahaṃ vā kiṃ tvayā krīto yena preṣyatvam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Or have I been bought by you, that I have come to the condition of a servant?'
Then, forgetting our agreement and tainted by anger,
I said the unpleasant words, 'You were bought by me for an āḍhaka of barley.'

children.text: asāv api ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā sahajākāravañcitām
children.translated_text: And he too, seeing that I had been betrayed by my natural form,
drew away from my nearness in alarm and said this:

children.text: api kāsi kutaś cāsi kenāsi vikṛtā kṛtā
children.translated_text: 'Who are you? From where have you come? By whom have you been made altered?

children.text: kaccit piṅgalikā nāsi kaś ca nāma yavāḍhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely you are not <s>Piṅgalikā</s>? And what is this āḍhaka of barley?'
Questioned by him in this way, I described what had happened.

children.text: so 'pi saṃjātanirvedo na jāte kva palāyitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He too, seized by revulsion, fled somewhere unknown.

children.text: tasmin deśāntaraṃ yāte tāte ca tridaśālayam
children.translated_text: When he had gone to another country and my father to the abode of the gods,
I, bereft of father and husband, came to this country.
Because of affection for my own homeland, queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s>
has shown favor to me and my sons with food, clothing, and protection.

children.text: tena devena yat pṛṣṭaṃ kutas te bālakā iti
children.translated_text: Therefore, when Your Majesty asked, 'Where are your boys from?',

children.text: evam ete mayā labdhās tuṣṭān nārāyaṇād iti ||
children.translated_text: I said, 'In this way they were obtained by me from a pleased <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.'

children.text: iti hṛṣṭamatir niśāmya tasyāś caritaṃ putrasamūhalābhahetum
children.translated_text: Having heard her story, the cause of her gaining a group of sons, with delighted mind,

children.text: sacivaiḥ sahitaś cakāra rājā sutasaṃprāptiphalaṃ kriyāvicāram ||
children.translated_text: the king, together with his ministers, considered a rite whose fruit would be the attainment of a son.
Then, after dismissing the court, the king said to his ministers,

children.text: yad bravīmi nibodhantu bhavantas tat sacetasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Let your honors listen attentively to what I say.

children.text: ṛṇaiḥ kila samāghrātaḥ puruṣo jāyate tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: A man, it is said, is touched by three debts:
to the seers, the gods, and the eaters of ancestral offerings, through studentship, sacrifice, and offspring.
Of these, I have learned the Veda and performed all the great sacrifices,
but, because I am sonless, I am held by the ancestors who feed on piṇḍa offerings.
And there is no higher cause of happiness than the touch of a son's limbs;

children.text: sukhibhiḥ sa hi nirdiṣṭaś candanād api śītalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by happy men it has been declared cooler even than sandalwood.
Enough of excessive elaboration. For householders, in every way,
there is no cause other than a son for attaining happiness seen and unseen.

children.text: tad asti yadi vaḥ kāṅkṣā niṣprajānāṃ prajāṃ prati
children.translated_text: Therefore, if you have any concern for offspring for the childless,
then undertake with me the worship of the deity.'

children.text: te tu sapramadāḥ śrutvā rājñaḥ putrārthinaḥ kathām
children.translated_text: Hearing the speech of the king who longed for a son, they, together with their wives,
their own intentions as good as fulfilled, replied with smiles showing:
'The birth of a son to the merchant's wife, the sight of the painting on the journey,
and the sight of <s>Piṅgalī</s>: this stratagem was undertaken by us.

children.text: asmābhiḥ sa ca devena tathaiva saphalīkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And that very stratagem has been brought to fruition by Your Majesty;

children.text: kṛtaḥ kāle prayogo hi nāphalo jātu jāyate ||
children.translated_text: for a rite performed at the proper time never becomes fruitless.
Therefore begin an observance corresponding to your resolve.'
Thus permitted by his ministers, he accepted it, saying, 'So be it.'
On an auspicious day, after worshipping the deities, the fire, and the twice-born,
he went to the <s>Nāgavana</s> garden with his wife and his ministers.
But <s>Māgadhī</s>, whose zeal had been aroused by queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s>,
was restrained with the words, 'Enough, friend, of this hardship for you.'
And she was told, 'You are still young, soft as a lotus-fiber thread,

children.text: anubhūtasukhā cāsi bhrātur bhartuś ca veśmani ||
children.translated_text: and you have experienced happiness in the houses of your brother and your husband.
But I, of wretched fortune, have endured
unbearable sufferings; therefore I am able to attend upon suffering.

children.text: yaś ca me bhavitā putraḥ sa bhavatyā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And the son who will be mine will be yours,
just as <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>, born from the womb of the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, belonged to <s>Bhavānī</s>.'
When she had turned back in this way with <s>Vāsavadattā</s>,
the king soon satisfied the king of kings through austerities.
But one day the royal couple awoke in great agitation,
crying to one another, 'Ah, queen!' and 'Ah, noble lord!'
Then, after sipping water and bowing to the lord of wealth,
the king respectfully recounted his dream before the priests and the others.

children.text: adya paśyāmy ahaṃ svapne vyomni kāmapi devatām
children.translated_text: 'Today in a dream I saw some goddess in the sky,
whose continuous flood of radiance had scattered the blueness of the vault of heaven.
She spoke to me in a voice deep and gentle:

children.text: tvām āhvayati vitteśas tadāśāṃ gamyatām ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The lord of wealth summons you; therefore go to his quarter."
When I assented, saying, "Om," she placed her hand, redder than twilight,
and set out through the sky toward the direction guarded by the lord of wealth.
Here <s>Gaṅgā</s> was borne by <s>Śarva</s>; here <s>Pārvatī</s> was married.'
showing us such places in the region of <s>Pārvatī</s>'s father.
As I was being led in this way, stage by stage, I then saw before me
the city of <s>Alakā</s>, whose ramparts were built of moonstone.
It was joined with countless hosts of the attendants of <s>Pārvatī</s>'s husband,
and outside it there was an incomparable grove of wish-granting trees.
Even the mansions there, whose peaks were mottled by webs of radiance from many jewels,
were made white by the moonlight from <s>Rudra</s>'s moon.
Having brought me down at the door of the palace of the lord of the <s>Guhyakas</s>,

children.text: vadati kṣaṇam atraiva sthīyatām iti devatā ||
children.translated_text: the goddess said, "Stay right here for a moment."

children.text: sā praviśya pratīhāryā saha nirgamya bhāṣate
children.translated_text: She entered, and then came out together with the door-keeper and said,
"The god has granted you entrance; come in."
Passing through six chambers like the mansions of the gods,
in the seventh inner court, rich with extraordinary splendor, I saw the lord of wealth.

children.text: atha tatrāpsarāḥ kācit kāṃcid āha nirīkṣya mām
children.translated_text: Then one <s>apsaras</s> there, looking at me, said to another,

children.text: sakhi nūnam asāv eṣa yasyāsau bhavitā sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Friend, surely this is the man whose son that one is to become.
I heard it in front of the sages while they were consulting together:

children.text: bharatānām ayaṃ vaṃśe viśuddhe jāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'May this one be born in the pure lineage of the <s>Bharatas</s>.'

children.text: na caiṣa kevalaṃ dhanyas tena putreṇa pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: And this king is not fortunate merely because of that son;
that son too will be a worthy object of noble praise.

children.text: tena tattādṛśaṃ putraṃ labhatām eṣa bhūpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore may this king obtain such a son as that,
and may that son have parents whose conduct is like that of <s>Śacī</s> and <s>Śakra</s>."
Because I was intent on the weighty business, I treated the heavenly women as straw;
with his attendant host present, I bowed low and saluted the lord of wealth.
But, observing human courtesy, he raised an arm thick as the lord of serpents
and said, "King among men, welcome. Be seated."
When a golden seat had been set for me near his jewel-like feet,

children.text: vyavadhāya tu mām āste devī nīcaistarāsanā ||
children.translated_text: the goddess sat apart from me on a lower seat.
Lutes sounded, struck by <s>Nārada</s> and others,
and the sound of drums was heard, accompanied by many kinds of hand movements.
<s>Urvaśī</s>, <s>Menakā</s>, <s>Rambhā</s>, <s>Citralekhā</s>, and <s>Kratusthalā</s>,
singing and beating time with their soles, made <s>Tilottamā</s> dance.
While events of this kind were taking place, prince <s>Nalakūbara</s>,
the son of the king of kings, came playing with boys.
He dragged a little toy cart made from a compact mass

children.text: krīḍāśakaṭikāṃ karṣann itaś cetaś ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: of great jewels whose essence was <s>Meru</s>, going here and there.
Then, when its wheel stumbled in a heap of flowers,
a jewel sprang out and fell onto a floor paved with powdered beryl.
Then <s>Kubera</s>, stretching out his hand, asked <s>Nalakūbara</s> for that jewel,

children.text: mahyam etad dadasveti tad ratnam udayācata ||
children.translated_text: saying, "Give that to me."
Placed by the prince in the palm of the king of kings,
the jewel shone like a bandhūka blossom set in the heart of a lotus.
It was a ruby surrounded by twenty-six pearls free of bad marks,
eight-cornered and full of dense radiance.

children.text: vittādhipatinā mahyaṃ dattaṃ devyai ca tan mayā
children.translated_text: The lord of wealth gave it to me, and I gave it to the queen;
she too, with flashing joy, placed it between her breasts.
Then it became a lion cub, its tail and mane quivering,

children.text: vidārya dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣim etasyāḥ praviśaty asau ||
children.translated_text: and, tearing open her right side, it entered her.

children.text: tadavasthām imāṃ dṛṣṭvā hā devīti vadann aham
children.translated_text: Seeing her in that condition, I cried, "Ah, queen!"

children.text: pratibuddha iti svapnam ācaṣṭe sma narādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and awoke. Thus the king related his dream.
Then <s>Ādityaśarman</s>, a Brahmin who knew the science of the stars and whose predictions came true,
joyfully explained the fruit of the dream.
"Great king, conquer the mass of your enemies by means of your son,
as one conquers stronger foes, passion and the rest, by powerful concentration.
Your son will be lord over the hosts of <s>Vidyādharas</s>,
with the moon and sun covered by dense masses of aerial palaces.

children.text: yās tā muktāparīvārās tasya ṣaḍviṃśati maṇeḥ
children.translated_text: Those twenty-six pearls that formed the retinue of the jewel:

children.text: mahākulā bhaviṣyanti bhāryās tava sutasya tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they will become the high-born wives of your son.

children.text: ye cāṣṭāv aśrayo ratnaṃ parito lakṣitās tvayā
children.translated_text: And the eight corners that you saw marked all around the jewel,

children.text: vidyās tā viddhi putrasya bhaviṣyantī bhaviṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: know those to be the sciences that your future son will possess."

children.text: evaṃ ca sthāpite svapne rājakīye dvijanmanā
children.translated_text: When the royal dream had thus been interpreted by the Brahmin,
queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s> there told her own dream.

children.text: āryaputreṇa yo dṛṣṭaḥ sa eva sakalo mayā
children.translated_text: "The very dream that the noble prince saw was seen in full by me as well,
and when my side was being torn open, I said, 'Ah, noble prince!'"
Hearing that the two dreams were alike,
<s>Ādityaśarman</s>'s certainty about his knowledge of the future became firm.
Then <s>Rumaṇvān</s> informed the lord of the earth,

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ svapno mayā yaḥ sa śravaṇenānugṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: "May the dream that I saw be favored with your hearing.
When Your Majesty had undertaken a vow,
all the inhabitants of <s>Cedi</s> and <s>Vatsa</s> were under vows for Your Majesty's obtaining offspring.
There, today, in a dream I saw the one who rides <s>Garuḍa</s>,

children.text: mārgitaś ca mayā dehi svāmine naḥ prajā iti ||
children.translated_text: and I asked him, 'Give progeny to our lord.'

children.text: sa vihasyoktavān pūrṇaḥ svāminas te manorathaḥ
children.translated_text: He laughed and said, 'Your lord's desire has been fulfilled;
I shall fulfill yours too,' and gave me an arrow.

children.text: sapraṇāmaṃ tam ādāya hṛdaye nidadhāmi ca
children.translated_text: Taking it with reverence, I placed it on my heart,
and as I awoke I saw this untimely moonlight."
This dream too was interpreted by the pleased <s>Ādityaśarman</s>:

children.text: yādṛśo 'sya suto bhavī tādṛśaḥ śrūyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Hear what kind of son this man will have.

children.text: sāyako hi guṇenārthī tasmād asya bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: For an arrow has need of a string;

children.text: putraḥ ṣāḍguṇyatattvajño yuktaś cāyaṃ guṇair guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore his son will know the true principles of the six royal policies and will be endowed with virtues."
For an arrow has its movement and stopping-place dependent on another, and it travels through the sky;
therefore the king's son's messenger will be a sky-roaming being.
Then <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s> told his own dream:
"Today the forty-nine <s>Maruts</s> came into my sight.
One of them, flashing with brightness and having the splendor of a swarm of fireflies,

children.text: svaṃ vimucya mudā mahyaṃ saṃnāhaṃ dattavān iti ||
children.translated_text: joyfully took off his own armor and gave it to me."
The Brahmin confirmed the dream thus: "A son, heroic and resolute, like his lord's armor,

children.text: bhavato bhavitety evaṃ svapnam āsthāpayad dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will be born to you." In this way the Brahmin established the dream.
It was then told by <s>Ṛṣabha</s>: "I saw a herd of cattle,

children.text: bravīti tatra mām ekā praviśemāṃ guhām iti ||
children.translated_text: and there one of them said to me, 'Enter this cave.'

children.text: tatra praviśatā dṛṣṭāś catuḥṣaṣṭir mayā kalāḥ
children.translated_text: As I entered there, I saw the sixty-four arts,
and the four great sciences arranged in a painting.
There, while I was being painted and looking at picture after picture,

children.text: bodhito jṛmbhaṇair mandrair bherīṇāṃ garjitair iti ||
children.translated_text: I was awakened by the deep yawning sounds, the roars, of drums."

children.text: sthāpito 'yam iti svapnaḥ putras tava bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: This dream was interpreted: "A son will be born to you,
intelligent and skilled in all the arts set out in the whole painting."

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ vasantakenāpi svapnaṃ kathitam ity atha
children.translated_text: Then a dream seen by <s>Vasantaka</s> too was told:
"Fire gave me a beautiful earring, shining brightly."
While the dreams were being interpreted, the darkness, broken by the radiances of the Sun's charioteer,
became red like the eyes of cakora birds.
In the ponds, awakened by the touch of lotuses tossed by a gentle wind,
the birds cried out with quarrelsome calls.
The loud sound of the temple drums swelled up,
frightening <s>Indra</s>'s inner apartments with its deep reverberation.
And groups of bards said to the king,
"O fulfiller of crowds of petitioners, may your own hope be fulfilled."

children.text: yuvā dhīraḥ sabhe yogyo yajamānasya jāyatām
children.translated_text: "May a young, steadfast son, fit for the assembly, be born to the sacrificer";
with such mantras and music the Brahmins blessed him.
By such signs and forms, which indicated success in the undertaking,
<s>Ādityaśarman</s>'s body became rough with horripilation.

children.text: padmāvatyā tato harṣād vivāha iva nṛtyati
children.translated_text: Then, from joy, as though at <s>Padmāvatī</s>'s wedding,
the company of courtesans danced while <s>Vasantaka</s> beat the sounding time.
But enough of excessive detail; let it be understood in brief:
even the fathers-in-law, surrounded by groups of brides, danced.
Because they were overcome by excessive joy, the <s>Gandharvas</s>,
forgetting the run of the notes, struck their parivādinī lutes with loosened strings.
While this and similar events were taking place at the beginning, the king,
having performed the consecration and other rites, honored the gods and Brahmins.
Then, entering while he was praised by groups of Brahmin bards,
he honored the citizens and the inner palace with gifts and other favors.
After a period measuring two months had passed,
he spread throughout the earth the news that the queen had conceived.

children.text: yena yena śrutā vārttā śabareṇa śukena vā
children.translated_text: By whomever that news was heard, whether by a <s>Śabara</s> or a parrot,

children.text: giriṣṭhaḥ pañjarastho vā mugdhas tatraiva tatra saḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether mountain-dwelling or cage-dwelling, each simple creature was spellbound on the spot.
Women skilled in childbirth, physicians for children and the like,
and others who knew the rites of pregnancy constantly attended her.
Seeing her face, its cheeks pale like fading madhūka blossoms and its eyes askance,

children.text: śvaśrūs tasyā mukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā bubudhe dohadavyathām ||
children.translated_text: her mother-in-law understood the pain of a dohada, a pregnancy craving.

children.text: pṛcchati sma ca tāṃ putri śīghram ācakṣva dohadam
children.translated_text: And she asked her, "Daughter, quickly tell me your dohada.

children.text: anākhyāte hi garbhasya vaiphalyam api dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: For when it is not told, even failure of the pregnancy is sometimes seen."
When, out of shame, she did not tell the craving,

children.text: tadā svavṛttaṃ sā vadhvai vyāhartum upacakrame ||
children.translated_text: then the mother-in-law began to relate her own story to the bride.

children.text: antarvatnīm apṛcchan mām ekadā śvaśuras tava
children.translated_text: "Once, when I was pregnant, your father-in-law asked me,

children.text: bādhate dohado yas tvāṃ sa kṣipraṃ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'The dohada that troubles you: let it be told quickly.'
Though I was affectionate toward him, because of even greater shame,
after he had asked many times I told it through the mouth of a friend.

children.text: iyaṃ māṃ bādhate śraddhā sāśu saṃpādyatām iti
children.translated_text: 'This longing troubles me; let it be fulfilled quickly.'
And that was accomplished by the ministers at <s>Śatānīka</s>'s command.
Wearing unguents, garments, ornaments, and garlands
red like the disk of the young sun, we wandered through the reddened city.
With red parasols and fans, with vehicles covered in red blankets,
and with surrounding groups like a grove of red aśokas,
then, mounting <s>Suyamuna</s>, red like a ruby mountain,

children.text: digdāhād iva raktānām apaśyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ diśām ||
children.translated_text: I saw the circle of the directions red, as if from the burning of the quarters.
Then, watched by people startled and confused by the wind of his wings,
a bird approached, like the eldest son of <s>Garuḍa</s>.

children.text: sarasāmiṣagṛddhaś ca mugdhām ādāya mām asau
children.translated_text: Greedy for fresh flesh, that creature took me, helpless,
and swiftly went into the sky while <s>Śatānīka</s> watched.

children.text: tataḥ pradeśe kasmiṃścid avatāritavān sa mām
children.translated_text: Then he set me down in some place, intending to eat me;

children.text: bhakṣayiṣyan niṣiddhaś ca kenāpy ākāśam āśrayat ||
children.translated_text: but, stopped by someone, he resorted to the sky.

children.text: paśyāmi sma ca tatra dvau kṛśāv ṛṣikumārakau
children.translated_text: There I saw two emaciated young ascetics,
their bodies tawny from contact with halos, their matted hair blazing.

children.text: tau mām avocatāṃ devi mā bhaiṣīr ayam āśramaḥ
children.translated_text: The two said to me, 'Queen, do not be afraid. This is the hermitage
of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, situated on the sacred slope of <s>Udayādri</s>.

children.text: āgaccha nanu pāvas tvāṃ tatrety ukte gatā satī
children.translated_text: Come now; the holy one is summoning you there.' When this was said, I went,
and I saw the eldest of the world, surrounded by the foremost ascetics.

children.text: vanditaś ca mayā dūrād āśiṣā mām avardhayat
children.translated_text: When I had saluted him from afar, he strengthened me with a blessing:
'Daughter, may you give birth to a son, an unfailing vessel of fame.'"

children.text: na cotkaṇṭhā tvayā kāryā svajane matsanāthayā
children.translated_text: And you should not feel longing, since you are protected by me among your own people.
For the settlement of those born in the line of <s>Āditya</s> is your final refuge.

children.text: iti viśvāsya māṃ vākyair madhurair evamādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Having reassured me with sweet words such as these,

children.text: āvāsaḥ kriyatāṃ vadhvā iti śiṣyān samādiśat ||
children.translated_text: he instructed his disciples, 'Let a dwelling be made for the bride.'
Quickly they made a dwelling of stone, timber, and bamboo,
surrounded by a ditch and a fence, and reported it to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
Thus made secure, I, an ascetic woman, lived there happily
while the rites for pregnancy were performed by the seers.

children.text: prasūtā cāsmi daśame māse putraṃ patiṃ tava
children.translated_text: And in the tenth month I bore a son, your husband,
whose prosperity was indicated by favorable planets beginning with the sun.
Then the preceptor of the <s>Sūrya</s> lineage himself performed the birth rite

children.text: divase dvādaśe nāma putrasya kṛtavān mama ||
children.translated_text: and on the twelfth day gave a name to my son.
'Since this boy has been well born on <s>Udaya</s> mountain,

children.text: tasmād udayano nāma prasiddhim upayātv iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore let him become famous under the name <s>Udayana</s>.'

children.text: vede gandharvavede ca sakalāsu kalāsu ca
children.translated_text: His understanding was trained in the Veda, in the <s>Gandharvaveda</s>,
in all the arts, and in the sciences, weapons, and martial treatises.
As the days passed in this way, he was restrained by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>:

children.text: mā kadācid bhavān asmād dūraṃ gā āśramād iti ||
children.translated_text: 'You must never go far from this hermitage.'
But because the kṣatra (warrior) class is harsh by nature, from the ascetic grove
he went out and amused himself with hunting in the forest.
One day, resplendent with divine garlands, sandal paste, and the like,
he fearfully bowed to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, who showed a smile.

children.text: vasiṣṭhaḥ pṛṣṭavān enam api dṛṣṭāḥ kumārakāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> asked him, 'Were the boys seen by you,
the sons of the bhogins (serpents), playing in the lotus pond?'

children.text: āma dṛṣṭā iti prokte sutena mama nīcakaiḥ
children.translated_text: When my son softly replied, 'Yes, they were seen,'
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said to him, 'Tell it in detail.'
When questioned, <s>Udayana</s> said: 'I was commanded by you,

children.text: na gantavyaṃ tvayā dūram etasmād āśramād iti ||
children.translated_text: "You must not go far from this hermitage."

children.text: ārabhya ca tataḥ kālāt kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ guruḥ
children.translated_text: From that time onward I was full of curiosity, wondering,
"For what reason does the guru keep restraining me?"
So, without considering the fault that would arise from breaking the guru's command,

children.text: dūram adyāśramād asmād gacchāmi diśam uttarām ||
children.translated_text: today I went far from this hermitage toward the northern quarter.
There I saw a lotus pond filled with various lotuses and waterbirds,
its river-water agitated by the jostling of wild elephants.
In it I saw boys of superhuman form,
with lovely reddish eyes, emerging, submerging, and swimming.

children.text: te māṃ taṭastham ālokya puñjībhūya sasaṃbhramāḥ
children.translated_text: When they saw me standing on the bank, they gathered together in alarm
and, with long sweeps of their long arms, took refuge in deep water.

children.text: ahaṃ tān uktavān asmi mā palāyadhvam āsyatām
children.translated_text: I said to them, 'Do not flee; stay here.

children.text: nanv ahaṃ bhavato draṣṭum āśramād ṛṣir āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely I am a seer come from the hermitage to see you.'

children.text: iti madvacanaṃ śrutvā teṣām ekena bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Hearing my words, one of them said,

children.text: kiṃ te 'smābhir mahāsattva bhāṣitair gamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'What use is speaking with us to you, great being? Go away.'

children.text: satyasatyaṃ na yakṣo 'smi na piśāco na rākṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Truth, truth: I am not a yakṣa, nor a piśāca, nor a rākṣasa;

children.text: tena mā bhaiṣṭa ḍhaukadhvam iti tān aham uktavān ||
children.translated_text: therefore do not be afraid; come near,' I said to them.

children.text: tais tu saṃjātaviśrambhaiḥ saṃharan vā muhūrtakam
children.translated_text: Then, when they had come to trust me, they invited me for a moment:

children.text: āgaccha prārthito mitra gṛhaṃ no gamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Come, friend, please; let us go to our house.'
When, in compliance with them, I promised, 'I will go,'

children.text: mām ādāya nimagnās te tasyaiva saraso 'mbhasi ||
children.translated_text: they took me and sank into the water of that very lake.
Then into a city where no moon, sun, planets, constellations, or stars had risen,
where masses of darkness were destroyed by the radiance of moon-, sun-, and jewel-lamps,
free of people old, sick, joyless, or deformed,
resounding with the sounds of instruments swelling within rows of lovely mansions,

children.text: aśeṣair viyutaṃ doṣair aśeṣaiḥ saṃyutaṃ guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: devoid of all faults and endowed with all virtues,
I was led by the delighted boys into that capital.

children.text: teṣām ekas tu mām āha bhogināṃ bhoginām iyam
children.translated_text: One of them said to me, 'This is the pleasurable city of the bhogins (serpents),
the abode called <s>Bhogavatī</s> of those whose lives last a kalpa.
I am the son of <s>Kambala</s>, and this one is the son of <s>Aśvatara</s>,
and the others are sons of other bearers of nāga hosts.'

children.text: tataḥ kambalaputreṇa nītvāhaṃ svaṃ gṛhaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Then I was led by <s>Kambala</s>'s son to his great house,
received honors such as arghya, and was made to wear adornment like this.

children.text: itare netum aicchanta svagṛhān māṃ mayoditāḥ
children.translated_text: The others wished to lead me to their own houses, but I said,

children.text: anujānīta mām adya suhṛdo mā sma kupyata ||
children.translated_text: 'Allow me to go today, friends; do not be angry.
Forbidden by my guru, I have come to this land,

children.text: bhītaś ca kupitāt tasmāt tasmān nayata mām iti ||
children.translated_text: and I am afraid of him when he is angry; therefore lead me back.'

children.text: te tu mām āhur uttiṣṭha gamyatāṃ svam idaṃ puram
children.translated_text: But they said to me, 'Rise; go back to your own city.
When you come again, you must keep the serpent folk free from longing.

children.text: tasyām eva ca ramyatvāt krīḍāmaḥ saṃtataṃ vayam
children.translated_text: Because of its beauty we play constantly in that very lotus pond;

children.text: suhṛdo 'pi yadīcchā syād gacchet tāṃ nalinīm iti ||
children.translated_text: if our friend wishes, he may go to that pond.'

children.text: ity uktvā mama tair vaktre paṭāntenāvaguṇṭhite
children.translated_text: Having said this, when they covered my face with the end of a cloth,

children.text: uttīrṇam aham ātmānaṃ paśyāmi sarasas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I saw myself risen up from the lake.

children.text: iti bhogavatīṃ dṛṣṭvā so 'ham āyāmi saṃprati
children.translated_text: Having thus seen <s>Bhogavatī</s>, I have now returned,

children.text: mamāsminn aparādhe ca pramāṇaṃ bhagavān iti ||
children.translated_text: and in this offense Your Reverence is the authority.'

children.text: vasiṣṭhas tam athāvocad upāyo 'yaṃ mayā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said to him, 'This was a means devised by me,
by which those nāga boys came within your sight.

children.text: idānīm api taiḥ sārdhaṃ gatvā bhogavatīṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Even now you should go with them to <s>Bhogavatī</s>
and learn in detail gāndharva (music) and the science of elephants.

children.text: yadi ca grāhayet kiṃcit tvāṃ nāgādhipatis tataḥ
children.translated_text: And if the nāga lord should teach you anything further, then
The lute <s>Ghoṣavatī</s>, together with the <s>nāga</s> modes, is to be learned by you.

children.text: aṅkam āropitāyāṃ ca tantryo yasyām anāhatāḥ
children.translated_text: And when it is placed upon the lap, its strings, unstruck,

children.text: madhuraṃ nisvaneyus tāṃ vidyāṃ ghoṣavatīm iti ||
children.translated_text: sound sweetly; know that art as <s>Ghoṣavatī</s>.

children.text: guror udayanaḥ śrutvā nāgalokaṃ gatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this from his teacher, <s>Udayana</s> then went to the <s>Nāga</s> world,
and after a very long time had passed, he returned with the lute in his hand.
Having made obeisance, and embraced by his teacher with tears,
he cooled with his limbs his mother's body, which had been scorched by the fire of separation from him.

children.text: ekadā tu sukhāsīno vasiṣṭhas tam abhāṣata
children.translated_text: But once, while he was sitting at ease, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said to him,
'Let us hear music produced by the sound of <s>Ghoṣavatī</s>.'

children.text: tannideśāc ca patyau te pragīte saha vīṇayā
children.translated_text: At his command, when your husband sang together with the lute,
even the wind, the teacher of the world's motion, did not stir.
Seeing the hermitage motionless, with its lions and elephants silent,

children.text: raktāṃ ghoṣavatīṃ muktvā tūṣṇīm āsīt patis tava ||
children.translated_text: your husband set down the beloved <s>Ghoṣavatī</s> and sat in silence.

children.text: uktaś caiṣa vasiṣṭhena na tvayāsmiṃs tapovane
children.translated_text: And he was told by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, 'In this grove of austerities

children.text: vādanīyā punar vīṇā geyaṃ vā śanakair api ||
children.translated_text: the lute must not be played by you again, nor may singing be done, even softly.
Other sounds too generally disturb those whose minds are collected

children.text: samādheḥ kiṃ punar yena sākṣiṇo 'pi vimohitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: from <s>samādhi</s> (deep concentration); how much more that by which even witnesses are bewildered.
Therefore, without injuring the <s>samādhi</s> of those whose passions have not departed,

children.text: dūre tapovanād asmād vīṇeyaṃ vādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: this lute should be played far away from this grove of austerities.'
And from that day onward <s>Udayana</s> captured the elephants
roaming on <s>Udayācala</s> with the delightful sounds of <s>Ghoṣavatī</s>.
Mounted on a tamed wild elephant, surrounded by lions and other wild beasts,
with sounding <s>Ghoṣavatī</s> in his hand, he used to come to the grove of austerities.

children.text: evaṃ yāti kvacit kāle bhagavān mām abhāṣata
children.translated_text: As time passed in this way, the venerable one said to me,

children.text: dārakas taruṇo jātaḥ kauśāmbīṃ gamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'The boy has become a young man; go to <s>Kauśāmbī</s>.'
When this desire had been expressed by me without words,
my son was consecrated by the teacher with the waters of sacred fords.

children.text: tacchiṣyās tu tadādiṣṭā mām ādāya saputrakām
children.translated_text: And his disciples, instructed by him, took me together with my son

children.text: ākāśena nayanti sma kṣaṇena nagarīm imām ||
children.translated_text: and carried us through the sky to this city in a moment.
Then I was set down by them in the lovely city garden,
and for a moment I relieved the weariness caused by traveling through the sky.

children.text: avatīrya tu te bhartā krīḍāpuṣkariṇīṃ pituḥ
children.translated_text: But your husband, after descending, was seen by the garden keepers
playing at breaking lotuses in his father's pleasure pond.

children.text: tair gatvā kathitaṃ rājñe deva devakumārakaḥ
children.translated_text: They went and reported to the king, 'O lord, a divine prince
has just now come from heaven and is entering the lotus pool.'

children.text: rājā tu drutam āgatya dṛṣṭvā devasamaṃ sutam
children.translated_text: But the king quickly came, saw his son, equal to a god,

children.text: deva evāyam ity uktvā praṇāmaṃ kartum udyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, saying 'This is indeed a god,' prepared to make obeisance.

children.text: tatas tapasvibhiḥ khasthaiḥ saṃbhrāntaiḥ sa nivāritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he was stopped by the alarmed ascetics standing in the sky:
'O king, you ought not to bow to <s>Udayana</s>'s son.

children.text: saṃdehaś ced imāṃ pṛccha mahiṣīṃ mṛgayāvatīm
children.translated_text: If there is doubt, ask this queen <s>Mṛgayāvatī</s>,
who is overcome by love, agitation, fear, and shame.'

children.text: rājā tu tān atho dṛṣṭvā mām apaśyat sutaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, seeing them, saw me, and then his son;

children.text: muhūrtaṃ cintayitvā tu vihasan prasthito gṛhān ||
children.translated_text: after thinking for a moment, he laughed and started toward the palace.
Then he was addressed by the seers, who stood before him in agitation:

children.text: na gantavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ naiṣa svapno nivartyatām ||
children.translated_text: 'Do not go, do not go; this is not a dream. Turn back.

children.text: atha vā bhavatu svapnaḥ svapne 'pi na virudhyate
children.translated_text: Or let it be a dream; even in a dream it is not wrong,
for a meeting with a beloved, though hard to obtain, is precious even in a dream.

children.text: yac ca brūmas tad ākarṇya cetaḥkarṇasukhāvaham
children.translated_text: And after hearing what we have to say, pleasant to the ear of the mind,

children.text: tato yasyāsi sāpatyām ādāya dayitām iti ||
children.translated_text: then take your beloved, together with her child, of whom you are the lord.'
And when he had turned back, they told him the whole event,
beginning with the carrying off by <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s> and the bringing to the hermitage.
But the king embraced his son and, unconscious in a swoon of joy,
was caught for a moment by his son as he fell upon the surface of the earth.

children.text: māṃ ca dṛṣṭvā ciraṃ dṛṣṭvā devadṛṣṭiviceṣṭayā
children.translated_text: And seeing me, gazing at me for a long time as one acts on seeing a deity,
he cast out a cluster of tear-drops with long sighs.

children.text: baddhāñjalir narapatir bravīti sma ca tān ṛṣīn
children.translated_text: With joined palms the king then said to those seers,
'Let the venerable teachers show favor by descending.'

children.text: tair uktaṃ na samādiṣṭā vasiṣṭhena vayaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: They said, 'We have not been instructed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> in that matter;

children.text: gacchāmo nāvatīryaiva svasti tubhyaṃ bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore we go without descending. May there be well-being for you.'

children.text: tān ayācata bhūpālo yat kiṃcit svāṅgadhāritam
children.translated_text: The king begged them, 'Leave behind something, whatever it may be, worn on your own bodies,
as a purifier for us, and then go as you please.'
They threw down their deerskins, their masses of matted hair bright like lightning,
and vanished on that very spot like clouds scattered by a violent wind.
But the devout king worshipped the deerskins as if they were divine objects,
and named that garden <s>Mṛgājina</s>.
From that day onward this <s>Mṛgājina</s> procession
was instituted by the king and became famous on earth.

children.text: tataḥ kṛtvā sutaṃ rājā yuvarājaṃ mṛgājine
children.translated_text: Then, having made his son crown prince at <s>Mṛgājina</s>,
the king, joyful at heart, entered the joyful city.

children.text: so 'yaṃ mayedṛśo labdhaḥ putraḥ sampādya dohadam
children.translated_text: Thus, after fulfilling my pregnancy craving, I obtained such a son.

children.text: tavāpi dohado yaḥ sa putri saṃpādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Daughter, let that pregnancy craving of yours also be fulfilled.

children.text: yadā tu naivākathayal lajjayā nṛpatis tadā
children.translated_text: But when, from shame, she would not tell the king,

children.text: māgadhīm uktavān pṛccha dohadaṃ bhaginīm iti ||
children.translated_text: he said to <s>Māgadhī</s>, 'Ask your sister her pregnancy craving.'

children.text: padmāvatī tu tāṃ pṛṣṭvā tadākhyātam avarṇayat
children.translated_text: <s>Padmāvatī</s> asked her, and then reported what she had said:

children.text: duḥsaṃpādā kila śraddhā mamety āha śanair iyam ||
children.translated_text: 'She says softly, "My desire, it seems, is difficult to fulfill."'

children.text: atha tām abravīd uccair hasitvā mṛgayāvatī
children.translated_text: Then <s>Mṛgayāvatī</s> laughed aloud and said to her,

children.text: mugdhe kiṃ nāma duḥsādhyam upāyacaturair nṛbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Innocent girl, what indeed is difficult to accomplish for kings skilled in stratagems?'

children.text: śrūyatāṃ vā purāvṛttaṃ mathurāyām abhūn nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Or listen to an event from long ago: in <s>Mathurā</s> there was a king,
<s>Ugrasena</s>, possessing a great army, a wind against the cloud of enemy forces.
He had a wife endowed with virtues, born from a family of pure conduct,
charming in behavior, who was charming even by name: <s>Manoramā</s>.
Once, when the season had arrived, rich with kuṭaja and arjuna trees,
and filled with the cries of peacocks, sāraṅgas, clouds, and frogs,
<s>Manoramā</s> entered the charming house-garden
to smell the kadamba-scented breeze, her first menstrual season having begun.

children.text: tadā ca drumilo nāma dānavo nabhasā vrajan
children.translated_text: At that time a dānava named <s>Drumila</s>, travelling through the sky,
had his gaze drawn by the garden's beauty and saw her there.
With him, who had assumed <s>Ugrasena</s>'s form and whose mind was wicked,
she came together, and at once she became pregnant.

children.text: strībhiś ca dohadaṃ pṛṣṭā kṛcchrād uktavatī hriyā
children.translated_text: When the women asked her about her dohada, her pregnancy craving, with difficulty she said in shame,
"I will satisfy my thirst with the blood, flesh, and entrails of <s>Viṣṇu</s>."
Hearing this, <s>Ugrasena</s> deliberated for a long time with his ministers,
and a <s>Viṣṇu</s> made of flour was created, its belly filled with ram's meat.
In the dim rays of a lamp, in her chamber,

children.text: nyastaḥ piṣṭamayo viṣṇuḥ kṣapāyāṃ kṣapitas tayā ||
children.translated_text: that flour-made <s>Viṣṇu</s> was placed at night and consumed by her.
When this dohada, though hard to accomplish, had been accomplished by a device,

children.text: vadhyaṃ yādavasiṃhasya kaṃsaṃ sutam asuta sā ||
children.translated_text: she gave birth to her son <s>Kaṃsa</s>, who was to be slain by the lion of the <s>Yādavas</s>.

children.text: tena bravīmi nāsty eva duḥsaṃpādā kriyā nṛbhiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: there is no act at all that men cannot accomplish.

children.text: tasmāt tavāpi yā śraddhā sāpi saṃpādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: So let that wish of yours too be carried out.

children.text: kathitaṃ ca tataḥ śrutvā padmāvatyeyam icchati
children.translated_text: Having heard the story thus told, this <s>Padmāvatī</s> desires
to see the whole earth while seated in an aerial car in the sky.
Then, laughing aloud, playful <s>Vasantaka</s> said,
"My lord, this is just the same longing that the slave-wives have.
But I have told them all, 'Climb onto a swing

children.text: dolām āruhya nabhasā muhur āyāta yāta ca ||
children.translated_text: hanging from a tall post, and go again and again through the air, back and forth.

children.text: upāyam anyaṃ patayo bhavatīnāṃ na jānate
children.translated_text: Your husbands know no other means.
So let your wish for sky-travel be fulfilled in that way.'"

children.text: tataḥ prahasitā sarve rumaṇvān idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then everyone laughed, and <s>Rumaṇvān</s> said this:
"Let the joking be stopped; let the matter at hand proceed."
<s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s> said, "What is there to consider here?
This is precisely the special domain of craftsmen."
But <s>Rumaṇvān</s> summoned carpenters and urged them:
"Let a machine that moves through the sky be made quickly."

children.text: athotkramya ciraṃ sarve mantrayitvā ca śilpinaḥ
children.translated_text: Then all the craftsmen withdrew, deliberated for a long time,
and spoke to <s>Rumaṇvān</s> with voices stumbling from fear:

children.text: caturvidhāni jānīmo vayaṃ yantrāṇi tad yathā
children.translated_text: "We know four kinds of machines, namely:
water-machines, stone-machines, dust-machines, and those made from heaps of reeds.
But the <s>Yavanas</s>, it is said, know sky-machines.

children.text: asmākaṃ tu na yātāni gocaraṃ cakṣuṣām iti ||
children.translated_text: They have not come within the range of our eyes."

children.text: tatra ca brāhmaṇaḥ kaścid abravīd āgrahārikaḥ
children.translated_text: Thereupon a certain Brahmin, an agrahāra-holder, said:

children.text: bhoḥ sabhe śrūyatāṃ tāvad yan mayākhyānakaṃ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: "O assembly, first hear a little story that I have heard.
There is a carpenter of <s>Mahāsena</s> named <s>Pukvasaka</s>.
He went with the military camp to the district of <s>Surāṣṭra</s>.
There he saw another handsome young artisan,

children.text: viśvilo nāma yaḥ śilpī sadṛśo viśvakarmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: a craftsman named <s>Viśvila</s>, equal to <s>Viśvakarman</s>.

children.text: atha pukvasakas tasya pitaraṃ mayam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pukvasaka</s> said to that man's father, <s>Maya</s>,

children.text: tava putrāya duhitā dattā ratnāvalī mayā ||
children.translated_text: 'I have given my daughter <s>Ratnāvalī</s> to your son.

children.text: praṣṭavyaś ca tvayā nāhaṃ kīdṛśī sā guṇair iti
children.translated_text: And you need not ask me, "What is she like in qualities?"
For she is a necklace of jewels of qualities: family, beauty, noble birth, and the rest.
Some advantage accrues to us from <s>Mahāsena</s>'s patronage.
Therefore send your son for the sake of accomplishing our advancement.'

children.text: mayena ca pratijñāto gatvā pukvasako gṛhān
children.translated_text: When <s>Maya</s> had agreed, <s>Pukvasaka</s> went home
and passed a long time longing for the arrival of his son-in-law.

children.text: kṛtvā rājakule karma kadācid gṛham āgatam
children.translated_text: Once, after doing work in the royal household, he came home,

children.text: bhaṇati sma na taṃ kaścit snāhi bhuṅkṣveti cākulaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but no one in the disturbed house said to him, 'Bathe and eat.'

children.text: bhāryayā kathitaṃ tasmai kim etad iti pṛṣṭayā
children.translated_text: When he asked, 'What is this?' his wife told him:
'The whole house has been thrown into confusion by some visitor.
He handed over his own rice grains for cooking,

children.text: mandako 'ham amībhir me maṇḍaḥ saṃpādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: saying, "I am weak; have gruel prepared for me from these."

children.text: kāṣṭhabhāraśataṃ dagdhaṃ na ca svidyanti taṇḍulāḥ
children.translated_text: A hundred loads of firewood have been burned, and still the rice grains do not soften.

children.text: tenāyam ākulo lokas tat kim etad bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: Because of him these people are confused; what can this be?'
Then <s>Pukvasaka</s> embraced his wife and said,

children.text: gṛhasthe vardhase diṣṭyā prāptas te duhitur varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Housewife, by good fortune you prosper: your daughter's bridegroom has arrived.'

children.text: kvāsau kvāsau viśvabhadra iti pṛcchati bhartari
children.translated_text: As her husband asked, 'Where is he? Where is that <s>Viśvabhadra</s>?'
his wife covered her head and showed him the workshop.
Then <s>Viśvila</s> quickly came out from the workshop
and, bowing low, saluted his teacher, whose arms were outstretched.
Raised up by his father-in-law, whose eyes were raining tears of joy,
he was embraced closely, like a friend seen after a long time.
After being honored with arghya and the other courtesies, he was asked by <s>Pukvasaka</s>,

children.text: kiṃmayās taṇḍulās tāta kathyatām iti so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: 'Dear boy, tell me: what are these rice grains made of?' He said:
'These rice grains were fashioned by me in the space of a ghaṭikā
from a piece of pale wood, from the karaghāṭa tree.'
Then <s>Pukvasaka</s> said, 'This is the workmanship of <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
Besides you too, a lion among craftsmen, there is no third.'

children.text: adyaiva ca dinaṃ bhadram ato ratnāvalīkaraḥ
children.translated_text: And this very day is auspicious; therefore let <s>Ratnāvalī</s>'s hand be taken.

children.text: gṛhyatām iti tenokte viśvilenoktam om iti ||
children.translated_text: When he said this, <s>Viśvila</s> replied, "So be it."
Having joined himself to <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, whose brilliant beauty was flashing,

children.text: saṃmīyate sma nāṅgeṣu daridra iva kāmukaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he could not be contained within his limbs, like a poor man in love.
As the two faced one another like painted <s>Vidyādharas</s>,
a long time passed for them, their eyes having abandoned blinking.

children.text: atha ratnāvalīṃ dṛṣṭvā vicintām iva viśvilaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Ratnāvalī</s> as if sunk in anxious thought, <s>Viśvila</s>,

children.text: kim etad iti saṃdihya kim etad iti pṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: wondering, "What is this?" asked, "What is this?"
When she did not speak, one girl said,

children.text: bhartṛdāraka yady asti śrotum icchā tataḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: "Young master, if you wish to hear it, then listen.

children.text: syālakās tava jalpanti pūrvam ekākinīṃ vayam
children.translated_text: Your brothers-in-law are chattering, 'Previously we supported our sister alone;

children.text: adhunā saha jāmātrā puṣṇīmo bhaginīm iti ||
children.translated_text: now we support our sister together with her husband.'"

children.text: iti śrutvā vanaṃ gatvā cittvā dārūṇi kānyapi
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Viśvila</s> went to the forest, cut some pieces of wood,
and then fitted together certain Yavana mechanisms.
With parts of trees prescribed in the vṛkṣāyurveda,
he made cooking utensils that conferred long life and health.
Selling those for a price a thousand times greater, he gave that wealth

children.text: śvaśurāya dadāti sma sa ca prītas tad ādade ||
children.translated_text: to his father-in-law, and he, pleased, accepted it.

children.text: evaṃ dineṣu gacchatsu vidrāṇa iva pukvasaḥ
children.translated_text: As the days passed in this way, <s>Pukvasa</s>, as if distressed,
summoned <s>Viśvila</s> and the others and spoke sorrowfully.

children.text: aham ājñāpito rājñā brahmadattaḥ suhṛd mama
children.translated_text: "I have been commanded by the king. <s>Brahmadatta</s>, my friend,
lord of the country of <s>Kāśī</s>, has asked me out of affection:

children.text: tava pukvasako nāma takṣāsti kuśalaḥ kila
children.translated_text: 'You have, I hear, a skilled carpenter named <s>Pukvasaka</s>.
Let him be sent to me for making a hall of justice.
Having built that temple in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a work equal to his own intelligence,
may he return unhindered.'

children.text: avaśyaṃ ca mayā tatra gantavyam anujīvinā
children.translated_text: And I, as a dependent, must necessarily go there;

children.text: martavyaṃ cāsya caṇḍasya rājño vākyam akurvatā ||
children.translated_text: if I do not carry out this fierce king's command, I must die.

children.text: dīrghakālaṃ ca tat karma daśā ceyam anuttarā
children.translated_text: The work will take a long time, and this condition is very hard to surpass;

children.text: tasmāt pukvasakaḥ sarvaiḥ sudṛṣṭaḥ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore let <s>Pukvasaka</s> be well looked upon by all of you."

children.text: viśvilena tataḥ proktam alaṃ trāsam upāsya vaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Viśvila</s> said, "Enough of giving way to fear.

children.text: bhṛtyaṃ vārāṇasīṃ yāntam anujānīta mām iti ||
children.translated_text: Permit me, your servant, to go to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>."
Permitted by his father-in-law and by the pleased king,

children.text: dūtaiḥ sa pratidūtaiś ca saha vārāṇasīṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he went to <s>Vārāṇasī</s> together with envoys and counter-envoys.
Although her husband had been gone for a long time, <s>Ratnāvalī</s>,
blind with grief, did not keep up her face, its faded cheeks washed by streams of constant tears,
marked by long, cold sighs, with her eyes fixed on the tip of her nose,
lacking the adornment of cared-for teeth and lips, with locks no longer smoothed down,
nor her hips with the girdle slipping and her garment soiled,

children.text: na dadhāti sma śokāndhā bāhū ca skhaladaṅgadau ||
children.translated_text: nor her arms with bracelets sliding from them.
While she was in such a condition, <s>Pukvasa</s>, alarmed, addressed

children.text: gṛhiṇīṃ cakitaḥ paśya niścintāṃ tanayām iti ||
children.translated_text: his wife: "Look at our daughter, so free from care."

children.text: sābravīt suṣṭhu paśyāmi lajjamānā ca te mukham
children.translated_text: She said, "I see very well, and from shame

children.text: na darśayāmi nanv evaṃ straiṇaṃ kimapi cāpalam ||
children.translated_text: I do not show you my face. Surely this is some feminine fickleness.
By her matchless beauty and by her countless virtues, the city,

children.text: vṛtā na labhate śāntim apaśyantī tam utsukā ||
children.translated_text: filled with longing when it does not see him, obtains no peace.
She who for a long time was cherished by him with looks, touches, and conversations,

children.text: seyam evam aśoketi mandabhāgyā bhaṇāmi kim ||
children.translated_text: is this same woman now without sorrow? What can I, ill-fated, say?"
As those two, wife and husband, were thus speaking with one another,
after a few days had passed <s>Ratnāvalī</s> conceived.
Then <s>Pukvasaka</s>, smiling with feigned anger, said to his wife,

children.text: bho paśya dayitāpatye duhituḥ prakriyām iti ||
children.translated_text: "See, dear one, the conduct of your daughter with regard to her husband."
She trembled with fear, from her husband's anger,

children.text: jātena ca nṛpāc caṇḍāt prākampata bhayena sā ||
children.translated_text: which had arisen because of her daughter's fault, and from the fierce king.

children.text: āsīd ayaṃ ca vṛttānto rājñāhṛtaś ca pukvasaḥ
children.translated_text: This was the situation, and <s>Pukvasa</s>, summoned by the king,
went to the royal palace, seeing the result of his daughter's fault.

children.text: sa vihasya nṛpeṇokto mā bhaiṣīr duhitus tava
children.translated_text: The king laughed and said to him, "Do not fear for your daughter.
The pregnancy was placed in her by your son-in-law himself; let this be understood.

children.text: ye mayā preṣitā dūtā jāmātrā bhavataḥ saha
children.translated_text: Those envoys whom I sent together with your son-in-law

children.text: nivṛttamātrais tair eva mahyam āveditaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: reported to me, as soon as they returned, as follows:

children.text: ārabhya prathamād eva prayāṇād eṣa viśvilaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Beginning with the very first journey, this <s>Viśvila</s>,
mounting a mechanical rooster, went off to some place.
And at night, when one watch remained, he came back under cover,
and, unnoticed by us, lay down on his own bed.
Once, when the envoys had awakened, he returned,
fell at their feet, and, dejected, begged them:
"This is not to be told to anyone, either to another craftsman or to anyone else.
The knowledge of aerial machines is hard for non-Yavanas to understand.
If this became widespread, like the knowledge of constructing beds,
it would be despised by the world, for human attachments last only a moment.

children.text: nindite vandanīye 'sminn āstāṃ tāvac ca pātakam
children.translated_text: Let the sin of censuring this praiseworthy thing remain aside for now;
the great visible fault is the taking away of one's livelihood.

children.text: ahaṃ hi bhāryayā sārdham uṣitvā rajanīṃ divā
children.translated_text: For I, after spending the night with my wife,

children.text: kurvan narapater ājñāṃ neṣyāmi divasān iti ||
children.translated_text: will pass the days doing the king's command by day."'

children.text: tac ca devakulaṃ tena ghaṭitaṃ kila tādṛśam
children.translated_text: And that temple was indeed built by him in such a way

children.text: draṣṭum icchā samutpannā yena duścakṣuṣām api ||
children.translated_text: that a desire to see it arose even among those whose eyes were hard to satisfy.
And he did not accept the unsurpassed heap of wealth

children.text: na gṛhṇāti sma vakti sma gurur me labhatām iti ||
children.translated_text: given by <s>Brahmadatta</s>; he said, "Let my teacher receive it."
Having spoken thus, <s>Mahāsena</s>, with a great heap of wealth,
and comforted <s>Pukvasa</s>, who was frightened at the taking of all his property.
<s>Viśvila</s> too, in a moment, had returned from <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,

children.text: ākāśayantram āsthāya praviṣṭaś ca gṛhān niśi ||
children.translated_text: having mounted the aerial machine, and entered the houses at night.
And when only a month had passed, <s>Pukvasa</s> said to <s>Viśvila</s>,

children.text: adya mām āha nṛpatiḥ śanair utsārya sasmitam ||
children.translated_text: "Today the king said this to me, gently sending the others away with a smile:
'You have told the knowledge of the aerial machine to my son-in-law;

children.text: yan mahyam api tat sarvam arthine kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore let all that be told to me also, since I am asking.'

children.text: mayā tu kathitaṃ tasmai na tasmai kathitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: But I said to him, 'It was not told to him by me;

children.text: tasmai tu kathitaṃ prītaiḥ śilpibhir yāvanair iti ||
children.translated_text: rather it was told to him by friendly Yavana craftsmen.'

children.text: rājñā tu kupitenoktaṃ nedaṃ lokavaco mṛṣā
children.translated_text: But the angry king said, 'This common saying is not false:

children.text: śilpinaḥ saha śāṭhyena jāyanta iti ghuṣyate ||
children.translated_text: it is proclaimed that craftsmen are born together with deceit.

children.text: tam idaṃ śāṭhyam ujjhitvā mannideśaṃ samācara
children.translated_text: So abandon this deceit and carry out my command;
otherwise take one good look at this world of the living.'

children.text: tad rakṣatā mama prāṇān saputrān anujīvinaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, protecting my life, and the lives of my sons and dependents,

children.text: rājñe tad yantravijñānam arthine kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: tell the king, who asks for it, that knowledge of the machine."

children.text: viśvilas tu pratijñāya śvaśurāya tathāstv iti
children.translated_text: But <s>Viśvila</s> promised his father-in-law, "So be it,"
and at night woke the sleeping <s>Ratnāvalī</s> and said this:
"I take leave of you; I am going back to my own home.

children.text: upāyais tava pitrāham asmāt sthānād vivāsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By your father's stratagems I have been driven away from this place.
He wants to obtain from me the knowledge of the aerial machine,

children.text: pracchādyaṃ ca tad asmābhir nidhānaṃ kṛpaṇair iva ||
children.translated_text: and that must be hidden by us like treasure by misers.

children.text: tad āstāṃ tāvad ātmā me tava vā dayitaḥ pitā
children.translated_text: So let it be, for the moment, whether it is myself or your dear father;
for the protection of this knowledge I would abandon even you."

children.text: iti ratnāvalī śrutvā bhartāram idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Ratnāvalī</s> said this to her husband:

children.text: kiṃ cāhaṃ durbhagā yena bhaktāṃ tyajasi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: "What am I, unfortunate woman that I am, that you abandon me though I am devoted to you?"
Then, mounting a vehicle shaped like a rooster together with his wife,

children.text: rātrāv ākāśam utpatya svasthānaṃ viśvilo yayau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvila</s> flew up into the sky at night and went to his own place.

children.text: te caivam aurasān bandhūñchilpaguptyai tyajanti ye
children.translated_text: And those who in this way abandon even their own blood relatives for the sake of guarding a craft--

children.text: te śilpaṃ darśayantīti kasyeyam asatī matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose false notion is this, that they will reveal the craft?

children.text: tasmād amī śaṭhā baddhāḥ pīḍyantāṃ tāḍanādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore these deceitful men, bound fast, should be tormented with beatings and the like;
for base men, incurable by conciliation and gifts, are to be dealt with by punishment.

children.text: iti senāpatiḥ śrutvā sarvān saṃyamya śilpinaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the general bound all the craftsmen

children.text: atāḍayad avocac ca yantram āyojyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and beat them, and said, "Set the machine in order."
In this very situation a certain newcomer said,

children.text: ahaṃ karomi vo yantraṃ mā sma tāḍyanta śilpinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I will make the machine for you. Let the craftsmen not be beaten.
Now let these materials for the machine be given."

children.text: tac ca sampāditaṃ sarvam acireṇa rumaṇvatā ||
children.translated_text: And all that was quickly supplied by <s>Rumaṇvat</s>.

children.text: teṣu cānyatamaḥ śilpī tam āgantum abhāṣata
children.translated_text: Then one of those craftsmen said to that newcomer,
"The general should be asked the measure of those who are to mount it.
Many craftsmen, when the number of persons to be carried was not known,
are heard to have been crushed by angry kings after their machines failed."

children.text: atha tenoktaṃ manye te varākā grāmyaśilpikāḥ
children.translated_text: Then he said, "I think those poor men were village craftsmen.

children.text: kiṃvā vacobhir bahubhiḥ kṣaṇam āsthīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Or what is the use of many words? Wait a moment."

children.text: ity uktvā garuḍākāram acireṇa cakāra saḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he quickly made a Garuḍa-shaped
aerial vehicle, fit for the sky and honored with mandāra flowers.
And he addressed the king: "O king, tormentor of kings,

children.text: ākramya garuḍaṃ krāma krāntapūrvāṃ mahīm imām ||
children.translated_text: mount <s>Garuḍa</s> and stride over this earth that has already been traversed."

children.text: atha rājāvadad devīṃ devi kiṃ sthīyate 'dhunā
children.translated_text: Then the king said to the queen, "Queen, why remain here now?

children.text: vimānam idam āruhya yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Mount this aerial vehicle and go wherever you wish."

children.text: avocat sā ca rājānam aryaputra tvayā vinā
children.translated_text: And she said to the king, "Noble prince, without you
I do not even go to a garden; how then to the unsupported sky?"
When the king said, "So the queen speaks," the craftsman replied,

children.text: nanu voḍhum idaṃ śaktaṃ sakalāṃ nagarīm iti ||
children.translated_text: "Surely this is able to carry the whole city."
Then the king, surrounded by the women of the inner apartments, with his wives and ministers,
and with the townspeople and guild groups, mounted the vehicle.
By it he entered the pure sky, whose expanse was mottled by the shadows of banners, flags, and the like,

children.text: puṇyam ākāśam āviśya prākprācīm agamad diśam ||
children.translated_text: and went eastward, to the eastern quarter.

children.text: dadarśa darśakas tatra yānaṃ yān nagaropari
children.translated_text: There <s>Darśaka</s> saw the vehicle going above the city,

children.text: devo vidyādharo vāpi bhoḥ ko 'yam iti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: and said, "Is this a god, or perhaps a <s>vidyādhara</s>? Ho, who is this?"
He was saluted by the king, with <s>Padmāvatī</s> at his side,
and, after being given leave, the king went on along the path of the wind.
Thus, after circling clockwise around the earth girdled by the ocean,
he went to the city of <s>Avanti</s>, where the water-gift had begun.
Knowing that the king was eager to experience the journey,
the craftsman stopped that machine, and then the lord of men was displeased.
When <s>Pradyota</s> saw it, tawny with the radiance of jewels,

children.text: kim etad iti saṃdehadolādolam abhūn manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his mind swung back and forth in doubt: "What is this?"

children.text: mahāṃś ced ayam utpāto ramaṇīyam ataḥ katham
children.translated_text: If this is a great portent, how is it beautiful?
If it is the gain of attaining what is desired, we have never heard of such a thing.
Before <s>Pradyota</s>, whose mind was thus in doubt, the lord of the <s>Vatsas</s>
slowly dropped an arrow on which letters had been written.

children.text: mahāsenas tam ādāya citram etad avācayat
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāsena</s> took it and read this strange message:

children.text: rājann udayanaś cauraḥ sadāras tvāṃ namasyati ||
children.translated_text: "O king, <s>Udayana</s> the thief, together with his wives, bows to you."
Hearing this, <s>Mahāsena</s> addressed his son-in-law:

children.text: caurāya dattam abhayaṃ tasmād avataratv iti ||
children.translated_text: "Immunity has been granted to a thief; therefore let him descend."
After seeing <s>Avanti</s> and <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, the aerial vehicle, and the water-giving,
his curiosity for sights, as they arose, had become diminished.

children.text: kāṃcid velām upāsyaivam āmantrya śvaśurau tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having remained in this way for a while, he then took leave of his parents-in-law,
and, with his vehicle gazed at by the people, alighted in <s>Kauśāmbī</s>.
After the immortals, brahmins, sacred fires, teachers, citizens, and dependents had been honored,
the king gave the order, "Let the craftsman be respectfully honored."
Then the lord of the earth saw a goddess standing in the sky,
outshining even brilliant lightning by her radiance.

children.text: tataś citrīyamāṇaṃ sā tam abhāṣata pārthivam
children.translated_text: Then she, while he was filled with wonder, addressed that king:

children.text: pūjitaiva tvayā yat tvāṃ pūjyaṃ pūjitavaty aham ||
children.translated_text: "Since you have honored me, who am worthy of honor, I too have honored you, who are worthy of honor.

children.text: vijñāpyaṃ śrūyatāṃ cedam asty ahaṃ guhyakāṅganā
children.translated_text: Listen now to this matter that I must report. I am a guhyakā woman,
an intimate attendant of the lord of the <s>Guhyakas</s>, known as <s>Bhadrā</s>.

children.text: kadācin nabhasā yāntī satī dṛṣṭavatī saraḥ
children.translated_text: Once, as I was travelling through the sky, I saw a lake,
shining like the sky, in a cave of the great mountain <s>Mahendra</s>.
There, playing in it, fanned with lotuses
held in the trunks of cow elephants, was the leader of a herd of wild elephants.

children.text: āsīc ca mama taṃ dṛṣṭvā karāmṛṣṭavaśāmukham
children.translated_text: When I saw him, with the face of his mate touched by his trunk, I thought:

children.text: kartāro hastiśikṣāyāṃ satyam āhur idaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: 'Those who are authorities on elephant-training truly say this as follows:
The maidens of gods, dānavas, gandharvas, piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas,

children.text: kanyāḥ sujātā diṅnāgair nānāsattvās tato gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: well-born through the elephants of the quarters, have passed from there into various beings.'
Then at once I fashioned for myself the form of a cow elephant,
and entered that very lake, whose water was split by the fragrance of rut.
My form was watched with sidelong glances by the jealous cow-elephant herd,
and the pleased herd-leader sported with me for a long time.
Then, when the Sun, whose charioteer is <s>Aruṇa</s>, had rays like moonbeams,

children.text: sa gajaḥ kṣālitakaṭaḥ kaṭakaṃ prāviśad gireḥ ||
children.translated_text: that elephant, his temples washed clean, entered the flank of the mountain.

children.text: ahaṃ tu vyasanasevā phalam utprekṣya dāruṇam
children.translated_text: But I, considering the dreadful fruit of indulging in such passion,
immediately resumed my own form and went to the assembly of the king of kings.
Clinging to <s>Dhanada</s>'s thigh, and remembering the trunk
of that herd-leader, I struck the lord of wealth with the fly-whisk.
He looked at me with a sidelong glance, his lip quivering with anger,
and, while the circle of the quarters trembled with fear, made me the vessel of a curse:
'Since I was struck by you with the fly-whisk while you were thinking of an elephant,

children.text: tvam avantipates tasmād abhavye hastinī bhava ||
children.translated_text: therefore, unworthy woman, become the cow elephant of the lord of <s>Avanti</s>.'
Then the yakṣa <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> said, 'For such a trifling offense,

children.text: prabhunā devadevena muktaḥ śāpo mahān iti ||
children.translated_text: a great curse has been released by the lord, the god of gods.'

children.text: śrutvedaṃ pūrṇabhadro 'pi śapto yasmāt tvam etayā
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> also was cursed: 'Since you,

children.text: śaptayā pīḍitas tasmād bhava hastī mahān iti ||
children.translated_text: because of this cursed woman, have been pained, therefore become a great elephant.'
Seeing us both with faces dejected by grief, the lord of wealth,
his anger uprooted, became soft in mind like fresh butter.

children.text: abravīc ca yadāhaṃ vāṃ smariṣyāmi kvacit tadā
children.translated_text: And he said, 'Whenever I remember the two of you,

children.text: śāpād asmād vimokṣyethe vibhītaṃ mā sma putrakau ||
children.translated_text: then you shall be released from this curse. Do not be afraid, my children.'
Thus I became <s>Bhadravatī</s>, the cow elephant of <s>Mahāsena</s>,
and <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> too became his male elephant, the fierce <s>Nalāgiri</s>.
While we were staying in subjection in <s>Mahāsena</s>'s palace,

children.text: āvayoś caritaṃ yat tat sarvaṃ pratyakṣam eva te ||
children.translated_text: all that history of the two of us was directly before your eyes.
And at that time, while I was carrying you away, I was remembered by the lord of wealth;

children.text: aham aprāpya kauśāmbīṃ vipannā gahane vane ||
children.translated_text: before reaching <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, I died in a dense forest.

children.text: na tathā vyasanenāsi pīḍitas tena tādṛśā
children.translated_text: You were not so afflicted by that misfortune of yours,

children.text: yathā mayi vipannāyāṃ priyadāraḥ striyām iva ||
children.translated_text: great as it was, as you were when I died, like a loving husband grieving for his wife.
After gaining a yakṣa birth, as an apsaras might after an animal birth,

children.text: tvām eva śocitavatī seva śaptaṃ śatakratum ||
children.translated_text: I grieved only for you, as <s>Śacī</s> grieved for cursed <s>Śatakratu</s>.

children.text: āsīc ca me kadā nāma kathaṃ nāma ca bhūpateḥ
children.translated_text: And I wondered, 'When, in what way, and what, indeed,

children.text: kaṃ nāma ca kariṣye 'ham upakāraṃ manāg iti ||
children.translated_text: small service shall I ever render to the king?'

children.text: nītaś cāsi mayā svapne tadā dhanapateḥ sabhām
children.translated_text: Then I led you in a dream to the assembly of the lord of wealth,
and carried you around the earth in an aerial car, while your son was safe in the womb.

children.text: bhaviṣyantaṃ ca te putraṃ magnaṃ kasyāṃcid āpadi
children.translated_text: Your future son, when a lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> is sunk in some calamity,

children.text: vidyādharendram uddhartā sukham āstāṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: will rescue him. May Your Majesty remain at ease.'

children.text: prākārasya tataḥ khaṇḍam apanīya jagāma sā
children.translated_text: Then, removing a section of the rampart, she departed;

children.text: yat tad bhadravatīdvāraṃ kauśāmbyāṃ prathitaṃ bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: that is the <s>Bhadravatī</s> Gate of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, famous on earth.
Then the words of the citizens were heard in every house:
'The true word of the siddha's command has been fulfilled by sky-going beings.'

children.text: sīmantonnayanāntakarmaviratāv autsukyagarbhā purī pratyāsannakaragṛheva taruṇī kṛcchrān nināya kṣapām
children.translated_text: When the rites ending with the parting of the pregnant woman's hair were finished, the city, pregnant with eagerness and like a young woman near the lying-in chamber, passed the night with difficulty.

children.text: śuddhānte ca śukādipañjaravayaḥkolāhale 'pi śrute rājā dārakajanmasaṃpadaghanaprahlādam utpraikṣata ||
children.translated_text: And in the inner palace, even amid the din of caged birds such as parrots, the king anticipated the dense delight brought by the wealth of a son's birth.
Then, in the season friendly to <s>Smara</s>, when the moon was joined with flowers,
and when the sun's rays were gentle, the queen gave birth to a son.
The birth of a son for the king, the birth of happiness for the world,

children.text: śaṅkājanma ca śatrūṇāṃ samaṃ samabhavat trayam ||
children.translated_text: and the birth of dread for his enemies: these three came about at the same time.
Then the astrologers, assembling with calculated horoscopes, said:
'May the father of a universal emperor conquer both worlds.'

children.text: tataḥ sacivabhāryāṇāṃ tasminn eva dine sutāḥ
children.translated_text: Then on that very day sons were born to the wives of the ministers,
a short time afterward, younger than the king's son.

children.text: kim utsavaḥ kiṃ vyasanaṃ kiṃ prāṇāḥ prāṇayantu kim
