children.translated_text: Was it a festival, or was it a calamity? Was it their very life? What should they love?
When this had come to the <s>Cedis</s> and <s>Vatsas</s>, there was no certainty.
When the birth-rite had been completed and the twelfth day had arrived,
the king and the ministers gave fitting names to their sons.
Because <s>Kubera</s> has a man as his vehicle, he is <s>Naravāhana</s>;
"Let him therefore be <s>Naravāhanadatta</s>, since he was given by him."

children.text: iti nāma kṛtaṃ rājñā putrasya sapurodhasā
children.translated_text: Thus the king, together with his family priest, gave his son his name,
after delighting the twice-born with gifts of land, gold, elephants, horses, and the like.

children.text: nāmnā hariśikhaṃ cakre rumaṇvān ātmajaṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rumaṇvān</s> made his own son <s>Hariśikha</s> by name, because

children.text: tasmai vitīrṇavān svapne devadevaḥ śaraṃ hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: the god of gods, <s>Hari</s>, had given him an arrow in a dream.
<s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s> made his son <s>Marubhūtika</s>,

children.text: saṃnāhachadmanā tasmai yatas taṃ maruto daduḥ ||
children.translated_text: because the <s>Maruts</s> had given him to him under the guise of armor.

children.text: cakāra gomukhaṃ putram ṛṣabhaḥ saṃjñayā yataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣabha</s> made his son <s>Gomukha</s> by designation, because

children.text: svayaṃ gobhiḥ prasannābhiś citraṃ tasmai pradarśitam ||
children.translated_text: a marvel had been shown to him by pleased cows themselves.

children.text: putraṃ tapantakaṃ nāmnā karoti sma vasantakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vasantaka</s> named his son <s>Tapantaka</s>,

children.text: yasmāt taṃ tapanas tasmai kuṇḍalachadmanā dadau ||
children.translated_text: because <s>Tapana</s> had given him to him under the guise of earrings.

children.text: evaṃ labdhaś ca jātaś ca yaḥ kṛtaṃ nāma yasya ca
children.translated_text: Thus he who was obtained and born, and whose name was made,

children.text: aham eva sa te caite sarve hariśikhādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is I myself; and these are all those others, <s>Hariśikha</s> and the rest.
We, after the rites such as first feeding had been performed at the proper times,

children.text: avardhāmahi laghv eva sanāthāḥ pādapā iva ||
children.translated_text: quickly grew up, like trees that have protectors.
Then we entered the princes' school, supervised by teachers,
together with fellow students and nurses.

children.text: avratair eva cāsmābhir abhyastāḥ sakalāḥ kalāḥ
children.translated_text: Even without formal vows we practiced all the arts,

children.text: savratais tu catasro 'pi vidyāḥ sarvaṃ ca vāṅmayam ||
children.translated_text: and with vows we studied the four sciences and all literature.
As the days passed in this way, one day <s>Marubhūtika</s>,
in his childish state, was playing with a ball on a day without lessons.

children.text: taṃ tu bālasvabhāvena tasmād ācchidya kandukam
children.translated_text: Then, with a child's nature, I snatched the ball from him,

children.text: ahaṃ javena mahatā prayātaḥ pitur antikam ||
children.translated_text: and ran with great speed to my father's side.
Then <s>Marubhūtika</s>, pursuing me at speed, with a stream of heavy breaths,
came up in anger, his hands clenched into fists.

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ tāteti tātena sa pṛṣṭa idam uktavān
children.translated_text: When my father asked him, "What is it, what is it, dear boy?" he said this:

children.text: kanduko me hṛto 'nena tam ayaṃ dāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "My ball has been taken by him. Let this one be made to give it back."
Then, embraced by the king and given another ball,
he was threatened with a raised finger by my father and went back to the princes' school.

children.text: aham apy aṅkam āropya tātena paribhāṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: I too was lifted onto my father's lap and reproved by him:

children.text: mā sma tāta punar bhrātṝn kopayeḥ kopanān iti ||
children.translated_text: "Dear boy, do not again anger your hot-tempered brothers."
Even though I was forbidden in that way, because of a child's playful nature,

children.text: yathainān kopayāmi sma tathaite mām akopayan ||
children.translated_text: just as I used to anger them, so they too angered me.
Once, while practicing, <s>Marubhūtika</s>

children.text: icchati sma ca visraṣṭuṃ mayā ca calitaṃ dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: wanted to release an iron arrow, and I shook the bow.

children.text: asāv api ca nārācaś calitāc cāpataś cyutaḥ
children.translated_text: That arrow too, falling from the shaken bow,
failed to touch the jasmine-bud target by only that much.

children.text: utsṛjya kupitaś cāpaṃ dhāvamānaḥ sa mām anu
children.translated_text: Angrily throwing down the bow, he ran after me
and then came near the king, who was seated in the audience hall.
Seeing <s>Marubhūtika</s> angry, <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>
became angry, rebuked him, and said this to the king:
"The prince, knower of all sciences and close to fresh youth,
should be consecrated as crown prince, great king.

children.text: yāvad yāvaddhi śāstrajñāḥ śāstrārthān na prayuñjate
children.translated_text: For so long as knowers of <s>śāstra</s> do not put the meanings of the <s>śāstras</s> into practice,

children.text: tāvat tāvad bhavanty eṣāṃ kuṇṭhāḥ kāryeṣu buddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for just so long their minds become blunted in practical affairs.
These sons of <s>Rumaṇvān</s> and the others, <s>Hariśikha</s> and the rest,
though they know the <s>śāstras</s>, are all the more blind in understanding.
Even over a small matter, forgetting themselves, excited and red-faced,

children.text: prabhum eva jighāṃsanti mṛgendraṃ markaṭā iva ||
children.translated_text: they try to strike at their own lord, like monkeys at a lion.
Therefore let these too be appointed to certain offices.
Let this request of mine be made fruitful."

children.text: yaugandharāyaṇavacaḥ subhagaṃ niśamya prītyā narendrasabham ucchrayitāgrahastam
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>'s graceful speech, the royal assembly, joyfully raising its hands high,

children.text: bhoḥ sādhu sādhu narakuñjara sādhu mantrin ity ujjhitāsanam abhāṣata nirvyavastham ||
children.translated_text: left its seats and cried out in disorder, "Good, good, elephant among men! Good, minister!"

children.text: tatas tātaḥ sabhāṃ dṛṣṭvā tathā saṃjātasaṃpadam
children.translated_text: Then my father, seeing the assembly thus filled with enthusiasm,
addressed them according to rank and spoke with restraint:
"What is there to ask here, when you, whose intelligence surpasses <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
speak even without being asked, your modesty banished by delight?

children.text: tena yad rocate sādhu pūjyebhyaḥ pūjitaṃ dinam
children.translated_text: Therefore, on whatever fine and honored day is pleasing to the venerable ones,

children.text: tatrāyaṃ svasutaḥ prītyā bālaḥ saṃskriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: on that day let this boy, my own son, be consecrated with affection."
Now at this juncture, <s>Kaliṅgasenā</s>, having been permitted to enter,
saluted the king from a distance.
When the king said to her, "Come," she, with steps not overly slow,
approached the side of the couch and sat on the seat indicated.
Adorned with a modest number of carefully set pearls and wearing spotless garments,
she shone like an autumnal spotless swan with white <s>kāśa</s>-plume fans.
Her hair, its loosened knot slipping down to the base of her neck,
was like the sky at dawn, with darkness resting on the peak of the western mountain.
She had reached the end of youth, like a river the end of the rainy season;
her form was restless with moving grace, yet, though full, seemed restrained.
Though modest, she seemed bold; though young, she seemed mature;

children.text: mitavāg api vācālā vyākhyātavyā hi tanmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: though sparing in speech, she seemed eloquent, for her state of mind required explanation.
Before her sat a girl, as if ten years old.

children.text: tayā me dṛṣṭir ākṛṣṭā guṇair naur iva mantharā ||
children.translated_text: By her my gaze was drawn, like a slow boat by ropes, through her virtues.
With thick, curling, glossy hair that had been arranged only recently,
that slender girl was like a mango creeper in which flocks of cuckoos had hidden.
As I looked at her without blinking, my natural pair of eyes seeming inadequate,
she made me, as it were, a thousand-eyed <s>Sahasrākṣa</s>.
Her face shone with teeth like the seeds of a ripe pomegranate,
and her lips were parted in the shape of pomegranate buds.
With her pale, fine garment raised up by a splendid crimson bodice,
she was like a garland of red lotuses fastened with lotus-fiber strips.

children.text: unnīyante sma bālāyāś cihnair aṅgāni komalaiḥ
children.translated_text: The tender limbs of the girl were revealed by their delicate marks,
as the fruits of a mango creeper are revealed by its buds.
Then the king asked, "Whose embodied beauty is this?
Tell me whose daughter she has become, and what her name is."
<s>Kaliṅgasenā</s> replied, "This pitiable girl is my daughter,

children.text: yām eva pṛcchati svāmī bhṛtyāṃ madanamañjukām ||
children.translated_text: the servant <s>Madanamañjukā</s>, about whom my lord is asking."

children.text: tataḥ sasneham āhūya mātar ehīti bhūpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king called her affectionately, saying, "Come to your mother,"

children.text: ūrūm āropayad bālāṃ sā cemāṃ vāmalocanām ||
children.translated_text: and placed on his lap that young girl, lovely-eyed as she was.

children.text: drutam ādityaśarmā ca gṛhītvā lagnam abravīt
children.translated_text: And <s>Ādityaśarman</s> quickly took the auspicious moment and announced it;

children.text: aho citram iti smeram abhūc ca nṛpater mukham ||
children.translated_text: the king's face became smiling, as if saying, "Ah, wonderful!"
Even by the noise produced from the rise of the horns of royal rams fighting

children.text: dhvanināpi na taccakṣur ākṣiptaṃ nihitaṃ mayi ||
children.translated_text: that eye, fixed on me, was not distracted.
But the king had abundant, spotless clothing and ornaments
given to <s>Sāmbā</s> and to her, and then dismissed the assembly.
The king went to the inner palace; I went to the prince's quarters;

children.text: dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca viśvasya bālā svaṃ bhavanaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: and the girl, after sighing long and hotly, went to her own house.
Then, on an auspicious day, surrounded by chief brahmins,
the king himself consecrated me, seated on the royal throne, as crown prince.
Likewise the king joyfully commanded <s>Hariśikha</s> as follows:

children.text: yatra prasthāpyate bhartā gantavyaṃ tava nirvyatham ||
children.translated_text: "Wherever your lord is sent, you must go there without hesitation.

children.text: senāpatiś ca mantrī ca bhavān bhavatu sodyamaḥ
children.translated_text: You shall be both general and minister, energetic in your duties."

children.text: ity ājñāpitavān rājā prahvaṃ hariśikhaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the king instructed the bowing <s>Hariśikha</s>.
"You, sword and shield in hand, must guard your lord without negligence."
With this command he made <s>Marubhūtika</s> delighted.

children.text: ādiśad gomukhaṃ bhartū ramaṇīyaṃ manas tvayā
children.translated_text: He ordered <s>Gomukha</s>, "Your lord's mind must be made pleasant by you
with charming activities and conversations free from reproach."
Then the king said to <s>Tapantaka</s>, who wore earrings:

children.text: na tyājyo bhavatā svāmī kadācid iti pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "You must never abandon your master at any time."
Surrounded by them and by others carrying parasols and fly-whisks,
with my body adorned for the auspicious rite, I paid homage to the gods and brahmins.

children.text: pitur mātaram āsīnāṃ pitaraṃ ca samantriṇam
children.translated_text: I also saluted my father's mother sitting there, my father together with his ministers,
and the flourishing royal harem, headed by my two mothers.
Then, mounted on a flower-chariot that sent forth auspicious sounds,
I went all around the city, which was covered with flowers, shoots, parched grain, and the like.
Then, after receiving the consecration, together with <s>Hariśikha</s> and the others,
intent on my own duties and enjoying myself, I passed a year.
When the yearly consecration was completed with the same pomp as before,
I produced firmness in all the sciences by repeated study.

children.text: evaṃ me samatīteṣu keṣucid divaseṣv aham
children.translated_text: Thus, when some days had passed for me,

children.text: prātar bhojanavelāyāṃ na paśyāmi sma gomukham ||
children.translated_text: one morning at mealtime I did not see <s>Gomukha</s>.

children.text: na cānena vinā mahyaṃ nirvāṇam api rocate
children.translated_text: And without him even liberation would not please me;
therefore, without him, we passed the day without eating.
When I said, "Find out where <s>Gomukha</s> is," <s>Marubhūtika</s>,

children.text: unmattakaḥ sa saṃvṛtta ity avocad gatāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having gone and returned, said, "He has become mad."
"And if the noble prince has no confidence in this now,

children.text: gatvā tapantakas tasya vikārān prekṣatām iti ||
children.translated_text: then let <s>Tapantaka</s> go and observe his derangements."

children.text: tatas tapantako gatvā punar āgatya coktavān
children.translated_text: Then <s>Tapantaka</s> went, returned again, and said,

children.text: āryaputra na tan mithyā yad āha marubhūtikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Noble prince, what <s>Marubhūtika</s> said is not false.
Looking at his face reflected in a spotless mirror, <s>Gomukha</s>,
shaking his head in anger, tears open his eyes.

children.text: kadācic ca smitaṃ kṛtvā prasanne netratārake
children.translated_text: Sometimes, after smiling, when the pupils of his eyes are clear,
he moves them now to the ends of his ears, now to the tip of his nose.
And his two lips, rubbed with beeswax and reddened by betel juice,
he opens wide apart and scratches even with the edge of his teeth.
Having seen such derangements and appearances of his, I have come back;
therefore, noble prince, treatment for him should be undertaken quickly."
Immediately afterward <s>Gomukha</s> came, his garment rumpled by lovemaking,
softly embarrassed because of his boldness, and bowed to me.

children.text: kaccit svastho 'si bhadreti mayoktaḥ sann abhāṣata
children.translated_text: When I said, "Are you well, good man?" he replied,

children.text: kim arthaṃ cāham svastho na hy ahaṃ marubhūtikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "For what reason would I not be well? I am not <s>Marubhūtika</s>.

children.text: yo hi nāgarakaṃ manyo manyate mām anāmayam
children.translated_text: For whoever, though thinking himself urbane, considers me unwell,
he is the madman, his mind fallen from its natural state.
Now, dear friend, I have begun to learn the inner doctrine of the treatise

children.text: ahaṃ śikṣitum ārabdhaḥ sa cāpi vyāpṛtaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: from <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>, and he too is always occupied.

children.text: vyācaṣṭe ca tadā mahyam antaraṃ labhate yadā
children.translated_text: He explains it to me whenever he gets an interval;

children.text: tena māṃ mā pratīkṣadhvaṃ bhojanāyodyatā iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore do not wait for me when you are ready for a meal."

children.text: tataś cārabhya divasāt sāyam āyātavān ayam
children.translated_text: And from that day on he came in the evening,

children.text: kadācid divase 'nyasmin dvayos triṣu gateṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: sometimes on another day, or when two or three days had passed.
Once, at the end of a meal, coming from somewhere with eagerness,

children.text: aho śobhanta ity uccaiḥ prāśaṃsat khaṇḍamodakān ||
children.translated_text: he loudly praised the pieces of sweet cake, saying, "Ah, they are splendid!"

children.text: mayā tu dāpitān anyān krudhyann iva vihāya saḥ
children.translated_text: But when I had others brought for him, he abandoned them as if angry,
and forcibly snatching them up, he himself carried off the leftover sweet cakes.
"Noble prince, the madness of your dear friend has become clear."

children.text: acikitsyaś ca saṃvṛtta ity avocat tapantakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Tapantaka</s> said, "He has become incurable."

children.text: evam ābharaṇaṃ vāsas tāmbūlaṃ candanādi ca
children.translated_text: Thus ornaments, clothing, betel, sandal-paste, and the like,

children.text: labdhalabdhaṃ gacchati sma gṛhītvā kvāpi gomukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever he obtained, <s>Gomukha</s> used to take and carry off somewhere.
When matters had gone on mostly in this way, <s>Rumaṇvān</s>,
having had his arrival announced, came to the prince's quarters and bowed to me.

children.text: taṃ tātam iva dṛṣṭvāham upakrāntaś ca vanditum
children.translated_text: Seeing him like a father, I began to bow down to him,

children.text: tena coddhatahastena tāta mā meti vāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but with his hand raised he stopped me, saying, "My son, do not."

children.text: uktaṃ ca na tvayā tāta bālena vāsmadādayaḥ
children.translated_text: And he said, "My son, we and others like us are not to be saluted by you as by a boy.

children.text: vandyas tvam adhunā prāpto loke 'smiṃl lokapālatām ||
children.translated_text: Now you are the one to be honored, having attained in this world the status of a guardian of the world.

children.text: anyac ca rājasaṃdeśam ākhyātum aham āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, I have come to report a message from the king.

children.text: yat tvām āha mahārājaḥ sabhṛtyaṃ tan nibodhyatām ||
children.translated_text: What the great king says to you together with your attendants, hear that.

children.text: puryām atra śaratkāle yātrā citrā pravartitā
children.translated_text: Here in the city, in the autumn season, a splendid festival has begun,

children.text: yā nāgavanayātreti na kvacin na vikathyate ||
children.translated_text: one that is everywhere spoken of as the Nāgavana festival.

children.text: etāvantaṃ ca sā kālaṃ yuṣmabhyaṃ na prakāśitā
children.translated_text: For so long a time it has not been made known to you,

children.text: mā bhūd vidyāvighāto vas tadvyākṣiptadhiyām iti ||
children.translated_text: lest there should be an obstacle to your learning, with your minds distracted by it.
A festival steals the mind, and childhood is a state whose mind is easily stolen,
and there is the learning that depends on concentration: the conjunction of the three is hard to manage.
And it has been said: for one who is not wakeful, dull-witted, pleasure-loving,

children.text: granthabhīroś ca sidhyanti na śāstrāṇi tapāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: and afraid of books, neither sciences nor austerities succeed.
Now, since you are to be instructed in what is to be understood and have reached tender youth,

children.text: bhavanto niḥsukhāḥ santaḥ saṃtapantīva me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you seem to scorch my heart by remaining without enjoyment.

children.text: tad asti yadi vaḥ kāṅkṣā taṃ yātrotsavam īkṣitum
children.translated_text: Therefore, if you have a desire to see that festival procession,

children.text: tato yāta nirāśaṅkā nāsti ced āsyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: then go without hesitation; but if not, remain here."

children.text: mayoktaṃ suhṛdaḥ pṛṣṭvā yanno niṣpadyate hitam
children.translated_text: I said, "After asking my friends what would turn out for our good,

children.text: tad vo vijñāpayiṣyāmi tāvat pṛcchāmi tān iti ||
children.translated_text: I shall inform you of that; for now I will ask them."
Then <s>Rumaṇvān</s>, with tears falling down his cheeks, said,

children.text: haihayānāṃ kulaṃ tuṅgaṃ ciraṃ vijayatāṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: "May the lofty family of the <s>Haihaya</s>s long conquer the world.
By your excellent conduct we have been made servants of your lineage,
in that our sons have been considered fit to answer such a question."

children.text: ity uktvā nirgate tasmin suhṛdaḥ pṛṣṭavān aham
children.translated_text: When he had spoken thus and gone out, I asked my friends,

children.text: yasya yad vaḥ sthitaṃ buddhau tena tat kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let each of you tell whatever is fixed in his mind."

children.text: tato hariśikhenoktaṃ na me gamanam īpsitam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hariśikha</s> said, "I do not wish to go,
because empty fortresses are seized by neighboring kings.
Your Highness has certainly heard what <s>Āruṇi</s> did,

children.text: vijñāya nagarīṃ śūnyāṃ yat tad āruṇinā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: when the lord of the earth was abroad and he learned that the city was empty.

children.text: durgasya ca kṛtā rakṣā rājā ca paritoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: The fortress would be guarded, the king would be pleased,

children.text: khyāpitaṃ dhīracittatvam ātmanaś ca bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: and my own steadiness of mind would be made known."

children.text: tvaṃ kim āttheti pṛṣṭaḥ sann avocan marubhūtikaḥ
children.translated_text: When asked, "What do you say?" <s>Marubhūtika</s> replied,

children.text: yuktaṃ hariśikhenoktam ity etac ca tapantakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "What <s>Hariśikha</s> has said is proper," and <s>Tapantaka</s> said the same.
Then <s>Gomukha</s>, smiling and as if with some envy, said,

children.text: kim atra bhaṇyate ko 'nyo mantrī hariśikhād varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "What is there to say here? What other minister is better than <s>Hariśikha</s>?

children.text: idaṃ tv ācakṣva kenāyaṃ niyukto durgarakṣaṇe
children.translated_text: But tell me this: by whom was he appointed to guard the fortress?

children.text: rakṣataś cāniyuktasya doṣam andha na paśyasi ||
children.translated_text: Do you not see, blind man, the fault in guarding it without being appointed?
The crown prince is young, learned, trained in weapons, not overly fond of amusements,
and aided by men like you. How could he fall into thoughtlessness?

children.text: yac ca rājoditaṃ vakṣye nāsti ced āsyatām iti
children.translated_text: And as to the king's statement, 'If you do not wish, remain here,'

children.text: tadāśayaparīkṣārtham api cet tan na duṣyati ||
children.translated_text: even if that was meant to test his intention, there is no fault in it.
Therefore men whose understanding of meanings is tied to texts set down in books
deserve favor in questions, not such deceitful ministers.
As for me, since I am skilled in the application of virtues and policy-means,
my association is with those who are clever in practical application.

children.text: sukhaṃ naḥ sevituṃ kālo na ṣāḍguṇyakadarthanām
children.translated_text: It is time for us to enjoy ourselves, not to be tormented by the sixfold policy.

children.text: yac coktaṃ dharmaśāstreṇa tat tāvad avadhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: And what has been said by the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> should first be considered:
with regard to age, action, wealth, learning, and noble birth,
one should move about here behaving in conformity with dress, speech, and intelligence.
Therefore get up; let us go to the festival, which shows wondrous sights,

children.text: krīḍiṣyāmaś ca kāntāsu sthalīṣu mṛgayām iti ||
children.translated_text: and let us sport in charming places and hunt."

children.text: tac ca me gomukhenoktaṃ praviṣṭaṃ hṛdayaṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: And because that speech spoken to me by <s>Gomukha</s> entered my heart,

children.text: yuktasac cānukūlaṃ ca vacaḥ kasmai na rocate ||
children.translated_text: for whom is a speech that is both reasonable and favorable not pleasing?

children.text: punaś ca gomukhenoktaṃ yātrāṃ lokasya gacchataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gomukha</s> then said again, "The festival procession of the people as they go
should be viewed after ascending to the palace terrace."
Then I ascended the palace, whose towers touched the clouds, whose flag-brilliance pressed upon the rainbow,
and whose splendor was noble, like the moon mounting the royal peak of the eastern mountain.
There I saw the people going out through the city gates,
adorned with varied ornaments and refinements, like speech from the mouth of a poet.
There, with horses, chariots, elephants, female elephants, palanquins, and the like,
even the retinue of householders went forth without lacking adornment.
As I was looking on in this way, I saw <s>Rumaṇvān</s>, mounted on a female elephant,
going out, accompanied by attendants dressed as noblemen.
After him came the harem, occupying a group of trained elephants,
preceded by the two mothers and attended by chamberlains and the rest.
And together with a makara-banner bearing a fluttering red pennant,
came a troupe of courtesans, drawing to themselves the minds of intoxicated people.

children.text: atha māṃ gomukho 'vocad aryaputra kim āsyate
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gomukha</s> said to me, "Your Highness, why sit still?

children.text: ayaṃ vaḥ samayo gantum ity athāham avātaram ||
children.translated_text: This is the proper time for you to go." Then I descended,
and, with my friends, mounted a chariot like a moving peak of <s>Meru</s>.
The road was filled with the sound of auspicious drums, mṛdaṅgas, and other instruments as I moved along.
With the piercing neighs of horses and the deep trumpeting of elephants,
it expanded like the roar of a mass of peacocks and clouds.
After crossing the royal road, whose girdle of market-stalls was crushed by the press of people,
I went to the royal gate.
There the king, standing at <s>Suyāmuna</s>, urged me, who stood there, by a gesture of permission,
waving his hand as if to say, "Go, go."

children.text: ahaṃ tu taṃ namaskṛtya harṣam asyābhivardhayan
children.translated_text: But I bowed to him, increasing his delight,
and set out while bands of bards raised cries of victory.
Then, going out through the eastern gate, wishing to see the abundance of people,
I took the royal road and began to go toward my residence.
Then I saw a carriage drawn by eight young bulls, bright as the moon and marked with saffron handprints,
with golden fittings,
wrapped in white cloth like a mansion bathed in moonlight,
moving slowly and coming near.
There, half hidden by the covering of the carriage, I saw a face
shining like snow, as if half blocked by a cloud.
Two soft coppery fingers were placed on the edge of the forehead,
and the joined hands were formed like a lovely lotus bud.
Since I was ignorant of the knowledge of love's courtesies,

children.text: na jānāmi sma kenāpi taṃ baddhaṃ vandanāñjalim ||
children.translated_text: I did not understand why that saluting añjali had been made.

children.text: atha māṃ gomukho 'vocat srastena mukuṭena vaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gomukha</s> said to me, "Your forehead is covered by your slipped crown;

children.text: lalāṭam āvṛtaṃ tena tat samādhīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore set it right."
Then, when I touched the edge of my forehead with my right hand,

children.text: yāne kanyābhir unmuktas tasmin kalakalaḥ paṭuḥ ||
children.translated_text: a loud outcry was let loose by the maidens in that carriage.
Turning his face aside, while the shaking of his side betrayed him,
<s>Gomukha</s> at once introduced another topic, hiding a smile.
Looking at the pleasure grounds built by <s>Rumaṇvat</s>,
we approached the <s>Kālindī</s>, crowded without a gap by people crossing over.

children.text: yat tat pravahaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ ca tan mayā
children.translated_text: That carriage which I had seen before, I saw again
being respectfully ferried across the <s>Yamunā</s> by <s>Rumaṇvat</s>.
The same man, encouraging the boatman and saying, "May the journey be successful,"
as he moved from boat to boat, had us too ferried across.
After happily spending the night in a pleasure house set up on the riverbank,

children.text: sthitvā krīḍāgṛhe rātrim utthitāḥ prasthitās tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: with all provisions arranged, we rose and departed from there.
Having gone no very great distance, and with difficulty finding space on the road,
we reached the garden of <s>Nāgavana</s>, whose beauty put <s>Nandana</s> to shame.
Watching the procession, full of endless successive happenings,
I went on, greatly delighted by the pleasant amusements and pointed out by the people's fingers.

children.text: senāpatis tu māṃ nītvā prāṃśu kāñcanatoraṇam
children.translated_text: Then the commander led me to a tall golden gateway
and lodged me in a festival house furnished with many kinds of amusements.
There, together with my circle of friends, performing activities such as play, bathing, and eating,

children.text: kriyāḥ kurvan nayāmi sma netronmeṣasamaṃ divam ||
children.translated_text: I passed the day as if it were the opening of an eye.
Then at evening the general came and said to us,

children.text: śvaḥ saṃpādayitā krīḍā yā vaḥ sā kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Tell me what amusement is to be prepared for you tomorrow."
When I replied, "Hunting," and the commander had gone away,
we passed the night and in the morning set out for the forest.
Other city youths too, pleased after receiving my permission,
went in groups, mounted on female elephants, camels, horses, and the like.
Then, ahead of us in an opening of the forest, I saw a Pulinda force too numerous to count,
like a forest of burnt stumps.
From it came forth a stout-bodied, short, copper-eyed commander,
<s>Siṃhaśatru</s>, and he bowed to the commander.
The latter said, "How is my brother's wife <s>Cintyamekhalā</s>?

children.text: tau vā śāmbarasāraṅgau putrau kuśalināv iti ||
children.translated_text: And are the two sons, <s>Śāmbara</s> and <s>Sāraṅga</s>, well?"

children.text: siṃhaśatrur avocat taṃ śivaṃ naḥ sakale kule
children.translated_text: <s>Siṃhaśatru</s> said to him, "All is well in our whole family.

children.text: yadarthaṃ vayam āhūtās tat samājñāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Let the purpose for which we have been summoned be commanded."

children.text: rumaṇvān abravīd eṣa kumāraḥ sasuhṛt tava
children.translated_text: <s>Rumaṇvān</s> said, "This prince, together with his friends, is your trust;

children.text: nyāsas tena sasainyena prayatnāt pālyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore he must be carefully protected by you with your army."
<s>Rumaṇvān</s> had heaps of blue, yellow, and saffron garments given,
and also a thousand jars of oil, to <s>Siṃhaśatru</s>.
When <s>Rumaṇvat</s>, having arranged careful protection for me and taken leave,
had gone back, <s>Gomukha</s> said, "Ah, your father has arranged this splendidly.
He understood our intention, namely that we would not turn back;
otherwise this would have become a harsh confinement in a prince's enclosure.
Then, by many methods of hunting, beginning with enclosure-hunting,

children.text: nighnanto ghātayantaś ca na tṛptim alabhāmahi ||
children.translated_text: we killed animals and had them killed, yet we did not gain satisfaction.
Then <s>Marubhūtika</s> sent to <s>Yama</s> a buffalo, lord of the wilds,
hostile to horses and elephants.
After that, deer with limbs variegated like jewel-bubbles

children.text: carantaḥ saṃcarantaś ca tatra vātamajā mṛgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: were seen there in herds, roaming and moving about, swift-born as if from the wind.
<s>Hariśikha</s> and the others showed eagerness for a long time to kill them,
but, their courage broken, turned back like cowards from heroes.

children.text: tais tu senāpatiḥ pṛṣṭo na dṛṣṭāḥ kaiścid īdṛśāḥ
children.translated_text: Then they asked the commander, "Such deer have not been seen by anyone.

children.text: mṛgā yadi ca jānāsi tato naḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: If you know about them, tell us."

children.text: tenoktam aham apy etān na jānāmi pitā tu me
children.translated_text: He said, "I too do not know them; but my father once

children.text: prastāve kvacid ācaṣṭa yāṃ vārttāṃ kathayāmi tām ||
children.translated_text: told a story on some occasion, and I shall tell that story.

children.text: utpadyate yadā loke cakravartī tadā kila
children.translated_text: When a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal emperor) is born in the world, then, they say,
Such kinds of deer are seen, having just such form and speed.
They cannot be reached even by the arrow of <s>Īśvara</s>,
which burned <s>Tripura</s> as its fuel; how much less by other arrows?

children.text: etān pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yena kṣiptaḥ śaraḥ kila
children.translated_text: Know that man to be a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal ruler), it is said,

children.text: tūṇam āyāti tasyaiva vitta taṃ cakravartinam ||
children.translated_text: whose arrow, once shot, circles around these deer and comes back to his very quiver.

children.text: tān ahaṃ baddhasaṃrambhaḥ prasthitaś ca vihiṃsitum
children.translated_text: I, my fury fastened upon them, set out to kill them,

children.text: te ca māṃ dūram ākṛṣya divaṃ haṃsā ivāsthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: but they drew me far away and then took to the sky like geese.
Then I dismounted from my horse, overcome by great fatigue,
and took shelter in the shade of trees on the bank of a lovely lake.
After searching for me a long time by the track of my horse's hooves,
<s>Hariśikha</s> and the others arrived, with the army following their path.

children.text: tataḥ kurvan parīhāsaṃ mām abhāṣata gomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gomukha</s>, making a joke, said to me,
"How many wind-deer have been killed by Your Highness?"

children.text: mayoktaṃ na mayaiko 'pi hataḥ kṣiptas tu yaḥ śaraḥ
children.translated_text: I said, "Not even one has been killed by me; but the arrow that was shot

children.text: pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sa tān eṣa tūṇaṃ mamāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: circled around them and has come back here to my quiver."
Then he said, "This king of arrows deserves worship,
for it is foremost among the clear signs of a <s>cakravartin</s>."

children.text: siṃhaśatrur atha tāmiṣuṃ mudā gomukhādibhir apūjayat saha
children.translated_text: Then <s>Siṃhaśatru</s>, together with <s>Gomukha</s> and the others, joyfully worshipped that arrow,
as though it were <s>Ambikā</s> granting the desired boon, in the delight born from the slaying of <s>Siddhasārtha</s>.
After that <s>Gomukha</s> began to cut a lotus leaf with his nails,
showing the skill used on the cheek-surfaces of women blinded with passion.
Then that leaf-cutting of his, on the moving water of the river,
seemed to become alive, because it was moved by the swift current.
As we praised <s>Gomukha</s> while it glided along with the current,
we saw the leaf-cut design, with its separate parts intermingled.
When we urged him, "Explain it in detail,"
<s>Gomukha</s> set forth the characteristics of leaf-cutting.
"Here, noble prince, leaf-cutting should be understood in brief

children.text: tryasraṃ ca caturasraṃ ca dīrghaṃ vṛttaṃ ca bhedataḥ ||
children.translated_text: as divided into triangular, square, long, and round forms.
With triangular forms one produces quadrupeds, mountains, houses, and the like;
with square forms, cities with halls, men, and so on;
with long forms, streams, rivers, roads, creepers, snakes, and the like;
with round forms, combinations of ornaments, pairs of birds, and so forth."
As <s>Gomukha</s> was speaking in this way, <s>Marubhūtika</s> came up

children.text: aho nu mahad āścaryam āryaputrety abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: and said, "Ah, noble prince, what a great wonder!"
<s>Hariśikha</s> said to him, "For people like you,
like tortoises in a well, with coarse eyes, absolutely everything is a wonder.
Saying to him, "Look, since you do not believe me," <s>Marubhūtika</s>

children.text: idam āścaryam ity uccaiḥ pulinaṃ no vyadarśayat ||
children.translated_text: showed us the sandbank, crying loudly, "This is the wonder!"
Then <s>Hariśikha</s>, after breaking into loud laughter, said,

children.text: āścaryaṃ pulinaṃ paśya namas tasmai sacakṣuṣe ||
children.translated_text: "Look at the wondrous sandbank! Homage to that keen-sighted man!
Water runs in low ground, and a sandbank is a place of sand.

children.text: āścaryaṃ yadi tan mūḍha dveṣaḥ kaḥ salile tava ||
children.translated_text: If that is a wonder, fool, what quarrel do you have with the water?"

children.text: so 'bravīt kena pulinam āścaryam iti bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: He replied, "Who said that the sandbank itself is the wonder?

children.text: puline yat tad āścaryam athavā dṛśyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: What is on the sandbank is the wonder; or rather, let it be looked at."

children.text: tenoktaṃ puline santi sikatāḥ kiṃ tad adbhutam
children.translated_text: <s>Hariśikha</s> said, "There is sand on a sandbank. What is remarkable in that?"

children.text: nety ukte tena dṛṣṭvā tu pulinaṃ gomukho 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Marubhūtika</s> said, "No," <s>Gomukha</s> looked at the sandbank and said:

children.text: mā mā bhadramukhaṃ kaścit paribhūn marubhūtikam
children.translated_text: "No, no; let no one disparage handsome-faced <s>Marubhūtika</s>.

children.text: mayā hi puline dṛṣṭaṃ saṃniviṣṭaṃ padadvayam ||
children.translated_text: For I have seen on the sandbank a pair of footprints set there.
<s>Hariśikha</s> too said, "If two footprints are a wonder,
look at this greater wonder: fourteen crores of footprints."
He replied, "There is no wonder in crores of footprints that have a connected sequence.
This pair has its sequence broken off, and therefore the two footprints are a wonder."
He said, "Suppose the rest had been wiped away by a hand?"

children.text: bhaveyur iti tenoktaṃ tataḥ syād eva vālukā ||
children.translated_text: The other replied, "Then it would surely have become loose sand."

children.text: yeyaṃ tīrataroḥ śākhā pulinaṃ yāvad āgatā
children.translated_text: "Suppose someone urbane had gone along this branch of the bank-side tree,

children.text: tayā gatvāvatīrṇaḥ syāt kaścin nāgarako yadi ||
children.translated_text: which reaches as far as the sandbank, and then had descended?
And suppose, holding onto this very branch, whose shoots hang down far,
he had gone back?" When he said this, the reply was, "The ground would be strewn with leaves."

children.text: kasya tarhīti tenokte divyasyety abravīt sa tam
children.translated_text: When he asked, "Whose footprints are they, then?" he answered, "Of a divine being."
Asked, "Of which divine being?" he indicated a <s>Vidyādhara</s>.

children.text: na spṛśanti bhuvaṃ devāḥ sthūlatvād yakṣarakṣasām
children.translated_text: "The gods do not touch the earth; because <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> are heavy,
their feet sink deep, especially on sandbanks.
Because the bodies of <s>siddhas</s>, together with sages, are emaciated by austerity,
their footprints have indistinct impressions of toes, heels, and the rest.
And in the case of other human beings, one determines by reasoning

children.text: avagāḍhaṃ bhavaty agre viparītaṃ tu yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that the front is deeply pressed down, while for women it is the reverse.

children.text: bhārākrāntaḥ sa cety ukte bhūyo hariśikho 'bravīt
children.translated_text: When it was said, "Then he was weighed down by a burden," <s>Hariśikha</s> again said,
"What burden could he have: a stone, a tree, or an enemy?"

children.text: śilāyām avagāḍhaṃ syāt parṇakīrṇaṃ ca pādape
children.translated_text: "If it were a stone, it would be deeply impressed; if a tree, the place would be scattered with leaves.
As for an enemy, he would not set an enemy down on a lovely sandbank.
Therefore his burden was a <s>Vidyādharī</s> whose magic had not yet been perfected,
for even after attaining magical accomplishment, they do not become lame in their movement.

children.text: āropitaṃ ca tenāsyā jaghanaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ bhujam
children.translated_text: And he placed her hip upon his right arm,

children.text: nimagnaṃ yena tasyedaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ kāminaḥ padam ||
children.translated_text: because of which this right foot of the lover sank down.
Do you not see the spot strewn with jasmine flowers
fallen from her head and scented with the perfume of her hair?"

children.text: ramaṇīyatarāṃ caiṣāṃ na tyakṣyati sa nimagnām
children.translated_text: and he will not abandon this more lovely woman of theirs, who has plunged in;
therefore let tracks be looked for elsewhere also by skilled men."

children.text: tataḥ paurair madīyaiś ca vicinvadbhir itas tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as my townsmen and my own men searched here and there,
the footprints of a woman and a man were seen near the water.

children.text: sahāsmābhis tam uddeśaṃ gatvā dṛṣṭvā ca gomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: Together with us <s>Gomukha</s> went to that place, and after seeing it

children.text: tena nāgarakenāpi bhāvyam ity etad uktavān ||
children.translated_text: he said, "This too must be the work of that <s>nāgaraka</s> (urbane gallant)."

children.text: kathaṃ vettheti pṛṣṭaś ca sa vihasyedam uktavān
children.translated_text: Asked, "How do you know?" he laughed and said this:

children.text: jñeyaṃ kim atra durjñānam athavā kathayāmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "What is there here that is hard to know? Or rather, I shall tell you.
Following another's mind, and restraining one's own mind:

children.text: yeyaṃ nāgarakair uktā sā nāgarakatā matā ||
children.translated_text: that which is praised by urbane men is considered <s>nāgarakatā</s> (urban gallantry).
Since this <s>nāgaraka</s> follows his beloved as she moves slowly,

children.text: ayaṃ nāgarako yasmād atikramya na gacchati ||
children.translated_text: he does not go past her and walk ahead.

children.text: idānīm eva tau yātau padavī dṛśyatām iyam
children.translated_text: The two have gone just now; look at this path.
Indeed, the grass is still bent down where their feet pressed it.
Following that fresh line of footprints,
we saw a <s>saptaparṇa</s> tree where a festival of bees had begun.
At its root, whatever had happened between the two as they sported in secret,
<s>Gomukha</s> described as though he had done it himself.

children.text: iha sā kupitā tasmai tena ceha prasāditā
children.translated_text: "Here she became angry with him, and here she was appeased by him.
Here a bed of flowers and young shoots was spread.

children.text: śrāntā cātropaviṣṭā sā tathā cedaṃ nirūpyatām
children.translated_text: Tired, she sat down here; and this should be examined:
the seat has its leaves crushed by the pressure of her hips.
Here, placing her hands on her hips and bending her heavy buttocks,
as she stretched herself, the ground sank under the tips of her feet.
Examining in this way, from beneath the <s>saptaparṇa</s>
we followed the trail of the two footprints as it went out.
Then we saw a bower of <s>mādhavī</s> creepers, inaccessible to moon, sun, fire, and wind,
a dwelling not barred to lovers.
It was continuously embraced by a flowering dark creeper,
stripped by bees whose intoxication had arisen from drinking <s>vāruṇī</s> wine.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca gomukhenoktam atraivāste sa kāmukaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing it, <s>Gomukha</s> said, "The lover is staying right here.

children.text: pracchannaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ ca na hīdaṃ tyāgam arhati ||
children.translated_text: Since this place is hidden and charming, it does not deserve to be abandoned.

children.text: na cāpi darśanaṃ yuktam āsīnasya yathāsukham
children.translated_text: But it is not proper to look at him while he sits at ease.

children.text: tasmān muhūrtam anyatra kvacid viśramyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore let us rest somewhere else for a moment."
Then we stood at the foot of a branching banyan,

children.text: chāyayā ca palāśānām atiṣṭhāma tale tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose root was dark and cool with <s>dūrvā</s> grass, and in the shade of <s>palāśa</s> trees.

children.text: gomukhas tu tad ālokya latāgṛhakam unmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Gomukha</s>, looking toward that little creeper-house,

children.text: nāsty asāv atra kāmīti saśiraḥkampam uktavān ||
children.translated_text: said with a shake of his head, "That lover is not here."
Then <s>Hariśikha</s> said, "Before you say, 'He is here,'
and now again, 'He is not here.' You are altogether mad."
He answered, "Why, dumb and blind man, do you not see

children.text: śikhaṇḍimithunaṃ kasmān mūkam andha na paśyasi ||
children.translated_text: this frightened pair of peacocks that has come out of the <s>mādhavī</s>-house?

children.text: yadi kaścid bhaved atra trastam etat tatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: If anyone were here, then that frightened pair
would fly up, uttering distressed cries, and enter the fortress of trees."
Then I sent the attendants off to search.

children.text: calayantas tu hastāṃs te śūnyam ākhyaṃl latāgṛham ||
children.translated_text: Moving their hands about, they reported that the creeper-house was empty.

children.text: svayaṃ tatrāpy apaśyāma racitaṃ prastaraṃ mahat
children.translated_text: There too we ourselves saw a large couch laid out,
with scattered leaves spread about as if young lovers had rolled on them.
Caught on branches of trees were a necklace, anklets, and a girdle,
and here and there fine linen red like lotus petals.
Somewhere there was also a <s>Vidyādhara</s>'s treasure, gleaming like a fallen sun:
a jeweled cuirass whose flashing gem-light made the eyes contract.

children.text: sarvaṃ tad grāhayāmi sma puruṣair bhūṣaṇādikam
children.translated_text: I had my men collect all that, the ornaments and the rest,
thinking, "When he is found, I shall return it to him." Then <s>Gomukha</s>

children.text: abravīd vairiṇā nūnaṃ sa nītaḥ saha kāntayā
children.translated_text: said, "Surely he has been carried off by an enemy, together with his beloved.
For these ornaments and the rest were abandoned by those two, since they were helpless.

children.text: dīrghāyuṣkaṃ ca taṃ vitta snigdhās tasya śiroruhāḥ
children.translated_text: Know that he is long-lived: his glossy hairs,
still fragrant even now, cling to a branch of a tree."
As we examined in this way and cast our eyes all around,
after going no great distance, somewhere in the forest, on a very tall tree,
we saw a <s>Vidyādhara</s> fastened to the trunk of a <s>kadamba</s>
by five iron spikes, immovable like a <s>Vidyādhara</s> mountain.

children.text: athāvatāryatām eṣa skandhād ity abhidhāya tān
children.translated_text: Then, saying to them, "Let this man be taken down from the trunk,"

children.text: apasṛtya tataś chāyām āśrayāmi sma śākhinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I withdrew from there and took shelter in the shade of a tree.

children.text: gomukhas tv abravīn naite kenacil lohaśaṅkavaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Gomukha</s> said, "These iron spikes

children.text: śakyāḥ kraṣṭum upāyena sarvair api surair iti ||
children.translated_text: cannot be pulled out by any means, even by all the gods.

children.text: athāham abruvaṃ smṛtvā rājājalpan mayā śrutam
children.translated_text: Then I said, remembering what I had heard while the king was speaking:

children.text: etā oṣadhayaḥ pañca sadāsthāḥ kila varmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: "Those five herbs, it is said, always remain in the cuirass.
One is <s>viśalyakaraṇī</s> (extractor of darts), another <s>māṃsavivardhanī</s> (flesh-restorer),
another <s>vraṇasaṃrohiṇī</s> (wound-closer), and another <s>varṇaprasādanī</s> (restorer of complexion).
The fifth among them is <s>mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s> (reviver of the dead), the supreme herb.

children.text: yadi varmaṇi tāḥ santi tābhiḥ saṃjīvyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: If those are in the cuirass, let him be revived by them."
After what seemed a moment, <s>Gomukha</s> came back astonished and said,
"By the grace of Your Highness, the sky-roamer has been brought back to life.

children.text: tā mahauṣadhayo dṛṣṭā nihitās tasya varmaṇi
children.translated_text: Those great herbs were found placed in his cuirass,

children.text: śalyaprote ca hariṇe prayuktāḥ kramaśas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then they were applied in order to a deer pierced by a dart.
When their power had been seen there, that handsome <s>Vidyādhara</s>
His damaged body was at once made whole; having regained composure, he said:

children.text: jīvitaḥ kena baddho 'ham ity athāhaṃ tam uktavān
children.translated_text: "By whom have I been kept alive, and to whom am I bound?" Then I said to him:
"By our noble prince, through four procedures."

children.text: tenoktaṃ kiṃ ca yuṣmākam aryaputro 'pi vidyate
children.translated_text: Then he said, "And does such a noble prince exist among you?"

children.text: āmeti ca mayā prokte tenoktaṃ na sa mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When I answered, "Yes," he said, "He is no human being.
Our noble prince too must be a god, or else a <s>vidyādhara</s> (sky-roaming magical being).

children.text: prasīdantu tam ākhyāta prasādaṃ cakṣuṣām iti ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious and tell me who he is, as a favor to my eyes."
I said, "We were instructed by the noble prince as follows:

children.text: jīvayitvābhyanujñeyo mā sma paśyat sa mām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'After he has been revived, he is to be dismissed; let him not see me.'

children.text: kṛtopakāras tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ nāyam icchati lajjayā
children.translated_text: Out of shame, this man whom he has helped does not wish to see you.
Come for another meeting later, dear sir; for now, depart."
Then, his hands hanging loose, after falling to his knees in homage,
and sighing, he spoke in a voice choked with distress:
"Now I am as good as truly dead, since I do not see
the master who bestowed life on me, the future <s>cakravartin</s> (universal emperor).

children.text: pradāya yadi me prāṇān paścāt tāpena khedyate
children.translated_text: If, after giving me my life, he is pained afterward by regret,

children.text: evaṃ muñcāmi bhūyas tān na cet paśyatu mām iti ||
children.translated_text: then I will give those lives up again; if not, let him see me."

children.text: mayā datte 'bhyanujñāne paśyatv evaṃ karotv iti
children.translated_text: When I gave permission, saying, "Let him see me; let him do so,"

children.text: gāṃ spṛśañ jānuśirasā sa mām idam abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: he touched the ground with knee and head and said this to me:
"The <s>vidyādhara</s> <s>Amṛtagati</s>, son of the sage <s>Kauśika</s>,
bows down and asks to be seen by the lord of all <s>vidyādhara</s>s."

children.text: ehīha ca mayāhūya spṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭhe nirāmayaḥ
children.translated_text: I called him here, touched him on the back now that he was free of injury,

children.text: suhṛddṛṣṭyā ca dṛṣṭaḥ san prahṛṣṭaḥ samupāviśat ||
children.translated_text: and looked at him with a friend's gaze; delighted, he sat down.
Then <s>Hariśikha</s> said, "What <s>Vṛṣasuta</s> said

children.text: satyaṃ tat priyasaṃbhāṣo mahānāgarako hy ayam ||
children.translated_text: is true: this man is pleasant in conversation and truly urbane."
Hearing this, <s>Amṛtagati</s> said this to us:

children.text: nedaṃ nāgarakatvaṃ me śrūyatāṃ ca kathā yathā ||
children.translated_text: "This is not urbanity on my part; hear my story as it happened.
On a mind- and eye-delighting peak of the Snow Mountain
there is a sage named <s>Kauśika</s>, to whom stone and gold are equal.
An apsaras named <s>Bindumatī</s>, abandoning the Nandana grove,
worshiped him diligently for a very long time.
One day <s>Kauśika</s> said to her, 'Choose a boon,' and she replied,

children.text: yadi me bhagavān prītaḥ tato 'patyaṃ dadātv iti ||
children.translated_text: 'If the blessed lord is pleased with me, then let him give me offspring.'
He then produced in her, in due order, a pair of children:

children.text: ahaṃ ca putraḥ putrī ca matsvasā matsanāmikā ||
children.translated_text: I was the son, and there was also a daughter, my sister, bearing my name.

children.text: so 'haṃ saṃvardhitas tena nāsti tad yan na śikṣitam
children.translated_text: Raised by him, I learned everything there was to learn,
and I possess those magical sciences; through them I became a <s>vidyādhara</s>.

children.text: ekadā pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā rudantam aham abruvam
children.translated_text: Once, seeing my father weeping, I said,

children.text: mādṛśaṃ putram utpādya kiṃ roditi bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Having produced a son like me, why do you weep?'

children.text: tenoktaṃ cakravartitvaṃ na te paśyāmi putraka
children.translated_text: He said, 'I do not see <s>cakravartin</s>-ship for you, my son.

children.text: aṅgād aṅgān madīyāt tu vṛthā jāto bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: Born from limb after limb of mine, you have come into being in vain.'

children.text: mayoktaṃ mama yaḥ svāmī sa mahyaṃ kathyatām iti
children.translated_text: I said, 'Tell me who my master is.'

children.text: tenoktaṃ cakravartī yaḥ sa cāpy anviṣyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'The one who is <s>cakravartin</s> must be sought out.'
I said, 'By what signs is <s>cakravartin</s>-ship recognized?

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tāni dhiyā mahyam ācaṣṭāṃ bhagavān iti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing those signs with insight, let the blessed one tell me.'

children.text: tenoktaṃ śatruṇā baddhaṃ yas tvāṃ śaṅkubhir āyasaiḥ
children.translated_text: He said, 'The one who will revive you when an enemy has bound you

children.text: jīvayiṣyati jānīyāt svāminaṃ taṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: with iron stakes: know him to be your master.'

children.text: mama tv aṅgārako nāma vyālakaś cābhavat suhṛt
children.translated_text: Now I had two friends, one named <s>Aṅgāraka</s> and one named <s>Vyālaka</s>.

children.text: saudaryo gamayāmi sma tābhyāṃ kālaṃ sukhaṃ saha ||
children.translated_text: I used to pass the time happily in their company.

children.text: atha vāyupatho nāma rājā tena sahāgamam
children.translated_text: Then, together with a king named <s>Vāyupatha</s>, I went
to a city named <s>Kāśyapasthalaka</s>, captivating to the mind.
There one day, as I was wandering in a pleasure grove,
I saw a maiden named <s>Kusumālikā</s>, surrounded by a retinue of girls.

children.text: praśasyavarṇasaṃsthānā sā me buddhau sthirā sthitā
children.translated_text: Her complexion and form were worthy of praise; she remained fixed in my mind
like a royal inscription set on a wall of Vindhya stone.

children.text: tām ādāya tayā sārdhaṃ suhṛdbhyāṃ ca manoharāḥ
children.translated_text: Taking her with me, and together with her and my two friends,
I wandered for pleasure through lovely rivers, mountains, trees, and open places.
Then I saw <s>Aṅgāraka</s> looking at <s>Kusumālikā</s>,
his neck bent in a sidelong glance caused by passion, shame, and fear.
Perceiving, 'He has been noticed by me,' he and his younger brother,

children.text: anāmantryaiva māṃ nīco nīcair utthāya yātavān ||
children.translated_text: the low fellow, rose quietly and went away without even taking leave of me.

children.text: ahaṃ tu jātavailakṣyāt saṃraktāc ca tatas trasan
children.translated_text: Because embarrassment had arisen, and because I was afraid of that passionate man,

children.text: na jānāmi kva yāmīti cakitaḥ saha kāntayā ||
children.translated_text: I was alarmed and did not know where to go with my beloved.
Today, reaching this lovely river from the mountain,
I descended on its bank, where the sand was soft and clean.

children.text: suratānubhave yogyaṃ dṛṣṭvā tac ca susaṃvṛtam
children.translated_text: Seeing there a well-hidden bower fit for the enjoyment of love,
I entered the creeper-house, covered with dark flowering vines.

children.text: yac ca śeṣam aśeṣaṃ tat kathitaṃ gomukhena vaḥ
children.translated_text: All the rest, without omission, has been told to you by <s>Gomukha</s>.
Therefore this was reliable instruction, not clever urbanity on my part.
For what commander who was not a <s>vidyādhara</s> could free
a man like me, bound by <s>vidyādhara</s>s? Thus the seer's word was true.
Servants serve those who are to be served with wisdom, life, wealth, and the like.
Therefore, by whatever means, accept my magical knowledge for the protection of myself."
Since I had just done him a kindness, and since I had little eagerness for it,

children.text: na gṛhītābruvaṃ cainam anugaccha priyām iti ||
children.translated_text: I did not accept it; I said to him, "Go after your beloved."

children.text: abravīc ca dinād asmāt pareṇāham aharniśam
children.translated_text: And he said, "From this day onward, day and night,
I will be vigilant in protecting your body."

children.text: smartavyaḥ saṃkaṭe cāham ity uktvā naḥ praṇamya ca
children.translated_text: "And in danger I am to be remembered," he said; then, after bowing to us,
he rose swiftly into the sky and set out eastward toward <s>Aṅgāraka</s>.

children.text: ādityaśarmavacanaṃ vacanaṃ ca yakṣyā yānaṃ pradakṣiṇam iṣoś ca marunmṛgāṇām
children.translated_text: The words of <s>Ādityaśarman</s>, the words of the <s>Yakṣī</s>, the auspicious course of the vehicle, and the arrow of the marunmṛgas,
together with what <s>Prahlādin</s> had said about his own journey, became clear, purified by the removal of the stain of doubt.
Then, when everything had been prepared there by <s>Rumaṇvān</s>, who was stationed for the journey,
I ate a generous meal and began to go on the expedition.
Mounting a pleasant chariot yoked with noble oxen,

children.text: haṃsair iva śaśāṅkābhair vimānaṃ yādasāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of the waters seemed to mount an aerial car drawn by swans as white as the moon.
<s>Gomukha</s> took up a parasol like the unbroken disk of the moon,
and <s>Marubhūtika</s> took a yak-tail fan with a polished golden handle.
Standing at the front of the chariot, <s>Tapantaka</s> held the reins,
while <s>Hariśikha</s>, with a strung bow in his hand, stood at my side.
After eating soft grass, and after being bathed and watered,

children.text: mandam mandaṃ ca naḥ sainyaṃ syandanaṃ parito 'gamat ||
children.translated_text: the rest of our army slowly, very slowly, went around the chariot.

children.text: evaṃprāye ca vṛttānte cāmaraṃ calayan manāk
children.translated_text: When matters had proceeded in this sort of way, <s>Marubhūtika</s>, gently waving the fan,
looked at <s>Hariśikha</s> and said these words:
"Through the prince's practicing the wicked sport of hunting,

children.text: pradāya prāṇinaḥ prāṇān dharmaḥ prāpto mahān iti ||
children.translated_text: he has gained great <s>dharma</s> by granting living beings their lives."
He replied, "What is surprising here? Since you have not attended on good men,
and since your only substance is fatigue and exertion, it is just like you to say such a thing.
Among land, friends, and gold, a friend is certainly superior;
because the other two are rooted in that, therefore a friend has been acquired.

children.text: tayoḥ saṃjalpator evam ahaṃ gomukham abruvam
children.translated_text: As the two of them were talking in this way, I said to <s>Gomukha</s>,

children.text: dharmādīnāṃ pradhānaṃ yat tad ācaṣṭāṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "Please tell me which is foremost among <s>dharma</s> and the others."
He said, "Since <s>dharma</s>, friendship, and wealth have desire as their purpose,
therefore desire is foremost; and desire consists in longing and pleasure.

children.text: puline hi padaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūrvam icchā prabhor abhūt
children.translated_text: For when the footprint was first seen on the sandbank, my lord felt a longing:

children.text: yenedam iha vinyastaṃ taṃ paśyeyaṃ kathaṃ nv iti ||
children.translated_text: 'How might I see the one by whom this has been set down here?'

children.text: taṃ ca dṛṣṭvāryaputreṇa sukham āsāditaṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: And since, after seeing that person, the prince obtained pleasure,

children.text: tan na mitraṃ na dharmārthau kiṃ tu kāmo 'yam arjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is not a friend, nor <s>dharma</s> and wealth, but this desire that has been acquired.

children.text: anyo 'py asti mahākāmaḥ sa yuṣmākaṃ na gocaraḥ
children.translated_text: There is another great form of desire too, but it is not within your range.
For you are outside the class of all desirous men, like wooden mannequins.
Men have been defined by those who know the <s>kāmaśāstra</s> as fourfold:

children.text: uttamā madhyamā hīnāś caturthās tu nakecana ||
children.translated_text: superior, middling, inferior, and, fourth, those who are nobodies.

children.text: uttamo gomukhas teṣām aryaputras tu madhyamaḥ
children.translated_text: Among them <s>Gomukha</s> is superior, while the prince is middling.
I shall describe the inferior ones, but you are nobodies."
Then, laughing out of anger, <s>Marubhūtika</s> said this:
"Ah, your refinement as a city man has come to perfection, you dependent retainer.
You young bull-calf, surely you really are <s>Gomukha</s>, 'cow-faced';

children.text: ko nāma mānuṣamukhaḥ sann aśuddham udāharet ||
children.translated_text: for what man with a human face would utter something impure?

children.text: uttamo gomukhas teṣām aryaputras tu madhyamaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Among them <s>Gomukha</s> is superior, while the prince is middling'--

children.text: prabhor adhikam ātmānam itthaṃ kaḥ kathayed iti ||
children.translated_text: who would speak in this way, making himself greater than his lord?"

children.text: tenoktaṃ dṛḍhamūḍho 'si na kiṃcid api budhyase
children.translated_text: He replied, "You are thoroughly foolish; you understand nothing at all.
A man does not become a supreme lover merely because he is a lord.

children.text: yaḥ kāmyate ca kāmī ca sa pradhānam ahaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: One who is desired and himself desires is foremost, as I am.

children.text: akāmī kāmyate yas tu madhyo 'sāv aryaputravat ||
children.translated_text: But one who does not desire and yet is desired is middling, like the prince.

children.text: yas tu kāmayate kāṃcid akāmāṃ so 'dhamaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: One who desires some woman who does not desire him is considered inferior.

children.text: te nakecana bhaṇyante ye na kāmyā na kāminaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who are neither desired nor desirous are called nobodies.

children.text: itīdaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yeṣāṃ tān vijānīta kāminaḥ
children.translated_text: Know as lovers those to whom this definition applies;

children.text: nakecana bhavantas tu yena nirlakṣaṇā iti ||
children.translated_text: but you are nobodies, since you are without any defining mark."

children.text: atha cāmaram ujjhitvā sphuṭann iva kutūhalāt
children.translated_text: Then, throwing down the fan, as though bursting with curiosity,
<s>Marubhūtika</s> asked <s>Gomukha</s>, whose face was thundering:
"Where is that woman, a honey-gathering bee, who is resolved

children.text: svāmino yauvanamadhu kvāsau kathaya tām iti ||
children.translated_text: to enjoy the honey of our lord's youth? Tell us of her."
He replied, "I shall tell the prince, if he asks,

children.text: na tubhyaṃ sthalamaṇḍūka na hi bhasmani hūyate ||
children.translated_text: but not you, land-frog; for an oblation is not poured on ashes."
Then <s>Marubhūtika</s>, with joined palms and bowing low, said to me,
"Let this man of firm pride be questioned; grant this favor."

children.text: icchatāpi tam ālāpaṃ lajjāṃ bhāvayatā mayā
children.translated_text: Although I too desired that conversation, I made a show of modesty,
and, when he had said what could not be refused, I consented: "Tell it."
Then <s>Gomukha</s> wiped his eyes, dimmed with tears of joy,

children.text: saṃkāsya śuddhakaṇṭhaś ca ramyām akathayat kathām ||
children.translated_text: cleared his pure throat, and told a charming story.
"Once, when the prince had been adorned with the office of heir apparent,
I went to the king's inner apartments to pay homage to the two queens.

children.text: tatra citraṃ mayā dṛṣṭam adṛṣṭaṃ divyamānuṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: There I saw a wonder, unseen by gods and men,
which, through the purity of its arrangement of colors, was like this king's realm.

children.text: padmāvatyā ca pṛṣṭo 'haṃ kim asmin putra gomukha
children.translated_text: And <s>Padmāvatī</s> asked me, 'My son <s>Gomukha</s>, what

children.text: paśyasīti tato devi trayam ity aham uktavān ||
children.translated_text: do you see in this?' Then I said, 'Queen, three things.'

children.text: kiṃ punas trayam ity ukte devyai kathitavān aham
children.translated_text: When the queen asked, 'But what are the three?' I told her:

children.text: ṛddhiṃ vaḥ śilpināṃ śilpaṃ bahuratnāṃ ca gām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Your prosperity, the craftsmen's craft, and the earth rich in many jewels.'

children.text: atha devyā vihasyoktaṃ cetasyaḥ khalu gomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the queen laughed and said, '<s>Gomukha</s> is certainly perceptive;

children.text: acetasyo hi puruṣaḥ katham evaṃ vaded iti ||
children.translated_text: for how could an undiscerning man speak in this way?'

children.text: āsīc ca mama tac chrutvā saṃdehādhyāsitaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: When I heard that, my mind became occupied by doubt:

children.text: cetasyaḥ kiṃ nu guṇavān āhosvid doṣavān iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Does cetasya mean a man of qualities, or rather a man of faults?'"

children.text: na ca pṛṣṭā mayā devī sasaṃdehe 'pi cetasi
children.translated_text: And I did not question the queen, though my mind was full of doubt,

children.text: mā sma budhyata sā bālam acetasyaṃ ca mām iti ||
children.translated_text: thinking, "Let her not take me for a boy and an unperceptive man."

children.text: apṛṣṭaḥ ko nu kathayec cetasyam iti cintayan
children.translated_text: "Who, unasked, would tell me what 'perceptive' means?" Thinking in this way,
I wandered through the palace and went out from the royal residence.
Then I saw a chariot yoked with horses adorned with splendid fly-whisks,
Persian steeds whose hoof-falls followed one another without a gap.

children.text: rathasya prājitā tasya puruṣo māṃ vinītavat
children.translated_text: The driver of that chariot, a man, respectfully
placed his folded hands, with the goad held inside them, on his head and said:
"Prince, I have a report to make. In this royal household we
are hereditary servants, living by service with chariots and vehicles.
I have been ordered by the king that these horses, used to carrying riders,

children.text: acirād bhavatā rathyāḥ kriyantāṃ turagā iti ||
children.translated_text: should quickly be made into chariot-horses by you.
I, hurrying as best I could, have trained their shoulders according to my ability,

children.text: na tu saṃbhāvayāmy etān kuśalair aparīkṣitān ||
children.translated_text: but I do not trust them without their being tested by experts.

children.text: tad evaṃ ratham āruhya parīkṣyantām amī tvayā
children.translated_text: Therefore mount this chariot and test these horses yourself,
as treatises are tested by one skilled in words, sentences, proofs, and meanings."
Hearing this and the rest, I bent my face down for a moment,

children.text: upacāro bhaved eṣa satyam evety acintayam ||
children.translated_text: and thought, "This must indeed be a courtesy; it is true."
Then I saw a long-eared, disciplined man in a long cloak,
a clerk with an inkpot beside him and a pen tucked at his ear.

children.text: so 'bravīn mahati kleśe pātitāḥ prabhuṇā vayam
children.translated_text: He said, "Our master has thrown us into great trouble.

children.text: sarvathā dhig imāṃ kṣudrāṃ śvavṛttim anujīvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In every way, shame on this petty dog-like livelihood that we depend on!
As many excellent men on earth as are perceptive,

children.text: acetasyāś ca kartavyaṃ teṣāṃ lekhyaṃ mayā kila ||
children.translated_text: and as many as are unperceptive, I must apparently make a written record of them.

children.text: na caikam api paśyāmi yuktaṃ cetasyalakṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: I do not see even one who is fitted with the marks of the perceptive,

children.text: acetasyās tu sakalāṃ kṣobhayanti mahīm iti ||
children.translated_text: while the unperceptive are throwing the whole earth into commotion."
And there another man, holding two books in his hand,
spoke about me, in amusement, with his finger outstretched:
"Having come here, do you not see this man of noble appearance, merciless one?
He is like a penniless physician seeking a cure for his livelihood.
Let this man first be entered at the head of the book of the unperceptive,

children.text: ya evam anunīto 'pi rathaṃ nāroḍhum icchati ||
children.translated_text: since even when thus entreated he does not wish to mount the chariot.

children.text: aprārthito 'pi yaḥ kaścid ārohati sa likhyatām
children.translated_text: But anyone who mounts it even without being asked should be written
at the head of the book of the perceptive, immediately after the salutation."
Then, out of greed for perceptiveness, I leapt far up at once,

children.text: mā smānyaḥ kaścid ārohad ity āroham ahaṃ rathaṃ ||
children.translated_text: and mounted the chariot, thinking, "Let no one else mount it first!"

children.text: tena vegavatā gacchann apaśyaṃ gajam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: As I went along in it swiftly, I saw an elephant ahead,
being made comfortable by the sweet words of its attendants.
The chariot-driver stopped the chariot and said to the elephant-rider,

children.text: anyato naya mātaṅgaṃ mā cetasyarathaṃ rudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Lead the elephant elsewhere; do not block the chariot of a perceptive man."
He replied, "Let the chariot occupied by a perceptive man go elsewhere.

children.text: vihantum aham etasya necchām icchāmi dantinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I do not wish to obstruct this tusker's desire.
Although its rut has not yet begun, its rut is brought on by soothing words

children.text: icchāyāś cāvighātena tena naḥ kṣamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and by not thwarting its wish; therefore excuse us."

children.text: avocam atha yantāraṃ na nāma yadi necchati
children.translated_text: Then I said to the driver, "No indeed; if the elephant-keeper does not wish it,
let the chariot be sent off by another road."

children.text: evaṃ nāmeti coktvā saḥ parivartitavān ratham
children.translated_text: Saying, "So be it," he turned the chariot around,
and added, "I shall take you through the middle of the abode of the perceptive."

children.text: āsīc ca mama dīrghāyur ayaṃ bhavatu kuñjaraḥ
children.translated_text: And I thought, "Long life to this elephant,

children.text: rundhatā yena me mārgaṃ cetasyā darśitā iti ||
children.translated_text: by which, in blocking my road, the perceptive people have been shown to me."
And I saw a merchants' street, its ground a broad pavement of stone slabs,
where most of the wares were garlands, ornaments, incense, and the like.
Passing beyond it, I saw lovely rows of mansions with charming fronts and gardens,
as though the thoughts of architects had been set down in bodily form.
In one place were proud women, wanton and behaving boldly,
serving just such men, intoxicated and turned away.
In another place a young man was following behind and coaxing a young woman,
while she rebuked him with words sweet and harsh at once:

children.text: ayi ballavakāpehi kiṃ mā chupasi durbhagām
children.translated_text: "Ah, little lover, go away. Why do you touch unlucky me,
touched by many little lovers, a lover-girl touched by lovers?"
In one place I saw one woman moving a vīṇā with gracefully bent fingers,
and another making a parivādinī lute ring by the touch of a plectrum.
Thus, as I rode about in the softly moving chariot,

children.text: paṭhantīḥ paṭṭikā vyagrāḥ paśyāmi sma kumārikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I saw girls, intent upon their tablets, reciting.

children.text: kaḥ punaḥ syād ayaṃ grantha iti śrotuṃ mayecchatā
children.translated_text: Wishing to hear what sort of treatise this might be,
I sent my ear toward them from a distance and heard clearly:

children.text: sametya pūrvaṃ na svapyāt suptaṃ ca na parityajet
children.translated_text: "After meeting first, one should not sleep; and when he has fallen asleep, one should not leave him.

children.text: prāṇāpānau ca yatnena samaṃ saṃdhārayed iti ||
children.translated_text: With care one should hold <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, the vital breaths, evenly."

children.text: āsīc ca mama kā etā viṭaśāstram adhīyate
children.translated_text: And I thought, "Who are these girls studying a libertine's manual?
I think the charioteer has tricked me into entering a brothel-quarter."
And another man, walking clockwise around a temple of <s>Kāmadeva</s>,
said, "I am successful; now I shall obtain sleep.

children.text: yo 'sau vinayagarveṇa duḥkham āste sa gomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>Gomukha</s>, who sits in misery because of his proud modesty,

children.text: avandhyaṃ yauvanaṃ kartum eṣa veśaṃ vigāhate ||
children.translated_text: is entering the brothel-quarter to make his youth not barren."
Then I said to the driver, "What has been done is improper.

children.text: adhunā tu rathaḥ kṣipraṃ pratīpaṃ nīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Now let the chariot be driven back quickly."

children.text: tenoktaṃ mā trasīr veśān nedaṃ mātaṅgapakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: He said, "Do not be afraid of brothel-quarters; this is not an elephant-pen.

children.text: na ca darśanamātreṇa kaścid bhavati doṣavān ||
children.translated_text: And no one becomes blameworthy merely by seeing.

children.text: atītaś ca mahān adhvā śiṣyate stokam antaram
children.translated_text: A long road had already been passed, and only a small interval remained.

children.text: rathaḥ kiṃ pṛṣṭhato yātu kiṃ puraḥ preryatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Should the chariot go behind, or should it be driven in front?"

children.text: mayā tu pura ity ukte tvaritaḥ sārathī ratham
children.translated_text: But when I said, "In front," the charioteer quickly
drove the chariot forward, and there I saw a mansion lofty as <s>Mandara</s>.
It had the appearance of a royal inner apartment, with its gateway occupied by doorkeepers,
filled chiefly with excellent young women and crowded with well-trained attendants.
From it maidens came out, adorned with lovely necklaces and other ornaments;
their radiance outshone lotuses, and they stood surrounding the chariot.
One of them, mature in bearing, with joined palms placed upon her head,
said to me, "Prince, there is a message: please come, she says."

children.text: mama tvāsīd aho śaktir bata puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then I thought, "Ah, what power belongs to meritorious action!

children.text: jagataḥ prabhur apy eṣā yena praiṣyeva bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: For by it even this mistress of the world speaks like a servant girl.
Enough of unconscious merits; let that word 'she says' disappear,

children.text: yaiḥ kṛtā paratantreyaṃ lakṣmīr yena ca sūcitā ||
children.translated_text: for by them this <s>Lakṣmī</s> has been made dependent, and by that word it has been shown."

children.text: kiṃ tu yāni na yānīti saṃśayāne kṣaṇaṃ mayi
children.translated_text: But while I hesitated for a moment, wondering, "Should I go or should I not go?"
those women looked back with lotus-faces faded by dejection.

children.text: anuyātā ca taddṛṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭam udghāṭitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: Following their glance, I saw, opened before me,
a window whose shutters were bright with rays from lattices of jewels.
Through it moved three fans, carrying the course of love's adornment,
their handles held by wandering hands, tawny with clusters of fingers.
Between the moving fans was hidden a face with its neck lifted high,
like a lotus on a raised stalk standing in a gap among the waves of a lake.

children.text: cañcat pradeśinīkaṃ ca pāṇim uccaiḥ prasāritam
children.translated_text: And a hand, with its forefinger trembling, was stretched high upward,
like a tender coral shoot reached by a gentle breeze.
Without even considering, "Who is this calling me?"

children.text: bhuvam āgatam ātmānam āśu cetitavān aham ||
children.translated_text: I quickly realized that I had come down from the carriage to the ground.
And the charioteer said to me, "Let the loving person
make her affection fruitful; therefore, prince, please enter.

children.text: yāvatīṃ ca bhavān velām ihāste tāvatīm aham
children.translated_text: For as long as your honor remains here, for that same length of time I
will stay, resting the draft-horses, which have become extremely weary."

children.text: gaṇikābhis tv ahaṃ tābhir āraṇyaka iva dvipaḥ
children.translated_text: Then those courtesans led me, like a forest elephant,

children.text: vārīm iva dṛḍhadvārām ādyāṃ kakṣyāṃ praveśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: into the first court, whose doors were firm as though they were waters.
There I saw a nāga maiden, accompanied by excellent attendants in places such as lotus pools,
being instructed in discipline.
But in the second court I saw a sedan chair of auspicious form,
with sedan-bearers and vehicles that proclaimed the skill of craftsmen.
In the third court I saw horses from many countries, good carriers,
with hosts of excellent marks and garlands of jingling ornaments.
In the fourth court there was a circle of cages for birds:
crying peacocks, partridges, parrots, mynahs, sarasa cranes, and flocks of cocks.
Beyond that were things of many shapes, fashioned by craftsmen
skilled in artistic arrangement, made of gold, silver, and copper.
In the sixth court, objects made fragrant with incense, unguents, and perfumes
were being prepared here and there by experts in the science of scents.
In the seventh court garments were being made with dyes, fumigation, and fresh fragrance,
including silk cloth, fine silk, dukūla linen, and the like.
In the eighth court I saw the treatments of jewels and pearls,
whose scattered brilliance was abundant: polishing, drilling, and other processes.

children.text: aṣṭasv api ca kakṣyāsu mahāmātrādayaś ciram
children.translated_text: And in all eight courts, ministers and others,

children.text: svakauśalāni śaṃsanto vighnanti sma gatiṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: continually proclaiming their own skills, kept obstructing my progress for a long time.
Again and again those maidens, adorned with beautiful forms, came up
and said, "Because of the worth of your work, you people are foolish.
This prince is entering for some purpose;
why is he being detained by unlucky men telling of their own crafts?"
Then women wearing golden earrings, with white garments and hair,
addressed me, offering an arghya of jewels and flowers:
"By one long-lived and akin to the wish-fulfilling jewel,

children.text: alaṃkṛtaṃ ca guptaṃ ca gamitaṃ ca pavitratām ||
children.translated_text: this house has been adorned, protected, and brought to purity.
Therefore, joining with intelligent people, become the leader of the intelligent;
for the virtues of the virtuous arise from association with the virtuous."
Then, with a retinue of groups of maidens, I reached a flight of stairs
from which the darkness had been dispelled by the brilliance of sun-stones.
After ascending the palace by it, I fixed my gaze on a painting,

children.text: prasupta iva saṃsāre citre dṛṣṭiṃ nyaveśayam ||
children.translated_text: as though on a world asleep and devoid of the stir of speech.

children.text: kalābhir atha citrābhir buddhiṃ sarvavidām iva
