children.translated_text: Then, among maidens, I saw a maiden whose form was an abode of immeasurable qualities,
like the intellect of those who know everything, surrounded by manifold arts.
Let inference, comparison, and verbal testimony remain far away;
even by direct perception her beauty is hard for observers to determine.
For after the eye has looked upon her, with consciousness stolen by fainting,
what does a stone-man in bodily form actually see?

children.text: neśvareṇa ca dharmeṇa na pradhānena nāṇubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Such a shape could not easily have been made by <s>Īśvara</s>, by <s>dharma</s>,
by <s>pradhāna</s>, by atoms, or by time, inherent nature, and the rest.
Enough of speaking about her beauty, and of the long account of her qualities.
You yourselves will consider her qualities and beauty.
So, in order to bow to her, with joined palms placed on my head,

children.text: tadrūpaṃ vismitaḥ paśyaṃs tūṣṇīm āsaṃ muhūrtakam ||
children.translated_text: I remained silent for a little while, gazing in wonder at her beauty.
She too raised her face, whose lotus-eyes were opening.

children.text: ciraṃ gomukha jīveti māṃ pūrvaṃ samabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: First she addressed me, saying, "Long may <s>Gomukha</s> live."

children.text: mama tv āsīd aho dhūrtā mugdhābhā cāpi khalv iyam
children.translated_text: But I thought, "Ah, she is a rogue, though she certainly has the appearance of an innocent girl,
and she is so free of pride, she by whom I have been asked for an appointment.

children.text: ninditā ca mayātmīyā buddhir vāk ca pramādinī
children.translated_text: And I condemned my own judgment, and my speech too, as careless.

children.text: hastau praśastau tābhyāṃ hi pūrvam eva kṛtāñjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: Only my hands were praiseworthy, for with them I had already made a respectful añjali.
On every side I was only a hand's measure, while my face and the rest were senseless;

children.text: apramattā hi jīvanti mṛtā eva pramādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the attentive live, but the careless are as good as dead."

children.text: iti cintayate mahyaṃ tayā dāpitam āsanam
children.translated_text: As I was thinking this, a seat was given to me by her,
with legs of shining ivory, and I sat down on it.

children.text: sā ha māṃ kṣaṇam āsīnam apṛcchad gomukhaḥ kutaḥ
children.translated_text: When I had sat there for a moment, she asked me, "From where
is <s>Gomukha</s> coming?" I replied, "From the royal residence."

children.text: tayoktaṃ kuśalī rājā devyau cāntaḥpurāṇi ca
children.translated_text: She said, "Is the king well, and the two queens, and the women of the inner apartments?
And are <s>Rumaṇvat</s> and the other ministers well, together with their households?"
Then, after murmuring something about "the prince," with the r-sound indistinct,

children.text: tūṣṇīṃbhūtā kṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭiṃ nāsāgre niścalām adhāt ||
children.translated_text: she became silent for a moment and fixed her gaze motionless on the tip of her nose.
When she had asked in order after the welfare of <s>Hariśikha</s> and the others,

children.text: mayā kuśalam ity uktaṃ mām apṛcchad asau punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and I had said, "They are well," she asked me again:

children.text: jānāmy eva yathā buddhiḥ sarvaiḥ sarvā sukheditā
children.translated_text: "I already know that everyone has reported every sort of welfare according to his understanding.

children.text: prakarṣo yasya yasyāṃ vo vidyāṃ kathaya tām iti ||
children.translated_text: Tell me the particular branch of learning in which each of you excels."
I said, "The noble prince is skilled in elephant-science,
and in the ocean of <s>gāndharva</s> knowledge, which ordinary men cannot enter.
<s>Hariśikha</s> excels in <s>daṇḍanīti</s> (statecraft), <s>Marubhūtika</s> in the śāstras,
and <s>Tapantaka</s> has reached mastery in the sciences of vehicles, chariots and the like.
But I, like a camel taking the tender top-shoots of śamī trees,
have grasped only desired portions of all the sciences."

children.text: sābravīd atha vidyānām āsām āsevanasya kaḥ
children.translated_text: Then she said, "What is the proper time for you

children.text: bhavatām ucitaḥ kālaḥ katamad vā vinodanam ||
children.translated_text: to cultivate these sciences, and what is your recreation?"
I replied, "At the end of the night we wake, praise the deities,
and, adorned with auspicious ornaments, afterwards study <s>itihāsa</s> (ancient narrative).
Then, when permitted by the physicians, wearing fragrant oil,
we practice mounts, wrestling, and weapons.

children.text: tataḥ snātvā ca bhuktvā ca muhūrtaṃ yāpitaśramāḥ
children.translated_text: After that, having bathed and eaten, and having passed a short time resting from fatigue,
we sit discussing treatises on polity and great poems.
Then, at the beginning of night, on a palace roof that outshines the dense moonlight,
we take our pleasure happily with lovely sounds of flute and lute."
Then, with the corner of her eye stretching as far as her ear,
she looked at a young woman sitting nearby, and then glanced toward me.
Thereupon, rising as if with difficulty, slow from the weight of her hips,

children.text: mayāsanne niviṣṭā sā manāg api na lakṣitā ||
children.translated_text: she sat down near me, but was not noticed by me in the slightest.

children.text: evam anyāpi gaṇikā tṛṇavad gaṇitā mayā
children.translated_text: Thus another courtesan too was counted by me as mere grass;
but then another arrived, a goddess of beauty made visible.

children.text: sābravīt kaṣṭam āyātam ito guru guror vacaḥ
children.translated_text: She said, "A painful situation has arisen: on this side is the word of my teacher's teacher,

children.text: itaś cātithisatkāraḥ kim atra kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and on this side the honoring of a guest. What is to be done here?"
I said, "Since teachers are weighty even for deities,

children.text: tasmād gurur guror ājñā saiva saṃpādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore the teacher's teacher's command is weightier; that alone should be fulfilled."

children.text: sābravīn na tvayotkaṇṭhā kāryā mitrāṇy apaśyatā
children.translated_text: She said, "You should not feel longing because you do not see your friends;
<s>Padmadevikā</s> will make you as if free from longing."
Guessing my intention, she said, as though embarrassed,

children.text: na yuktam ananujñātaiḥ preṣyair āsannam āsitum ||
children.translated_text: "It is not proper for servants who have not been permitted to sit close by.
But here is a couch spread out, a refuge. Let the young lord
enter and remove the fatigue caused by the jolting of the chariot."
So, at her direction, I entered and reclined
on a lovely, blossoming bed with golden and jeweled frame and cushions.

children.text: pādasthāne tataḥ sthitvā sābravīt kaḥ karotu vaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, standing at the place of my feet, she said, "Who is to perform for you
a foot-massage that those of poor merit could not hope for?"

children.text: pādasaṃvāhanaṃ kāryaṃ bhadraṃ syād yena kenacit
children.translated_text: I said, "A foot-massage may be done by anyone at all
by whom there would be benefit. What need is there here for a special masseuse?"

children.text: tayā tv ālambite pāde pāṇibhyām abhavan mama
children.translated_text: But when she took hold of my feet with her hands, I thought,
"By whom has this poison-maiden been set upon me, though I am blameless?

children.text: karaṇāny asvatantrāṇi na jāne kīdṛśaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: My senses are not under my control; I do not know what sort of mind I have.

children.text: viceṣṭāni ca me 'ṅgāni dhig anāryām imām iti ||
children.translated_text: My limbs are behaving strangely. Shame on this ignoble woman!"

children.text: sā tu saṃvāhya caraṇau muhūrtam idam abravīt
children.translated_text: But after massaging my two feet for a while, she said this:

children.text: kathaṃ dāsajano vakṣaḥ śrāntaṃ vaḥ sevatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "How may the servant-folk attend to your chest, which is weary?"

children.text: mama tv āsīt pragalbheyam anācārā ca yā mama
children.translated_text: I thought, "This woman is forward and ill-behaved,
since she wishes to place upon my chest hands that have touched the soles of my feet."
Guessing my thought, she said, showing a smile,

children.text: uraḥ spṛśati vaḥ ko vā karābhyāṃ mūḍhadhīr iti ||
children.translated_text: "What fool would touch your chest with hands?"

children.text: āsīc ca mama kāpy eṣā devatā brahmavādinī
children.translated_text: And I thought, "This must be some goddess, a speaker of sacred truth,
since those who are possessed by passion do not know another's mind."
She said, "For a chest wearied by the jolting of a chariot,
there is an irreproachable massage called 'pressed by the breasts.'

children.text: yadi vāham anugrāhyā vakṣo vā prabalaśramam
children.translated_text: So if I am to be favored, or if your chest is powerfully fatigued,

children.text: tato mām anujānīta bhartṛtantrā hi yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then permit me; for women are dependent on their master."

children.text: āsīc ca mama dhīreyaṃ nirastakaruṇā ca yā
children.translated_text: And I thought, "This woman is firm and devoid of pity,

children.text: anujñāṃ labhate yāvat tāvad āste nirākulā ||
children.translated_text: for until she gets permission she remains undisturbed."

children.text: athainām abruvaṃ bāle parāyattaṃ nibodha mām
children.translated_text: Then I said to her, "Girl, understand that I am dependent on another.
Let the one who knows the science of massage proceed on her own authority."

children.text: urasā stanasāreṇa sā madīyam uras tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then she, with the firm mass of her breasts, pressed my chest with her own breast...
she began to massage me, trembling and filled with fear.
In every way, enough of this digressive story as it spreads out;
one never grows weary of a charming subject whose matter is concise.

children.text: tataḥ krīḍāgṛhāt tasmād bāhyāṃ tām eva vīthikām
children.translated_text: Then from that pleasure-house I went out to that very outer street,
and after a moment the noble lady's daughter came to that very place.

children.text: vanditvā prasthitaṃ sā māṃ kṣaṇam ālokya vismitā
children.translated_text: She bowed, and, as I was setting out, looked at me for a moment in astonishment;
sweet in speech, she addressed me, hiding her distress with a smile.

children.text: idaṃ bhavanam ātmīyaṃ pratyavekṣyaṃ sadā tvayā
children.translated_text: 'This house, which is your own, must always be looked after by you;
even a snake, when it is seen over time, becomes familiar.'
Then <s>Padmadevikā</s>, taking hold of the end of my garment,

children.text: vijñāpyam asti me kiṃcit tac ca nādyety abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: said, 'There is something I have to tell you, but not today.'
Then, with <s>Padmadevikā</s>, who dwelt in my heart,

children.text: tam eva ratham āruhya kumārāgāram āgamam ||
children.translated_text: I mounted that same chariot and returned to the prince's residence.

children.text: tatra yuṣmān abhuñjānān paśyāmi sma mayā vinā
children.translated_text: There I saw you eating without me,

children.text: upahāsaṃ ca kurvantaṃ taṃ tathā marubhūtikam ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Marubhūtika</s> making mockery in that way.

children.text: dine 'nyatra ca sevitvā kṣaṇaṃ yuṣmān ahaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: On another day, after spending a moment with you again,
I went to the noble lady's daughter and attended upon <s>Padmadevikā</s>.
And the noble lady's daughter said to me, 'Your friends are impatient;

children.text: vṛttānto 'yam atas teṣāṃ mā gamat karṇagocaram ||
children.translated_text: therefore this affair must not come within range of their ears.'
Then, as I was setting out, <s>Padmadevikā</s> said to me,

children.text: tad vaḥ kiṃ vismṛtaṃ kāryam iti meti mayoditam ||
children.translated_text: 'Has that business of yours been forgotten?' and I replied, 'No.'

children.text: tayoktaṃ kathayiṣyāmi punar apy āgatāya te
children.translated_text: She said, 'I shall tell it to you when you come again;

children.text: dhatte saṃdhriyamāṇaṃ hi rahasyaṃ ramyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: for a secret, when it is held back, takes on charm.'
Then on the following day I went to the house of the noble lady's daughter,
and saw the womenfolk silent with grief, their tears increased.
With her face covered by both hands, leaning against a pillar and turned away,
I saw <s>Padmadevikā</s> weeping in a low voice.
I asked her, 'When <s>Vatsarāja</s> rules well over this great kingdom,

children.text: jaṅgamasya kutaḥ śoko yuvarāje ca rājati ||
children.translated_text: and when the crown prince shines, whence can grief come for any living being?'

children.text: na kiṃcid api sāvocan mayā pṛṣṭāsakṛd yadā
children.translated_text: When she said nothing at all, though I asked her again and again,

children.text: tadā kila viṣaṇṇo 'haṃ mumoha ca papāta ca ||
children.translated_text: then, they say, I became dejected, fainted, and fell.

children.text: tatra caikā pramṛjyāsraṃ mām avocat sacetanam
children.translated_text: There one woman wiped away her tears and spoke to me when I had regained consciousness:
'This <s>Padmadevikā</s>, whose lord is you, is enviable, not to be pitied.

children.text: asyās tu svāminīṃ paśya yuvarāje virājati
children.translated_text: But look at her mistress, in whom the crown prince shines;

children.text: yasyāḥ śokopataptāyā yato rakṣas tato bhayam ||
children.translated_text: for she, scorched by grief, fears danger from the very place whence protection should come.

children.text: atha vā paśya tām eva paśyatām eva pīḍyate
children.translated_text: Or rather, look at that lady herself: before the eyes of those who watch, she is being tormented,
she whose very life is bound up with sharing sorrow with friends like you.'
Then, going by the route she had indicated to the pleasure-grove,
I saw the noble lady's daughter there on the bank of a lotus-pond.
A couch spread with lotus-fibres, moss, lotuses, and lotus leaves
she was drying up with her sighs and with her repeated tossings.
A girl named <s>Mudrikālatikā</s>, a thief of the eyes,
sat with her feet placed in that lady's lap, meditating on <s>Puruṣottama</s>.
Then, approaching in agitation, with folded hands, I said to her,
'May the lady honor me by granting me the bracelet of her sorrow.'
She said, 'Enough; you are one who shares in ever-increasing happiness,
so do not hear my story, which has no remedy for me and brings shame and grief.
For what lover of women wandering in <s>Nandana</s>
would cross over and enter the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, deep with sea-monsters?'
Then <s>Mudrikālatikā</s>, trying to conciliate her, said,
'The young mistress remembers someone; she has not been slighted.

children.text: yadi ca svayam ākhyātum aśaktā bhartṛdārikā
children.translated_text: And if the young mistress is unable to tell it herself,

children.text: tato mām anujānātu dhṛṣṭo hi gaṇikājanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then let her give me permission, for courtesan women are bold.'

children.text: evam uktābravīd evam evaṃ nāma nigadyatām
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, she said, 'Let it be told just so, exactly in this way;

children.text: akṛtvā sāhasaṃ kair vā mahāl labdho manorathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for by whom has a great desire ever been obtained without making a bold venture?

children.text: na cemaṃ gomukhād anyaḥ śrotum ālāpam arhati
children.translated_text: And no one other than <s>Gomukha</s> is worthy to hear this speech,
for a messenger skilled in division and reconciliation is appointed in such a task.'
Then, after clearing the people away from that place, <s>Mudrikālatikā</s>

children.text: mahyam ākhyātum ārabdhā kṣaṇam adhīyatāṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: began to tell me the story: let your mind attend for a moment.
There was a king named <s>Bharata</s>, devoted to the final aim of the three goals of life;

children.text: sa samāhṛtavān kāntāḥ kumārīr ā mahodadheḥ ||
children.translated_text: he gathered lovely maidens from as far as the great ocean.
'I shall marry all these at once, after they have gone to a private place,
and I shall enjoy uninterrupted pleasures,' he thought.

children.text: yasyāś ca prathamaṃ tena gṛhītaḥ kampanaḥ karaḥ
children.translated_text: But the woman whose trembling hand was first taken by him,
in her alone he found satisfaction, in that form won by pure merit.
As for the others who remained, women captivating mind and eye,
he arranged them into eight groups, shaped like branches of the wish-tree.
And in each group the king made a chief woman, covered with jingling ornaments,
and granted her a seat, parasol, and chowries.

children.text: tā gaṇāntargatā yasmād anyāsāṃ ca mahattamāḥ
children.translated_text: Because they were included within groups and were the greatest among the others,
they received from the lord of men the word '<s>mahāgaṇikā</s>' (great courtesan).

children.text: mahāguṇās tataś cānyās tato 'py anyās tataḥ parāḥ
children.translated_text: Then there were others called '<s>mahāguṇā</s>' (greatly accomplished), and after them others, and beyond them still others,
down to base women whose hips were hardened by the knocking together of pots.

children.text: ya eṣa gaṇikābheda idānīm api dṛśyate
children.translated_text: This classification of courtesans, which is seen even now,

children.text: tataḥ kālāt prabhṛty eva bharatena pravartitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was instituted by <s>Bharata</s> from that very time onward.

children.text: gaṇamukhyās tu yās tāsām ekasyāṃ kila saṃtatau
children.translated_text: And in the lineage of one of those women who were chiefs of groups,
this <s>Kaliṅgasenā</s> was born, like a lotus in a lake.
Shaming the wealth of beauty of the women of gods, demons, and serpents,
this daughter, <s>Madanamañjukā</s>, was obtained by her.

children.text: eṣā rājakulaṃ yāntīṃ dṛṣṭvā mātaram ekadā
children.translated_text: Once, seeing her mother going to the royal palace,

children.text: aham apy āci yāmīti punaḥ punar abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: she said again and again, "I too will go there."

children.text: jñātvā tu dṛḍhanirbandhāṃ sācī duhitaraṃ priyām
children.translated_text: Then, knowing that her beloved daughter was firmly insistent,
she took her, adorned with childish ornaments, to the king's assembly.

children.text: atha rājakulād eṣā nivṛttā lakṣitā mayā
children.translated_text: Then, when she had returned from the royal palace, I noticed her
with cheeks, eyes, and lips blossoming, as if she were pleased.
Whether standing, setting out, seated, or sitting down, constantly
she told stories among her friends about what had happened at the royal court.
Having with difficulty driven through the rest of the day and the night while awake,

children.text: prātaḥ sādaram ādatta citraṃ maṇḍanam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the morning she eagerly undertook her own splendid adornment.
Seeing her mother set out for the royal court,

children.text: tayā pṛṣṭā kva yāsīti yatra tvam iti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: when asked by her, "Where are you going?" she replied, "Where you are."

children.text: tayoktam ananujñātaiḥ putri gantuṃ na labhyate
children.translated_text: Her mother said, "Daughter, those who have not been permitted may not go
to the royal court; kings are harsh and have little affection.
Therefore turn back, mother; when permission has been obtained, you will go.

children.text: dhṛṣṭā hi dveṣyatāṃ yānti praṇayinyo 'pi yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For bold women, even if beloved, come to be disliked."

children.text: madhurāś copapannāś ca śrutvā mātur imā giraḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of her mother, sweet and reasonable though they were,
this girl, thinking them bitter and hard to bear, turned back.
Like the wife of a poor merchant who has seen a treasure and then lost it,
she abandoned sleep, food, and conversation, and made her bed her only refuge.
Once, while her friends had begun a conversation, she said to them,

children.text: svaptum icchāmy ahaṃ sakhyas tāvan nirgamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Friends, I want to sleep; for now, go out."

children.text: yātāsu tāsu manasā yatsatyaṃ mama śaṅkitam
children.translated_text: When they had gone, truthfully, this suspicion arose in my mind:

children.text: etāḥ prasthāpitāḥ sakhyaḥ kim akāraṇam etayā ||
children.translated_text: "Why has she sent these friends away without any cause?

children.text: yā sakhībhir vinā nidrāṃ naiva labdhavatī purā
children.translated_text: She who formerly could never get sleep without her friends--

children.text: tasyās tā eva nighnanti nidrām iti na badhyate ||
children.translated_text: it does not make sense that those very friends are now destroying her sleep."
Thinking this, I stood concealed by a latticed window,
and saw her busy with adornment, mirror in hand.
Standing facing the royal palace, with joined palms she said,

children.text: janmāntare 'pi bhūyāsam ahaṃ tasmin vadhūr iti ||
children.translated_text: "May I become his bride, even in another birth."
Immediately fastening a silk noose around her neck,
she quickly suspended herself from a wall-peg.
Coming as swiftly as an arrow, as it was about to steal her life,
I pulled away that noose from her throat, like the noose of Death.
Then, bringing a couch and with wet breezes from fans,
I forcibly brought her consciousness back from the palace of the king of the dead.
Gradually opening her eyes, slow and with copper-red pupils,

children.text: ninīya mayi mattaś ca pratyāhṛtyedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: she directed them toward me and, drawing them back from me, said this:

children.text: tan mitram atikaṣṭād yad vyasanāt kila rakṣati
children.translated_text: "A friend, they say, is one who saves someone from a calamity of extreme pain;

children.text: vyasane praharantyā tu śatrutvaṃ darśitaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: but by striking at me in calamity, you have shown yourself an enemy.

children.text: ahaṃ hi sarvaduḥkhānām idam utpannam ālayam
children.translated_text: For I am this dwelling-place that has arisen for all sorrows;

children.text: tvayā jīvitam ujhantī vidhṛtā kim akāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: as I was giving up life, why did you hold me back without cause?
After passing the time favorably with me until a single moment,
by thwarting my resolve you have shown your hostility.

children.text: yad etad ucyate loke sarvathā na tad anyathā
children.translated_text: What is said in the world is in no way otherwise:
a friend who is hard to manage by every means is a great enemy."

children.text: bruvāṇām ity asaṃbaddham ity enām aham abruvam
children.translated_text: As she spoke in this incoherent way, I said to her,

children.text: svāmini prabhur ity asmān upālambhena takṣasi ||
children.translated_text: "Mistress, you are carving us up with reproach, as though you alone were master.

children.text: idaṃ kathaya nas tāvad vyasane 'bhyudaye 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Tell us this much: in misfortune or even in prosperity,
when you, our mistress, have come into some affair, in what matter have we not been admitted inside?
You have now become pitiable, since, casting aside your retinue of servants,

children.text: tanum ekākinī tyaktvā sukham āsitum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: you wish to abandon your body alone and sit at ease.

children.text: duḥkhahetum ataḥ śaṃsa yadi sādhyaṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Therefore tell us the cause of your sorrow; if it can be remedied,
then we shall all live; if the contrary, we shall die."

children.text: atha sthitvā kṣaṇaṃ tūṣṇīṃ śanakair idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then, after remaining silent for a moment, she said this softly:
"What is there to be told even to you, whose body shares one life with mine?

children.text: atha jānanty api tvaṃ māṃ nirlajjayitum icchasi
children.translated_text: And yet, though you know me, you wish to make me shameless;

children.text: idam ākhyāya te ko vā strībhyaḥ sāhasikaḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: after I have told you this, who could be more reckless than women?
I went to the royal palace, and, when the lord had respectfully summoned me,
I was then placed upon his right thigh, shaped like an iron bar.

children.text: upaviṣṭas tu nṛpater ūrau vāme nṛpātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: But the king's son was seated on the king's left thigh;

children.text: mayā dṛṣṭaḥ praviṣṭaś ca hṛdayaṃ me anivāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he was seen by me, and unchecked he entered my heart.

children.text: dahane 'pi vasann antar na dahaty araṇīṃ sa tu
children.translated_text: Though he lives inside the fire, he does not burn the fire-stick there;

children.text: saumyo 'pi puṇyavān asmān nirdhūmaṃ dagdhum icchati ||
children.translated_text: yet, though gentle and blessed, he wishes to burn us without smoke.

children.text: sa hetur asya duḥkhasya sakṛddarśanam āgataḥ
children.translated_text: He is the cause of this sorrow, having come within my sight only once;

children.text: adhunā śrūyamāṇo 'pi kiṃ vā vilapitair iti ||
children.translated_text: and now, even when he is merely heard of, what is the use of lamentations?"

children.text: śrutvedam aham asyās tu jātā yat satyam ākulā
children.translated_text: Hearing this from her, I, in truth, became agitated,
suspecting that this remedy would be as difficult as making the ocean rise up.
With loud laughter, saying "Ha, ha!" and concealing my despondency,

children.text: etām āśvāsayāmi sma niḥsārair vacanair iti ||
children.translated_text: I reassured her with empty words, saying:
"Mistress, abandon your anguish. For your pleasure I could bring even the lord of the Vidyādharas

children.text: vaśayeyaṃ tava prītyai kiṃ punaḥ puruṣeśvaram ||
children.translated_text: under control; how much more, then, a lord of men?

children.text: kiṃ tu tvāravatā śakyaṃ na labdhaṃ phalam īpsitam
children.translated_text: But the desired result cannot be obtained by haste;
for even kings employ conciliation and the other means only in sequence.
Therefore, with the utmost firmness, restraining your restless mind,
unnoticed by people, endure for a few days."

children.text: taṃ ceyaṃ siddham evārtham arthibhāvād abudhyata
children.translated_text: And because she was so desirous, she understood that matter as already accomplished.
and inwardly she revealed her satisfaction, her lotus-face blooming.
Day after day I put her off with words that were sweet but false,
connected with the accomplishment of the task and showing her hope.
When she thought herself deceived by fruitless replies,

children.text: moktukāmā tadā prāṇān punar utprekṣitā mayā ||
children.translated_text: and wished to abandon her life, I again discerned it.

children.text: tataḥ saṃbhrāntayā gatvā mayāsyā mātur antikam
children.translated_text: Then I went in haste to her mother,
and, after consulting together with her, this plan was carried out.
"<s>Gomukha</s> is like a second body of the prince;

children.text: sa kenacid upāyena veśam āśu praveśyatām ||
children.translated_text: by some means let him quickly be made to enter the courtesan house.
He himself, because he is his companion, will bring the prince,
with speech stealing the mind and ear, like a cuckoo bringing spring."
And then this affair was told by <s>Kaliṅgasenā</s>

children.text: padmāvatyai tayā cāsi cetasya iti bhāṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Padmāvatī</s>, and by her it was said, "You are in her thoughts."
Then, through charioteers, scribes, elephant-riders, and the like,

children.text: dhūrtair asmatprayuktais tvaṃ veśam etaṃ praveśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: through rogues sent by us, you were made to enter this courtesan house.

children.text: tisṛṇāṃ ca prayuktānām abhavad bhavataḥ priyā
children.translated_text: And of the three women sent, sweet <s>Padmadevikā</s>
became dear to you, like the tone-string among lute strings.
But she, having accomplished her own object and turning away from her friend's interest,
does not inform you, from fear that her own aim will be ruined.
Seeing no other means, the princess was set in motion,
saying, "Let her be seen, hopeless, with long sighs for an incurable condition."

children.text: tad idaṃ duḥsahaṃ duḥkhaṃ yasmād asmākam āgatam
children.translated_text: Since this unbearable suffering has come upon us from that,

children.text: tvadāyattaḥ sa śeṣaś ca saṃvidhattāṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: and the remainder depends on you, please arrange it.
Then I said, "Why, through neglect, have you ladies brought
this blade of grass, which could have been cut by the nails, to needing an axe?"

children.text: svayam eva tato gatvā devī vijñāpitā mayā
children.translated_text: After that I myself went and informed the queen:

children.text: mucyatām eṣa saṃtāpaḥ siddhaṃ viddhi prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: "Let this anxiety be released; know that the purpose is accomplished.
The queen desires the prince; he is fond of such virtues;
and <s>Gomukha</s> is the joiner: blessed is this meeting of the three.

children.text: nāsty eva ca mamāyāsaḥ śaratkāntyunmanā yataḥ
children.translated_text: And there is no effort at all for me, since, his mind carried away by autumn beauty,
the royal goose approaches the lotus-bed by itself.
Enough of this net of talk; in every way, before long
I shall make the prince bow to my mistress."

children.text: sābravīn na nasaṃbhāvyam idaṃ nāgarake tvayi
children.translated_text: She said, "This is not impossible in you, a man-about-town;

children.text: kiṃ tu prastāvam āsādya yatethāḥ kāryasiddhaye ||
children.translated_text: but, having found the occasion, you should strive for the success of the task.
For actions undertaken at the wrong occasion come to fruitlessness,
or even to an unwanted result, after angering one's masters."
Then, having bowed to her, I went to the prince's residence,
and came back bringing leftovers, sweetmeats and the like.

children.text: tāṃ ca vijñāpayāmi sma rājaputreṇa modakaḥ
children.translated_text: And I informed her, "The sweetmeat was taken up by the prince himself

children.text: svayam ārabhya hastābhyāṃ yuṣmabhyaṃ prahitā iti ||
children.translated_text: and sent to you with his own hands."

children.text: sābravīj jālam apy etad āśvāsayati mādṛśam
children.translated_text: She said, "Even this deception gives reassurance to one like me;

children.text: āśvāsanti kṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛgā hi mṛgatṛṣṇikām ||
children.translated_text: for deer are reassured for a moment when they see a mirage."
With garlands, sandal-paste, betel, garments, ornaments, and incense,
I reassured her, saying, "These have been sent by you."

children.text: eṣa vijñāpayāmy adya śvo vijñāpayiteti ca
children.translated_text: "I shall inform him today; I shall inform him tomorrow":
without obtaining an opportunity, I passed all this time.

children.text: atha mām abravīd devyāḥ purato mudrikālatā
children.translated_text: Then, in the presence of the queen, <s>Mudrikālatā</s> said to me,
"Ah, great expectation should be placed in you, a great man-about-town.
After roaring so, 'I shall make him bow,'
why is this innocent woman being deceived with leaves, flowers, fruits, and the like?

children.text: athavā tiṣṭha tāvat tvam aham evānayāmi tam
children.translated_text: Or rather, wait there. I myself will bring him;

children.text: viraktam api saṃdhātum alaṃ kauśalam asti naḥ ||
children.translated_text: we have skill enough to unite even one who is indifferent."

children.text: evam uttejitas tasyā gurubhir vacanair aham
children.translated_text: Thus provoked by those weighty words of hers,
I said, "You will know by the result," and became attentive to the occasion.

children.text: yātrāyāṃ tu pravṛttāyām abhyāse 'tra yad eva me
children.translated_text: But when the procession had begun, whatever practice I had here,

children.text: tan mayā kāritā yūyaṃ kṣiptvā hariśikhādikān ||
children.translated_text: I made you perform that, having pushed aside <s>Hariśikha</s> and the others.

children.text: yat tat pravahaṇaṃ gacchat pathi yuṣmābhir īkṣitam
children.translated_text: That conveyance which you saw going along the road
was occupied by the noble lady, thundering like a cloud with lightning.
There that half of her face, with a finger placed on her forehead,

children.text: yuṣmabhyaṃ darśitaṃ vandyaṃ tat tayā vandamānayā ||
children.translated_text: was shown to you by her as she was bowing.

children.text: yac ca vijñāpitā yūyam ānataṃ mukuṭaṃ manāk
children.translated_text: And when you were requested by me, "Lift up
your lowered crown a little," in that too there was this purpose:
"This is their urbane salutation to the noble prince,

children.text: kṛtas toṣayatā kāntām asmākaṃ svāminīm iti ||
children.translated_text: made by him while pleasing our mistress, his beloved."
This queen <s>Madanamañjukā</s> desires Your Majesty,
whose very life is wisdom and valor, as <s>Lakṣmī</s> desires a king.
And she, come to hand without effort, ought not to be rejected,
like a fresh garland of mālatī, attractive in the form of its qualities.
She has been bitten by the serpent of <s>Anaṅga</s>; quickly give her consideration.

children.text: na hy āśīviṣadagdha antrāḥ kṣamante divasān iti ||
children.translated_text: For those whose entrails are burned by a venomous snake cannot endure for days."
Having heard from <s>Gomukha</s> this story, new and dear in its telling,
my shame carried away by that account, I spoke openly:
"At that very time, when she was sitting in the king's lap,
she scattered in our heart an unspoiled seed of the tree of love.
Watered again and again by the waters of hearing her virtues,
it grew, troubling my mind, with a harsh swelling sprout."

children.text: tad dohadam ivāsādya priyāṃ pravahaṇe sthitām
children.translated_text: Having encountered my beloved seated in the carriage as though she were its longing,
the tree of Love seemed to put forth shoots that produced trembling and sighs.
"Show her to me before the great tree of Love, while its limbs are not yet fully grown,

children.text: na samākramya mṛdnāti tāvad darśaya tām iti ||
children.translated_text: mounts and crushes me," I said.
He said, "The two dancing masters had quarreled with each other,

children.text: tvatpravīṇo 'ham ity uktau tau ca bhūpatinā kila ||
children.translated_text: each saying, 'I am the one more skilled for you,' and then, so it is said, the king addressed them:

children.text: alaṃ vāṃ kalahaṃ kṛtvā karmaśāstravidau yuvām
children.translated_text: 'Enough of making this quarrel, you two who know the art and science of performance.

children.text: yasya yā kuśalā śiṣyā sa nartayatu tām iti ||
children.translated_text: Whichever pupil is skilled under each of you, let him cause her to dance.'

children.text: śvaḥ suyāmunadantāṃ ca tasmād aryasutāṃ ca naḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore tomorrow the king will see <s>Suyāmunadantā</s>

children.text: nṛtyantīṃ nṛpatir draṣṭā tatra draṣṭāstha tām iti ||
children.translated_text: and our noble young lady dancing; there you will see her."

children.text: yā svābhāvikarūpakhaṇḍitajagadrūpābhimānā priyā śṛṅgārādirasaprayogasubhagā jāyeta sā kīdṛśī
children.translated_text: What would she be like, that beloved whose natural beauty has broken the pride of the world's beauty, made lovely by the performance of the erotic and other rasas?

children.text: ity adhyāsitacetasā katham api prakrāntayā cintayā paryaṅkāṅkavivartinārtatanunā nītā triyāmā mayā ||
children.translated_text: With my mind possessed by such a thought, somehow begun, I spent the night with my distressed body turning about on the couch.
Then, dressed in the manner of a townsman and surrounded by friends dressed in the same way,

children.text: saṃprasthāpya manaḥ pūrvaṃ nṛpāsthānam agām aham ||
children.translated_text: after sending my mind ahead first, I went to the royal assembly.
There I bowed to the king, who was seated on a dais arranged like <s>Puṣpaka</s>,
and, permitted by him, I took another seat on the platform.
Then, seeing the arena of the stage crowded with expert spectators,
the two dance-masters bowed and said to the king:
"O king, your servants have arrived in the nearby tiring-room.

children.text: draṣṭum icchatha yāṃ pūrvam ājñāpayata tām iti ||
children.translated_text: Command which one you wish to see first."
He said, "<s>Gomukha</s> is skilled in the arts and sciences of dance, song, and the rest;

children.text: gomukhaḥ sa ca yām āha sā pūrvaṃ nṛtyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: the one he names, let her dance first."

children.text: tābhyām āgatya pṛṣṭaś ca kā pūrvaṃ nṛtyatām iti
children.translated_text: When the two came and asked him, "Which one should dance first?"
he directed her teacher, saying, "<s>Suyāmunadantā</s>."
Then, when she danced, the connoisseurs of dance danced along,
but the rest of the audience became motionless, as if fallen into deep sleep.

children.text: pratyāhṛtya tataś ceto hriyamāṇaṃ balāt tayā
children.translated_text: Then I drew back my mind, which was being forcibly carried away by her,
through the movements of mind, eyes, and limbs that could not be acquired by training, and I thought:

children.text: nānugantum alaṃ rambhā nṛttam asyāḥ samenakā
children.translated_text: "<s>Rambhā</s>, together with <s>Menakā</s>, is not able to keep up with her dance.

children.text: kuta eva parājetum abalā bālikā priyā ||
children.translated_text: How, then, could my beloved, a powerless young girl, possibly defeat her?"
As a royal swan, blind with thirst, when it has reached a lotus-pond,
might see its water muddied with mire, so I imagined my beloved.

children.text: avocaṃ gomukhaṃ cedaṃ jīyamānāṃ priyām aham
children.translated_text: And I said this to <s>Gomukha</s>: "I am unable to watch

children.text: aśaktaḥ prekṣituṃ tena raṅgān nirgamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: my beloved being defeated by her; therefore let us leave the theater."

children.text: tenoktam icchayā gantum āgantuṃ vā na labhyate
children.translated_text: He said, "It is not possible to go or come at will
from the house of <s>Vatsarāja</s>; therefore remain for a moment."
Then, when she had stopped, like the old sun in splendor,

children.text: jīvalokam iva jyotsnā priyā raṅgam arañjayat ||
children.translated_text: my beloved, like moonlight the world of living beings, delighted the stage.
I asked <s>Gomukha</s>, "Which of these is <s>Padmadevikā</s>
and which is <s>Mudrikālatikā</s>?" He laughed and said this:

children.text: kīrtikāntyor iyaṃ madhye yā lakṣmīr iva rājate
children.translated_text: "She who shines in the midst of glory and beauty like <s>Lakṣmī</s>

children.text: eṣā naḥ svāminī devī vāmato mudrikālatā ||
children.translated_text: is our mistress, the lady; on the left is <s>Mudrikālatā</s>.

children.text: na ceyaṃ śakyate jetum alaṃ vaḥ śaṅkayā yataḥ
children.translated_text: And she cannot be defeated. Away with your doubt, since
who has ever seen autumn moonlight conquered by the glow of a firefly?
I have seen her surpass

children.text: dṛṣṭā saṃbhāvayāmy asyās tena nṛttaguṇān iti ||
children.translated_text: many hundreds of dancers; therefore I have confidence in her virtues in dance."
While I, facing <s>Gomukha</s>, was listening attentively,

children.text: tāvaj jaya jayety uccair vimuktaḥ prekṣakair dhvaniḥ ||
children.translated_text: the spectators suddenly let out a loud cry of "Victory! Victory!"

children.text: raṅgād dṛṣṭā ca niryāntī bādhyamāneva sā mayā
children.translated_text: And she was seen going out from the stage, as though oppressed by me,
with dejection, trembling, pallor, and despair as if they were natural to her.
Then, after the assembly was dismissed, I bowed to the king
and went to my own residence, with thoughts of my beloved going before me.

children.text: gomukhaṃ cābravaṃ kasmān mām idānīm upekṣase
children.translated_text: And I said to <s>Gomukha</s>, "Why are you now neglecting me?

children.text: na hy ādeśam upekṣante tvādṛśā mādṛśām iti ||
children.translated_text: For men like you do not neglect the commands of men like me."
He said, "Someone else should be sent to gain her trust.

children.text: śraddhāsyati na me vākyaṃ vipralabdhā hi sā mayā ||
children.translated_text: She will not trust my words, for she has been deceived by me."
When I said, "Take any one of these men and go,"
he said, "In this matter <s>Marubhūtika</s> alone is suitable.

children.text: ayaṃ hariśikhas tāvan nītyā vakragatiḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>Hariśikha</s>, for his part, has been made crooked in his ways by policy;
seeing a hundred dangers, he may perhaps draw a snare.
In this most painful tangle of the four calamities,
where women are the chief factor, how could the prince be set in motion?
Thus, with finger-counting calculations, as a pretended scholar

children.text: vihanyād api naḥ kāryaṃ tasmād eṣa na yujyate ||
children.translated_text: he might even ruin our business; therefore he is not suitable.
<s>Tapantaka</s> too is foolish because of his youth and has an empty expression;

children.text: tasmād evaṃvidhe kārye niyogaṃ nāyam arhati ||
children.translated_text: therefore he is not fit for an assignment in a matter of this kind.
But <s>Marubhūtika</s>, because his very nature is courage, is capable;
he is practiced in daring acts, and so he should be sent."

children.text: tatas tau sahitau yātau cirāt tu marubhūtikam
children.translated_text: Then the two went together. After a long time, when <s>Marubhūtika</s>

children.text: prāptaṃ hariśikho 'pṛcchat kiṃ vṛttaṃ bhavator iti ||
children.translated_text: had arrived, <s>Hariśikha</s> asked him, "What happened to you two?"
He said, "As we two were going through the middle of the courtesans' quarter,

children.text: āyāty abhimukhī yaiva saiva yāti parāṅmukhī ||
children.translated_text: the very woman who comes toward us turns away again.
And, breaking her fingers in anger, with red eyes she says,

children.text: na spraṣṭavyo na saṃbhāṣyo gomukhaḥ pāpavān iti ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Gomukha</s>, the sinful man, is not to be touched and not to be spoken to.'"
with golden-pillared gateways thronged by angry doorkeepers
we two entered through the doors of the inner chambers into the place where the noble prince was staying.
There one girl said, "Girls, look at this wonder:
by his cleverness this rogue has turned cow-dung into milk-rice.
This was his offense to this extent: a snake, taker of life, was produced;
look, by this very talkative man that same thing has been made into a virtue."
When, though he was bowing, he was not received graciously by the mistress because of her anger,

children.text: saṃbhrāntaś ca vilakṣaś ca tadā tām āha gomukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Gomukha</s>, flustered and abashed, said to her:

children.text: manye niṣkāraṇaṃ kopaṃ devyāḥ ko nāma mādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: "I think the lady's anger is without cause. What servant like me,
knowing his master's mind, would ever anger his master?"
Then another girl, holding a palm-leaf fan, spoke in anger:

children.text: kathaṃ niṣkāraṇo nāma kim idaṃ laghu kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: "How can it be without cause? Is this a small cause?
When she was longing for the long-desired sight of someone, as for a mirror of yearning,

children.text: tvayā nartayatā kāntā kim iyaṃ sukham āsitā ||
children.translated_text: did this beloved woman sit happily while you made her dance?

children.text: athavā tad gataṃ nāma svāmī kiṃ karaṇaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Or let that pass. What had your master done to you,

children.text: paśyann abhimukhaṃ prītyā sa tathā vimukhīkṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that, while he was looking straight toward her with love, he was turned away in that way?

children.text: bhavān paśyatu vā mā vā tvadvidheyo yuvā janaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether you look or not, young people are obedient to you.

children.text: tvam icchasi jayaṃ yasyāḥ kim asau na parājitā ||
children.translated_text: Is not the woman whose victory you wish the one who has not been defeated?"
Then <s>Gomukha</s>, lifting up his face that had been bent down in fear,

children.text: uktavān paśyatānarthaṃ doṣo bhūto guṇo 'pi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: said, "Look at this misfortune: even our virtue has become a fault.

children.text: yadi prāk svāminī nṛtyet tayā rājā sutoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: If the mistress had danced first, the king, being fully delighted by her,
and his curiosity satisfied, might never have looked at the other woman at all.

children.text: tadā ca guṇavidveṣī jano vaktā bhaved yathā
children.translated_text: Then people hostile to merit would have said this:
'<s>Madanamañjukā</s> was seen by the king out of partiality.'

children.text: itarā yadi nṛtyantī tena dṛṣṭā bhavet tadā
children.translated_text: But if he had seen the other woman dancing,

children.text: norvaśīm api paśyet saḥ kuto madanamañjukām ||
children.translated_text: he would not have looked even at <s>Urvaśī</s>; how much less at <s>Madanamañjukā</s>.

children.text: prītyā yaś conmukhaḥ paśyan kṛtaḥ svāmī parāṅmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: And listen how I used that stratagem
by which the master, who was looking toward her with love, was made to turn away.
<s>Suyāmunadantā</s> could not be defeated through imitations,
even by <s>Bharata</s> himself dancing in person.

children.text: aryaputre tu vimukhe yuṣmābhiḥ sā parājitā
children.translated_text: But when the noble prince turned away, she was defeated by you
through your natural pallor, confusion, sweating, and trembling.

children.text: tena bravīmi sevāpi yāti yady aparādhatām
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: if even service passes into offense,
then servants who have pleased their masters with devotion are, alas, badly placed.
Or rather, even a messenger who has committed an offense deserves honor;
therefore, because a message is to be heard from him, honor me."
Then she turned back there, her face clear with favor,
her lips bathed in the moonlight of a slight smile,

children.text: ayi candramukhaṃ mā sma gomukhaṃ puruṣaṃ vada
children.translated_text: and said, "Dear girl, do not call a moon-faced man <s>Gomukha</s>.
For those who stand near the lord of <s>Vatsa</s> are not heard to betray women's friends.

children.text: anālāpena yac cāsi kṣaṇam āyāsito mayā
children.translated_text: And because I troubled you for a moment by not speaking,

children.text: tat kṣamasva na hi svāsthā bādhante tvādṛśām iti ||
children.translated_text: forgive that; women who are not in their right state do trouble people like you."

children.text: tataḥ sā gomukhenoktā draṣṭum icchati vaḥ priyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then she was told by <s>Gomukha</s>, "Your beloved wishes to see you.

children.text: saṃdehaś ced iyaṃ mudrā tadīyā dṛśyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: If there is doubt, let this seal of his be inspected."

children.text: tayoktaṃ kumbhakārāṇāṃ koṭir vasati vaḥ pure
children.translated_text: She said, "A crore of potters lives in your city.

children.text: koṭiḥ kim iti nānītā na hi te kṣīṇamṛttikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why was a crore not brought? Surely they have no shortage of clay."

children.text: tenoktaṃ kena vānītā mudrā vā mṛttikāmayī
children.translated_text: He said, "Who would have brought a seal made of clay?
Sensible people, when they have undertaken a great task, do not act carelessly.
The son of <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>, the dear friend of your beloved,
sent with affection by his master, is <s>Marubhūtika</s>; let him be seen."

children.text: atha devī namaskṛtya prītā vijñāpitā mayā
children.translated_text: Then, after bowing to the lady, I joyfully informed her:

children.text: yat saṃdiśati naḥ svāmī yuṣmabhyaṃ tan niśāmyatām ||
children.translated_text: "Please listen to what our master sends as a message to you.

children.text: preritaḥ tvām ahaṃ draṣṭuṃ yena lakṣmīm ivālasaḥ
children.translated_text: I have been sent by him to see you, languid as <s>Lakṣmī</s>;
let this bashful one be put at ease by playing with people like us."

children.text: prasthitāyāṃ tato devyām āha māṃ padmadevikā
children.translated_text: Then, when the lady had set out, <s>Padmadevikā</s> said to me,

children.text: iyaṃ prasādhyate yāvat tāvad āstāṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "Until she is won over, please remain here."

children.text: devyā saha praviśyāntar muhūrtād iva sā tataḥ
children.translated_text: After going inside with the lady, she soon returned
and said, greatly delighted, her lotus-eyes expanded:
"By me this matter was reported to <s>Kaliṅgasenā</s>, by her, after she had gone, to <s>Rumaṇvat</s>,
and by him too this whole affair was reported to the king.

children.text: tenoktaṃ kim ihākhyeyaṃ taruṇo nanu dārakaḥ
children.translated_text: He said, 'What is there to be explained in this? Surely the boy is young;
therefore let him experience the pleasures of the world of the living.'
So she has been permitted by the king and also by her teacher <s>Manmatha</s>.

children.text: iyam āyāti te paścād yātu tāvad bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: She is coming after you; let your honor go ahead for now."
Then the door-keeper entered in agitation and reported.

children.text: sayāno gomukhaḥ prāha laghu śrāvaya mām iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gomukha</s>, lying there, said, "Quickly let me hear it."

children.text: mayoktaṃ gomukhas tāvad ekākī praviśatv iti
children.translated_text: I said, "Let <s>Gomukha</s> enter alone first."

children.text: sa praviśyoktavān dvāre devī kiṃ vidhṛteti mām ||
children.translated_text: He entered and said to me at the door, "Why has the lady been kept back?"
I said, "My mind is bewildered, since I do not know the company of women.

children.text: kuru nāgarakaṃ tāvat tvaṃ mām ity aham uktavān ||
children.translated_text: First make me a man-about-town."
He said, "'Horses are trained at the time of battle':

children.text: yad etad ghuṣyate loke tad etat tathyatāṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: what is proclaimed in the world has now become true.
Urbanity cannot be obtained through instruction,
for, like the knowledge of liberation, it is accomplished by repeated practice.

children.text: saṃkṣepatas tu vakṣyāmi yad yad devī kariṣyati
children.translated_text: But in brief I shall tell you: whatever the lady does,

children.text: tat tad evānukuryās tvaṃ dakṣo hi labhate śriyam ||
children.translated_text: you should do exactly that, for the skillful man obtains fortune."

children.text: anuśiṣya sa mām evaṃ niryāyānīya ca priyām
children.translated_text: Having instructed me in this way, he went out, brought in my beloved,

children.text: sukhaṃ supyāstam ity uktvā yathāsvaṃ sasuhṛdgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, saying, "May you sleep happily," went off with his friends, each to his own place.

children.text: tataḥ praviśya dayitā mām ardhākṣṇā niraikṣata
children.translated_text: Then the beloved entered and looked at me with half an eye.

children.text: kṛtaṃ tathaiva ca mayā vanditena ca vanditā ||
children.translated_text: And just as she did, so I did; when bowed to, I bowed to her in return.

children.text: sarvathā yad yad evāham anayā kāritas tadā
children.translated_text: In every way, whatever I was made to do by her then,
I imitated that very thing, like the pupil of a dancing teacher.
Then, understanding that I was compliant and knew the meaning of her signals,
she smiled and, trembling and horripilating, pressed her body tightly against mine.
Then, no longer even considering the sequence of imitations begun by her,
I came under the control of some bodiless being.
When we had come into womanhood and manhood, and sleep was undesired,

children.text: pradoṣa eva kṣaṇadā kṣīṇā kṣaṇavad āvayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: the night, beginning at dusk, passed for us like a single moment.
In the morning <s>Gomukha</s>, taking my beloved in the carriage itself,
brought her to her mother's house, while my mind went before her.
When some days had passed in this way, while my passion kept increasing,

children.text: dineṣu mama samprāptaḥ senānīr idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the general came to me and said this:
"Today, when eight muhūrtas have passed,
the king, with the approval of the astrologers, will announce, after the rites of appeasement at night:
'I shall ferry across the <s>Yamunā</s> the people who have come for the expedition.

children.text: yuṣmābhir api kartavyaṃ yat tad ājñāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is to be done by you also, let that be commanded.'"
I said, "<s>Gomukha</s> will go and inform you."

children.text: iti tasmin nate mahyaṃ gomukhena niveditam ||
children.translated_text: When he had bowed to me, <s>Gomukha</s> reported:
"Tomorrow the company of courtesans, with their company of lovers, will go.

children.text: tenaiva sahitā yūyaṃ gantāraḥ śanakair iti ||
children.translated_text: You too, together with that same group, are to go slowly."
But when this affair had been told by <s>Gomukha</s> to <s>Rumaṇvat</s>,
I set out with my friends in the morning, behind the crowd of people.

children.text: tac ca krīḍāgṛhaṃ prāpya kalpitaṃ yamunātaṭe
children.translated_text: Reaching that pleasure-house prepared on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
I spent the day eager for the beginning of night.
After sitting in the night with my beloved, who had been brought by <s>Gomukha</s>,
when the night had almost passed, I saw her weeping.

children.text: kim etad iti pṛṣṭā ca mayā saṃbhrāntacetasā
children.translated_text: When I, with a frightened mind, asked, "What is this?"
and she said nothing, another girl spoke:
"A fault, they say, leaves the faulty through association with the virtuous;
but the fault of the word 'courtesan' has not left her even today.

children.text: kāśirājasya yā kanyā vṛtā tubhyaṃ purodhasā
children.translated_text: The daughter of the king of <s>Kāśī</s>, who has been chosen for you by the chaplain,
is to have this woman as her fly-whisk bearer, it seems.

children.text: seyam utprekṣya tad duḥkhaṃ dāruṇaṃ maraṇād api
children.translated_text: Imagining that sorrow, more terrible even than death,
she has resolved to drink poison and wishes to abandon her life."
I said, "I too shall cast off this body, tormented by the pain of separation from you,
constantly tossed about, sober, and insensible, and I shall remain without feeling."

children.text: ity asminn eva samaye prāptā hariśikhādayaḥ
children.translated_text: At just that moment <s>Hariśikha</s> and the others arrived.
Hearing this terrifying account, they became fearful.
Then, after conferring with his friends, <s>Marubhūtika</s> said,

children.text: vayam eva viṣaṃ pūrvaṃ pibāmaḥ kalpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "We ourselves shall drink the poison first; let it be prepared."
Then <s>Hariśikha</s> said, "Where is that <s>Gomukha</s> now?

children.text: yo hi mūlam anarthasya sa tāvat pāyyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Since he is the root of the disaster, let him first be made to drink."
A girl sent by him to summon <s>Gomukha</s> returned

children.text: abravīd gomukho vakti kiṃ mayātaḥ prayojanam ||
children.translated_text: and said, "<s>Gomukha</s> says, 'What business have I with this?
I have begun to study the long-forgotten chapter named Long Life

children.text: aham adhyetum ārabdho vaidyāt prāṇapradād iti ||
children.translated_text: from the life-giving physician.'"
Then <s>Hariśikha</s>, angry, said to <s>Marubhūtika</s>,

children.text: preryamāṇaṃ galāṣṭrābhiḥ śīghram ānaya taṃ śaṭham ||
children.translated_text: "Quickly bring that rogue, driving him on with a halter at his neck.

children.text: yas tvayā ghaṭito 'narthaḥ svāmino jīvitaḥ sukham
children.translated_text: The disaster that was brought about by you, namely the master's living happily

children.text: svāminyā saha saṃyogaḥ so 'yam evaṃ vijṛmbhate ||
children.translated_text: and his union with the mistress, is now expanding in this way."

children.text: so 'bravīt so 'yam āyāto vādaḥ saṃprati satyatām
children.translated_text: He said, "Now that saying has come true:
'Thinking, "I shall get a fever," the shaven-headed man drinks gruel.'

children.text: sa kālas tāvad āyātu svāminī yad viśaṅkitā
children.translated_text: Let that time first come, the one about which the mistress is anxious.

children.text: tatraiva vidyāma nyañco pāsyāmas tyajyatāṃ tvarā ||
children.translated_text: There indeed we shall know, and we shall drink; abandon haste.
Or rather, enough with chatter. Let <s>Tapantaka</s> inform the king,

children.text: vijñāpayatu tenāsya dattaḥ pūrvam ayaṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for this boon was given to him earlier by the king:
'Even without occasion, you must make a request of me;

children.text: siddhiṃ yāsyati cāvaśyaṃ mā sma śaṅkāṃ karod iti ||
children.translated_text: it will certainly succeed. Do not have any doubt.'"
Having reassured her with these favorable words,

children.text: mātur evānayan mūlaṃ prāviśāma tataḥ purīm ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gomukha</s> brought her to her mother's side, and then we entered the city.
While I was at <s>Kumāravaṭaka</s>, I instructed <s>Tapantaka</s>:

children.text: gomukhena yad ākhyātaṃ tat kāryaṃ sādhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "The matter that was explained by <s>Gomukha</s> must be accomplished."

children.text: tapantakas tu sāsphoṭam idaṃ siddhim iti bruvan
children.translated_text: But <s>Tapantaka</s>, clapping his hands and saying, "This is success,"
went to the royal palace and, after coming back from there, said this:

children.text: rājapādair ahaṃ pṛṣṭas tāta kiṃ kriyatām iti
children.translated_text: "I was asked by the royal feet, 'Dear boy, what should be done?'

children.text: śālīnena mayāpy uktaṃ modako dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and I, being modest, said, 'Let a sweetmeat be given.'"
Thus, because of his pettiness, <s>Tapantaka</s>

children.text: yācate sma prahīṇatvād gatvā gatvā mahīpatim ||
children.translated_text: went again and again to the king and kept asking for worthless things, garlands, fruits, and the like.

children.text: iti saśarīrayā kṣaṇam iva kṣaṇadāḥ kṣapayan saha viśarīrayā dayitayā virasān divasān
children.translated_text: Thus, passing nights as though they were a moment with my embodied beloved, and tasteless days with her disembodied form,

children.text: dinarajanīvihāraviparītam aham caritai rathacaraṇāhvayasya caritāni viḍambitavān ||
children.translated_text: I, by conduct contrary to the day-and-night behavior of the one called <s>Rathacaraṇa</s>, mimicked the behavior of that bird.
Then, when I had done what had to be done and was sitting comfortably at daybreak,
<s>Gomukha</s>, pale with shame like a defeated disputant, said to me:

children.text: aham aryasutāṃ nītvā gṛhaṃ svagṛham āgataḥ
children.translated_text: "After taking the noble lady home, I came to my own house.
After that too, I went to the king's inner apartments to salute the queens."

children.text: vanditā ca vihasyāha devī padmāvatī yathā
children.translated_text: And, when she had been saluted, Queen <s>Padmāvatī</s> laughed and said:

children.text: kiṃkāraṇaṃ vadhūr adya nāsmān āyāti vanditum ||
children.translated_text: "For what reason does the bride not come today to salute us?

children.text: bhrātrā te kiṃ na muktaiva na vādyāpi vibudhyate
children.translated_text: Has your brother not released her, or has she perhaps not yet awakened?

children.text: kopitā vā bhaved bhartrā śiṣṭā duścaritair iti ||
children.translated_text: Or could she have been angered by her husband, or scolded for misbehavior?"
Then <s>Padmadevikā</s> came, beating her breast and crying out;

children.text: nāsti naḥ svāminīty uktvā devyor nipatitā puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: saying, "Our mistress is gone," she fell down before the two queens.

children.text: tato devyau tataḥ śeṣam aśeṣam avarodhanam
children.translated_text: Then the two queens, then all the rest of the inner apartments,

children.text: rājā ca śrutavṛttāntaḥ sāsthāno dhairyam atyajat ||
children.translated_text: and the king too, when he heard what had happened, lost their courage, court and all.
Then, after <s>Padmadevikā</s> of <s>Māgadha</s> soon regained consciousness,
she was asked, "How do you know that she is gone?" and replied, "Listen."
"Just as soon as <s>Gomukha</s> had led her into her own residence,
at once we smelled a fragrance that was not human.

children.text: akasmāc ca kṣaṇaṃ nidrāṃ gacchāmaḥ pratibudhya ca
children.translated_text: Suddenly we fell asleep for a moment, and when we awoke

children.text: śūnyām īkṣāmahe śayyām aśrīkāṃ nalinīm iva ||
children.translated_text: we saw the couch empty, like a lotus-pond bereft of beauty.

children.text: tato hā heti vikruśya samūrchāḥ kṣaṇam āsmahe
children.translated_text: Then, crying 'Ah! Ah!' we remained senseless for a moment,

children.text: na kvacic ca vicinvatyaḥ paśyāmaḥ svāminīm iti ||
children.translated_text: and, though we searched everywhere, we did not see our mistress."
But here <s>Kaliṅgasenā</s>, her voice choked with grief, said:
"I think this has happened through that act of a wicked <s>vidyādhara</s>.
Long ago I took the little girl <s>Madanamañcukā</s>
to the roof of the palace and played with her there, cool in the company of moonlight.
'Come, <s>vidyādharas</s>, come; take this pretty girl,

children.text: ekām eva mayā labdhāṃ sutāṃ durlabhikām iti ||
children.translated_text: my only daughter, obtained with difficulty,' I said.
Then someone descended from the sky, gleaming with shield, sword, armlets, necklaces, and the like,
wearing divine fragrance, garlands, and garments.

children.text: dūrād eva ca māṃ bhītāṃ mā bhaiṣīr iti sāntvayan
children.translated_text: From afar, consoling me as I was frightened, saying, 'Do not be afraid,'
he said this to me, while my daughter was terrified by his deep voice:

children.text: yadi mahyam iyaṃ dattā satyena tanayā tvayā
children.translated_text: 'If this daughter has truly been given to me by you,

children.text: tato muñca nayāmy enāṃ nyāsabhūtā hi kanyakā ||
children.translated_text: then let her go; I will take her, for the girl is a deposit entrusted to me.
By name I am <s>Mānasavega</s>, chief of the hosts of <s>vidyādharas</s>,
my mind illumined by knowledge of all that can be known.'

children.text: anicchantī tatas tasya saṃnidhau ciram āsitum
children.translated_text: Then, not wishing to remain long in his presence,

children.text: prayatnād dhairyam ādhāya pragalbheva tam abravam ||
children.translated_text: I gathered courage with effort and, as if bold, said to him:

children.text: arhaty avaśyam eveyam īdṛśī tvādṛśaṃ patim
children.translated_text: 'Such a girl certainly deserves a husband such as you,

children.text: na punar dīyate tāvad bālikā śaiśavād iti ||
children.translated_text: but while she is still a child she is not yet to be given away.'
Then he saluted me, blazing like a mass of meteors,
and, though visible, disappeared in a moment with great speed.

children.text: tena bravīmi tenādya tat smṛtvā kṣudrabuddhinā
children.translated_text: Therefore I say this: remembering that today, perhaps by him,
by that petty-minded lowest of <s>vidyādharas</s>, she may have been carried off.
In every way Queen <s>Madanamañjukā</s> is not seen here;

children.text: yad atrānantaraṃ nyāyyaṃ tad anuṣṭhīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: whatever is proper next in this matter, let that be done."

children.text: tataḥ samutpatann eva śokaḥ krodhena māmakaḥ
children.translated_text: Then my grief, as it rose up, was driven on by anger,
like a cloud driven by a mighty wind.
"Thief of women, wicked man, fool <s>Mānasavega</s>,

children.text: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha kva yāsīti prālapaṃ gaganonmukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: stop, stop! Where are you going?" I raved, looking up at the sky.
At once, and then gradually, I was dried up by anger and grief,
like a lotus-pond in winter by wind and frost.
But <s>Gomukha</s>, summoned by the king, returned and said this;

children.text: kim etad iti pṛṣṭena vṛttānto 'yaṃ mayoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when he asked, "What is this?" this whole affair was told by me.
Then the king, distraught with sorrow, pulling up his upper garment that had slipped in his agitation,
set out to come to you.

children.text: antare ca rumaṇvantam āha keyaṃ pramāditā
children.translated_text: On the way he said to <s>Rumaṇvant</s>, "What negligence is this?
In every way your skill in policy has been proclaimed by the people.

children.text: yuktaṃ tadā yadālocya mahat sīdat prayojanam
children.translated_text: Was it fitting that, after deliberation, when a great purpose was sinking,
I should be deceived by you and Queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s>?
Even now, while I, a capable minister, am alive,

children.text: apanītā vadhūḥ kasmād bālān mama sutād iti ||
children.translated_text: why was the bride taken away from my young son?"

children.text: sa tam āha nivartadhvam alaṃ tatra gatena vaḥ
children.translated_text: He said to him, "Turn back; there is no use in your going there.

children.text: yuṣmān dṛṣṭvā hi sa śiśuḥ prāṇān api parityajet ||
children.translated_text: For if the boy sees you, he might even give up his life.

children.text: ājñāpayatha māṃ yac ca yac ca vijñāpayāmi vaḥ
children.translated_text: Command me as to whatever you wish, and whatever I report to you,

children.text: āsīnān āsane tena nivṛtya sthīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: let it be received while you turn back and remain seated on your seat."

children.text: upaviṣṭāya cācaṣṭa sphuṭaṃ divyena sā hṛtā
children.translated_text: And to him, once he had sat down, he stated plainly: "She was carried off by a divine being.

children.text: anāthāpi na vaḥ kācit kenacit paribhūyate ||
children.translated_text: No woman belonging to you, even if helpless, is overcome by anyone.
As far as the inner apartments and the garden-grounds, and even the household birds,

children.text: nāsty asau yo na cāsmābhir īkṣitaś cāracakṣuṣā ||
children.translated_text: there is no one whom we have not observed with the eye of spies.

children.text: ākāśe tu na me prajñā kramate divyagocare
children.translated_text: But in the sky, in the sphere of divine beings, my understanding does not move;
therefore in my heart I believe she was carried off by that <s>vidyādhara</s>.
Or else, let the crown prince search in the garden;

children.text: kadācit kupitā bhartre tatrāsīta vadhūr iti ||
children.translated_text: perhaps the bride, angry with her husband, is sitting there.
For five places are heard of for women of good family who are angry with their husbands,

children.text: sādhubhiḥ kathyamānāni pañca sthānāni tad yathā ||
children.translated_text: as they are described by good men, namely:
the house of the mother-in-law, of a brother, of a husband's sister, or of the husband's friend,
or temples and pleasure-groves empty of corrupt traffic."
At this point <s>Marubhūtika</s> told a story:

children.text: prastāve yan mayā pūrvaṃ śrutaṃ tad avadhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: "Listen to what I once heard in a relevant connection.
There was a maiden named <s>Sāvitrī</s>, daughter of <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s>,
who, by the forms of her conduct, surpassed <s>Sāvitrī</s> herself.
Once the sage <s>Aṅgiras</s> asked <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s>:

children.text: brahmann akṛtadāro 'smi sutā me dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Brahman, I am unmarried; let your daughter be given to me.'"

children.text: so 'bravīd bhavataḥ ko 'nyas trailokye 'pi varo varaḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "What other suitor than you, even in the three worlds, is the best of suitors?

children.text: kiṃ tu datteyam anyasmai kṣamatāṃ bhagavān iti ||
children.translated_text: But I am to be given to another; let your honor forgive me."

children.text: tasya bhrātā vṛṣo nāma sa cāṅgirasam abravīt
children.translated_text: His brother, named <s>Vṛṣa</s>, said to <s>Aṅgiras</s>,

children.text: amṛtā nāma duhitā mama sā gṛhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "I have a daughter named <s>Amṛtā</s>; let her be taken in marriage."

children.text: pariṇīya tu tāṃ kanyām amṛtām amṛtopamām
children.translated_text: Having married that maiden <s>Amṛtā</s>, who was like nectar,
<s>Aṅgiras</s> considered himself immortal, as though he had drunk nectar.

children.text: sā kadācit kathaṃcit taṃ kāraṇe 'lpe 'pi pīḍitā
children.translated_text: Once, when she had somehow been hurt by him even over a small matter,
the beloved of the seer's son reproached her lord:
"With reddened eyes you yourself sought <s>Sāvitrī</s>;

children.text: ahaṃ tv anicchate tubhyaṃ pitrā dattā balād iti ||
children.translated_text: but I was given to you by my father by force, though I did not want it."
He soothed <s>Amṛtā</s> with many kinds of oaths,
and passed some time; then one day, when the sun had set,
as he sat engaged in the evening rite, seated and keeping silence,

children.text: apṛcchad amṛtāgatya kiṃ dhyāyati bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Amṛtā</s> came and asked him, "What is your honor meditating on?"

children.text: tena vanditasaṃdhyena cirād uktaṃ nanu priye
children.translated_text: After he had completed the evening worship, he said after a long while, "Surely, beloved,

children.text: devīṃ vihāya sāvitrīṃ kim anyac cintayāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: apart from the goddess <s>Sāvitrī</s>, what else would I think about?"

children.text: atha sā śrutam ity uktvā svasminn āśramapādape
children.translated_text: Then she said, "I have heard," and on a tree in her own hermitage,
after bowing to the deities, she suspended her body.
With the noose drawn tight around her neck, she saw before her a goddess,
with a mass of tawny matted hair like lightning, with rosary and water-pot.
Then the goddess, lighting up the ascetic grove with the radiance of her teeth,
spoke to <s>Amṛtā</s>, as though sprinkling her with nectar:

children.text: putri mā sma tyaja prāṇān dustyajān dharmasādhanān
children.translated_text: "Daughter, do not abandon your life, hard to abandon and the means of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: straiṇam ajñānam āśritya saṃtuṣṭo hi patis tvayā ||
children.translated_text: You have satisfied your husband; you acted from womanly ignorance.
It was not <s>Sāvitrī</s>, daughter of <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s>, whom he was thinking of,
but me, bowed to by the seven worlds beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: sarvathā matprasādāt te putri putro bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: In every way, by my favor, daughter, you will have a son,

children.text: balena tapasā yasya na samāno bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: whose equal in strength and austerity there will not be."

children.text: iti dattvā varaṃ tasyai sāvitrī divam āśrayat
children.translated_text: Having given her this boon, <s>Sāvitrī</s> went to heaven,
and <s>Amṛtā</s>, free from doubt, was united again with her husband.

children.text: tena bravīmi kupitā kadācid amṛteva sā
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: if she, angry like <s>Amṛtā</s>,

children.text: udyānaṃ praviśet tatra svayam anviṣyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: has entered the garden, she should be searched for there in person."
Then I set out, mounted in a palanquin, forgetful of my appearance,
seeing groups of courtesans whose forms stole the eyes and mind.

children.text: āsīc ca mama devībhyāṃ prayogo 'yam anuṣṭhitaḥ
children.translated_text: And this stratagem had been carried out by the queens:

children.text: api nāmāsya kasyāṃcit striyāṃ bhāvo bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: "Perhaps feeling for some woman may arise in him."
But that was a delusive imagining; for in one born of <s>Saṃkalpa</s>,
no desire for other women comes into being.
Then, thinking in this way, I reached the charming house of my beloved's mother,
empty of my beloved, like the sky without moonlight.

children.text: prakāśān aprakāśāṃś ca pradeśān bahuśo bahūn
children.translated_text: Searching again and again through many places, open and hidden,

children.text: anviṣyanto bhramāma sma na cāpaśyāma tatra tām ||
children.translated_text: we wandered about, but we did not see her there.
And, entering the house-garden by the path pointed out by <s>Gomukha</s>,
I asked the branch-dwelling witnesses, the monkeys and birds, for news of my beloved.

children.text: kebhyaścit kupitaḥ śāpān kebhyaścid vitaran karān
children.translated_text: Angry at some, giving supplicating hands to others,
I made a farce of an actor thick with emotion but ignorant of dramatic science.
Then <s>Marubhūtika</s> quickly approached, delighted,
and said, "Noble prince, the noble princess has been seen by me."
Then, stroking his blossoming face with my hand,

children.text: api satyam idaṃ saumya syāt krīḍety aham abravam ||
children.translated_text: I said, "Friend, can this be true, or is it a joke?"

children.text: so 'bravīt satyam apy etat krīḍā yaiṣātiharṣajā
children.translated_text: He said, "It is true; and if this is play, it is play born from excessive joy.

children.text: asatye hy atra yā krīḍā tad unmattavijṛmbhitam ||
children.translated_text: For any play in falsehood here would be the outbreak of madness.
Or rather, enough with reflection, the enemy of great success.

children.text: tvaritaṃ gamyatāṃ yasmān nārtaḥ kālam udīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: Go quickly, since a person in distress does not wait for the proper time."

children.text: paśyāmi sma tato gacchann aśokaśiśum agrataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as I went, I saw in front of me a young aśoka tree,
red with masses of blossoms, its shoots reaching down to the ground.
Thinking, "Why does the aśoka have flowers out of season?"
I saw the giver of my life hidden bashfully against its trunk.

children.text: āsīc ca mama kiṃ citraṃ yat pādasparśadohadaḥ
children.translated_text: And I thought, "What wonder is it that the aśoka, whose longing is for the touch of a foot,
has blossomed at once after gaining contact with all her limbs?
The great wonder here is this: when she looked upon it,
why did the whole garden not blossom at once under this forest deity's glance?
In every way the trees are insentient, since, when my beloved is seen,
fortunate lady, they remain unchanged, like charcoal, chaff, and ash."

children.text: athāliṅgitum ārabdhaḥ sānurāgam ahaṃ ca tām
children.translated_text: Then I began to embrace her with affection,

children.text: tayā cāṅgāni saṃhṛtya mā tāvad iti vāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but she drew in her limbs and stopped me, saying, "Not yet."
Then, seeing me embarrassed by the check to my outstretched arms,
she said, "May the noble prince forgive this obstruction.

children.text: ārādhitavatī yakṣam ahaṃ kanyā satī yathā
children.translated_text: When I was still a maiden, I propitiated a yakṣa, saying,
'May I become the noble prince's beloved attendant.
And when your business is accomplished, with my own hand

children.text: pānaṃ hastena dāsyāmi prasīdatu bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: I will give you a drink fragrant with śamī and parched grain; be gracious.'

children.text: sa ca tasya prasādān me yātaḥ siddhiṃ manorathaḥ
children.translated_text: By his favor that desire of mine has come to fulfillment,

children.text: āyācitaṃ tu yakṣāya na mayā pratiyācitam ||
children.translated_text: but I did not ask the yakṣa to release me from what I had promised.
Therefore I was taken by that drink-loving one to the assembly of <s>Dhanapati</s>,

children.text: vṛttāntaḥ kathitaś cāyam athokto dhanadena saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and this account was told; then <s>Dhanada</s> said to him:
'She will give you what was promised very soon.

children.text: nītvā samarpaya kṣipraṃ dārakāya vadhūm iti ||
children.translated_text: Take the bride and quickly hand her over to the boy.'"

children.text: tena cāham ihānītā gaganāgamanāc ca me
children.translated_text: And I was brought here by him; from traveling through the sky

children.text: śarīraṃ paruṣībhūtaṃ vāritā stha tato mayā ||
children.translated_text: my body had become rough, and so you were held back by me then.

children.text: tasmai yakṣāya yuṣmābhiḥ sa me saṃpādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore have that <s>yakṣa</s> satisfied for my sake.
Then the superintendent of courtesans reported the king's command to her:
"From today onward, let you women have the status of respectable wives."

children.text: taṃ cākarṇya mahāmanoratham idaṃ pūrṇaṃ cirāt kāṅkṣitaṃ naiva prītivikāsihārihasitaṃ dhatte sma kāntāmukham
children.translated_text: And when she heard this, though the great desire she had long wished for had now been fulfilled, my beloved's face did not assume a charming smile blooming with joy.

children.text: yācñāvṛttikadarthitair bahubhir apy āptair na hi prārthakāḥ prītiṃ yānti tathā yathā tanubhir apy arthaiḥ sukhābhyāgataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For petitioners, harassed by a life of asking, do not become so pleased by many gains won through influential friends as they do by even small gains that come easily.

children.text: tato divasam āsitvā kāntāmātur ahaṃ gṛhe
children.translated_text: Then, after spending the day in my beloved's mother's house,
I married my beloved, dressed as a new bride, in the evening.
By the favor of the noble lords' feet she had obtained the status of a respectable wife;

children.text: tām ādāya svam āvāsaṃ pravṛttotsavam āgamam ||
children.translated_text: taking her, I came to my own residence, where a festival had begun.

children.text: tatra sā sadhanādhyakṣaṃ taṃ yakṣaṃ kusumādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: There she worshiped that <s>yakṣa</s>, the overseer of her wealth, with flowers and the like,
and by offering him drink she satisfied him, though he was very hard to please.
Then my beloved took up a ruby cup,

children.text: ādāya madhunaḥ pūrṇāṃ tato mām abravīt priyā ||
children.translated_text: filled with wine whose sheen was like liquid ruby, and said to me:
"Because it is foremost among auspicious things and grants success in undertakings,

children.text: eṣā dhanapateḥ śeṣā svādur āsvādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: this remnant from the Lord of Wealth is sweet; please taste it."
I said, "Without permission from my honored father, I do not wish to enjoy even good things,

children.text: nāhaṃ sevitum icchāmi kiṃ punar vyasanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: much less a great vice."
Then, with firm insistence and oaths that could not be transgressed,
after a long time she reduced me, unwilling, to silence and made me drink.
When I had drunk one cup of wine, she asked me with a smile,

children.text: kimāsvādam idaṃ pānam iti pratyabravaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "What taste does this drink have?" Then I answered:
"In the drinking it has a sweet taste, but in the aftertaste it is bitter;
at the end it is astringent and pungent, and at the finish somewhat so."

children.text: sābravīd vyaktam adyāpi na jānītha rasaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: She said, "Clearly you still do not know the flavor.

children.text: pīyatām iti pītaṃ ca punas tadvacanānmayā ||
children.translated_text: Drink again." And at her words I drank again.

children.text: idaṃ kīdṛśam ity asyai pṛcchatyai kathitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: When she asked me, "What is this one like?" I told her,
