children.text: kim artham api me cittaṃ gatam asvasthatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "For some reason my mind has become unsteady."

children.text: tayoktam aparāpy ekā śuktir āsvādyatāṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: She said, "Then taste one more cup;

children.text: gamiṣyaty acirād eva cittaṃ te svasthatām iti ||
children.translated_text: before long your mind will return to steadiness."

children.text: tasyām api ca pītāyām apaśyaṃ vegavadbhramān
children.translated_text: And when that too had been drunk, I saw swift whirling motions:
trees, palaces, mountains, and other stationary things seemed to move.
And just as she, by refined means, oaths, and the like,

children.text: anicchan pāyitaḥ pānaṃ tathā tām apy apāyayam ||
children.translated_text: had made me drink though I was unwilling, so I made her drink too.
Then, overpowered by the two mighty forces of intoxication and Love,

children.text: yad eva rucitam tābhyāṃ tat taivāsmi pravartitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I was made to do exactly whatever pleased those two.

children.text: yaḥ saṃtoṣayituṃ yakṣaṃ vivāhaḥ kṛtrimaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The marriage that had been contrived to satisfy the <s>yakṣa</s>
gave her, in the same way, only a contrived maidenhood.
Then in the morning <s>Hariśikha</s> came up, smelled the house
pervaded by the scent of wine, and said with his mind alarmed:
"Noble prince, this seems to be an unprecedented smell.
I think you were made to drink against your will by the prince's lady."

children.text: sa mayoktaḥ sakhe sakhyā tavāhaṃ pāyito balāt
children.translated_text: I said to him, "Friend, I was indeed made to drink by your friend by force.

children.text: bhavatāpi rucau satyāṃ sthīyatāṃ pīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: If you too are inclined, stay here and drink."
He said, "I do not see drinking, the headman of the village of vices,

children.text: pānaṃ sādhu na paśyāmi kiṃ punar mantriṇām iti ||
children.translated_text: as good even for you, much less for ministers."
I said, "When the noble lords, together with their friends, are protecting us completely,

children.text: pālayatsu kim asmākam ātmabhir vañcitair iti ||
children.translated_text: what do our deceived selves matter?"
He said, "A matter that has arisen should be reported by ministers and counselors;

children.text: anuṣṭhāne punas tasya svātantryaṃ svāminām iti ||
children.translated_text: but in carrying it out, independence belongs to the masters."
Seeing him drinking together with us two, <s>Marubhūtika</s>

children.text: niḥśaṅkaḥ pātum ārabdhas taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tapantakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: began to drink without hesitation; and seeing him, <s>Tapantaka</s> did too.
Then <s>Gomukha</s>, splendid with red unguents, garlands, and garments,
bowed to me, repeating affectionate talk.
As he sat too close, spoke with excessive affection,
and massaged my feet, <s>Hariśikha</s> angrily said to him:

children.text: unmatta kim asaṃbaddhaṃ bhāṣamāṇaḥ puraḥ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: "Madman, why are you upsetting the master
by speaking incoherently before him? Sit away from him."
He said, "Fool, this is not an outburst produced by the power of intoxication.

children.text: svāmino niḥsapatnau tu pādāv icchāmi sevitum ||
children.translated_text: I wish to serve my master's two feet while they have no rivals.
But when they will be worshiped by the heads of both lords of <s>Vaitardha</s>,
then for us they will have rivals."
At the mention of the name <s>Vaitardha</s>, <s>Madanamañjukā</s>
showed her delight with a smile and, with tearful eyes, said:
"Ah, utterances adorned with the chief qualities of cleverness and sweetness

children.text: ālāpā nirgatāḥ saumyād gomukhasya mukhād iti ||
children.translated_text: have come from the mouth of gentle <s>Gomukha</s>."

children.text: mayoktaṃ bhaṇa paśyāmas tvayā kasmāc ciraṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: I said, "Speak; let us hear why you stayed away so long,

children.text: ko vā tavedam ākāram ujjvalaṃ kṛtavān iti ||
children.translated_text: and who made this bright appearance of yours."
He said, "After we had been summoned by the <s>Māgadhī</s> into the king's presence,

children.text: ājñāpitās tava bhrātrā pānam āsevitaṃ niśi ||
children.translated_text: we were commanded by your brother: 'Wine was enjoyed last night.

children.text: tena pānagṛhāt pānaṃ svādyamānaṃ svadeta yat
children.translated_text: Therefore whatever drink, when tasted from the drinking hall, proves delicious,

children.text: svayam āsvādya tad bhrātre tvayā prasthāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: taste it yourself and have it sent on by you to your brother.'
So I, after being adorned by the two queens with their own hands,
I was brought to the drinking hall, with the superintendent of drinking going before me.

children.text: tatra cāsvādayann eva tat tat pānaṃ manāṅ manāk
children.translated_text: And there, tasting each of those drinks little by little,

children.text: matto 'haṃ preṣayāmi sma yuṣmabhyam api saṃtatam ||
children.translated_text: I, being drunk, kept sending some constantly to you as well.
Therefore drink without hesitation the <s>kāpiśāyana</s> wine,
permitted, together with your ministers, by your delighted elders.
Then, enjoying drink with my circle of beloveds and friends,
I passed the days with my attendants delighted.
Once <s>Madanamañjukā</s>, lying on the same couch,
said, 'When I am sleeping happily I am not to be looked at by you.'

children.text: mama tv āsīt kim ity eṣā nivārayati mām iti
children.translated_text: But I thought, 'Why does she forbid me?'
In truth, my mind was all the more rippled with curiosity.
Once, at midnight, when I, a moving creature with the appearance of something motionless,
awoke thirsty as the drink was passing into its after-effect,

children.text: tataḥ parijanaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasuptam abhavan mama
children.translated_text: then, seeing the attendants asleep, it occurred to me:

children.text: na yuktaṃ sukhasuptasya śatror api nibodhanam ||
children.translated_text: 'It is not right to wake even an enemy who is sleeping happily.
But a wife is half one's own body; therefore <s>Madanamañjukā</s>

children.text: pratibodhya jalaṃ yāce taddhi me na virūpyate ||
children.translated_text: I shall wake and ask for water, for that is not improper for me.'

children.text: iti nirdhārya tasyāṃ ca mayā dṛṣṭir nipātitā
children.translated_text: Having decided this, I cast my gaze upon her,

children.text: yāvad anyaiva sā kāpi nārīrūpaiva candrikā ||
children.translated_text: and behold, she was some entirely different woman, moonlight itself in female form.

children.text: āsīc ca mama kiṃ yakṣī kiṃ gandharvī kim apsarāḥ
children.translated_text: Then I wondered, 'Is she a <s>yakṣī</s>? Is she a <s>gandharvī</s>? Is she an <s>apsaras</s>?

children.text: mānuṣī syāt kulastrī syād gaṇikā syād iyaṃ na hi ||
children.translated_text: She cannot be a human woman, a woman of good family, or a courtesan.
Since she does not fit even one of these by her marks,

children.text: tasmād vidyādharī prāptā kāpi kenāpi hetunā ||
children.translated_text: therefore some <s>vidyādharī</s> has come here for some reason.'
Having decided this, I skillfully took her foot-buds, soft as the palate of a female elephant,
and massaged them firmly.

children.text: sā tu saṃtyājitā nidrāṃ sadyaś caraṇapīḍayā
children.translated_text: But she, her sleep immediately driven away by the pressure on her feet,

children.text: mām ālokya tathābhūtaṃ bhītā bhūmāv upāviśat ||
children.translated_text: looked at me in that state and, frightened, sat down on the floor.

children.text: abravīc ca na kartavyam aryaputreṇa sāhasam
children.translated_text: And she said, 'The noble prince must not do anything rash.
For women are objects of compassion for strong men such as you.'

children.text: tataḥ śrutveti yat satyam ātmany evāsmi lajjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing this, in truth I was ashamed of myself,

children.text: evaṃ kāriṇam apy eṣā saṃbhāvayati mām iti ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'Even when I act like this, she regards me with respect.'
Seeing me ashamed, with my face bent near my knees,
she quickly said this, as if removing my shame:

children.text: śrūyatāṃ cāpriyaṃ sā te priyā madanamañjukā
children.translated_text: 'Hear something unpleasant: that beloved <s>Madanamañjukā</s> of yours
passes her days distracted by remembrance of your virtues.'

children.text: āsīn me manasi hṛtā na sā mṛtā sā yā dṛṣṭer vrajati na gocaraṃ priyā me
children.translated_text: In my mind I thought, 'She has been carried off, not killed; she is my beloved who no longer comes within the range of sight.

children.text: jyotsnā hi sphuṭadhavalāpi kaumudīndor andhānāṃ bahalatamomalīmasaiva ||
children.translated_text: For even the clearly white moonlight of the bright moon is, for the blind, smeared with dense darkness.'

children.text: tatas tām abravaṃ bhīru tvam eva hi mama priyā
children.translated_text: Then I said to her, 'Timid one, you yourself are my beloved;

children.text: tathāpi tu vinodena tiṣṭhāmaḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless, let us pass the time with diversion. Tell me.'
The names of elders, gods, and twice-born men are indeed to be uttered;

children.text: yasmāt tena viśuddhyarthaṃ svānam ācaritaṃ tayā ||
children.translated_text: therefore, for purification, she first recited her own name.
There is a mountain named <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, as lofty as Mount <s>Meru</s>,
the abode of <s>vidyādhara</s> families rich in heroes, scholars, and wealth.
There was a <s>vidyādhara</s> lord, learned and swift, named <s>Vegavān</s>,
who, though richer than <s>Kubera</s>, was as if destitute at life's close.
He too had a queen named <s>Pṛthivī</s>, born in a lofty lineage,

children.text: tṛṇāya manyate sthairyād yā devīṃ pṛthivīm api ||
children.translated_text: who, by her firmness, regarded even the goddess Earth as a blade of grass.

children.text: tau ca putram avindantau ciraṃ duḥkham atiṣṭhatām
children.translated_text: The two of them, not obtaining a son, remained long in sorrow,

children.text: prauḍhāyā iva kanyāyāḥ pitarau sadṛśaṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: like the parents of a grown daughter who have not found a suitable bridegroom.
Desiring a son, they began to propitiate the family vidyā named <s>Manaḥputrikā</s>,
and when she was pleased she said to them:
'A son will be born to you whose <s>vidyādhara</s> prowess surpasses all <s>vidyādharas</s>.

children.text: bhavitā bhavatoḥ putraḥ putrakau duḥkham ujhatam ||
children.translated_text: Dear children, abandon your sorrow.

children.text: ekā ca duhitā yasyāḥ kalāśālī bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And there will be one daughter whose husband will be rich in the arts,
a brave lord of the <s>vidyādharas</s>, like bodiless <s>Anaṅga</s> complete with all limbs.'

children.text: kāle kvacid atīte ca prasūtā pṛthivī sutam
children.translated_text: When some time had passed, <s>Pṛthivī</s> gave birth to a son,
like the well-guarded goddess Earth producing the three aims of life unharmed.
Since he was given by the family vidyā <s>Manaḥputrikā</s>,
the son was adorned by his father with the name <s>Mānasavega</s>.
When three years had passed, for the daughter who was born
<s>Vegavān</s> made a name from his own; therefore she was <s>Vegavatī</s>.
Having obtained the children they desired, those two, rejoicing day and night,
passed a long time as though it were only a single day and night.
One day <s>Vegavān</s>, bathed and having satisfied fire, gods, and twice-born men,
saw himself seated on the auspicious throne in the disk of a mirror.
Then, like a swan perched on the summit of a mountain of collyrium,
he saw a lotus-fiber-white hair on his own head.
Then, leaving the auspicious seat and standing on the bare ground,

children.text: pṛṣṭo mānasavegena kim etad iti vegavān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vegavān</s> was asked by <s>Mānasavega</s>, 'What is this?'
He said, 'On seeing gray hair, those born in the lineage of <s>Manaḥputrikā</s>
undertake austerities, or the practices prescribed by the <s>Vedānta</s>.

children.text: tat prajāḥ pālayeḥ putra prajās tvāṃ pālayantu ca
children.translated_text: Therefore protect the subjects, my son, and may the subjects protect you;

children.text: pālitair hi mṛgendro 'pi kānanair eva pālyate ||
children.translated_text: for even the lord of beasts, when the forests are protected, is protected by those very forests.'
Then, while <s>Mānasavega</s> and the subjects cried out,
the king, only faintly longing for pleasures, went away to the ascetic grove.
Though the queen was being turned back by her husband with reasoned words,

children.text: na nivṛttā yadā devī tadopāyaṃ prayuktavān ||
children.translated_text: when she did not turn back, he employed a stratagem.
"Today I have fallen from my kingdom, and today this faithful wife

children.text: na me sampādayaty ājñām aho dharmaḥ satām iti ||
children.translated_text: does not carry out my command. Ah, such is the <s>dharma</s> of the good!"

children.text: tato hrītā ca bhītā ca sāśruśreṇiḥ savepathuḥ
children.translated_text: Then, ashamed and afraid, with a row of tears and trembling,

children.text: pādayoḥ patitā patyur vyajñāpayad asau śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: she fell at her husband's feet and slowly made her plea.

children.text: yadā tarhi mayā yūyaṃ pāvayantas tapovanam
children.translated_text: "When, then, while you purify the hermitage,

children.text: upāsyāḥ pāvanatamaṃ sa kālaḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: are you to be attended by me, most purifying one? Let that time be told."
He said, "When you have seen your hard-to-obtain son established on a firm throne,

children.text: bhartāraṃ vegavatyāś ca dṛṣṭvā draṣṭāsi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: and also as the husband of <s>Vegavatī</s>, then you shall see me."

children.text: evaṃ caiva ca kalyāṇi pitā vijñāpyatām iti
children.translated_text: "And in just this way, blessed lady, her father should be informed."
So addressed by her mother, <s>Vegavatī</s> bowed to her father and said:

children.text: tāta tvayi vanaṃ yāte ko me dāsyati modakān
children.translated_text: "Father, when you have gone to the forest, who will give me sweets,
or fruits and flowers produced by the wish-fulfilling tree?"
He said, "Whatever rare thing, whatever it may be, you need,

children.text: tat tan mānasavegas te bhrātā dātāsyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: your brother <s>Mānasavega</s> shall give you that and that."

children.text: iti rājyakalatramitraputrān gṛhadhāmaṃ ca tṛṇāya manyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, regarding kingdom, wife, friends, sons, and household as mere grass,

children.text: gurusattvarajastamaḥkalaṅkāṃ prakṛtiṃ hātum agād vanaṃ narendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king went to the forest to abandon <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature), stained by the heavy blemish of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>.
<s>Mānasavega</s> too, skilled in applying the three powers,
made royal fortune, unsteady as a plantain leaf, fixed and immovable.

children.text: atha yāte kvacit kāle mātaṅgādhipateḥ sutā
children.translated_text: Then, when some time had passed, the daughter of the lord of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>,
a friend named <s>Vāyumuktā</s>, came at the <s>Āṣāḍha</s> season, surrounded by companions.

children.text: sā sma vegavatīm āha rājaputri kim āsyate
children.translated_text: She said to <s>Vegavatī</s>, "Princess, why are you sitting here?
Get up; let us go by the path of the sky to <s>Malaya</s> mountain.
Let us amuse ourselves on its lovely peaks, groves, and slopes,
with blindfold games, stories, dolls, and balls."

children.text: tayoktaṃ nāsti me śaktir gantum ākāśavartmanā
children.translated_text: She replied, "I have no power to go by the aerial path;
I have not obtained the family <s>vidyā</s> (magical lore), friend, so forgive that."

children.text: upahasya tatas tās tām uccais tāḍitapāṇayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, mocking her and loudly clapping their hands,
they spread garment-wings and rose into the sky like young swans.
<s>Vegavatī</s> too, distressed, came to her brother's presence,

children.text: tena coktāṅkam āropya mātaḥ kiṃ dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and he placed her on his lap and said, "Dear one, what shall be given?"

children.text: tayoktaṃ dehi me vidyāṃ mahārāja sasādhanām
children.translated_text: She said, "Great king, give me <s>vidyā</s>, together with its means of practice,
for today I was laughed at by friends whose <s>vidyās</s> were perfected."

children.text: acireṇaiva dāsyāmi mātar ity abhidhāya sā
children.translated_text: Saying, "I will give it very soon, dear one,"
her brother dismissed her, deceived with worthless childish ornaments.
One day <s>Gaurimadyaśāḥ</s>, sister of <s>Gaurimuṇḍa</s>,

children.text: gatā vegavatīṃ draṣṭum āṣāḍhaṃ sasakhī sakhīm ||
children.translated_text: went with her friends at the <s>Āṣāḍha</s> season to see her friend <s>Vegavatī</s>.

children.text: upahasya ca tāṃ sāpi vipakṣām iva sārasīm
children.translated_text: She too mocked her, like a wingless crane in an opposing party,
and, winged like a royal swan, went off toward <s>Himācala</s>.
<s>Vegavatī</s> too went to the assembly and said to her brother,

children.text: kim ayaṃ kṣipyate kālo vidyā me dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Why is this time being wasted? Let my <s>vidyā</s> be given to me."

children.text: tenoktam api dāsyāmi tvarase kim akāraṇam
children.translated_text: He said, "I will indeed give it. Why are you hurrying without reason?

children.text: gurukāryakriyāvyagraṃ kiṃ na paśyasi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: Do you not see me occupied with an important duty?"
She went away, quivering under the weight of resentment and as if in haste,

children.text: apatan mātur utsaṅge saṃtapteva vaśā hrade ||
children.translated_text: and fell into her mother's lap like a heat-stricken cow into a lake.

children.text: pṛthivī tu samāhūya sacivau bhartur abravīt
children.translated_text: But <s>Pṛthivī</s>, summoning her husband's two ministers, said:

children.text: acireṇa pitur mūlaṃ dārikāṃ nayataṃ yuvām ||
children.translated_text: "Soon take the girl to her father's side.

children.text: antaraṅgo hi saṃbandhaḥ putraiḥ pitror akṛtrimaḥ
children.translated_text: For the close bond between children and parents is natural and unfeigned;

children.text: bhrātaras tu dviṣanty eva bhrātṝn ekodarān api ||
children.translated_text: but brothers hate even brothers born from the same womb."
Those two took her by the sky-path to the hermitage,
having relieved her weariness at watering stations and resting places along the road.
Then there they saw groups of ascetics performing austerities,
their bodies all bones, bearing matted locks tawny like lightning.

children.text: pṛcchanti sma ca tatraikam abhivādya tapasvinam
children.translated_text: After saluting one ascetic there, they asked him:

children.text: brahman brūhi tam uddeśaṃ yatrāste vegavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "Brahman, tell us the place where <s>Vegavān</s> is staying."
He said, "He is on the mountain peak, standing on the tip of his big toe,
and with his eye he follows the moving sun.
And this is his leaf-hut, in whose courtyard a lion and an elephant,

children.text: aṅgaṇe krīḍataḥ prītāv imau ca śikhipannagau ||
children.translated_text: and these two, a peacock and a snake, play together in affection.

children.text: āsannāgamanaś cāsau dagdhaṃ hi kaṭhinaiḥ karaiḥ
children.translated_text: His arrival is near; for, burned by his hard rays,
this sun is growing dim in order to cool his eye."

children.text: tapastāntaṃ tataḥ kāyaṃ sakāyam iva vegavān
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vegavān</s>, carrying a body exhausted by austerity as though it were another body,
came, bearing bodily hardship, surrounded by <s>Vaikhānasa</s> ascetics and deer.
Then <s>Vegavatī</s>, seeing <s>Vegavān</s> in such a state,

children.text: abravīn mantriṇau nāyaṃ mama tātaḥ sa vegavān ||
children.translated_text: said to the two ministers, "This is not my father, that <s>Vegavān</s>.
The splendors of his moon-bright umbrella, together with the splendors of his crown,
used to illumine the rushing line of feudatory chiefs before him.
But this man comes together with lions, elephants, tigers, deer, and ascetics,
all having abandoned their enmity. Surely he is some magician."

children.text: tābhyām uktaṃ sa evāyaṃ tathā cetthaṃ ca dṛśyate
children.translated_text: The two said, "This is that very man; since this is so, he is seen in this way.

children.text: tādṛśā eva dṛśyante tathā cetthaṃ ca sādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Good men are seen just so, when they are in such a state."
Told, "Honor your father," she bowed, her eyes wet,
and her father lifted her onto his lap, which was wounded by growing darbha shoots.
The two ministers too, standing at a proper distance from their lord,
saluted him with head and words; then <s>Vegavān</s> addressed them:
"Come close to me. Enough of standing so far away.
That drama of kingship, mere pleasing of the people, has passed away."
Then <s>Vegavān</s> questioned the two as they stood on the nearby ritual ground.

children.text: rājño mānasavegasya rājyaṃ no varṇyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let the kingdom of King <s>Mānasavega</s> be described to us."

children.text: tābhyām uktam aśakyaṃ tad guṇāḍhyenāpi śaṃsitum
children.translated_text: The two replied, "That could not be fully described even by <s>Guṇāḍhya</s>;

children.text: tam apekṣya tu rājānaḥ śeṣāś chattraviḍambakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: compared with him, the remaining kings are mere mockeries of royal parasols."

children.text: iyaṃ māṇavikā kasmād ānīteti ca pṛcchate
children.translated_text: And when he asked, "Why has this young girl been brought here?"

children.text: vidyālābhārtham ity uktaṃ tasmai tābhyāṃ savistaram ||
children.translated_text: the two explained to him in detail, "It is for the sake of obtaining <s>vidyā</s> (supernatural knowledge)."
He said, "Before long she will depart, having obtained <s>vidyā</s>;

children.text: yuvābhyāṃ nītipannābhyāṃ sa bālaḥ pālyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: this boy is to be guarded by you two, who are accomplished in policy."

children.text: vegavatyapi sotsāhā karoti sma mahat tapaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vegavatī</s> too, full of zeal, performed great austerity,
having arranged her required food as fruits, roots, water, and air.
By bringing water, sweeping the paths, gathering flowers, and the like,
she propitiated even those <s>Vaikhānasa</s> ascetics who are hard to propitiate.
Once, while she was picking a blossoming forest jasmine,
she came crying to the hermitage, "Alas, I have been bitten by a snake!"
There she was surrounded by the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> boys who were nearby,

children.text: mā rājadārike bhaiṣīr ity uktvā parivāritā ||
children.translated_text: after they had said, "Do not be afraid, princess."

children.text: kvāsau kvāsau khalaḥ sarpa iti pṛṣṭā kumārakaiḥ
children.translated_text: When the boys asked, "Where is that wicked snake? Where is it?"
she told them, "In that jasmine thicket."

children.text: te tv ālokya tam uddeśam avocann uccakaistarām
children.translated_text: But after looking at that spot, they said very loudly,

children.text: rājaputri na sarpo 'yam ayaṃ sarpāntakaḥ śikhī ||
children.translated_text: "Princess, this is not a snake; this is a peacock, the destroyer of snakes.
Seeing its outstretched neck, resembling a hooded venomous serpent,

children.text: tvayā sarpa iti jñātaṃ tasmād āśvasyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: you thought it was a snake. So take heart."
That peacock was brought by the boys to the courtyard of the hut
and was made by her to dance in various ways as she beat out the rhythm.

children.text: prekṣaṇīyaṃ ca tad draṣṭum adṛṣṭaṃ vanavāsibhiḥ
children.translated_text: To see that spectacle, worth seeing and never before seen by forest-dwellers,
all the inhabitants of the ascetic grove assembled and stood there.
Just at this event, when <s>Vegavān</s> had arrived,
the ascetics approached him as he rested and said this:
"O king, the princess has performed austerity that is very hard to perform.

children.text: vayam ārādhitāḥ prītās tadvidyāṃ labhatām iti ||
children.translated_text: We have been propitiated and are pleased; therefore let her obtain that <s>vidyā</s>."

children.text: tenoktaṃ yadi ca prītā no bhavanto 'nujānate
children.translated_text: He said, "If you are pleased and grant us permission,
then let her receive the <s>vidyās</s>, attended by their five auxiliaries.

children.text: anayā yat tapas taptam asmābhiś cedam īdṛśam
children.translated_text: Since such austerity has been performed by her, and since this much has been done by us,

children.text: tad asyāḥ kulavidyānām alaṃ bhavatu siddhaye ||
children.translated_text: let that be sufficient for the success of her family <s>vidyās</s>.
And whatever power of <s>Mānasavega</s> has been produced by his perfection in <s>vidyās</s>,
let this girl obtain four times that strength.

children.text: yaś cāsyāḥ ko 'pi dīrghāyur grahīṣyati varaḥ karam
children.translated_text: And whatever long-lived suitor shall take her hand,

children.text: rājyasya daśamaṃ bhāgaṃ sa madīyasya bhokṣyati ||
children.translated_text: he shall enjoy a tenth part of my kingdom."

children.text: evam uktvā tatas tasyās tat sarvaṃ kṛtavān pitā
children.translated_text: Having spoken so, her father then did all that for her.
She too, having obtained permission, swiftly flew up into the sky.
Then, like a streak of gold, she by her radiance
made the dark expanse of sky tawny as she went, as if it were a touchstone.
Seen by <s>Mānasavega</s>, whose eyes whirled with agitation,
she descended into his assembly, like a goose into a lotus grove.
When he had somehow recognized her, he, as if ashamed,
embraced her, placed her on his lap, and brought her to her mother.
Her mother too, in haste, disregarding even her affection for her daughter,

children.text: apṛcchad api kalyāṇi kuśalī vegavān iti ||
children.translated_text: asked, "My dear, is <s>Vegavān</s> well?"
"Why this fruitless prattle? Attend only to the essential point:

children.text: yāsau vegavatī sāhaṃ tasya vegavataḥ sutā ||
children.translated_text: I am that <s>Vegavatī</s>, daughter of that <s>Vegavān</s>.

children.text: atīte tu kvacit kāle saśarīreva cārutā
children.translated_text: At some time in the past, beauty itself, as though embodied,
a certain excellent woman, was brought by <s>Mānasavega</s> to the earth.

children.text: sā ca tadguṇabhūyiṣṭhāṃ dṛḍhaṃ dveṣṭi kathām api
children.translated_text: And she strongly hates even talk chiefly concerned with his virtues,
as a virtuous woman whose faults have been exhausted hates talk praising desire.

children.text: sa kadācit kvacit kāṃcid dṛṣṭvā tāpasakanyakām
children.translated_text: Once, somewhere, he saw a certain ascetic maiden

children.text: balād bhoktum upakrāntas tayā coktaṃ sphurad ruṣā ||
children.translated_text: and began to enjoy her by force; but she, trembling with anger, said:
"It would be fitting to burn a sinner-minded man like you with the fire of a curse;

children.text: kiṃtu vegavataḥ sādhoḥ putratvaṃ tena mucyase ||
children.translated_text: but because you are the son of the good <s>Vegavān</s>, by that you are spared.
In any case, accept a boon that has the name of a curse:
people like you, usually unsteady in heart, can be reached through fear.
When you desire by force any woman who does not desire you,

children.text: bhavataḥ śatadhā mūrdhā dagdhabuddheḥ sphuṭed iti ||
children.translated_text: your head, man of burnt understanding, shall split into a hundred pieces."

children.text: tatas trastas tataḥ śāpād akāmāṃ kāminīm asau
children.translated_text: Therefore, terrified by that curse, he

children.text: api notsahate draṣṭuṃ kuta eva niṣevitum ||
children.translated_text: does not dare even to look at an unwilling beloved woman, much less to enjoy her.

children.text: sa tu mām abravīn mātas tathā madanamañjukā
children.translated_text: But he said to me, "Mother, <s>Madanamañjukā</s>

children.text: protsāhyatāṃ yathā kṣipram upasarpati mām iti ||
children.translated_text: should be encouraged in such a way that she quickly approaches me."
Then I, with the curiosity of a child's nature,
saw <s>Madanamañjukā</s> in the middle of the aśoka grove,
occupying a small hut made of grown leaves and creepers,
like a faded campaka garland in an old banana-leaf case.
At the head of her leaf-bed a cover had been placed,
and inside the hut a water-filled jar had been set by her.
Then, after winning <s>Mañjukā</s>'s confidence, I said:

children.text: kas te mānuṣakeṇārthaḥ kuru vidyādharaṃ patiṃ ||
children.translated_text: "What use have you for a human man? Take a <s>vidyādhara</s> as your husband.
Silly girl, humans are beset by many diseases and other troubles,
but <s>vidyādharas</s>, through the power of their <s>vidyās</s>, are free from troubles.

children.text: rājā mānasavegas tu bhartā te varṇyatāṃ katham
children.translated_text: And how is King <s>Mānasavega</s> to be described as your husband,
he who is king of the <s>vidyādhara</s> kings rich in abundant splendor?"

children.text: doṣān api manuṣyāṇāṃ gṛhṇāmi sma yathā yathā
children.translated_text: And in whatever ways I kept taking up even the faults of human beings,
In just that way her face became bright with eyes swollen by affection.

children.text: guṇān vidyādharāṇāṃ tu gṛhṇāmi sma yathā yathā
children.translated_text: But whenever I began to mention the virtues of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>,
then in that same measure her face became twisted-eyed with anger.
And when those two passing emotions, affection and anger, left her,
then grief took hold of her, with sighing, tears, and trembling.
Then, wiping away her cold tears, I said to her,

children.text: alaṃ bhagini saṃtapya jīvitaṃ rakṣyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Enough, sister, of tormenting yourself; preserve your life."

children.text: tayā tūktaṃ mayā nedam ātmaduḥkhena rudyate
children.translated_text: But she said, "I am not weeping from pain for myself.

children.text: aśakyaṃ tu bhayaṃ bhīmam āhṛtaṃ mandayā mayā ||
children.translated_text: Rather, foolish as I am, I have brought on a terrible, irresistible danger.
He knows every science and art, is the equal of all handsome men,

children.text: kulavidyādhanair yaś ca tuṅgair api na mādyati ||
children.translated_text: and is not made proud even by lofty birth, learning, and wealth.

children.text: sa madvṛttāntam ajñātvā daśāṃ yāsyati kāmapi
children.translated_text: Not knowing my story, that king of the lunar line,
together with his inner apartments, ministers, and kingdom, will come to some wretched state.

children.text: kiṃ tu pratyāśayā prāṇān ekayā dhārayāmy aham
children.translated_text: Yet I keep my life by one single hope:
that he was clearly designated by the <s>Vidyādharas</s> and others with explicit commands.
This lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> will make the little <s>Vidyādhara</s> serpents,
puffed up with the poison of a mere fragment of magic knowledge, vomit out their venom.

children.text: tataḥ śrutveti yat satyaṃ jātāhaṃ jātasaṃśayā
children.translated_text: Then, hearing this as true, I became filled with doubt:

children.text: vidyādharanarendraḥ syād uta na syād asāv iti ||
children.translated_text: is he to be the lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>, or is he not?

children.text: kiṃ kācid dūtikā yātu sāpy asaktā parīkṣitum
children.translated_text: Should some messenger-woman go? Even she would be unable to test him.

children.text: dūtikā matsamā nāsti svayam eva vrajāmy ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no messenger like me; therefore I myself will go.

children.text: tataḥ svārthāhitotsāhā pṛcchāmi sma tava priyām
children.translated_text: Then, eager for my own purpose and for another's good, I asked your beloved:

children.text: tava priyāya kiṃ vārtā tvadīyā dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'What news of you should be given to your beloved?'

children.text: atha kṣaṇam iva dhyātvā tayoktaṃ smayamānayā
children.translated_text: Then, after thinking for a moment, she said with a smile,

children.text: tulyam evāvayoḥ kāryaṃ śaktau satyāṃ kim āsyate ||
children.translated_text: 'The business of us both is the same; when there is power, why sit still?

children.text: idaṃ hi guru kartavyaṃ kṣiptakālaṃ ca sīdati
children.translated_text: This is a grave duty, and it fails when time is wasted.

children.text: īdṛśaṃ tvādṛśī karma kāryate katham anyathā ||
children.translated_text: How otherwise could a deed like this be carried out by one like you?

children.text: iyaṃ maṇḍalitā veṇī mayā sakhi tavāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: This coiled braid of mine, friend, here before you,
is like a restless, dreadful female serpent, eager to bite.

children.text: dāhyā vā dahaneneyaṃ mocyā vā gṛdhrajambukaiḥ
children.translated_text: Either it must be burned by fire, or handed over to vultures and jackals,
or be burned by the noble prince; terrible it is, with a terrible end.

children.text: gatvā cāgaccha doleva na sthātavyaṃ kvacic ciram
children.translated_text: Go and come back like a swing; do not remain long anywhere.

children.text: asaṅgā hi gatiḥ sakhyāḥ kāntaṃ yāntyāḥ smṛter iva ||
children.translated_text: For the course of a friend going to her beloved must be unhindered, like thought.'
Spoken to thus by <s>Ajjukā</s>, I quickly came here through the sky,

children.text: apaśyam aryaputraṃ ca hā kvāsīti pravādinam ||
children.translated_text: and I saw the noble prince crying out, 'Ah, where are you?'
After considering a blameless means for offering myself,
I showed myself to you in the form of <s>Ajjukā</s>.
And when you, longing for an embrace, were held back,
that was the fault of maidenhood in one born from a pure family.
And the marriage that I caused to be performed for the sake of giving what had not been asked,

children.text: sa ca saṃskartum ātmānaṃ kvātra yakṣaḥ kva cājjukā ||
children.translated_text: that too was to consecrate myself; what yakṣa was there here, and what <s>Ajjukā</s>?

children.text: yac ca pātum anicchantaḥ pāyitāḥ stha balān madhu
children.translated_text: And when you did not wish to drink, yet were made to drink wine by force,

children.text: tatra yat kāraṇaṃ tac ca prāyaḥ pratyakṣam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the reason for that too, in most respects, is plainly before your eyes.

children.text: na draṣṭavyāsmi supteti pratiṣiddhāḥ stha yan mayā
children.translated_text: And when I forbade you, saying, 'I must not be seen while asleep,'
that was to increase your curiosity; girlish nature is contrary.
In every way, enough with detail. <s>Ajjukā</s>, your <s>Madanamañjukā</s>,
has been carried off by wicked <s>Mānasavega</s>, like <s>Lakṣmī</s>.

children.text: tad ājñāpaya māṃ kṣipram imāṃ madanamañjukām
children.translated_text: Therefore command me quickly: I will bring back this <s>Madanamañjukā</s>,

children.text: ānayāmi parair nītāṃ śuddhā nītir iva śriyam ||
children.translated_text: carried off by others, as pure policy brings back royal fortune.

children.text: āsīc ca mama na nyāyyaṃ praiṣaṇīyajanocitam
children.translated_text: And it was not proper for me to make a high-born wife
perform a husband's task fit for a dispatched servant."

children.text: athainām abruvaṃ caṇḍi śrutam ehi śayāvahai
children.translated_text: Then I said to her, "Fierce one, I have heard. Come, let us lie down.

children.text: na hi tāmraśikhaṇḍānām adyāpi sphurati dhvaniḥ ||
children.translated_text: For even now the sound of the red-crested cocks has not begun."
"I too am born in the white lunar line, with forearm and little finger hard as the thunderbolt.
How could I bring back my wives while my enemies remain unslain, blocking the front and rear of my beloved battle?"
Thereafter, in due order, the three headed by <s>Hariśikha</s> arrived,

children.text: prabhāte mām avandanta na tu vegavataḥ sutām ||
children.translated_text: and at daybreak they saluted me, but not the daughter of <s>Vegavat</s>.

children.text: gomukhas tv acirāt prāptaḥ prathamaṃ mām avandata
children.translated_text: But <s>Gomukha</s>, arriving soon after, first saluted me,
and then, with devotion, <s>Vegavatī</s>, who was seated near us.

children.text: asau hariśikhenoktaḥ suṣṭhu khalv asi paṇḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hariśikha</s> said to him, "You are indeed very learned.
For learned men are impartial in considering who is worthy or unworthy of salutation."
Then he replied, "You yourself are more learned than I,

children.text: vandyalakṣaṇayuktāṃ yo vandyām api na vandate ||
children.translated_text: since you do not salute one who is worthy and possesses the marks of one to be honored.

children.text: bhaṇa kena na pūjyeyaṃ yā naḥ pūjyena pūjitā
children.translated_text: Tell me, why should she not be honored, she whom our honored lord has honored?
Surely, dull-witted man, people honor the one honored by the honorable.
A lady, through relation to the lord, deserves salutation like the lord himself.

children.text: candrāsannair hi nakṣatrair lokaḥ kāryāṇi kāryate ||
children.translated_text: For people perform their rites by means of stars standing near the moon."

children.text: ityādi vadatas tasya pakṣam utkarṣayann iva
children.translated_text: As he said this and seemed to strengthen her side,
I related the story of <s>Vegavatī</s> as she had described it.
Delighted at the report and turn of events concerning the <s>Vidyādhara</s> princesses,
they went, saluted, and informed the commander of the army.
By him it was reported to my revered father, and by them to my mothers.
Then, while masses of joyful kettledrums sounded as if for <s>Vṛtraśatru</s>,
amid a glad uproar, dreadful with the crashing roar
of deep, portentous storm clouds, day and night passed as it continued to swell.

children.text: atha senāpatiḥ prāptaḥ prātar mām idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then the commander of the army arrived in the morning and said this to me.

children.text: idānīm eva devībhyāṃ devo vijñāpito yathā ||
children.translated_text: Just now the king was informed by the queens as follows:
"At a wedding celebration, we have never seen a boy himself taken
by any second bride at all.

children.text: tena prasādo yady asti vegavatyā tataḥ saha
children.translated_text: Therefore, if there is favor, let the marriage
of <s>Naravāhanadatta</s> with <s>Vegavatī</s> be performed."

children.text: devena tu vihasyoktam evam astu kim āsyate
children.translated_text: But the king laughed and said, "So be it. Why sit waiting?

children.text: mamāpi hi manasy āsīd ayam eva manorathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This very wish was in my own mind too.

children.text: kiṃ tu mātā varasyātra devī bhavatu māgadhī
children.translated_text: Only let queen <s>Māgadhī</s> be the bridegroom's mother here;
I am the father, and the whole harem is on this bridegroom's side.
Let the son of <s>Vāsavadattā</s> and the daughter of <s>Vegavān</s> be joined;

children.text: rumaṇvadādayaḥ pakṣe tasyā evaṃ bhavantv iti ||
children.translated_text: let <s>Rumaṇvat</s> and the others be on her side in this way."
Then I, surrounded by friends, was led to mother <s>Padmāvatī</s>'s inner apartments,
an auspicious circle made splendid with arrangements of pictures and jewels.
<s>Vegavatī</s> too was led by women who had husbands and many sons
to the elder mother's house, filled with the uproar of play.

children.text: tapantakas tu māgadhyā preṣitaḥ prekṣituṃ vadhūm
children.translated_text: But <s>Tapantaka</s>, sent by <s>Māgadhī</s> to inspect the bride,
was made black with ink on his face and chest by the elder mother.
Then, trembling with anger, he returned and said,
"Prince, look at this kind of insult done to me.

children.text: śvaśrūs te māṃ khalīkṛtya sāntarhāsam avocata
children.translated_text: Your mother-in-law, having mocked me, said with a hidden laugh,

children.text: kva yāsi jālma labdho 'si preṣitas tvaṃ caraḥ kila ||
children.translated_text: 'Where are you going, rogue? You are caught; you were surely sent as a spy.
This is my only little daughter, won by a hundred entreaties;

children.text: asyāḥ saubhāgyam utpādyam avaśyaṃ kārmaṇair mayā ||
children.translated_text: her good fortune must certainly be produced by magic rites by me.
The mother of the bridegroom himself is a great performer of magic rites,
by whom even her husband, though weighty in firmness, has been made to dance in the palm of her hand.
While she is long nurturing her son with her garland of magic rites,

children.text: kiṃ mayā preṣitaḥ kaścid bhavān iva caras tayā ||
children.translated_text: has anyone like you been sent by her as a spy against me?'
After saying this, she made me receive a fearsome series of crescent-shaped blows,

children.text: devyāḥ niṣkramitaḥ svasmād aham antaḥpurād iti ||
children.translated_text: and I was driven out of the queen's own inner apartments."

children.text: tapantakena yā prāptā tatra gatvā viḍambanā
children.translated_text: The humiliation that <s>Tapantaka</s> met after going there
was suffered many times over by the spies sent by the elder mother.
While this affair was unfolding and the ocean of the harem was intoxicated,
I took <s>Vegavatī</s>'s hand, sanctified with mantras.

children.text: atha gatvā svam āvāsaṃ vāsāvāsaṃ praviśya ca
children.translated_text: Then, going to my own residence and entering the dwelling for the night,
I saw <s>Vegavatī</s> as if in a quite different condition.
When addressed, she gave no answer; grasping the edge of her garment, she went

children.text: śayanaṃ ca navoḍheva sevate sma parāṅmukhī ||
children.translated_text: to the bed and, like a newly married woman, lay turned away.

children.text: upasṛtya śanaiś caināṃ bravīmi sma vilakṣakaḥ
children.translated_text: Approaching her slowly, somewhat embarrassed, I said,
"Poor girl, give up this pain caused by playing at bashfulness."

children.text: tayā tu katham apy uktaṃ sphuṭitasmitacandrikam
children.translated_text: But somehow she spoke, with the moonlight of a clear smile breaking forth:
"Prince, what play is there? This command of the elders is weightier.
By my father-in-law's order, in this wedding drama
I have played the difficult role of bride, though the time allowed was brief.
She must be acted so that she appears splendid;
therefore this command of the elders is not to be transgressed. Forgive it."
With her, as this talk of the wedding flowed on,
I passed the night, though it had come, compressed into a single moment.
But when not very little time had passed, <s>Tapantaka</s>, agitated and restless,
hurried and stumbling in speech, said to me:
"Prince, while wandering in the city garden I saw four city goddesses,
their moonlike faces withered by distress.

children.text: nṛpasyāniṣṭam āśaṅkya manye kim api dāruṇam
children.translated_text: Fearing some terrible misfortune for the king, I think

children.text: anyad uccalitāḥ sthānaṃ vihāyemāṃ purīm iti ||
children.translated_text: they have gone elsewhere, leaving their place and this city."

children.text: mayā vegavatī pṛṣṭā kās tā iti tayoditam
children.translated_text: I asked <s>Vegavatī</s>, "Who are they?" She said:
"They are my friends, banished in anger by <s>Mānasavega</s>.

children.text: mama prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ svayam ādāya tāḥ sakhīḥ
children.translated_text: Grant me this favor: I shall myself bring those friends.
In the mere opening of an eye, behold me returned."

children.text: utpatantī mayā dṛṣṭā vegād vegavatī nabhaḥ
children.translated_text: I saw <s>Vegavatī</s> spring swiftly up into the sky,
and then seated on her own seat, surrounded by her friends.
The news of her arrival spread suddenly over the earth,
like the radiance of the moon just released by <s>Svarbhānu</s>.
Then the commander came with learned brahmins,
his large eyes moist with affection, and spoke respectfully:
"The king says to <s>Vegavatī</s>: 'They say that four sisters of yours,

children.text: catasraḥ kila tiṣṭhanti bhaginyaḥ kanyakās tava ||
children.translated_text: maidens, stand near at hand for marriage.
I too have four unmarried sons, young and handsome,
skilled in weapons, treatises, and the arts.
If the princess considers us suitable for alliance,

children.text: tatas tā dārikās tebhyaḥ putrebhyo me dadātv iti ||
children.translated_text: then let her give those girls to my sons.'"
Through <s>Dhīragaṇikā</s>, who conveyed her words, she said,
"I have been favored by the king with favors that bear fruit."

children.text: abhūc ca dārikāpakṣe tadā devī kanīyasī
children.translated_text: Then, on the girls' side, there was the younger queen,

children.text: ahaṃ ca varapakṣe tu tātaḥ sāntaḥpuro 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: while on the bridegrooms' side I was there, and father with the inner apartments.

children.text: yā samṛddhis tadā dṛṣṭā vatsarājakule mayā
children.translated_text: The prosperity that I saw then in the family of <s>Vatsarāja</s>

children.text: tām adyāpi na paśyāmi prāpyāpi śriyam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: I do not see even today, though I have obtained such fortune.
Then <s>Hariśikha</s> and the others grasped the hands of the <s>vidyādhara</s> maidens,
hands moist with perspiration and lovely as lotuses.
When the weddings had been completed, they, like sons of a king of kings,
went to their fathers' houses as though to the palaces of a king of kings.

children.text: prabhāte tān ahaṃ prāptān savrīḍān iva pṛṣṭavān
children.translated_text: At dawn, when they had arrived, I questioned them as if they were embarrassed:

children.text: yātā yasya yathā rātriḥ sa tathā varṇayatv iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let each man describe how the night passed for him."
Then <s>Gomukha</s>, loudly clapping his hands, said:

children.text: tathaiteṣāṃ gatā rātrir mā sma gacchad yathā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Their night passed in such a way; may it never pass that way again.
First, this <s>Hariśikha</s>, skilled in courting maidens,
was scolded by his wife as he touched her: 'Know me to be a minister's daughter!'
Then, embracing the bed and drawn together into a lump like a tortoise shrinking in,
he spent a cruel night, rejected even by sleep.
But this <s>Marubhūtika</s>, though jostled by his wife,

children.text: śūro 'ham iti bhāryāyāḥ pādasthānaṃ na muktavān ||
children.translated_text: saying, 'I am brave,' did not leave the place at his wife's feet.

children.text: tapantakaḥ punaḥ śayyāṃ tyaktvā supto mahītale
children.translated_text: <s>Tapantaka</s>, on the other hand, abandoned the bed and slept on the ground;
for, when there is mud to be washed off, it is better to avoid touching it from afar.
So how will bold <s>vidyādhara</s> women delight
these unlucky men, fearful of union with their beloveds?"
Then <s>Hariśikha</s> said, "Ah, you are a refined city man,
you who, through excessive good fortune, were driven even from the house by your wife.

children.text: yo hi vāsagṛhe suptaḥ prītayā saha kāntayā
children.translated_text: For how could a man who slept in the bedchamber with his loving beloved

children.text: sa kathaṃ paravṛttāntaiḥ kṣapāṃ kṣapitavān iti ||
children.translated_text: have passed the night away with the affairs of others?"
While they were thus mocking one another with unrestrained talk,

children.text: ramamāṇaḥ kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā sasuhṛt pānam ācaram ||
children.translated_text: I stayed for a while enjoying myself with my friends and drank.
Then on the next day, invited by <s>Vegavatī</s>,

children.text: sabhāryāḥ suhṛdas te 'pi tābhir eva sahāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those friends too came with their wives, accompanied by those very women.

children.text: mayoktaṃ yasya yasyāś ca pānaṃ saha na duṣyati
children.translated_text: I said, "For whichever man and woman drinking together is not improper,

children.text: sa tayā sā ca tenaiva pānam āsevatām iti ||
children.translated_text: let him drink with her, and let her drink with him."
<s>Gomukha</s> then drew even <s>Hariśikha</s>'s wife by the hand
and sat down in the drinking place called <s>Śobhājitamṛṇālinī</s>.
<s>Gomukha</s>'s wife said, "If free choice is allowed,

children.text: gṛhītas tarhi niḥśaṅkaṃ mayā hariśikhaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Hariśikha</s> has been chosen without hesitation by me myself."

children.text: āsīnāyāṃ tatas tasyāṃ tena sārdham anantaram
children.translated_text: When she had then sat down with him,
<s>Marubhūtika</s> took <s>Tapantaka</s>'s wife.
But <s>Marubhūtika</s>'s wife approached <s>Tapantaka</s>

children.text: abravīt pariśeṣo 'yaṃ kim anyat kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and said, "This one is what remains; what else is to be done?"
Thus the friends, pure in intention, with their friends' wives,

children.text: vayaṃ ca sahitā dāraiḥ krīḍantaḥ sukham āsmahi ||
children.translated_text: and we together with our wives, remained happily at play.

children.text: kadācit kupitā mahyaṃ yena kenāpi hetunā
children.translated_text: Once <s>Vegavatī</s> became angry with me for some reason or other,
and, though I tried to conciliate her, she slept apart.
After lying awake for a long time, I then fell into deep sleep,
and suddenly awoke, the pupils of my eyes quivering.
Opening my eyes, reddened by prolonged sleep,
I saw myself being carried through the air by someone.
My mind governed by doubt, I wondered,

children.text: ko nu mā nayatīty āsaṃ saṃdehādhīnamānasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Who indeed, among gods, asuras, gandharvas, piśācas, pretas, and rākṣasas, is carrying me?"

children.text: devādīnām ayaṃ sparśo lakṣaṇair na hi vidyate
children.translated_text: "This touch does not have the marks of gods and the rest;
therefore I have been seized by a wicked-minded <s>vidyādhara</s>.
Even when he has fallen into an enemy's hands, it does not befit a kṣatriya,
whose hands and feet are his weapons and allies, to be killed in vain like a cripple.

children.text: tasmād ahaṃ yathāśakti vyāyamya dviṣatā saha
children.translated_text: Therefore, having struggled with the enemy as much as I can,
I shall die." Having resolved this, I prepared to strike him.
Then he laughed and said, "Good, elephant among kṣatriyas.

children.text: svasyāḥ susadṛśaṃ jāteḥ karma vyavasitaṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: You have undertaken an action fitting your own birth.

children.text: vandhyas tu tava saṃkalpaḥ phūtkāro vāsuker iva
children.translated_text: But your intention is fruitless, like the hiss of <s>Vāsuki</s>
when his power has been restrained by a mantra; therefore think on your deity.
Yet I am pleased by this mind of yours, drunk with valor;

children.text: tasmād dadāmi te 'bhīṣṭaṃ dvayor anyataraṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: therefore I grant you the desired one of two boons.

children.text: brūhi kiṃ mriyase dṛṣṭvā priyāṃ madanamañjukām
children.translated_text: Tell me: will you die after seeing your beloved <s>Madanamañjukā</s>,
or shall you be torn apart by makaras in the waters of the great ocean?"

children.text: mama tv āsīn mṛṇālīva cikkhalāt kaluṣād iyam
children.translated_text: But to me this speech, though it issued even from an enemy,
was clear and tender, like a lotus-fiber from foul, turbid mud.

children.text: yadi nāma priyāṃ dṛṣṭvā nyaseyaṃ kāyaśṛṅkhalām
children.translated_text: "If indeed, after seeing my beloved, I lay down the chain of my body,

children.text: tato me śatrumitreṇa bhaved upakṛtaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: then a great favor will have been done for me by an enemy turned friend.

children.text: yaṃ yam eva smaran bhāvaṃ tyajaty ante kaḍevaram
children.translated_text: Whatever state a person remembers when he abandons the body at the end,

children.text: taṃ tam eva kilāpnoti tadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that very state, they say, he attains, being then filled with that state.

children.text: yas tu paśyan puraḥ prītyā priyāṃ prāṇair viyujyate
children.translated_text: But the fortunate man who, seeing his beloved before him with love,
is separated from his life, is united with her immediately thereafter."

children.text: iti saṃkalpayann eva raṇantīṃ kiṅkiṇīm adhaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as I was resolving this, I heard below the sound of tinkling girdle-bells

children.text: śṛṇomi sma prabhātendoḥ paśyāmi sma tanuprabhām ||
children.translated_text: and saw a slender radiance like that of the moon at dawn.

children.text: tāṃ diśaṃ prahitākṣeṇa dṛṣṭā vegavatī mayā
children.translated_text: When I cast my eyes in that direction, I saw <s>Vegavatī</s>,
the moonlight split by the gleam of her reed-arrow and sword,
with the blazing luster of fire born from swelling anger,
like a mass of doomsday fire wishing to burn the worlds.
Yet merely from seeing me, with dense winds of joyful sighs,
she completely extinguished the fire of her anger, though it was thick and unbroken.
Then, placing sword and shield upon her bowed shoulders,
and putting her joined hands upon her head, she spoke humbly, distressed with shame:
"Great king, do not kill this restrained son of <s>Vatsarāja</s>,
this crown prince, who has such a bearing, the husband of your sister.

children.text: yathāhaṃ tava mātuś ca tathāyaṃ mama vallabhaḥ
children.translated_text: As I am dear to you and to your mother, so this man is my beloved."
Therefore let him be released unharmed together with his own wife."
Then, quivering, with a powerful burst of rage and gnashing his teeth,
he spoke to his sister in a voice terrible like a lion's roar:
"Shame on you, a vile woman whose earth-dwelling husband,
chosen by yourself, cannot be kept away, you wicked daughter of your own fancy, with a mind bright as an autumn moon.

children.text: tasyāḥ puro nihatyainaṃ yāsau mām avamanyate
children.translated_text: After killing this man before her, since she despises me,

children.text: tāṃ ca tvāṃ ca tatas tasya gamayiṣyāmi pṛṣṭhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall send both her and you after him."
"Now you are the one killed," she said to her brother;
and by him too, in haste, I was thrown down through the midst of the clouds.
Then <s>Vegavatī</s>, meditating on her family <s>vidyā</s> (magical knowledge), said:
"Goddess, let this noble husband be protected like your own son.
As a leaf lifted by a whirl of wind, circling and circling,

children.text: śanaiḥ śanair mahīṃ yāyāt tathāyaṃ nīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: would come to the earth very slowly, so let this man be carried down."
Then that wicked man, without <s>dharma</s> (righteous restraint) or compassion, raised his sword

children.text: hantuṃ vegavatīm eva pravṛttaḥ prārthitas tayā ||
children.translated_text: and set out to kill <s>Vegavatī</s> herself, though she entreated him:
"Swords do not fall upon women, sisters, and young girls

children.text: nipatanti na nistriṃśāḥ śūrāṇāṃ tvādṛśām iti ||
children.translated_text: who have been fondled on one's lap and breast, at least not swords of heroes like you."
But upon <s>Vegavatī</s>'s waist, delicate and fearful even of the touch of silk,
he brought down a sword-edge capable of cutting through a pillar of adamant.
Then I saw eight <s>Vegavatīs</s>, encircled by fierce weapons,
armed for battle like attendants of <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.
One of them, with the edge of her sword, cut through <s>Mānasavega</s>'s middle,
hard as a thunderbolt, as if it were a hollow plantain-stem.
Then two <s>Mānasavegas</s>, terrifying and gleaming with swords,
arose whole from the two pieces of his body.

children.text: ekā vegavatī kṛttā bhavanty aṣṭau tathāvidhāḥ
children.translated_text: When one <s>Vegavatī</s> was cut down, eight such women appeared;

children.text: tathā mānasavegau dvau prāgalbhetām itas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in the same way two <s>Mānasavegas</s> grew bold here and there.
Thus the sky was filled with hosts of <s>Mānasavegas</s>
and, in a moment, with fourfold numbers of <s>Vegavatīs</s> fighting them.

children.text: ahaṃ tu tanmahāyuddhaṃ paśyann eva śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: But I, while watching that great battle, little by little
fell into a sea-like well, deep and with its water gone far below.
Then, though I was overcome by intense despondency, I laughed and remembered
these words of <s>Saṃjaya</s>, when he was placed in painful distress:
"Escaping somehow from <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, with my mount overrun,
I have fallen into <s>Sātyaki</s>'s army, like a sinner into hell.

children.text: kathaṃ duruttarād asmān mamottāro bhaved iti
children.translated_text: How could I get out of this, so hard to cross?"

children.text: upāyaṃ cintayann eva smarāmi sma kathām imām ||
children.translated_text: And while considering a means, I remembered this tale.
There were once three Brahmin boys who were brothers:
<s>Ekata</s> was the eldest of them, and <s>Dvita</s> and <s>Trita</s> were the middle and youngest.
After the three had studied the threefold Vedic lore, they are said to have informed their teacher:

children.text: gurave dātum icchāmaḥ kāṅkṣitāṃ dakṣiṇām iti ||
children.translated_text: "We wish to give our teacher the fee he desires."
He said, "Go to your own homes, take wives,

children.text: utpādyatām apatyaṃ ca kratubhiś cejyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: produce offspring, and perform sacrifices."

children.text: tair uktam aparā kācid dakṣiṇā mṛgyatām iti
children.translated_text: They said, "Let some other teacher's fee be sought."

children.text: tenoktam alam etena graheṇa bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Enough of this insistence of yours."

children.text: tasmān naivātinirbandhān nivartante sma te yadā
children.translated_text: But when they would not desist from excessive persistence,

children.text: tadā kruddhena guruṇā yācitā dakṣiṇām imām ||
children.translated_text: then the angry teacher requested this fee:
"Give me one thousand cows with white ears,

children.text: kumbhodhnīnāṃ sahasraṃ me datta sthāta ca mā ciram ||
children.translated_text: black like cuckoos and with pot-like udders, and do not delay."

children.text: te tu bhrāntvā mahīṃ kṛtsnām ārūḍhās tuhinācalam
children.translated_text: They wandered over the whole earth and climbed the snowy mountain;

children.text: jñātāḥ kila kubereṇa kauverīṃ prasthitā diśam ||
children.translated_text: as they set out toward <s>Kubera</s>'s northern quarter, <s>Kubera</s> is said to have noticed them.

children.text: kuberasyāpi kiṃ nāsti tena te gurudakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: What, indeed, is not possessed even by <s>Kubera</s>? Therefore, after giving them
the teacher's fee, he sent them on; delighted, they descended from the snowy mountain.

children.text: saṃcaranto bahūn deśāṃś cārayantaś ca gāḥ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Wandering through many lands and slowly pasturing the cows,
they reached hot plains near <s>Caṇḍeśvara</s>, scorched by the fierce sun's rays.
Once <s>Ekata</s>, looking at the cows, said to <s>Dvita</s> and <s>Trita</s>:

children.text: lobhanīyam idaṃ dravyaṃ na parityāgam arhati ||
children.translated_text: "This wealth is tempting and does not deserve to be given away.
Just as some madman, greedy for hearing applause,
might enter fire, so this is what we are intending to do.

children.text: tenedam upapannaṃ ca guruṇā ca mayoditam
children.translated_text: Therefore let this proposal, proper and also spoken by the teacher and by me,

children.text: ramaṇīyavipākaṃ ca vākyaṃ naḥ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and pleasant in its result, be carried out by us."

children.text: athovāca dvitaḥ prīto yuktam āryeṇa cintitam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dvita</s>, pleased, said, "What our elder has thought is fitting;

children.text: na hi svārtheṣu muhyanti buddhayas tvādṛśām iti ||
children.translated_text: the judgments of men like you do not become confused in matters of self-interest."

children.text: ekatas tu tritaṃ dṛṣṭvā tūṣṇīm āsīnam uktavān
children.translated_text: But <s>Ekata</s>, seeing <s>Trita</s> sitting silent, said:

children.text: yad atra yuktaṃ tad brūtāṃ kim udāste bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "Say what is proper here. Why do you remain silent?"

children.text: tenoktaṃ ninditaṃ kurvan na kaścin na nivāryate
children.translated_text: He said, "No one doing a blameworthy thing is not to be restrained;

children.text: pitāpi hi viṣaṃ khādan naiva putrair upekṣyate ||
children.translated_text: even a father eating poison is not simply ignored by his sons.

children.text: tena vijñāpayāmi tvāṃ kriyatāṃ ca vaco mama
children.translated_text: Therefore I make this request of you, and let my words be done:

children.text: buddhivṛddhena hi grāhyaṃ bālād api subhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: a well-spoken saying should be accepted even from a child by one mature in understanding.

children.text: anāryapriyam āryeṇa na kāryaṃ kāryam īdṛśam
children.translated_text: A noble man should not do such a deed, dear to ignoble people.

children.text: kāryaṃ cen mahyam ātmīyam aṃśam āryaḥ prayacchatu ||
children.translated_text: But if it must be done, let my noble elder give me my own share.
I shall give it to the teacher, who is to be aided with his fee,
and, casting off the burden of my promise, I shall become light."

children.text: tataḥ kruddhau ca lubdhau ca kaniṣṭhaṃ jyeṣṭhamadhyamau
children.translated_text: Then the eldest and the middle brother, angry and greedy,
wished to kill the youngest, their minds blinded by greed for the milk.
At some time, blinded by thirst, among a crowd of travelers
The bottom of the well was seen, with no water visible.
To remove their doubt whether there was water there or not,

children.text: teṣām anyatamaḥ pānthaḥ kūpe loṣṭum apātayat ||
children.translated_text: one of those travelers dropped a clod into the well.

children.text: tataḥ ṣvād iti kṛtvā taj jarjaraṃ ghaṭakarparam
children.translated_text: Then, making a sound like 'ṣvād,' it broke a brittle potsherd,

children.text: babhañja sa ca saṃdehaḥ pathikānāṃ nyavartata ||
children.translated_text: and that doubt of the travelers came to an end.
Then <s>Trita</s>, filled with compassion, descended into the well,
and by means of ropes he had the whole set of vessels raised by the travelers.

children.text: tena gāvaś ca pānthāś ca bhrātarau ca mahātmanā
children.translated_text: By that great-souled man the cows, the travelers, and his two brothers
were bathed and given drink, as water was drawn up again and again.
But when the travelers had gone away, and <s>Ekata</s> and <s>Dvita</s> had attained their purpose,

children.text: kūpa eva tritaṃ tyaktvā sagoyūthau palāyitau ||
children.translated_text: they fled with the herd of cows, leaving <s>Trita</s> in the well itself.

children.text: tritas tu ghaṭam ālokya rajjvaiva saha pātitam
children.translated_text: <s>Trita</s>, seeing that the pot had been dropped down together with the rope,
lost hope and for a moment considered a means of getting out.

children.text: āṃ smṛtaṃ labdham ity uktvā vedavṛttāntapeśalaḥ
children.translated_text: Saying, 'Ah, I have remembered; it is found,' that great-minded man, skilled in Vedic tradition,
performed in his mind alone an <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering rite) to <s>Mahendra</s>.
Immediately afterward, rising up, clouds dark with midnight gloom,
bearing bows and lightning, poured down water.
As the well was gradually filled with fresh water,

children.text: prataran prataran dhīraṃ golehyād utthitas tritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: steady <s>Trita</s>, swimming again and again, rose up out of it.

children.text: gatvā ca stokam adhvānaṃ gokhurālīṃ nirūpayan
children.translated_text: After going a short distance and tracing the line of cows' hoofprints,
he saw, as it were, liberation embodied: a bearer of the triple staff.

children.text: abhivādya tam aprākṣīn mārge bhagavatā kvacit
children.translated_text: Having saluted him, he asked, 'Reverend sir, on the road anywhere,

children.text: na dṛṣṭāv evamākārau sagoyūthau dvijāv iti ||
children.translated_text: have you seen two Brahmins of such appearance, together with a herd of cows?'

children.text: tenoktaṃ na mayā dṛṣṭau tau mahāpāpakāriṇau
children.translated_text: He replied, 'I have not seen those two great sinners,

children.text: yau tvāṃ pātālagambhīre kūpe bhrātaram aujhatām ||
children.translated_text: who abandoned you, their brother, in a well as deep as the underworld.

children.text: praṣṭavyāv api na kṣudrau draṣṭavyāv api na tvayā
children.translated_text: Those two petty men should not even be questioned by you, nor even looked at.

children.text: yāv evaṃ ninditācārau praṣṭavyau kuta eva tau ||
children.translated_text: Since their conduct is so blameworthy, how could they be persons to ask about?'

children.text: tam uvāca tritaḥ krodhād dhūrtaṃ kaluṣamānasam
children.translated_text: In anger <s>Trita</s> said to him, a fraud with a stained mind,
'Shame on you, wicked false ascetic, expert in slandering good men!
Those whose piled darkness of delusion has been scattered by the moonbeams of knowledge,

children.text: tādṛśā eva jānanti sādhavaṃ na bhavādṛśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: good men of that kind know goodness, not people like you.'
Then the head of that wandering ascetic, red like a pure copper pot,
became bright with expanding splendor and adorned with a crown.

children.text: śarīraṃ ca sahasrākṣaṃ karaṃ ca kuliśākulam
children.translated_text: His body became thousand-eyed, and his hand filled with the thunderbolt;
taking on such forms and the like, he became wholly <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: varaṃ brūhīti tenoktas tritas tuṣṭas tam abravīt
children.translated_text: When he said, 'Choose a boon,' delighted <s>Trita</s> replied to him,

children.text: bhrātarau me sapāpau ced apāpau bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'If my two brothers are sinful, let them become sinless.'

children.text: punar brūhīti tenoktaḥ punar apy abravīt tritaḥ
children.translated_text: When he said again, 'Choose another,' <s>Trita</s> again replied,

children.text: gurū me gurave gās tāḥ prītau vitaratām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Let my elder brothers, pleased, hand over those cows to my teacher.'
Again, when the most pleased <s>Hari</s> said, 'Ask,'

children.text: paryāptam iti tenokte prītaḥ śakro divaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: and he answered, 'Enough,' pleased <s>Śakra</s> went to heaven.
Thus, after accomplishing a mental <s>iṣṭi</s> whose deity was <s>Mahendra</s>,
<s>Trita</s> rose from that pit as deep as the underworld.

children.text: tathāham api tām iṣṭiṃ kiṃ na kuryāṃ manomayīm
children.translated_text: So why should I too not perform that <s>iṣṭi</s>, made of mind?

children.text: yājakais tu vinā yajñaṃ kṣatriyasya virudhyate ||
children.translated_text: But for a kṣatriya, a sacrifice without officiating priests is improper.

children.text: tasmād asmād upāyena kenottiṣṭheyam ity aham
children.translated_text: Therefore, by what means might I rise from this place?

children.text: iti ceti ca nirdhārya smṛtyāmitagatiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Determining this and that, through recollection I reached <s>Amitagati</s>.
At that time, when he had been released from being tied to the stake, he had asked me,

children.text: kaṣṭām āpadam āpanno vidhaye māṃ smarer iti ||
children.translated_text: 'If you fall into a hard calamity, remember me for help.'
Better that the body, unable to bear the pain of asking, be abandoned,
than that hope of receiving a return favor be held while one is broken by suffering.

children.text: evaṃ ca cintayann eva kūpe kūpataros tale
children.translated_text: While I was thinking thus at the foot of the well-tree in the well,

children.text: apaśyam aham ātmānaṃ taṃ cāmitagatiṃ puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: I saw myself there, and <s>Amitagati</s> before me.

children.text: māṃ cāvocat sa vanditvā harṣaghargharayā girā
children.translated_text: After saluting me, he spoke to me in a voice choked with joy:
'This person has been purified by remembering you; what shall he do?'
I instructed him, 'Give assistance to <s>Vegavatī</s>,
who is fighting in the sky with her stronger brother.'
He said, 'Whoever, through delusion, wishes to give help

children.text: kartum icchati yo mohān mahāgaurīṃ sa rakṣati ||
children.translated_text: to the noble maiden <s>Vegavatī</s> is protecting <s>Mahāgaurī</s>.
But an order has first been given, and it must be carried out by a dependent;
for a master differs from a servant merely by the possession of command.

children.text: tāvat sarojajalajadhvajavajralakṣmyā tvatpādapaṅkajayugaṃ na namāmi yāvat
children.translated_text: I shall not bow to your pair of lotus feet, beautiful with marks of lotus, banner, and thunderbolt, until
they have been worshipped by the enemy's head, its neck cut by my sword and its throat-veins streaming blood.'
Then that man, without bowing to me, with sword in hand and armor on,
rose into the sky when the moonlight of the dim moon and planets was faint.
As he flew upward into the sky with the speed of an arrow,

children.text: na pṛcchāmi sma panthānaṃ deśaṃ nagaram eva vā ||
children.translated_text: I did not ask him about the road, the country, or even the city.
Plunging into a forest crowded with anthills, stumps, and thorns,
full of lions, elephants, and tigers, I went on.
Then I saw the eastern quarter reddening with the glow of dawn,
as though lit by the fire-brilliance of <s>Amitagati</s>'s anger.
After traversing some distance, in a region where the trees were not very dense,
I saw a circle of cows, their bells making clamorous sounds.

children.text: anumāya tatas tena vasantaṃ deśam antike
children.translated_text: Inferring from that that an inhabited district was nearby,
I went on with renewed confidence and in a moment left the forest.
As if afraid of the beginning of the frosty season, from the lotus ponds...
As I went along at sunrise, I saw dusky shadows.
Then I came to a garden with a grove of kunda flowers, its tips dark-blue with swarms of bees,
and with the bases of its trees encircled by watering basins.
There I questioned a garden attendant who was busy sweeping,

children.text: pṛṣṭavān asmi kasyedam udyānam iti so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: asking, "Whose garden is this?" He said:
"How is it that even a divine prince, whose mind is pure with divine knowledge,
asks us, as if taking us for ignorant men blind with lack of understanding?

children.text: athavā kiṃ na etena mahātmāno hi mādṛśaiḥ
children.translated_text: Or rather, what is the use of this? For great-souled beings

children.text: krīḍanti tena devena svayaṃ vijñāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: play with men like me. Therefore let your divine self know it for himself."
Then, entering a second garden still more beautiful than that one,
I saw a garden mansion with a lofty gateway.

children.text: praviśāmi sma tatrāham eko dauvārikaś ca mām
children.translated_text: I was entering it, alone, when a doorkeeper

children.text: antare vetram ādhāya tiṣṭheti dvāry adhārayat ||
children.translated_text: put his cane across my way and stopped me at the door, saying, "Stay there."

children.text: athāvocad dvitīyas taṃ dhik tvāṃ nirbuddhacakṣuṣam
children.translated_text: Then a second doorkeeper said to him, "Fie on you, whose eyes are without understanding!
In your delusion you are barring this sky-roamer.

children.text: kiṃ kadācit tvayā dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vā kaścid īdṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Have you ever seen or heard of anyone like this,

children.text: evaṃ vā praviśan dhīraṃ dharaṇīdhīradhīr iti ||
children.translated_text: or of anyone entering in such a way, steady as the steadfast earth itself?"

children.text: tenoktam ananujñātaṃ bhartrā nāradam apy aham
children.translated_text: The first replied, "Without permission from my master, I would not admit

children.text: viśantaṃ nānujānāmi kiṃ punaḥ saumyam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Nārada</s> if he were entering; how much less a gracious man such as this?
Yet even while he is being held back, this man, with the firm gait of an elephant of the quarters,
will certainly enter. Men like me amount only to harsh speech."
Then I entered the garden mansion, which stirred longing without any apparent cause,
where vīṇās were sounding and birds and monkeys had been tamed.
There, seated on a stone slab with a painted-cloth cushion,
I saw a man like an immortal, a lord among refined city-dwellers.

children.text: upasṛtya tam ābhāṣya bhoḥ sādho sukham āsyate
children.translated_text: Approaching him and addressing him, I said, "Good sir, are you sitting comfortably?

children.text: kaccid vā pratyavekṣyante bahukṛtvaḥ kalā iti ||
children.translated_text: And are the arts being reviewed again and again?"

children.text: vīṇāvyāsaktacittatvāt paśyati sma na mām asau
children.translated_text: Because his mind was absorbed in the vīṇā, he did not see me.

children.text: avakṣiptaṃ hi dṛśyāni manaḥ paśyati nekṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: For it is the mind, when directed toward visible things, that sees them, not the eyes.

children.text: mayā tu calitā vīṇā gṛhītvāgre yadā tadā
children.translated_text: But when I took hold of the front of the vīṇā and moved it,

children.text: vīṇātaś cakṣur ākṣipya mayi nikṣiptavān asau ||
children.translated_text: he drew his gaze away from the vīṇā and fixed it on me.
Then, startled, he rose, his upper garment slipping down,

children.text: mām upāveśayat prītas tasminn eva śilāsane ||
children.translated_text: and gladly seated me on that very stone seat.
He massaged my body, wearied by walking,

children.text: prakṣālya ca svayaṃ pādau dattārghaḥ samupāviśat ||
children.translated_text: washed my feet himself, offered water of welcome, and sat down.

children.text: anuyuktaś ca sa mayā ko 'yaṃ janapadas tvayā
children.translated_text: I then asked him, "What is this country that is adorned by you,

children.text: bhūṣitaḥ katamac cedaṃ puraṃ saccaritair iti ||
children.translated_text: and what is this city, made splendid by good conduct?"

children.text: atha tena vihasyoktaṃ saṃbhāvyā nabhasā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: Then he laughed and said, "Travel through the sky

children.text: tvādṛśāṃ devaputrāṇām ajñānaṃ tu na yujyate ||
children.translated_text: may be expected of divine princes like you, but ignorance is not fitting.

children.text: yo hi deśāntaraṃ yāti mugdho 'pi dharaṇīcaraḥ
children.translated_text: For even a simple earth-walker who goes to another country
does not enter a place lying before him without first learning what it is.
This land is bright as moonlight, and the city is plain in the moonlight;

children.text: na jñātā pathikeneti duḥśliṣṭam iva dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: for a traveler not to know it looks somehow incoherent.
Therefore you must be a prince of the immortals, descended from the sky,
hiding behind the disguise of ignorance in order to sport with men like me."
Then, after considering this, I gave a reply that had the appearance of an answer:
"I am a brahmin from the country of <s>Vatsa</s>; my parents live there.
Once, dissatisfied with my wives, I listened to spell-casters

children.text: śrutvā dārair asaṃtuṣṭo yakṣīṃ kāṃcid asādhayam ||
children.translated_text: and brought a certain <s>yakṣī</s> under my control.

children.text: sā cāhaṃ ca tataḥ prītau śaile śaile vane vane
children.translated_text: Then she and I, both delighted, on mountain after mountain and in forest after forest,

children.text: yad vā yad rucitaṃ tasyai tatra tatrāramāvahi ||
children.translated_text: enjoyed ourselves wherever something pleased her.

children.text: cintitaṃ ca mayā rātrau na me yakṣyā prayojanam
children.translated_text: At night I thought, 'I have no use for a <s>yakṣī</s>.
I shall propitiate a netherworld spell and enjoy an <s>asurī</s>.'
Then that <s>yakṣa</s> maiden, her mind spoiled by jealousy,

children.text: ānīya nabhasā nyastaḥ pure 'smin bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: carried me through the sky and set me down in this city of yours."

children.text: tenoktaṃ na na saṃbhāvyā yakṣarakṣaḥsu caṇḍatā
children.translated_text: He said, "No, no, fierceness among <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> is quite plausible.

children.text: paścāt tāpagṛhītā tu na sā yuṣmān vimokṣyati ||
children.translated_text: But later, seized by remorse, she will release you.

children.text: ko 'yaṃ janapadaḥ syāt kā purīti ca yad ucyate
children.translated_text: As to your question, 'What country is this, and what city?',

children.text: aṅgā janapadaḥ sphītaś campā ceyaṃ mahāpurī ||
children.translated_text: the country is the prosperous <s>Aṅga</s>, and this great city is <s>Campā</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ ca dattako nāma vaṇik paurapuraskṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And I am a merchant named <s>Dattaka</s>, honored by the townspeople,
famous as <s>Vīṇādattaka</s> because of my love for the vīṇā."
Then he summoned an attendant and spoke something in his ear.

children.text: gāḍhaṃ parikaraṃ badhnan dhāvamānaḥ sa cāgamat ||
children.translated_text: The man tied his garment tight, ran off, and came back.
In a moment he returned, his belly heaving with breath,
and said to <s>Dattaka</s>, "My lord, the carriage has arrived."
Then <s>Dattaka</s>, delighted, took a ring from his own finger
and gave it to that man who had carried out the swift errand.
Then, with hands joined, he said, "Lover of a <s>yakṣī</s>, please proceed
to your servant's house with the purifying placement of your feet."
Then I climbed into the carriage that was carrying <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>,
and, taking a lovely route, went toward <s>Campā</s>.

children.text: śṛṇomi sma ca paurāṇāṃ jalpatām itaretaram
children.translated_text: I heard the townspeople talking with one another:

children.text: ciraṃjīvadbhir āścaryaṃ pṛthivyāṃ kiṃ na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: "What wonder is not seen on earth by those who live long?
How far apart are <s>Dattaka</s>, commander of refined city-men, holding his head high,

children.text: kva ca kasyāpi pānthasya rajjubhāge vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and his taking a place at the carrying-rope of some traveler!
Then another said there, "For just this reason he is the best of men,
because he has taken the rope-position for this highest of men.
And this has been inferred from the bearing of one weighted with a mass of virtues."
And indeed even <s>Vasanta</s> is spoken of as his charioteer.
All around I saw, in one place, ploughmen who had abandoned their ploughs
and were intent on playing vīṇās at the bases of their ploughs.
Elsewhere, beneath a banyan tree, there was a circle of cowherds with an unrestrained herd of cattle,
beating stringless vīṇās that gave pain to the ears.
And as I came near the city gate, I saw, spread out for sale,
a row of carts filled with every part of vīṇās.
With my ears shattered by the mallets of stringless sound,
I reached the merchants' street, which looked like a scattered hoard of lotuses.

children.text: kuṅkumaṃ kretum āyātaḥ kaścid vāṇijam abravīt
children.translated_text: Someone who had come to buy saffron said to a merchant,
his mind distracted by vīṇās, "Give me a vīṇā."

children.text: cirād ākarṇya tad vākyaṃ kupitaḥ sa tam abravīt
children.translated_text: After listening to that speech for a long time, the merchant grew angry and said to him,

children.text: vaṇijo 'nye kim utsannā yena khādasi mām iti ||
