children.translated_text: "Have all the other merchants perished, that you are devouring me?"
In this way carpenters, blacksmiths, potters, leatherworkers, and the like,
people of low birth and occupation, were attached to the vīṇā and played it.
Then at last, after a long time, I reached the gate of <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>'s house,
auspicious with golden jars filled with water.

children.text: tatra yānād avaplutya prāviśaṃ gṛham ṛddhimat
children.translated_text: There I leapt down from the vehicle and entered the prosperous house,

children.text: utthāsnur iva medhāvī viśālaṃ hṛdayaṃ śriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: vast, like the heart of Fortune herself, as if she were about to rise.
But <s>Dattaka</s>, standing before us, addressed his male and female servants:
"From today onward you must carry out this man's commands."

children.text: atha vyajñāpayan prahvāḥ sūpakārāḥ sametya mām
children.translated_text: Then the cooks came together, bowed, and informed me:

children.text: ājñāpayata yuṣmākaṃ kaḥ pākaḥ sādhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Command us. What dish is to be prepared for you?"

children.text: mama tv āsīn mayā tāvad brāhmaṇatvaṃ prakāśitam
children.translated_text: But I thought, "For now I have revealed that I am a brahmin,
and brahmins are fond of sweet things such as ghee, milk, and jaggery.

children.text: tad idaṃ yuktam ity etac cintayitvedam uktavān
children.translated_text: Therefore this is appropriate." Having considered this, I said,
"Well then, let pāyasa be prepared, such as can be taken in the hollow of the hands."
Then, shaking his hand as he went, the cook said,
"Where now are those who know the science of preparing food to go?
The cookery treatises that were composed by <s>Bhīmasena</s> and others

children.text: karmakaryo 'pi tāny asmin gṛhe prāyeṇa jānate ||
children.translated_text: are generally known in this house even by the servants.
But now that they have obtained as master a lover of yakṣīs, an expert in food,
they have become useless, fulfilled in a dish of pāyasa.

children.text: aho nāgarakaḥ svāmī svayaṃ pravahaṇena yaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, what a refined master, who by his own carriage
has brought a painted yakṣa here as a lover of yakṣīs!
By all means, fie on the intoxication born of wealth, ignorant of what ought to be done,
by which even someone like me has been reduced to service under such people!"
Then a young attendant, skilled in the science of massage,
rubbed my body pleasantly with scented oil.
Afterwards, having had the rubbing with powder, the bath, the putting on of unworn garments,
and the salutation to the gods performed, I went to the dining hall.
There <s>Dattaka</s>, after bowing to me where I sat in the dining place,
sat down among a row of his brothers, nephews, and others.
My golden bowl, shaped like a potter's wheel,
was filled by the cook with moon-white pāyasa.
Beside the bowl of pāyasa, in vessels made of brilliant jewels,
honey and ghee were set on stands of the finest substance.

children.text: cintitaṃ ca mayā jāto mahānayam upadravaḥ
children.translated_text: And I thought, "This has become a great calamity.
What have I, accustomed to wine and meat, to do with this ghee-laden pāyasa?

children.text: kena nāma prakāreṇa tyajeyam idam ity aham
children.translated_text: By what means can I get rid of this?" After considering,
I threw away a mouthful of pāyasa, saying, "I have been burned."

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃpratyayārthaṃ ca haran dāharujaṃ kila
children.translated_text: And to convince them, as though removing the pain of the burn,
I repeatedly cooled my mouth with mouthfuls of cold water.

children.text: ballavas tu puraḥ sthitvā vīṇādattakam uktavān
children.translated_text: But the cook stood in front and said to <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>,

children.text: nāyaṃ vipraḥ kathaṃ vipraḥ pradviṣyād ghṛtapāyasam ||
children.translated_text: "This man is no brahmin. How could a brahmin hate ghee-pāyasa?"
And the masseur reported this: "His breath, perfumed with the smell of liquor,

children.text: niśvāso 'sya mayā ghrātaḥ śanakair niścarann iti ||
children.translated_text: was smelled by me as it came out softly."
<s>Dattaka</s>, however, covered his own mouth with the tips of his fingers
and, shaking his head, stopped him as he was speaking.

children.text: abravīc ca payaḥpānaṃ yūyaṃ pibata pānakam
children.translated_text: He said, "You drink milk-drinks; you drink sweet drinks.
Let the gathering also be honored by the drinking of sweet drink."

children.text: mayā tu jātatarṣeṇa pāne pariṇatiṃ gate
children.translated_text: But when the drinking had reached its end and I had grown thirsty,
I drank that sweet drink, because of its likeness to liquor, with the very thought that it was liquor.
Having eaten refined food, beginning with varieties of cut meat and crowded with many preparations,
I rose together with <s>Dattaka</s>.
In the place where the meal had been cleared away, on a floor strewn with flowers,

children.text: kāntam adhyāsi paryaṅkaṃ nyastaṃ tatraiva maṇḍape ||
children.translated_text: I sat down on a lovely couch set there in the hall.
With betel fragrant with camphor, triphalā, nutmeg, cloves, and cardamom,
I produced both fragrance and color in my mouth.

children.text: evaṃ ca sukham āsīno vīṇādattakam abravam
children.translated_text: And as I was sitting comfortably in this way, I said to <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>,

children.text: vīṇonmattir iyaṃ kasmāc campāyāṃ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Tell me, why is there this vīṇā-madness in <s>Campā</s>?"
He said, "Here in <s>Campā</s> there is a merchant-lord named <s>Sānudāsa</s>.
He has a daughter named <s>Gandharvadattā</s>, a beauty of the three worlds.

children.text: sa ca tāṃ dhriyamāṇo 'pi varair varaguṇākaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Although she is sought by suitors who are mines of excellent qualities,
for some reason of his own intention he gives her to no one.
Unable to refuse those who ask for her at every moment,

children.text: tena śulkam upanyastaṃ duḥsaṃpādaṃ surair api ||
children.translated_text: he has set a bride-price difficult for even the gods to accomplish.

children.text: apūrvaṃ kila gāyantyās tasyāḥ kim api gītakam
children.translated_text: When she sings, it is said, some unprecedented song of hers...

children.text: yo 'nuvādayitā vīṇāṃ pariṇetā sa tām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Whoever can accompany the vīṇā will marry her.'
'I must marry this woman, I must marry her': thus, shamelessly,

children.text: na kaścid yo na campāyāṃ vīṇayonmattakaḥ kila ||
children.translated_text: there was no one in <s>Campā</s>, it is said, who was not driven mad by the vīṇā.
And before the townsmen, the sixty-four suitors who desired her,

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe ṣaṣṭhe gate māse sā tad gāyati gītakam ||
children.translated_text: every sixth month she sang that song.

children.text: anena ca prakāreṇa yātaḥ kālo mahān ayam
children.translated_text: In this way a long time passed,

children.text: na cāpi vīṇayā kaścid anugacchati tām iti ||
children.translated_text: and yet no one could accompany her on the vīṇā.
At the end of this tale two men, looking like learned Brahmins,
old and carrying canes, spoke to <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>:
'We have been sent by the merchant with a message to you.

children.text: yadi sajjā suhṛdgoṣṭhī samasyā kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: If the company of friends is ready, let the riddle be set.'

children.text: tenoktaṃ suhṛdaḥ sajjā yadi vaḥ susthitā gṛhāḥ
children.translated_text: He replied, 'The friends are ready, if all is well in your houses.

children.text: kalyā gandharvadattā vā sva eva kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Kalyā</s>, or <s>Gandharvadattā</s> herself, do it right here.'

children.text: tatas taṃ pṛṣṭavān asmi mahotsāhena cetasā
children.translated_text: Then, with my mind greatly eager, I asked him,

children.text: rūpaṃ gandharvadattāyāḥ kīdṛg ity atha so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: 'What is <s>Gandharvadattā</s>'s beauty like?' Then he said:
'Her beauty is veiled by the covering of the halo of its own radiance, and the inner chambers of palaces are flooded by the mass of light from her eyes.

children.text: utkṛṣṭavismayavimohitamānasena rūpaṃ nirūpayitum eva mayā na śakyam ||
children.translated_text: With my mind stunned and bewildered by supreme wonder, I am simply unable to describe her form.'
Then, merely by hearing with my ears
that abundance, a treasury of <s>Gandharvadattā</s>'s virtues, my mind was brought under her control.

children.text: pṛcchāmi sma ca bhūyas tam api śakyā bhaven mayā
children.translated_text: Again I asked him, 'Could it be possible for me

children.text: draṣṭuṃ gandharvadatteti tena coktaṃ na śakyate ||
children.translated_text: to see <s>Gandharvadattā</s>?' And he replied, 'It is not possible.

children.text: agāndharveṇa sā draṣṭuṃ devenāpi na śakyate
children.translated_text: She cannot be seen even by a god who is not trained in <s>gāndharva</s> (music).

children.text: yadi cecchatha tāṃ draṣṭuṃ gāndharvaṃ śikṣyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: If you wish to see her, learn <s>gāndharva</s>.'
I said, 'Even when the <s>Nāradīya</s> is completed, one obtains the title "gāndharva," it is said;

children.text: gāndharvaśabdas tat tasmād asmākaṃ kāryatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore let that be done for us.'
Then he summoned a harsh-voiced vīṇā teacher,
an unfortunate man named <s>Bhūtika</s>, whose knowledge of pitches and notes was lost.

children.text: āsīc ca mama taṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṛtaṃ naravānaram
children.translated_text: When I saw that misshapen man-monkey,
I thought, 'Enough of the <s>Nāradīya</s> for me; done with <s>Gandharvadattā</s>.'
Even the gain of a kingdom, after becoming the pupil of such a person, would be blameworthy;

children.text: anyāyāgatam aiśvaryaṃ nindanty eva hi sādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for good people always condemn prosperity obtained by improper means.
<s>Vīṇādattaka</s> and the others honored him

children.text: apūjayan mayā cāsau na draṣṭum api pāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by rising and saluting him, but I could not even bring myself to look at him.

children.text: atha ruṣṭakaṭākṣeṇa lohitākṣaḥ sa vīkṣya mām
children.translated_text: Then that red-eyed man, seeing me with an angry sidelong glance,
sat down on a small seat provided by <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>.

children.text: abravīd dattakas taṃ ca yakṣībhartur dvijanmanaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Dattaka</s> said to him,
'Sir, teach the <s>Nāradīya</s> to this twice-born husband of a <s>Yakṣī</s>.'
He replied, 'Because he is proud, this man despises me,

children.text: na ca pārayate dātuṃ dāridryāt kākaṇīm api ||
children.translated_text: and because of poverty he cannot manage to give even a <s>kākaṇī</s> (small coin).
Knowledge comes by service to the teacher or by abundant wealth;

children.text: na cāsminn ekam apy asti yady asti pratipadyatām ||
children.translated_text: not even one of these is present in him. If it is present, let him undertake it.'
<s>Dattaka</s> said, 'Teacher, you have spoken in an ugly way.

children.text: ko yakṣīkāmukaṃ śakto daridram iti jalpitum ||
children.translated_text: Who is able to chatter that the lover of a <s>Yakṣī</s> is poor?

children.text: yasya dāsaḥ sadāso 'haṃ tvaṃ jānāsy eva mādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: I am always the servant of the servant of the one whose servant I am; you know what people like me are.

children.text: sa yakṣīkāmukaḥ kasmād daridra iti bhaṇyate ||
children.translated_text: Why, then, is that lover of a <s>Yakṣī</s> called poor?
Take even a hundred gold coins, as is fitting for you.

children.text: patite droṇamegho 'pi na tiṣṭhati jalaṃ sthale ||
children.translated_text: When it has fallen on the ground, even the water of a <s>Droṇa</s>-cloud does not remain standing.'
Then, after worshipping <s>Sarasvatī</s> with <s>Nārada</s> and the others as her retinue,
he brought me a vīṇā whose strings were badly arranged.

children.text: mayā tu sā viparyaksthā sthāpitāṅke yadā tadā
children.translated_text: But when I placed it upside down on my lap,

children.text: bhūtiko māṃ dhig ity uktvā vīṇādattakam uktavān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūtika</s> said 'Shame on you!' to me and spoke to <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>:

children.text: na yakṣīkāmuko mandaḥ śakyaḥ śikṣayituṃ mayā
children.translated_text: 'I cannot teach this dull lover of a <s>Yakṣī</s>;

children.text: vīṇāgrahaṇam apy eṣa na jānāti sukhaiditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: softly raised, he does not even know how to hold a vīṇā.

children.text: na nāma svayam etena yadi vīṇā na vāditā
children.translated_text: Even if he has never played the vīṇā himself,
has this ruined-eyed fellow never seen even painted musicians?'

children.text: iti saṃtakṣya māṃ vāgbhir ātodyaṃ parivartya ca
children.translated_text: Thus cutting me with words and turning the instrument around,

children.text: sa niṣādo niṣādaṃ me ṣaḍja ityupadiṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: that base fellow instructed me, saying that my <s>niṣāda</s> (seventh note) was <s>ṣaḍja</s> (first note).
Then, overcome with anger and striking hard,

children.text: catasraḥ pañca vā tantryaś chinnāś caḍ iti visvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I snapped four or five strings with a discordant 'chaḍ.'
Then he said to <s>Dattaka</s>, 'Without collecting a supply of string-winders,

children.text: akṛtvā kiṃ karoty asya nāradīyaṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: why are you having this man's <s>Nāradīya</s> instruction done?'

children.text: ahaṃ tu vismṛtacchadmā chinnatantrīm api kṣaṇam
children.translated_text: But I, forgetting my disguise, for a moment, even with the strings broken,
played the vīṇā softly, because my ears had been steeped in pitch.
Then <s>Dattaka</s> and the others, their eyes opened wide and their ears pricked up,

children.text: kim etad iti jalpanto mām aikṣanta savismayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: looked at me in amazement, saying, 'What is this?'
But <s>Bhūtika</s>, his luster gone through fear, anger, shame, and wonder,

children.text: kākatālīyam ity uktvā gata eva sadakṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: said, 'It was a mere accident,' and went away with his fee.
Thus, after passing the day and taking my evening meal,
I entered sleeping quarters scented with garlands and incense.
Then I enjoyed a bed spread with coverings as soft as swan wings and silk,
with feet made of shining slabs of diamond.
Two young women, whose beauty drew the eyes of the world and whose true ornaments were their own loveliness,
professional beauties, slowly massaged my feet.
With words whose syllables were made still more charming by both natural and artful sweetness,

children.text: vacobhiḥ kila te cittaṃ madīyaṃ hartum aicchatām ||
children.translated_text: they wished, it seemed, to steal my mind.

children.text: vegavatyā vimuktaṃ ca pratibhānti sma tāni mām
children.translated_text: But, since it had been released by <s>Vegavatī</s>, those words appeared to me...
they were tasteless to my ears, like the braying of donkeys.
And since I did not wish to hear them, I made a pretense of sleep.

children.text: atha prasupta evāsmi nirāśe te ca jagmatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then I remained as though asleep, and they, despairing, went away.
When half the night had passed, and my consciousness could be inferred only from my breathing,
I cast off deep sleep, as though I had seen reality and cast off ignorance.
Then I cast my eye on the vīṇā of <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>,
standing on an ivory peg and covered with a painted cloth.

children.text: mama tv āsīd avaśyaṃ māṃ netā śvas tatra dattakaḥ
children.translated_text: But I thought, 'Tomorrow <s>Dattaka</s> will surely take me there,

children.text: vīṇā ca vādanīyā syāc cirotsṛṣṭā ca sā mayā ||
children.translated_text: and the vīṇā will have to be played, though I have long since given it up.
A skill, even when cultivated with devotion, is mastered only with difficulty;

children.text: bhaktyā mātuḥ sapatnīva nisargakuṭilā hi sā ||
children.translated_text: for, like a mother's co-wife, it is naturally crooked even toward devotion.

children.text: vīṇā saṃnihitā ceyaṃ velā ceyaṃ nirākulā
children.translated_text: This vīṇā is close at hand, and this time is free from disturbance;

children.text: jijñāse tāvad ity enāṃ vicāryāhaṃ gṛhītavān ||
children.translated_text: let me test it first.' Having considered this, I took it up.

children.text: utkarṣann apakarṣaṃś ca kāścit kāścin manāṅ manāk
children.translated_text: Raising some strings and lowering others, little by little,
I touched them with the branches of my hand, trying to set them in order.
Then I heard voices outside my own dwelling room:

children.text: samudrasena godatta dhāva dhāva sakhe drutam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Samudrasena</s>, <s>Godatta</s>, run, run quickly, my friend!
In the house of the noble <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>, who has performed meritorious deeds,
the blessed <s>Sarasvatī</s> herself is tuning the vīṇā.
If such is the rise of sound while the vīṇā is being tuned,
what indeed will it be like when the tuning is completed?

children.text: tasmāt sarasvatīvīṇe dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca saṃhate
children.translated_text: Therefore, after seeing <s>Sarasvatī</s> and the vīṇā together and hearing them,
our eyes and ears will attain the power of purification.'
Then in haste I hung that vīṇā back on the ivory peg,
covered my body from head to foot, and, as it were, fell asleep.
But the townsmen turned back, speaking with dejected minds:
'How can <s>Sarasvatī</s> be seen by lowly people like us?'
When the night had been passed and I had performed my morning duties,
<s>Dattaka</s> bowed to me, dressed without ostentation, and said:
'These men-about-town have arrived with their various vehicles prepared and adorned;
therefore you too should go to the musical contest.
Command a vehicle, whether an elephant-cow, a horse, or the like;

children.text: yena vo rocate gantuṃ tena prasthīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: set out by whatever conveyance pleases you.'
I said, 'You may go comfortably in a carriage;

children.text: ahaṃ tu pādacāreṇa gacchāmi śanakair iti ||
children.translated_text: I, however, will go slowly on foot.'
Then, out of regard for me, <s>Dattaka</s> put me at the front
and set out on foot with the circle of townsmen.

children.text: amantrayanta yāntaś ca kruddhā nāgarakā mithaḥ
children.translated_text: As they went, the angry townsmen conferred among themselves:
'This calamity, in the form of a yakṣī's lover, has befallen us.
By his favor we have abandoned our decorated vehicles,
and with our feet we walk through streets as long as our hopes.'
As I strode along the broad, extended streets like the valleys of <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: apaśyaṃ veśmanāṃ mālās tasyaiva sirasām iva ||
children.translated_text: I saw rows of houses, as though they were that mountain's very peaks.
And in the mansions I heard noble women talking, their glances sent through the windows,
their speech as charming as the call of cuckoos.
'Hey <s>Māgadhī</s>, <s>Vaidehī</s>, <s>Malayavatī</s>, <s>Yavanī</s>,
friends, run and look: the yakṣī's lover is coming!
They say this man was thrown down from the sky by a wicked yakṣī,
her mind stolen by jealousy, and was obtained by the well-born <s>Dattaka</s>.

children.text: dhruvaṃ sā rākṣasī yakṣī yadi vā mṛttikāmayī
children.translated_text: Surely she is a rākṣasī-yakṣī, or else made of clay,

children.text: kruddhayā mugdhayā vāpi yayā svārtho na cetitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether angry or foolish, since she did not understand her own interest.

children.text: athavā sarvam evedam alīkaṃ pratibhāti mām
children.translated_text: Or rather, all this seems false to me.

children.text: kva yakṣīkāmikaḥ kvāyaṃ kāmaḥ kāmī rater iva ||
children.translated_text: What has a yakṣī's lover to do with him? This is <s>Kāma</s> himself, a lover like the beloved of <s>Rati</s>.'
Thus, pointed out on every side with fingers,
and worshipped with garlands of lotus-like eyes, I went on.

children.text: atha nāgarakāḥ prāpan sudhāṃ gṛhapater gṛham
children.translated_text: Then the townsmen reached the house of the householder, <s>Sudhā</s>,
as their longings seemed to reach the body of <s>Gandharvadattā</s>.
It had been fashioned from those very substances, gems, gold, ivory, and the rest;

children.text: sphuraddivyaprabhāvāt tu na vidma kiṃmayair iti ||
children.translated_text: yet, because of its flashing divine splendor, we did not know what it was made of.
Then in the first courtyard I saw sixty-four seats set out,
wrapped in broad fine cloth.

children.text: teṣu nāgarakaḥ kaścit kāṃścid āha sma sasmitam
children.translated_text: Among them, one townsman said to some others with a smile,
'Ah, a great insult has come upon the yakṣī's lover!
The friends, <s>Dattaka</s> and the others, admitted together with their attendants,
have arrived sixty-four in number, and there are exactly that many seats.
Seeing the yakṣī's lover as the sixty-fifth, without a seat,

children.text: yat satyaṃ lajjito 'smīti tataś coktam ṛjur bhavān ||
children.translated_text: I am truly ashamed.' Then someone said, 'You are straightforward.
For the man to whom <s>Dattaka</s>, with son, cattle, and kinsmen, is subject,
even <s>Gandharvadattā</s> is easy to obtain; how much more a seat?'

children.text: pañcaṣaṣṭam adṛṣṭvā tu nikṣiptaṃ tatra dattakaḥ
children.translated_text: But when <s>Dattaka</s> saw that no sixty-fifth seat had been placed there,

children.text: dattavān svayam ākṛṣya mahyam ātmīyam āsanam ||
children.translated_text: he himself drew over his own seat and gave it to me.

children.text: te 'pi nāgarakāḥ śeṣāḥ sthite tiṣṭhati dattake
children.translated_text: And the remaining townsmen, while <s>Dattaka</s> stood there,

children.text: tiṣṭhanti sma sthitā eva bhṛtakā iva bhartari ||
children.translated_text: remained standing just as they were, like hirelings when their master stands.
Then another seat, bright with splendor, was given to <s>Dattaka</s>;

children.text: sa tad adhyāsta śeṣāś ca yathāsanam upāviśan ||
children.translated_text: he sat on it, and the others sat down on their proper seats.
Then three hundred courtesans came out from that house,
like daughters of Asuras from the city of a great Asura.
One woman, holding vessels for adornment and pitchers, poured out water.

children.text: tāsāṃ pratyekam ekaikā teṣāṃ pādān adhāvata ||
children.translated_text: Each of those women washed the feet of each of them individually.

children.text: madīyas tu yayā pādaḥ pāṇibhyām avalambitaḥ
children.translated_text: But as for mine, the woman by whom my foot was held with both hands
washed it only with the water of her sweat, her body gone slack.
And the woman who, with rolling eyes, was pouring out water
dropped the water-pitcher from her hand when her hand grew loose.

children.text: praviśan dhautapādaś ca śṛṇomi sma prajalpitāḥ
children.translated_text: And, entering after my feet had been washed, I heard women chattering,
hidden within the high enclosure, their voices charming to the ear:
"This terrible calamity has been arranged by <s>Sānudāsa</s>,
the bride-price of <s>Gandharvadattā</s> called vīṇā-playing.

children.text: yadi rūpam upanyasyec chulkaṃ gṛhapatis tataḥ
children.translated_text: If the householder had set beauty as the bride-price, then
the young lady would obtain no husband other than the lover of yakṣīs.

children.text: vīṇāyāṃ tu prayuktāyāṃ bhagno 'yaṃ no manorathaḥ
children.translated_text: But since vīṇā-playing has been imposed, our hope has been broken,

children.text: hyo yasmād bhūtikenāsya nāradīyaṃ kṛtaṃ kila ||
children.translated_text: for yesterday, they say, <s>Bhūtika</s> made his skill Nārada-like.

children.text: idaṃ tāvan mahad duḥkhaṃ yad yakṣīkāmuko 'nayā
children.translated_text: This, to begin with, is a great sorrow: that for her this lover of yakṣīs
has not become unattainable; because of the flaw in the bride-price she is not out of reach.

children.text: idaṃ tu duḥsahataraṃ yad imāṃ bakulāvalīm
children.translated_text: But this is still harder to bear: that this <s>Bakulāvalī</s>

children.text: anātmajño balāt ko 'pi gale tāṃ lambayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will be hung by force around his neck by some man who does not know himself.
The bride-price is vīṇā-playing, the townsmen are pressing their claims,

children.text: prajāpatiś ca durlagnaḥ sarvathā śivam astv iti ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Prajāpati</s> has made an unlucky conjunction; in every way, may there be welfare."
Then I entered a spacious hall whose pavement was clear as the still water of the <s>Kālindī</s>,
and whose pillars were slabs of blazing jewels.
The hall shone with townsmen adorned with varied brilliance,
like a slope of <s>Meru</s> with wish-trees in bloom.
Then, like a goose pushing aside a circle of lotus leaves,
a chamberlain came out, drawing aside the curtain-cloth.
Bowing humbly, he said to the gathering of townsmen:
"The merchant respectfully announces to you: welcome, lovers of excellence.
By you, splendid in appearance and sound within, this house
has been purified as if by golden jars of <s>Gaṅgā</s> water.
If all have assembled and the fatigue of arrival has passed,
then let the command be given for <s>Gandharvadattā</s>."
They looked at one another, the radiance of their faces faded,
and, ashamed and bereft of reply, stared toward the empty quarters of the sky.

children.text: tataḥ kañcukinā vaktraṃ kṣaṇād dīnatayā kṛtam
children.translated_text: Then in a moment the chamberlain made his face pitiful,
with eyes and cheeks sunken like those of a coward in battle.

children.text: pratyekaṃ ca mukhāny eṣām avalokya ciraṃ ciram
children.translated_text: And when, after looking again and again for a long time at each of their faces,

children.text: sa yadā yātum ārabdhas tadāhūya mayoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he began to go, I called him and said:

children.text: samāptapratikarmā vā kalyā vā yadi sā tataḥ
children.translated_text: "If she has finished her adornment, or if she is ready, then

children.text: āgacchatu kim adyāpi dṛṣṭair nāgarakair iti ||
children.translated_text: let her come. What is there still to be gained by looking at these townsmen?"
At just this much, that face of <s>Dattaka</s>, so withered before,
grew full, heaving with a sigh, its cheeks wet with sweat.
Then the delighted attendants of <s>Sānudāsa</s> said:
"O lover of yakṣīs, you are worthy of honor; by you everything has been made splendid.
By even your mere word we have breathed again after a long time;

children.text: avagrahe hi jīmūto visphūrjann api śobhate ||
children.translated_text: for in a drought a cloud is beautiful even when it only thunders.

children.text: tad evaṃ yādṛśaṃ rūpaṃ yādṛśī cātidhīratā
children.translated_text: Therefore, if knowledge should be like this beauty

children.text: tādṛśaṃ yadi vijñānaṃ bhavet kiṃ na bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: and like this extreme steadiness, what could not come to pass?"
And one townsman, showing a smile, said to another:
"In this world shameless men with lifted faces live happily.

children.text: ko hi vedajaḍaṃ muktvā chāndasaṃ chāttram atrapam
children.translated_text: For who, except a dull Vedic pupil, a shameless student of the Vedas,
would raise his face so among great men?
Even the word "lover of yakṣīs" is only a word in his case.

children.text: kva ca priyaguṇā yakṣī guṇarddhiḥ kva cedṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where is a yakṣī rich in lovely qualities, and where is such a man as this?

children.text: yat kiṃcid api bālānāṃ cetastoṣāya kalpate
children.translated_text: Anything at all can serve to please the minds of children;

children.text: utkaṭena hi nāmnāpi prāyas tuṣyanti ḍiṇḍikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for simpletons are usually satisfied even with a grand name."

children.text: śrutvedam itareṇoktaṃ mā sma nindad bhavān imam
children.translated_text: Hearing this, another said: "Sir, do not criticize this man.
Who knows the conduct of men who move in hidden ways?
Although he gives orders with outstanding boldness as the beloved of a yakṣī,

children.text: yathā paricitaśrīkas tathā māṃ prati śobhate ||
children.translated_text: to me he appears as one familiar with good fortune."

children.text: tato javanikāṃ prerya kanyā kañcukibhir vṛtā
children.translated_text: Then, pushing aside the curtain, the maiden, surrounded by chamberlains,
Lady <s>Gandharvadattā</s> came forth, overpowering the splendor of the hall.

children.text: kathayāmi kathaṃ rūpaṃ tasyāḥ saṃkṣiptam ucyate
children.translated_text: How can I describe her beauty? It may be said briefly:
surely the hosts of apsarases have now taken to renunciation.
And in the middle of the hall a four-sided seat made of ruby stone had been prepared;
she occupied it like a crescent moon upon a twilight cloud.
Because they were overcome by her radiance, the townsmen shrank away,
like beds of white lotuses before the young crescent moon.
Then she humbled the assembly, empty of wisdom and speech
and distinguished only by beauty, as though it were a row of pillars in the hall.
Then, raising his right hand, the chamberlain said:
"Listen to the merchant's words, O elephants among townsmen.

children.text: āste gandharvadatteyam iyaṃ vīṇā ca sāritā
children.translated_text: Here sits <s>Gandharvadattā</s>, and here is the vīṇā <s>Sāritā</s>.

children.text: yo vo vādayituṃ śaktaḥ sa kiṃ tiṣṭhati ḍhaukatām ||
children.translated_text: Whichever of you is able to play it, why does he stand still? Let him approach.

children.text: aśeṣair na ca kartavyā paripāṭir apārthikā
children.translated_text: And a pointless order of turns should not be made by all of you;

children.text: sā hi yuṣmākam asyāś ca lajjākhedaprayojanā ||
children.translated_text: for that would serve only to bring embarrassment and fatigue to you and to her.

children.text: tataḥ svayaṃ bhavadbhiś ca yasmin vo bhāvanāhitā
children.translated_text: Therefore let the man in whom you yourselves have placed your confidence

children.text: yuṣmān ātmānam etāṃ ca sa kleśān mocayatv iti ||
children.translated_text: free you, himself, and her from distress."
Then all the townsmen said to <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>,

children.text: tvaṃ naḥ pūjyaḥ pravīṇaś ca tasmād utthīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'You are honored by us and are skilled; therefore please rise.'

children.text: sa yadā kampitaśirā necchati sma tadāparaḥ
children.translated_text: When he, shaking his head, would not consent, another man,
the most highly regarded among them, went and played the vīṇā.
As he produced notes free from faults

children.text: sampādayati śabdo 'bhūd uccakaiḥ sādhu sādhv iti ||
children.translated_text: and chiefly marked by sweetness, there arose a loud cry: 'Good, good!'
Then, when <s>Gandharvadattā</s> had sung, it occurred to me,
'Ah, now I understand: these men are laboring in vain for that very reason.
Long ago, when <s>Cakrapāṇi</s>, in the form of a dwarf, deceived <s>Bali</s>,
he is said to have crossed the triple heaven in three strides.
And a certain <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, served by hosts of gandharvas,

children.text: krāmantaṃ gaganaṃ vegāt triś cakāra pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: swiftly circled him three times as he strode through the sky.

children.text: tena ca svayam utpādya stuvatā garuḍadhvajam
children.translated_text: Then, himself composing and singing praise of <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s>,
he sang a wondrous song called the <s>Nārāyaṇastuti</s>.
After that it was obtained by <s>Nārada</s>, from <s>Nārada</s> by the enemy of <s>Vṛtra</s>,
then from him by <s>Arjuna</s>, and, so it is said, by the daughter of <s>Virāṭa</s>.
From her <s>Parīkṣit</s> would obtain it, from his mother, and from him <s>Janamejaya</s>.

children.text: iti kramāgataṃ tātas tātād āgamitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: Thus handed down in succession, it came from father to father and has been brought down to me.
It is connected with the <s>gāndhāra-grāma</s> (the gāndhāra tonal scale); what has <s>Gāndhāra</s> to do with mortals?

children.text: svargān nānyatra gāndhāra ity āhur nāradādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> and the others say that <s>Gāndhāra</s> exists nowhere except in heaven.

children.text: tena yo 'yaṃ na jānāti na ced abhyupagacchati
children.translated_text: Therefore, if a man does not know this and does not acknowledge it,

children.text: tad asaṃpādayann eva jāyate doṣavān asau ||
children.translated_text: he becomes faulty precisely by failing to bring it to perfection.

children.text: ahaṃ punar idaṃ jānan sadyaḥ pariṇamatphalam
children.translated_text: But I, knowing this song whose fruit ripens at once,
will exert myself as far as I can before the townsmen.'
While I was forming this resolve, that bull among townsmen,
smiling from embarrassment, returned to his own seat.
Then, when that ornament of his circle of friends had been checked,
the performance broke down like a senior wrestler who has been subdued.
Then <s>Dattaka</s>, seeing me filled with eagerness
and about to rise from my seat, was seized with shame, as if he thought ignorance possible.
But I had supposedly moved from my seat for another reason,
and by that he said, 'One should stand somewhere else than in a cramped place.'

children.text: tatas tam uktavān asmi kim idaṃ na tvayā śrutam
children.translated_text: Then I said to him, 'What is this? Have you not heard

children.text: pathā sakṛt pravṛttāyāḥ kiṃ karoty avaguṇṭhanam ||
children.translated_text: what a veil can do for one who has once set out upon the road?
Just as I entered the gathering of friends through a boy's impetuosity,
so too I have boldly given orders to <s>Gandharvadattā</s>.

children.text: tad asyā baṭuvidyāyāḥ prāntam aprāpya mādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore a man like me, before reaching the end of this boyish learning,

children.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ vañcito 'smīti paścāt tāpena khedyate ||
children.translated_text: is tormented afterward by regret, saying, "Alas, I have been cheated!"

children.text: yatra cāmī na lajjante salajjāḥ suhṛdas tava
children.translated_text: And where these modest friends of yours are not ashamed,
there a man who boasts of shamelessness is ashamed precisely by his shame.
When I argued in this way, <s>Dattaka</s> too had no answer.

children.text: aho sāhasam ity uktvā tūṣṇīṃbhāvam upeyivān ||
children.translated_text: Saying, 'Ah, what daring!' he fell silent.

children.text: aham apy āsanaṃ tyaktvā tiryak paśyati dattake
children.translated_text: I too left my seat, while <s>Dattaka</s> looked sideways,
and took the seat placed beside <s>Gandharvadattā</s>.
Then, seeing the vīṇā brought by the chamberlain, I said,
'Sir, have another one brought. A man like me will not touch this one.
I have seen its belly completely filled with spider-web threads,
by which the whole series of taut strings has been made dull.'
With the tips of their teeth shown in smiles and their glances cast aside,

children.text: mām ālokya tathābhūtam uktaṃ nāgarakair iti ||
children.translated_text: the townsmen looked at me in that state and said:
'This Brahmin should be honored with the foremost banner of shamelessness,
since he has begun a venture that amounts to proclaiming his own excellence.
The branches of our hands have grown hard at the tips with string-calluses,

children.text: karaśākhāś ca no jātā na ca saṃbhāvanedṛśī ||
children.translated_text: and our fingernails are broken, yet no such honor is ours.

children.text: ayaṃ tu komalāgrābhis tantrīr aṅgulibhiḥ spṛśan
children.translated_text: But this man, with soft-tipped fingers touching the strings,
a master of the Veda and its auxiliaries, when will he play the vīṇā?
In every way I have understood this intention of his:
"First I shall produce pleasure for my eyes.
Until the vīṇā is removed and until another is brought,
I shall gaze without obstruction on <s>Gandharvadattā</s>'s beauty.
In streets, squares, and festivals, in the presence of people, I shall say,

children.text: īdṛśī tādṛśī dṛṣṭā rūpiṇī yuvatir mayā ||
children.translated_text: "Such and such a beautiful young woman was seen by me."
And as for his saying that this shell of a vīṇā is stretched with spider-web threads,

children.text: kiṃ tat satyaṃ mṛṣety etad devair vijñāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: let the gods determine whether that is true or false."'

children.text: udveṣṭite ca tat tasmin dṛṣṭaṃ veṣṭanacarmaṇi
children.translated_text: But when its wrapping was unwound, there was seen inside the covering leather
a mass of webbing, thick with circles of spiders thrown into panic.

children.text: atha gandharvadattāyā jātam aṅgaṃ nirīkṣya mām
children.translated_text: Then, as <s>Gandharvadattā</s> looked at me, her body became
confused and overcome with trembling, sweat, horripilation, and bashfulness.
Another vīṇā too, after I struck it and it gave a sharp twang,
was at once set aside because its strings were spoiled by hair.
Then <s>Sānudāsa</s> himself came, carrying a vīṇā
worshipped with fragrant flowers and having a sounding-board shaped like a tortoise.
After circumambulating me, with the hair of his body changed by emotion,
he handed me that sweet-sounding instrument as if it were <s>Gandharvadattā</s> herself.

children.text: mayā tu dhautapādena vīṇāṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: But I, with washed feet, circumambulated the vīṇā
and took my place on the surface of a stool covered with unused cloth.
And when the strings had merely been touched a little by the tips of my fingers themselves...
The string-bindings, in their proper places, produced <s>dhaivata</s> and the other notes.
Then, as the strings slowly swelled in the <s>gāndhāra</s> note,
I said to <s>Gandharvadattā</s>, 'Timid one, sing.'
Though she was bold, when she heard that <s>gāndhāra</s>, fit for the ears of immortals,

children.text: tathā ca dhṛṣṭam ādiṣṭā bālāśālīnatāṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: and was so boldly commanded, the young woman fell into maidenly modesty.
Urging on her, frightened and made mute by shame,

children.text: tad eva gītakaṃ divyam ahaṃ mandam avādayam ||
children.translated_text: I softly played that same divine song.
When the army of her shame had been carried off, and the path had been shown,
holy <s>Sarasvatī</s> began to flow, as though to purify the world.

children.text: vṛttibhir dakṣiṇādyābhis tad gītaṃ gītakaṃ tayā
children.translated_text: That <s>gītaka</s> (song) was sung by her in modes such as the southern one,

children.text: upary upari pāṇyantaiḥ pāṇibhir yojitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: and I joined it higher and higher with hand-strokes ending in the hands.
Then this world became as if darkness, unknown and without distinguishing marks;
the whole world was only ears, with her song alone as their object.
In the assembly, deeply entranced, while she sang and I played softly,
we were overpowered by the sharp sounds of drums from those in aerial cars.
When showers of flowers, together with jewels, fell from heaven,
the chamberlain addressed the members of the assembly, who had regained consciousness:

children.text: bho bho nirmatsarāḥ santaḥ satyam ākhyāta sādhavaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Ho, ho, good men without envy, noble sirs, tell the truth:

children.text: gītaṃ yad anayānena kiṃ tat saṃvāditaṃ na hi ||
children.translated_text: was what she sang not harmonized by this man?'
Then they all raised their hands and said loudly,
'Let this man obtain the maiden, won by a lawful bride-price.'
Then, when the screen had been taken away, the chamberlain drove out
the townsmen, as if they were unbelievers expelled from heaven.
They went out with their splendor destroyed and their hopes broken;
what man of merit would not be pained by the fruitlessness of virtues well practiced?
But I, <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>, was admitted inside by the merchant,

children.text: parīkṣya bahuśo rājñā sacivo guṇavān iva ||
children.translated_text: after being tested many times by the king, like a virtuous minister.
As the townsmen were leaving, the foremost of them said:
'Lord, you are the lover of a yakṣī, a god of superhuman valor.

children.text: vayaṃ gandharvadattā ca sānudāsaś ca sānugaḥ
children.translated_text: We, <s>Gandharvadattā</s>, <s>Sānudāsa</s> with his servants, and his followers
have been rescued by you from a difficult calamity as if in sport.

children.text: kāśmaryaḥ khadirāḥ śākāś campakāś ca saveṇavaḥ
children.translated_text: May the kāśmarya, khadira, śāka, campaka, and bamboos,
which were uprooted for the parts of instruments, grow again as before.
Let the agnihotras be offered; let the twice-born attend to the twilight rites;
let maidens be married, and let women of good families give birth.
Let wandering ascetics, <s>Nirgranthas</s>, monks, <s>Pāśupatas</s>, and the rest
study their own doctrines as received from the mouths of their teachers.
Now that the affliction of the vīṇā has been quieted, let the cities together with <s>Kīra</s>,
and the <s>Aṅgas</s> with <s>Campā</s> and <s>Magadha</s>, lie down happily, their limbs well.'
Then the householder, distressed by fear that his request might be refused,
looked at <s>Vīṇādattaka</s> and spoke in a very low voice:
'Today is an auspicious day. Therefore this hand of <s>Gandharvadattā</s>,
praiseworthy and won by manly valor, should be ritually consecrated.'
Though I desired her, I displayed a false firmness,
and spoke words mixed with a smile, slow with seeming indifference:
'I am a twice-born man, born from a spotless family equal to <s>Meru</s> and <s>Kailāsa</s>;

children.text: pariṇetuṃ na me yuktam asavarṇām imām iti ||
children.translated_text: it is not proper for me to marry this woman of a different varṇa.'
Then <s>Sānudāsa</s> said, 'Marry her without concern;

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ hi savarṇeyam utkṛṣṭā vā bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: for she is of your own varṇa, or perhaps even superior.'

children.text: āsīc ca mama kiṃ mattaḥ kim unmattaḥ kim ārjavaḥ
children.translated_text: And I thought: 'Is this man drunk, or mad, or merely straightforward?

children.text: ayaṃ yasmād asaṃbaddham abuddhir iva bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: For he speaks incoherently, like a man without understanding.

children.text: ahaṃ ceyaṃ ca yady asya brāhmaṇāv iti niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: If he is certain that I and this woman are both Brahmins,

children.text: tato mat katham utkṛṣṭā brāhmaṇī brāhmaṇād iyam ||
children.translated_text: then how is this Brahmin woman superior to me, a Brahmin?

children.text: atha imāṃ brāhmaṇīm eṣa manyate kṣatriyaṃ tu mām
children.translated_text: But if he thinks this woman a Brahmin and me a kṣatriya,

children.text: tathā sati kathāpy eṣā kriyamāṇā virudhyate ||
children.translated_text: then, in that case, even making this proposal is contradictory.

children.text: kiṃ tu saṃbhāvyate nāyam asaṃbaddhaṃ prabhāṣitum
children.translated_text: Yet he cannot be supposed to speak nonsense,
since he speaks as one whose mind is trained in the meanings of <s>dharma</s> and <s>arthaśāstra</s>.
A higher-born man is not tainted when he takes a lower-born wife,

children.text: te ca svā caiva nṛpater ity uktaṃ manunā yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Manu</s> has said, "Those women, and his own as well, are for a king."

children.text: pratyākhyānaṃ ca nitarām iyaṃ nārhati ninditam
children.translated_text: And she by no means deserves the reproach of rejection,
since she has been given to me by my teacher, whose command is unbroken.

children.text: yad ahaṃ grāhitas tena vijñānam atimānuṣam
children.translated_text: The superhuman knowledge with which I was made to be endowed came from him;

children.text: dāpitā yena tenaiva tena tenaiva dāpitā ||
children.translated_text: by that same one, by that very same one, she too was made to be given.
Nor does a maiden who must necessarily be accepted deserve, for long,
the humiliation of rejection, especially when she herself is desirous.
Therefore enough of this obstinacy of mine.' Having so decided,
I accepted <s>Sānudāsa</s>'s request, saying, 'So be it.'
Then, like the son of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the son of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>
took <s>Gandharvadattā</s>'s hand with the marriage rite.

children.text: mandaṃ pādatalena tālam anayā yat kuṭṭayantyāciraṃ gītaṃ mām abhi visphuratkuharitaṃ tāraiḥ subhugnabhruvā
children.translated_text: By that song which she, with beautifully bent brows, sang toward me with ringing high notes while long tapping time softly with the sole of her foot,

children.text: tenaiva pratanūkṛtām apaharann asyāḥ krameṇa trapāṃ nirvāṇān mahatāntareṇa subhagaṃ saṃsāram ajñāsiṣam ||
children.translated_text: and by which she gradually stole away her own thinned-out shame, I understood worldly life to be lovely, though far removed from <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
Together with <s>Gandharvadattā</s> and <s>Dattaka</s>,
I passed the days happily, as <s>Smara</s> does with <s>Rati</s> and <s>Vasanta</s>.
Then, when <s>Gandharvadattā</s> had gone to pay homage to her elders,
<s>Sānudāsa</s> bowed, sat down, and spoke:

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ hi savarṇeyam utkṛṣṭā veti yan mayā
children.translated_text: "Because I earlier informed you that she is of your own class, or even superior,

children.text: yūyaṃ vijñāpitāḥ pūrvaṃ tad etad avadhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: please listen to this matter now.
Here in <s>Campā</s> there once was a merchant named <s>Mitravarman</s>,

children.text: nāmitro nāpi madhyasthaḥ sādhor yasyābhavad bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: for whom, good man that he was, there was on earth neither enemy nor indifferent person.

children.text: tasya mitravatī nāma nāmnā susadṛśī priyā
children.translated_text: He had a beloved wife named <s>Mitravatī</s>, well matched to her name,

children.text: bhāryā maitrīva sādhor yā śatror api hitaiṣiṇī ||
children.translated_text: who, like friendship itself for a good man, wished well even to an enemy.
While those two virtuous people had not obtained a virtuous son,

children.text: aputrān ātmanaḥ paurāḥ saputrān api menire ||
children.translated_text: the townspeople, though they had sons, considered themselves sonless.
One day a Digambara named <s>Sānu</s> came for alms,
able to endure a three-night fast, like <s>Vardhamāna</s>.

children.text: daṃpatibhyām asau tābhyāṃ krītābhyāṃ prīṇitas tathā
children.translated_text: He was so gratified by that couple, who had won him over,
that even unasked he expounded the <s>dharmas</s> taught by <s>Ṛṣabha</s>.
Knowing the essence of the Praśna and other treatises, and understanding their minds,
he, whose instruction was clear, foretold for them a future virtuous son.

children.text: yaś ca putras tayor jātas tasya nāmākarot pitā
children.translated_text: When a son was born to them, his father gave him this name:

children.text: ādiṣṭaḥ sānunā yat tat sānudāso bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: "Since he was foretold by <s>Sānu</s>, let him be <s>Sānudāsa</s>."

children.text: ekaputro 'py asau pitrā durlabhatvāc ca vallabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Though he was an only son, and dear to his father because he had been hard to obtain,
by being taught the sciences he was brought to a state unfamiliar with childhood games.

children.text: upādhyāyaiś ca sotsāhair vinītaḥ sa tathā yathā
children.translated_text: And by zealous teachers he was trained in such a way
that, bashful, he regarded even his own wives as other men's wives.
By that excessive modesty of his, outside the common ways of the world, O king,

children.text: pitarau suhṛdo dārā na kaścin nākulīkṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: no one was made uneasy: not his parents, friends, or wives.

children.text: ādiṣṭaḥ sānunā yo 'sau tayoḥ putraḥ suvṛttayoḥ
children.translated_text: That son of those two people of good conduct, who was predicted by <s>Sānu</s>,

children.text: aham eva sa vo dāsaḥ sānudāsas tathāguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I myself am: your servant <s>Sānudāsa</s>, with just such qualities.

children.text: mama tu dhruvako nāma dhruvamaitrīsukhaḥ sakhā
children.translated_text: Now I have a friend named <s>Dhruvaka</s>, whose happiness lay in steady friendship;

children.text: sa ca mām abravīn mitra kriyatāṃ tad bravīmi yat ||
children.translated_text: and he said to me, "Friend, do what I am about to tell you.
On the bank of the lotus pond in the garden, your friends, together with their wives,
after enjoying water-play, are eating and drinking.

children.text: bhavatāpi sadāreṇa tatra gatvā mayā saha
children.translated_text: You too, with your wife, should go there with me
and today make your beauty, youth, and birth bear fruit.

children.text: dharmārthayoḥ phalaṃ yena sukham eva nirākṛtam
children.translated_text: When a man rejects pleasure itself, the fruit of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>,
where could there be a worse sinner than one who has made <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> fruitless?
And someone who practices <s>dharma</s> in order to obtain happiness in another birth,

children.text: tyaktadṛṣṭasukhaḥ so 'pi vada ko nāma paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while abandoning visible pleasure, tell me, what sort of wise man is he?

children.text: na cāpi svārthasiddhyarthaṃ mayā tvaṃ vipralabhyase
children.translated_text: Nor am I deceiving you for the sake of accomplishing some purpose of my own.

children.text: tathā hi bhīmasenasya vākyam ākarṇyatāṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: For listen to the statement of <s>Bhīmasena</s> as follows:
'Abandoning pleasure whose time has arrived,
and hoping for future pleasure: this is not the way of the intelligent.'"

children.text: mayā tu sa vihasyoktas tuccha eva prayojane
children.translated_text: But I laughed and said to him,

children.text: idaṃ saṃrambhagāmbhīryaṃ śaṅkām iva karoti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: "This solemn intensity over a trivial purpose almost creates suspicion.

children.text: yadi pītaṃ na vā pītaṃ svadārasahitair madhu
children.translated_text: If wine is either drunk or not drunk by men together with their own wives,

children.text: lābhaḥ kas tatra hānir vā rāgo 'yam abhivāsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what gain or loss is there in that? This is passion merely given a pleasing scent.
The fire of passion in living beings is generally kindled by nature itself;

children.text: tam indhayati yan mitra tatra kiṃ nāma pauruṣam ||
children.translated_text: when one fuels it, friend, what manly effort is there in that?
But the man who extinguishes that blazing fire, fed by the ghee-fuel of imagining sense-objects,
with the waters of words of dispassion: he is capable.

children.text: phalaṃ yadi ca dharmasya sukham īdṛśam iṣyate
children.translated_text: And if pleasure of this kind is regarded as the fruit of <s>dharma</s>,
then let there be an end to <s>dharma</s> and to the pleasure that is its fruit.

children.text: yāṃ yathāsukham āsīnām aśnantīṃ ca striyaṃ prati
children.translated_text: When, because of prohibition, one does not look at a woman

children.text: nekṣyate pratiṣedhāt sā katham evaṃ viḍambyate ||
children.translated_text: sitting and eating as she pleases, how is she mocked in this way?
A wife standing in the middle of a party circle, her mind overcome by intoxication,
as if seized by a faint from poison, is a disgrace to her husband.

children.text: athavā gacchatu bhavān yathāsukham ahaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Or rather, you may go as you please; but I, for my part,

children.text: na yāsyāmi na dhāsyāmi dāraiḥ saha sabhām iti ||
children.translated_text: will not go, nor will I place my wife in such an assembly."

children.text: sa tataḥ sthirasaṃkalpaṃ māṃ dṛṣṭvā pratyavasthitam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing me firm in my resolve and standing opposed,
he took my hand with a smile, as if sorrowful, and said:

children.text: suhṛdām agrataḥ kṛtvā pratijñām aham āgataḥ
children.translated_text: "I made a promise in front of my friends and came here,
saying, 'This <s>Sānudāsa</s> has been brought with his wife; let him be seen.'
When I am loudly mocked by my friends,
how will you be able to look at my face, withered from the breaking of my promise?

children.text: tat prasīdāsatāṃ nāma dārā yadi virudhyate
children.translated_text: Therefore be gracious. If bringing your wife is unsuitable,
then let the fulfillment of my promise be accomplished by you alone.

children.text: sadoṣaṃ yadi pānaṃ ca svayaṃ mā sma pibas tataḥ
children.translated_text: And if drinking has fault in it, then do not drink yourself;
just watch your friends drinking, together with their wives and sons."
Then, going with him to the lotus pond in the city garden,

children.text: tāṃ tadā dṛṣṭavān asmi sakalatrāṃ suhṛtsabhām ||
children.translated_text: I saw that gathering of friends with their wives.
With flower ornaments and garments whose splendor put <s>Indra</s>'s bow to shame,
it looked like a lotus pool on dry land, casting off the appearance of the water-lotus pond.
Then <s>Dhruvaka</s> brought me a high seat,

children.text: kalpitaṃ dhruvako mahyam uccam āharad āsanam ||
children.translated_text: arranged with networks of <s>Mādhavī</s> blossoms and mango shoots.
Seated there, I saw my friends giving drink to their beloveds,
and drinking wine offered from the palms of their delighted beloveds.
In one place I heard a spring melody being sung,
accompanied by the sounds of flute and lute, while bees and cuckoos cried out.
Leaving the tips of the kurabaka trees,
the bees had fallen upon the karṇikāras, lovely in color and form, as if their noses had been cut off.
From root to crest, the tilaka, aśoka, and kiṃśuka trees were in full bloom;
for from an insubstantial actor arise excessively heightened <s>rasas</s> (flavors and moods).
Then a man, his body smeared with mud and his garment muddied with water-weeds,

children.text: utthitaḥ puruṣaḥ ko 'pi sarasaḥ sarasas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: rose up from that lake, someone very merry indeed.
Taking up a lotus-leaf cup filled by someone,

children.text: bhoḥ puṣkaramadhu prāptaṃ mayeti ca mudāvadat ||
children.translated_text: he joyfully said, 'Look, I have obtained <s>puṣkaramadhu</s> (lotus honey)!'

children.text: pratiṣiddhaḥ sa caikena mūrkha mā caṇḍam āraṭīḥ
children.translated_text: But one man stopped him: 'Fool, do not shout so wildly.
You have not obtained lotus honey; you have acquired this calamity.

children.text: yadi tāvad idaṃ sarve pibanti suhṛdas tataḥ
children.translated_text: For if all your friends drink this,
not even a drop, a share the size of an atom, will remain.

children.text: dīyate yadi vā rājñe durlabhaṃ pārthivair api
children.translated_text: Or if it is given to the king, though it is rare even for kings,

children.text: aparaṃ so 'pi yāceta ratnagṛddhā hi pārthivāḥ ||
children.translated_text: he too will ask for more, since kings are greedy for treasures.

children.text: taṃ ca karṇejapāḥ kecid vakṣyanti priyavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: And some whisperers in his ear, men who speak pleasing words, will say to him,

children.text: rājann aparam apy asti tatra prāptam idaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "O king, there is still more there, since this was obtained from there."

children.text: etāvad eva tatrāsīn nātiriktam iti bruvan
children.translated_text: If he says, "There was only this much there, nothing more,"
by what means will he prove the absence of what is more?

children.text: iti protsāhitaḥ pāpair labdhāsvādaś ca pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus urged on by wicked men, and having tasted its flavor, the king

children.text: haret sarvasvam asmākaṃ tasmāt tasmai na dīyate ||
children.translated_text: would take all our property; therefore it must not be given to him.

children.text: kiṃtu rasyatarāsvādaṃ na ca madyaṃ yatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: But since it has a most delicious taste, and yet is not wine,

children.text: idaṃ puṣkaramadhv eṣa sānudāsaḥ pibatv iti ||
children.translated_text: let this <s>Sānudāsa</s> drink this lotus honey.'
Because it was so hard to obtain, and because my friends begged me,

children.text: na ca madyam iti śrutvā pītavān asmi tan madhu ||
children.translated_text: and hearing that it was not wine, I drank that honey.

children.text: āsīc ca mama ko nāma ṣaṇṇām eṣa raso bhavet
children.translated_text: Then I wondered, 'Which one of the six <s>rasas</s> could this taste of mine be?

children.text: lakṣyate na hi sādṛśyam etasya madhurādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: No likeness to sweet and the other tastes is perceived in it.

children.text: na cāhaṃ ṣaḍbhir ārabdhaḥ saṃhatya madhurādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Nor was I fashioned by the six tastes, sweet and the rest, combined together,

children.text: sarvajñair api durjñānā yenāsminn ekaśo rasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: such that, even by all-knowing men, its tastes in me would be hard to discern one by one.

children.text: tena manyata evāyaṃ saptamaḥ suraso rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore this must be considered a seventh, supremely delicious <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: rasite 'mṛtam apy asmin gacched virasatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Once this has been tasted, even nectar would fall into tastelessness.'
Then, made shameless by the fragrance of that flavor and by thirst,

children.text: bādhate māṃ pipāseti śanair dhruvakam abruvam ||
children.translated_text: I said softly to <s>Dhruvaka</s>, 'Thirst is tormenting me.'

children.text: tena dattaṃ tu tat pītvā svabhāvāpoḍhamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: After drinking what he gave me, my mind was driven from its natural state,

children.text: tat puropavanaṃ vegāc cakravad bhramad abhramam ||
children.translated_text: and I staggered swiftly through that city garden, spinning as if like a wheel.
Then, clear and sweet like a long flute at dawn,
I heard the sound of a woman's crying, faint and slow.

children.text: atha gatvā tam uddeśam apaśyaṃ mādhavīgṛhe
children.translated_text: So I went to that place, and in a bower of mādhavī creepers I saw
a woman sitting there, as if she were the very goddess of the mādhavī grove.
Even in tales, stories, poems, and plays,
we had never heard of such a woman, even when one was being described.

children.text: tatas tām abravaṃ sāmnā bhadre yadi na duṣyati
children.translated_text: Then I said to her gently, 'Good lady, if it is not improper,

children.text: duḥkhasyāsya tato hetur mahyam ākhyāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: please tell me the cause of this sorrow.'
Then she spoke in a low voice, broken by weeping:

children.text: duḥsahasyāsya duḥkhasya nanu hetur bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Surely you are the cause of this unbearable sorrow.'
Then, with my head bowed in shame, I said softly,

children.text: yadīdaṃ matkṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhīru mā tvaṃ rudas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Timid one, if this sorrow has been caused by me, then do not weep.

children.text: yad anantam anantārghaṃ tan manye draviṇaṃ tṛṇam
children.translated_text: I regard limitless and priceless wealth as straw,

children.text: śarīrakam apīdaṃ me kvacid vyāpāryatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and even this body of mine may be employed somewhere.'
Then she said with a smile, her eyes clouded by tears of joy,
'It is precisely this body of yours that I desire.
For I am <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>, a sky-going daughter of a yakṣa,
and by the mind-born god I have been made to form a great longing for you.

children.text: tad ehi gṛham asmākaṃ satyaṃ mantrayase yadi
children.translated_text: So come to our house, if you are truly giving counsel honestly;

children.text: śarīrasyāsya te tatra viniyogo bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: there let this body of yours find its employment.'

children.text: kṛṣyamāṇas tayā cāhaṃ pāṇāv ādāya mantharam
children.translated_text: And as she drew me along slowly, taking me by the hand,
I entered the lordly mansion, shaped like the inner apartments of the asuras.
There I saw a fair woman, with white and black hair,
marked by lines of folds on her large belly and wrapped in pure, fine garments.

children.text: sā mām arghyeṇa saṃbhāvya mūrdhni cāghrāya sādaram
children.translated_text: She honored me with arghya and affectionately smelled my head,
and said, 'My son, you are weary from the road; rest.'
Then, showing regard, she ordered the maidservants: '<s>Sānudāsa</s> is thirsty;

children.text: tat puṣkaramadhu svādu śīghram ānīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: bring the sweet lotus honey quickly.'

children.text: mama tv āsīd dhruvaṃ yakṣī gaṅgadattānyathā kutaḥ
children.translated_text: But I thought, '<s>Gaṅgadattā</s> must certainly be a yakṣī; otherwise how

children.text: gṛhe puṣkaramadhv asyā duṣprāpaṃ mānuṣair iti ||
children.translated_text: could she have in her house this lotus honey, so hard for human beings to obtain?'
I entered a bedchamber perfumed by the powerful fragrance
of lotus honey and strewn with spring flowers.

children.text: pītvā ca puṣkaramadhu prītayā sahitas tayā
children.translated_text: And after drinking lotus honey together with her, delighted as she was,
I offered to her my own body, which I had promised before.
By giving my own body to me, who had formerly helped her,
she too, in order to repay the favor, presented her own body.

children.text: āsīn me yan mayā dattvā śarīraṃ puṇyam arjitam
children.translated_text: I thought, 'By giving my body I had earned merit;
through gaining the maiden's body, its fruit has ripened immediately.'

children.text: iti tatra ciraṃ sthitvā pṛcchāmi sma priyāṃ priye
children.translated_text: After staying there a long time, I asked my beloved, 'Dear one,

children.text: kim idānīṃ suhṛdgoṣṭhī karītīty atha sābravīt ||
children.translated_text: what is my gathering of friends doing now?' Then she said:

children.text: yadi te draṣṭum icchāsti mayaiva sahitas tataḥ
children.translated_text: 'If you wish to see them, then together with me
go and look at your circle of friends, bewildered by the excess of drink.

children.text: mayālambitahastaṃ tvāṃ na kaścid api paśyati
children.translated_text: As long as I hold your hand, no one at all will see you;
therefore, unseen by your company of friends, watch them freely.'
Then, supported by <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>, I went to that garden.
I saw the circle of friends, their faces turned aside with smiles.
Then a certain friend, with a casual expression, said:

children.text: na dṛśyate sānudāsaḥ kva nu yāto bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Sānudāsa</s> is not to be seen. Where can he have gone?"

children.text: apareṇoktam āścaryam adṛṣṭaṃ kiṃ na paśyasi
children.translated_text: Another said, "Amazing! Do you not see what has never been seen before?
A yakṣa maiden, hard to win, has been won by <s>Sānudāsa</s>.
Held by the hand by the yakṣī, invisible,
this fortunate <s>Sānudāsa</s> is moving among his friends. Let him be seen!"

children.text: gaṅgadattām athāvocam adṛśyo yady ahaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then I said to <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>, "If I am invisible,

children.text: bhadre katham anenoktam adṛśyo dṛśyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: dear one, how did this man say, 'Though invisible, let him be seen'?"
Then, though I tried hard to hold it back in the gathering of people,
laughter suddenly burst forth, swelling like a flood of water.
One of them, dancing with the sound of clapping and laughter,

children.text: mām avocad adṛśyāya yakṣībhartre namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: said to me, "Homage to you, invisible husband of a yakṣī!
What has lotus-wine to do with a rare yakṣa maiden here?

children.text: drākṣāmadhu tvayā pītaṃ sādhitā ca vilāsinī ||
children.translated_text: You drank grape-wine, and you won the charming woman.
In every way this hard-to-cure disease of modesty in you
has today been treated by the skillful group of friend-physicians.

children.text: sa bhavān gaṅgadattāyā gṛhaṃ yātu nirāmayaḥ
children.translated_text: So let Your Honour go, cured, to <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>'s house;
and let all your friends too, having achieved their purpose, go each as is proper."

children.text: ahaṃ tu puṣkaramadhu chadmanā chalito 'pi taiḥ
children.translated_text: But though I had been deceived by them under the pretext of lotus-wine,
having learned the taste of the wine that was my beloved, I did not become angry with them.

children.text: āsīc ca mama te dhīrā ye svabhyastamadhupriyāḥ
children.translated_text: And I thought: "Those steadfast men are brave who, though fond of wine well practiced,
become liberation-seeking renunciants after the touch of wine has been spoiled.
But I, having once tasted the liquor-flavor of women,

children.text: na prāṇimi vinā tasmād dhiṅ nikṛṣṭaṃ ca mām iti ||
children.translated_text: cannot live without it. Fie on lowly me!"

children.text: atha gacchati sma ravir astabhūdharaṃ vasitadrumān adhi śakuntapaṅktayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the sun went to the mountain of setting, the rows of birds to the trees where they dwelt,

children.text: madamandam ātmabhavanāni nāgarāḥ priyayā sahāham api tanniveśanam ||
children.translated_text: the townsmen, slow with intoxication, to their own homes, and I too with my beloved to her dwelling.

children.text: tatra prasannayā kālaṃ priyayā ca prasannayā
children.translated_text: There, cheerful, with my cheerful beloved,
I cheerfully passed the time with <s>Dhruvaka</s> and the other friends.
As ten thousand after ten thousand went away with the passing of the days,
the great heap of wealth, though great, was exhausted over a long time.

children.text: kadācic cāham āhūya nīto dārikayā gṛham
children.translated_text: Once I was summoned and brought home by a maid,
and by my mother I was made to hear the hard-to-hear news of my father's ascent to heaven.

children.text: guruṇā guruśokena pīḍyamānaṃ ca māṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: While I was being crushed by heavy, weighty grief, the king summoned me
and said, "Son, I myself am <s>Mitravarman</s> for you.
Now you must live according to the conduct of a young man of good family;

children.text: sa hīha paraloke ca sukhāya prāṇinām iti ||
children.translated_text: for that brings happiness to living beings both here and in the next world."
And after adorning me with ornaments, garments, and sandal paste,

children.text: pitryaṃ śreṣṭhipadaṃ kṛtvā gṛhaṃ yāhīty abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: he installed me in my father's merchant-chief's post and said, "Go home."
When a little time had passed, <s>Dhruvaka</s>, full of pity, said:
"<s>Gaṅgadattā</s> too is grieving; she should be consoled."

children.text: mayā tūktam idānīṃ me bālakālaś calo gataḥ
children.translated_text: But I said, "Now my unstable childhood has gone by.
A different time has arrived, harsh with the burden of a household.
What has attachment to courtesans to do with taking on a household?
A young monkey is certainly not fit to bear a chariot-yoke.
Now <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>'s childishness has turned into fickleness;
let her too follow the path taken by her mother and grandmother.

children.text: durācāraiva sā veśyā ciraṃ yasyāḥ satīvratam
children.translated_text: That courtesan is badly behaved indeed whose vow of chastity lasts long;

children.text: na hi vedam adhīyānaḥ śūdraḥ sadbhiḥ praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: for a Śūdra studying the <s>Veda</s> is not praised by good people.

children.text: sadoṣam api na tyājyaṃ sahajaṃ karma sādhubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Even if it has faults, one's inborn work is not to be abandoned by the virtuous;

children.text: itīdaṃ vacanaṃ viṣṇoḥ sāpi saṃmānayatv iti ||
children.translated_text: let her too honor this saying of <s>Viṣṇu</s>."
He said, "Attachment to a courtesan is forbidden for householders,
but not respectful attention to a courtesan afflicted by grief.
Therefore I say: after consoling <s>Gaṅgadattā</s> together with her mother,

children.text: ayam āgata evāsi tyaja niṣṭhuratām iti ||
children.translated_text: say, 'Here I have come,' and abandon harshness."
Because passion for her had arisen in me, and because <s>Dhruvaka</s> entreated me,
even while foreseeing fault, I went to that house.

children.text: atha sā madviyogena madduḥkhena ca karśitā
children.translated_text: Then she, emaciated by separation from me and by grief on my account,
with her attendants crying, was with difficulty restored by me.
She bathed together with me, offered handfuls of water,
and set a bowl filled with wine in the courtyard of the house.
But <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>'s mother, holding a cup, said:
"Son, let a libation be made for the sake of driving away grief."

children.text: mama tv āsīt prapañco 'yaṃ viṣamaḥ prastuto 'nayā
children.translated_text: But I thought, "This dangerous stratagem has been set in motion by her.

children.text: nūnam asmān iyaṃ vṛddhā mugdhān ākṛṣṭum icchati ||
children.translated_text: Surely this old woman wants to draw us gullible men in.

children.text: īdṛśī ca vacodakṣā sadākṣiṇyaś ca mādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Since she is so skilled in speech, since one like me is always courteous,

children.text: nirdākṣiṇyā ca devī śrīr iti jāto 'smi śaṅkitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and since Lady Fortune is without courtesy, I became suspicious.

children.text: avaśyaṃ ca madīyā śrīr gaṅgadattāṃ gamiṣyati
children.translated_text: My wealth will certainly go to <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>;
for generally creatures form friendships with those of similar character.
Or rather, <s>Gaṅgadattā</s> herself is a worthy field for giving;

children.text: dānaṃ hi tatra dātavyaṃ yatra cittaṃ prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: for a gift should be given where the mind is pleased."
Having decided in this way and that, with a mind tasting fear,
I partook of the drink, whose taste was as bitter as triphalā.

children.text: na vartate sakṛt pātum atas triḥ pīyatām iti
children.translated_text: "It is not proper to drink only once; therefore it should be drunk three times."
I honored the command of the courtesan's mother with "Om."

children.text: yathā yathā ca māṃ mandam ārohan madirāmadaḥ
children.translated_text: And as the dull intoxication of wine climbed up over me,
so, correspondingly, my powerful grief for my father descended.
After that, at my command, my attendants
constantly brought wine from the wine-halls.

children.text: tadīyāś ca madīyāś ca gataśokam avekṣya mām
children.translated_text: And her women and mine, seeing me freed from grief,

children.text: gāyanti sma hasanti sma kecit tatrārudann api ||
children.translated_text: sang and laughed; some there even wept.

children.text: iti vismāritas tābhiḥ pitṛśokam ahaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Thus, made by them to forget my grief for my father,
I passed the days devoted to liquor and to love.
One day a courtesan, sent by the brothel-madam, said:

children.text: śvaśrūs tvām āha rūkṣo 'si gātram abhyajyatāṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: "Your mother-in-law says, 'You are dry; your body should be anointed.
<s>Gangadatta</s> too has become harsh through lack of oil and affection;

children.text: tasmād iyam api sneham aṅgeṣu nidadhātv iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore let this woman also apply oil and affection to your limbs.'"
She brought me a coarse cloth, soiled with oil,

children.text: skandhaḥ kaṭukatailena mrakṣitaś ca tayā mama ||
children.translated_text: and my shoulders were smeared by her with pungent oil.

children.text: uktaś cāsmi punar yāvad dārikāyā muhūrtakam
children.translated_text: And I was told again, "For the little while during which

children.text: abhyaṅgaḥ kriyate tāvad bhavān avataratv iti ||
children.translated_text: the girl's oil-massage is being done, please go down."
Then I descended from the upper apartment to the next, the sixth level,
and there I saw craftsmen who worked at setting gems.

children.text: sasaṃbhramaiś ca tair uktaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭair aham
children.translated_text: With hurried respect and folded hands they said to me:
"Merchant's son, you are expert; we are ashamed before you.
Before you, who are skilled in every science, art, and craft,

children.text: sarvajñānām api trāsāt prasaranti na pāṇayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the hands even of all-knowing masters do not move, from fear.

children.text: tasmād avataratv asmād dīrghāyuḥ pañcamaṃ puram
children.translated_text: Therefore let the long-lived sir descend from this to the fifth level;
let this work of ornamentation quickly reach completion."
In this way, by similar devices, by painters and the like
I was brought down in order from all the five remaining levels.
Then, by the inner servants and pot-carrying slave-girls in the courtyard,
I was driven outside with the words, "You are being sprinkled with cow-dung water."

children.text: śrūyate sma ca tasyaiva prāsādasyopari dhvaniḥ
children.translated_text: And there was heard above that very mansion

children.text: bandinaḥ paṭhataḥ ślokam uccakair uccarann iti ||
children.translated_text: the sound of a bard reciting a verse and uttering it loudly:

children.text: jaya rājasiṃha paradantimaṇḍalaṃ vijitaiva vādimṛgasaṃhatis tvayā
children.translated_text: "Victory, lion among kings! The circle of enemy elephants, like a herd of disputing beasts, has indeed been conquered by you.
You shine with a spread of rays, the mane of virtues, bright as the splendor of the full lord of stars."

children.text: cintitaṃ ca mayā manye praviṣṭaḥ ko 'pyayaṃ viṭaḥ
children.translated_text: And I thought, "I suppose some libertine has entered here,
some son of a whore whose virtues are being heard from bards.
How could there be even the scent of virtue in this man,
who has devoured shame, lives in a prostitute's house, and proclaims his own virtues?"
Thus envying him, with my neck stripped of shame,
I set out toward my own house, made an object of contempt by the townspeople.

children.text: ya eva māṃ suhṛt kaścid apaśyat saṃmukhāgatam
children.translated_text: Whatever friend of mine saw me coming face to face,

children.text: sa evāmīlayad dṛṣṭiṃ hā kiṃ dṛṣṭam iti bruvan ||
children.translated_text: that very man closed his eyes, saying, "Ah, what have I seen?"
Through whatever courtyard I went, whether of an acquaintance or of another man,
there the townspeople would pour down cow-dung water.
Loathed by people through displays of this sort,
I reached the door of my own house, which was occupied by an unknown man.

children.text: tena ca praviśann eva pūrvābhyāsād aśaṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: And as I was entering, unsuspecting from former habit,
I was stopped by an angry doorkeeper, crying, "Stop, stop!"
Then I asked him, my shame dulled by suspicion,

children.text: bhadra sarvaṃ na jānāmi tat tvam ākhyāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Good sir, I do not understand all this; please tell me the truth."

children.text: tenoktam īdṛśaṃ tattvaṃ na tvaṃ paragṛhaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "This is the truth: you should not again
enter another man's house without suspicion, through a door where a doorkeeper stands."

children.text: mayoktam atha sāsūyaṃ kiṃ ca mitravatī mṛtā
children.translated_text: Then I said, with resentment, "What, has <s>Mitravati</s> died?"

children.text: tenoktaṃ kaccid āyuṣmān sānudāso bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Surely you, long-lived sir, are <s>Sanudasa</s>?"
But I, whose speech had been harsh, was ashamed before that man of gentle speech

children.text: lajjamānaḥ sthitas tūṣṇīm atha tenoditaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and stood silent. Then he spoke again:

children.text: jīvaty eva mṛtā tāta mātā mitravatī tava
children.translated_text: "Your mother <s>Mitravati</s> is alive, dear boy, yet as good as dead;

children.text: spṛhayaty anapatyābhyo yā strībhyaḥ putravaty api ||
children.translated_text: though she has a son, she envies women who have none.
By this one grown and intrusive passion of yours,
the <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> proper to your family, though joined together, have been cut off.

children.text: gṛhaṃ vikrīya niḥsāram anāthā jananī tava
children.translated_text: Having sold the worthless house, your mother, without a protector,

children.text: saha pautreṇa vadhvā ca kutrāpy anyatra tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: lives somewhere else with her grandson and daughter-in-law.
The carpenter who is working here in the front court

children.text: āste mitravatī yatra tad ayaṃ pṛcchyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: should be asked where <s>Mitravati</s> is staying."

children.text: sa ca gatvā mayā dṛṣṭaḥ pratyabhijñāya māṃ cirāt
children.translated_text: I went to him, and when he saw me and recognized me after so long,

children.text: hā kaṣṭam iti kṛtvoccair duḥkhaskhalitam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: he cried aloud, "Alas, misery!" and spoke with grief-choked words:
"Because her wealth was taken and poverty came, by your favor,
dear boy, your mother lives with her daughter-in-law in the paupers' quarter."

children.text: daridravāṭakaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ kutreti sa mayā punaḥ
children.translated_text: When I asked him again, "Where is the paupers' quarter?"
he answered, "To the south, not far from the <s>Candala</s> quarter."
Walking slowly along the street of the poor settlement,
I saw poor people wasted by decay, with the appearance of the dead.

children.text: atha nimbataror mūle dattakaṃ nāma putrakam
children.translated_text: Then, at the foot of a neem tree, I saw the little son named <s>Dattaka</s>,
surrounded by many children.

children.text: bālakānām ayaṃ rājā te 'nye mantryādayaḥ kila
children.translated_text: He was the king of the children, it seems, and the others were ministers and the like;

children.text: dadāti sma tatas tebhyaḥ svāḥ sa kulmāṣapiṇḍikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then he was giving them his own little balls of boiled pulse.

children.text: yas tu teṣāṃ pratīhāraḥ sa rājāṃśaṃ prakalpitām
children.translated_text: But the one among them who was the doorkeeper stole
the little ball of pulse set apart as the king's portion, and ate it because he was hungry.
<s>Dattaka</s> too, his own share stolen, loudly calling his mother,
went to a hut whose courtyard was blocked with rubbish.
with an enclosure made of mats and with old, sparse vīraṇa reeds,
and with moonlike shafts of sunlight entering through countless holes in the layers of covering.
Following behind <s>Dattaka</s>, I went to that courtyard of the hut,
and the maidservant recognized me and reported it to <s>Mitravatī</s>.

children.text: sā tu niṣkramya saṃbhrāntā mām āliṅgya tathāvidham
children.translated_text: But she came out in agitation, embraced me in that condition,
and, as if sunk in deep sleep, neither moved nor breathed.

children.text: sadyaḥ putreṇa saṃyuktā svāminā ca vinākṛtā
children.translated_text: United at once with her son, yet deprived of her husband,
she bathed me with tears whose touch was neither warm nor cold.

children.text: nilīnāṃ ca kuṭīkoṇe paśyāmi sma kuṭumbinīm
children.translated_text: And in a corner of the hut I saw my wife hidden away,

children.text: alaṃ vā vistaraṃ kṛtvā mūrtām iva daridratām ||
children.translated_text: or rather, enough of enlarging on it: she was poverty itself embodied.
With chaff-covered grains of <s>kodrava</s> (millet), what clung to my limbs
from that bad maidservant's ministrations was carefully removed by my mother herself.
Full of holes covered with lac, with a broken lip and a worn-out mouth,
<s>Ālukā</s> had brought hot water from another house to give me.

children.text: snapayantyā ca māṃ bhagnā karmakaryā pramattayā
children.translated_text: But while she was bathing me, the careless working woman broke it,
