and then her mistress, <s>Taḍitodarī</s>, cried out fiercely:
'Ah, when you have perished, Lady <s>Ālukā</s>, cowherdess,

children.text: śūnyam adya jagajjātam adya mātā mṛtā mama ||
children.translated_text: the world today has become empty; today my mother has died.

children.text: mama mātur vivāhe tvaṃ labdhā jñātikulāt kila
children.translated_text: At my mother's wedding, they say, you were obtained from her kinsmen;

children.text: tena tvām anuśocāmi dvitīyāṃ jananīm iva ||
children.translated_text: therefore I grieve for you as for a second mother.'
As she lamented so piteously, my heart was softened with compassion,
and, tearing my garment, I gave half of it to her.
Then, after bathing in the lotus pond, my gaunt ribs seeming almost to drink,
I ate with difficulty a meal of <s>kodrava</s> (millet) rice, with sour gruel for relish.
But enough of listening so long to this story of poverty;

children.text: śrūyamāṇam api hy etad duḥkhāyaiva bhavādṛśām ||
children.translated_text: even when merely heard, such a thing brings pain to people like you.

children.text: so 'haṃ katham api kṣiptvā varṣalakṣāyatāṃ kṣapām
children.translated_text: So, after somehow passing a night that seemed a hundred thousand years long,
I was filled with irresistible dispassion and in the morning said to my mother:
'Only after taking back fourfold the wealth that has been lost by me

children.text: gṛham mayā praveṣṭavyaṃ na praveṣṭavyam anyathā ||
children.translated_text: will I enter the house; otherwise I must not enter it.
Therefore, mother, as if without a son, or as if your son were dead,
pass the days by diverting yourself with painful work.'

children.text: tayoktaṃ mā gamaḥ putra tvāṃ sadāraṃ sadārakam
children.translated_text: She said, 'Do not go, my son. I will support you, with wife and child,
living at ease, by blameworthy labors.'
I said, 'A man who is able and is maintained by an aged mother

children.text: yaḥ śaktaḥ puruṣas tasya ślāghyam ekasya jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: through painful labors has a life that is praiseworthy only for that mother alone.
So, mother, enough of clinging to this timidity of yours;
surely you are the wife of my father, whose heart was heavy as <s>Sumeru</s>.'
Thus firm in my insistence, I bowed to my mother,
and left the dreadful poor quarter as if leaving a hell from hell.

children.text: ambā dūram anuvrajya hitaṃ mahyam upādiśat
children.translated_text: My mother followed me a long way and gave me good advice:

children.text: tāmraliptīṃ vraje putra yatrāste mātulas tava ||
children.translated_text: 'Go, my son, to <s>Tāmraliptī</s>, where your maternal uncle lives.
For men in misfortune, their mother's relatives are a refuge;
but a wise man should avoid his father's relatives, because they become his own enemies.'
Having given such instructions and also a small portion of boiled rice,
she turned back, and I set out on the road leading to the eastern country.
I saw foreign travelers with tattered umbrellas and sandals,
with old leather bags and cooking tubes hanging from their shoulders.
Seeing me in just the same sort of condition as themselves,
an object of pity, those men spoke among one another:

children.text: aho kaṣṭam idaṃ dṛṣṭam asmābhiś ceṣṭitaṃ vidheḥ
children.translated_text: 'Ah, this is a painful act of fate that we have seen:

children.text: kva sādhuḥ sānudāso 'yaṃ kveyam etādṛśī daśā ||
children.translated_text: where is the noble <s>Sānudāsa</s>, and where is this condition of his?
Or rather, he is not to be pitied, since his great wealth is not lost;
for what is lost for great souls whose virtues are not lost?'

children.text: māṃ cāvocan vayaṃ sarve bhavataḥ paricārakāḥ
children.translated_text: And they said to me, 'We are all your attendants;

children.text: etasmād asahāyatvān mā sma śaṅkāṃ karor iti ||
children.translated_text: do not be anxious because of this lack of companions.'

children.text: atha māṃ ramayantas te ramaṇīyakathāḥ pathi
children.translated_text: Then, delighting me with charming tales on the road,
they traveled some distance, while I did not notice the weariness of the way.
When the sun, with its spreading heat, had contracted the shade of the world
and stood over everything, I reached a very large lake.
But deceiving their gaze, I bathed at a distance,
and ate that ambrosia-like, saltless <s>kodrava</s> (millet) food without oil.

children.text: te 'pi plutair udāttaiś ca vyāhāraiḥ parito diśam
children.translated_text: They too, with loud, raised cries in every direction,

children.text: sānudāsa kva yāsīti vyāharan māṃ sasaṃbhramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: called out in alarm, '<s>Sānudāsa</s>, where are you going?'
And when they saw that I had finished bathing and eating and returned, they said to me,

children.text: dhik pramādahatān asmān bhavatā chalitā vayam ||
children.translated_text: 'Shame on us, ruined by carelessness; we have been deceived by you.
By us various foods fit to be eaten were prepared in the cooking pot,

children.text: bhavatā ca na saṃbhuktam etad asmād anarthakam ||
children.translated_text: but you did not eat with us; this is a misfortune for us.

children.text: idānīm api yat kiṃcit tvayā tatropayujyatām
children.translated_text: Even now, whatever there is there should be used by you;

children.text: anyathāsmābhir apy adya sthātavyaṃ kṣudhitair iti ||
children.translated_text: otherwise we too must remain hungry today.'

children.text: tatas tadarthitaḥ kiṃcid bhakṣayitvā sahaiva taiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, urged by them, I ate a little together with those men,
and setting out in the evening I reached the village <s>Siddhakacchapa</s>.

children.text: tatra māṃ rathyayāyāntaṃ kaścid dṛṣṭvā kuṭumbikaḥ
children.translated_text: There, as I was coming along the street, a certain householder saw me,
bowed down, and said, 'Come; please go to my own house.'
When the travelers had given permission and I had entered the house,
the householder himself washed my feet, although I tried to stop him.
For me, whose bodily weariness had been removed by oiling, rubbing, and bathing,
He gave me a stout washed cotton garment, dyed red with mineral pigment.
Then, after I had eaten a meal mostly of milk-rice from a fresh vessel,

children.text: śayanīye niṣaṇṇaṃ mām avocat sa kuṭumbikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that householder spoke to me as I sat on a bed.

children.text: tvadīyas tāta vṛttāntaḥ sarvaḥ saṃvidito mama
children.translated_text: 'Dear boy, your whole story is known to me.
To whose eyes is the swallowing of the sun by <s>Svarbhānu</s> not visible?
Through the favor of <s>Mitravarman</s>, whose wealth has the substance of <s>Meru</s> and the ocean,
thousands of dependents like me are prosperous.

children.text: ahaṃ siddhārthako nāma vaṇigbhṛtyaḥ pitus tava
children.translated_text: I am named <s>Siddhārthaka</s>, a merchant's servant of your father.

children.text: tena tvadīyam evedaṃ yat kiṃcid draviṇaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: Therefore whatever wealth I have here is really yours.

children.text: mūlam etad upādāya vardhantāṃ te vibhūtayaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking this as capital, let your fortunes grow,
benefiting many beings, like the branches of a great tree.
When a few days have passed, you will go to <s>Tāmraliptī</s>
with a caravan under my care; until then, rest.'
Then, considering in my mind that this was proper, and saying, 'So be it,'

children.text: prātiṣṭhe saha sārthena tena siddhārthakena ca ||
children.translated_text: I set out with that caravan and with <s>Siddhārthaka</s>.
Then I heard the bragging of fierce <s>Ḍiṇḍikas</s>,
as if they were bursting with joy over their various weapons.
'Listen, firm as mountains in our vow to break <s>Dhātakī</s>.

children.text: khaṇḍacarmeti me nāma muṇḍāḥ pāśupatā vayam ||
children.translated_text: My name is <s>Khaṇḍacarma</s>; we are shaven-headed <s>Pāśupatas</s>.
If, on the front of battle, I do not send even a thousand thieves,

children.text: na nayeyaṃ yadi svargaṃ gaccheyaṃ nirayaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: brave men though they are, to heaven, then let me go to hell.

children.text: taskarān yadi paśyāmas tatas tvāṃ devi caṇḍike
children.translated_text: If we see robbers, then, goddess <s>Caṇḍikā</s>,
we shall satisfy you with fresh blood from buffaloes and goats.'
So we went into the middle of the forest and camped by a river
with deep ravines, like the terrible <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, our merit exhausted.
At the time of a dark-fortnight night, black and avoiding all clamor,
a Pulinda army, unbearable like <s>Kālarātrī</s>, fell upon us.

children.text: tathā kathitavantas te tām ālokyaiva ḍiṇḍikāḥ
children.translated_text: Although those <s>Ḍiṇḍikas</s> had spoken in that way, as soon as they saw it
they ran off, abandoning the wealth of their weapons, shame, and reputation.
While the caravan was being plundered, I, intent only on saving my life,
my sense of direction confused by panic, fled as a fugitive.

children.text: taskaro 'yam iti bhraṣṭaḥ sārthikād api dhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: When even a caravan man running after me fell away, thinking, 'This is a thief,'
by the end of the day I reached a village at the edge of the forest, deep in the wilds.

children.text: tasya madhena gacchantaṃ māṃ pariṣvajya vṛddhikā
children.translated_text: As I was going through the middle of it, an old woman embraced me,
and, in a voice made hoarse by age, began to weep as follows:
'Son, you are hard-hearted, since you went away to another country,

children.text: vṛddhāṃ duḥkhitakām asvāṃ tyaktvā deśāntaraṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: leaving me, an old woman with my relatives gone, distressed and helpless.

children.text: mādṛśīṃ mātaraṃ dīnāṃ tyaktvā yad upacīyate
children.translated_text: The sin that is increased by abandoning a wretched mother like me
is not washed away even by one who has gone to <s>Prayāga</s>.
So, while you are wearing away the sin committed by pilgrimage,
stay in your own house, serving me.'

children.text: mama tv āsīd aho kaṣṭam aparo 'yam upadravaḥ
children.translated_text: But I thought, 'Ah, misery! This is another calamity.

children.text: manye mūrtimatī kāpi vipattir iyam āgatā ||
children.translated_text: I suppose some embodied misfortune has come upon me.
For disasters, ever watchful, constantly stand near
heedless men like me, just as prosperity does near the wise.'

children.text: atha māṃ ciram īkṣitvā tayoktaṃ lajjamānayā
children.translated_text: Then, after looking at me for a long time, she said in embarrassment,
'Son, because you resemble my son, I have treated you so badly.

children.text: athavā putra evāsi mamety uktvānayad gṛham
children.translated_text: Or rather, you are indeed my son,' she said, and led me home.
There she made me free from weariness with massage of the limbs, food, and the like.
In the morning, when I was setting out, I bowed to her and said,

children.text: campāyāṃ sānudāsasya gṛham amba vrajer iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Mother, go to <s>Sānudāsa</s>'s house in <s>Campā</s>.'

children.text: śrāntaśrāntaś ca viśrāntaḥ pṛṣṭvā panthānam antare
children.translated_text: Very weary, resting again and again, and asking the road on the way,
I went to <s>Tāmraliptī</s>, which put <s>Amarāvatī</s> to shame.

children.text: bhoḥ sādho gaṅgadattasya gṛham ākhyāyatām iti
children.translated_text: 'Good sir, please tell me the house of <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>,'

children.text: yaṃ yam eva sma pṛcchāmi sa sa evaivam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: I asked one person after another, and each one replied in just this way:

children.text: tāmraliptyāṃ pure bhrāntas tvatto dhūrtataro janaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Wandering in the city of <s>Tāmraliptī</s>, you are a man more crooked than you seem.
You are a village townsman, speaking like a badly clever fellow.

children.text: iti saṃpṛcchamānāya yadā mahyaṃ na kaścana
children.translated_text: When, though I asked and asked in this way, no one

children.text: ācaṣṭe sma tadā khinnaḥ sann upāviśam āpaṇe ||
children.translated_text: told me, I became dejected and sat down in a shop.

children.text: tatra māṃ pṛṣṭavān eko vaṇik pāṇḍaramastakaḥ
children.translated_text: There a merchant with a white head questioned me:

children.text: udvigna iva vicchāyaḥ kiṃnimittaṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Why are you so anxious and pale?'
And when, out of compassion, he asked, I told him
the cause of my anxiety; then he too said with a laugh:
'These people of <s>Tāmraliptī</s> think you speak crookedly.

children.text: gṛhaṃ hi gaṅgadattasya na pṛcchanti yathāsthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: People do not ask where <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>'s house is as if it were unknown.
The man who does not know the disk of the full-moon moon

children.text: na sa jānāti dhūrto vā gaṅgadattasya mandiram ||
children.translated_text: would be either ignorant or a rogue if he did not know <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>'s mansion.
Or perhaps you see here <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s>, standing fixed

children.text: pravṛddhāṃś ca viśuddhā:mśu gaṅgadattasya tad gṛham ||
children.translated_text: and greatly increased and pure-rayed: that is <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>'s house.

children.text: athavā gaccha mugdheti mām uktvā svayam eva saḥ
children.translated_text: Or rather, come, simpleton,' he said to me, and he himself,
kindly helping one who asked, led me to the door of <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>'s house.
Hearing that I had come from there, a succession of doorkeepers
reported it to my maternal uncle, who was in the innermost apartment.
Then, like the flood of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> falling in a cavern of the snowy mountain,
a sound of lamentation began, deep within and resounding inside.
Then, coming out from that mansion with his wives and servants,

children.text: gaṅgāyāṃ gaṅgadattena pitre dattaṃ jalaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> offered water in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> for my father.
There I passed a little time enjoying a great happiness that had sorrow hidden within it,
like nectar that had been split open by poison.
One day, when I had found an interval of rest, my uncle said to me,

children.text: bhāgineyārthaye yat tvāṃ tad anuṣṭhātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: 'Nephew, what I ask of you, you ought to carry out.

children.text: yad anantam akupyaṃ ca draviṇaṃ mama paśyasi
children.translated_text: The endless and imperishable wealth that you see as mine
has arisen from <s>Mitravarman</s>, that heap of virtue and riches.

children.text: svasmāt svasmāt tad ādāya pratijñātāc caturguṇam
children.translated_text: Taking from each and every one what was promised, four times over,
go back to see your mother, who is faded from separation from you.

children.text: tasmiṃś ca kṣīṇa evānyā gantrī te dravyasaṃhatiḥ
children.translated_text: And when that is exhausted, another mass of wealth will go to you;

children.text: akṣayaprabhavo hy asyā gaṅgāyā himavān iva ||
children.translated_text: for its source is inexhaustible, like the <s>Himavān</s> mountain for this <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: sve svasmin sati cānante lipsānyasmin vigarhitā
children.translated_text: When one's own property is endless, desire for another's is blameworthy.
For who, after understanding the meaning of the Vedas with their limbs, would study the alphabet?'
Then, while <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> was admonishing me with words such as these, I said,

children.text: sāre 'rthe dṛḍhanirbandhaṃ mā māṃ vyāhata mātula ||
children.translated_text: 'Uncle, do not restrain me firmly when the matter is important and substantial.

children.text: pravartyo gurubhiḥ kārye yatra bālo balād api
children.translated_text: Where a child must be set to a task by his elders even by force,

children.text: svayam eva pravṛttas tair nivartyeta kathaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: how could he then be turned back by them when he has begun it of his own accord?

children.text: yac coktaṃ māmakair arthaiḥ kuṭumbaṃ jīvyatām iti
children.translated_text: And as for what was said, that my family should live on my funds,
that is not to be taught to one like me, who has his own hands and feet.

children.text: mātulād dhanam ādāya yo jīvati samātṛkaḥ
children.translated_text: The man who, together with his mother, lives by taking wealth from his maternal uncle
surely lives as nothing but a maternal-uncle's man, a creature of unmanly spirit.'

children.text: sthirasattvaṃ sa buddhvā mām ālāpair evamādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that I was firm in spirit, through trustworthy servants and speeches of this kind
he had me guarded with careful watchfulness.

children.text: palāyamānaṃ kaḥ śakto mriyamāṇaṃ ca rakṣitum
children.translated_text: After hearing this saying from the world, 'Who is able to protect a man who is fleeing, or one who is dying?'
I became intent on flight.
Then I went, unseen by anyone, to a certain sea-merchant
who was about to set out for the great ocean, and respectfully greeted him.

children.text: tasmai ca kathayāmi sma prakṛṣṭān ātmano guṇān
children.translated_text: And I began to tell him of my own outstanding abilities;

children.text: tṛṣṇādāsīvidheyā hi kiṃ na kurvanti pātakam ||
children.translated_text: for what sin do those who are subject to the slave-woman Thirst not commit?
'I am the son of <s>Mitravarman</s>, who lives at <s>Campā</s>,
skilled in all the arts, beginning with the testing of every kind of jewel.

children.text: yuṣmābhiś ca sanāthatvam aham icchāmi sādhubhiḥ
children.translated_text: And I wish to gain protection through good men such as you;

children.text: tvādṛṅnātho hy anātho 'pi mukhyo nāthavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: for even an unprotected man who has a protector like you is foremost among those with protectors.'
As soon as he heard the name of <s>Mitravarman</s>, overcome with joy,

children.text: śraddadhāti sma duḥsādhyāṃ mayi sarvajñatām api ||
children.translated_text: he believed in me even an all-knowing expertise that would be hard to attain.
And he said, 'Formerly we were protected by <s>Mitravarman</s>;

children.text: adhunā bhavatā tāta tataḥ prasthīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: now, my son, we are protected by you. Therefore let us set out.'
Then, after honoring the gods, brahmins, and teachers, on an auspicious, bright
and favorable lunar day and constellation, the merchant launched the ship.

Then the merchants set out on that endless, inexhaustible expanse, an ocean-home of waves and clouds, filled with makaras, crocodiles, whirlpools, and sea-monsters, gleaming like the throat of <s>Pinākadhara</s>,

children.text: mahārṇavanabhastalaṃ lavaṇasindhunauchadmanā viyatpatharathena tena vaṇijas tataḥ prasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sky-like surface of the great ocean, by means of that ship on the salt sea, as if by a chariot on the path of the sky.

children.text: kathaṃ vā na vimānaṃ tad yena mānasaraṃhasā
children.translated_text: And how could that not have been an aerial car, by which, with the speed of the mind,
a hundred yojanas were traversed in the mere opening of the eyes?
Then, struck by a lordly water-elephant rising up from the water,

children.text: viśīrṇabandhanaḥ potaḥ paṭṭaśaḥ sphuṭati sma saḥ ||
children.translated_text: that ship, its fastenings shattered, split apart into pieces.

children.text: yasya keśeṣu jīmūtā iti gītām anusmaran
children.translated_text: Remembering the song, 'In whose hair are the clouds,'

children.text: daivāt phalakam ālambya prāpaṃ toyanidhes taṭam ||
children.translated_text: by fate I grasped a plank and reached the shore of the ocean.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ viśramya tatrāhaṃ hā kiṃ vṛttam iti bruvan
children.translated_text: Resting there for a moment and crying, 'Ah, what has happened?'
I wandered about on the edge of the sea, with the directions turning and turning in confusion.
There, the ends of rivers and the borders of mountains were everywhere overrun
with forests of sandalwood, aloe, camphor, clove, and lavalī creepers.
There the forests, crowded with fruiting trees such as plantains and coconuts,
were being broken by wild elephants.
Then, somewhere at the mouth of a cave whose front half was blocked by a rock,
I saw a woman whose front half was blocked by a rock.
Then, with a motionless eye, measuring her according to her proper form,
she looked at me, frightened because of my straightness and unchanging stillness.

children.text: āsīc ca mama kāpy eṣā dānavī devatāpi vā
children.translated_text: And I thought, 'This must be some dānavī, or perhaps a goddess;

children.text: na hi rūpaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ nāryāḥ kasyāścid īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: for I have never seen the form of any woman like this.
Or else she is some hungry night-wandering woman
who has come here, wearing the bodice of a divine form, after seeing me alone.
For rakṣasīs, taking the forms of apsarases, strike at the weak points

children.text: randhreṣu praharantīti yat tan mām idam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: of careless men like me. That is what has now come upon me.

children.text: tasmād asmād ahaṃ deśāt palāye sabhayād iti
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall flee from this frightening place.'

children.text: prasthitaś cintayitvā ca sā ca mām ity abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Having thought this, I set out, and she said this to me:

children.text: bhoḥ sādho mā bhavat te bhīr nāhaṃ naktaṃcarāṅganā
children.translated_text: 'Good sir, do not be afraid. I am not a night-wandering woman.
Know me to be a human woman, fallen from a shipwreck's disaster.'
Then, on hearing this, with my hair standing upright from the height of my terror,
I bowed to the two saviors of the world, <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: āsīc ca mama divyeyam iti saṃprati niścitam
children.translated_text: And I thought, 'Now it is certain that she is divine,
since she is unblinking and because she has a mind that knows another's thoughts.

children.text: yady eṣā rākṣasī tasmāt kva gataḥ syāṃ palāyitaḥ
children.translated_text: If she is a rakṣasī, then where could I go by fleeing from her?'
Having decided this, I turned back and said this to her, though she was frightened:

children.text: yadi tvaṃ mānuṣī satyaṃ darīdvārād itas tataḥ
children.translated_text: 'If you are truly a human woman, then come out from the mouth of the cave

children.text: nirgatyātmānam ācakṣva divyā cet pāhi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: and declare yourself from there; but if you are divine, protect me.'

children.text: atha hrīteva sā kiṃcin netre saṃmīlya sāśruṇī
children.translated_text: Then, as if ashamed, she half-closed her tear-filled eyes a little.
She let it fall upon the front of her body, half of her garment being held in place by the rock.

children.text: tataḥ saṃmīlite dṛṣṭvā tayā netre mamābhavat
children.translated_text: Then, when I saw that her eyes were closed, this thought came to me:
"Surely this poor naked woman is indeed a human woman."
Then, turning my face away, I tore my own cloak

children.text: idaṃ vassveti tām uktvā tasyai tasyārdham akṣipam ||
children.translated_text: and, saying to her, "Put this on," I threw half of it to her.
With the parts that ought to be covered covered by her arms, half the cloth, and her hair,
she then sat down upon a rock broad enough for her own hips.
Then, not standing too close, frightened because she was another man's wife,

children.text: bhadre kasyāsi kā veti tām apṛccham avāṅmukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I asked her, with face lowered, "Good lady, whose are you, and who are you?"
Seeing a human man in a region where human beings were hard to find,
as if she had found a kinsman in a wilderness, she trustingly began to speak:
"There is a merchant named <s>Sāgara</s>, for whom righteous conduct, wealth, and every aim are good,
in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in a house like the palace of a king of kings.
His wife, named <s>Yavanī</s>, was born in the <s>Yavana</s> country,

children.text: yā prakṛṣṭe 'pi saubhāgye patiṃ devam ivārcati ||
children.translated_text: and although her good fortune is extraordinary, she honors her husband like a god.

children.text: tayoḥ sāgaradinnākhyaḥ putraḥ pitror guṇaiḥ samaḥ
children.translated_text: They have a son named <s>Sāgaradinna</s>, equal to his parents in virtues,

children.text: jyeṣṭhaḥ samudradinnaś ca tatsanāmā ca kanyakā ||
children.translated_text: an elder son <s>Samudradinna</s>, and also a daughter bearing that same name.
To the son <s>Sānudāsa</s> of the good merchant <s>Mitravarman</s>,

children.text: sutāya sānudāsāya sā ca pitrā pratiśrutā ||
children.translated_text: who is the very ornament of <s>Campā</s>, that daughter was promised by her father.

children.text: sānudāsaś ca rūpeṇa smareṇa sadṛśaḥ kila
children.translated_text: And <s>Sānudāsa</s>, it is said, was like <s>Smara</s> in beauty,

children.text: sakalaṃ ca kalājālaṃ vedeti jagati śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and common report in the world says that he knows the whole net of arts.

children.text: athavā na kalājālaṃ jālaṃ veda sa kevalam
children.translated_text: Or rather, he knows no net of arts; he knows only a net.

children.text: ko hi nāma kalāśālī karma tādṛśam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: For what man accomplished in the arts would commit such a deed?
For his whole store of virtues and wealth was carried off by a courtesan,
and he was killed by robbers in the slaughter of a caravan, together with brahmins and caṇḍālas alike.

children.text: tac ca vaiśasam ākarṇya sānudāsasya duḥśravam
children.translated_text: Hearing of that terrible disaster of <s>Sānudāsa</s>, so painful to hear,

children.text: sāgarasya kuṭumbaṃ tat prasthitaṃ yavanīṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: the household of <s>Sāgara</s> set out toward the <s>Yavana</s> woman.
And when the ship was wrecked, it perished in the salt water,
like a multitude of creatures at the destruction of the circle of the earth.
That ill-fated girl called <s>Samudradinnā</s>

children.text: na tasyai nirdayenāpi sindhunā dattam antaram ||
children.translated_text: was not given an opening even by the pitiless ocean.

children.text: sāgareṇa ca yā kanyā sānudāsāya kalpitā
children.translated_text: I am that unlucky girl whom <s>Sāgara</s> had assigned to <s>Sānudāsa</s>,

children.text: sāgareṇa nirastā ca mandabhāgyāham eva sā ||
children.translated_text: and whom the ocean has cast away.

children.text: kiṃ kartavyaṃ kva gantavyaṃ kiṃ vṛttaṃ kiṃ nu vartate
children.translated_text: "What is to be done? Where is one to go? What has happened? What is happening now?"
Passing the time with such thoughts, I remain here, dearly clinging to life.
With the flesh of oysters broken on the shore and cooked by wildfire,

children.text: prajñātaiḥ phalamūlaiś ca puṣṇāmi viphalāṃ tanum ||
children.translated_text: and with such fruits and roots as I can recognize, I nourish this fruitless body.
And from the greediness of the merchant class, by carrying them again and again from the sand,

children.text: mauktikasya guhākoṇe rāśiḥ prāṃśur mayā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I have made a tall heap of pearls in the corner of a cave.

children.text: mama tāvad iyaṃ vārttā tvadīyākhyāyatām iti
children.translated_text: For my part, this is my story. Now let yours be told."

children.text: iti pṛṣṭasya me cittam iti cittam abhūt tayā ||
children.translated_text: When she had questioned me in this way, this thought arose in my mind:

children.text: sānudāso 'ham eveti yady asyai kathayāmy aham
children.translated_text: "If I tell her, 'I myself am <s>Sānudāsa</s>,'

children.text: anyad eva kim apy eṣā mayi saṃbhāvayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: she will imagine something quite different about me.

children.text: saṃbhāvayatu nāmeyam ahaṃ punar imāṃ katham
children.translated_text: Let her imagine it, if she must; but how could I,

children.text: vipanmagnām upekṣeyaṃ puruṣaḥ san striyam satīm ||
children.translated_text: being a man, neglect this virtuous woman sunk in misfortune?

children.text: api cedaṃ smarāmy eva tātapādair yathā vṛtā
children.translated_text: Moreover, I remember that she was chosen by my revered father,

children.text: pitrā ceyaṃ pratijñātā tena vyarthā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: and that she was promised by her father; therefore deliberation is pointless."

children.text: athetthaṃ kathayāmi sma campāyām abhavad vaṇik
children.translated_text: Then I told her thus: "In <s>Campā</s> there was a merchant
named <s>Mitravarman</s>, who, prosperous and sound, still lives even now through his fame.

children.text: yasya mitravatī jāyā sānudāsaḥ sutas tayoḥ
children.translated_text: His wife was <s>Mitravatī</s>; their son was <s>Sānudāsa</s>.

children.text: sa tābhyām ekaputratvāj jñāpitaḥ sakalāḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because he was their only son, they had him taught all the arts.
But he, with his false learning and turned away from worldly conduct,
was brought by friends, knaves who knew his mind, into association with a slave woman.

children.text: sānudāsaḥ sa evāhaṃ sarvasvaṃ me tayā hṛtam
children.translated_text: That very <s>Sānudāsa</s> am I. All my property was taken by her,
and then, knowing me to be useless, she tried to drive me out."

children.text: athāsminn antare sā māṃ bhāṣamāṇam abhāṣata
children.translated_text: Then, in the midst of this, as I was speaking, she spoke to me:

children.text: kiṃcit pṛcchāmi yat tan me yūyam ākhyātum arhatha ||
children.translated_text: "I ask you something; you should tell me the answer.
When a coarse bathing cloth, grimy with oil, was brought,

children.text: prāsādāgre yad uktāḥ stha dāsyā tat kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: what were you told by the slave woman on the top of the mansion? Tell that."
But I said, "I was told by her, 'The young lady

children.text: abhyaṅgaḥ kriyate tasmād bhavān avataratv iti ||
children.translated_text: is being anointed for a moment; therefore let your honor come down.'"
Then she asked, "In the sixth city, by the jewel-polishing

children.text: kim uktāḥ śilpibhir yūyam iti pratyabruvaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: craftsmen, what were you told?" Then I answered:

children.text: tair ukto 'haṃ pravīṇo 'si tvatto lajjāmahe vayam
children.translated_text: "They said to me, 'You are skilled; we are ashamed before you.

children.text: tasmād asmāt purāt ṣaṣṭhāt pañcamaṃ gamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore go from this sixth city to the fifth.'"

children.text: ityādi yat tayā pṛṣṭaṃ vṛttaṃ vṛttaṃ mayākhilam
children.translated_text: Whatever she asked about in this way, event after event,
I answered it all completely, down to the final destruction of the caravan.
Then, though from modesty she shrank limb into limb
like a female tortoise, she embraced me with a sidelong glance, lovely with the ointment of Love.

children.text: tatas tāṃ pṛṣṭavān asmi bhīru kiṃ kriyatām iti
children.translated_text: After that I asked her, "Timid one, what is to be done?"

children.text: sātha prasārayat svinnaṃ sphurantaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ karam ||
children.translated_text: Then she stretched out her damp, trembling right hand.

children.text: gambhīraṃ dhvanati tataḥ samudratūrye gāyatsu śrutimadhuraṃ śilīmukheṣu
children.translated_text: Then, while the ocean-drum thundered deeply and the bees sang sweetly to the ear,

children.text: nṛtyatsu sphuṭaraṭiteṣu nīlakaṇṭheṣv ālambe karam ibhatālutāmram asyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: while the clear-crying peacocks danced, I took her hand, copper-red like an elephant's palate.
Then all that suffering of hers, caused by the shipwreck and the rest,

children.text: sarvam ekapade naṣṭaṃ sādhāv apakṛtaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: vanished in a single instant, like a wrong done to a good man.
I used to laugh at heretics and householders who longed for liberation and heaven,
while I myself had a great happiness immediately at hand, though those men were full of anxious thoughts.
With aphrodisiac meats of water-creatures such as fish, turtles, and crabs,
and with coconuts and the like, strengthening and nourishing the body,
on the sandbanks of the ocean, crowded with pearls and coral,
we two wandered happily, with our necks outstretched like a pair of royal swans.
Sometimes, beside mountain peaks with thickets and waterfalls,
surrounded by fruit-bearing trees, we were like a young elephant and a she-elephant.
With cloves, areca nuts, camphor, betel, and other things that were not hard to obtain,
together with sandal, I constantly adorned my body with the accessories of bodiless Love.
Dwelling in caves and vine-houses, and wearing the bark of trees as clothing,

children.text: devam ātmabhuvaṃ dhyāntau jātau svaḥ kāmayoginau ||
children.translated_text: meditating on the self-born god, we became, as it were, yogins of love.

children.text: tataḥ samudradinnā mām ity avocat kadācana
children.translated_text: Then one day <s>Samudradinna</s> said this to me:
'Noble son, perform the practice used by merchants whose ship has broken apart.

children.text: divā prāṃśos taror agre prāṃśur ucchrīyatāṃ dhvajaḥ
children.translated_text: By day a tall banner should be raised on the top of a tall tree;
by night a fire should be kindled on the high shore of the sea.
Perhaps some sailor, seeing a sign of us two,

children.text: svadeśam ānayed āvāṃ dharmo 'yaṃ vaṇijām iti ||
children.translated_text: will bring us back to our own country. This is the duty of merchants.'

children.text: yuktam āheti nirdhārya tathaiva kṛtavān aham
children.translated_text: Deciding that she had spoken rightly, I did exactly so;

children.text: āptānām upadeśo hi pramāṇaṃ yoṣitām api ||
children.translated_text: for the advice of trusted people is authoritative, even when it comes from women.
Then, at dawn, along the high, rushing, curving crests of the breakers,
a boat came toward us like a row of diving birds.
I boarded that swift craft, manned by two helmsmen;
like a cloud riding a line of eastern wind, I set out across a great distance.

children.text: paśyāmi sma tataḥ sindhau bohitthaṃ sthiram asthire
children.translated_text: Then I saw on the unsteady ocean a ship standing firm,
like a steadfast man standing in a crowd of cowards.
There I saw a merchant who was a vessel of great riches,
like <s>Kailāsa</s> with its bright summit, a great treasure of the <s>Mahāpadma</s> kind.

children.text: abhivādayamānaṃ ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā tena saspṛham
children.translated_text: When he saw me bowing before him, he gazed at me with longing,
and spoke with tears in his eyes and throat, his voice faltering:

children.text: kiṃ jātiḥ kasya putro 'si kiṃ vā māteti sarvathā
children.translated_text: 'What is your birth? Whose son are you? And who is your mother? In every way...

children.text: kiṃ tvayā tāta pṛṣṭena mitravarmasuto bhavān ||
children.translated_text: But why need I ask you, dear boy? You are the son of <s>Mitravarman</s>.

children.text: kathaṃ punar amuṃ deśam āgato 'sīti pṛcchate
children.translated_text: How, then, have you come to this region?' When he asked this,
I told him in detail everything that had happened before.

children.text: tenoktam asi dīrghāyur jāmātā tanayaś ca me
children.translated_text: He said, 'May you live long. You are both my son-in-law and my son,

children.text: ātmā sāgaradattaś ca mitravarmā ca me yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Sāgaradatta</s>, <s>Mitravarman</s>, and I are one self.

children.text: gaccha sāgaradattasya tanayāṃ tac ca mauktikam
children.translated_text: Go; let <s>Sāgaradatta</s>'s daughter and that pearl
be brought here from the shore in a ship with many sailors.

children.text: anyac cāsiddharātro 'haṃ kiṃ ca potaṃ na paśyasi
children.translated_text: And besides, I have had an unsuccessful night; indeed, do you not see my ship,
empty like a pond whose water has been taken away by drought?

children.text: mamedaṃ vahanaṃ riktaṃ voḍhavyaṃ sāravat tava
children.translated_text: This empty vessel of mine should carry your valuable cargo;
like the alliance of a man whose horse is lost and one whose chariot is burned, this union of ours is praiseworthy.

children.text: mūlyaṃ tasya ca yat tan nau samabhāgaṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Whatever its value is, it will be divided equally between us;

children.text: pūrvaṃ saṃmantritārghas tvaṃ dharmo 'yaṃ vaṇijām iti ||
children.translated_text: you shall first agree on the price with us. This is the duty of merchants.'

children.text: tac ca mauktikam ānīya potas tena prapūritaḥ
children.translated_text: After that pearl was brought, the ship was filled with it,
and <s>Samudradinna</s> bowed at the merchant's feet.
He gave her ten thousand coins, garments, and ornaments,

children.text: tena dattāni vadatā vadhūs tvaṃ me suteti ca ||
children.translated_text: saying, 'You are my daughter-in-law, my daughter.'
But this has been told at too great length; hear the summary.

children.text: preritaṃ yānapātraṃ ca tad vipannaṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: That ship was sent forth, and, as before, it was wrecked.
Even when I had lost hope of life as the ship was sinking,
I tied a few pearls into the middle of my topknot.

children.text: tāś ca vijñāpayāmi sma parasmin mama janmani
children.translated_text: And I addressed them respectfully: 'In my next birth,

children.text: bhagavatyaḥ sadā bhaktam upatiṣṭhata mām iti ||
children.translated_text: blessed ladies, always attend upon me, your devotee.'
When events were going on in this way, I saw my beloved close by,
come near, clinging to a plank as to a boat across the spaces between the waves.
She was calling out to me, her hand stretched forth,
but that helpless woman was forcibly carried away by a fickle wave.

children.text: tasmai kruddhas taraṃgāya mahāmoham ahaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Angry at that wave, I fell into a deep stupor,

children.text: cetaye yāvad ātmānaṃ loṭantam udadhes taṭe ||
children.translated_text: until I became aware of myself rolling on the shore of the ocean.
Having lost my beloved, and cast free after letting her go, I was distraught from separation from her;
as I went on, I lamented without restraint in that lonely place.
'Homage to you, lord, giver of the joy of delusive extinction;
shame on unconscious consciousness, empty of knowledge of the right time and the wrong time.

children.text: mauktikaṃ gṛhyatāṃ nāma tat te svaṃ svaṃ mahodadhe
children.translated_text: Take the pearl, if you must; it is your own property, great ocean.

children.text: sādho sādhvī vipadbandhuḥ priyā me mucyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Good sir, release my faithful beloved, my companion in calamity.'

children.text: yāś ca tāḥ śirasi nyastā muktāḥ pote nimajjati
children.translated_text: And those pearls which had been placed on my head when the ship was sinking,

children.text: siraḥ kaṇḍūyamānena tāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ pāṇinā mayā ||
children.translated_text: I touched with my hand while scratching my head.
Then, having only that much wealth, I tested them;

children.text: tat kiṃ parīkṣitaṃ tāsāṃ yā na dṛṣṭāḥ parīkṣakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but what testing could there be of pearls not seen by proper examiners?

children.text: sa śokas tāsu dṛṣṭāsu yat satyam abhavat tanuḥ
children.translated_text: When those pearls were seen, that grief truly became slight;

children.text: yad etad draviṇaṃ nāma prāṇā hy ete bahiścarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for what is called wealth is one's very life-breaths moving outside the body.

children.text: śāṭakānte ca tā buddhvā dṛḍhayā granthimālayā
children.translated_text: Realizing that they were at the end of my cloth, in a firm chain of knots,
I went along the shore, steady-minded through the warmth of wealth.
At times my feet slipped in the mire of plantain fruit;
at times the pain of my thirst was cut off by coconut water;
with tender shoots entwined by cardamom, pepper, and betel vines...
my eyes drawn on by groves of jackfruit and areca palms, beautiful with fruit,
and here and there among thickets of campaka whose flowers had been scattered by the leaps of monkeys and other creatures,
easing the weariness of the journey as I went on.
And when the sun at day's end had limbs tawny with evening,
I reached a village dusty with dust raised by rushing herds of cows.

children.text: tatas tatra vasaty arthaṃ yaṃ yaṃ yāce sma kaṃcana
children.translated_text: Then, whomever I asked there for a place to stay,

children.text: dhanninuṃ colliditi ca bravīti sma hasan sa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: each man laughed and said, 'dhanninuṃ colliditi.'
Then one bilingual householder took me to his house,

children.text: jāmāteva cirāt prāptaḥ priyaḥ prītyāsmi satkṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and I was affectionately honored like a dear son-in-law arrived after a long time.
At the beginning of the night I asked him, as he sat near his own bed,

children.text: deśo 'yaṃ katamaḥ sādho katamad vātra pattanam ||
children.translated_text: 'Good sir, what country is this, and what city is here?'
He said, 'This is the <s>Pāṇḍya</s> country, along the southern ocean,
where the sight of a petitioner is delightful as the gaining of the great <s>Mahāpadma</s> treasure.

children.text: itaś ca pāṇḍyamathurā grāmān mṛduni yojane
children.translated_text: And from here <s>Pāṇḍyamathurā</s> is an easy yojana from the village.

children.text: viśramya rajanīm atra prātar gantāsi tām iti ||
children.translated_text: Rest here for the night; in the morning you will go there.'
The night was passed by me both with sleep, together with my beloved, and sleeplessness from anxiety over wealth;

children.text: saṃkṣiptā ca nirastā ca yāpitā yāminī mayā ||
children.translated_text: thus it was both shortened and driven away.
In the morning, after I had gone two krośas, I saw, surrounded by a grove of plantains,
a charity pavilion crowded with groups of travelers.
And I saw foreigners having shaving done for them,
and being honored with oiling, rubbing, clothing, food, and the like.
After I too had undergone shaving and the other rites, had received clothing and excellent food,
and was lying on a bed, I was questioned by the master of the sattra at nightfall:

children.text: kvacit kaścit tvayā dṛṣṭaḥ prājño vāṇijadārakaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Have you seen anywhere a certain wise merchant's son,
named <s>Sānudāsa</s>, tall, dark, and with copper-colored corners of his eyes?

children.text: tatas taṃ pṛṣṭavān asmi sānudāsena kiṃ tava
children.translated_text: Then I asked him, 'What is <s>Sānudāsa</s> to you,

children.text: kasya vā sānudāso 'sāv iti tenoditaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or whose <s>Sānudāsa</s> is he?' Then he said:
'He is the virtuous nephew of one named <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>,
an adornment of <s>Tāmraliptī</s>; he went to sea by ship.
And that ship, they say, struck hard by a storm in the ocean,
broke apart and filled with water, like a cloud in the sky.
And this report, spreading about and causing an extreme fainting fit,
made <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> faint, like a cruel venomous serpent-woman.
He too has established sattras in all countries, in wildernesses and at crossings,
and in towns on the seashore,
thinking, "Perhaps someday, in some sattra, some traveler

children.text: pānthaḥ kaścit kvacit satre pravṛttiṃ kathayed iti ||
children.translated_text: may tell news that <s>Sānudāsa</s>, cast from the ship, is alive."

children.text: tat te yadi sa dīrghāyur āyuṣmandarśanaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, if that long-lived man has come within your sight, O long-lived one,

children.text: ācakṣva nas tato dīnā janatā jīvyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: tell us, so that then these wretched people may live.'

children.text: mama tv āsīt pratijñāyāḥ kiyatsampāditaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: But I thought, 'How much of my vow has been accomplished
if, casting off shame, I reveal myself to this man?
Therefore I shall say this.' Having decided so, I said:

children.text: sānudāsaḥ punaḥ potam āruhya gatavān iti ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Sānudāsa</s> has again boarded a ship and gone away.'
And in the morning I went to <s>Pāṇḍyamathurā</s>, possessed of hundreds of wonders,
as if it were a slab of wish-fulfilling gem that had fulfilled almost every desire.
There I entered a shop crowded with heaps of jewels of varied brilliance,
like the ocean after its water had been drunk by <s>Agastya</s>.
There two men came up, bringing an ornament;
of the two, one was the buyer and the other the seller of it.

children.text: tau taṃ vāṇijam abrūtāṃ ratnatattvavidā tvayā
children.translated_text: They said to that merchant, 'Since you know the true nature of jewels,
please state the proper price of this ornament.'

children.text: tenāpi tac ciraṃ dṛṣṭvā na jānāmīti bhāṣite
children.translated_text: But when he too, after looking at it for a long time, said, 'I do not know,'

children.text: tau māṃ niścalayā dṛṣṭyā dṛṣṭavantam apṛcchatām ||
children.translated_text: they asked me, who was looking at it with a motionless gaze.

children.text: niścalasnigdhayā dṛṣṭyā suṣṭhu dṛṣṭam idaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: 'You have looked at this very carefully with a steady and attentive gaze;

children.text: manyāvahe vijānāti mūlyam asya bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: we think that you know its price.'
Then, smiling, I said with my hand upturned in indifference,
'This is certainly not very hard to know. Why are you two troubled for nothing?

children.text: koṭir asya samaṃ mūlyaṃ ratnatattvavido viduḥ
children.translated_text: Those who know the true nature of jewels know that its exact price is a crore;
anything more or less than that depends on the wishes of the buyer and seller.'

children.text: atha vikrāyakas toṣān muktāśrur mām avocata
children.translated_text: Then the seller, shedding tears from delight, said to me,

children.text: yadīyaṃ mūlyam etasya dhanaṃ dhanyās tato vayam ||
children.translated_text: 'If this sum is its price, then we are fortunate and blessed.

children.text: api bhūṣaṇam etan me koṭimūlyaṃ bhaved iti
children.translated_text: May this ornament of mine be worth a crore,

children.text: sadaiva me manasy āsīd ayam eva manorathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: such was always my wish in my mind.'
Then the buyer said, 'This too was my wish,

children.text: api nāma labheyāham idaṃ koṭyeti cetasi ||
children.translated_text: thinking, "If only I might obtain this for a crore."'

children.text: tatas tāv astuvātāṃ māṃ namas te viśvakarmaṇe
children.translated_text: Then those two praised me: 'Homage to you, <s>Viśvakarman</s>!

children.text: ko hi mānuṣadurbodham idaṃ budhyate mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For what human being could understand this thing, hard for human beings to know?
We two, wishing to buy and sell, have many times gone all around the city
for the sake of examining this object.

children.text: pṛthivī mūlyam asyeti kaścid āha parīkṣakaḥ
children.translated_text: One examiner said, "The earth is its price";

children.text: ajānan kākinīty anyo na kiṃcid iti cāparaḥ ||
children.translated_text: another, not knowing, said, "A kākinī," and another said, "Nothing."

children.text: tvatkṛtena tu mūlyena janitaṃ nau mahatsukham
children.translated_text: But by the price given by you a great happiness has been produced for us both;

children.text: etad ekārthayor āsīd abhīṣṭam ubhayor api ||
children.translated_text: this was the single desired object of both of us.'
After praising me in such words and being delighted, those two bestowed on me
ten thousand suvarṇas, together with excellent ornaments and garments.

children.text: atha vārttām imāṃ śrutvā nṛpeṇāhūya sādaram
children.translated_text: Then, when the king heard this news, I was respectfully summoned
and tested in jewels that had been rejected by the examiners.
with many servants, much wealth, and a pleasure-garden full of many affairs

children.text: viśālaṃ bahuśālaṃ ca prītaḥ prādāt sa me gṛham ||
children.translated_text: Pleased, he gave me a spacious house with many halls.

children.text: ataḥ param ahaṃ tasyām āsaṃ puri parīkṣakaḥ
children.translated_text: After that I lived in that city as an examiner,

children.text: dharmeṇaiva ca māṃ kaścin na parīkṣām akārayat ||
children.translated_text: and no one had me conduct an examination except honestly and fairly.

children.text: evaṃ ca vasatas tatra mameyam abhavan matiḥ
children.translated_text: As I was living there in this way, this thought arose in me:
'By what thing, bought for a small price, might a great profit arise?'

children.text: upalabhyas tato lokāt karpāso guṇavān iti
children.translated_text: Then, having learned from the people that cotton was of good quality,
I had seven heaps of it made, resembling the peaks of <s>Kailāsa</s>.

children.text: dhik karpāsakathāṃ tucchāṃ sarvathā mūṣakeṇa te
children.translated_text: Fie on the worthless tale of cotton; in every way, by a mouse,
through the flame of a lamp, those heaps of yours were reduced to heaps of ash.

children.text: mathurāyāṃ ca maryādā gṛhaṃ yasya pradīpyate
children.translated_text: And in <s>Mathurā</s> the rule is that the man whose house catches fire

children.text: prakṣipyate sa tatraiva sakuṭumbo raṭann iti ||
children.translated_text: is thrown right into it together with his family, crying out.

children.text: atha hastadvitīyo 'ham iyaṃ dig iti saṃbhraman
children.translated_text: Then I, with only my hands as companions, confusedly thinking, 'This is the direction,'
fled in panic, aiming for the northern quarter.

children.text: dhāvitvā ca triyāmārdham aharardhaṃ ca raṃhasā
children.translated_text: After running swiftly for half the night and half the day,
I escaped from that dangerous place and, utterly exhausted, slept at the foot of a banyan tree.
Then, when the moon with cool rays was shining and my overpowering fatigue had subsided,
I heard the sound of people all around that great banyan.

children.text: āsīc ca mama hā kaṣṭaṃ hanta naṣṭo 'smi saṃprati
children.translated_text: And I thought, 'Alas, disaster! Ah, now I am lost,

children.text: jvalati jvalane kṣipto nirghṛṇair draviḍair iti ||
children.translated_text: thrown into a blazing fire by merciless <s>Draviḍa</s>s.'
Then I saw travel gear, including patched cloaks, old umbrellas, and sandals,
and travelers' outfits, as they spoke in the language of <s>Gauḍa</s>.

children.text: hā mātar jīvito 'smīti tān ālokyāśvasaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing them, I then took heart, thinking, 'Ah, mother, I am alive!'

children.text: rakṣomukto hi nāśvasyāt ko vā dṛṣṭvā narān naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For what man, freed from rakṣasas, would not take heart on seeing men?
Then they spread beds of leaves, set down their gear,
sat all around me, rested, and asked me,

children.text: āgacchati kuto deśān nagarād vā bhavān iti
children.translated_text: 'From what country or city does your honor come?'
I too told them, 'From a city in the land of the <s>Pāṇḍya</s>s.'

children.text: atha taiḥ saspṛhaiḥ pṛṣṭaṃ mathurāyāṃ tvayā yadi
children.translated_text: Then, full of eagerness, they asked, 'If in <s>Mathurā</s>

children.text: sānudāso vaṇigdṛṣṭas tato naḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: you have seen the merchant <s>Sānudāsa</s>, then please tell us.'

children.text: mayoktaṃ sānudāsākhyo vaṇik tatra na vidyate
children.translated_text: I said, 'There is no merchant there named <s>Sānudāsa</s>.

children.text: bhavantaḥ katamat tatra pṛcchantīty ucyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Tell me which one there you are asking about.'

children.text: tatas te kathayanti sma tāmraliptyāṃ vaṇikpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Then they began to say, 'In <s>Tāmraliptī</s> there is a lord of merchants,

children.text: gaṅgadatto guṇān yasya na na veda bhavān api ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>, whose virtues even you surely know.

children.text: ye guṇān na vidus tasya sadvīpāt prāṅmahodadheḥ
children.translated_text: Those who do not know his virtues, proclaimed by a fame spreading

children.text: vyāpinyā kīrtitān kīrtyā na jātās te 'thavā mṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as far as the islands east of the great ocean, have either not been born or are dead.
His sister's son, <s>Sānudāsa</s>, lost, they say, because of a shipwreck,
is staying in <s>Pāṇḍya</s> <s>Mathurā</s>, having gathered a stock of cotton.

children.text: gaṅgadattas tu pānthebhyaḥ pravṛttim upalabhya tām
children.translated_text: But <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>, having obtained that report from travelers,

children.text: āhūyāha sma suhṛdaḥ prītāṃś ca paricārakān ||
children.translated_text: summoned his friends and beloved attendants and said:

children.text: ye me śoṇitam āyānti gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāpathāt
children.translated_text: 'Those who bring me my own blood from the <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>

children.text: tān ahaṃ suhṛdaḥ sphītais toṣayāmi dhanair iti ||
children.translated_text: I shall satisfy with abundant wealth, as friends.'

children.text: tad vayaṃ gaṅgadattena tam ānetuṃ visarjitāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore we have been sent by <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> to bring him back.

children.text: yadi cāsau tvayā dṛṣṭas tad ācaṣṭāṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: And if you have seen him, then let your honor tell us.'

children.text: mama tv āsīd varaṃ kṣiptas tatraivāhaṃ vibhāvasau
children.translated_text: But I thought, 'Better that I had been thrown into the fire right there

children.text: na tv apūrṇapratijñena mātur ānanam īkṣitum ||
children.translated_text: than that I should look upon my mother's face with my promise unfulfilled.'
Then I began to say this: 'The poor <s>Sānudāsa</s>,

children.text: karpāse jvalati kṣiptaḥ pāṇḍyair niṣkaruṇair iti ||
children.translated_text: when the cotton was burning, was thrown into it by the pitiless <s>Pāṇḍya</s>s.'

children.text: tatas tāḍitavakṣaskās tāram āraṭya te ciram
children.translated_text: Then, beating their breasts and wailing loudly for a long time,
they began to confer in voices made thin by grief:
'You were requested by <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> and came for the sake of <s>Sānudāsa</s>.
How will you be able to report to him the news of that man's death?
And when this inauspicious report, fit for the laughter of <s>Vaivasvata</s>, has been heard,

children.text: campāyāṃ tāmraliptyāṃ ca jīvitavyaṃ na kenacit ||
children.translated_text: no one in <s>Campā</s> or <s>Tāmraliptī</s> will be able to go on living.
Therefore abandon your own selves and become free of debt to your master.
Let <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> learn that news from some other source.'
Then, lighting a pile of wood and intending to enter it,

children.text: stuvanto devatāḥ svāḥ svāḥ paryakrāman pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: they praised their own deities and circumambulated it clockwise.

children.text: mama tv āsīd aho kaṣṭaṃ baddho 'haṃ naraśambaraḥ
children.translated_text: But I thought, 'Ah, misery! I am caught, a human <s>Śambara</s>.

children.text: sotsāhair api durlaṅghyaṃ jālaṃ jālmaiḥ prasāritam ||
children.translated_text: These villains have spread a net that even the energetic can scarcely cross.'

children.text: athoccair āraṭāmi sma bho bho tyajata sāhasam
children.translated_text: Then I cried out loudly, 'Ho! Ho! Abandon this rash act.

children.text: sānudāsaḥ sa evāhaṃ vidheyo bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: I am that very <s>Sānudāsa</s>, ready to obey your commands.'
Then their breaths, which had been ready to depart because of grief,
came up to their throats because of the joy of finding me.
Since some life remained, their dear breaths turned back,
and, moist with joy, they leapt about, shaking the grove with their clapping.

children.text: te stuvantas tato hṛṣṭāḥ sugataṃ saugatā iva
children.translated_text: Then, delighted, praising the <s>Sugata</s> like Buddhists,
they circumambulated me many times and bowed to me with their heads.
Then, placing me in a palanquin, with journeys that were not very long,
they brought me to <s>Tāmraliptī</s>, pleased as though they had found treasure.
Then my maternal uncle, joyful and with splendid pomp, came out to meet me,
as if I had come to marry the daughter of a king.
That festival could not be described even by <s>Vyāsa</s> at length;
I shall tell it to you in brief, for this is the way of those whose speech falters.

children.text: tiṣṭhantu tāvad akalaṅkakuṭumbidārāḥ śītāṃśubhāsvadanilair api ye na dṛṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Let alone, for the moment, the spotless wives of householders, who are not seen even by the moon, the sun, and the wind...

children.text: sindūrapāṭalitakhaṇḍanaṭair naṭadbhir nagnāṭakair api narendrapatheṣu gītam ||
children.translated_text: It was sung on the king's highways even by naked performers dancing, their bodies reddened with sindūra.

children.text: vidyāvṛttais tato viprair gaṅgadattaḥ svayaṃ ca mām
children.translated_text: Then brahmins distinguished by learning and conduct, and <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> himself,

children.text: madhurair upapannaiś ca vacanair ity abodhayat ||
children.translated_text: roused me with sweet and fitting words as follows:

children.text: pitā me dhriyate bhartā bhṛtyān āttena kiṃ mama
children.translated_text: 'Formerly you were indifferent, thinking: "My father, my maintainer, is alive;
what need have I to weary myself for servants who are already supported?"
But now you are bound by a mother, wife, children, elders, and the like,

children.text: avaśyabharaṇīyaiś ca rakṣyaiś ca paravān bhavān ||
children.translated_text: who must certainly be maintained and protected.
Therefore that household group, whose maintainer is you and whose maintainer is away,

children.text: asārathāv iva rathe dhruvaṃ yan na bravīmi tat ||
children.translated_text: is surely like a chariot without a charioteer; I hardly need say so.
So, dear son, because they are longing with longing to see you,

children.text: svakuṭumbam anukaṇṭhaṃ kuru yāhi gṛhān iti ||
children.translated_text: show compassion to your own family and go home.'

children.text: ekadā kaṃcid adrākṣam āceraṃ nāma vāṇijam
children.translated_text: One day I saw a merchant named <s>Ācera</s>,
who was going to <s>Suvarṇabhūmi</s> with countless merchants.

children.text: tair gatvā saha potena kaṃcid adhvānam ambudheḥ
children.translated_text: After traveling with them by ship over some distance of the ocean,
we left the vessel on the shore and set out along the bank.
Then we encamped at the foot of a great mountain whose peaks licked the clouds,
crowded with trees and glowing red in the shining light.
After food had been brought there and we were sitting on beds of leaves,

children.text: ity asmān anuśāsti sma sārthavāhaḥ kṣapākṣaye ||
children.translated_text: the caravan-leader instructed us in this way at the end of night:
'Tie your provision-bags firmly in three parts upon your backs,
and hang oil-flasks from your necks, merchants.
Grasp tightly with your hands these cane-creepers, soft, thick,
and free from the defects of drying and the rest, and climb the mountain.

children.text: latām anīdṛśīṃ mohād yaḥ kaścid avalambate
children.translated_text: If anyone through confusion grasps a creeper that is not like these,

children.text: pramīto himavaty asmin sa prayāti parāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: he dies on this snowy mountain and goes to the other world.
This is called the Cane Path, a destroyer of every courage,
like a great <s>Vināyaka</s> for those set in motion by the hope of gold.'
Having heard this and the rest, we and those like us became despondent,
yet, seized by the demon of greed for gold, we did just as he said.
Then one man, after climbing far, had the tip of his cane-creeper broken;
as if his cord had been sliced by a razor, he came down to earth like a hero.

children.text: vayam evācalāgraṃ tad āruhya paridevya ca
children.translated_text: We ourselves climbed to the summit of that mountain, lamented,

children.text: nirupya ca jalaṃ tasmai tatraivāneṣmahi kṣapām ||
children.translated_text: set aside water for him, and spent the night right there.
In the morning, after traveling a long road, we saw a river
crowded with stones in the shapes of cows, horses, goats, and sheep.
Then <s>Ācera</s>, standing in front, loudly held back the travelers:

children.text: mā mā spṛkṣata vāry etad bho bho tiṣṭhata tiṣṭhata ||
children.translated_text: 'Do not, do not touch this water! Friends, stop, stop!

children.text: mūḍhaiḥ spṛṣṭam idaṃ yair yais te te pāṣāṇatāṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: All the fools by whom this has been touched have turned into stone.

children.text: atha vā svayam evaināṃ suhṛdaḥ kiṃ na paśyatha ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, friends, why do you not see it yourselves?

children.text: vaṃśān paśyatha yān asyāḥ parasmin saritas taṭe
children.translated_text: Look at the bamboos on the far bank of this river;
the strong wind from the far bank bends them toward this near shore.
Take firmly in your hands one among these bamboos

children.text: eṣām anyatamaṃ gāḍhaṃ gṛhṇīdhvaṃ maskaraṃ karaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is not spoiled by thinness, softness, rottenness, dryness, or other defects.

children.text: vāte mantharatāṃ yāte maskarāt tuṅgatāṃ gatāt
children.translated_text: When the wind has grown slow and the bamboo, risen high,
has reached the far side of the river, descend slowly.
But whoever grasps a bamboo with defects such as rottenness or dryness
falls from it and goes to a body as fixed as a mountain.
This is called the Bamboo Path, terrifying among great roads;
it is quickly crossed with skill by skillful men who do not despair.'
As a child, at the command of a spell-reciter, would enter an asura's cave
without reflecting at all, so we attempted that.

children.text: teṣām ekaṃ kṛśād vaṃśād viśīrṇād apatat tataḥ
children.translated_text: Of them, one fell from a thin and broken bamboo;

children.text: śilābhūtāṃ tanuṃ tyaktvā gatiṃ māheśvarīm agāt ||
children.translated_text: abandoning a body become stone, he attained the state of <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: avatīrya tu vaṃśebhyas tyaktvā dūreṇa tāṃ nadīm
children.translated_text: But after we had come down from the bamboos and left that river far behind,

children.text: tasmai salilam anyasya amadāma nyavasāma ca ||
children.translated_text: we gave him water from another source and encamped.
In the early morning, after making the road carry us for two yojanas,
I then saw a path extremely narrow, like that of a serpent.
On both sides of it was a terrifying, unprecedented abyss,
with a mass of blind darkness that frightened even the dispeller of darkness.
Then <s>Ācera</s> said to the travelers, 'With wood, leaves, grass, and the like,
both wet and dry, let this wilderness be made smoky.
When they see this, Kirātas come from all directions

children.text: chāgān vikretum āyānti kirātāḥ parito diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to sell goats fitted with saddles and tiger-skin coverings.
Buy them with safflower oil, pieces of cloth,
broken rice, sindūra, salt, and grease as well.
Then mount the backs of the goats, take long bamboos in your hands,
and cross the road, brittle as the rod of a black eyebrow.
And if other travelers, having taken gold from the gold mine,
should ever return by this same path,

children.text: tatas tair asmadīyaiś ca saṃmukhīnair ihāntare
children.translated_text: then, when they and our own people meet face to face here midway,
they must enter the abyss along with their hopes of gold.

children.text: na mahāsaṃkaṭād asmān mārgād utkramya vidyate
children.translated_text: Off this road of great danger there is no place
for a line of goats to stand, nor any room to turn back.
Therefore at the front of the line there should set out a brave man,
practiced with the lance, quick-witted, and experienced in battle.
Even one such capable man can strike down a succession of opponents,

children.text: na parābhāvyate yāvad apareṇa pareṇa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he is not overpowered by another after another so long as he is not defeated by the next.'
And this, called the <s>Ajapatha</s>, the Goat Path, is terrifying even when merely heard of;
when seen, it is especially like a precipice for those who wish to fall.
While <s>Ācera</s> was speaking in this way,
a troop of mlecchas came up, their tall bows bent in circles, with a herd of goats in front.
When they had gone back and the buying and selling had been completed,
the travelers bathed and, crying aloud, worshiped <s>Śaṅkara</s> and <s>Keśava</s>.
Then the long line of goats, with the travelers mounted, set out,

children.text: raṃhasiny api niṣkampā nivāte naur ivāmbhasi ||
children.translated_text: swift yet unwavering, like a boat on water when there is no wind.

children.text: tasyāś ca pathikaśreṇyāḥ saptamaḥ paścimād aham
children.translated_text: In that row of travelers I was seventh from the rear,
and <s>Ācera</s> was sixth, directly behind me.
When events had taken this sort of course, there was heard loudly from afar
the 'ṣṭhā, ṣṭha' sound, raised ahead by bamboos being struck,

children.text: chāgānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ ca dhīrāṇām api sādakaḥ
children.translated_text: and also the noise that could break even steady goats and men,

children.text: majjatāṃ dhvāntajambāle me me hā heti ca dhvaniḥ ||
children.translated_text: the cries of 'me, me!' and 'alas, alas!' as they sank into the mire of darkness.
In every way, within a single instant the opposing caravan was destroyed,
while ours, standing from the seventh onward, remained as the sole remnant.

children.text: atha mām avaśāsti sma grāmaṇīḥ kim udāsyate
children.translated_text: Then the headman ordered me, 'Why are you idle?

children.text: ekakaḥ puruṣaś cāyaṃ paraḥ svar nīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: This enemy, though alone, must be sent to heaven.'

children.text: paras tu vaṃśam ujjhitvā baddhvā mūrdhani cāñjalim
children.translated_text: But the opponent dropped his bamboo, joined his hands above his head,
and, helpless because his caravan of travelers had been killed, pleaded helplessly with me:
'My family line, with only one branch left, is sinking;
you should not, by cutting off that branch, destroy it utterly.

children.text: eka eva priyaḥ putraḥ pitror aham acakṣuṣoḥ
children.translated_text: I am the one beloved son of my two blind parents;

children.text: andhayaṣṭhis tayos tasmād bhrātar māṃ mā vadhīr iti ||
children.translated_text: I am their blind man's staff. Therefore, brother, do not kill me.'

children.text: āsīc ca mama dhik prāṇān pāpapāṃsuvidhūsarān
children.translated_text: And I thought, 'Shame on my life, grey with the dust of sin;

children.text: dhig dhig eva suvarṇaṃ tat prāpyaṃ prāṇivadhena yat ||
children.translated_text: shame, shame indeed on that gold which must be obtained by killing living beings.

children.text: tasmān nihantu mām eṣa varākaḥ priyajīvitaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore let this poor man, to whom life is dear, kill me instead;
my life will then be of use to his two dim-sighted parents.'
Then <s>Ācera</s>, copper-colored and pale with anger and despondency,
spoke to me in a harsh, slow voice, as if his speech were choked:
'Hey, young bullock, unable to judge the proper and improper time!

children.text: kva kṛpāṇocitaḥ kālaḥ kva kṛpā kṛpaṇocitā ||
children.translated_text: What has a time fit for the sword to do with pity fit for a wretch?
Ah, your compassion is well proven, you knower of doctrine,
since for the sake of one petty man you wish to kill sixteen.

children.text: sacchāge nihate hyasmiñ jīvitāḥ syuś caturdaśa
children.translated_text: For if this fine goat is killed, fourteen will live;

children.text: ahate tu sahānena bhavatā ca hatā vayam ||
children.translated_text: but if it is not struck down, we are killed along with this man and you.

children.text: na cāpi rakṣituṃ kṣudram ātmānaṃ dustyajaṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: Nor should one, in order to save a petty creature, abandon the self that is so hard to abandon;

children.text: ātmā tu satataṃ rakṣyo dārair api dhanair api ||
children.translated_text: the self must always be protected, even at the cost of wives and wealth.'
Uttering this and the like, a long declamation made up only of the <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>,

children.text: sa pārtham iva māṃ viṣṇuḥ karma krūram akārayat ||
children.translated_text: he, like <s>Viṣṇu</s> with <s>Pārtha</s>, made me perform the cruel deed.
Then I, overcome by powerful shame and condemning the action,
struck the delicate feet of the opposing goat.
Then, as that kid sank into the ocean of darkness,
the traveler riding with it sank together with his thirst for wealth.
But we, with our small band reduced by the difficult road,
like survivors from the battle of the <s>Bhārata</s>, remained seven, our effort broken.

children.text: taṃ ca deśaṃ parikramya prāpya viṣṇupadītaṭam
children.translated_text: After circling around that region and reaching the bank of the <s>Viṣṇupadī</s>,
we gave water-offerings, mixed with tears, to the dead.

children.text: tatas tat tādṛśaṃ duḥkhaṃ bādhitaṃ no bubhukṣayā
children.translated_text: Then that grief of ours, terrible as it was, was overpowered by hunger;
for embodied beings there is no bodily pain equal to hunger.
Then, as we lay on beds of leaves without having obtained food,
our eyes troubled by scant sleep, the leader awakened us and said:

children.text: amī chāgāḥ pramāpyantāṃ tatas tanmāṃsam adyatām
children.translated_text: 'Let these goats be killed, and then let their meat be eaten.
Let bags be sewn from their hides, turned inside out.

children.text: tathā ca paridhīyantāṃ muktvā vighnakṛtaṃ ghṛṇām
children.translated_text: And put them on, abandoning the pity that creates obstacles,

children.text: yathā tāsām asṛkklinnaṃ yad antas tad bahir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: so that what is inside them, wet with blood, is outside.
Birds, like winged carriers, with their beaks split wide,
come from the gold-land to this land.
Thinking us lumps of meat, they will take us up through the sky in their beaks

children.text: suvarṇabhūmaye yānti tat tat saṃpādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and go to <s>Suvarṇabhūmi</s>. So arrange that.'

children.text: athāham abravaṃ brūte janatā yat tathaiva tat
children.translated_text: Then I said, 'What people say is exactly true:

children.text: tyajyatāṃ tat suvarṇaṃ yac chinatti śravaṇe iti ||
children.translated_text: let that gold be abandoned which cuts even at the hearing.

children.text: yenāhaṃ durgamān mārgād dharmeṇaiva tu durgateḥ
children.translated_text: Since from the difficult road, and indeed from misfortune,

children.text: tāritaś chāganāgena hanyāṃ taṃ nirghṛṇaḥ katham ||
children.translated_text: I was rescued by dharma through that elephant among goats, how could I heartlessly kill him?

children.text: tasmād alaṃ suvarṇena prāṇair evāthavā kṛtam
children.translated_text: Therefore enough of gold; or rather, enough even of life itself,

children.text: yena tenaiva dattebhyas tebhyo hanyāṃ suhṛttamam ||
children.translated_text: if I should kill that best of friends, the very one by whom these lives were given back.

children.text: athācero 'vadat pānthān ajaḥ svaḥ svaḥ pramāpyatām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Ācera</s> said to the travelers, 'Let each man's own goat be killed;

children.text: ayaṃ tu sānudāsīyaḥ sudūre mucyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: but this one belonging to <s>Sānudāsa</s> should be released far away.'

children.text: teṣām ekatamaḥ pānthas tam ajaṃ kvāpi nītavān
children.translated_text: One of the travelers took that goat somewhere,
and, returning with a hide hanging from a staff, said this:
'I exchanged another goat for <s>Sānudāsa</s>'s goat;

children.text: tadīyaṃ cedam ānītam ajinaṃ dṛśyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and this hide of his has been brought. Look at it.'

children.text: mayā tu pratyabhijñāya tasyaivājasya carma tat
children.translated_text: But I recognized that hide as belonging to that very goat,

children.text: uktaṃ nāsau tvayā muktaḥ prāṇair muktaḥ priyair iti ||
children.translated_text: and said, 'He was not released by you; he was released from his dear life.'
Then, on the strength of a trustworthy statement,
we inferred that this journey through the sky was more frightening than crossing the ocean and devoid of reason.
Then the sky, along with the quarters, was covered by birds of pale hue,

children.text: śāradair iva jīmūtaiḥ sāśam ākāśam āvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: with ill-omened cries, like autumn clouds.
The elephant, its massive mountain-like shoulders battered by the wind of their wings,
became like a mountain whose ring of wings had been cut away by the edge of <s>Śakra</s>'s weapon.

children.text: atha kaṇṭhagataprāṇān asmān ādāya khaṃ khagāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the birds took us, whose lives had reached our throats, into the sky,
and all seven of them attacked the seven of us like <s>Garutmats</s> attacking serpents.

children.text: pariśiṣṭo 'paras teṣāṃ sa ca madgrāhiṇo balāt
children.translated_text: One other among them remained over, and he, because my captor had taken me by force,
being without a share, pitilessly tried to tear apart me alone.

children.text: atha raudram abhūd yuddhaṃ gṛdhrayoḥ svārthagṛddhayoḥ
children.translated_text: Then there was a terrible battle between the two vultures, each greedy for his own gain,
like that of ten-necked <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, terrifying those who move through the sky.
I was pulled in turn from the beak of one bird to the beak of the other,

children.text: kaccic ca skhalitas tasyāḥ khastaḥ śaṃkaram asmaram ||
children.translated_text: and somehow, slipping from that beak and falling from the sky, I remembered <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
By the tips of their beaks and claws, hard as points of diamond,

children.text: kuṭṭitaṃ tat tayoś carma jātaṃ tita:ujarjaram ||
children.translated_text: that leather covering of theirs, beaten again and again, became utterly tattered.
Then I was squeezed out from the battered leather casing
and fell into some lake that astonished the mind with its beauty.
There, after rubbing my blood-red limbs with lotuses,

children.text: snātas tarpitadevaś ca paścād amṛtam āharam ||
children.translated_text: I bathed, satisfied the gods, and afterward took in water like nectar.

children.text: tattaṭe kṣaṇam āsitvā niṣadya ca gataśramaḥ
children.translated_text: After sitting for a moment on its bank and resting until my weariness had gone,
I saw that forest, filled with many unprecedented wonders.
There I forgot the pain born from the battle of the <s>Bhāruṇḍas</s>,
as though I were wandering in <s>Nandana</s> after escaping the forest of sword-leaves.
There was not even one tree there with withered and discolored leaves, or struck by lightning-fire,

children.text: apuṣpaḥ phalahīno vā yatraiko 'pi na pādapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or without flowers, or without fruit.
Kadambas, mālatīs, kundas, mādhavīs, mallikās, and others
there always had shoots speckled dark by swarms of bees.
The ground was adorned with grasses four finger-breadths high,
dark as the throat of a peacock and soft as hare's wool.
There lions, tigers, peacocks, serpents, and others,
compassionate, observed vows on leaves, flowers, water, and air.
Still unsated in my desire to see, I wandered all around the forest

children.text: kasyāpi caraṇaiḥ kṣuṇṇām adrākṣaṃ padavīm iva ||
children.translated_text: and saw what seemed to be a path trodden by someone's feet.

children.text: tayā saṃcaramāṇaś ca mantharaṃ dūram antaram
children.translated_text: Moving slowly along it for a long distance,
I reached a shallow river with low banks on both sides.
I crossed that river, whose shoals were golden and whose sand was mixed with jewels and gold,
and, after bathing properly, I worshiped the deities and teachers.
Near the bank of the river, surrounded by a grove of plantains,
I saw an ascetics' forest where monkeys sat cross-legged.
There I beheld a lord of sages, his matted hair tawny like fresh lightning, seated upon the surface of a broad mat of kuśa grass,
like the āhavanīya fire placed in the belly of a fire-pit whose wooden fuel had been stilled by oblations of ghee.
I approached to bow to him, as gentle moonlight streamed from him,
like the winter sun whose touch quiets inner heat.
Then he, his cheeks wet with tears of joy, said to me,
"Is it well with your merchant <s>Sānudāsa</s>?"

children.text: mama tv āsīt tato nāma divyaṃ cakṣus tapasvinām
children.translated_text: Then this thought arose in me: surely ascetics have a divine eye
by which they see every matter that is beyond the range of the fleshly eye.

children.text: yan me yādṛcchikaṃ nāma yac ca vyāpārahetukam
children.translated_text: The name that came to me by chance, and the name connected with my trade,

children.text: tat kīrtitam anenādya na kadācid api śrutam ||
children.translated_text: he has uttered today, though he had never heard it before.
As I was thinking this and had taken the seat he indicated,
the best of sages, smiling, spoke thus, slowly because of his modesty:

children.text: tvayā yac cintitaṃ tāta tataḥ prati tathaiva tat
children.translated_text: "What you have thought, dear son, is exactly so in that respect.

children.text: nāmamātrakathā nāti citraṃ hi tapasaḥ phalam ||
children.translated_text: The mere telling of a name is not very marvelous, for it is a fruit of austerity.

children.text: dhruvakādyair yathā madyam upāyaiḥ pāyito bhavān
children.translated_text: How you were made to drink liquor by <s>Dhruvaka</s> and the others through various means,
and how, in the garden, you met <s>Gaṅgadattā</s> through <s>Vadhukā</s>;
how you were released from the battle of the <s>Bhāruṇḍas</s>, as from between the fangs of <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: vimuktas tvam iha prāptaḥ sarvaṃ tad viditaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: and came here: all of that is known to me.
You have experienced disasters with conveyances and vessels, dear son,
and have crossed mountains, wildernesses, and rivers very hard to cross.

children.text: yadarthaṃ cāyam āyāsaḥ prāptaḥ kṛcchratamas tvayā
children.translated_text: As for the purpose for which this labor, most difficult, has been undergone by you,

children.text: mitravaty eva tat sarvaṃ mātā te kathayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: your mother in <s>Mitravatī</s> will tell you all of it.
This whole undertaking of yours is for the attainment of gold,

children.text: tac ca samprāptadeśīyam ato mā viṣadad bhavān ||
children.translated_text: and that is in a region now reached; therefore do not be despondent.
For one like you, firm in courage and obedient to the instruction of one like me,
gold is easily attained by wise men with energy. Where could it go?
Therefore, sleeping in a leaf-hut and eating the parts of trees,
stay in this hermitage for a few days."
Then, while he brought forest food pleasing to my desired taste

children.text: vāneyam āharann annaṃ kṛṣṭapacyam ahaṃ dviṣan ||
children.translated_text: and increasing purity, vigor, and nourishment, I came to dislike food ripened by the plough.
Lying on a bed of leaves spread inside a leaf-hut,
I did not miss the lofty couch or the residence of <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>.
Thus, though I had forgotten sorrow through superhuman pleasures,
I constantly thought of my mother dwelling in the poor quarter.
I even praised the dangers that ended in travel through the sky:

children.text: suvarṇaprāptaye prāptā yā vipat saṃpad eva sā ||
children.translated_text: a disaster incurred for the sake of obtaining gold is itself prosperity.

children.text: ekadā taṃ mahātmānam abhitaḥ prāptam ambarāt
children.translated_text: One day, near that great-souled one, I saw coming from the sky
