a flying palace, radiant as <s>Meru</s>, like merit made visible.
From him the maidens came forth, their faces lit with splendor,
like streaks of lightning from a cloud crossed by the bow of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: tatas tāḥ samparikramya praṇamya ca yatiprabhum
children.translated_text: Then, having circumambulated those around him and bowed to the lord of ascetics,
they ascended into the sky like rays from the moon.

children.text: ekā tu na gatā tāsām aṅkam āropya tāṃ muniḥ
children.translated_text: But one among them did not go; setting her on his lap, the sage,
his speech choked with joy, wiped her eyes and spoke to her:
Daughter <s>Gandharvadattā</s>, this <s>Sānudāsa</s> is your father.
Even disregarding us, he is to be honored by you with devotion.
And I regarded that excessive honor as utter mockery,
like a <s>Pramatha</s> being playfully worshiped by <s>Mahāgaurī</s>.

children.text: sā kadācin mayā pṛṣṭā ko 'yaṃ kā vā tvam ity atha
children.translated_text: Once I asked her, Who is this man, and who are you? Then,

children.text: śrūyatām iti bhāṣitvā tayor vṛttam avartayat ||
children.translated_text: after saying, Listen, she related the story of those two.
This man, of the <s>Bharadvāja</s> lineage, is a support of ascetics,
<s>Bharadvāja</s> the Vidyādhara, since he was intent on attaining vidyās.
And <s>Puraṃdara</s>, distressed by his great austerity,
was shaken, it is said, when his seat, naturally unmoving, began to move.
Even at the time of embracing <s>Śacī</s>, while thinking of a certain ascetic,
<s>Vāsava</s> lived in misery, his mind troubled by despondency.
But after learning from <s>Nārada</s> that <s>Bharadvāja</s> was an ascetic,
<s>Hari</s> appointed <s>Suprabhā</s>, the daughter of the lord of the Gandharvas:
In beauty, youth, and good fortune

children.text: atiśeṣe tvam ity eṣā pratītiḥ piṣṭapatraye ||
children.translated_text: you surpass even <s>Urvaśī</s>, proud as she is; such is the belief in the three worlds.

children.text: bharadvājam ato gatvā tvam ārādhaya sundari
children.translated_text: Therefore go to <s>Bharadvāja</s> and win his favor, beautiful one,
so that your beauty and good fortune may become fruitful.
Then <s>Suprabhā</s>, through words, glances, and gestures before that sage,
with amorous charms wished to draw away his mind, fixed on reality.

children.text: yadā nāśakad ākraṣṭum abdair bahutithair api
children.translated_text: When she could not draw it away even after very many years,
then, in despair, she undertook the work of a servant.
By gathering flowers, fetching water and food, sweeping the hut, and the like,

children.text: toṣito 'yam avocat tāṃ varaḥ kas te bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: she pleased him, and he said to her, What boon shall be yours?
She said, That good fortune for which the women of the thirty gods yearned

children.text: tan me bhagavatā dhairyāt saubhāgyaṃ durbhagīkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: has, holy one, been turned into misfortune for me by your firmness.
The mere feminine good fortune of beauty, ornaments, garlands, and unguents,
whose charms are purposeless, exists only with husbands who desire love.

children.text: tena vijñāpayāmy etat prītaś ced dayase varam
children.translated_text: Therefore I make this request: if you are pleased and grant a boon,

children.text: jagato 'pi varas tasmād bhavān evāstu no varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since you are the best even in the world, may you yourself be my chosen bridegroom.
For young maidens whose minds are battered by Love,
what other boon could be better than a man dear to mind and eyes?
Therefore, though the Blessed One has no fondness for passion,

children.text: vaśitvād rāgam ālambya saubhāgyaṃ me dadātv iti ||
children.translated_text: out of compassion, by his self-mastery let him take up passion and give me good fortune.

children.text: anurodhāc ca tenāsyām ekaiva janitā sutā
children.translated_text: And because of her entreaty, one daughter only was begotten by him in her;

children.text: ciram ārādhito bhaktyā virakto 'pi hi rajyate ||
children.translated_text: for even one who is detached becomes attached when long worshiped with devotion.

children.text: sā tu suprabhayā nītvā pitryaṃ viśvāvasoḥ puram
children.translated_text: But <s>Suprabhā</s> took her to the paternal city of <s>Viśvāvasu</s>,

children.text: vardhitā ca vinītā ca vidyāsu ca kalāsu ca ||
children.translated_text: and she was raised and instructed in vidyās and arts.

children.text: atha gandharvarājas tām ānīya duhituḥ sutām
children.translated_text: Then the Gandharva king brought that daughter of his daughter
and said to <s>Bharadvāja</s>, Let her name be given.

children.text: astu gandharvadatteyaṃ mahyaṃ dattā yatas tvayā
children.translated_text: Let this one be <s>Gandharvadattā</s>, since she has been given by you to me;

children.text: iti tasyāḥ kṛtaṃ nāma bharadvājena sārthakam ||
children.translated_text: thus a meaningful name was made for her by <s>Bharadvāja</s>.

children.text: suprabhāyāṃ tu yā kanyā bharadvājād ajāyata
children.translated_text: As for the girl who was born from <s>Bharadvāja</s> in <s>Suprabhā</s>,

children.text: nāmnā gandharvadatteti vitta mām eva tām iti ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Gandharvadattā</s>, know me to be that very one.
One time, on a dark night, I saw a mass of rock,
its trees lit up by the radiance of a network of gold-colored stones.

children.text: mama tv āsīd ayaṃ śailo hiraṇmayaśilaḥ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: But I thought, This mountain clearly has golden rock,
and there is auspicious gold on it, the cause of our prosperity.
Having decided thus, with my mind fettered by the snare of hope for gold,
I filled that spacious leaf-hut with stones.

children.text: tās tu prātaḥ śilā dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭo gandharvadattayā
children.translated_text: But in the morning, seeing those stones, <s>Gandharvadattā</s> asked me,

children.text: kim etad iti tasyai ca yathāvṛttaṃ nyavedayam ||
children.translated_text: What is this? and I told her exactly what had happened.

children.text: tayā tu kathitaṃ pitre mām āhūya sa cāvadat
children.translated_text: She told it to her father; he summoned me and said,

children.text: āyuṣman na hiraṇmayyaḥ śilā eva hi tāḥ śilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Long-lived one, they are not golden; those stones are indeed merely stones.
This is the light of herbs, golden-bright in darkness;
released at night, it expands with a brilliance that overpowers other lights.

children.text: dṛṣṭavān asi sauvarṇās tatsaṃparkād imāḥ śilāḥ
children.translated_text: Because of contact with it you saw these stones as golden,
and to those whose eyes are closed by the darkness of craving the quarters look yellow.

children.text: aham eva suvarṇaṃ ca campāṃ pratigamaṃ ca te
children.translated_text: I myself will soon arrange both gold
and your return to <s>Campā</s>; therefore abandon your agitation.

children.text: yāś ca tās tuṣṭatuṣṭena muhūrtenāhṛtāḥ śilāḥ
children.translated_text: Those stones, which I had brought in a moment while pleased and delighted,
were all cleared away by me with pain upon pain over the whole day.

children.text: ekadā kacchapīṃ vīṇāṃ mahyaṃ dattvāvadat muniḥ
children.translated_text: Once the sage gave me a kacchapī lute and said,

children.text: yad bravīmi tad ākarṇya tvam anuṣṭhātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: After hearing what I say, you should carry it out.
The account of me that was reported to you by <s>Gandharvadattā</s>

children.text: sa tathaiva yatas tasmād asmākam iyam ātmajā ||
children.translated_text: is exactly so; therefore this girl is our daughter.
And she is destined to be the dear consort of the future lord of the Vidyādharas;

children.text: na hi sāgarajanmā śrīḥ śrīpater anyam arhati ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Śrī</s>, born from the ocean, deserves no one other than <s>Śrīpati</s>.

children.text: tena campām iyaṃ nītvā deyā te cakravartine
children.translated_text: Therefore she must be taken by you to <s>Campā</s> and given to that emperor;

children.text: cihnair yaiś ca sa vijñeyaḥ kriyantāṃ tāni cetasi ||
children.translated_text: fix in your mind the signs by which he is to be recognized.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe ṣaṣṭhe bhavān māse gandharvān saṃnipātayet
children.translated_text: Every sixth month you should assemble the Gandharvas

children.text: puras teṣām iyaṃ gāyād geyaṃ nārāyaṇastutim ||
children.translated_text: In front of them she should sing this song, a hymn of praise to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: yas tu saṃvādayet kaścid gandharvas teṣu vīṇayā
children.translated_text: And whichever Gandharva among them should accompany it on the vīṇā,

children.text: vādayet tac ca yas tasmai dadyāḥ svatanayām iti ||
children.translated_text: and should play it, to him you should give your own daughter.

children.text: sarvathā bhavatāṃ yad yad vṛttaṃ gandharvasaṃsadi
children.translated_text: In every detail, whatever had happened to you in the assembly of the Gandharvas,
down to the playing of the vīṇā, all that was reported by him.

children.text: athāvāṃ munir āha sma khinnau sthaḥ putrakau ciram
children.translated_text: Then the sage said to us, 'My sons, you have been weary for a long time;

children.text: khedocchedāya tac campāṃ pratiṣṭhethāṃ yuvām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore go on to <s>Campā</s>, for the removal of your fatigue.'

children.text: tatas taṃ praṇipatyāhaṃ calitaḥ pracalo mudā
children.translated_text: Then, after bowing to him, I set out, thrilled and joyful;
after passing three watches of the night, I fell asleep.
Then I heard a superhuman sound from wooden vīṇās,
together with the resonance of flutes, lovely to mind and ear.
It was high, like instruments with coppery peaks, belonging to players of auspicious music,
skilled at driving sleep away and praised by bards.
Then, fully awake, I saw myself
occupying a couch with limbs of gold and latticework of jewels.
It was spread with patterned Chinese silk, beneath a canopy on a clear pavement,
in a cloth pavilion flashing with rows of polished golden poles.
On a seat of blue jewel stone, while the sun was covered by an awning,
sat the daughter of <s>Suprabhā</s>, intent on practicing the vīṇā.
There was also a whole cluster of tents, bright with varied colors and filled with handsome, well-dressed people,
packed with sacks full of gold.
There were merchants buying and selling jewels, gold, and other goods,
and narrow passages crowded with attentive camel-men.
In short, enough of excessive elaboration: in every way it was impossible for dull men to describe;

children.text: svapne 'pi na narair dṛṣṭā samṛddhiḥ kaiścid apy asau ||
children.translated_text: such prosperity had never been seen by any men even in a dream.

children.text: bhāradvājīm athāpṛcchaṃ mātaḥ kim idam adbhutam
children.translated_text: Then I asked <s>Bhāradvājī</s>, 'Mother, what is this wonder?

children.text: gandharvanagaraṃ māyā svapno vāyaṃ bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: Could this be a city of Gandharvas, an illusion, or a dream?'
'This is the fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of austerity earned by <s>Bharadvāja</s>;
for austerity well practiced by good people has immeasurable power.
Therefore this wealth, since it is endless and able to withstand expenditure as desired,
should be deposited everywhere except in the earth, among worthy recipients and the like.
Abandon concern about income and be intent on concern about expenditure;
for you certainly have, as a source of income, the sage's golden mountain.

children.text: kadā paśyāmi jananīm iti cākulatāṃ tyaja
children.translated_text: Give up the agitation, "When shall I see my mother?"

children.text: sārthasthānād itaś campā nanu krośeṣu pañcasu ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Campā</s> is only five krośas from the caravan-station here.'

children.text: sa ca me svapnam āyādiviṣayaḥ saṃśayas tayā
children.translated_text: And that doubt of mine about whether it was a dream or something actually perceived
was at once dispelled by her certainty-giving wisdom, as if by decisive insight.
Then I saw <s>Dhruvaka</s>, his face lowered out of embarrassment,
the rogue surrounded by friends of just that kind.

children.text: tam utthāyātha paryaṅkāt parirabhya ca sādaram
children.translated_text: Then, rising from the couch and respectfully embracing him,
I made him sit on my own bed, his embarrassment gone.
With conversation, embraces, golden seats, and the like,
I generously satisfied the whole group of friends, each according to seniority.
After that all <s>Campā</s>, with actors and dancers at its head,
surrounded that caravan, its frenzy of delight greatly increased.
One person after another, whose stream of breath had been broken by the height of joy,

children.text: amṛtaiva janaḥ kaścic cirāt kaścid udaśvasat ||
children.translated_text: drew breath again after a long time, as if revived by nectar.
With delicious streams of food, with jewels, garments, garlands, and the like,
and with abundant distributions of gold, I enriched the townsmen's guilds.

children.text: yaiś ca gomayapānīyaṃ kṣiptaṃ mama puraḥsarāḥ
children.translated_text: And those who had thrown cow-dung water before me
I especially lifted out of the hell of poverty.
Then I said to <s>Dhruvaka</s>, 'Good sir, from that hovel of poverty
of most dreadful appearance, have my mother brought to her own house.
For whatever amount of money that house was sold by mother,
you should redeem it from the buyer even for a hundred times that.
Who can bear to see a mother, such a sovereign lady,

children.text: draṣṭuṃ śaknoti yas tasya kṣudrakān dhig asūn iti ||
children.translated_text: gone into a poor hut? Shame on his petty breaths of life!'

children.text: tatas tena vihasyoktaṃ kva devī kva daridratā
children.translated_text: Then he said with a laugh, 'What has the goddess to do with poverty?
Who has seen the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> with its stream of water cut off?

children.text: tad eva bhavanaṃ devyāḥ samṛddhiḥ saiva cācalā
children.translated_text: That very house is the goddess's; that same prosperity is unmoving,
but now it has been made bright by you, like a night-lotus bed by the moon.'

children.text: iti tat kṣaṇasaṃkṣiptaṃ kṣiptvā sakṣaṇadaṃ dinam
children.translated_text: Thus, casting aside that day, compressed into a moment, together with its night,
at good daybreak I entered <s>Campā</s> like the lord of wealth entering <s>Alakā</s>.
Going through streets and lanes, with guild after guild before me,

children.text: gatvā narendram adrākṣaṃ surendram iva bhāsvaram ||
children.translated_text: I saw the king, shining like <s>Surendra</s>.

children.text: vandanāya tato dūrād dharaṇīm aham āśliṣam
children.translated_text: Then from afar I embraced the ground in order to bow,

children.text: asāv api mudāhūya mām āśliṣad akaitavam ||
children.translated_text: and he too, joyfully summoning me, sincerely embraced me.

children.text: sāravadbhir anantaiś ca mām asau bhūṣaṇāmbaraiḥ
children.translated_text: With excellent and countless ornaments and garments
he honored me and commanded, 'Son, let your mother be seen.'
Then with a heap of jewels and gold like the substance of <s>Sumeru</s>,
I filled the king's hard-to-fill netherworld of thirst.
Then, surrounded by the king's pleased retinue,

children.text: paṭhadbhiś ca tato viprair ātmīyam agamaṃ gṛham ||
children.translated_text: and by Brahmins reciting, I went to my own house.
In that unrestrained dance, with drums and other instruments sounding softly,

children.text: paurair harṣakṛtotsāhair na kṣuṇṇaḥ katham apy aham ||
children.translated_text: I was somehow not crushed by the townspeople whose zeal was created by joy.

children.text: ambām athārghajalapātrabhṛtaṃ nirīkṣya dūrād apāsarad asau janatā vihastā
children.translated_text: Then, when they saw my mother carrying a vessel of arghya-water from afar, that crowd withdrew in confusion.

children.text: pūrṇād ivāndhatamasāni tuṣārakānter āryāt pṛthag janaśatāni hi saṃbhramanti ||
children.translated_text: For hundreds of ordinary people, apart from the noble man, wander in blind darkness, as if separated from the full moon of snowy radiance.

children.text: labdhāntaras tataḥ pādau śirasā mātur aspṛśam
children.translated_text: Then, having found an opening, I touched my mother's feet with my head.
She too, with a half-full bowl of milk, fell upon me.

children.text: cirāc ca labdhaniśvāsā mām udasthāpayat tataḥ
children.translated_text: And after a long while, having recovered her breath, she raised me up.
Taking me by the hand, she led me into the inner hall of the house.
There I provided for the gods, the twice-born, and my teachers, together with the distressed and petitioners,

children.text: sphītaiḥ parijanaṃ ca svaṃ vibhavaiḥ samayojayam ||
children.translated_text: and also for my own attendants, with abundant wealth.
Then, when the state of my body had been restored as far as the taking of food,
at my mother's command I entered a dwelling exceedingly beautiful.
Sitting there on a couch, I saw my first wife seated level with the ground,
her face covered by the branches of her hands.
As I wiped her eyes, flowing with constant tears, out of pity for her,
I saw <s>Gaṅgadattā</s> clinging to the wall and turned away.

children.text: vāṅmātreṇāpi yat satyaṃ na sā saṃmānitā mayā
children.translated_text: For in truth she had not been honored by me even with a single word;
indeed, even the most venerable sages remember insults.
And seeing that dwelling-house, its floor covered with flowers,
I remembered the bank of the <s>Sindhu</s>, a house of many flowering creepers.

children.text: samudradinnayā sārdham anubhūtaṃ ca tatra yat
children.translated_text: I remembered too what I had experienced there with <s>Samudradinnā</s>,
our confident conduct of standing, going, singing, and the rest.

children.text: mama tv āsīd varaṃ duḥkham anubhūtaṃ mahan mayā
children.translated_text: But I thought, 'Better was that great sorrow which I had undergone,

children.text: hṛdayād vyāvṛtād yena kvāpi priyatamā gatā ||
children.translated_text: by which my beloved had gone somewhere from my heart when it was turned away.

children.text: duḥkhaśūnyaṃ tu tad dṛṣṭvā randhrān veṣaṇatatparā
children.translated_text: But now, seeing that heart empty of sorrow, she has looked for an opening,
and, pitiless, has entered it unhindered.

children.text: praviṣṭā hṛdayaṃ sā me yathāvāsagṛhaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: She has entered my heart just as she entered the dwelling-house;
would that this woman too might enter it. This longing is hard to realize.

children.text: sā hi hi mām āhvayaty eva paritrāyasva mām iti
children.translated_text: For surely she is calling to me, "Save me, save me!"
drawn away by the hand of a wave and carried off by the wicked ocean.'
As I was tormented by such thoughts, she, whose composure had been driven away by joy,
entered and quickly embraced me with limbs on which the hairs stood high.
But seeing that union with her was utterly impossible,
I kept thinking of that very woman, to be rescued from the crest of an ocean wave.
Forgetting the other circumstances because my mind was attached to her,

children.text: tām evāśvāsayāmi sma mā sma bhīrur bhaver iti ||
children.translated_text: I comforted that very woman, saying, 'Do not be afraid, timid one.'

children.text: atha bhīteva sāvocat svagṛhe vartate bhavān
children.translated_text: Then she, as if frightened, said, 'You are in your own house;

children.text: vipannavahanaḥ kaṣṭe na tu kṣārāmbudhāv iti ||
children.translated_text: your vehicle has perished in trouble, but you are not in the salt ocean.'
Then, with my mind drawn back by her from the dreadful salt ocean,

children.text: gṛhaṃ tat paritaḥ paśyann apaśyaṃ vanitādvayam ||
children.translated_text: I looked around that house and saw two women.
And remembering proper conduct in the presence of co-wives,

children.text: vakṣaḥsthāpi satī nāsau dorbhyām āliṅgitā mayā ||
children.translated_text: although she was placed upon my breast, I did not embrace her with my arms.
Then, in that changed situation, constrained by the presence of my wives,
my mother came in unannounced, her eyes troubled by fear.
When I rose up in confusion together with <s>Samudradinnā</s>,

children.text: ambā śayanam adhyāste śeṣās tv āsata bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: my mother took the bed, while the others sat on the ground.

children.text: tataḥ kiṃcid ivāmbāyai yat satyaṃ kupito 'bhavam
children.translated_text: Then, truth to tell, I became somewhat angry with my mother;
for even a mother who does not know the right time is despised by her son.
Then my mother laughed and said, 'Do not take me for one ignorant of the proper time.
After all, I am the wife of <s>Mitravarman</s>, who is almost omniscient.
If I were to come here in the presence of your wives,

children.text: vyanaśiṣyan mahat kāryaṃ tac cedam avadhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: a great matter would be ruined; so let this be heard.
Through hundreds of prayers a son was born as sonship for us both;
you were raised and taught by your father the four sciences.
But because of constant study of the books of wandering ascetics, Śākyas, and Nirgranthas,
talk of maintaining a household became exceedingly unfortunate for you.

children.text: tataḥ samantrinā rājñā saṃmantrya gurubhiś ca te
children.translated_text: Therefore the king, together with his minister, after consulting your teachers

children.text: suhṛdbhir dhruvakādyais tvam udyāne madhu pāyitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and your friends such as <s>Dhruvaka</s>, had you made to drink wine in the garden.

children.text: gaṅgadattā ca tair eva yojitā bhavatā saha
children.translated_text: And <s>Gaṅgadattā</s> was joined with you by those same men;

children.text: tayā tathā kṛtaś cāsi yathā vettha tvam eva tat ||
children.translated_text: and by her you were made such as you yourself know.

children.text: prakāreṇa ca yena tvaṃ gṛhaṃ nivāsitas tayā
children.translated_text: The manner in which you were made by her to live at home
was told to <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>'s mother by the king himself.

children.text: daridravāṭake yac ca rātriṃdivam asi sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: And as for your staying day and night in the poor quarter,

children.text: tad evaikam asau rājñā kalpitaś cāraṇādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that alone was arranged by the king through bards and other agents.

children.text: jānāty eva ca dīrghāyuḥ kva campā kva daridratā
children.translated_text: Long-lived one, he knows very well: what has <s>Campā</s> to do with poverty?
By whom has a full-moon night been seen stained with darkness?

children.text: sarvadaiva hi campāyām asmin balini pālake
children.translated_text: For always in <s>Campā</s>, under this powerful protector,

children.text: balāv iva mahīpāle balirājyaṃ na durlabham ||
children.translated_text: as under king <s>Bali</s> himself, the kingdom of <s>Bali</s> is not hard to obtain.

children.text: yāṃ ca rātriṃ bhavān suptas tasmin durgatavāṭake
children.translated_text: And on the night when you slept in that poor quarter,
<s>Gaṅgadattā</s> lay there beneath my cot.

children.text: tasyāḥ prabhṛti bhīmāyā yāvad adyatanīṃ niśām
children.translated_text: From that dreadful night up to the present night,
she has sat here in this interval on the ground beneath my cot.

children.text: yac ca tad dhanam etasyai tvayā dattaṃ tad etayā
children.translated_text: And the wealth which you gave to her
has all been placed by her in your treasury, entered in writing.
Therefore this woman, because she is loving and longs to see you,
and because she remembers a false rejection, does not deserve rejection.
And if she is humiliated by you in the presence of her co-wives,
being timid, because she is a woman, she might even give up her life.

children.text: etan manasi kṛtvārtham akāle 'py aham āgatā
children.translated_text: Keeping this matter in mind, I have come even at the wrong time.'
What time, indeed, is there for those who have weighty aims to accomplish to sink down in despondency?
This account of <s>Gaṅgadattā</s> has now been told to you;
now hear how the bride <s>Samudradinnā</s> came back.
You set out with travelers beginning with those from <s>Daridravāṭaka</s>;

children.text: prayuktās te nṛpeṇaiva sa ca siddhārthako vaṇik ||
children.translated_text: they had been sent by the king himself, and so had that merchant <s>Siddhārthaka</s>.

children.text: antare yac ca te vṛttaṃ sārthadhvaṃsādi bhīṣaṇam
children.translated_text: And the dreadful things that happened to you on the way, such as the destruction of the caravan,
down to your entry into <s>Tāmraliptī</s>, the rest of that was told by <s>Siddhārthaka</s>.
How, after you had fallen away in the wreck of the ship and were wandering on the shore of the ocean,
the hand of <s>Samudradinnā</s> was taken by you;

children.text: punaś ca bhinnapotaś ca pāṇḍyapuryāṃ ca yat tava
children.translated_text: and again, when the ship was broken, what happened to you in <s>Pāṇḍyapurī</s>,
ending with the burning of the cotton, and your coming to <s>Tāmraliptī</s>;
all that was made known to me by <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>

children.text: khyāpitaṃ yāvad ācero bhavantaṃ kvāpi nītavān ||
children.translated_text: through a continuous succession of letter-carriers, until <s>Ācera</s> led you away somewhere.
After that, since news of you had been cut off, I found none of it,
and from despair-born disgust I became eager for the next world.
While matters were much like this, the two brothers-in-law, announced by the doorkeepers,
then entered together with <s>Samudradinnā</s>.
After receiving hospitality with arghya-water and the like, and after resting from their fatigue for a moment,
the two looked at me awkwardly, addressed me, and spoke as follows:

children.text: tava putrāya pitrā nas tanayeyaṃ pratiśrutā
children.translated_text: 'This daughter of ours had been promised by our father to your son;
but he, confused by youth, was taken by <s>Gaṅgadattā</s>.
And when he, accepted by her, was going to his maternal uncle's house,

children.text: na śakyate yad ākhyātuṃ pulindaiḥ kila tat kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: what the <s>Pulindas</s> did cannot, in truth, be told.

children.text: vaiśasaṃ duḥśravaṃ śrutvā tat sūnor mitravarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: After hearing that dreadful, hard-to-hear slaughter of our son <s>Mitravarman</s>,

children.text: niṣpratyāśaṃ kuṭumbaṃ naḥ prasthitaṃ yavanān prati ||
children.translated_text: our family, without hope, set out toward the <s>Yavanas</s>.
Then, having boarded a ship and honored Brahmins and deities,
we entered the sea, imagining the destruction of our misfortune.

children.text: tataḥ prajavinaṃ potaṃ taṃ pracaṇḍaḥ prabhañjanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then a fierce storm split apart that swift, quivering ship,
as a lion splits a lordly elephant.
But we, through the power of karma, were lifted by waves swift as arrows
onto the backs of planks and brought to the shore of the ocean.
The bride, however, in the sea that had become a single flood and was crowded with rolling waves,
was tossed about like a young sārasa bird in the sky by a wandering cloud.
Abandoning hope for <s>Samudradinnā</s>, and hope for wealth as well, with great tears
we then went to our maternal grandfather's house in the land of the <s>Yavanas</s>.

children.text: tatrāsmākaṃ kuṭumbaṃ tad dūrād utsukam āgatam
children.translated_text: There our family, eagerly come from far away,
became satisfied like a flock of geese in a rich lake.

children.text: etha yāte kvacit kāle pitā vām ittham ādiśat
children.translated_text: Then, when some time had passed there, our father instructed the two of us in this way:

children.text: āsāte kim udāsīnau bhavantau sthavirāv iva ||
children.translated_text: "Why are you two sitting idle like old men?
You are young, whole in body, healthy, and expert in the science of trade;

children.text: svajanānnena jīvantau kum ucyethe janair yuvām ||
children.translated_text: living on the food of relatives, what will people call you?
Therefore take precious goods born from the ocean, such as pearls and coral,
and cross the sea in a vessel."
Promising, "So be it," we did exactly that; then we saw a woman
clinging to a plank, swimming and weeping.
Without touching that other man's wife with our hands, we said to the sailors,
"Bring her onto the ship by means of the small boat."
When she had climbed aboard, we turned away because she was another man's wife and asked her,

children.text: mātaḥ kasyāsi kā veti sā ca nīcair avocata ||
children.translated_text: "Mother, whose are you, and who are you?" And she spoke softly:
"By your voices, long familiar to me, I recognize you two.
Are you perhaps the two sons of <s>Sāgaradatta</s>?"

children.text: tatas tasyāś cirābhyastaṃ pratyabhijñāya tad vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, recognizing that long-familiar voice of hers,
we said to her, "Can you be the lovely <s>Samudradinnā</s>?"
Then, crying loudly, while we turned aside to left and right,
she clasped our two legs tightly with her arms.

children.text: abhāṣata ca hā tāta hā mamāmbā priyātmajā
children.translated_text: And she said, "Alas, father! Alas, my mother, dear to her child!

children.text: dhikkāraḥ sāgaraṃ pāpaṃ yena tau kvāpi yāpitau ||
children.translated_text: Shame on the wicked ocean, by which those two have been sent somewhere!

children.text: hāryaputra kva yāto 'si hatasneha vihāya mām
children.translated_text: Alas, noble husband, where have you gone, hard-hearted, abandoning me?
This is not the dharma of good men whose beloved wives have fallen into distress."
Then, because the word "noble husband" caused fear and uncertainty,
we, our minds made cold with apprehension, spoke to her thus:

children.text: alaṃ sundari kranditvā jīvataḥ pitarau tava
children.translated_text: "Enough of crying, beautiful one. Your parents are alive;

children.text: āryaputraḥ punar yas te sa nau niścīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: but let us determine who this noble husband of yours is."
Then, hearing that her parents were safe, her mind freed from grief,

children.text: āvāṃ mā bhaiṣṭam ity uktvā svaṃ vṛttaṃ vṛttam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: she told us, "Do not be afraid," and related her own story just as it had happened:

children.text: asty ahaṃ vahanād bhraṣṭā bhrāmyantī jaladhes taṭe
children.translated_text: "After I had fallen from the ship and was wandering on the shore of the ocean,

children.text: yasmai dattāsmi yuṣmābhis tam adrākṣaṃ vipadgatam ||
children.translated_text: I saw, fallen into calamity, the man to whom I had been given by you.
When our own accounts had been made to agree, he took my hand;

children.text: jāyante hi supuṇyānām utsavā vyasaneṣv api ||
children.translated_text: for festivals arise even in calamities for people of great merit.
He comforted me, skillful in the tender care of a young woman,

children.text: tathā yathā priyatamau nāsmaraṃ pitarāv api ||
children.translated_text: so that I did not remember even my most beloved parents.
Then today, having by chance boarded the same ship,

children.text: prasthitau svaḥ svadeśāya vipannaḥ sa ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: we two set out for our own country, and he perished as before.

children.text: sa ca vāṃ bhāginībhartā sākrandāyāḥ puro mama
children.translated_text: And that husband of your sister, before my eyes as I cried out,

children.text: saṃpraty eva taraṃgeṇa gamitaḥ kvāpi vairiṇā ||
children.translated_text: has just now been driven somewhere by an enemy wave.

children.text: nabhasvajjavanair bhaṅgair bhaṅgurair āvṛtaḥ sa ca
children.translated_text: And he was covered by breaking billows, fragile and swift as the wind.
And suddenly I was rescued by you two from enemies that had arisen.
Therefore, with my limbs scorched by the fire of separation from him, in the ocean,

children.text: śīte śītalayiṣyāmi muñcataṃ māṃ yuvām iti ||
children.translated_text: I shall cool them in the cold water. Let the two of you release me.
Then, by her fitting words, confidence was produced in us,
and, filled with supreme joy, we embraced one another.
Just as there has been a reunion for you two, whose ship was wrecked,

children.text: bhaviṣyati tathā bhūyaś citraṃ hi caritaṃ vidheḥ ||
children.translated_text: so it will happen again; strange indeed is the working of fate.
With such words and others, which were causes for diverting her mind,
we steadied her and crossed the great ocean.

children.text: tac ca muktāpravālādi gurumūlyaṃ yad āhṛtam
children.translated_text: And whatever costly pearls, coral, and the like had been brought,
we turned that into a thousandfold profit.

children.text: vadhūḥ samudradinnā te gurusāraṃ ca taddhanam
children.translated_text: Your daughter-in-law <s>Samudradinnā</s>, and that wealth of great value,

children.text: sarvam arpitam āvābhyāṃ tubhyaṃ tat parigṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: all this has been handed over by us to you; please receive it.
Thus <s>Samudradinnā</s> is an example that those freed from the destruction of a ship
and reunited with their kinsmen may yet be joined again with them.
As before, <s>Sānudāsa</s> too, released from the disaster of the ship,

children.text: āgamiṣyati tad devi muñca kātaratām iti ||
children.translated_text: will come; therefore, queen, abandon your timidity.

children.text: ity uktvā sadhanaskandhāṃ nikṣipya bhāginīṃ mayi
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, and having entrusted their sister to me along with a heap of wealth,
those two, treated with due honor, went back the way they had come.
Thus this <s>Samudradinnā</s> has come to your house,
like fortune to a man of praiseworthy birth, joined with destiny and effort.
Therefore, while guarding these wives of yours, protected by <s>dharma</s> and good conduct,
and while honoring elders, I acted as I did in this affair.
By means of this prosperity, this divine conveyance that would shame the Lord of Wealth,

children.text: pitrā tulyo bhavatv eṣa śāpo nāśaṃsitas tava ||
children.translated_text: let him become equal to his father; may that curse of yours, which you did not truly wish, come to nothing.

children.text: tasmād dhanam idaṃ bhuñjan bhuñjānaś ca yathāgamam
children.translated_text: Therefore, enjoying this wealth and using it as prescribed,

children.text: devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca yātvānṛṇyaṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: may you attain freedom from debt toward the gods and the ancestors.
With loving wives and with friends bound merely by friendship,
some time passed for me as I took pleasure in <s>Campā</s>.
One day, while I was playing with dice together with <s>Gandharvadattā</s>,
I suddenly saw before me a man in the attire of a woman.
His two hands were adorned with a skull and peacock feathers,
and at his throat was an ornament for adornment, shining like a misplaced rainbow.
And <s>Gandharvadattā</s> herself gave him a seat,
washed his feet with devotion, and adorned him with her own ornaments.

children.text: tac ca me gurugāmbhīryaṃ kvāpi nītam asūyayā
children.translated_text: Then my grave dignity was carried off somewhere by jealousy,
as that of a lion cub is carried off by the urge to kill a rutting elephant.
I thought: Here this woman alone is at fault, proud of her family;

children.text: eṣa strīpuruṣaḥ śocyo yo na strī na pumān iti ||
children.translated_text: this woman-man is pitiable, being neither woman nor man.
Then, directing himself at me, he, with eyes reddened by anger,
released a peacock-feather missile, saying, You are struck down.

children.text: sa me keśakalāpāgram īṣad āmṛśya yātavān
children.translated_text: It slightly touched the tip of my mass of hair and went on,
like <s>Karṇa</s>'s serpent-missile against the crest of <s>Arjuna</s>'s diadem.

children.text: svayam eva ca tat tasya kapālam apatat karāt
children.translated_text: And of itself that skull fell from his hand,
like the gear of an elephant whose strength is gone and whose array is about to collapse.
Then that rogue, outwitted as if by rustic cunning,

children.text: dhūmrachāyaḥ śanair jalpan dhig dhiṅ mām iti nirgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: smoke-colored, slowly muttering Shame, shame on me, went out.
Then <s>Gandharvadattā</s>, unafraid, approached me as I blazed with resentment,
like a river approaching the great ocean that holds the submarine fire.

children.text: mama tv āsīd aho strīṇām atrāsamatrapaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: But I thought: Ah, the mind of women is without fear or shame,

children.text: yat pureva pragalbheyam upasarpati mām iti ||
children.translated_text: since this bold woman approaches me just as before.

children.text: sā mām avocad bhīteva śītalībhavata kṣaṇam
children.translated_text: She said to me, as if frightened: Grow cool for a moment;

children.text: kiṃcid vijñāpayāmy eṣa yātu vaḥ krodhapāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I must tell you something. Let this fire of your anger depart.
This man is named <s>Vikacika</s>, brother of <s>Gaurimuṇḍa</s>,
the lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> who dwells on <s>Gaurīśikhara</s>, and he is a practitioner.

children.text: bhūtavrataṃ ca nāmedaṃ bahuvidhnaṃ caraty ayam
children.translated_text: He is performing this <s>bhūtavrata</s> (spirit-vow), which has many obstacles.

children.text: samāpte 'sminn avighnena vandhyāḥ syur no manorathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is completed without obstacle, our wishes will not be fruitless.

children.text: yā ca pūjayate taṃ strī gaurīvratavicāriṇam
children.translated_text: And the woman who honors him while he observes the vow of <s>Gaurī</s>,

children.text: tasyai varaṃ mahāgaurī dayate śāpam anyathā ||
children.translated_text: to her <s>Mahāgaurī</s> grants a boon; otherwise, she grants a curse.
I tell you briefly: apart from anger, mighty one,
there is no obstacle-making <s>Vināyaka</s> more destructive of all accomplishments.
By breaking his great vow, which was almost accomplished,

children.text: tuṣṭayā toṣitā gaurī mayā yūyaṃ ca roṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I have satisfied <s>Gaurī</s> with satisfaction, but I have made you angry.

children.text: tad etasyāsya yuṣmabhyaṃ kruddhebhyaḥ krudhyatas tathā
children.translated_text: Therefore, when he became angry at you as you were angry at him,
the great spell that had come from <s>Gaurī</s> slipped from him, like learning from a dull mind.

children.text: tena yuṣmākam evedaṃ kāryaṃ kurvāṇayā guru
children.translated_text: Thus, while I was doing this weighty service for you yourselves,

children.text: yan mayā roṣitā yūyam etan me mṛṣyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: I angered you. Forgive this fault of mine.

children.text: sa ca krodhagrahaś caṇḍaḥ śanakaiḥ śanakair mama
children.translated_text: And that fierce seizure of anger in me,
was slowly, slowly removed from my heart by my beloved, whose words were like spells.
Thus encouraged by her, while I was sitting engaged in mantra practices
with <s>Sānudāsa</s>, on one occasion he spoke as follows.
Here in <s>Campā</s> itself there was a king who loved his chosen wife.
Asked by him about her pregnancy craving, his bashful wife said:
Among playful makaras, crocodiles, crabs, fish, and tortoises,

children.text: krīḍeyaṃ saha yuṣmābhir jale jalanidher iti ||
children.translated_text: I wish to play with you in the water of the ocean.
And the king, with his Magadhan forces and all their divisions, swiftly dammed the river,
and, since his command was never fruitless, had a lake dug as broad as the sea.
There, in a boat shaped like a heavenly palace and densely fitted with wooden mechanisms in the forms of crocodiles and the like,
the two kings, standing aboard, moved about.

children.text: ārabhya ca tataḥ kālāt tatra yātrā pravartitā
children.translated_text: And from that time onward that excursion was instituted there
by the king on days when the cuckoos were thoroughly delighted.
Now those days had arrived, filled with the clear calls of cuckoos,

children.text: sā ca yātreyam āyātā ramyāmṛtabhujām api ||
children.translated_text: and this excursion too had come, charming even to those who feed on nectar.

children.text: iṣyate yadi ca draṣṭuṃ saha gandharvadattayā
children.translated_text: If it is desired to see it together with <s>Gandharvadattā</s>,
then let it be seen with retinues such as ours.
Then, after passing the night, in the morning I boarded a boat
and went out from <s>Campā</s>, worshipped by the lotus-like eyes of the townspeople.
Then I saw a settlement resting in the shade of eye-delighting gardens,
splendid like the city of the King of Kings.
And in its midst I saw a <s>Mātaṅga</s>, steadier than a rutting elephant,
black, yet of shining stature, like a dense rain cloud.
And an old woman, black with the dark blue of the <s>Kālindī</s>, with tawny hair,
like a monsoon night encircled by flashing lightning.
There a girl was seen, swaying playfully on a swing,
like a garland of blue lotuses caressed by a gentle wind.

children.text: cintitaṃ ca mayā kāntā yadi me kālikā bhavet
children.translated_text: And I thought, If my beloved were to be a dark one,
then it would be this slender girl, who has cast away saffron-fairness.

children.text: sthānāc cācalitaivāsau dṛṣṭyā māṃ dūram anvagāt
children.translated_text: And without moving at all from her place, she followed me far with her gaze,
like a bright garland of palāśa blossoms following the sun.

children.text: tāṃ cāliṅgitavān asmi dṛṣṭyā dūrībhavann api
children.translated_text: And though I was going far away, I embraced her with my gaze,
with utter tenderness, as the sun embraces the east with its light.
Thus, as affectionate glances were sent out as messenger and counter-messenger,

children.text: tayā mama mayā tasyā nītāḥ prāṇā vidheyatām ||
children.translated_text: my life-breaths were brought under her control, and hers under mine.
Then, inwardly abusing the gardens that separated us two,
I went to the <s>Mātaṅgī</s> in mind, but to the great lake in body.
And because my mind was fixed elsewhere, I did not see that wondrous festival procession,

children.text: tatrasthenaiva no dṛṣṭaḥ saṃsāra iva yoginā ||
children.translated_text: though I was right there, just as a yogin does not see saṃsāra.

children.text: atha yātrotsave tatra pītveva madhu bhāskaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then at that festival, the sun, as if having drunk honey,
moved very slowly and took on a copper-red disk.

children.text: mama tv āsīd yathā devaḥ prācīṃ kamalinīpriyaḥ
children.translated_text: But to me it seemed as though the god <s>Bhānu</s>, beloved of the eastern lotus-bed,
were going west without first appeasing her.
In the same way, having first described that <s>Mātaṅgī</s> in <s>Gandharvadattā</s>'s presence,

children.text: mātaṅgīm anusarpāmi yathā rājā tathā prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I would follow after the <s>Mātaṅgī</s>; as the king acts, so act the subjects.

children.text: athavā mānuṣair eva yaḥ panthāḥ kāmibhir gataḥ
children.translated_text: Or rather, I shall follow the very path
that has been taken by human lovers; one should not imitate the conduct of gods.
Then I said, Let <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s daughter, together with her attendants,
be conveyed into the city first by you, with the carriage.
For, if she goes behind the crowd, the dust on the road
will cover with alien grime her spotless row of curls adorned with blue lotuses.
Watching the beauty of the festival-goers as they enter the city,

children.text: purastād aham āyāmi saha nāgarakair iti ||
children.translated_text: I shall come presently with the townsmen.
Then, when <s>Gandharvadattā</s> had set out toward the city,

children.text: dārike dve parāvṛtya vanditvā mām avocatām ||
children.translated_text: two maidservants turned back, bowed to me, and spoke.
The lady has commanded us: You two must entertain
the lord, who is without amusement, with gentle conversations.

children.text: tatas te madayitvāhaṃ toṣayitvā ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after charming those two and satisfying them with ornaments,
I came near the settlement in a swiftly moving carriage.
And there, still on the swing, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> beauty
looked plainly at me as I approached, as though I were merely passing by.

children.text: viśrabdham atha tāṃ draṣṭuṃ śanair yānam acodayam
children.translated_text: Then, so that I might look at her at leisure, I had the carriage driven slowly;

children.text: tatas tad api samprāptaṃ javena kulaṭādvayam ||
children.translated_text: but that pair of loose women also arrived there at speed.

children.text: āsīc ca mama yal loke prasiddham abhidhīyate
children.translated_text: And what is famously said in the world happened to me exactly so:
good things are beset with many obstacles.

children.text: duḥkhena ca gṛhaṃ gatvā śūnyaḥ saṃmānya ca priyām
children.translated_text: With difficulty I went home and, empty-hearted, paid honor to my beloved;
then I longed for sleep, hoping for union with the <s>Mātaṅgī</s>.

children.text: ardharātre tu sahasā pratibuddhā muneḥ sutā
children.translated_text: But at midnight the sage's daughter suddenly woke up

children.text: prayukte mayi ye dāsyau te pānīyam ayācata ||
children.translated_text: and asked for water for the two maidservants whom she had sent to me.
When their faces had been washed and wiped, and their faces pleasantly adorned,
she seated the pair of wanton women before her without fuss and questioned them.
The prince saw that rolling-eyed <s>Mātaṅgī</s>,
or rather he was seen by that restless-eyed one: so the two reported.
That worn-out girl was not looked at by the prince
as much as the prince was looked at by her with unblinking eyes.

children.text: tataḥ prāk pratibuddhaṃ mām apṛcchat suprabhāsutā
children.translated_text: Then, before dawn, the daughter of <s>Suprabhā</s> woke me and asked loudly,
Are you awake or sleeping? I replied, I am awake.

children.text: tayoktam ayam ārambho yuṣmākaṃ dṛśyate yathā
children.translated_text: She said, From the way this undertaking of yours appears,

children.text: tathā nalinikāṃ nūnaṃ kartum icchasi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: surely you wish to make me into a <s>Nalinikā</s>.

children.text: kvāsau nalinikā kā vā kasya veti mayodite
children.translated_text: When I said, Where is this <s>Nalinikā</s>, who is she, and whose is she?,
<s>Bharadvāja</s>'s daughter began to relate the story.
At the western edge of the ocean there is a city named <s>Kānanadvīpa</s>,
whose people are well-conducted and wealthy, and which is like the city of <s>Mahendra</s>.
There was a king of men there, beloved of his subjects and not inferior to <s>Mahendra</s> in virtues;
his son was <s>Manohara</s>, charming even by his name.
Although he knew all that was to be known, he was especially fond of the science of perfumes;
for among beings of many tastes, each one desires something particular.
His two friends were <s>Bakula</s> and <s>Aśoka</s>, as if they were the two friends of spring.

children.text: vasantam iva taṃ premṇā na kadācid amuñcatām ||
children.translated_text: Out of affection they never left him, as one never leaves the spring.
Once, after bowing, a doorkeeper
reported to the prince, who was staying in the princes' residence with his friends:
"A man named <s>Sumaṅgala</s>, trained under <s>Buddhagandha</s>,
not rustic and steady in speech, wishes for some reason to see you."
Saying, "Go, admit him," <s>Manohara</s> addressed the doorkeeper,
then took up unguent and quickly burned incense.
<s>Sumaṅgala</s>, having been permitted, entered as far as the doorway,
pressed his head with his hands, contracted his body, and drew back.
"From smelling this incense of mine, which is at odds with perfumes and garlands,
a headache has arisen," he said.
Then, when his own pouch had been opened, in a flat casket

children.text: manoharaṃ muhuḥ paśyan svayaṃ dhūpam ayojayat ||
children.translated_text: he himself prepared incense, repeatedly looking at <s>Manohara</s>.
After making obeisance, he said to <s>Manohara</s>,
"Let this incense, in harmony with a pleasant fragrance, be burned."
Then, together with <s>Bakula</s> and <s>Aśoka</s>, <s>Manohara</s>, delighted with that fragrance,
honored <s>Sumaṅgala</s> as one who knew the science of scents.
And <s>Sumaṅgala</s>, thus treated with honor,
pleased the clever prince in only three or four days.
One day <s>Manohara</s>, with <s>Bakula</s>, <s>Aśoka</s>, and <s>Sumaṅgala</s> leading the way,
went to see a beautiful yakṣa sanctuary.

children.text: tatra tatra tatas tena paśyatā tat tad adbhutam
children.translated_text: There, as he looked here and there at one marvel after another,
he saw the likeness of a yakṣī set in a painting.
Though lifeless, she seemed to tremble; though mute, she seemed softly spoken.

children.text: citre nyastāpi sā tena citte nyastātirāgiṇā ||
children.translated_text: Though set in the picture, she was set in the heart of him, who was deeply enamored.
Leaving aside other things worth seeing, that delight of the mind's eyes,
he attended to her alone with pleasing perfumes, incense, and the like.
His judgment about what could and could not be enjoyed was driven away by powerful Love;

children.text: nitambād ambaraṃ tasyāḥ sa kilākraṣṭum aihata ||
children.translated_text: indeed, he tried to draw the garment from her hips.

children.text: citrabhittim atha tyaktvā sāpi padmeva padminīm
children.translated_text: Then she too, leaving the painted wall like <s>Padmā</s> leaving a lotus pond,

children.text: viṣṇor vakṣa iva śyāmam asevata nabhastalam ||
children.translated_text: resorted to the dark expanse of the sky, as <s>Padmā</s> resorts to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s breast.
And she said to the prince, "By name I am <s>Sukumārikā</s>,
a yakṣī who, through the curse of the lord of yakṣas, has come to have a painted body.
He, whose anger was momentary and who was compassionate toward women,
when I begged for the end of the curse, reflected and encouraged me thus:
"The man who overcomes you while your body is set in a painting

children.text: sa eva kṛtaśāpāntas tava bhartā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will himself end your curse and become your husband."

children.text: iti tvaṃ rājarājena bhartā me pratipāditaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus you have been assigned as my husband by <s>Rājarāja</s>;
for even the curse of great souls is matched by the granting of a boon.

children.text: yadi te 'sti mayi prītis tataḥ krīḍatsurāsuram
children.translated_text: If you have affection for me, then go to the mountain named <s>Śrīkuñja</s>,
the abode of yakṣas, where gods and demons sport."
Then the yakṣī disappeared, and <s>Manohara</s> fell into deep bewilderment;
seeing him in such a condition, <s>Bakula</s> and the others sank into despondency.

children.text: labdhasaṃjñaś ca tair uktaḥ śrutvā yakṣīkathām asau
children.translated_text: When he had regained consciousness, they said to him, after hearing the yakṣī's story,
"Do not become distraught; <s>Sukumārikā</s> is easily attainable.

children.text: yady asau durgamaḥ śailas tatas taṃ sukumārikā
children.translated_text: If that mountain were impossible to reach, then <s>Sukumārikā</s>,

children.text: yuṣmatsaṃbhogam icchantī na tathā kathayed iti ||
children.translated_text: desiring union with you, would not have spoken in that way."

children.text: ekadā pitaraṃ draṣṭuṃ sa gataḥ sasuhṛdgaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: One day he went with his band of friends to see his father,
and saw a ship-merchant who had returned from a successful voyage.
After giving a great jewel to the king, he was honored by the king,

children.text: pṛṣṭas tena bhavān kiṃ kim āścaryaṃ dṛṣṭavān iti ||
children.translated_text: who asked him, "What wonders, one after another, have you seen?"

children.text: tenoktam ambudhes tīre devena vasatā satā
children.translated_text: He replied, "Your Majesty, living as I did on the shore of the ocean,

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ kiṃ nāma nāścaryam āścaryanidhir ambudhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: what wonder indeed have I not seen? The ocean is a treasury of wonders.
But one day, when my ship had been seized by the wind,
I saw a mountain tawny with dense golden radiance, garlanded with lofty peaks.

children.text: kim etad iti pṛṣṭaś ca mayā niryāmako 'vadat
children.translated_text: When I asked, 'What is this?' the navigator said to me,

children.text: vṛddhair eṣa samākhyātaḥ śrīkuñjaḥ śṛṅgavān iti ||
children.translated_text: 'This, possessed of peaks, is called <s>Śrīkuñja</s> by the elders.'
Having reported this and the rest, that merchant went to his own house;
the prince too, after bowing to the king, followed the merchant.

children.text: pradadāv atha sarvasvaṃ tasmai trāsena vāṇijaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the merchant, out of fear, gave him all his wealth;

children.text: rājaputrād gṛhaprāptād āḍhyaḥ ko nāma na traset ||
children.translated_text: for what rich man would not tremble when a prince has come to his house?
But he accepted only a garland of flowers and said,
"The pupils of a teacher do not deserve an insult disguised as hospitality.

children.text: kiṃtu yas tātapādebhyaḥ śrīkuñjaḥ kathitas tvayā
children.translated_text: But that <s>Śrīkuñja</s> which you described to my revered father

children.text: sa kutūhaline mahyaṃ spaṣṭam ākhyāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: must be clearly described to me, for I am curious."

children.text: pratyāśvastas tatas tasya vacobhir madhurair asau
children.translated_text: Reassured then by his sweet words,

children.text: śrīkuñjaṃ sahitaṃ cihnair ity ākhyātuṃ pracakrame ||
children.translated_text: the merchant began to describe <s>Śrīkuñja</s> together with its identifying marks:
"Now one day our ship, like a bull elephant maddened with rut,
was deprived of steadiness by the wind and went out of control.
When the tumultuous wind had grown calm, and the sea and sky were still,
we saw water-creatures of strange form.
In one place there were lions, tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, bears, and sambars,
playing in herds as they rose up and sank down.
Elsewhere there were pairs of women and men with unpierced ears, unclothed,
speaking by mere sounds and following the ways of animals.
In one place we saw lofty elephants flying up, with long wings,
then hiding in the great ocean like mountains for fear their wings would be cut off.

children.text: avāc ca sahasā modaḥ kauveryāḥ pavanāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And suddenly a fragrance from <s>Kauverī</s>, carried by the wind, blew toward us.

children.text: yasyāghrāṇāya sampannaṃ manye ghrāṇam ayaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: I think this whole world has been furnished with a nose in order to smell it.
Wishing to see its source, with eyes full of curiosity,
we saw from afar the mountain <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>, inhabited by <s>Kinnaras</s>.

children.text: kim etad iti pṛṣṭaś ca mayā niryāmako 'bravīt
children.translated_text: And when I asked, "What is this?" the helmsman replied,

children.text: vṛddhair eṣa samākhyātaḥ śrīkuñjaḥ śṛṅgavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "The elders call this peak-bearing mountain <s>Śrīkuñja</s>."

children.text: ityādi kathitaṃ tena yad yat tat tan manoharaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever of this kind he related, every delightful detail,
<s>Manohara</s> clearly marked down in a small chart, with the seas, directions, and regions.
Then, having had a ship brought, manned by trustworthy helmsmen,
he, with <s>Bakula</s> and the others as companions, entered the great ocean.
Driven by a mighty favorable wind,
he soon reached the desired direction by ship.
Made certain by signs corresponding to the places on the chart,
he went to <s>Śrīkuñja</s> all at once with mind, eyes, and body.
Then the ship reached a stairway of blue stone washed by billows of ocean water,
high and broad as the expanse of the sky.

children.text: tatraiva suhṛdas tyaktvā yad utkaṇṭho manoharaḥ
children.translated_text: Leaving his friends right there, <s>Manohara</s>, eager for her,
climbed the mountain peak by that stairway, as one climbs <s>Triviṣṭapa</s> by <s>dharma</s> (merit).
While joyful crowds of female and male <s>Yakṣas</s> looked on,
he went, seeing <s>Sukumārikā</s> with the eye of imagination.
There some women said, "<s>Sukumārikā</s> has attained her goal,
she who has set her love upon this prince among men and immortals.
For among gods, asuras, and men, whom would this <s>Manohara</s> not please,
endowed as he is with innate and acquired qualities of body and the rest?"
Then <s>Manohara</s> saw the <s>Yakṣiṇī</s> playing in a broad palace courtyard,
mind-created and her own, as if she were in his very breast.
She came forward to meet him, modest and not bold like a woman who lives by beauty,
and, taking his hand, sweaty and bristling with horripilation, led him inside.
There he saw her father, who had begun a game of dice,
red-eyed, shining like gold, intoxicated, and big-bellied.

children.text: upaveśya ca tenāṅke ghrātvā mūrdhni manoharaḥ
children.translated_text: After seating <s>Manohara</s> on his lap and smelling his head,
he gave him leave, saying, "See your mother-in-law," and he entered the women's apartments.
There, in the full bloom of youth and shining with garlands of karṇikāra flowers,
were even the grandmothers of his mother-in-law and father-in-law.

children.text: abhivādya ca tās tatra sa tābhir abhinanditaḥ
children.translated_text: Having bowed to them there, and having been welcomed by them,
he was lovingly permitted and entered the maiden's chamber.
The drinking of divine wine, the hearing of divine lute-music,
and unions with divine women stole <s>Manohara</s>'s mind.
As he sat there thus for what seemed a moment, <s>Sukumārikā</s> said to him,
"Five days have passed, prince; you must go back.
This is one region of the world of the gods, and therefore
a mere human cannot remain here beyond the fifth day.
And, abandoning you, the sailors would go away;
they wait five days for the owner of the vessel.
When the prince heard this, his radiance became dim and dimmer,
like that of a son of the gods falling from heaven.
Seeing him in such a state, <s>Sukumārikā</s> said,
"From today onward I shall go to your own home."

children.text: sa tayā dhīrito gatvā potam udvignavāhakam
children.translated_text: Encouraged by her, he went to the ship, whose crew was anxious,
and there he saw his friends with divine jewels, garments, and garlands.

children.text: sthitāḥ stha divasān etān kva kathaṃ veti coditāḥ
children.translated_text: When he asked them, "Have you stayed here through these days? Where, and how?"

children.text: tena te kathayanti sma yathā yūyaṃ tathā vayaṃ ||
children.translated_text: they told him, "As with you, so with us.
At <s>Sukumārikā</s>'s command, delighted <s>Guhyaka</s> women

children.text: asmān upacaranti sma surān iva surāṅganāḥ ||
children.translated_text: attended on us as celestial women attend on gods.
Men who worship <s>Mahādeva</s> go after death,

children.text: sevamānā vayaṃ devaṃ devatām amṛtā gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: but we, serving the god, reached divine women while still alive.
Thus, enamored of the tale of the <s>Yakṣī</s>, they crossed the long and fearful road,
the great ocean, through the power of those women alone.
They entered the city, whose royal road was empty, abandoned by all activities
that serve as means for attaining the three aims, because it was pained by separation from him.

children.text: athaikā brāhmaṇī vṛddhā kimartham api nirgatā
children.translated_text: Then an old Brahmin woman, who had gone out for some purpose,
saw <s>Manohara</s> with his head covered.
Recognizing him, her gait faltering with joy,
she went to the king, who was absorbed in meditation, and delighted him.
The king restrained the ministers and the other citizens, saying,

children.text: mā vocad dārakaṃ kaścit kva gato 'bhūd bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let no one say to the boy, 'Where had you gone?'"
The prince too, embarrassed, bowed to the king,

children.text: so 'pi tasyāṅkam āropya harati sma vilakṣatām ||
children.translated_text: and the king, placing him on his lap, removed his embarrassment.

children.text: svaṃ ca mandiram āgatya sa sumaṅgalam uktavān
children.translated_text: Having come to his own palace, he said to <s>Sumaṅgala</s>,
"Prepare incense that is the essence and fruit of the science of perfumes.
Today your friend, accompanied by her friends, is coming,
and they say that love-play in which fragrance is foremost is faultless.
And what among us is proclaimed as the king of fragrances, <s>Yakṣakardama</s>,
is only like mud for them; therefore it is called <s>Yakṣakardama</s>.

children.text: tasmād ādaram āsthāya śāstram adya prakāśyatām
children.translated_text: Therefore take pains and display the science today;
for elegance is the penetrated essence of the whole <s>Dhanurveda</s>.

children.text: iti protsāhitas tena svārthena ca sumaṅgalaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus encouraged by him, and by his own interest as well, <s>Sumaṅgala</s>
arranged incense, bathing scents, perfumes, and the rest according to instruction.
But <s>Manohara</s>, together with his friends, having made a lover's elaborate arrangement,
occupied a bed of sorrow, empty of the beloved who had been near.

children.text: tataḥ sa tādṛśo gandhas tathāyatnena sādhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that fragrance, of such a kind and prepared with such effort,
was driven on as if by another keen wind, like a rain-cloud.
And <s>Sukumārikā</s>, as though paling with her radiance the moonlight of moonstones and the like,
entered suddenly and alighted on the couch.

children.text: tataḥ sasmitam ālokya bakulādīn uvāca sā
children.translated_text: Then, looking with a smile at <s>Bakula</s> and the others, she said,
"I have come with my attendants. Go and rest."
When they had bowed and gone away, the prince and <s>Sukumārikā</s>,
both longing in just that way, passed the night as they wished.
In the morning <s>Bakula</s> and the others, with bodies lovely from enjoyment,
reported to the prince what had happened during the night.

children.text: rātrau rātrau sametānāṃ viyuktānāṃ divā divā
children.translated_text: Thus, meeting every night and parting every day,

children.text: iti saṃvatsaro yātas tābhis teṣām acetitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a year passed for them with those women without their noticing it.

children.text: ekadā syandamānāśruḥ sākrandā sā tam abravīt
children.translated_text: One day, with tears streaming and with cries, she said to him,
"Such is the union of those who are their own masters with those who are dependent on another.
From today, lord, I must serve <s>Dhaneśvara</s>
for a year, together with my friends, having undertaken <s>brahmacarya</s> (a vow of chastity).
And on the eighth lunar day and other festival days I shall go to my own house

children.text: svagṛhāya gamiṣyāmi tatra gacched bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: to bow to my parents; you should go there too.

children.text: tvatsaṅgasubhagā yā dik tām api prekṣya jīvyate
children.translated_text: One can live even by looking toward the direction made blessed by contact with you;
what need, then, to speak of seeing you, a drink beside which nectar itself is put to shame?"
When she had spoken thus and gone away, <s>Bakula</s> and the others arrived

children.text: khaṃ paśyantam apaśyaṃs tam iyaṃ yātīti vādinam ||
children.translated_text: and saw him staring into the sky, saying, "She has gone."
Then, while the prince, along with <s>Bakula</s> and <s>Aśoka</s>, was grieving,
<s>Sumaṅgala</s>, his voice loudly choked with delight, spoke:

children.text: kim astāne viṣādena potam āruhya māmakam
children.translated_text: "Why this dejection where it is not called for? Board my boat,
and, since I know the route, let us go in a moment to that mountain of the <s>Guhyakas</s>.

children.text: dhyāyantas tatra tāḥ kāntāḥ paśyantaś cāntarāntarā
children.translated_text: There, meditating on those beloved women and seeing them from time to time,
our lives sustained by hope of union, let us pass the year."

children.text: tataḥ sa tena potena prasthitaś ca mahārṇavam
children.translated_text: Then he set out upon the great ocean in that boat,

children.text: sa ca potaḥ samīreṇa dūraṃ hṛtvā vipāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the boat, carried far away by the wind, was wrecked.

children.text: rājaputras tu dayitāṃ siddhāṃ vidyām iva smaran
children.translated_text: The prince, however, remembering his beloved like a perfected spell,

children.text: tāṃ na cetitavān eva vipattiṃ māradāruṇām ||
children.translated_text: did not even notice that disaster, terrible as death.
As he was creeping along the shore-bank, as though just escaped from the ocean,
he was seized by a band of thieves, and his ornaments were taken.
Then that band of thieves was surrounded on every side by a cavalry force,

children.text: veṣṭitaṃ kuṭṭitaṃ baddham udbaddhaṃ pādapeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: beaten, bound, and hanged upon trees.
And one man, very handsome in form, bowed down to him,
set him on the back of a female elephant, and went ahead with his troops.
After going a short distance, accompanied by the qualities praised by bards,
<s>Manohara</s> reached a city whose squares were smeared with saffron.
He came on, hearing the sharp jingling of jeweled festoons and garlands,
like the sweet cries of many garlands of birds.
And he entered the royal palace, splendid in keeping with the city,
where the king, like <s>Śakra</s>, sat in a vast hall.

children.text: avatīrya ca hastinyāḥ sa rājānam avandata
children.translated_text: Dismounting from the elephant, he bowed to the king,

children.text: gāḍham āliṅgya tenāpi ciraṃ prītyā nirūpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the king too embraced him firmly and looked at him for a long time with affection.
Looking again and again at the limbs of his body, the king then said,

children.text: kutaḥ sumaṅgalād anyaś cakṣuṣmān iti bhūpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Who other than <s>Sumaṅgala</s> could be a man with eyes?"

children.text: āsīc ca rājaputrasya sa evāyaṃ sumaṅgalaḥ
children.translated_text: And the prince thought, "This must be that very <s>Sumaṅgala</s>;

children.text: bhaved aham iva bhraṣṭaḥ potabhaṅgabhayād iti ||
children.translated_text: perhaps, like me, he was thrown off through fear when the boat broke apart."

children.text: gaccha viśramya tāteti rājñoktaḥ prāviśat puram
children.translated_text: Told by the king, "Go and rest, my child," he entered the palace,

children.text: apaśyan natamūrdhānaṃ sa tam eva sumaṅgalam ||
children.translated_text: and saw that very <s>Sumaṅgala</s> with bowed head.

children.text: pṛcchati sma ca taṃ bhadra mitre prāṇasame tava
children.translated_text: He asked him, "Good sir, are my two arms, <s>Bakula</s> and <s>Aśoka</s>,

children.text: bhujau me bakulāśokau kaccit kuśalināv iti ||
children.translated_text: your friends and dear as my life, safe?"
He replied, "<s>Bakula</s> and <s>Aśoka</s> have gone home safely.
Please be gracious enough to hear how I came here.
This city is <s>Nāgapura</s>, whose virtues need no repeated telling;

children.text: dṛṣṭam eva hi yuṣmābhir nṛpaś caiṣa puraṃdaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: indeed, you have seen it yourself, and this king is <s>Purandara</s>.

children.text: jayanta iti putro 'sya śūraḥ cāruḥ kaviḥ paṭuḥ
children.translated_text: He has a son named <s>Jayanta</s>, brave, handsome, eloquent, and clever;
it was he who brought you from the forest near the ocean.

children.text: sutā nalinikā nāma nṛpates tasya tādṛśī
children.translated_text: That king has a daughter named <s>Nalinikā</s>, of just such excellence,

children.text: yasyā na pramadāloke na cāsti sadṛśo varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for whom there is no equal in the world of women, nor any comparable bridegroom.

children.text: varaṃ varayatā tasyāḥ pitrā dvīpāntarāṇy api
children.translated_text: When her father sought to choose a husband for her, men skilled in discerning differences
of qualities and beauty were sent even to far-off islands, and were worn out in vain.

children.text: anena ca prapañcena yadā kālo bahurgataḥ
children.translated_text: When much time had passed in this undertaking,

children.text: tadā mām ayam āhūya sadainyasmitam uktavān ||
children.translated_text: he summoned me and, with a pitiable smile, said:
"You are not only the foremost among all our chief officers;

children.text: nātho 'pi bhava nas tāta saṃkaṭād uddharann itaḥ ||
children.translated_text: be also our protector, dear one, rescuing us from this difficulty.

children.text: kulaśīlavayorūpair yaḥ syād asyāḥ samo varaḥ
children.translated_text: Search attentively for the bridegroom who may be equal to her
in family, character, age, and beauty; give up the fever born of wealth's intoxication.
For even a man rich in abundant solid wealth, if destitute of the wealth of virtues,
is to good people far more pitiable than the poor."
Then I painted <s>Nalinikā</s>'s likeness on a panel,
and, seeking a husband for her, wandered over the earth with its eighteen islands.

children.text: yadā tu paṭuyatno 'pi nālabhe varam īpsitam
children.translated_text: But when, despite vigorous effort, I did not obtain the desired bridegroom,
then, my mind set on abandoning life, I was about to enter the great ocean.

children.text: gataś ca kānanadvīpaṃ dṛṣṭavān asmi saṃcaran
children.translated_text: And, having gone to a forest-island, I saw, while wandering...
The noble treasures attending you are constantly attached to the telling of your virtues.
Then that firm courage of mine, with such a resolve upon death,
was driven away by your fame, as a mass of darkness is driven away by moonlight.
And since I knew from common report that you were devoted to the science of perfumes,

children.text: ātmāpi gandhaśāstrajñas tadā vaḥ śrāvito mayā ||
children.translated_text: at that time I too made myself heard by you as a knower of the science of perfumes.
For servants whose nature of knowledge is equal to that of their masters

children.text: rañjayanti manaḥ kṣipraṃ guṇair api nirākṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly delight the mind, even if they are surpassed in qualities.
And as for the incense that was burned, disagreeing with the scents of the garlands,

children.text: suhṛdbhiḥ saha yuṣmābhir ahaṃ jijñāsitas tadā ||
children.translated_text: at that time I was being tested by you together with your friends.
And when I had compounded incense corresponding to the garlands' scents,

children.text: dhūpaṃ tat phalake nyastām apaśyaṃ bhartṛdārikām ||
children.translated_text: I saw the princess placed upon a panel.

children.text: tām ālokya tato yuṣmān manye 'haṃ dhanyajanmanām
children.translated_text: Seeing her, I then regarded you as blessed in birth,

children.text: ātmano rājaputryāś ca vidhātuś ca kṛtārthatām ||
children.translated_text: and thought myself, the princess, and the creator fulfilled.

children.text: so 'haṃ svārthaparo yuṣmān apahartum ito gataḥ
children.translated_text: Intent on my own interest, I went from here to abduct you,
until I myself was carried away by your very virtues, charming to good men's minds.

children.text: tathāpi satkṛto yuṣmān hartum evāham udyataḥ
children.translated_text: Even so, though honored, I was bent on abducting you;
servants who desire what is dear to their masters do indeed commit sin.
Through the merits of <s>Nalinikā</s>, which were the cause of union with you,
<s>Sukumārikā</s> went away under the pretext of service-conduct.

children.text: idaṃ cāntaram āsādya mayā yūyaṃ tvarāvatā
children.translated_text: Seizing this opportunity, I, acting in haste,
had brought a boat close by and caused you to descend into the sea.

children.text: pradeśe yatra cāmbhodhir vipannaṃ vahanaṃ vahet
children.translated_text: In the region where the ocean would carry a wrecked vessel,

children.text: vipannavahanas tatra na ca kaścana vidyate ||
children.translated_text: there is no one there whose vessel has been wrecked.

children.text: tena tau bakulāśokāv avipannau gṛhān gatau
children.translated_text: Therefore those two, <s>Bakula</s> and <s>Aśoka</s>, went home unharmed,

children.text: idaṃ ca puram āyātā yathā yūyaṃ tathā vayam ||
children.translated_text: and just as you came to this city, so did we.
Therefore <s>Nalinikā</s> should be followed by you this very day;

children.text: na hi śrīḥ svayam āyāntī kālātikramam arhati ||
children.translated_text: for good fortune, when it comes of itself, does not deserve delay.
But <s>Manohara</s>, having obtained her, charming in every way,
enjoyed her as he wished, like an elephant a lotus-bed.

children.text: sumaṅgalena sā coktā mā sma śethāḥ pṛthaṅniśi
children.translated_text: And <s>Sumaṅgala</s> said to her, 'Do not sleep apart at night;

children.text: patyus te dayitā yakṣī maivaṃ naiṣīd asāv iti ||
children.translated_text: that yakṣī, your husband's beloved, would not have remained so.'
Once, angered at the prince, the princess,

children.text: unnidraiva sanidreva suptā kila pṛthak kṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: though sleepless, as if asleep, is said to have slept apart for a moment.
Then, when the period of service was complete, at the end of a year,
<s>Sukumārikā</s> found <s>Manohara</s> sleeping apart and carried him away.
As <s>Nalinikā</s>'s husband was carried off by <s>Sukumārikā</s>,

children.text: yuṣmān api hared eṣā tathā mātaṅgakanyakā ||
children.translated_text: so this <s>mātaṅga</s> girl may carry you off as well.

children.text: manyadhve yādṛśīm enāṃ kanyakā neyam īdṛśī
children.translated_text: Whatever sort you think this girl to be, she is not such a one;
for sons of gods do not become enamored of caṇḍāla girls.
Remembering this affair of <s>Nalinikā</s>, you were told by me,

children.text: na me nalinikāvārttā virasāntā bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: lest my story of <s>Nalinikā</s> should end without savor.

children.text: ananyagatasaṃkalpam evaṃ māṃ mā sma kalpayaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Do not think of me thus, as having my intention fixed on no one else';

children.text: iti jihmaṃ puras tasyāḥ kāmukācāram ācaram ||
children.translated_text: with such crooked words before her I practiced the conduct of a lover.

children.text: gandharvadattāvacanāt priyatvaṃ mātaṅgakanyā sutarām agān me
children.translated_text: Because of <s>Gandharvadattā</s>'s words the <s>mātaṅga</s> girl became still dearer to me;

children.text: madaṃ vidhatte madirā prakṛtyā kim aṅga kāntānanasaṅgaramyā ||
children.translated_text: wine naturally produces intoxication; how much more when it is lovely from contact with a beloved's mouth?
Thus I passed the remainder of spring, with its pale-red buds,
and days made pleasant by lovely breezes and sandal.
One day <s>Dattaka</s> came to me laughing and said,
'Noble prince, a strange object of sport has come to you.

children.text: rājamārge mayā dṛṣṭā vṛddhā strī bhāsvaraprabhā
children.translated_text: On the royal road I saw an old woman of brilliant radiance,
being worshipped by townspeople seeking boons, who cried, "Goddess, goddess!"
And she, as if possessed of power, said to me, "Child, accept this:

children.text: tava bhartre mayā dattā kanyājinavatīti mām ||
children.translated_text: the maiden <s>Jinavatī</s> has been given by me to your master."

children.text: uktā sā ca mayā devi bhṛtyatvāt paravān aham
children.translated_text: And I said to her, "Goddess, as a servant I am dependent on another;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā svāminam āyāmi tat kṣaṇaṃ kṣamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: having seen my master, I will come. Forgive this moment."'

children.text: sa mayoktas tayā sākaṃ hasantaḥ sukham āsmahe
children.translated_text: I said to him, 'Together with her we shall sit happily, laughing;
therefore let her come here, and let this word of mine be spoken:
"The giving and receiving of a maiden should be done after consulting many people;

children.text: praṣṭavyāḥ santi cāsmākaṃ tāvat pṛcchāmi tān aham ||
children.translated_text: there are persons who must first be asked by us, and I shall ask them.

children.text: anyac cāgamyatām etad gṛhaṃ yadi na duṣyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, please come to this house, if that is not improper;
honoring a guest such as you is a cause of blessings."'

children.text: tataḥ prasthāpito gatvā pratyāgatya ca dattakaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Dattaka</s>, having been sent off, went and returned,
and addressed me with speech holding deep fear within it.
'Hearing your message, she said with a terrible laugh,
"Ah, the conduct of the very high-born, of those who serve good men!

children.text: kim atrodayano rājā praṣṭavyaḥ suhṛdā tava
children.translated_text: Is King <s>Udayana</s> here to be asked by your friend,
or Queen <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, or the woman of the <s>Magadha</s> line?
Or are <s>Rumaṇvat</s> and the others here, or <s>Hariśikha</s> and the others,

children.text: āha yat santi me kecit tāvat pṛcchāmi tān iti ||
children.translated_text: that he says, 'There are some people of mine; let me first ask them'?

children.text: ājñāpayati yac caiṣa mām ihāgamyatām iti
children.translated_text: And as for this command of his to me, 'Come here,'
are elders thus insulted by those who attend elders?

children.text: athavā kim ahaṃ tasya samīpaṃ kim asau mama
children.translated_text: Or rather, what am I to his presence, and what is he to mine?
He himself will soon experience whether he will go."
Having spoken thus, with rows of flames issuing from her mouth,
she burned one part of <s>Campā</s> and vanished like a great firebrand.'

children.text: mama tv āsīd vidagdheyaṃ vṛddhā vipraśnikā dhruvam
children.translated_text: But I thought, 'Surely this clever old woman is a questioner of riddles,
or else she is skilled in conjuring; she may be a worker of illusions.'
But for <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s daughter there arose a fever of distress,
a cause of sharp terror, burning my heart with anguish.
With lotus-fiber breezes, strings of pearls, water, wet cloths, and sandal paste,
and with embraces from my own limbs, her heat did not subside.
Then clouds, marked by the meeting of rainbows and circles of cranes,
and dark as a waterless sky, covered the heavens.
To remove her burning, amid rain-bearing western winds,
we climbed to the palace roof, white with dense, bright lime-plaster.
There, after blocking the drains and the rest with the upper garments of maidservants and servants,
I held water made cold by the gleaming western wind.
There hunchbacks and dwarfs, sinking only up to the chest of others,
made <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s daughter laugh, her burning slowly quieted.
Seeing us sporting thus in the great lake atop the palace,
the hot-rayed sun entered the western ocean as if to sport in the water.
But <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s daughter, after enjoying the coolness for a long time,
was freed from her accidental burning and became afflicted by cold.
Covering her constantly with my chest, arms, and garments,
I made her rid of the cold by means that removed both heat and chill.
And when the coverings were taken away, water flowed from the palace

children.text: prāsādāt prāsravat toyaṃ sumeror iva nirjharaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: through crocodile-mouthed drains, like waterfalls from <s>Sumeru</s>.
That palace roof, its ornaments broken by the press of scattered water-play,
looked like the ocean after it had been drunk by the sage.
There, spotless from being washed with jarfuls of fresh rainwater,
