I attended on the attendants with gifts suited to each of them.
When the beginning of the night had been passed thus with my beloved, and I had honored my dear one,
I was overcome by deep sleep, which overwhelms both pleasure and pain.
And when a portion of the night had gone by, awakened by a hard touch,
I saw a man with deep eyes and a cave-like gaping mouth.

children.text: anumāya ca taṃ pretaṃ mantragarbham upāgatam
children.translated_text: Inferring that he was a <s>preta</s> come under the power of a spell,

children.text: kvāpi māṃ netum icchantaṃ netum aicchaṃ yamālayam ||
children.translated_text: wishing to take me somewhere, I wanted instead to send him to <s>Yama</s>'s abode.

children.text: bharadvājātmajā trastā mā sma nidrāṃ jahād iti
children.translated_text: But lest <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s daughter, frightened, should wake from sleep,

children.text: na taṃ tatra nihanmi sma bhīṣaṇāraṭiśaṅkitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I did not kill him there, fearing a terrifying cry.
Lifting me onto his frost-numb, wood-hard back,
he carried me down from the palace roof by the stairway.

children.text: tatprabhāvāc ca nidrāndhāḥ suptā jāgarikāḥ kṣitau
children.translated_text: By his power, the chamber-guards and watchmen, blind with sleep,

children.text: kakṣārakṣās tam adrākṣur na niryāntam acetanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: did not see him going out, though they lay asleep on the ground.

children.text: niṣkrāntaś ca parāvṛtya kakṣādvāraṃ yad aikṣata
children.translated_text: And after he had gone out, when he turned and looked at the chamber door,
the pair of door-leaves there slowly closed by itself.

children.text: gṛhād dūram atītaś ca jānubhyāṃ tam atāḍayam
children.translated_text: When he had gone far from the house, I struck him with my knees,

children.text: prahāraḥ sa tu me jāto jānupīḍāprayojanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but that blow of mine served only to give pain to my knees.

children.text: yac ca kiṃcid ahaṃ draṣṭum aicchaṃ paṭukutūhalaḥ
children.translated_text: And whenever, with keen curiosity, I wanted to see anything at all,

children.text: kulaputraḥ sa tatra sma kiṃcit kālaṃ na gacchati ||
children.translated_text: that noble fellow would not go on for a little while.
In streets spread wide like the spaces of the quarters and the sky,

children.text: apaśyaṃ dvīpināṃ kṛttīs tathedam abhavan mama ||
children.translated_text: I saw leopard skins stretched out, and this thought occurred to me:
'How can there be so many leopard skins in a forest,

children.text: āstīrṇāni kimarthaṃ vā kenāpi viśikhāsv iti ||
children.translated_text: and why have they been spread by someone in the streets?'
But as far as the palace could be perceived, through latticed windows,
the roadway was spread with continuous clusters of lamp-flames falling from them.

children.text: apanītavitarkaś ca tair gataḥ stokam antaram
children.translated_text: Freed from that conjecture, I went on a short distance,

children.text: prāsāde kvacid aśrauṣaṃ vacaḥ kasyāpi kāminaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in some palace I heard the words of a certain lover:

children.text: ayi candraka kiṃ śeṣe nanu bhrātar vibudhyatām
children.translated_text: 'Hey, <s>Candraka</s>, why are you sleeping? Brother, wake up. Surely you hear
the owl hooting with its beautiful voice.
Let ten thousand be given to him, and ornaments too;

children.text: ayaṃ naḥ sukhahetūnām agraṇīḥ suhṛdām iti ||
children.translated_text: he is the foremost among our friends, the causes of happiness.'
Immediately afterward the blue-throated peacock, kinsman of deer, frogs, and rain-clouds,
cried with a throat filled with longing.

children.text: tataḥ kāmī jvalatkrodhaś candrakaṃ caṇḍam abravīt
children.translated_text: Then the lover, blazing with anger, said fiercely to <s>Candraka</s>,
'Let the head of this wicked bird be cut off.'

children.text: mayā tarkayatā cedaṃ viruddham iti niścitam
children.translated_text: Reflecting that this was contradictory, I determined this:
there was a proper reason for honoring the one and dishonoring the other.
The wife of this city gentleman, her mind transferred to another man,
though sleeping on the same bed, slept turned away from her husband.
When she heard the owl's cry, terrifying to timid women,
she turned back in fear and tightly embraced her husband.
Therefore, by this man whose wife was estranged, yet who was attached to his wife,
the beloved's embrace was welcomed, even though fear of the owl came first.

children.text: tena pūjām ulūkasya suhṛdaḥ kṛtavān ayam
children.translated_text: For that reason he performed worship for the owl as a friend,

children.text: yenāsya vimukhī kāntā trāsād abhimukhī kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: by whom his beloved, turned away from him, was made to face him through fear.
But when she heard the peacock's cries, which arouse longing for one's lover,

children.text: patyuḥ kaṇṭhaṃ parityajya sthitā bhūyaḥ parāṅmukhī ||
children.translated_text: she abandoned her husband's neck and stood turned away once more.
Therefore, in anger, he had the peacock's head cut off,
because, by crying, it had made his beloved, who faced him, turn away.
Then, after passing that place, I heard the words of two people mad with passion,
an adulterous woman and a rake who had both suffered punishment:
'My nose, slender and prominent, by which fragrances stealing mind and sense of smell

children.text: āghrātā mama sā nāsā tvatkṛte vikṛtā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: were smelled, has been made deformed for your sake.
And my ears, once adorned with earrings and shaped like loops for scissors,

children.text: karṇau mama tathā bhūtau bhavatāṃ bhavato yathā ||
children.translated_text: have become such for your sake, just as yours have become because of me.'

children.text: sāham evaṃvidhā jātā vipralabdhā khalu tvayā
children.translated_text: "Having become such as this, I have indeed been deceived by you;

children.text: kṛtaghna tvam apīdānīm avajānāsi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: and now, ungrateful man, you despise me too," she said.

children.text: athāvocat patis tasyāḥ kiṃ māṃ indasi nandini
children.translated_text: Then her husband said, "Why do you reproach me, fair lady?

children.text: mayāpi nanu yat prāptaṃ tvadarthaṃ tan na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Surely what I too have suffered for your sake is not being considered.
By this hand the gods were satisfied with flowers, incense, and the like, and the ancestors with rice-balls and water,
and twice-born men of every kind were gratified with gifts.
With this hand, armed with a sword, the trunks of elephants were cut off,
their rival elephants crushed by heroes mounted on their backs.
By this hand were enjoyed the breasts of my own remaining wives and of other men's wives,
broad, soft, high, full, and fragrant with choice sandalwood.
That right hand of mine, red like a blossoming lotus,

children.text: kṛttaḥ śastreṇa saṃdhānād bandhanād iva pallavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was cut off by a blade, like a tender shoot severed from its joint.
Now hear, fierce lady, the prowess of my left foot,
by which the earth, bounded by the ocean, was traversed for bathing at sacred fords.
With that same foot, surrounded by the guards of inner apartments,
I lightly crossed ramparts, walls, and moats hundreds of times.
This foot of mine, swift as the wind, with coppery, high-nailed toes,

children.text: pādo me yādṛśo jātas tādṛśaḥ kasya kathyatām ||
children.translated_text: has become such as it is; tell me, whose is like it?

children.text: athavā yaḥ samudrasya tulayā tulayej jalam
children.translated_text: Or rather, the dull-witted man who could measure the ocean's water with a balance

children.text: sa guṇān pāṇipādasya gaṇayen mandadhīr girā ||
children.translated_text: might count in speech the virtues of my hand and foot.

children.text: sarvathā dhig adhīraṃ māṃ yas tvādṛśyāḥ striyaḥ puraḥ
children.translated_text: In every way, shame on me, unsteady man that I am,
for praising the merits of my own hand and foot before a woman like you."

children.text: athānyatra śṛṇomi sma pādaḥ ślokasya śobhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, elsewhere, I heard him say, "A fine quarter-verse

children.text: āgatas taṃ likhāmy āśu datta me vartikām iti ||
children.translated_text: has come to me; I shall write it at once. Give me a stylus."
Thus, curious and seeing endless happenings in <s>Campā</s>,
I came, borne by a corpse, to the northern gate of the city.

children.text: mama tv āsīn na mām eṣa gataprāṇo jighāṃsati
children.translated_text: But I thought, "This lifeless one does not want to kill me;

children.text: uttareṇa hi nīyante na dvāreṇa jighāṃsitum ||
children.translated_text: for corpses are carried out by the northern gate, not in order to be killed.

children.text: cintayann iti niryātaḥ prākāraṃ samayā vrajan
children.translated_text: Going along beside the rampart and thinking so, once outside,
I saw a little boy, flesh wasted away and life departed.
Then, looking at the treatment suitable for a child for a moment, I thought,
"This poor child has died, dried up by Śuṣkarevatī.

children.text: yadi jīvantam adrakṣyaṃ likhitvā maṇḍalaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: If I had seen him alive, then, after drawing a maṇḍala,

children.text: atrāsye maraṇād enam iṣṭvā krūragrahān iti ||
children.translated_text: I would have worshipped the cruel grahas and saved him here from death."
And elsewhere I saw a man adorned with bright garments and ornaments,
his life gone forth; then this occurred to me:
"By rope, weapon, fire, water, old age, fever, poison, or hunger,

children.text: nāyam anyatamenāpi kena nāma mṛto bhavet ||
children.translated_text: by which one of these, indeed, can this man have died?
Ah, surely this passionate man, after making love to another man's beloved,
was sitting in the pleasure of sleep and awoke thirsty.

children.text: sukhasupteti cānena na sā strī pratibodhitā
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'She is happily asleep,' he did not wake that woman,
but himself drank the water standing in a vessel at the window.
Seeing that water-vessel with its lid removed,
a snake, blinded by the fire of its own poison, had entered it earlier.

children.text: tena tadviṣam udgīrṇaṃ tena tad dūṣitaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: By it that poison was disgorged; by that the water was tainted;

children.text: tena pītena mūḍho 'yaṃ sadyaḥ prāṇair viyojitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by drinking it this foolish man was immediately separated from his life.
And by the girls of that woman, another man's beloved,
he was hastily thrown through a hole at the top of the wall onto the bank of the moat.

children.text: amṛto yadi dṛṣṭaḥ syāj jīvitaḥ syād ayaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: If he had been seen before he was dead, I could have made him live
by silently recollecting mantras, maṇḍalas, and mudrās."
Then elsewhere I saw a certain woman, shaming the daughters of the Asuras,
hanged from the branch of an aśoka tree.
Her limbs shone with flower-pollen, vermilion, saffron, and red lac,
and the broad expanse of her hips was wrapped in a dark lower garment.
Not far from her she had thrown down a priceless jeweled ornament,
gleaming with cut stones and moonlight-like luster, laid on Chinese silk.

children.text: kimartham anayā straiṇaṃ kṛtaṃ sāhasam ity aham
children.translated_text: Why had this woman committed such a rash act proper to women?

children.text: parāmṛśya bahūn pakṣān idaṃ niścitavān dhiyā ||
children.translated_text: After considering many possibilities, I settled this in my mind:

children.text: iyaṃ pativratā yoṣin nūnaṃ bhartuś ca vallabhā
children.translated_text: "This woman was surely a devoted wife, and beloved by her husband;

children.text: na vimānitavān etāṃ patiḥ parihasann api ||
children.translated_text: her husband had never slighted her even in jest.
But while he was asleep, drunk, curious, or angry,
that careless man uttered the name of some other woman.
By that unheard-before blow, crushing like a thunderbolt,

children.text: gāḍhaṃ tāḍitayā krūraṃ kṛtaṃ karmedam etayā ||
children.translated_text: she was struck hard, and so she did this cruel deed.
In every way, for sons and wives, the father or husband is like an enemy

children.text: nāsti yas tānitasnehāl lālayaty eva kevalam ||
children.translated_text: when, from excessive affection for them, he only indulges them.
A little disregard is better for children, not excessive indulgence;
for even intelligent people are seen sinking when overindulged.

children.text: vasanābharaṇaṃ yac ca bhūtale svayam ujjhitam
children.translated_text: And the garment and ornament that she herself cast on the ground
were left there by her to avoid the touch of a thief's hand.

children.text: niścaurā cedṛśī campā yan merugurur apy ayam
children.translated_text: Such is thiefless <s>Campā</s>: even this ornament, heavy as <s>Meru</s>,
is seen as an unworthy thing, like rubbish.

children.text: etāni cānyāni ca nāgarāṇāṃ paśyan vicitrāṇi viceṣṭitāni
children.translated_text: Seeing these and other strange actions of the citizens,
I went to the habitation of the revivers, where the darkness was removed by the light of funeral pyres.
Then there I saw flesh-eating female jackals,
frightened by dogs with harsh barks and making piteous, fearsome cries.
There was someone with garment thrown off, arms raised, and a mass of hair disheveled
At one place there was a circle of <s>ḍākinī</s>s dancing all around a corpse;
at another, a man with a drawn sword, holding a skull-bowl,
saying, "Let great flesh be bought, O great beings!"
the four quarters guarded by bands of armed men;
at another place, a sādhaka (adept), sword of siddhi in hand, flying up into the sky.
Seeing many such events and more in <s>Pretaketaka</s>,

children.text: yātrāṃ yā gacchatā dṛṣṭā sā dṛṣṭā sthavirā mayā ||
children.translated_text: the journey that I saw as I went along, O elder, was just such a thing.
At the foot of a banyan, in a funeral fire, with a ladle placed in her left hand,
she was offering human blood with a mantra ending in the syllable "haṃ."

children.text: taṃ ca pretam asau dṛṣṭvā sādhitādeśam āgatam
children.translated_text: And when she saw that ghost, mastered by her rite and come at her command,
her eyes widened with deep delight, she completed the remainder of the rite.
Then, after honoring him with an offering of arghya, she said to him who had performed the act,
"Welcome to the moon-faced one; let the prince be released."

children.text: mama tv āsīd aho kaṣṭā candramasyāpad āgatā
children.translated_text: But I thought, "Alas, some calamity has befallen the moon,
since the face of this crow-faced creature is compared with it."

children.text: sa tu māṃ śanakair muktvā bāhujaṅghaṃ prasārya ca
children.translated_text: But he gently released me, stretched out his arms and legs,
faced south, cried out loudly, and fell upon the ground.
Then the old <s>Mātaṅga</s> woman, having given me a seat, said to me,

children.text: śmaśānam āgato 'smīti khedaṃ mā manaso gamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Do not let distress enter your mind because you have come to a cremation ground.
In the cremation ground blessed <s>Rudra</s>, with <s>Rudrāṇī</s> and <s>Vināyaka</s>,
together with the Mothers and the host of <s>Pramatha</s>s, is present at the three junctions of the day.

children.text: yatra rudraḥ surās tatra sarve haripuraḥsarāḥ
children.translated_text: Where <s>Rudra</s> is, there are all the gods, headed by <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: na hy anyatra tuṣārāṃśur anyatrāsya marīcayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the moon is not in one place while its rays are in another.
And many Brahmins seeking liberation, heaven, wealth, and pleasure

children.text: prāptāḥ pretavane siddhiṃ tasmān nedam amaṅgalam ||
children.translated_text: are heard to have attained siddhi (accomplishment) in the forest of ghosts; therefore this is not inauspicious.

children.text: yadarthaṃ tvaṃ mamānītas tad etat saṃniśāmyatām
children.translated_text: Now listen carefully to the purpose for which you have been brought by me;

children.text: na hi niṣkāraṇaḥ khedas tvādṛśām upapadyate ||
children.translated_text: for distress without cause is not fitting for such men as you.
There was <s>Mahāsiṃha</s>, lord among the chiefs of the <s>Mātaṅga</s>s, crusher of enemies,
my husband, like a great lion embodied in a mighty-armed man.

children.text: ahaṃ dhanamatī nāma mantraśaktiś ca yā mama
children.translated_text: I am named <s>Dhanamatī</s>; as for the mantra-power that is mine,

children.text: sā dineṣu gamiṣyatsu vijñātā bhavatā svayam ||
children.translated_text: you will know it yourself as the days pass.
<s>Mahāsiṃha</s>, after begetting a son named <s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s>, came to his end,
like a mass of flowers whose wealth is an endless burden of fruit.
<s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s> has a daughter named <s>Ajinavatī</s>,
whom the daughters of the thirty gods envy night and day.
When she went with us on the pilgrimage to the great lake,
you were seen by her, with <s>Bhāradvājī</s> as your companion, seated in a boat.
Then some condition arose in her, hard to know in its cause,

children.text: durlabhe bhavati strīṇāṃ dṛṣṭe tvādṛśi yādṛśī ||
children.translated_text: such as arises in women when a rare man like you has been seen.
When, though repeatedly questioned by her friends about the cause of her pain,

children.text: yadā nākathayaj jñātā mantraśaktyā mayā tadā ||
children.translated_text: she would not tell it, then it was known by me through mantra-power.
Without considering the sorrow that might be born from the breaking of a request,
I myself, wishing to preserve my granddaughter's life, chose you.

children.text: dīrghāyuṣā yadā cāhaṃ paribhūtā tathā tvayā
children.translated_text: And when I, old as I am, was thus slighted by you,

children.text: sādhayitvā tathā pretaṃ tvam ihānāyito mayā ||
children.translated_text: I mastered that ghost in that way and had you brought here.
Therefore I give <s>Ajinavatī</s> to you, even by force;
for the gods obtain what they desire even when they do not wear the garland.

children.text: sātha paścānmukhī sthitvā pautrīm ehīty abhāṣata
children.translated_text: Then she stood facing backward and said, "Come, granddaughter."
And there, at that very place, she too appeared, though she had not come before.
"Take by the hand as your husband this heir of the lord of <s>Cedi</s> and <s>Vatsa</s>,

children.text: varaṃ pāṇau gṛhāṇeti tām avocat pitāmahī ||
children.translated_text: whom I have brought under control with my mantras," the grandmother said to her.

children.text: madīyaṃ ca tadīyena svinnaṃ svinnena pāṇinā
children.translated_text: Then with her own sweating right hand she took my right hand,
sweating and trembling, with its own sweat and tremor.
By the glow of her hand, coppery, and by her white-and-dark glances falling on it,
I saw a mingling of colors even on my own hand, though it was saffron-hued.

children.text: atha mām avadad vṛddhā śvaśuro dṛśyatām iti
children.translated_text: Then the old woman said to me, "Look upon your father-in-law."

children.text: tatas tām avadaṃ devi jano 'yaṃ paravān iti ||
children.translated_text: Then I said to her, "Lady, this man is subject to another's power."
Next I saw a man radiant like the orb of the sun,
turning about a circle of moonstone-like eyes, beautiful with streaming light.
<s>Dhanamatī</s> told me, "This is the lord of the <s>Vidyādhara</s>s,
<s>Gaurimuṇḍa</s>, who wishes to propitiate great <s>Gaurī</s>.
And these two, <s>Vyāla</s> and <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, are his brothers and attendants,

children.text: yāv etau pārśvayor asya bhujāv iva mahābalau ||
children.translated_text: the two who stand at his sides like arms, exceedingly strong.
That <s>Amitagati</s>, bound by one of them in a kadamba tree, was freed by you;
this is that <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, the one who carried off <s>Kusumālikā</s>.

children.text: ārabhya ca tataḥ kālād gaurimuṇḍaḥ sahānujaḥ
children.translated_text: And beginning from that time, <s>Gaurimuṇḍa</s>, together with his younger brothers,

children.text: dviṣantam antaraṃ prāpya bhavantaṃ hantum icchati ||
children.translated_text: wants to find an opening and kill you, his enemy.

children.text: tena mānasavegaś ca gaurimuṇḍādayaś ca te
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Mānasavega</s>, <s>Gaurimuṇḍa</s>, and those others

children.text: anantāś ca mahāntaś ca bhaviṣyantaś ca śatravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will be your enemies, boundless, great, and yet to come.
May the gods, gurus, and Brahmins protect you when you are careless, alone,
bereft of divine power, against enemies the opposite of this alliance.
Thus this connection of yours is not for the girl alone;
with <s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s> as an ally, it has a great purpose.

children.text: mama tv abhūd abhūn mitram eko 'mitagatir mama
children.translated_text: For me, <s>Amitagati</s> alone was once my friend;
now <s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s> too is mine, with his mother of very great power."
Even as I was thinking in this way, I saw an aerial chariot,
its moonlight mingled with shadow, descending from the sky.
Though I was going in that vehicle, as if unmoving, with the speed of thought,
I came as though traveling through the sky, like one crossing the ocean in a ship.
Then from afar, from the aerial palace, I saw the circle of the earth,
rounded like a mirror and bounded by <s>Lokāloka</s> and the other limits.
This sky is perceived as such, open and without obstruction,

children.text: sa tu nāsti pradeśo 'sya yo vimānair anāvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet there is no region of it that is not covered by vimānas.
Even the vimāna of a lesser god is crowded with hundreds of apsarases,
has pleasure groves and sport mountains, and extends for a yojana.

children.text: so 'ham evam anantāni kāntimanti mahānti ca
children.translated_text: Thus I went on, seeing countless vimānas,

children.text: gacchāmi sma vimānāni paśyann āyānti yānti ca ||
children.translated_text: brilliant and vast, coming and going.

children.text: kasminn api tato deśe kasyāpi śikhare gireḥ
children.translated_text: Then, in some region, on the peak of some mountain,

children.text: kasyām api diśi sphītam adṛśyata puraḥ puram ||
children.translated_text: in some direction ahead, a flourishing city came into view.

children.text: tasmāc codapatad bhāsvad vimānaṃ vyāpnuvan nabhaḥ
children.translated_text: From it a radiant vimāna rose up, filling the sky,
like the thousand-rayed disk of the sun from the summit of the eastern mountain.
It came together with my own vimāna,
as one elephant's body comes close against another body without a gap.
Dark in his limbs, with tall limbs, coppery eye-corners, and long eyes,

children.text: āgamat puruṣas tasmāt prabhāva iva dehavān ||
children.translated_text: a man came from it, like power itself embodied.
Then, recognizing him as the one I had seen at the great festival,
and as the <s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s> described by <s>Dhanamati</s>, I bowed to him.
And he, his body hairs raised and damp with sweat born of joy,

children.text: aṅgair aṅgaṃ samāliṅgya snehārdraiḥ karkaśair api ||
children.translated_text: embraced me limb to limb with limbs moist from affection, rough though they were.
Then he stepped far back, bent down his raised head,

children.text: jyogbhartar jaya deveti sa mām uktvedam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and, saying, "Long live, my lord; victory, O noble one," he spoke this to me:

children.text: asmābhiḥ sevakaiḥ kāryam idaṃ yuṣmāsu bhartṛṣu
children.translated_text: "This is what we servants should do toward masters such as you;

children.text: āliṅganaṃ tu bhartṝṇāṃ bhṛtyaiḥ paribhavo mahān ||
children.translated_text: but for servants to embrace their masters is a great impropriety.
Even though young, a man like you is not to be slighted as merely a son-in-law;

children.text: mahatī devatā hy eṣā tvādṛgrūpeṇa tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: for a great divinity stands here in a form like yours."

children.text: ityādi bahu tat tan māṃ yāvad eva vadaty asau
children.translated_text: While he was saying many such things to me,
I reached <s>Caṇḍasiṃhapura</s>, filled with the tumult of festival.

children.text: tasya kiṃ varṇyate yatra viśālaṃ viśikhātalam
children.translated_text: What can be said of that city, where the broad surface of the streets
was wondrously variegated with many great jewels fit for <s>Indrāṇī</s>'s girdle?
By this much, the loveliness of its moats, walls, palaces,
and temples, whose splendor had to be imagined, has already been indicated.

children.text: tasya kiṃ varṇyate yasya māṇavāḥ smitimānasāḥ
children.translated_text: What can be said of that city, whose boys, cheerful in mind,

children.text: na stanyam api yāvante jananīr api bālakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: did not even ask their mothers for milk when they were children?

children.text: tasya kiṃ varṇyate yatra paśupālasutair api
children.translated_text: What can be said of that city, where even by cowherd boys
all learning in its entirety was studied as if it were the alphabet?

children.text: tasya kiṃ varṇyate yatra yoginām eva kevalam
children.translated_text: What can be said of that city, where only yogins

children.text: prakṣayo na ca jāyante rathyāḥ prāsādasaṃkaṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: came to dissolution, while the streets, crowded with palaces, never fell into decay?
The fault by which seekers of liberation become terrified of saṃsāra
is heard there only in the treatises on liberation taught by <s>Kapila</s> and others.
And since it was untainted by the real faults that stain corrupt saṃsāra,
what could be more delightful than that city, with its stainless qualities?

children.text: na cedaṃ caṇḍasiṃhasya puram ekaṃ praśasyate
children.translated_text: Nor is this city of <s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s> alone praised;

children.text: anyeṣām api siddhānām īdṛśāny adhikāny api ||
children.translated_text: other siddhas too have cities like this, and even greater ones.
Descending from that sky-palace which had come down to the ground,
I entered the maiden's quarters, a palace bright with white hangings.

children.text: tasmin parijano divyaiḥ prakārair mām upācarat
children.translated_text: There the attendants honored me in divine ways,
and <s>Ajinavatī</s>, summoned by her mother for some reason, went away.

children.text: sā yadā tan niśāśeṣam uttaraṃ ca divāniśam
children.translated_text: When she had not returned through the rest of that night

children.text: nāgataiva tad āsīn me tvarāturamater matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor through the following day and night, my mind became sick with impatience.
By sight, smiles, conversation, touch, embraces, and the rest,

children.text: samastair asamastaiś ca ramayanti priyāḥ priyān ||
children.translated_text: beloved women delight their beloveds, both all together and each separately.

children.text: kiraṇair indulekheva gataiva saha tair asau
children.translated_text: But she, like a crescent moon with its rays, had gone away together with all those delights,
and here I remained, my mind scorched by sorrow.

children.text: tat kim etat kathaṃ nv etad ityādi bahu cintayan
children.translated_text: Thinking many thoughts, such as, "What is this? How can this be?"
I looked upon the city, with its inner palace thrown into confusion by an obstacle to the marriage.

children.text: āsīc ca mama campāyāḥ preto mām anayan niśi
children.translated_text: And I thought, "A preta carried me from <s>Campā</s> by night,
on the fourteenth day of the dark half of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, when the moon was in <s>Ārdrā</s>.
Surely this marriage of ours will be arranged by the king at the beginning of the bright half of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>,
on the fifth day, under the <s>Uttara Phalgunī</s> stars.
This king is of great lineage and is learned in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>;

children.text: tad brāhmeṇa vivāhena sūnoḥ saṃskāram icchati ||
children.translated_text: therefore he wants the <s>saṃskāra</s> for his child by a <s>brāhma</s> marriage.

children.text: upāsya caturaḥ kaṣṭān pāvakān iva vāsarān
children.translated_text: After enduring four difficult days like fires,

children.text: tāṃ prāpaṃ kanyakām ante tapaḥsiddhim ivepsitām ||
children.translated_text: at last I obtained that maiden, like the desired perfection won by austerity.
Together with her, in the rainy month, dark with masses of dense rainclouds,

children.text: tayā saha prāvṛṣamāsi ramyām aśuklapakṣāntaniśām ivaikām ||
children.translated_text: with the hosts of stars and the moon's disk unseen, I enjoyed a lovely season as if it were one night at the end of the dark fortnight.
Once, when she was with her attendants and there was a sound of suppressed weeping,

children.text: anuyuktā mayā kaccin nṛpaḥ kuśalavān iti ||
children.translated_text: I questioned her: "Is the king well?"
But although she forbade her, a girl named <s>Megharājikā</s>
began to report to me, "Listen, young lord.
Formerly there was a base sky-roamer named <s>Vikacika</s>, lawless,

children.text: svais tyaktaḥ sāparādhatvāt kiṃcit kālam ihāsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who, abandoned by his own people because of his offense, stayed here for some time.
Thinking, 'The girl is visible to everyone,' he saw the young princess

children.text: āsīnāṃ pitur utsaṅge dṛṣṭvā rājānam uktavān ||
children.translated_text: sitting in her father's lap, and said to the king:

children.text: duhitā tava yady eṣā tato mahyaṃ pradīyatām
children.translated_text: 'If this is your daughter, then let her be given to me;
and the number of my virtues is already known to you.'"

children.text: tenoktaṃ kena na jñātāḥ prasiddhā hi guṇās tava
children.translated_text: By him it was said, "By whom are your famous virtues not known?

children.text: kiṃ tu komalajanmeyaṃ prauḍhā tāvad bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: But this girl is of tender birth; let her first come to maturity."
When he too had taken leave of the king and was about to go to his own country,
he caused a proclamation to be heard in the city, reaching women, children, and cowherds:
"The king has given me his daughter <s>Ajinavatī</s>, together with honors.

children.text: diṣṭyā vṛddhir bhavaty adya mameva bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: By good fortune, today there is prosperity for me just as for you."
Hearing that the princess had a prince as her husband,
that shameless man, forgetting the favor done to him, spoke angrily to the king:
"What is this conduct of yours, you who pride yourself on good conduct,

children.text: yad dattvā tanayāṃ mahyam anyasmai dattavān iti ||
children.translated_text: that after giving your daughter to me you have given her to another?
Or rather, enough of reproaching you, since you have no shame.

children.text: sutā vā vyavahāro vā yuddhaṃ vā dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Let the daughter be given, or legal process, or battle."

children.text: athāha vihasan rājā na yuddhaṃ na mamātmajām
children.translated_text: Then the king said with a laugh, "Long-lived sir, you deserve to obtain neither battle

children.text: labdhum arhati dīrghāyur vyavahāras tu dīyate ||
children.translated_text: nor my daughter; but legal process shall be granted."
Having said this, the king, together with his ministers and his mother,
went to <s>Saptaparṇapura</s>, with <s>Vāyumukta</s> as chief overseer.
"If you two also wish, you who beautify the quarters and the sky,
go there together like <s>Rohiṇī</s> and the moon."

children.text: mayoktaṃ bhīru mā bhaiṣīḥ kiṃnarīkaṇṭhi mā rudaḥ
children.translated_text: I said, "Timid one, do not be afraid; kinnarī-throated one, do not weep.

children.text: megharājyā yathākhyātaṃ jitaḥ sa capalas tathā ||
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Megharājī</s> reported, that fickle man has been defeated."
By my words of consolation, like the touch of the young sun,
her lotus face, faded by the frost of terror, opened out.

children.text: mām ādāya tataḥ pāṇau sā gatvāmbaravartmanā
children.translated_text: Then, taking me by the hand, she went by the path of the sky
and stopped in the garden of <s>Saptaparṇapura</s>, in <s>Saptaparṇapura</s>.

children.text: abravīc ca nirutkaṇṭhaiḥ kṣaṇam ekam ihāsyatām
children.translated_text: And she said, "Stay here without anxiety for a single moment,

children.text: yāvad emi sakhīṃ dṛṣṭvā vanditvā ca gurūn iti ||
children.translated_text: until I return after seeing my friend and paying respect to my elders."

children.text: tasyām utpatya yātāyām udyāne saṃcarann aham
children.translated_text: When she had flown up and gone, I wandered in the garden
and saw saptaparṇa flowers the color of large pearls.
With those, and with strong fibers of plantain, I strung
a necklace trembling with bandhūka blossoms and strewn inside with lotuses.
With flowers shining like many jeweled stones, such as rubies and sapphires,
I fashioned conch-bracelets, anklets, and girdles.

children.text: avatīrya tato vyomnaḥ sā priyā priyavādinī
children.translated_text: Then that beloved, sweet-speaking dear one, descended from the sky,

children.text: nirjitaḥ sa durātmeti hṛṣṭā mām apy aharṣayat ||
children.translated_text: and, joyful that "that wicked man has been defeated," made me joyful too.

children.text: katham ity anuyuktā ca mayā sādaram abravīt
children.translated_text: When I respectfully asked, "How?" she said:
"Speakers, even when wishing to speak, disregard questioning.
I went to <s>Vāyumūla</s>; greeted by the women of the inner apartments,
I saw my friend <s>Vāyumuktā</s>, who was staying in the maidens' inner palace.
While I was sitting there for a moment, I heard a kettledrum
resounding with a terrifying roar that conquered the thunder of clouds.

children.text: kim etad iti pṛṣṭā sā saṃbhramotkarṇayā mayā
children.translated_text: Alarmed and with ears raised, I asked her, 'What is this?'

children.text: sakhī svāṃ dārikām āha yāhi vijñāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: My friend said to her own maid, 'Go; let it be found out.'
She returned after a moment, her breasts trembling from panting,

children.text: vardhase devi diṣṭyeti mām uktvoktavatī punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, saying to me, 'By good fortune you prosper, lady,' she spoke again:

children.text: bherīṃ tāḍitavān eṣa gatvā vikacikaḥ sabhām
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Vikacika</s> went to the assembly and struck the drum,
and the assembly members, together with <s>Vāyumukta</s> and the assessors, assembled.

children.text: te tam āhur bhavān kasmād bherīṃ tāḍitavān iti
children.translated_text: They said to him, "Why have you struck the drum?"

children.text: āryaveṣaḥ sa tān āha puraḥ sthitvā nirāsanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He, dressed as an Arya, stood before them without a seat and said:
"<s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s>, after giving his daughter to me in the presence of the city,

children.text: anyasmin dattavān yatra nāgaraṃ pṛcchyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: has given her to another; let the city be questioned on this."

children.text: ucyatām iti coktena tātena kila saṃsadā
children.translated_text: And when my father and the assembly said, "Let it be stated,"

children.text: megharājyā yad ākhyātaṃ tad evākhyātam āha ca ||
children.translated_text: he related exactly what <s>Megharājī</s> had reported.
He also said, "Those witnesses, residents of my city, whom this man names,

children.text: pṛcchyantāṃ te 'pi teṣāṃ ced aviruddhā pramāṇatā ||
children.translated_text: let them too be questioned, if their status as evidence is not contradicted."
Then <s>Vāyumukta</s>, after consulting with the assembly members, said:
"What need is there to examine this king, who is like <s>Manu</s>?
For the validity of direct perception, king of the means of proof
and cutter-off of inquiry and doubt, is not established by inference.
Therefore, in the legal case, the claimant <s>Vikacika</s> has been defeated

children.text: arthī vikacikaḥ kanyām anyāṃ mṛgayatām iti ||
children.translated_text: by the defendant king; let him seek another maiden."

children.text: tato vikacikaḥ kruddhaḥ jhaṭity utthāya saṃsadaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vikacika</s>, enraged, suddenly rose from the assembly

children.text: utpatya nabhasā gacchann uccair āha sabhāsadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, flying up through the sky, said loudly to the assembly members:

children.text: dhik khalān khalu caṇḍālān pakṣapātahatāñ jaḍān
children.translated_text: "Fie on these wicked caṇḍālas, dull men ruined by partiality!

children.text: aham eva hi kartavye kartavye buddhivān iti ||
children.translated_text: I alone am clever whenever a thing must be done."

children.text: āsīc ca mama yat satyam āśaṅkākaluṣaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: And truly my mind became stained with suspicion:

children.text: kasmin punar asau kārye kartavye buddhimān iti ||
children.translated_text: in what task to be done would he prove clever?"
Then, after adorning her with those ornaments of autumn flowers,
I said this to her, whose body stole the beauty of autumn:
"These ornaments of graceful play, placed by me upon your limbs
while I was delighted by the dear report, shine beautifully, fair-limbed one."

children.text: sā tatas tān alaṃkārān dviṣatī kaṇṭakān iva
children.translated_text: Then she, hating those ornaments like thorns,
shook her body and said to me, with a smile slowed by jealousy:

children.text: aparāsv api bhāryāsu yuṣmābhir idam āhitam
children.translated_text: "This has been put by you on other wives too.

children.text: na hi dṛṣṭaṃ vinābhyāsāt kriyākauśalam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: For such skill in an action is not seen without practice.

children.text: tasmān nirmālyatulyena na kāryam amunā mama
children.translated_text: Therefore I have no use for this thing, equal to a cast-off garland.

children.text: kā hi durlabham ātmānaṃ kitavaiḥ paribhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: What woman would let her hard-to-win self be slighted by cheats?

children.text: mama tv āsīd apūrveyam asyā viṣamaśīlatā
children.translated_text: But to me this harshness of hers seemed unprecedented
and very hard to turn back by stratagems, prostrations, oaths, and the like.
And a woman, because her substance is light, is unsteady like a row of waves;
like a boat against the current, she is quickly turned about by the skilled.
Living for a long time in the house of one's wife's relatives is a cause of misfortune.

children.text: yadi vipratyayaḥ kaścid bhartāraṃ kiṃ na paśyasi ||
children.translated_text: If there is any mistrust, why do you not look at the husband?

children.text: bhartrā te cāṭukāreṇa bhāryāṃ toṣayatā kila
children.translated_text: By your husband, a flatterer, who was trying to please his wife,

children.text: tat kṛtaṃ durvidagdhena yena bhāryaiva roṣitā ||
children.translated_text: that was done by the foolishly clever man by which the wife herself was angered.

children.text: subhagaṃ karaṇaṃ yad yat samācarati durbhagaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever auspicious measure a luckless man undertakes,
by that very measure his misfortune grows all the more.
In every way I shall warn even the sons I may have in the future:

children.text: mā ciraṃ putrakāḥ sthāta bhāryājñātigṛheṣv iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Dear sons, do not stay long in the houses of your wives' relatives.'
But when she saw my face, embarrassed, frightened, and disconcerted,

children.text: asnigdhasmitayā hā hā kim etad iti bhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: she said, with an unloving smile, 'Ah, ah, what is this?'

children.text: ataḥ param ayukto 'yaṃ prapañca iti tām aham
children.translated_text: Then, thinking, 'After this, this elaboration is improper,'
I embraced the woman, whose limbs were trembling with distress, and drew her onto my lap.
But she, having recovered reassurance and standing at the landing-place of the pool,
cried out loudly in distress, 'Noble husband, be gracious!'

children.text: paśyāmi sma tataḥ khasthaṃ taṃ vidyādharapāṃsanam
children.translated_text: Then I saw that vile <s>Vidyādhara</s> in the sky,
surrounded by a wide disk whose edges flashed with quivering rays.
With a roar made terrible by anger he said, 'Earth-walker,

children.text: te paśyata iyaṃ kāntā hriyate dhriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: look: this beloved of yours is being carried off. Hold her if you can.'
Because my composure had been overthrown by anger, and I could not distinguish what should and should not be said,
I, imagining a sisterly relation, rebuked him in this way:
'Why do you boast, low man, saying, "I range through the sky"?

children.text: kāko 'pi hi nabhaścārī na ca muñcati nīcatām ||
children.translated_text: A crow too moves through the air, yet it does not give up its low nature.

children.text: yaḥ siṃhaśirasi nyasya kākaś caraṇam utpatet
children.translated_text: If a crow sets its foot on a lion's head and flies away,

children.text: na tena paribhūtaḥ syāt kesarī dharaṇīcaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the maned lion, though he walks on the earth, is not thereby humiliated.
Even though he was being provoked in this way, he did not descend to the ground.
Looking all around in alarm, he spoke as if with contempt:
'If one like me, with the valor of <s>Vainateya</s>, were angry

children.text: tvādṛśe mādṛśaḥ krudhyan kena pāpān na śocyatām ||
children.translated_text: at one like you, resembling a land-tortoise, what sinner would not deserve pity?'

children.text: ity uktvā karuṇākrandāṃ tām asau khecarādhamaḥ
children.translated_text: Having said this, that vilest sky-goer took her, crying piteously,

children.text: bhuvaḥ śyena iva śyāmām ādāyodapatad divam ||
children.translated_text: dark like the earth, and flew up into the sky like a hawk from the ground.
Then I saw a divine woman descending from heaven,
her garment drawn tight by the blaze of great flames, ominous like a portentous meteor.
And I saw the king, surrounded by a troop of fierce <s>Vidyādhara</s>s,
angry like <s>Mahākāla</s> attended by hosts of <s>Gaṇa</s>s and immortals.
With face upturned, following <s>Caṇḍasiṃha</s>,
I somehow went off elsewhere, my memory stolen by bewilderment over the directions.
As I wandered, wearied, among rough trees in a dense grove,

children.text: cirād ākarṇito dhīrād uccakair uccaran dhvaniḥ ||
children.translated_text: after a long time I heard a loud sound uttered in a steady voice:

children.text: he he kālākṣi kālākṣi gaṅge gaṅge mahīti ca
children.translated_text: 'Hey, hey, <s>Kālākṣī</s>, <s>Kālākṣī</s>! <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Gaṅgā</s>! <s>Mahī</s>!'

children.text: vatsalānāṃ vivatsānāṃ rambhaś ca subhago gavām ||
children.translated_text: and the pleasing lowing of affectionate cows separated from their calves.

children.text: gatvā ca tvarayāpaśyaṃ yāṣṭīkaṃ pālam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: Going quickly, I saw before me a staff-bearing cowherd,
with bristling hair thick like horse-gram, broad with massive thighs and shanks.
His shoulders and neck were handsome like the arms of rival wrestlers,
and his ears were rough with calluses from swift slapping blows.

children.text: tatas tam abravaṃ sāmnā satataṃ mahitaṃ gavām
children.translated_text: Then I spoke gently to him, who was always honored among the cows:

children.text: bhraṣṭaḥ panthā mamāṭavyāṃ tam ākhyātu bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: 'I have lost my road in the forest; please tell it to me.'
He said, 'Spend the night in the cattle settlement, free from fatigue;

children.text: prage draṣṭā svapanthānaṃ tadeta svagṛhān iti ||
children.translated_text: in the morning you will see your own road. So come to my house.'
Going with him, I saw a cowherd hamlet near the cattle enclosure,
like an ocean struck by <s>Mandara</s>, shaken by the deep sound of churning.
There the hut grounds, with their courtyards and no paved floors,
had their surfaces made pleasant by being swept with fresh green cow-dung.
There the hut-courtyards, enclosed by clumps of bandhūka and mango saplings,
put to shame the hands and lower lips of the <s>Ābhīra</s> women.
There even lotus-beds were embarrassed by nets of bottle-gourd vines
that blocked the cottage roofs and threatened them with finger-like buds.
In it the lanes, crowded with dust, sweepings, and mire hard to see and hard to look at,
had indescribable floors, with unrestrained calves leaping about.
There, with limbs pure as karṇikāra blossoms and broad expanses of hips,

children.text: sa tādṛṅmalinaḥ strīṇāṃ yatra veṣo vibhūṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even such dirty clothing was an ornament for the women.
There, because the woodland cattle station was old, the cowherds were straightforward like cows,

children.text: gopyas tu caturācārā naṭīr apy atiśerate ||
children.translated_text: but the cowherd women, clever in their ways, surpassed even actresses.
While my mind was carried away by a cowherd settlement of this and other kinds,

children.text: māṃ gopaḥ svagṛhaṃ nītvā gṛhiṇīm āhvayan mudā ||
children.translated_text: the cowherd led me to his house and joyfully called his wife:
'Where are you, daughter of <s>Sudeva</s>, young cowherd girl?

children.text: devas te gṛham āyātaḥ sa bhaktyārādhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Your deity has come to the house; let him be worshipped with devotion.'
Then, like a digit of the moon from a fragment of cloud,
a fair woman came out of the house, scattering a delicate moonlight from her body.
Let images made of wood, ivory, and stone be left aside;

children.text: na tāṃ vedhāḥ kṣamaḥ sraṣṭuṃ madhūcchiṣṭamayīm api ||
children.translated_text: the Creator could not have made her even out of beeswax.

children.text: bhāvabhir vartamānaiś ca kavibhiḥ kim udāhṛtaiḥ
children.translated_text: What need is there to mention present emotions and poets?

children.text: na tāṃ varṇayituṃ śaktau vyāsavālmīkināv api ||
children.translated_text: Even <s>Vyāsa</s> and <s>Vālmīki</s> would not be able to describe her.
With a clear mind, like a sister, she massaged me, seated on a cow-dung stool,
tirelessly from head to foot for a long time.

children.text: yaṃ yam evopasāraṃ sā tuccham apy ācaren mayi
children.translated_text: Whatever service she performed for me, even a trifling one,
I submitted to all of it, fearing a failure of courtesy.
With water standing in bronze vessels she washed my feet,
and with joy she put fresh butter on my head and on my other limbs.
After anointing me there with a paste of kaṇa, while my head was still wet,
I was rubbed with lodhra, karbūra, and mustā, and bathed by her.
And after eating pure food, with little grain but much milk,
I, a drinker of liquor, considered myself as though freed from sin.

children.text: kalpayitvā tu me gopaḥ śayyāṃ valkalapallavaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the cowherd prepared a bed for me from bark and young leaves,

children.text: etat te gṛham ity uktvā aṃsabhāro vrajam avrajat ||
children.translated_text: and, saying, 'This is your house,' went to the cattle-station with a load on his shoulder.

children.text: mama tv āsīd ayaṃ manye vītarāgādibandhanaḥ
children.translated_text: But I thought: 'This man, I suppose, is free from the bonds of passion and the rest.

children.text: sakleśaḥ ko nu viśvasyād dāreṣu ca pareṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: What man still afflicted by defilement would trust in wives, whether his own or another's?
Even among animals whose mates are held in common, and whose minds are shaken by jealousy,
battles are seen, with death out in the open.
But this man has entrusted to me his beloved wife,

children.text: mayi nikṣipya yātīti vyakta eṣa sa puṃgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who could captivate a sage's mind, and gone away; clearly he is a bull among men.
Or else, among rustic householders unskilled in outward social usage,
whose systems are ruled by women, what is the point of testing proper conduct?
Washermen's wives, standard-bearers' wives, cowherd women, gardeners' wives, and actresses,

children.text: dṛśyante yāḥ sadācārāḥ sā tāsāṃ bālaśīlatā ||
children.translated_text: when they are seen to be well behaved, have only the virtue of children.

children.text: eṣā tu gopayoṣāpi rūpiṇy api taruṇy api
children.translated_text: Yet this cowherd woman, though beautiful and young too,
has such deep firmness; the minds of others are hard to fathom.'

children.text: cintām etāṃ kurvataḥ kāryavandhyām āsīt sā me sopakāraiva rātrīḥ
children.translated_text: As I pondered this fruitless anxiety, that night was in fact helpful to me,

children.text: sadyaḥ kāntākaṇṭhaviśleṣaduḥkham ārāt sahyaṃ cetasā yan na soḍham ||
children.translated_text: because the immediate pain of separation from my beloved's neck, not borne by my mind when near, became bearable at a distance.

children.text: tataḥ prātaḥ sa māṃ gopaḥ kṛpālur iva tattvavit
children.translated_text: Then in the morning that cowherd, compassionate and as if knowing the truth,
soon drew me out from the terrible wilderness of worldly wandering.
'This is your village of <s>Saṃbhava</s>, with its tall thickets of bamboo in front;
its boundary-fields, crowded with ploughs, can be seen.
Rest here, and then go on to the other country you have in mind.'

children.text: iti mām idam uktvāsau nivṛttaḥ kṛtabandhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this to me, he turned back, his tie of obligation fulfilled.
Then, enjoying the shade of dense sugarcane, which cast away the autumn heat,
I, scorched by the sun's rays, set out on my way.
At times I praised lakes whose pleasure-groves of blooming lotuses were open,
like stretches of ground at the end of summer, with caves wide open and sparse.
At times, curious, I looked at ponds containing rice within them,
as though they were thickets dense with water-grass.
At times my eyes were pleased by lakes as if filled with water from the overflowing <s>Kālindī</s>,
with their banks made white by swans, the twice-born birds.
And my gaze was drawn by ploughed fields, with soft, pale dust,
as if by the sandy banks of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, agreeable in their appearance and treatment.
Thus, made to forget my beloved by the beauty of the autumn season and its like,

children.text: gacchan puruṣam adrākṣaṃ grāmād āyāntam antike ||
children.translated_text: as I went along I saw a man coming from a village nearby.

children.text: sa tu māṃ ciram īkṣitvā bravīti sma savismayaḥ
children.translated_text: He looked at me for a long time, and then said with amazement,
'Strange! You are very much like the younger <s>Ārya</s>.'

children.text: mama tv āsīd asaṃdigdhaṃ dṛṣṭavān eṣa gomukham
children.translated_text: But I thought without doubt, 'This man has seen <s>Gomukha</s>,

children.text: na hi tasmād ṛte kaścid asti matsadṛśaḥ kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: for apart from him there is no one on earth who resembles me.'

children.text: pṛcchāmi sma ca taṃ bhadra sa kaniṣṭhaḥ kva tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: And I asked him, 'Good sir, where does that younger man stay,

children.text: kīdṛśā vā vinodena gamayed divasān iti ||
children.translated_text: and in what manner does he pass his days for amusement?'

children.text: tatas tenoktam atraiva grāme gṛhapatir dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he said, 'Here in this very village there is a twice-born householder,
generous with common resources, a pleasant speaker, named <s>Prasannaka</s>.

children.text: ekadā brāhmaṇaḥ pṛṣṭas tena brahmasabhāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: One day a brahmin who had gone to the brahmin assembly was asked by him,

children.text: āgataḥ katamād deśāt kimarthaṃ vā bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "From what country has your honor come, and for what purpose?"
He replied, "We two brahmins have come from the region of <s>Avanti</s>,

children.text: bhrātarau sa ca me jyeṣṭho yātrāyām anyato gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: brothers; and my elder brother has gone elsewhere on the journey.
Searching for him, I have arrived at this village;
here a gathering of all the students has come together."

children.text: ity ukte tena tenoktam idaṃ vaḥ sadhanaṃ gṛham
children.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Prasannaka</s> said to him, "This house, with its property, is yours;

children.text: yena yenātra vaḥ kāryaṃ tat tad ādīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: whatever business you have here, take whatever is needed for it."

children.text: gṛhe gṛhapates tasya kṣamāvān api śīlataḥ
children.translated_text: In that householder's house, although by nature patient,
he lives like <s>Durvāsas</s>, worshiped by terrified servants.

children.text: hālikatvān na jānāmi jñātā kiṃ kim asāv iti
children.translated_text: Since I am a ploughman, I do not know what all he knows,

children.text: yanmātraṃ tu vijānāmi tanmātraṃ kathayāmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but I shall tell you only as much as I do know.
First, what need is there to mention students, whose full learning has not yet been attained?

children.text: ācāryā api vidyāsu tasyaiva chāttratāṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even teachers in the sciences have become his pupils.
And they say, "What is the use of us, who merely dejectedly sink ourselves?

children.text: viśvakarmātha vā brahmā kasmān nāyam upāsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why has this man not been worshiped as <s>Viśvakarman</s>, or as <s>Brahmā</s>?"
With such amusements and talk he waits for the elder <s>Ārya</s>,

children.text: utkaṇṭhaḥ sarvataḥ paśyañ jīmūtam iva cātakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: longing and looking everywhere, like a cātaka bird for a rain cloud.

children.text: āryajyeṣṭho bhavān eva yadi tal laghu kathyatām
children.translated_text: If you yourself are the elder <s>Ārya</s>, then say so quickly,
so that untimely moonlight may suddenly bloom in the village.'

children.text: āma saumya sa evāham iti saṃvādito mayā
children.translated_text: When I answered him, 'Yes, my friend, I am that very man,'

children.text: ūrdhvacūḍaḥ sa vegena prati grāmam adhāvata ||
children.translated_text: he ran swiftly toward the village, with his hair-tuft standing upright.
And, suddenly raised up by him in the village, terrifying the timid,
there arose a roar of delight, crowded with the clapping of hands.
Then <s>Gomukha</s>, his face blooming, came out from the village,

children.text: dūrād eva yathādīrgham apatan mama pādayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from far away fell at full length at my feet.

children.text: bālair āliṅgitaiḥ putrair dāraiś ca na tathā priyaiḥ
children.translated_text: Not by sons embraced as children, nor by beloved wives,

children.text: janyate janitā prītis tena me suhṛdā yathā ||
children.translated_text: is such affection produced in a father as was produced in me by that friend.
And from afar, with a smiling face, that man named <s>Prasannaka</s>...
Having embraced him, and accompanied by him, I reached the village of <s>Saṃbhava</s>.
And the village people, who had gone up onto platforms, roofs, terraces, mansions, and the like,
pointed me out with their fingers as I was going along.
With my band of attendants delighted, in a pleasant lodging,
I was given a lavish reception, hard to accomplish, and made the day pass like a moment.
Then <s>Gomukha</s> spoke to me while I was in the sleeping chamber:

children.text: nītavantaḥ kathaṃ yūyam iyato divasān iti ||
children.translated_text: 'How did you all pass so many days?'
And when, after the end of my stay in the cowherd settlement, I had told my own story,
<s>Gomukha</s>, asked about his own affairs, related them fully and affectionately.

children.text: asty ahaṃ svagṛhāt prātar yuṣmān sevitum āgataḥ
children.translated_text: 'As for me, I came from my own house in the morning to attend upon you,

children.text: pratibuddhān na cāpaśyaṃ pāṇḍāv api divākare ||
children.translated_text: but I did not see you awake, even when the sun had grown pale-bright.
Then a maidservant sent by me, bewildered, entered,

children.text: hā śūnyam iti sākrandā nirgatā vāsamandirāt ||
children.translated_text: and crying, "Ah, it is empty!" came out from the residence.
Then the regions, the <s>Vindhya</s>, and the sky, filled with the echoing roar of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>'s lament,
seemed to shriek violently, as though afflicted.

children.text: atha tāḍitahastena mā mā bhaiṣṭeti vādinā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Ādityaśarman</s>, striking his hand and saying, "Do not, do not be afraid,"
restrained the people with an authoritative command.

children.text: sa cāvocan mahīpālam alaṃ gatvā viṣaṇṇatām
children.translated_text: And he said to the king, 'Enough of sinking into despondency.

children.text: na hy adarśanamātreṇa bhānoḥ saṃbhāvyate cyutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For merely because the sun is not seen, its fall is not to be imagined.
He whose protection is <s>Vegavatī</s>, able to protect the earth,

children.text: brahmajātir ivāvadhyā sa kasmād duḥsthatām iyāt ||
children.translated_text: and who is inviolable like one born of <s>Brahman</s>, why should he come to distress?
Or else, rise, bathe, offer oblations, eat, and sing;
afterwards, to obtain news, let the sky be watched.'

children.text: idaṃ śrutvāpi naivāsīt kasmaicid aśane ruciḥ
children.translated_text: Even after hearing this, no one had any appetite for food.
For what, apart from the object of longing, pleases a person who is full of longing?
Then the townspeople, their faces turned upward and looking everywhere at the sky,
saw something in the east, like a fragment of a broken cloud.

children.text: kim etad iti paurāṇāṃ yāvad vākyaṃ samāpyate
children.translated_text: Before the townspeople's words, 'What is this?' had come to an end,
I saw <s>Amitagati</s> close before me in the sky.
And at about an arrow-shot's distance from him was the queen, adorned in bridal dress,
the daughter of <s>Vegavat</s>, going toward the inner apartments.
Then I reported to the lord, 'Your Majesty, <s>Prajñaptikauśikī</s>:
by good fortune <s>Amitagati</s> has arrived; let him be received with affection.'

children.text: sa tu mām abravīt karṇe kathaṃ katham ayaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: But he said in my ear, 'How, how is this <s>Vidyādhara</s>
to be honored by me, a mere human being?'

children.text: tatas tam uktavān asmi yayā hariśikhādayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then I said to him, 'With the same regard by which <s>Hariśikha</s> and the others were seen,
let <s>Amitagati</s> be looked upon confidently.'

children.text: āgacchāgaccha tāteti sa tam āhūtam āgatam
children.translated_text: Saying, 'Come, come, child,' he called him; when he had come,
he stretched out his arms and touched his back and head as he bowed.

children.text: so 'pi nyubjikayā dūram apasṛtya praṇamya ca
children.translated_text: He too, withdrawing some distance with a deep bow, and bowing again,
was called once more and ordered to sit on a high seat.

children.text: taṃ rājā kṣaṇam āsīnam akhedam idam uktavān
children.translated_text: To him, seated for a moment, the king spoke these untroubled words:

children.text: bhrātuḥ kathaya vṛttāntam iti tenoditaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Tell me the account of my brother.' Then he said this:
'By King <s>Mānasavega</s> the <s>cakravartin</s> was hurled down from the sky
into a well of blind darkness; then he rose out of it by his own strength.

children.text: vegavaty api sakrodhā jitvā bhrātaram ambare
children.translated_text: <s>Vegavatī</s> too, enraged, defeated her brother in the air,
and, coming here together with me, has gone to the king's inner apartments.
The crown prince too is in <s>Campā</s>, in the house of <s>Vīṇādattaka</s>,

children.text: sukhaṃ tiṣṭhati mā bhūt tadviśaṅkā bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: staying happily; let there be no anxiety about him among you.'
Commanded by the king, 'Son, go see the mothers,'

children.text: sa mayā sahito gatvā devyau dūrād avandata ||
children.translated_text: he went with me and bowed to the two queens from afar.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ cāntaḥpure sthitvā niryātaḥ sa mayoditaḥ
children.translated_text: After staying a moment in the inner palace, he came out, and I said to him,

children.text: vistareṇa sakhe mahyaṃ bhartur vṛttaṃ nivedyatām ||
children.translated_text: 'Friend, tell me in detail the story of my lord.

children.text: bhidyante na rahasyāni gurūṇāṃ saṃnidhau tathā
children.translated_text: Secrets are not disclosed in the presence of elders in the same way
as among friends who have shared secrets and are free from suspicion.'

children.text: athoktaṃ tena yady evaṃ vivikte kvacid āsyatām
children.translated_text: Then he said, 'If that is so, let us sit somewhere secluded.

children.text: na hīdaṃ śakyam ākhyātuṃ na śrotuṃ prasthitair iti ||
children.translated_text: For this cannot be told or heard while we are on the move.'
Then, in a recess of the inner palace from which the crowd had been cleared,

children.text: āsīnāya sa me vṛttaṃ yuṣmadvṛttam avartayat ||
children.translated_text: he sat down and related to me the story concerning you.
'I was freed by the crown prince from being bound to the stake,

children.text: tenaiva ca kṛtānujñaḥ prāyām aṅgārakaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: and, with his permission, I set out toward <s>Aṅgāraka</s>.
And out of fear of the <s>cakravartin</s>, that man abandoned <s>Kusumālikā</s>.
What weak man is not afraid when the other has a powerful refuge?

children.text: so 'ham ādāya viśrabdhaṃ tvatsakhīm āśrame pituḥ
children.translated_text: So I confidently took your friend to my father's hermitage,
and spent these days at times in <s>Kāśyapasthala</s>.
Today I was favored by the remembering <s>cakravartin</s>;

children.text: sa ca gatvā mayā dṛṣṭas tiṣṭhann avaṭasaṃkaṭe ||
children.translated_text: I went and saw him standing in the narrow pit.
And he, standing on the edge of the pit, favored me with this command:

children.text: yudhyamānāṃ saha bhrātrā rakṣa vegavatīm iti ||
children.translated_text: "Protect <s>Vegavatī</s> as she fights with her brother."

children.text: utpatya ca mayā dṛṣṭā nirjitā bhrātṛśātravā
children.translated_text: Leaping up, I saw her, her brother and enemy defeated,
like an empress of <s>yoginīs</s> with her own passion torn out.

children.text: sā tu māṃ praṇataṃ dūrād ājñāpitavatī laghu
children.translated_text: But when I bowed to her from afar, she quickly commanded me:

children.text: bhrātaḥ prajñaptim āvartya svāmī vijñāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Brother, repeat the <s>Prajñapti</s> and find out about my lord."
I informed her, "Lady, he is staying in the house of <s>Dattaka</s>,
a resident of <s>Campā</s>; he should be met there."

children.text: atha dūreṇa māṃ jitvā vegād vegavatī gatā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vegavatī</s>, outstripping me by far, went with speed,
like a succession of winds driving a rain-heavy cloud.
And after a very long time, having reached <s>Campā</s>, I, at <s>Dattaka</s>'s house...
He saw a goddess invisible to human beings in the presence of the god,
and the lord of the sky seated upon a couch marked by the coils of serpents,
like the lord of the world lying in the lap of the serpent <s>Ananta</s>.
And <s>Dattaka</s> was asked with respect by the crown prince:

children.text: rūpaṃ gandharvadattāyāḥ kīdṛg ity ucyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Tell me, what is the beauty of <s>Gandharvadattā</s> like?"
Then <s>Vegavatī</s>, darkened by anger, misery, and embarrassment,
said, "So I see my husband's conduct when I am away."

children.text: varṇitaṃ dattakenāpi rūpaṃ tasyās tathā yathā
children.translated_text: And <s>Dattaka</s> described her beauty in such a way

children.text: sadyo vikasitaṃ bhartur devyās tu mlānam ānanam ||
children.translated_text: that the husband's face at once blossomed, but the queen's face withered.
Then the husband said softly, "<s>Dattaka</s> is a frog in a well,
since this man praises the beauty of <s>Gandharvadattā</s>.

children.text: yadi paśyed ayaṃ mugdhaḥ priyāṃ madanamañjukām
children.translated_text: If this simpleton were to see my beloved <s>Madanamañjukā</s>,

children.text: dūre gandharvadattāstāṃ rambhām api na varṇayet ||
children.translated_text: he would not praise <s>Gandharvadattā</s>, far less even <s>Rambhā</s>.
And the noble daughter said to me, gently shaking her head,

children.text: bahu śrotavyam atrāsti nipuṇaṃ śrūyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "There is much here to be heard; listen carefully."

children.text: punar apy uktavān svāmī sā tathāpi priyā priyā
children.translated_text: Again my lord said, "Even so, she was a dear beloved,

children.text: priyāṃ vegavatīṃ prāpya yat satyaṃ vismṛtaiva me ||
children.translated_text: but having obtained dear <s>Vegavatī</s>, to tell the truth, I had quite forgotten that beloved."
Then at once I saw all her limbs, though folded in shame,
as if blooming, with the hairs on her body standing erect.

children.text: uktaś cāsmi tayā smitvā bhrātar gacchāva saṃprati
children.translated_text: And she said to me with a smile, "Brother, let us go now,
before something else, impossible to speak of, is said by him."
A single sharp word ruins much sweet speech,
like a drop of poisoned water in a broad vessel of milk.

children.text: yāvatyā velayā devyā vākyam ityādi kalpitam
children.translated_text: In the same span of time in which the queen had composed a remark beginning, "This speech...,"

children.text: devaḥ saṃcintya tāvatyā paścād ūhitavān idam ||
children.translated_text: the king, after reflecting, then inferred this:

children.text: yathā prāpya dvitīyāṃ me vismṛtā prathamā priyā
children.translated_text: "Just as, when I obtained a second beloved, the first was forgotten by me,
so, when a third is obtained, the second will be forgotten.
In poems, women, garments, and moons, even when they are generally flawed,
creatures by their very nature take pleasure in those that are not old.
Therefore let the bride-price for <s>Gandharvadattā</s> be procured;
I shall seize her by force, as <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> seized <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>."

children.text: iti dāruṇayā patyur iyaṃ vācā vimohitā
children.translated_text: Bewildered by this cruel speech of her husband,
she fell motionless to the ground, as if struck by the glance of a glance-poisoning serpent.
Then I, confused about what should be done, somehow
did not inform the lord of that event, though it called for a hundred remedies.

children.text: utthāya ca sasaṃjñeyaṃ divam utpatya bhāṣate
children.translated_text: Then she rose, having regained consciousness, flew up into the sky, and said:
"Bowing to my teacher's feet, I shall destroy this body.

children.text: athavā kuru bandhutvaṃ bhrātaḥ kāṣṭhāni saṃhara
children.translated_text: Or else, brother, act as my kinsman: gather the firewood.

children.text: rājadvāre śmaśāne vā yas tiṣṭhati sa bāndhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who stands by one at the king's gate or at the cremation ground is a kinsman.
For embodied beings experience sufferings while they have bodies;

children.text: duḥkhādhikaraṇaṃ tan me śarīraṃ dahyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: so let my body, the seat of suffering, be burned."

children.text: mayokteyaṃ kva devasya devī vegavataḥ sutā
children.translated_text: I said, "How far apart are the god's queen, the daughter of <s>Vegavata</s>,

children.text: kva cāsadṛśam etat te vadanān nirgataṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and this unworthy speech that has come from your mouth?

children.text: yadi tyaktaśarīrāṇāṃ śarīraṃ na punar bhavet
children.translated_text: If those who have cast off the body did not have a body again,
then the self would not be in conflict with the teachers of non-self.
What weary seekers of liberation gain only after a long time through the restraint of mental activity
is obtained by poison no bigger than a knot of nut-grass.
Therefore abandon nihilism, censured by all the omniscient ones,
and protect the body, queen, as the basis of <s>dharma</s> (religious duty)."

children.text: tayā tu sarvam evedam aśrutvā śūnyacetasā
children.translated_text: But she, empty-minded, heard none of all this

children.text: nanu saṃhara dārūṇi kiṃ cireṇeti bhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: and said, "Come, gather the wood. Why delay?"

children.text: mayoktaṃ yadi yuṣmākam ayaṃ cetasi niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: I said, "If this is the decision in your mind,

children.text: aham eva tataḥ pūrvaṃ praviśāmi citām iti ||
children.translated_text: then I myself will enter the pyre first."
Then she, angered, spoke harsh words to me:

children.text: mām anumriyamāṇas tvam ucyase kiṃ janair iti ||
children.translated_text: "What will people say of you, if you die after me?"

children.text: athainām uktavān asmi satyam etad virudhyate
children.translated_text: Then I said to her, "This is truly contradictory;

children.text: jīvitaṃ tu mahādoṣaṃ tathā ca śrūyatāṃ kathā ||
children.translated_text: yet life has a great fault. And so listen to a story.
While she sat in the sky, I drew away her mind,
spreading out the patchwork blanket of a tale made of loosely joined speech.
There is a bank of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, shaped like tall, pale reeds,
hard to traverse because of wilderness trees, chiefly jujube and khadira.
Sword-bearing thieves, like <s>Śambara</s>, who plunder prosperous borderlands,

children.text: durgarājaṃ yam āśritya rājabhyo 'pi na bibhyati ||
children.translated_text: take refuge in that king of fortresses and do not fear even kings.
Through its power, the rutting tusked elephants of the wild, among herds made sparse by tigers,
cry out like dogs in cattle-pens.
And the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, with floods of milk-white water,
quenches the pain produced by the flames of forest fires at the end of the hot season.
There, in one place, in a clump of reeds surrounded by a thicket of jujube,

children.text: bilaṃ kṛtvā śatadvāram uvāsa kila mūṣika ||
children.translated_text: a mouse once made a burrow with a hundred openings and lived there.

children.text: vāneyaiḥ pāvanair annair jāhnavīyaiś ca vāribhiḥ
children.translated_text: With pure forest foods and waters from the <s>Jāhnavī</s>,
he maintained his servants like a <s>Vaikhānasa</s> in a hermitage.
Once, when he was away, intent on bringing food,
a friend of his, a mouse accustomed to the city, came to his house.
After sitting down and being honored by the female mouse with water for reception and for washing the feet,

children.text: tām apṛcchat kva yāto naḥ sakhā sakhi bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: he asked her, "Friend, where may our friend have gone?"

children.text: tayāhārārtham ity ukte prasthitaṃ tam uvāca sā
children.translated_text: When she said, "For food," she then addressed him as he was setting out:

children.text: ayam āyāti te bhrātā sumuhūrtam udīkṣyatām ||
children.translated_text: "This brother of yours is coming; wait for a very short while."

children.text: asatkāre gṛhād yāte kṛtaghne 'pi sa te sakhā
children.translated_text: When he had gone from the house without honor, though he was ungrateful, he was still your friend;
for seven nights he is deprived of the desire for sleep and food.

children.text: tvaṃ punas tasya mitraṃ ca cirāc ca gṛham āgataḥ
children.translated_text: But you are his friend, and after a long time have come to his house;

children.text: nirātithyaś ca yāmīti vṛṣas tvam aviṣāṇakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet you say, 'I shall go without hospitality': you are a bull without horns.
While this speech was going on, the sun was made grey by smoke
black as the limbs of naked ascetics, as if by the darkness of <s>Svarbhānu</s>.
Then winds blew, carrying streams of embers and ash,
causing <s>Gaṅgā</s> to dance.
Then line upon line of spotted deer and gokarṇa deer,
leaping over bewildered tigers, ran toward <s>Jāhnavī</s>.

children.text: athāsau mūṣikaḥ pāpas tām āmantrya sasaṃbhramaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that wicked mouse addressed her in alarm
and began to go away; she, alarmed, said to him:
'Ah, city-dwelling has been clearly shown by my husband's brother;
he has undertaken a great exploit by which he protects himself.
City people, versed in treatises on <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and wealth, are said to say:

children.text: ātmārthe sakalāṃ jahyāt paṇḍitaḥ pṛthivīm iti ||
children.translated_text: 'For his own sake a wise man should abandon the whole earth.'
But by that friend of yours, indifferent to his own body,
friends and enemies fallen into danger were protected like his own virtues.
Or rather, enough talk; this is no time to sit aside.
Save the little sons from fear of the forest fire.
I am unable to move these many innocent ones, whose eyes have not yet opened,
because they were born only five nights ago.

children.text: tvaṃ punaḥ puruṣaḥ śaktaḥ priyāpatyaś ca yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: You, however, are male and capable, and you are devoted to your dear offspring;
therefore carry the sons to the high bank of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.'
But that wicked mouse, clinging to the tail of a terrified tiger,
and simply ignoring the she-mouse, went away to the bank of <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Then, as though a shower of stones were falling on paved floors,
a sharp crackling sound arose all around the marshland.

children.text: athālocya bubhukṣos taṃ kakṣaṃ kakṣaṃ vibhāvasoḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as the hungry fire looked at thicket after thicket,
its whole body, through the guise of flames, became as if made of tongues.
The forest fire, like the fire at the end of an age, burned the long world of reed-thickets;
then, having no fuel, it became calm on reaching the open space of <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s bank.
After that, with the earth covered by heaps of ash scattered by a strong wind,
the marshland was seen in a moment, filled with tall anthills.

children.text: etasminn īdṛśe kāle śaṅkāgrastaḥ sa mūṣikaḥ
children.translated_text: At such a time, that mouse, seized by suspicion,

children.text: anumāya cirāc cihnair ājagāma svam ālayam ||
children.translated_text: after a long while inferred the signs and came back to his own dwelling.
There he then saw his beloved unconscious inside the house,
sweating from the hot eddies of smoke produced by the passage of the flames.
With all her limbs she embraced all the little ones, whose lives were gone,
sitting in a long sleep, their eyes not closed.

children.text: atha mūḍhaś ciraṃ sthitvā prabuddho vilalāpa saḥ
children.translated_text: Then the fool stood for a long time; after recovering his senses he lamented,
for those afflicted by the loss of kin have lamentation as their only solace.
'The great elements, being elements, are indeed for the welfare of beings.

children.text: mahābhūtena bhūtāṅge bhavatā kim idaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: O great element, what is this that you have done to the bodies of beings?
Better even the great sins, beginning with killing a brahmin,

children.text: na punar yat tvayā pāpa duṣkaraṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: than the hard-to-do evil deed, sinner, that you have done.
Surely killing a brahmin and the like come to an end through expiations,
but killings committed against children and women who have sought refuge are hard to exhaust.
Since this family of mice has been burned by you without compassion,
therefore for ten thousand births you shall become a mouse.
Or else let this blazing fire of a curse burn

children.text: tam eva capalaṃ yena sarvabhakṣaḥ kṛto bhavān ||
children.translated_text: that very restless one by whom you were made an eater of everything.'

children.text: ityādi vilapantaṃ taṃ sametya sa suhṛd dhruvaḥ
children.translated_text: As he was lamenting in such words, his steadfast friend came up

children.text: mūṣikair aparaiḥ sārdham alīkam avadad vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with other mice and spoke a false speech.

children.text: svayam eva sakhe sakhyā strītvād vāmasvabhāvayā
children.translated_text: 'Friend, by my companion herself, because she was a woman of contrary nature,
even though I begged her, the family was brought to ruin.
Ten times I said to her, 'Lady, together with me,

children.text: gaṅgākūlaṃ tribhir vāraiḥ śāvakān nayatām iti ||
children.translated_text: take the little ones to the bank of <s>Gaṅgā</s> in three trips.'

children.text: asaṃbhrāntā ca mām āha kātarāṇāṃ bhavādṛśām
children.translated_text: But she, unalarmed, said to me, 'The minds of fearful men like you
see hundreds of dangers even in a situation that is clear.
Between the edge of the reed-bed and the cane-brake there is a great pool,
and rows of rose-apple and vañjula trees with dark, dense leaves.

children.text: na cāgner asti sāmarthyam adāhyaṃ dagdhum īdṛśam
children.translated_text: Fire has no power to burn such an unburnable place;

children.text: so 'tidūreṇa vicchinnaḥ katham asmān dahed iti ||
children.translated_text: it is cut off by a very great distance, so how could it burn us?'

children.text: sa tu mitrīyamāṇas taṃ ciram ālokya pṛṣṭavān
children.translated_text: But one who had been acting as a friend looked at him for a long time and asked,

children.text: evam uktaḥ prajāvatyā bhavān kiṃ kṛtavān iti ||
children.translated_text: 'When your mate with offspring had spoken so, what did you do?'
He said, 'Because of her contrary nature, when she resisted in this way,

children.text: niṣpratyāśas tadā prāṇān ahaṃ rakṣitavān iti ||
children.translated_text: then, without hope, I saved my own life.'
While that wicked fellow stood there ashamed, bent down and face lowered,

children.text: ākhur anyatamas teṣāṃ tam asādhum abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: one mouse among them addressed that wicked one:

children.text: tuṣān gopayatā tyaktāḥ prājñena kalamās tvayā
children.translated_text: 'Protecting the husks, wise man, you abandoned the rice grains;

children.text: rakṣatā sutyajān prāṇāṃs tyaktā yad dustyajā guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: saving lives that are easy to abandon, you abandoned virtues that are hard to abandon.

children.text: prāṇānāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca viśeṣaḥ syāt kiyān iti
children.translated_text: What difference could there be between lives and virtues?

children.text: mīmāṃsitvā ciraṃ devāḥ sāmyam eṣām akalpayan ||
children.translated_text: After pondering for a long time, the gods established their equality.

children.text: tān prajāpatir āhaitya mā kṛdhvaṃ viṣamaṃ samam
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them, 'Do not make what is unequal equal:
lives are wavering like waves; virtues are firm as <s>Meru</s>.'

children.text: athavā mṛta eva tvam utkrāntaṃ paśya te yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Or rather, you are already dead; see, your fame has departed.'
The good, who live by fame, are frightened of dying in disgrace.
"Friend, your family was burned by that fire before my eyes,

children.text: ahaṃ jīvita ity etat ko brūyān mūṣikād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: and I survived: who but a mouse could say that?"

children.text: iti te tam upālabhya parisaṃsthāpya cetaram
children.translated_text: Thus, after reproaching him, consoling the other one,
and performing the funeral rites for his family, they went back as they had come.

children.text: sa cākhur mūṣikaśreṇyā tasmād ārabhya vāsarāt
children.translated_text: And from that day onward that mouse was made by the guild of mice
to be excluded from seats, places, conversation, and fellowship.
But I, having seen my mistress purified by the fire of the pyre,

children.text: akṣatāṅgaḥ svayaṃ mandaḥ kiṃ vakṣyāmi puraḥ prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: while my own limbs are unhurt, dull as I am, what shall I say before my lord?
Association with good men is the cause of the four aims, beginning with <s>dharma</s> (religious duty);
for one who is shunned by good men, that fourfold set is lost.
