children.text: tad gariṣṭhād ato doṣāl laghiṣṭhaṃ maraṇaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: Therefore, rather than this most weighty fault, I have accepted
the lighter thing, death. Enough of life stained by infamy."

children.text: yāvac ca samayaṃ baddhvā kathā parisamāpyate
children.translated_text: And by the time the story was finished, after a time had been fixed,

children.text: tāvad āvām anuprāptāv āsthānaṃ bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: we two had reached your audience hall.
Then, honored by the king with garments, ornaments, and the like,
he was pleased, bowed to the pleased ruler, and disappeared.
When he had departed a short while later, the commander addressed the lord:
"Let <s>Hariśikha</s> and the others go to <s>Campā</s> with the army train.

children.text: rājaputrasya nāgantuṃ na sthātuṃ tatra yujyate
children.translated_text: It is not proper for the prince either not to go or to stay there
like a helpless wayfarer living in a capital city.
Let five hundred elephants set out, with riders trained in weapons,

children.text: tāvanty eva sahasrāṇi tādṛśām eva vājinām ||
children.translated_text: and just as many thousands of horses, with men of the same kind.
Let foot soldiers also proceed, four times the number of the horses;

children.text: pattirakṣyā hi mātaṅgāḥ karmaṇyāḥ samareṣv iti ||
children.translated_text: for elephants, useful in battles, must be guarded by infantry."

children.text: prāptakālam idaṃ stutvā rājā senāpater vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Praising this timely advice of the commander,
the king sent us, accompanied by the army train, to your presence.
Then we set forth through the shade of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, resonant with monkeys and elephants,
and with the clear waters of mountain streams.

children.text: saṃniviṣṭaṃ ca tat tantram anyasmin vindhyasānuṣu
children.translated_text: When that army had encamped on one of the <s>Vindhya</s> ridges,
a band of thieves approached, with drums and horns sounding.
No tree, stone, bird, deer, or path could be seen;
the <s>Vindhya</s> seemed to be turning into a land of <s>Pulindas</s>.
Then we were overwhelmed by continuous arrows

children.text: saṃtatair vayam ākrāntāḥ śalabhair iva śālayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: released from masses of <s>Pulinda</s> bows, like rice fields by locusts.
Then what was done by the general mounted on an elephant

children.text: pratyakṣam api yad dṛṣṭaṃ na kaścit samabhāvayat ||
children.translated_text: no one thought possible, though it was seen directly.
Excellent arrows, passing beyond the edges of spear-discs whirled by his hand,
turned back and struck only the enemy.
His body, enveloped by circling lances, could not be seen;
but from the result it was imagined to have a thousand arms.
When the dwellers in the <s>Vindhya</s> wilderness had overrun the four quarters,
we saw arrows released by him falling all at once.
<s>Yaugandharāyaṇi</s>, sword in hand flashing with rays,

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ sarveṇa sarveṣāṃ pulīndrāṇāṃ puraḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was seen by everyone standing in front of all the <s>Pulindas</s>.
In every way he faced the enemy host with weapons raised;
it was watched by companies of apsarases standing in nearby aerial cars.
<s>Tapantaka</s> made a terrible destruction of the opposing side,
such as even <s>Droṇa</s> did not make when he released the <s>brahmāstra</s>.
I too, rushing here and there on my horse,
with useless effort, was laughed at by both our men and the enemy.
Then your force was split apart by the band of robbers,
like a cluster of sunbeams by a mass of mist.
At that confused moment an enemy hidden by the trunk of a śāla tree
struck my maddened horse hard in a vital spot with an arrow.
But the horse, disregarding the blows of my feet,
and also stumps, stones, and pits, ran on at full speed.
At day's end, after emerging from the dense <s>Vindhya</s> forest,

children.text: sthita evāmucat prāṇān paścāt kāyam apātayat ||
children.translated_text: he gave up his life while still standing, and only afterward let his body fall.

children.text: tataḥ saṃhṛtya dārūṇi gurūṇi ca bahūni ca
children.translated_text: Then, gathering much heavy firewood,
I performed his funeral rite, together with the water offering.
With my mind confused by loss of direction, I climbed a tall tree
and saw this little village nearby, with its cattle in turmoil.
I came here, and by this good man I was honored in such a way

children.text: yathā gurur yathā devo yathā rājā yathāvvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: as one would honor a teacher, a god, a king, or a bridegroom.
And <s>Hariśikha</s> and the others killed that commander of the thieves;

children.text: iti mahyam iyaṃ vārttā kathitā pathikair iti ||
children.translated_text: this news was told to me by travelers."
That night passed pleasantly for me, my eyes wakeful and eager to hear tales of the virtues of beloved friends;

children.text: sarvendriyārthajanitāni hi sevyamānā dīrghāsvavṛttir iva hanti sukhāni nidrā ||
children.translated_text: for sleep, when indulged in, destroys pleasures born from all the objects of the senses, like a long interruption of activity.
There, entertained by that excellent friend <s>Gomukha</s>,

children.text: māsam āsiṣi vipraiś ca prasannaiḥ saprasannakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I stayed for a month with gracious Brahmins and cheerful attendants.
One day <s>Gomukha</s> said, "One yojana from this village
is the holy city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, holy because <s>Avimukta</s> is never abandoned.
Whatever charming diversion there is, from <s>Prāgjyotiṣa</s>, <s>Kaśmīra</s>, <s>Dvārakā</s>, or <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>,
all of it is easy to find there.
And there, perhaps, some news may be obtained from some traveler."
There is news of <s>Hariśikhā</s> and the others; therefore let her come here.

children.text: tam uktvā yuktam āttheti taṃ cāmantrya prasannakam
children.translated_text: Having said to him, "You speak rightly," and having taken leave of <s>Prasannaka</s>,
I went from the crying <s>Saṃbhavagrāma</s> toward <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
Then, when a short interval had passed, <s>Gomukha</s> said to me,

children.text: vahāni kim ahaṃ yuṣmān yūyaṃ vahata mām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Shall I carry you, or will you carry me?"

children.text: cintitaṃ ca mayā hanta vinaṣṭaḥ khalu gomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: And I thought, "Alas, <s>Gomukha</s> is surely ruined;

children.text: yūyaṃ māṃ vahatety eṣa no brūyāt katham anyathā ||
children.translated_text: otherwise how would he say to us, 'You carry me'?
He bows even to the shadow of my seat;

children.text: ariṣṭāviṣṭatāṃ muktvā katham itthaṃ sa vakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: unless possessed by some evil omen, how could he speak like this?"
I said to him very humbly, "Your feet, sir, are greatly tired;

children.text: tan madīyam aśaṅkena pṛṣṭham āruhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore climb onto my back without hesitation."

children.text: tena coktaṃ vilakṣeṇa mā grahīta yathāśrutam
children.translated_text: He said in embarrassment, "Do not take what I said literally.
Such a thought is not to be entertained, even if one like me has met with misfortune.

children.text: kiṃtu yaḥ kiṃcid ācaṣṭe pānthasya pathikaḥ pathi
children.translated_text: But whatever a traveler says to another traveler on the road,
that man becomes his bearer, because he makes him forget his weariness."
I said to him, "You yourself are skilled in every turn of events,

children.text: ākhyātuṃ ca vijānāti yat tataḥ kathayatv iti ||
children.translated_text: and you know how to narrate; so tell a story."
He said, "The learned say that there are five subjects for stories:
<s>dharma</s> (religious duty), wealth, pleasure, nirvāṇa (liberation), and medicine, each with its elaborations.
Among these, action of body, speech, and mind for the benefit of beings
is the source of all <s>dharmas</s>, as the earth is the source of worlds.
The means by which neutral people and enemies come to friendship

children.text: sarvārthānām asau hetur guṇānām iva sajjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is the cause of all aims, as a good man is the cause of virtues.
Avoiding other men's wives and courtesans, contentment, mildness in anger,

children.text: nātisaktiś ca dāreṣu sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ viparyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and no excessive attachment even to one's own wives: this is happiness; the opposite is suffering.
The masters know nirvāṇa as the complete absence of connection
between the embodied person and attachment to pleasure and the like, together with all its auxiliaries and bodiless desire.
Even if he eats at midnight, a man hungry for the highest truth
and rejecting quack physicians is avoided by diseases from afar.
For among seers who have seen the essence of worldly existence, who like me,
a worthless man, would mock doctrines whose essence is weighty?

children.text: tena yat kiṃcid ucchāstraṃ bālabhāvād udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: Therefore whatever I have said that is outside the scriptures, uttered from childishness,
this worthless chatter of my parrot-like speech, let it be forgiven."
Listening to stories beginning with this, I then reached <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,
called the ornament of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, filled without break with temples of the gods.
There, in a deserted building situated outside the city,
we occupied a pavilion variegated with old timber and plaster.

children.text: gomukhas tu kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā mām avocad gataśramam
children.translated_text: But <s>Gomukha</s>, after resting a moment, said to me when my fatigue was gone,
"Remain here for a little while without anxiety.

children.text: yatra sthātavyam asmābhir upalabhya tam āśrayam
children.translated_text: Once I have found the lodging where we should stay,

children.text: āgacchāmīti mām uktvā calair uccalitaḥ padaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I will come back." Saying this to me, he set off with quick-moving steps.
After going some sixteen or twenty paces, he suddenly stopped;

children.text: tataḥ kimapi niścitya nivṛtto mām abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: then, having decided something, he turned back and spoke to me:

children.text: yad idaṃ yuṣmadaṅgeṣu divyaṃ bhūṣaṇam āhitam
children.translated_text: "These divine ornaments placed on your limbs,

children.text: idam ādāya gacchāmi sthātuṃ nāsyeha yujyate ||
children.translated_text: I will take with me; it is not proper for them to remain here.
<s>Vārāṇasī</s> is occupied by great thieves, crows at holy places,
heretics with hidden armor, such as triple-staff ascetics and white-robed men.
Seeing you alone, ornamented and unarmed,

children.text: teṣāṃ sāhasikaḥ kaścid anarthaṃ cintayed iti ||
children.translated_text: some reckless man among them might plan harm."
I agreed, saying, "Let it be so, then."
Taking those ornaments, he quickly entered the city.
Then, not long after he had gone, a wandering ascetic and a brahmacārin,
tired from walking about, sat down in that very place.

children.text: āsīc ca mama tāv etau nūnaṃ pāṣaṇḍitaskarau
children.translated_text: And I thought, "Surely these two are sectarian thieves;
they must want to rob me, unarmed and without assistance.
Even among thousands of such men with daggers in their hands,
my mind would have only sluggish respect for them, as for cattle with their horns removed.
But toward men whose weapons are at the root of their thighs and whose armor is renunciation,

children.text: prayuṅkte nirghṛṇaḥ śastraṃ ko 'nyaḥ klībatamas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: what man could be more cowardly than one who mercilessly uses a weapon?"
Seeing me thinking such thoughts, that staff-bearing ascetic,
as if hopeless and distressed, said to the brahmacārin:
"By texts strung together with garrulous chatter, Sāṃkhya, Yoga, and the rest,

children.text: vipralabdhāḥ sukhaṃ tyaktvā mokṣamārge kila sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: we have been deceived: abandoning pleasure, we supposedly stand on the path to liberation.

children.text: yathā tṛṇam upādātum ambarāmbhojam eva vā
children.translated_text: As if someone were to perform great austerity in order to obtain a blade of grass

children.text: kaścin mahat tapaḥ kuryān mokṣārtho nas tathā śramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or a lotus in the sky, so is our labor undertaken for the sake of liberation.
If liberation is as easy to obtain as grass, then effort is fruitless;
but if it is as hard to obtain as a lotus in the sky, then seekers of liberation are lost.
For the existence of the next world, the reason is the statement of an omniscient one;
and the existence of an omniscient one is established by the five divine proofs.
But even the reason adduced to prove the existence of an omniscient being
is tainted by the serpent-venom of faults such as being unproved and contradictory.
Therefore enough of poetic rags stitched together from a libertine's flatteries;
let us enjoy sense objects as freely as we please."
But the brahmacārin, agitated, said to the wandering ascetic,
"Why have you extended this worthless wrestler's cudgel of an argument?
Let sound propositions, reasons, and examples remain aside for the moment;
you are refuted even by a conclusion that is not contrary to any system."
Establishing the nonexistence of the next world by dry reasoning,
you will become truly pitiable, afflicted by the talk of contentious disputation.

children.text: athavāstām idaṃ tāvad idaṃ tāvan nigadyatām
children.translated_text: Or rather, let this stand for now; for the present let this be said:

children.text: smṛtīnāṃ viṭakāvyatvaṃ kathaṃ veda bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: how does your honor know that the <s>smṛtis</s> are libertine poetry?
He said, "I know the marks of men
and of nearly all embodied beings, taught by <s>Nandīśa</s> and others.

children.text: yaś caiṣa puruṣaḥ ko'pi pānthaḥ pāṃsulapādakaḥ
children.translated_text: And this man here, whoever he is, a traveler with dusty feet,
is said to become the <s>Indra</s> of the lords of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>.
Seeing him occupying this rickety pavilion,
I suppose all scriptures to be as pithless as a wrestler's staff.
Books whose subject is unseen are inferred to have meaning
from those whose subjects are seen, such as the <s>Gāruḍa</s> texts, just as donors are inferred from beggars.
And just as the science of bodily marks is false, since it is libertine poetry,
so the <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the rest should be considered."
The other then said to him, "The wise call fate
the karma accumulated in former births, bearing pleasant and unpleasant fruit.

children.text: yac cedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ nāma śarīreṣu śarīriṇām
children.translated_text: And this so-called mark in the bodies
of embodied beings is the sign of former karma called fate.
Yet fate bears fruit for no one who lacks human effort;
for even <s>Īśvara</s> depends on the full complex of time and causes.
But this youth is young, healthy, and throws gods and demons into the shade by his beauty,
while, through a defective and sluggish movement of his cheeks, he seems matched with dullness.

children.text: yathā dhanur adhānuṣkaṃ yathā bījam avāpakam
children.translated_text: As a bow without an archer, as a seed without a sower,
so for a man fate without human effort has mere existence as its fruit."
The mendicant said, "Fate is stronger than human effort;

children.text: jñāpakaṃ cāsya pakṣasya śrūyatāṃ yan mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: listen to a proof of this position, which I heard.
There is a village on the bank of the <s>Sindhu</s> called <s>Brahmasthalaka</s>;
there lived <s>Vedaśarman</s>, an excellent Brahmin learned in the four <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: tasya yo 'nyatamaḥ śiṣyaḥ pāṭhaṃ prati dṛḍhodyamaḥ
children.translated_text: One of his students was especially firm in his effort at recitation,

children.text: tasmād eva ca sa chāttrair āhūyata dṛḍhodyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for that very reason the students called him <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>.
<s>Vedaśarman</s> had always arranged food
and clothing for him in the house of a householder named <s>Tamobhedaka</s>.
There a <s>Pāñcarātrika</s> mendicant named <s>Bhinnatamāḥ</s>

children.text: vāsam āvasathe tasya karoti sma dṛḍhodyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: used to dwell in his lodging with <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>.
In this way, by that man of sharp faith and intelligence,
the four <s>Vedas</s> were studied in ten years.
Then <s>Bhinnatamāḥ</s>, after speaking for a long time about caste and stages of life,
addressed him at dusk, when the crowd of people had grown quiet:
'This tantric establishment, with many cows, buffalo cows, fields, female slaves, and male slaves,

children.text: tantrasthānam upāntaṃ ca cāṭādibhyaś ca rakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: has been brought to its limit by me and protected from thieves and the like.
But the mendicant's duty that is prescribed, chiefly meditation and study,
does not exist even in name for me, who am engaged in the work of a merchant.
Now, however, the torpor of old age has come, stealing away
the movements of speech and body, as if close to the next world.
For householders established in their vow but lazy in their own duties,
the sages prescribed visiting sacred fords as a means of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: āha vedāntavādaś ca tārakaṃ brahma tantrayet
children.translated_text: And the doctrine of <s>Vedānta</s> says that one should contemplate the saving <s>Brahman</s>;
therefore seekers of liberation should not abandon <s>Avimukta</s>.

children.text: śvaḥ prasthātāsmahe tasmāt prātar vārāṇasīṃ prati
children.translated_text: Therefore tomorrow morning we shall set out for <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,

children.text: buddhadharme praśastā hi dharmasya tvaritā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for in the teaching of the enlightened, a swift course in <s>dharma</s> is praised.
You too, since you acknowledge the authority of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>,
must by obligation take a wife and sons.
And the <s>dharma</s> of the householder stage depends on wealth such as cattle;

children.text: na ca pratigrahād anyad viprasya dhanasādhanam ||
children.translated_text: for a Brahmin there is no means of acquiring wealth other than accepting gifts.

children.text: tat sukhopanataṃ caitad anindyam atibhūri ca
children.translated_text: Therefore take this wealth of ours, easily come to hand, blameless,
very abundant, and together with female and male slaves.'
He said, 'A man like me is unable to question

children.text: na vikalpayituṃ śaktaḥ kiṃ punar nyāyyam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: what you have commanded, even if it were improper; how much less something so just.
But after taking leave of those who stand in my father's place,
the givers of learning and life, I shall carry out your command when the night has passed.'

children.text: yātāyāṃ tu triyāmāyāṃ tam āmantrayituṃ gatam
children.translated_text: When the night had gone by, the mendicant, though ready to depart,
waited a long time for him, who had gone to take leave.

children.text: yadā tu divasārdhe 'pi gate chāttraḥ sa nāgataḥ
children.translated_text: But when even half the day had passed and that student had not come,

children.text: taṃ gaveṣayituṃ bhikṣuḥ svayam eva tadā gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the mendicant himself went to search for him.
He saw him in the courtyard of <s>Tamobhedaka</s>'s house,
walking slowly and reciting softly.

children.text: uktaṃ ca bhavatā kasmād iyacciram iha sthitam
children.translated_text: And he said, 'Why have you stayed here so long, sir?

children.text: athārthenaiva tenārthas tathā naḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Now let the matter be told to us by you just as it is.'

children.text: tatas tenoktam etasmin gṛhe kenāpi hetunā
children.translated_text: Then he said, 'In this house, for some reason,
all the household staff are busy and run here and there.

children.text: yāṃ yām eva ca pṛcchāmi kim etad iti dārikām
children.translated_text: And whichever girl I ask, "What is this?"

children.text: sā sā mām āha saṃrabdhā śivaṃ dhyātu bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: each one says to me angrily, "Let your honor meditate on <s>Śiva</s>."

children.text: taṃ cādyāpi na pṛcchāmi tamobhedakam ākulam
children.translated_text: Even now I have not asked <s>Tamobhedaka</s>, who is distressed;

children.text: tenāhaṃ nāgataḥ kṣipraṃ sakāśaṃ bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore I did not come quickly into your presence.'
Then <s>Bhinnatamāḥ</s> smiled and said to <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>,

children.text: yenāyam ākulo lokas tad ahaṃ kathayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: 'I shall tell you why this household is so disturbed.
The childbirth of <s>Tamobhedaka</s>'s wife is at hand.'"
This household retinue there will be in utter confusion in place after place.

children.text: dārikā jāyate cāsya tāṃ ca tvaṃ pariṇeṣyasi
children.translated_text: And a little daughter will be born to this man, and you will marry her;
and she, seized as if by the demon of passion, will behave wickedly.

children.text: iti tasmin kṛtādeśe gate svavivadhaṃ prati
children.translated_text: When that command had been given to him and he had gone back to his own dwelling,
the other man began to think, his mind trembling with suspicion:
"If this brahmin's wife gives birth to a daughter,
then the utterance of the one whose darkness is broken will not prove false in meaning.
From the manifest power of mantras in rites of exorcistic cries, possession, poison, and cutting off,
the efficacy of the remaining mantras too is inferred."

children.text: iti cintayatas tasya dīno gṛhapatir gṛhāt
children.translated_text: As he was thinking this, the wretched householder came out from the house,

children.text: hā daivaṃ khalam ityādi lapan nīcair vinirgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: muttering softly, "Ah, treacherous fate!" and the like.
And after a moment, like a cat seized by a dog and crying out,
from within the house there arose a sound harsh as a kennel of dogs.
Then women who had been adorned, their heads covered by modesty,
came out through the side door, with hands spread open in despair.
And the group of servants addressed the grieving cluster of relatives,

children.text: amantrayata vāmasya vidheḥ kiṃ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: saying, "What can be done against hostile fate?"
But while such a commotion was spreading through that house, he, firm in resolve,
made fearful by the command of the accomplished mendicant, thought:
"Let people see fate, established by such a mendicant's words,
overcome by human effort.
Having abandoned the country of <s>Sindhu</s>, de...

children.text: ayaṃ pariharāmy enāṃ dūrataḥ kardamām iti ||
children.translated_text: I shall avoid this girl from afar, as one avoids mud."
After reflecting in this way and the like, without even consulting the respectable people,
he fled a road of ten yojanas in a single day.

children.text: sadvīpāṃ ca parikramya varṣair dvādaśabhir mahīm
children.translated_text: And after circling the earth with its islands in twelve years,
he came to the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, wishing to attend upon the sacred bathing places.
Then, tormented by heat and thirst, and desiring shade and water,
he entered someone's house in a certain brahmin village.
There he asked a brahmin woman sitting in the veranda, her hair like arka-cotton,

children.text: yayāce brāhmaṇīm amba pānīyaṃ dāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Mother, please have water given to me."

children.text: sā tv abhāṣata saṃbhrāntā hale putri tamālike
children.translated_text: But she, flustered, said, "Hey, daughter <s>Tamālikā</s>,
take a seat and water and come out quickly."
Then, with a little stool in her hand and wearing a black-and-white bodice,
a girl came out of the house, the ends of her side-locks tawny.
Looking around with restless eyes and constantly smiling,
with a lame, halting gait, she reached <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s> after a long time.

children.text: āsyatām atra mitreti vadantyā śūnyayā tayā
children.translated_text: As that empty-headed girl said to him, "Sit here, friend,"
she set the water vessel down before him, thinking it was the stool.

children.text: atha tām abravīd vṛddhā muktvaitām avinītatām
children.translated_text: Then the old woman said to her, "Stop this rudeness;
pour out water from another water-pot."
But she, with violent trembling produced by feigned fright,
her lips bent by an inward smile, carried out the old woman's order.

children.text: tato gataśramaṃ vṛddhā pṛcchati sma dṛḍhodyamam
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>'s fatigue had gone, the old woman asked him,

children.text: āgacchati kuto deśāt kaṃ vā yāti bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "From what country is your honor coming, and to what one are you going?"

children.text: tenoktaṃ na sa deśo 'sti nāgacchāmi yataḥ kṣitau
children.translated_text: He said, "There is no country on earth from which I have not come;

children.text: yac ca brūtha kva yāsīti tatra vijñāpayāmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and as for your asking where I am going, I will explain that to you.
In some brahmin village, by teaching boys,
I wish to pass my days, content with the villagers."

children.text: tatas tam abravīd vṛddhā nītijñaiḥ satyam ucyate
children.translated_text: Then the old woman said to him, "Those who know policy speak truly:

children.text: na hy ataptena lohena taptaṃ saṃdhīyate kvacit ||
children.translated_text: hot iron is never joined with iron that has not been heated.
I have two sons' sons, only just initiated,

children.text: tau ca saṃyojitau puṇyair arthināv arthinā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: and by good fortune those seekers have been joined with you, who are also a seeker.
You seek teaching, and they desire study;
let there be a conjunction for you, like a lost horse and a burned cart."

children.text: tatas tasyai pratijñāya tau baṭū pāṭhayann asau
children.translated_text: Then, after promising her, he taught those two boys
and stayed for two years with another group of pupils.

children.text: ekadā tām abhāṣanta vṛddhām āgatya bāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: One day the relatives came to the old woman and said,
"Why is this <s>Tamālikā</s> not being given to <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>?

children.text: ye jāmātṛguṇās teṣāṃ kaścid asti kvacid vare
children.translated_text: Whatever qualities belong to sons-in-law, some occur in some suitor somewhere;

children.text: dṛḍhodyame punaḥ paśya yadi kaṃcin na paśyasi ||
children.translated_text: but in <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>, look whether there is any that you do not see.
Since one hard to obtain has become easy to obtain, let this man be accepted.

children.text: kena vanyaḥ karī vārīm āgataḥ svayam ujjhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who would let go a wild elephant that has come to the water of its own accord?"

children.text: iti tair bodhitā vṛddhā pratītā tān ayācata
children.translated_text: Thus instructed by them, the old woman, convinced, requested them:

children.text: yady evaṃ svayam evāyaṃ pūjyair abhyarthyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "If this is so, let this man himself be asked by your honors."

children.text: te tatas tam abhāṣanta bhautika brahmacāriṇā
children.translated_text: Then they said to him, "O brahmacārin learned in real things,

children.text: āmnātāś cāvabuddhāś ca vedāḥ sasmṛtayas tvayā ||
children.translated_text: the Vedas, together with the Smṛtis, have been recited and understood by you.
And now a pure wife must necessarily be taken;
otherwise let the drying of your breast, throat, and lips not be fruitless.
Therefore let this wholly pure <s>Tamālikā</s> be accepted,
the chief limb of the highest stage of life, like the threefold Veda embodied."

children.text: evamādi sa tair uktaḥ kṣaṇam etad acintayat
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by them and so on, he thought about this for a moment:

children.text: yuktaṃ yad brāhmaṇair uktam atra tāvat kim ucyate ||
children.translated_text: "What the brahmins have said is proper; what, then, can be said here?

children.text: yaś cāsau sindhuviṣaye dūṣitaḥ kṛtyayā tayā
children.translated_text: And that girl in the <s>Sindhu</s> region, tainted by that evil spell,
is also, like the far shore of the ocean, extremely hard to reach because of the distance.
But if, by fate, this is that very girl brought from the country of <s>Sindhu</s>,

children.text: sūcīsūtragate daivāt tataḥ kaḥ kutra mokṣyate ||
children.translated_text: then, once she has gone by fate onto the needle's thread, who will escape anywhere?"

children.text: evamādi sa niścitya pratiśrutya tatheti ca
children.translated_text: Having resolved thus and the like, and having promised, "So be it,"

children.text: pariṇīya ca tāṃ kanyāṃ saṃvatsaram ayāpayat ||
children.translated_text: And after marrying that girl, he spent a year.
Then, when the three-watch night had passed, <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>, firm in resolve,
asked <s>Tamālikā</s>, whose sleep had ended and was shown by her yawning:

children.text: brūhi sundari paśyāma kuṭumbasyāsya kaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: "Speak, beautiful one; let us see who is the master of this household.

children.text: keyaṃ bhavati te vṛddhā kāv etau baṭukāv iti ||
children.translated_text: Who is this old woman to you, and who are these two boys?"
But she, whose long sorrow was told by a long sigh,
with rows of teardrops flowing, spoke in faltering syllables:

children.text: asyā brāhmaṇavṛddhāyāḥ priyaḥ sādhur abhūt patiḥ
children.translated_text: "This old brahmin woman's beloved husband was a virtuous man,
by whose riches of learning pupils, sacrificers, and beggars were satisfied.
By him his daughter was given to a student as a resident son-in-law,
to one who had mastered the whole Veda and possessed virtues such as patience.

children.text: tāḍitaś caraṇenāpi yaḥ kṣamāvān abhūt purā
children.translated_text: He who formerly remained forbearing even when struck with a foot
was brought, through the condition of son-in-law, by anger into the state of a black serpent.
Taking even great honor to be dishonor,
he needlessly caused distress to his mother-in-law and father-in-law, and to himself.
One day his brother-in-law said to him jokingly,
"Dear sir, you are like <s>Durvāsas</s>, hard to propitiate."

children.text: yady evaṃ durdurūḍhena kiṃ mayārādhitena vaḥ
children.translated_text: "If that is so, what use to you is my being propitiated with such bad approach?"

children.text: ity uktvā mantharālāpaḥ sadāro gata eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: So saying in slow speech, he went away with his wife.
Overhearing the insults of his mother-in-law, father-in-law, and their friends,
he went without concern to his own country, <s>Sindhudeśa</s>.
There, settling in a village named <s>Brahmasthalaka</s>,
he soon performed the obligatory and occasional rites.

children.text: tasya tasyāṃ ca bhāryāyāṃ kālarātrisamā sutā
children.translated_text: To him, by that wife, a daughter like <s>Kālarātri</s> was born,

children.text: yamau ca tanayau jātau yamakālau kulasya yau ||
children.translated_text: and twin sons, who were twin deaths for the family.

children.text: aham eva ca sā kanyā tau caitau kākatālukau
children.translated_text: I myself am that girl, and these two are those ill-omened pair,

children.text: yair mātāpitarāv eva bālair eva samāhitau ||
children.translated_text: by whom our mother and father themselves were destroyed while they were still children.
And one region of <s>Sindhudeśa</s>, by the <s>Sindhu</s> with its fierce current,
was suddenly seized and carried away by a great, irresistible flood.
Then, out of fear of that, it was decided by our mother and father:

children.text: mātāmahagṛhaṃ yāntu bālā me niviśantv iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let my children go to their maternal grandfather's house; let them live there."
Then <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>, pierced by arrows of suspicion, said to her:

children.text: śeṣaṃ sujñānam evāsyāḥ kathāyāḥ sthīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "The rest of this story is easy to know; let it stop here."
And for him that all-knowing wandering ascetic <s>Bhāskara</s> had spoken truly,
since the darkness of ignorance had plainly been split apart.
"Now I have experienced those two commands of his as just such things;
to avoid the third, I will abandon the earth."
Then, after wandering for twelve years through other islands,
he became weary and, with his head somewhat whitened, thought:
"What the wandering ascetic foretold, that woman, maddened by madness,
has surely by now done, doing what should not be done.

children.text: asmābhiś ca na vedoktaṃ na vedāntoktamohitam
children.translated_text: And by us no good taught by the Veda, nor taught by the Vedānta, has been secured;
a man's lifespan has somehow been drunk up, as if by spreading wounds.
Therefore, going to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, for the sake of attending holy bathing-places,

children.text: puṇyaṃ svargaphalaṃ kurvann ayāmi divasān iti ||
children.translated_text: I will pass my days doing merit whose fruit is heaven."
Then, crossing the ocean, he came to <s>Gaṅgāsāgara</s>;

children.text: tato vārāṇasīṃ prāpad amuñcann eva jāhnavīm ||
children.translated_text: from there he reached <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, never leaving the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.
Just as he was entering, he saw before him a great <s>Pāśupata</s>,
adorned with human bones, his speech and gait unsteady.
And after him came a woman with ear and neck ornaments mostly of crystal,
with eyes reddened and rolling from liquor, and with a variegated necklace on her throat.
She doubled the road by her crooked turns and reversals of gait,
like a female serpent that had not cast off its own slough.

children.text: sā tu kāpālikenoktā drutam ehi kapālini
children.translated_text: But she was addressed by the <s>Kāpālika</s>: "Come quickly, <s>Kapālinī</s>,
before the incense-time of <s>Avimukta</s> passes by.
After praising the fixed lord beyond the three states with cries of huṃ-huṃ and the like,
then I will look for liquor in the taverns."

children.text: evaṃprāye ca vṛttānte ciraṃ dṛṣṭvā dṛḍhodyamam
children.translated_text: While an incident of this sort was taking place, after looking long at <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>,
<s>Kapālinī</s>, crying out loudly, fell at his feet.
Again the <s>Kāpālika</s> said, "Let go of the brahmin traveler.

children.text: parihāsaś ciraṃ caṇḍi viruddhas tyajyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Enough of the long jest, fierce woman; let this improper behavior be abandoned."

children.text: sābravīd eṣa me bhartā daivataiḥ pratipāditaḥ
children.translated_text: She said, "This is my husband, assigned to me by the gods.

children.text: tvaṃ tu dhṛṣṭaviṭo bhūtvā kiṃ vyāharasi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: But you, becoming an insolent libertine, why do you speak to me?"

children.text: taṃ ca prapañcam ālokya sa pradeśaḥ sakautukaiḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that spectacle, that place, full of curiosity,
was filled with countless people, including śramaṇas and brahmins.
And she said, "O knower of the four Vedas, you are wholly empty of Veda.

children.text: savedaḥ ko hi nirvedaṃ vedoktaiḥ karmabhir vrajet ||
children.translated_text: For who, possessing the Veda, would grow indifferent to the rites enjoined by the Veda?
You have not produced sons; the agnihotra has not been tended;
the ancestors have not been honored with funeral cakes; you have wandered about like one turned to air.

children.text: tvayā dṛḍhodyama tyaktā sāhaṃ mandā tamālikā
children.translated_text: I am that poor <s>Tamālikā</s>, abandoned by you, <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>.
Wandering from household to household, I practice this way of life of an unchaste woman.
Young women, dwelling in homes without elders and bereft of husbands:

children.text: yair aduṣṭāḥ striyo dṛṣṭās te dṛṣṭāḥ kenacit kvacit ||
children.translated_text: by whom have such women ever been seen undefiled anywhere?

children.text: tena tyaktavatā dārān yat tvayā pāpam arjitam
children.translated_text: Therefore, the sin that you earned by abandoning your wife

children.text: tān eva bharamāṇena tat samucchidyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: must be cut off by supporting those very ones."
Then the brahmins said to <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>, blinded by shame and despondency:

children.text: bhagavatyā yad uktaṃ tat tattvataḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "What has been said by the venerable lady must be told truthfully."
Then by him, in the presence of the twice-born and the other people, about himself and about her...
What had happened while he was living at <s>Brahmasthalaka</s> and elsewhere was reported.
Then the Brahmins said, "Brahman, let the Brahmin woman be accepted;
good people do not practice the abandonment of a loving wife.

children.text: yac ca kiṃcid akartavyam anāthyād anayā kṛtam
children.translated_text: And whatever improper act this woman has done because she was without protection,

children.text: tasya kṛcchratamaiḥ kṛcchrair viśuddhiḥ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: let purification for that be performed by the most severe penances."
He said, "The venerable ones know what sort of sin

children.text: pūjyānām eva tad buddham idaṃ budhyata yādṛśam ||
children.translated_text: can be removed by expiations; understand what sort this one is.
Women who go to men of lower caste are said to be sinners;

children.text: iyaṃ tv aśubhasāvarṇaṃ yam upāste sa dṛśyatām ||
children.translated_text: but let the one whom this woman attends, a man of inauspicious kind, be seen.

children.text: tad upāstām iyaṃ bhadrā yam upāsac chivaṃ dhruvam
children.translated_text: Therefore let this good woman attend upon the one whom she attended, surely <s>Śiva</s>,
her husband, the great <s>Pāśupata</s>, who brings happiness."
When he had spoken thus, she, her modesty increased, said to him,

children.text: ā mṛtyos tvatsamīpasthā nayāmi divasān iti ||
children.translated_text: "Remaining near you until death, I will pass my days."
Then one Brahmin among them addressed <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>:
"Brahman, let my beautiful daughter be married.

children.text: dhanaṃ me dhanadasyeva saiva caikā sutā yataḥ
children.translated_text: Since my wealth is like <s>Dhanada</s>'s wealth, and she is my only daughter,

children.text: tatas tasya ca tasyāś ca bhaved bhartā bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore you would become the husband of both it and her."

children.text: āsīc cāsya kim adyāpi syān na syād iti cintayā
children.translated_text: And in him there was still the anxious thought, "Can it happen even now, or can it not?"
for by this woman the mendicant's words had been made fulfilled.

children.text: pratijñāya ca tāṃ kanyāṃ dadānād brāhmaṇāt svayam
children.translated_text: After pledging himself, <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s> personally married that girl,
given by the Brahmin together with a mass of great wealth.
<s>Tamālikā</s> too, cutting off her hair and wearing a saffron robe,
passed the time living near <s>Dṛḍhodyama</s>'s house.
<s>Dṛḍhodyama</s> also, constantly performing the duties of a twice-born man,
worshiped <s>Jahnu</s>'s daughter, caressed by the highest limb of <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: tat tena yena kṛtaduṣkarapauruṣeṇa vākyaṃ na bhinnatamasaḥ kṛtam apramāṇam
children.translated_text: Thus, by him whose manly effort had performed a deed difficult to do, the statement of the ascetic whose darkness had been broken was not made false;

children.text: śūreṇa daivahariṇā prabhuṇā prasahya tasmāj jitaḥ puruṣakāragajādhirājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore the elephant-king of human effort was forcibly conquered by the brave lord, the lion of fate.
Then the mendicant was addressed, with a slight laugh, by the celibate student:
"Listen to how human effort has supremacy.
There was a merchant dwelling in <s>Ujjayinī</s>, named <s>Sāgaradatta</s>,
whose possessions were wealth well acquired and whose mind was deep as the ocean.
When he had gone to the sea and was traveling in a launched ship,
another ship was seen, marked by a fluttering banner.

children.text: aṅgāpotam amuṃ yena potaṃ prerayateti saḥ
children.translated_text: "Bring this ship alongside that ship,"

children.text: yāvan niryāmakān āha tāvat potau samīyatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: he was saying to the pilots, and by then the two ships came together.
Then <s>Sāgaradatta</s> said to that ship-owner,

children.text: yūyaṃ ye vā yatas tyā vā tan naḥ pratyucyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Who you are, or from where, or whose men you are, tell us that."
He said, "I am <s>Buddhavarman</s>, a merchant dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>.

children.text: bhavantaḥ ke kuto veti tataḥ so 'pi nyavedayat ||
children.translated_text: Who are you, and from where?" Then he too related it.
Then, with poetry, stories, drinking, lute songs, and gambling,
the two, enjoying themselves, plunged into the hard-to-fathom great ocean.
After going to <s>Kāñcanadvīpa</s>, whose outskirts were full of endless gold,
they returned and reached a seaport town on the ocean shore.
Then <s>Sāgaradatta</s> said to <s>Buddhavarman</s>,

children.text: prītir naḥ sthiratāṃ yāyād yathā saṃpādyatāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: "Let our affection be made to attain permanence in whatever way it can.
I left home when my wife was far advanced in pregnancy;

children.text: tasyāś ca divasir ebhir jātam anyatarad dvayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: by these days, one of the two has been born to her.

children.text: duhitā cet tato dattā bhavatputrāya sā mayā
children.translated_text: If it is a daughter, then she has been given by me to your son;

children.text: putraś cet tvaṃ tatas tasmai dadyāḥ svatanayām iti ||
children.translated_text: if it is a son, then you should give your own daughter to him."

children.text: tenoktaṃ mahad āścaryam iyam eva hi no matiḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "This is a great wonder; this very thought was ours.

children.text: athavā kim ihāścaryam ekam evāvayor vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, what is wonderful here? The two of us have one and the same body."
Thus, having made an alliance and embraced one another,
the two went to their own places with great buffalo caravans.
They bowed before the kings, the lords of <s>Avanti</s> and <s>Magadha</s>,
and, highly honored at their command, went toward their own homes.

children.text: tatra satkriyamāṇau ca satkurvāṇau ca saṃtatam
children.translated_text: There, being honored continually and themselves continually honoring
kinsmen, Brahmins, and others, they passed the days.
Then, while <s>Sāgaradatta</s> was sitting on his couch,
a little girl, shining like a garland of jasmine, was placed in his lap.
"Whose is this jasmine garland?" he asked his wife;
and she too, embarrassed, softly answered, "Whose else could she be?"

children.text: tena coktam idaṃ yādṛg bālikā kundamālikā
children.translated_text: He said, "Since this little girl is such a <s>Kundamālikā</s>,

children.text: yayoḥ syād īdṛśaḥ putraḥ pitarau tau saputrakau ||
children.translated_text: the parents whose son might be like this are parents blessed with a son.

children.text: tasmād duhitṛmāteti mā gās tvaṃ bhīru bhīrutām
children.translated_text: Therefore, mother of a daughter, timid woman, do not go into timidity;

children.text: na kīrtijananī vidyā nindyā bhavitum arhati ||
children.translated_text: knowledge that gives birth to fame does not deserve to be blamed.
Having reassured her with these and similar words,
he told her of the meeting on the ocean and of his friendship with <s>Buddhavarman</s>.

children.text: kasyeyaṃ kundamāleti tām apṛcchad yataḥ pitā
children.translated_text: Because her father had asked her, "Whose is this jasmine garland?"

children.text: prasiddhā tasya nāmnāpi sā tataḥ kundamālikā ||
children.translated_text: she thereafter became famous also by that name, <s>Kundamālikā</s>.
<s>Buddhavarman</s> too asked his silent wife,

children.text: tasmin garbhe tavotpannaṃ yat tan naḥ kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Tell us what was born to you from that pregnancy."
Then she handed over to him that son: dwarfish, one-eyed, rough,

children.text: lambauṣṭhaṃ bhugnapṛṣṭhaṃ ca sā taṃ putraṃ samarpayat ||
children.translated_text: pot-bellied, snaggle-toothed, long-lipped, and bent-backed.

children.text: so 'bravīt kiṃ vṛthaivāyaṃ dhṛtaḥ kurubhakas tvayā
children.translated_text: He said, "Why has this stunted child been kept by you for nothing?

children.text: kasmād īkṣaṇikāṃ pṛṣṭvā garbha eva na pātitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why, after consulting a female prognosticator, was he not dropped while still in the womb?"

children.text: yaḥ sa sāgaradattena saha saṃbandhakaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The alliance that had been made with <s>Sāgaradatta</s>
has been rejected by this misshapen ghost.

children.text: saṃdiśed yadi nāmāsāv ahaṃ duhitṛvān iti
children.translated_text: If indeed he should send word, 'I have a daughter,'

children.text: tadā kiṃ pratisaṃdeśyaṃ mayāhaṃ putravān iti ||
children.translated_text: then what reply am I to send: 'I have a son'?

children.text: bhāryāṃ cāvocad āgacched dūto mālavakād yadi
children.translated_text: And he told his wife, 'If a messenger should come from <s>Mālavaka</s>,

children.text: enaṃ kurubhakaṃ tasmai na kaścit kathayed iti ||
children.translated_text: no one must tell him about this <s>Kurubhaka</s>.'

children.text: ayaṃ kurubhakaḥ kasmād iti yat taṃ pitābravīt
children.translated_text: As to why he was called <s>Kurubhaka</s>: because his father had said of him, 'Why is this boy a kurubhaka?'

children.text: vyāharanti sma taṃ paurās tataḥ kurubhakākhyayā ||
children.translated_text: thereafter the townsmen spoke of him by the name <s>Kurubhaka</s>.

children.text: athātīte kvacit kāle buddhivarmā rahaḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after some time had passed, <s>Buddhivarman</s>, sitting in private,
read a letter sent by <s>Sāgaradatta</s>.

children.text: sv asti rājagṛhe pūjyaṃ buddhavarmāṇam ūrjitam
children.translated_text: 'Hail! From <s>Ujjayinī</s>, <s>Sāgara</s>, embracing the venerable, prosperous <s>Buddhivarman</s>
in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, makes this known.
A daughter has been born to your friend, adorned with auspicious marks,

children.text: rūpeṇa sadṛśī yasyāḥ pramadā na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and no woman equal to her in beauty will exist.

children.text: tavāpi yadi bhāryāyāḥ putro jātaḥ śivaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: If a son has also been born to your wife, then all is well;

children.text: kanyā ced vāmaśīlena devena muṣitā vayam ||
children.translated_text: but if it is a daughter, we have been robbed by an ill-disposed god.

children.text: nirnimittāpi hi prītir yā na saṃbandhabṛṃhitā
children.translated_text: For even affection that has no cause, when strengthened by kinship,
attains firmness, like prosperity when energy is its protector.'

children.text: tataḥ satkṛtya taṃ dūtam apṛcchad gṛhiṇīṃ vaṇik
children.translated_text: Then the merchant, after honoring that messenger, asked his wife,

children.text: tasminn evaṃ gate kārye brūhi kiṃ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Since the matter has come to this, tell me: what should be done?'

children.text: tayoktaṃ dvyaṅgulaprajñā jānīyur vā striyaḥ kiyat
children.translated_text: She said, 'What much would women know, with wisdom only two fingers wide?

children.text: kiṃ tu pṛṣṭeti vakṣyāmi pṛṣṭadhṛṣṭā hi mādṛśī ||
children.translated_text: Still, since I have been asked, I will speak; women like me are bold when questioned.
Truth mixed with falsehood is the merchant's practice; traders should not abandon it.

children.text: sahajaṃ hi tyajan vṛttaṃ durvṛtta iti nindyate ||
children.translated_text: For one who abandons an inborn practice is censured as badly behaved.
A son, at least, has been born to you; where is the falsehood in that?

children.text: ye punas tasya doṣās tān mithyā bhaṇa guṇā iti ||
children.translated_text: As for his defects, falsely call them virtues.

children.text: ākhyāyante hi sarvārthāḥ kṛtrimair eva nāmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: For all things are described precisely by artificial names;

children.text: āhur madhurakaṃ kecit taṃ tādṛṅmārakaṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: some call that kind of death-dealing poison "sweet-maker."

children.text: kārye hi guruṇi prāpte mithyā satyam apīṣyate
children.translated_text: When a weighty matter has arisen, falsehood too is regarded as truth;

children.text: aśvatthāmā hato drauṇir ity ūce kiṃ na pāṇḍavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: did not the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> say, "<s>Aśvatthāman</s>, son of <s>Droṇa</s>, has been killed"?
Driven by greed for wealth, people like you enter the caustic ocean,
dreadful with the roar of Time, as though it were a lotus pond for sport.
The daughter of that lord of sea-merchants will not enter your house
without a heap of wealth, the very essence of the ocean.

children.text: tasmān mā smāvamanyadhvam adhanyair durlabhāṃ śriyam
children.translated_text: Therefore do not despise prosperity, hard for the unlucky to obtain,
attainable only through hundreds of painful efforts, as though it were not won with difficulty.'

children.text: ityādivacanaṃ tasyāḥ sūktam ity abhinandya saḥ
children.translated_text: Approving her words and the rest as well spoken,
he gave a message for <s>Sāgaradatta</s> in the messenger's presence:

children.text: vaktavyaḥ suhṛd asmākam asmākam api dārakaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Our friend should be told: to us too a boy

children.text: utpannas tādṛśo yasya kathitā katham ākṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been born, of such a kind that how could his appearance be described?

children.text: athavā ye guṇāḥ ke'pi tasya śārīramānasāḥ
children.translated_text: Or rather, whatever bodily and mental qualities he has,

children.text: svayam evāsi tān dṛṣṭā kiṃ nas taiḥ kathitair iti ||
children.translated_text: you yourself will see them; what need have we to describe them?'

children.text: ityādi bahu saṃkīrṇam asau saṃdiśya sādaram
children.translated_text: After respectfully sending many confused messages of this sort,
he dispatched the messenger, providing provisions for the road.
In this way eight years passed through exchanges of messengers;
then a messenger, speaking plainly, said to <s>Buddhivarman</s>:
'I have been told by <s>Sāgaradatta</s> together with his wife:

children.text: jāmātaram anālokya mā smāgacchad bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "Do not come without having seen the son-in-law."

children.text: tan mām ujjayanīṃ yūyaṃ yadi gacchantam icchatha
children.translated_text: Therefore, if you want me to go to <s>Ujjayinī</s>,

children.text: taṃ me dārakam ākhyāta tadīyāṃś ca guṇān iti ||
children.translated_text: tell me about that boy and about his qualities.'
But he, after considering for a moment, spoke with complete presence of mind:
'He is staying in his maternal uncle's house in <s>Tāmralipti</s>, studying.'
By this elaboration too four or five years went by;
then three or four messengers arrived, clever in speech.
Disregarding the hospitality shown to them, they said to <s>Buddhivarman</s>,

children.text: āha saṃbandhinī yat tvāṃ sadāraṃ tan niśāmyatām ||
children.translated_text: 'Listen to what your kinswoman by marriage says to you and your wife.
These thirteen or fourteen years have passed,

children.text: adyāpi ca na paśyāmo vayaṃ jāmātur ākṛtim ||
children.translated_text: and even today we do not see the son-in-law's appearance.
They say that buying and selling, sir, concern merchandise that has been seen;

children.text: iti lokapravādo 'yaṃ bhavatāpi na kiṃ śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: have you too not heard this common saying?

children.text: tvaṃ yac cāttha paṭhann āste tāmraliptyām asāv iti
children.translated_text: And as for what you say, that he is staying in <s>Tāmralipti</s> studying,

children.text: idam apy atidurbaddhaṃ savyājam iva vācakam ||
children.translated_text: this statement too is very badly put together and seems to be only a pretext.

children.text: yeṣāṃ karma ca vṛttiś ca vihite pāṭhapāṭhane
children.translated_text: Even for those whose duty and livelihood have been ordained as teaching and recitation,

children.text: teṣām api paricchinnaḥ pāṭhakālaḥ kiyān api ||
children.translated_text: the period of study is limited to some extent.
But that your son, abandoning every other activity,

children.text: paṭhatā sakalaṃ janma neyam ity asamañjasam ||
children.translated_text: should spend his whole life studying is unreasonable.
Therefore, abandoning this game, terrifying with <s>Yama</s>'s laughter,

children.text: atra vā tāmraliptyāṃ vā dārako darśyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: let the boy be shown, either here or in <s>Tāmralipti</s>.'

children.text: iti yāvad asau tāvat pūjyair viśramyatām iti
children.translated_text: When they had said this, he replied, 'Let my honorable guests rest for now,'

children.text: tān uktvā gṛhiṇīm ūce buddhavarmā sasaṃbhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Buddhivarman</s>, alarmed, said to his wife:
'Because I was foolish and did not consider the fault that would come later,
with my mind seized by vain hope, I followed a woman's advice.
Those defects of your son, such as being one-eyed and having protruding teeth:
after all this time, which one of them has disappeared?

children.text: vardhamāṇe śarīre hi nijā doṣāḥ śarīriṇām
children.translated_text: For when the body grows, the inborn defects of embodied beings
increase all the more, like the limbs of the body.
Therefore show the messengers your son, whose form is like that of an attendant of <s>Hara</s>.'
Or rather, let such a stratagem be devised by the learned man.

children.text: tayā coktaṃ mayopāyaḥ kīdṛśo 'py atra cintitaḥ
children.translated_text: And she said, "I have thought of some sort of stratagem here;

children.text: yady asau rocate tubhyaṃ tataḥ prastūyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: if it pleases you, then let it be set forth."

children.text: ucyatām iti tenoktā karṇe kimapi sābravīt
children.translated_text: When he said, "Let it be told," she whispered something in his ear.

children.text: so 'pi śobhanam ity uktvā tam upāyaṃ prayuktavān ||
children.translated_text: He too said, "Good," and put that stratagem into practice.
In private, he humbly petitioned a brahmin friend,
one who lived on gifts from him and was delighted by hundreds of affectionate words.
"What need is there to describe the qualities possessed by my son,

children.text: ākāraś ca prakāraś ca yādṛk kiṃ tasya kathyate ||
children.translated_text: who is famous as <s>Śvetakāka</s>, and what his appearance and character are like?

children.text: yac ca sāgaradattena mayā ca paribhāṣitam
children.translated_text: And what has been agreed upon by <s>Sāgaradatta</s> and me,
all that is known to you, along with the arrival of the messenger.

children.text: tena nas tena sauhārdaṃ suhṛdā sthiratāṃ naya
children.translated_text: Therefore bring our friendship with that friend to firmness.

children.text: athavā svārtha evāyaṃ tava dhiṅ māṃ mudhākulam ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, this is your own interest; shame on me, vainly confused as I am.

children.text: ya eṣa bhavataḥ putro yajñaguptaḥ surūpavān
children.translated_text: This son of yours, <s>Yajñagupta</s>, is handsome,
knows the truth of the Śruti, Smṛti, and the rest, and is skilled in the arts.
Let him marry <s>Sāgaradatta</s>'s daughter,
and, bringing just such a girl, let him give her to my son.

children.text: yac ca ratnasuvarṇādi lapsyate draviṇaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: And whatever wealth of jewels, gold, and the like is obtained from that,
a share of it will be yours." He was ashamed as he made this proposal.
When he had been addressed by him with such words and others like them, the brahmin, excited by greed for his own advantage,

children.text: abravīt tvadvidheyaiḥ kiṃ madvidhaiḥ prārthitair iti ||
children.translated_text: said, "What need have men like me for anything sought by men obedient to you?"
Then, summoning <s>Yajñagupta</s> in the presence of <s>Buddhavarman</s>,
his father made him hear this affair, which had already been secretly planned.
He said, "The words of elders, whether reasonable or otherwise,

children.text: śiśubhir na vicāryāṇi tasmād evaṃ bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: are not to be examined by children; therefore let it be so."
Then, after a few days had passed, <s>Yajñagupta</s>, adorned with his own ornaments,
was shown by <s>Buddhavarman</s> to the prospective relatives.

children.text: abravīc cāyam āyātas tāmraliptyāḥ sa dārakaḥ
children.translated_text: And he said, "This boy has come from <s>Tāmralipti</s>;

children.text: ākāraś ca guṇāś cāsya dṛśyantāṃ yādṛśā iti ||
children.translated_text: look at what his appearance and qualities are like."

children.text: tatas tair vismitair uktam anindyā kundamālikā
children.translated_text: Then those men, astonished, said, "Blameless <s>Kundamālikā</s>
will be united with this <s>Bālavasanta</s>.
It is pointless to investigate his qualities,
for such steadiness of appearance is not seen in men without qualities.

children.text: kiṃ tu nāmāsya duḥśliṣṭam ayaṃ kurubhakaḥ kila
children.translated_text: Only, his name is badly joined: this fellow is called <s>Kurubhaka</s>.
For the name 'crooked-palāśa' is not fitting for a <s>pārijāta</s> tree.

children.text: athavā duḥśravaṃ nāma śrūyate mahatām api
children.translated_text: Or rather, an unpleasant name is heard even among great beings:

children.text: kledur ity ucyate candro mātariśveti mārutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the moon is called 'moist-maker,' and the wind '<s>Mātariśvan</s>.'

children.text: na cāpi guṇavad vācya vācakaṃ paribhūyate
children.translated_text: Nor is a word that denotes something full of qualities despised because of the denoting word;
for it is because of the weakness of the support that what depends on it is despised.
In every way, since the caravan-leader's wife has today given birth,
the friendship between the two of you has become immutable as the summit.
Therefore, going very quickly, while she has abandoned sleep, food, and the rest,
we shall congratulate, by good fortune, the caravan-leader's wife.
And by you too, on an auspicious day, the wedding procession should be set in motion;

children.text: na hīdānīṃ vivāhasya kaścid asti vighātakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for now there is no obstacle at all to the marriage."

children.text: ity uktvā teṣu yāteṣu sāravatprābhṛteṣu saḥ
children.translated_text: When they, with substantial gifts, had spoken thus and departed,
he chose <s>Yajñagupta</s> as bridegroom and sent forth the wedding procession.

children.text: yo 'sau kurubhakas taṃ ca yajñaguptaṃ cakāra saḥ
children.translated_text: And that man made the fellow who was <s>Kurubhaka</s> into <s>Yajñagupta</s>;

children.text: saṃjñayā yajñaguptaṃ tu varaṃ kurubhakaṃ vaṇik ||
children.translated_text: but the merchant made the bridegroom <s>Yajñagupta</s> into <s>Kurubhaka</s> by name.
The merchant's son too, dressed in an assumed brahmin's outfit and wearing a gold ring of measured weight,
was there as the bridegroom's companion.
After a long time the wedding procession reached the city of <s>Avanti</s>,
like <s>Yakṣasena</s>'s <s>Alakā</s>, with the story of the beloved one longed for.
It stayed in the lodging for the bridal party set up on the bank of the <s>Śiprā</s>,
delightful with gardens whose beauty had been brought by spring.
That day, lines of townspeople, curious and with eyes unsated,
looked at the bridegroom, making even great <s>Mahākāla</s> seem like straw.
And he passed some time with rogues of <s>Ujjayinī</s>, scholars clever in crooked speech,
and with men skilled in flute and lute.
Then he was addressed by his brother-in-law, who had put on ceremonial food and ornaments:

children.text: sajjaṃ vaḥ pānam annaṃ ca kim ādhve bhujyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Drink and food are ready for you. Why should they be eaten on the road?"
Looking at a single dining platform with many seats,

children.text: kena kenātra bhoktavyam iti syālakam uktavān ||
children.translated_text: he said to the brother-in-law, "By whom is each place here to be occupied for eating?"
He replied, "This middle seat, with golden frame, high coral legs,
and fine covering, is to be occupied by you.

children.text: ye caite dattavetrāṅge yuṣmān ubhayataḥ same
children.translated_text: And these equal seats on both sides of you, fitted with cane arms,
are for your elder and younger brothers-in-law to occupy.
As for the long row of seats on both sides,
the rest of the line of brothers-in-law is to sit there beside you."

children.text: varas tu kṣaṇam avyūha syālam etad abhāṣata
children.translated_text: But the bridegroom, after delaying for a moment, said this to the brother-in-law:

children.text: asmābhiḥ saha yuṣmābhir na kāryaṃ pānabhojanam ||
children.translated_text: "There must be no drinking or eating by us together with you.

children.text: gotrācāro 'yam asmākaṃ tāvat pānaṃ na sevyate
children.translated_text: This is our family custom: drinking is not enjoyed,

children.text: bhujyate vāparaiḥ sārdhaṃ yāvan na pariṇīyate ||
children.translated_text: nor is food eaten together with others until the marriage has been completed.
After I have married, returned, and properly obtained my father's permission,

children.text: kāryam etan na vā kāryaṃ vinādeśād guror iti ||
children.translated_text: this may be done or may not be done; without the elder's order, it is not to be done."

children.text: evaṃ nāmety anujñātaḥ śvaśureṇa varaḥ pṛthak
children.translated_text: When his father-in-law allowed him, saying, "So indeed let it be," the bridegroom, separately,
with the affinal relatives made downcast, took purified food.
And when a watch of the night had passed, with the circle of instruments roaring,
He went to the house of <s>Sāgaradatta</s> in order to marry.
There he took the bride's hand, gleaming like gold,
and, remembering his teacher's words, the steadfast groom kept his hand unchanged.
But there, after walking around the fire, he was allegedly seized by a fierce colic,

children.text: pāṇibhyām udaraṃ dhṛtvā mumoha ca papāta ca ||
children.translated_text: and, holding his belly with both hands, he fainted and fell down.
When his inhaling and exhaling had grown still and his eyes were closed,
a great wailing broke out, making even the bold leaders speechless.
Then his mother-in-law, seeing her son-in-law and beating her breast and head,
cried loudly to <s>Kundamālikā</s>, who was in the same condition as her husband:

children.text: hā hatāsi vinaṣṭāsi dhik tvāṃ pracchannarākṣasīm
children.translated_text: "Ah, you are slain, you are ruined! Shame on you, hidden demoness,
by whom this husband, whose beauty surpassed <s>Pradyumna</s>'s, has been destroyed!

children.text: tvam eva na mṛtā kasmād ahaṃ vā duḥkhabhāginī
children.translated_text: Why did you yourself not die, or I, the wretched sharer of grief,

children.text: yayā tvaṃ sakalaṃ janma draṣṭavyāmṛtayā mṛtā ||
children.translated_text: since, while still alive to be seen, you have died for your whole life?

children.text: kathaṃ jīvati sā yā strī bālaiva mṛtabhartṛkā
children.translated_text: How can a woman live who, while still a girl, has a dead husband?
For to women a husband is far weightier than life itself.

children.text: yā ca mātā sutām iṣṭāṃ cārutāśīlaśālinīm
children.translated_text: And the mother who can look upon her beloved daughter, endowed with beauty and good conduct,

children.text: śaktā vidhavikāṃ draṣṭuṃ jyeṣṭhā kālasya sā svasā ||
children.translated_text: as a widow, is the elder sister of Death."

children.text: ityādi vilapanty eva sā ca niśceṣṭanābhavat
children.translated_text: Even as she was lamenting in this way, she too became motionless,
while the place between the son-in-law's heart and belly slowly began to throb.
Then, when the son-in-law had become like that, for the crowd of townspeople
there was no break in the air between joyful laughter and loud guffaws.
Slowly he breathed out, and with lashes trembling askew
he opened his reddish eyes with their heavy pupils.
Then <s>Sāgaradatta</s> held such a great festival
as would be hard even for a king, like an old man who has obtained a son.

children.text: kim etad iti pṛṣṭaś ca sa vaidyaiḥ pratyuvāca tān
children.translated_text: When the physicians asked him, "What is this?" he answered them,

children.text: āmāśayagataṃ śūlaṃ bādhate guru mām iti ||
children.translated_text: "A terrible colic lodged in my stomach is tormenting me."
Then the attentive physicians, while the son-in-law stayed in the bridal chamber,
treated the colic whose cause was undigested matter.
As he was being tormented by pains, and at intervals finding sleep,
the night somehow passed for his little bride, who stayed awake.
Made to fast by drinking decoctions of dry ginger, ativiṣā, and musta,
and taking very little food without fat, he became thinner every day.
<s>Kundamālikā</s> herself busied herself with grinding medicines and the like,
as if, distressed by fear for her husband's illness, she had forgotten bridal modesty.

children.text: tataḥ patim upāsīnāṃ sa kubjaḥ kundamālikām
children.translated_text: Then that hunchback, while <s>Kundamālikā</s> was sitting beside her husband,
touched her limbs in jest, making her body shrink with fear, as it were.

children.text: abravīc ca vimuñcainaṃ kirāṭam apaṭuṃ viṭam
children.translated_text: And he said, "Leave this Kirāta, this inept libertine;

children.text: devatāgurubhir dattaṃ kāntaṃ toṣaya mām iti ||
children.translated_text: satisfy me, your lover given by gods and teachers."
Then the bride, rising from that place and offended at her husband's bedside,

children.text: keyaṃ kelir anāryeti vadhūr bhartāram abravīt ||
children.translated_text: said to her husband, "What kind of jest is this, ignoble man?"

children.text: sa tāṃ sasmitam āha sma mā sma grāmeyikā bhava
children.translated_text: He said to her with a smile, "Do not be rustic.

children.text: kā hi nāgarikaṃmanyā hāsyāt naṭabaṭos traset ||
children.translated_text: What woman who thinks herself refined would be frightened by the joke of an actor-boy?
Such petty men among the wealthy generally bear the fruit of chatter;

children.text: na hi mūkaṃ śukaṃ kaścic ciraṃ dharati pañjare ||
children.translated_text: for no one keeps a mute parrot long in a cage.
Therefore, timid girl, do not be frightened by this toy,

children.text: hasataḥ spṛśataś cāṅgaṃ bhīru mā vitrasīr iti ||
children.translated_text: babbling incoherently, laughing, and touching your body."
Although instructed by him in this way, she, born in a family of good conduct,
harshly rebuked him as a man used by fierce slave-girls at the water jars.

children.text: āsīc ca yajñaguptasya yāvad evaiṣa mūḍhakaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Yajñagupta</s> thought, "Only so long as this little fool

children.text: rahasyaṃ na bhinatty etat tāvan nyāyyam ito gatam ||
children.translated_text: does not break this secret is it proper to leave from here."
At some point the physicians, their treatments fruitless, asked him,
"What does your honor desire in drink, food, and recreation?"

children.text: tataḥ kṣāmatarālāpas tān avocac cirād asau
children.translated_text: Then, after a long time, he spoke to them in a very weak voice:

children.text: pitarau draṣṭum icchāmi priyaputrau priyāv iti ||
children.translated_text: "I wish to see my parents, dear to their dear son."
Then the physicians reported this to <s>Sāgaradatta</s>:

children.text: evaṃ vadati jāmātā tac ca pratividhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: "Your son-in-law speaks in this way; let this be attended to.
Whatever treatment of the stomach a physician ought to perform,

children.text: kṛtam apy akṛtaṃ tat tad etasmiñ jātam āture ||
children.translated_text: all that, though done, has become as good as undone in this sick man.

children.text: svadeśāya tu yāto 'yaṃ bhaved api nirāmayaḥ
children.translated_text: But if he went to his own country, he might even become free of illness;
for seeing one's friends is a medicine whose success is famous in the world."
With a host of attendants headed by a nurse, with wealth, necklaces, and a great herd of camels,

children.text: śyāmāṃ niśām iva kṛśena tuṣārabhāsā prāsthāpayat saha vareṇa vaṇiktanūjām ||
children.translated_text: he sent the merchant's daughter off with the groom, like dark night accompanied by a thin moon.

children.text: prayāṇakaiś ca yāvadbhir agād rājagṛhaṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: For as many stages as the groom was to go to <s>Rājagṛha</s>,

children.text: śreṣṭhī ca dviguṇān prītān prāhiṇot paricārakān ||
children.translated_text: the merchant sent twice as many devoted attendants.
And he told them, "From each stage of the journey, two by two of you

children.text: nivartitavyaṃ yuṣmābhir iti cāsāv uvāca tān ||
children.translated_text: must turn back with news of the son-in-law."

children.text: prathamād vāsakād yau ca nivṛttau paricārakau
children.translated_text: The two attendants who returned from the first lodging-place

children.text: śreṣṭhine kathitaṃ tābhyāṃ varaḥ svastho manāg iti ||
children.translated_text: reported to the merchant, "The groom is somewhat well."

children.text: yathā yathā ca yāti sma vāsakān uttarottarān
children.translated_text: And as he went on to successive lodging-places, one after another,

children.text: śanakaiḥ śanakair māndyam atyajat sa tathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: little by little he left his illness behind in just that way.
From another lodging-place, two other attendants turned back
and told <s>Sāgaradatta</s> that the groom's body was cheerful and strong.
Then he, blinded by joy and neglecting to examine the recipients,
distributed treasures even to everyone from four-Veda brahmins down to caṇḍālas.
But in the morning the counterfeit groom abandoned the pomp of being a son-in-law.
Having assumed the appearance of a brahmin, he set out on foot along the road.

children.text: vaiṣeṇāgantunā muktaḥ sa reje nijayā śriyā
children.translated_text: Released by the visiting <s>Vaiṣeṇa</s>, he shone with his own splendor,
like the moon freed from a cloud garlanded with Indra's bow and lightning.
And that excellent conveyance, occupied by <s>Kundamālikā</s>,
the wicked <s>Kurubhaka</s>, of fine appearance, mounted with delight.
Seeing him, misshapen in form and surpassing the attendants of <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
the bride shook her body and closed both her eyes.
Then the whole eager crowd, abandoning its duties,
hurried out from the city to see the bride and groom.
And when the townspeople saw those two joined in such an ill-fastened bond, like a pearl and an iron ball,
they waved their hands and abused <s>Prajāpati</s>.
"Even <s>Kāma</s>, acting as he pleases, is still not to be praised so much;

children.text: kiṃ punar yaḥ sadācāraḥ sargahetur bhavādṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how much less one such as you, whose proper conduct is the cause of creation.
In every way, you alone are the supreme lord of those whose nature is perverse,
since you have joined these two hard-to-join beings, an apsaras and a ghost."
<s>Buddhavarmā</s> too went out, preceded by all the guilds,
and brought the bride home to a house whose beauty surpassed the royal palace.
There, with the little bride on his lap, he said to his wife:

children.text: iyam evāstu te putras tanayā ca vadhūr iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let this very girl be your son, your daughter, and your daughter-in-law."
While honors were being paid, bards were offering praise,

children.text: naṭādiṣu ca nṛtyatsu sārkaṃ tad agamad dinam ||
children.translated_text: and actors and others were dancing, that day passed together with the sun.
Then <s>Kundamālikā</s> entered an eye- and mind-delighting residence
together with the hunchback, <s>Yajñagupta</s>'s friend.
There the bride took a decorated seat set near the bed,
and the groom's friend too took the next one, a raised seat.
Then all those people there, their minds blinded by confusion,
bent their faces down and wrote leaves from bottom to top.
In this painful situation <s>Kundamālikā</s> thought:

children.text: api nāmaiṣa māṃ muktvā brāhmaṇo na vrajed iti ||
children.translated_text: "May this brahmin not leave me and go away."
But <s>Kurubhaka</s>, wishing to sport in private, also thought:

children.text: api nāmaiṣa niryāyād bahir vāsagṛhād iti ||
children.translated_text: "May this man go out of the bridal chamber."

children.text: yajñaguptas tayor buddhvā tat kālocitam iṅgitam
children.translated_text: <s>Yajñagupta</s>, understanding the timely signals of those two

children.text: gamanaṃ cātmanaḥ śreyas tato nirgantum aihata ||
children.translated_text: and that departure was best for himself, then tried to go out.

children.text: sā tam ucchalitaṃ dṛṣṭvā saviṣādam abhāṣata
children.translated_text: Seeing him spring up, she spoke to him sorrowfully:

children.text: dārān āpadgatān muktvā prasthitaḥ kva bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "Where are you going, leaving your wife fallen into distress?"

children.text: tenoktaṃ yasya dārās tvaṃ vidhātrā parikalpitā
children.translated_text: He said, "You are the wife whom the creator has assigned to him.

children.text: āpannāsmīti mā vocas tiṣṭhantī tasya saṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: Do not say, 'I am in distress,' while you are standing in his presence.
So let him enjoy the embrace and kisses that come from you.
We, however, are donkey-natured, entitled only to the burden."

children.text: ittham uktvā sa cānyābhiḥ preṣyābhiḥ saha niryayau
children.translated_text: After saying this, he went out with the other maidservants,

children.text: anicchām aicchad ākraṣṭuṃ grāmyaḥ kurubhakaś ca tām ||
children.translated_text: and the vulgar <s>Kurubhaka</s> tried to drag her, unwilling, toward himself.
Then, with the louder and louder jingling of her hip and foot ornaments,

children.text: vyāharantīva taṃ vipraṃ nirjagāma javena sā ||
children.translated_text: as if calling out to that brahmin, she quickly went out.
But in the house courtyard, crowded with drunken and excited townspeople and dancing servants,

children.text: yajñaguptas tayā naiva dṛṣṭas tatra gṛhāṅgaṇe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yajñagupta</s> was not seen by her at all.
Deceived by the mistaken resemblance, thinking "This is he, this is he going,"

children.text: yaṃ kaṃcid api sā yāntam anvayāsīt tadāśayā ||
children.translated_text: she followed anyone at all who was going, with the same intention.
And, rushing out impetuously, she descended onto the street road;
frightened by the noise of the hiṇḍī instrument, she went to a potter's hut.
There she saw a Kāpālika fast asleep in a stupor from liquor,

children.text: suśliṣṭā hanta rakṣeyam ity adhyavasitaṃ tayā ||
children.translated_text: and decided, "Ah, if I cling closely to this, I will be saved."
Then she removed the very valuable ornaments from her body,
and, practiced in merchants' habits, tied them tightly in her garment.
Taking the skull-staff and the other equipment of the Kāpālika,

children.text: ghūrṇamānā madād grāmaṃ bāhyaṃ niragamat purāt ||
children.translated_text: staggering as if from drink, she went out of the city to the outer village.

children.text: tatra ca brāhmaṇī kācit tayā śvetaśiroruhā
children.translated_text: There she saw a certain brahmin woman, white-haired,
sitting on the veranda of her own house and cutting cotton.

children.text: ekākiny eva sā daivaṃ ninditvā karuṇasvanā
children.translated_text: Alone there, with a pitiful voice, after blaming fate,

children.text: dhik kṣudraṃ buddhavarmāṇam iti sakrodham abravīt ||
children.translated_text: the woman angrily said, "Shame on the vile <s>Buddhavarmā</s>!"
She asked her, "Noble lady, what evil deed belongs to that man,

children.text: sādhoḥ kiṃ duṣkṛtaṃ tasya nindyate yad asāv iti ||
children.translated_text: a good man rich in sincere virtues, that he is being blamed?"

children.text: tayoktam atimugdho vā dhūrto vā bhagavann asi
children.translated_text: The woman replied, "Reverend sir, you are either very naive or a rogue,

children.text: tadīyaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ yena prakāśam api na śrutam ||
children.translated_text: since you have not heard even openly of his evil deed.

children.text: athavā śroṣyati bhavān anyatas tat suduḥśravam
children.translated_text: Or rather, you will hear from someone else that most painful thing to hear;

children.text: mādṛśī tu na śaktaiva vaktuṃ prakṛtikātarā ||
children.translated_text: but one like me, timid by nature, is not able to tell it."

children.text: yāvac cedam asāv āha tāvad uccaistarāṃ pure
children.translated_text: While she was saying this, at that very moment throughout the city
a proclamation, broken by the high sound of a drum, went around:
"Ah! By the king's command, whatever townsman reports

children.text: nāgaraḥ kaścid ācaṣṭe sa dāridryeṇa mucyate ||
children.translated_text: the bride of <s>Buddhavarmā</s> shall be released from poverty.

children.text: yaḥ punaḥ svagṛhe mohāt pracchādayati taṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: But whoever, through folly, hides her in his own house,

children.text: pāṭayaty adhanaṃ kṛtvā dāruṇaiḥ krakacair iti ||
children.translated_text: the king will make him penniless and have him split with cruel saws."
Then, hearing this, the brahmin woman, her face flooded with tears,
overcome with delight, both laughed and wept.

children.text: abravīc ca kim āścaryaṃ yad ujjayaniko janaḥ
children.translated_text: And she said, "What wonder is it that the people of <s>Ujjayinī</s>
are not deceived by rogues equal to <s>Mūladeva</s>?
Well done, well done, most wise and well-born <s>Kundamālikā</s>,
by whom the wicked <s>Buddhavarmā</s> has been deceived together with the hunchback.

children.text: yathā rājagṛhaṃ putri tvayedaṃ sukham āsitam
children.translated_text: Just as, my daughter, this royal residence has been happily occupied by you,
Having met with <s>Yajñagupta</s>, you too should remain there in that same way."

children.text: ityādi bruvatīṃ śrutvā cintayāmāsa tām asau
children.translated_text: Hearing her say this and more, the woman thought of her:
"This is a mother to me without cause; she will protect me."

children.text: śanaiś cākathayat tasyai vṛttaṃ vṛttāntam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: And little by little she told her the true account of what had happened to herself.

children.text: gāḍham āliṅgya sā caināṃ prītā prāveśayad gṛham ||
children.translated_text: The other woman, delighted, embraced her tightly and brought her into the house.
There she removed from her that <s>Kāpālika</s> bundle,
and massaged her limbs, which were wearied by its weight.

children.text: abhyajya snapayitvā ca sukhoṣṇaiḥ salilair asau
children.translated_text: After anointing her and bathing her with pleasantly warm water,
she placed her on a bed spread with broad pieces of cloth.

children.text: paridhāya ca tām eva bībhatsām asthiśṛṅkhalām
children.translated_text: Then, putting on that very same grisly chain of bones,

children.text: bhrāmyatsaṃbhrāntapauraṃ tat sā prātaḥ prāviśat puram ||
children.translated_text: she entered the city in the morning, where the townspeople were wandering about in confusion.
"Why are these people moving about in such agitation?"
she asked a certain inhabitant of the city.

children.text: tenoktam iha ca sthāne śreṣṭhino buddhavarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "Here, in this place, the merchant <s>Buddhavarman</s>
has a son named <s>Kurubhaka</s>, whose appearance belies his own name.
For him, by another impotent twice-born man,
