greedy like an actor, his own wife was handed over after marriage.

children.text: sā taṃ kurubhakaṃ tyaktvā mārgayantī ca taṃ dvijam
children.translated_text: She abandoned that <s>Kurubhaka</s> and, searching for that Brahmin,

children.text: pradoṣe kvāpy apakrāntā lokas tenāyam ākulaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went away somewhere at dusk. For that reason these people are disturbed."
Then, after hearing this from him, she said with a smile inside,

children.text: bhadra ṣaṇḍhasya tasyāśu gṛhaṃ nayata mām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Good sir, take me quickly to that eunuch's house."
Then, preceded by townspeople won over by her sweet speech,
she reached <s>Yajñagupta</s>'s house, adorned with the sound of Brahmins.
There, at the door of the fire-room, surrounded by the activity of exposition,
she saw <s>Yajñagupta</s> sitting with his pupils.
Then, setting down her <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> and arranging herself in the <s>svastika</s> posture,

children.text: ko 'yaṃ vyākhyāyate grantha ity apṛcchat samatsarā ||
children.translated_text: she asked, with indignation, "What text is being expounded here?"
He replied, "Venerable one, this is the <s>Mānava Dharma-saṃhitā</s>;
in it the four <s>āśramas</s> and the four <s>varṇas</s> are described."

children.text: tayoktaṃ kim alīkena na hīyaṃ dharmasaṃhitā
children.translated_text: She said, "Why this falsehood? This is certainly no <s>dharma-saṃhitā</s>.
I think this is <s>Lokāyata</s>, dear to unrestrained people.
What has a <s>dharma-saṃhitā</s> to do with this unrighteous conduct of yours?

children.text: na hi vaidyaḥ svaśāstrajñaḥ kuṣṭhī māṃsaṃ niṣevate ||
children.translated_text: A physician who knows his own science does not consume the flesh of a leper.
While expounding the <s>Mānava Dharma-saṃhitā</s> as a Brahmin,
you married off a bride in violation of proper sameness of caste.
And she, sound in body, beautiful, skilled in the arts,
and young, was given, they say, to a one-eyed, crippled bedbug.

children.text: tan māheśvara pṛcchāmi kim artham idam īdṛśam
children.translated_text: So, <s>Māheśvara</s>, I ask: for what reason

children.text: tvayā kṛtam akartavyaṃ yuktaṃ cet kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: was such an act, not to be done, done by you? If it is proper, say so."

children.text: so 'bravīd bhagavan yuktam ayuktaṃ vā bhavatv idam
children.translated_text: He said, "Venerable one, whether this is proper or improper,
it was carried out by obedient people because the guru's command had authority that could not be altered.

children.text: tathā hi jāmadagnyena durlaṅghyād vacanāt pituḥ
children.translated_text: For in the same way <s>Jāmadagnya</s>, because of his father's command, hard to transgress,

children.text: mātuḥ kṛttaṃ śiras tatra kim āha bhagavān iti ||
children.translated_text: cut off his mother's head. What does Your Reverence say about that?"
She said, "Events belonging to divine beings are not an example for one who is not divine.

children.text: na hi rudreṇa pīteti pibanti brāhmaṇāḥ surām ||
children.translated_text: Brahmins do not drink liquor because <s>Rudra</s> drank it.

children.text: na ca prājñena kartavyaṃ sarvam eva guror vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor should a wise man do absolutely every word of a guru.

children.text: guruḥ kiṃ nāma na brūyād duḥkhakrodhādibādhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What indeed might a guru not say when oppressed by pain, anger, and the like?
If a father, his head tormented by sharp pain, should say to his son,

children.text: śiro me chinddhi putreti kiṃ kāryaṃ tena tat tathā ||
children.translated_text: 'Cut off my head, my son,' should that be done by him just so?

children.text: yac ca mātuḥ śiraḥ kṛttaṃ rāmeṇa vacanāt pituḥ
children.translated_text: And as for his mother's head being cut off by <s>Rāma</s> at his father's command,

children.text: tat tasyaiva prabhāvena sadyaḥ saṃghaṭitaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: through his own divine power it was immediately joined together again.
But you, lacking divine power, have done an improper deed
at a guru's command; how can that be made otherwise?

children.text: idānīm api tām eva bhavān vineṣyati priyām
children.translated_text: Even now you must bring back that beloved woman herself.

children.text: guruvākyaṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ yad gataṃ gatam eva tat ||
children.translated_text: The guru's command was fulfilled before; what is past is simply past."
When she had spoken these words, he sat without an answer.

children.text: vādivācye hi nirdoṣe kiṃ vācyaṃ prativādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when the speaker's statement is faultless, what can the opponent say?

children.text: evaṃ ca ciram āsitvā nabhomadhyagate ravau
children.translated_text: And after remaining thus for a long time, when the sun had reached mid-sky,
she took leave of him on the pretext that it was time for alms and departed.

children.text: tena coktā svam evedam ṛddhimac ca gṛhaṃ tava
children.translated_text: And he said to her, "This very prosperous house is your own;
therefore let Your Reverence always take food here."
Then she laughed and said, "The food of an atheist such as you
is unfit for sharing, because it is not to be eaten even by <s>Kāpālikas</s>.

children.text: kṛtvāpi tu mahat pāpaṃ paścāt tāpaṃ karoti yaḥ
children.translated_text: But one who, even after committing a great sin, feels remorse afterward
and undertakes restraint again attains the state of one whose food may be eaten."

children.text: evamādi tam uktvāsau gatvā ca brāhmaṇīgṛham
children.translated_text: After saying this and the like to him, she went to the old Brahmin woman's house,

children.text: apanīya ca taṃ veṣam ācaran majjanādikam ||
children.translated_text: removed that costume, and performed bathing and the other rites.

children.text: taṃ ca kāpālikaṃ kalpaṃ sāyam ādāya sā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then in the evening, taking up that <s>Kāpālika</s> equipment again,
she went to <s>Yajñagupta</s>'s house and passed the rest of the day.

children.text: annakālaṃ ca rātriṃ ca nayantī brāhmaṇīgṛhe
children.translated_text: Passing mealtime and the night in the old Brahmin woman's house,

children.text: śeṣaṃ ca yajñaguptasya sānayad divasān bahūn ||
children.translated_text: she spent the remainder of many days at <s>Yajñagupta</s>'s.
Once, when her mind had come under the sway of longing, she thought:

children.text: akāryam idam etena kṛtaṃ karma dvijanmanā ||
children.translated_text: "This improper deed was done by this twice-born man.
Because of that, he can be led by me if desire is displayed;

children.text: kārye hi sulabhopāye na muhyanti sumedhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the wise are not bewildered when the means to their aim is easy.
Then a single pearl necklace, red with trembling rays,
she caused to be sold by that old Brahmin woman.
And gold and silver equal to that value, pure, coined and uncoined,
had been placed by her in a pair of copper jars and deposited at the boundary.
Then, after remaining for a long time in conversation based on the lore of alchemical operations and the lore of hidden treasures,
she addressed <s>Yajñagupta</s>.

children.text: ekarātraṃ vased grāme pañcarātraṃ muniḥ pure
children.translated_text: "A sage should stay one night in a village and five nights in a city:

children.text: iti pravrajitācāram etaṃ veda bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: you know this as the conduct of one who has gone forth.

children.text: etāvantam ahaṃ kālaṃ vatsa rājagṛhe sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: For so long a time, my child, I have stayed in <s>Rājagṛha</s>;
therefore, having abandoned the conduct of renunciation, I have been cheated of joy.
For even householders sink when bound by the chain of attachment;
what then of seekers of release, detached and free from attachment even to their own bodies?

children.text: tena vārāṇasīṃ gantum aham icchāmi saṃprati
children.translated_text: Therefore I now wish to go to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>;
for followers of the <s>Somasiddhānta</s> depend upon seeing holy bathing places.
And further, I know a remedy for the disease of poverty,
an āgama (esoteric scripture) for digging up treasures, called the <s>Mahākālamata</s>.
And while I, wearied by meditation, was wandering about at the edge of the forest,

children.text: ujjvalair lakṣitaś cihnaiḥ kenāpi nihito nidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: a treasure deposited by someone was indicated by bright signs.

children.text: yadi cāsti mayi prītis tataḥ svīkriyatām asau
children.translated_text: If you have affection for me, then let that treasure be accepted;

children.text: saphalāḥ khalu saṃparkāḥ sādhubhis tvādṛśair iti ||
children.translated_text: for contacts with good men such as you are indeed fruitful."

children.text: yajñaguptas tam utkhāya nidhiṃ tatsahitas tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yajñagupta</s>, having dug up that treasure together with her,
brought it secretly home, accompanied by a steadfast and very trusted disciple.

children.text: tatra pitre nidhānaṃ tat prītaḥ kathitavān asau
children.translated_text: There, delighted, he told his father about that treasure
and about that <s>Kāpālika</s>'s knowledge of the <s>Mahākālamata</s>.

children.text: tam uvāca pitā putraṃ tyaktvā vedān anarthakān
children.translated_text: His father said to him, his son, "Abandon the useless Vedas;
study the great knowledge of the great mendicant, the <s>Mahākālamata</s>.

children.text: divyaṃ cakṣur idaṃ tāta mahākālamataṃ matam
children.translated_text: This <s>Mahākālamata</s>, dear boy, is considered a divine eye,

children.text: nidhigarbhāṃ naro yena chidrāṃ paśyati medinīm ||
children.translated_text: by which a man sees the earth, pregnant with treasures, as though pierced with openings.
Therefore that great <s>Pāśupata</s>, like <s>Mahākāla</s>,
must be carefully propitiated by you for the sake of the <s>Mahākālamata</s>."
Encouraged thus by him, who desired the <s>Mahākālamata</s>,
<s>Yajñagupta</s> spoke to <s>Kundamālikā</s> as she was setting out:

children.text: aham apy anugacchāmi bhavantaṃ tīrtham asthiram
children.translated_text: "I too will follow you, revered sir, on this uncertain pilgrimage,
for it is a cause of great visible and invisible welfare for people like me."
Although she tried to restrain him with words of feeble effort,
he, longing for the <s>Mahākālamata</s>, did not turn back at all.

children.text: atha vārāṇasīṃ gatvā yajñaguptāya sā dadau
children.translated_text: Then, having gone to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, she gave <s>Yajñagupta</s>
a jewel of no very great value and said this to him:
"With the price of this jewel, live here as comfortably as you wish,

children.text: na tu tāruṇyamūḍhena saṃbhāṣyā gaṇikā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: but, bewildered by youth, you must not converse with a courtesan.
A śrotriya (learned brahmin) like you, about nineteen years old and curious,
if controlled by prostitutes, surely falls into subjection even with respect to his own wives.
And when all the blood of his limbs has been drunk by courtesan-ḍākinīs,

children.text: yaj jīvati tad āścaryaṃ kva dharmaḥ kva yaśaḥsukhe ||
children.translated_text: that he lives is a wonder; where then are dharma, fame, and happiness?"

children.text: ityādim ādeśam asau tadīyaṃ tathety anujñāya tathā cakāra
children.translated_text: Accepting this and the rest of her instruction with "So be it," he acted accordingly;

children.text: ārādhyavākyāni hi bhūtikāmāḥ sevāvidhijñā na vikalpayanti ||
children.translated_text: for those who desire prosperity and know the rule of service do not question the words of those who are to be honored.

children.text: caturaḥ pañca vā māsān vārāṇasyāṃ vihṛtya tau
children.translated_text: After the two had stayed four or five months in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,

children.text: naimiṣaṃ jagmatus tasmād gaṅgādvāraṃ tataḥ kurūn ||
children.translated_text: they went from there to <s>Naimiṣa</s>, then to <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>, and then to the <s>Kurus</s>.
From the <s>Kurus</s> they went to <s>Puṣkara</s>; having spent the rainy season there,
at the end of <s>Kārttika</s> they saw the very holy <s>Mahālaya</s>.
Then one day <s>Kundamālikā</s> said to <s>Yajñagupta</s>,
"After obtaining much wealth, I shall give you a treasure.
Take it and go home; it accomplishes both visible and invisible ends.
For householders who keep a household are joined to the three aims of life.
The foolish, who have not heard scripture, and widowers, or even those without wealth,
are indeed devoted to pilgrimage for the sake of dharma.

children.text: aham apy adhunā gacchāmy avantinagarīṃ prati
children.translated_text: I too now am going toward the city of <s>Avanti</s>,
for it is a mine of <s>Kāpālikas</s>, as of courtesans.
There the great <s>Pāśupatas</s>, with whetted, sharp spears,
are said to fight during the pilgrimage, having fighting alone as their purpose.

children.text: tatra kāpālikaḥ kaścin nihanyād api māṃ balī
children.translated_text: There some strong <s>Kāpālika</s> might even kill me;
for those who move within a cage of weapons escape only by the accident of crow and palm fruit.

children.text: ujjayanyāṃ ca yat pāpaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtavān asi
children.translated_text: And because of the sin, the evil deed, that you committed in <s>Ujjayinī</s>,

children.text: svargavad brahmaghātena tena sā durgamā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: that city is hard for you to approach, like heaven for one who has killed a brahmin.
Therefore I suspect that your going there would bring toil without fruit;

children.text: prāvṛtya ca tataḥ paśya sanidhiḥ pitarāv iti ||
children.translated_text: return from there, and then, with the treasure, see your parents."

children.text: āsīc cāsya prasannau me pādāv asya mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: And he thought, "The feet of this great-souled one are gracious to me;
ah, now I have obtained the <s>Mahākālamata</s>.
For a person in danger of life gives up, for the sake of preserving life,

children.text: sarvam apy ujhati sphītaṃ kimu grantham anarthakam ||
children.translated_text: everything, even if abundant; how much more a useless book?
And this man, indifferent to his own life, has long been honored by me;

children.text: mahākālamataṃ tan me kathaṃ nāma na dāsyati ||
children.translated_text: how indeed could he fail to give me that <s>Mahākālamata</s>?

children.text: yaṃ ca doṣam ahaṃ tatra kṛtavān guruśāsanāt
children.translated_text: And as for the fault that I committed there by the command of my teacher,

children.text: tasya pracchādanopāyo yat kiṃcid iva tucchakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: some slight means of concealing it is quite trivial.
No one will notice me hiding in temple corners, a black-cloaked wanderer,
with rough and tangled hair."
Having resolved, "That is proper," and so forth, he said to <s>Kundamālikā</s>,

children.text: kiṃ cāntevāsināṃ yuktaṃ moktum ācāryam āpadi ||
children.translated_text: "And is it right for disciples to abandon their teacher in distress?

children.text: yā gatir bhavataḥ saiva mamāpi sahacāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever course is yours, that same course is mine too, as your companion."

children.text: na hi gacchati pūrṇendau kalaṅko 'sya na gacchati ||
children.translated_text: For the blemish on the full moon does not pass away; this man's blemish does not pass away.
As he spoke such charming words, her mind filled with delight,
<s>Kundamālikā</s> gave him permission to go.
Then, after going to the city of <s>Avanti</s>, she said to <s>Yajñagupta</s>,
"Good sir, here at <s>Bhadravaṭa</s> relieve the fatigue of the road.

children.text: āgacchāmi nidhiṃ dṛṣṭvā nihitaṃ kenacit kvacit
children.translated_text: I shall come back after seeing a treasure deposited somewhere by someone.

children.text: yāvat tāvat tvayotkaṇṭhā na kāryā mām apaśyatā ||
children.translated_text: Until then you must not feel longing while you do not see me.
Since treasures are hard to find in <s>Ujjayinī</s> here and there,

children.text: āśaṅke ciram ātmānaṃ paribhrāntam itas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I suspect that I may wander a long time from place to place.
Whether they have long life and children, or even fathers, or not, all alike,

children.text: na hy aujjayanakāḥ paurāḥ sthirān nidadhate nidhīn ||
children.translated_text: the citizens of <s>Ujjayinī</s> do not lay down lasting treasures."
Having said such things to him, she went to the bank of the river <s>Śiprā</s>,
cast off her <s>kāpālika</s> (skull-bearing ascetic) attire, and made her body spotless.
Dressed in garments white as jasmine and adorned with conch-shell and crystal,
she shone like an autumn sky thronged with moonlight and stars.
With her breasts splitting a necklace of varied color at her throat,
and with a gourd set in a net-sling and a begging-bowl, she set out.
Then drunken <s>kāpālikas</s>, drinking as they sat in a circle,
called out loudly to her with hands whose fingers were crooked.

children.text: ehy ehi taralāpāṅgi yas te kāpālikaḥ priyaḥ
children.translated_text: "Come, come, you with restless sidelong glances; whichever <s>kāpālika</s> is dear to you,

children.text: tena sārdhaṃ yathāśraddhaṃ pānam āsevyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: with him enjoy drinking as much as you like."

children.text: tatas tatrāpi sā tebhyaḥ prakṛtyā pratibhāvatī
children.translated_text: Then there too, naturally quick-witted,

children.text: tān atidrutayā gatyā jagāma ca jagāda ca ||
children.translated_text: she went past them with very rapid steps and said:

children.text: paśyantīṃ ca ramaṇīyāṃ spṛśyamānāṃ ca bhīṣaṇām
children.translated_text: "Enough, reverend sirs, of looking at me, a poison-maiden of the eyes,
beautiful to see and terrifying to touch.
For my husband is a <s>gandharva</s>, more cruel than a <s>rākṣasa</s>,

children.text: īrṣyāvān apramattaś ca sadā rakṣati mām asau ||
children.translated_text: jealous and vigilant; he always guards me.
Because of him, when men like you, struck by the arrows of Love, assail me,

children.text: yameneva kṣayaṃ nītā koṭir yuṣmādṛśām iti ||
children.translated_text: crores of them have been brought to destruction, as if by <s>Yama</s>."

children.text: tataḥ kāpālikair uktam uktaṃ yad anayā śriyā
children.translated_text: Then the <s>kāpālikas</s> said, "What has been said by this beauty

children.text: tan na kevalam etasyām adhikaṃ copapadyate ||
children.translated_text: is not merely fitting in her case; even more than that is reasonable.
For the sake of this beloved form of hers, the cause of sleeplessness in the three worlds,
it is a wonder that <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s> do not fight.

children.text: tasmād gandharvam anyaṃ vā kaṃcit trailokyasundaram
children.translated_text: Therefore let this woman favor some <s>gandharva</s> or other being,
handsome in the three worlds, with loving glances."
Then, drawing along a crowd of heretical ascetics,
she went to her father's house, borne onward by the clamor of blessings.
Entering that seven-courtyard house, crowded with groups happy at the occasion,
she said at the door of her mother's chamber, "Give alms."
A maidservant came out from the house with alms in hand
and saw <s>Kundamālikā</s> from head to toe.

children.text: cirāc ca pratyabhijñāya ghnatī sahṛdayaṃ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: After a long moment she recognized her and, striking her head in distress,
entered and quietly told her mistress:
"You are undone, you are ruined: that daughter of yours, borne by the earth,
<s>Kundamālikā</s>, with a trembling garland of śirīṣa flowers,
wearing on her body the stain of <s>kāpālika</s> attire,

children.text: iyaṃ tiṣṭhati te dvāri svayaṃ vā dṛśyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: is standing at your door. See her yourself."

children.text: idam ākarṇya niṣkrāntā sā tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāvidhām
children.translated_text: Hearing this, her mother came out; seeing her in such a state,

children.text: vācyatām anapekṣyaiva snehād etac cacāra sā ||
children.translated_text: without waiting for an explanation, out of affection she did this:

children.text: bibheda lavaśaḥ picchaṃ kapālaṃ ca kapālaśaḥ
children.translated_text: she broke the peacock-feather ornament into pieces and the skull into fragments;
again and again she cut away the bead and the conch-and-crystal ornament.

children.text: pāṭayitvā ca tāṃ tasyās tantuśaḥ kaṇṭhakaṇṭhikām
children.translated_text: After tearing that necklace at her throat thread by thread,
and purifying her with an auspicious bath, she led her into the inner apartments.
There her mother said to her, "Child, speak confidently to your mother.

children.text: kim etad evam eveti sā tatas tām abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: What is this? Is it simply as it appears?" Then she answered her:

children.text: akasmād bhrāntir ambāyāḥ kathaṃ tava sutā satī
children.translated_text: "Why this sudden confusion in mother? How could your daughter, being chaste,
practice a <s>kāpālika</s> vow, even if urged on by unchaste women?

children.text: āstāṃ tāvat kathā ceyaṃ tātapādān ihāhvaya
children.translated_text: Let this matter rest for the moment; summon my revered father here.

children.text: asti me guru kartavyaṃ sādhyate tac ca tair iti ||
children.translated_text: I have an important duty, and it must be accomplished by him."
Then <s>Sāgaradatta</s>, called and come there, looked at her

children.text: kiṃ kim etat kathaṃ ceti śaśaṅke viṣasāda ca ||
children.translated_text: and, saying, "What is this? How has this happened?" became anxious and despondent.

children.text: taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtam atrastā kundamālikā
children.translated_text: Seeing him in such a condition, <s>Kundamālikā</s>, unafraid,
embraced him to reassure him, bowed to him, and laughed.
When he was reassured, she said to him, "Your son-in-law is staying

children.text: jāmātā tava sa syālais tasmād ānāyyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: with his brothers-in-law at the <s>Bhadravaṭa</s> hermitage; therefore have him brought."

children.text: tadādiṣṭaiś ca saṃrabdhair gṛhītaḥ syālakair asau
children.translated_text: At his command, those excited brothers-in-law seized him,
falsely addressing him with harsh words: "You are caught, thief of a son!"

children.text: kiṃ tiṣṭhasi śaṭhottiṣṭha pratiṣṭha svapuraṃ prati
children.translated_text: "Why are you standing there, rogue? Get up; set out for your own city.

children.text: tvām āhūyati rājeti sasmitāś cainam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: The king summons you," they said to him with smiles.
Then, recognizing them and imagining death or imprisonment,

children.text: mānastokam ṛcaṃ japtvā śikhābandhaṃ cakāra saḥ ||
children.translated_text: he muttered the <s>Mā nastoke</s> verse and tied up his topknot.

children.text: sasāntvaṃ cābravīd aṅga kṣaṇam etad udīkṣyatām
children.translated_text: With soothing words he said, "Friends, please wait this one moment

children.text: mama kāpāliko mitraṃ yāvad āyāty asāv iti ||
children.translated_text: until that <s>kāpālika</s> friend of mine arrives."

children.text: sa tais tāraṃ vihasyoktas tvaṃ yan mitram udīkṣase
children.translated_text: They laughed loudly and said to him, "That friend whom you are waiting for

children.text: sa gataḥ prathamaṃ tatra tenaiva grāhito bhavān ||
children.translated_text: went there first; by that very man you have been apprehended.
With useless friendship, with speech like...
even friends turn away from villains such as you."

children.text: taṃ viṣaṇṇaṃ prahṛṣṭās te mūkaṃ bahupaṭusvanāḥ
children.translated_text: They were delighted, though he was dejected; they were loud with many skilled voices, though he was silent.
Taking him, they came to the house, which was surrounded by joyful kinsmen.
There, when <s>Sāgaradatta</s>, his skin bristling with joy,
embraced his son-in-law, the latter's body seemed to become alive again.
After the honoring service beginning with arghya had been performed for him, and after his meal had been concluded,
he lay down on a great bed spread out in a lovely pavilion.

children.text: tatrāsya śvaśurau syālāḥ syālabhāryāś ca sātmajāḥ
children.translated_text: There his wife's parents, brothers-in-law, and the brothers-in-law's wives with their children,

children.text: āptāś ca śreṣṭhinaḥ paurāḥ paritaḥ samupāviśan ||
children.translated_text: and the intimates and townsmen of the merchant, sat down all around him.
Then the merchant's daughter came, her ornaments jingling sweetly,
like autumn, with a stainless sky and with clamorous royal swans.

children.text: guravaḥ satkṛtā mūrdhnā vācā savayasas tayā
children.translated_text: The elders were honored by her with her head, and those of her own age with speech;
<s>Yajñagupta</s>, however, was honored with a glance filled with passionate collyrium.

children.text: adhyāsya ca puraḥ pitror asau vāmanam āsanam
children.translated_text: Then, sitting on a low seat before her parents,
she told the story of herself, just as the marriage and the rest had occurred.

children.text: āsīc ca yajñaguptasya dhig dhiṅ me viphalāḥ kalāḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Yajñagupta</s> thought, "Shame, shame on my arts, which have proved fruitless,
since I, with two-finger intelligence, have been deceived by a maiden of good family.
Or rather, men like me alone are two-finger-witted;
women have intellects sharp as the tip of kuśa grass, whose action is of this sort.
What greater wonder is there than this: by this city-bred woman,
while gait and posture remained unchanged, even the voice was altered?
How did the foolish <s>Pārthas</s> remain in the city of <s>Virāṭa</s>?

children.text: iti ye vicikitseyus teṣām eṣā nidarśanam ||
children.translated_text: For those who might doubt this, she is the demonstration.

children.text: sarvathā guruvākyena yan mayā caritaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: In every way, because the grave deed I did was done at my guru's word,

children.text: tasmād asmy anayaivādya mocitaḥ pātakād iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore today I have been freed by this very woman from sin."
Hearing this whole account, the delighted king
had <s>Kundamālikā</s>, together with his son-in-law, brought to his own house.
There, after giving <s>Yajñagupta</s> a gift consisting of many great villages

children.text: sa dattvā yajñaguptāya sasmitas tām abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: and much gold, he addressed her with a smile:

children.text: yathā dvijātikarmabhyo na hīyate patis tava
children.translated_text: "Daughter, see to it, with your firmness,

children.text: tvayā dhīratayā putri tathā saṃpādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: that your husband does not fall away from the duties of the twice-born."
By her, whose jealousy was restrained by the goad of extreme steadiness, her husband was made to marry a twice-born maiden;

children.text: na hi kṣitīśān avilaṅghyaśāsanān vilaṅghayanti priyajīvitaśriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for those to whom life and prosperity are dear do not transgress kings whose commands cannot be overstepped.

children.text: dvijātikanyāṃ ratiputrakāmyayā sukhāya śuddhāya ca kundamālikām
children.translated_text: Enjoying the twice-born maiden out of desire for love and a son, and <s>Kundamālikā</s> for pure happiness,

children.text: niṣevamānaḥ sukṛtaṃ ca saṃtataṃ nināya vipraḥ saphalaṃ samāśatam ||
children.translated_text: and continually performing merit, the Brahmin brought a full hundred years to fruitful completion.

children.text: paugaṇḍāya vitīrṇayāpi vidhinā yasmād vaṇikkanyayā citropāyaparaṃparācaturayā prāptaḥ patir vāñchitaḥ
children.translated_text: Since, though she had been assigned by fate to a boy, the merchant's daughter, skilled in a succession of ingenious means, obtained the husband she desired,

children.text: saṃtoṣakṣatasattvasattvadayitaḥ saṃsevitaḥ kātarais tasmāt pauruṣamārutena balinā daivādrir unmūlitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore the mountain of fate, resorted to by the timid and dear to those whose courage is broken by resignation, was uprooted by the strong wind of human effort.

children.text: ity ākhyāya kathitau ca mithaḥ pravrajitau gatau
children.translated_text: Having told this story, and after the two had spoken with one another, the two mendicants went away;
and <s>Gomukha</s>, mounting a swift vessel, returned.

children.text: mām avocat sa vanditvā prītidāsaḥ punarvasuḥ
children.translated_text: After bowing to me, <s>Punarvasu</s>, a servant through affection, said to me,
"Let the leader of all the ranks of townsmen be seen."
Then I saw a man bowing down, not heavily adorned,
young, yet putting elders to shame by his modesty.
I embraced him, whose greatness had been described by <s>Gomukha</s>;

children.text: saṃbhāvitaguṇāḥ sadbhir arhanty eva ca satkriyām ||
children.translated_text: for those whose virtues have been recognized by good men surely deserve honor.
Then, mounting that conveyance borne along by <s>Punarvasu</s>,
I descended to his dwelling as a sea-trader descends to the ocean.
After attending to food, the means that keeps the body in existence,
I passed the rest of the day entertained by hearing songs.

children.text: tataḥ suptajane kāle pṛṣṭavān asmi gomukham
children.translated_text: Then, when the people were asleep, I asked <s>Gomukha</s>,

children.text: katham eṣa tvayā prāptaḥ suhṛd ity atha so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: "How was this friend obtained by you?" Then he said:

children.text: śrūyatām asty ahaṃ yuṣmān vanditvā punar āgataḥ
children.translated_text: "Listen. After bowing to you, I came back again,

children.text: na ca kaṃcana paśyāmi yogyam āśrayadāyinam ||
children.translated_text: and I saw no one suitable to give me shelter.
Then I thought: For all good men who give wealth, learning, and the like,
there is no opening apart from a royal house.
For assemblies of good men, impelled by the need for livelihood and security,
generally enter the king's gate, like rivers entering the ocean.

children.text: rājadvāraṃ tato gatvā yāciṣye kaṃcid āśrayam
children.translated_text: So, going to the king's gate, I shall ask for some support;

children.text: rājadvāraṃ hi kāryāṇāṃ dvāram uktaṃ budhair iti ||
children.translated_text: for the king's gate is said by the wise to be the gate of undertakings.
When I went there, crowded with the clamor of people seeking punishment and favor,
I remembered the lord of the dead and the lord of wealth.
This man appears to be a person of great human conduct;
therefore a request for support from him will not turn out false.
This other man, though well dressed, has the disagreeable look of a miser;

children.text: tena saṃbhāvyate nāsmāt prārthanāphalam aṇv api ||
children.translated_text: therefore not even the smallest fruit of a request can be expected from him.

children.text: puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ tatra ciram itthaṃ vicārayan
children.translated_text: While I was thus considering man after man there for a long time,
I saw a door-keeper come out from inside.
With his head bowed just once, he honored all the petitioners'
blessings, salutations, and cries of victory.
Then, seeing that merely presenting a request brought success in one's business,
the petitioners there all at once stated their business.

children.text: tebhyas tenāpi sāmānyam ekam evottaraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: To them he too made one general reply:

children.text: bhavataḥ sumukho rājā mā tvariṣṭa bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "The king is favorable to you; Your Honor should not be impatient."
Then he took off from his body the doorkeeper's costume, the tunic, and the rest,
and placed them on a nearby attendant.
And when I saw him, the search for a refuge was as good as finished;

children.text: na hi dṛṣṭasuvarṇādriḥ tāmraṃ dhamati vātikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for a man who has seen a mountain of gold does not smelt copper.
Then, after saying farewell to him, as he was going back to his own house,

children.text: māṃ muhuḥ paśyatā prītyā tenaiva sahito 'gamam ||
children.translated_text: I went along with that very man, who looked at me again and again with affection.

children.text: gṛhe ca kṛtasatkāram asau mām anuyuktavān
children.translated_text: And at his house, after honoring me, he questioned me:

children.text: āgacchati kutaḥ kiṃ vā mad icchati bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "From where do you come, and what does your honor want of me?"

children.text: mayoktaṃ bhrātarāv āvāṃ dvijau dvāv āgamārthinau
children.translated_text: I said, "We are two brothers, two brahmins seeking learning,
who have come from the land of <s>Avanti</s>, having heard that this is a seat of knowledge.
We wish to live here, taken under your protection;
for even a weak man, guarded by one stronger than himself, is strong."
He said, "For men such as you, eager to take in virtue,
whose speech and appearance are not vulgar, let my own house be yours."

children.text: muhūrtaṃ tatra cāsīnaḥ śrutavān aham utthitam
children.translated_text: While I was sitting there for a moment, I heard, for an instant, an uproar that had arisen,
like the clamor of waves on an agitated ocean.
Seeing me with ears intent on hearing it, he said to me with a smile,

children.text: kiṃ tvam etan na vettheti na vedeti mayoditam ||
children.translated_text: "Do you not know what this is?" I said, "I do not know."
"This young merchant named <s>Punarvasu</s>, a generous giver,
surrounded by a band of gamblers, is playing in the gambling hall.

children.text: yadā vijayate dyūte sa sarvaṃ draviṇaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Whenever he wins at dice, then he gives away all his money
to the crowd of petitioners; this is their tumultuous noise.
But when he is losing, the petitioners, with their heads resting on their knees,
their speech stolen away by dejection, meditate on auspicious fortune.

children.text: yadi kautūhalaṃ tatra tato 'sau dṛśyatām iti
children.translated_text: If you are curious about it, then he may be seen there."
When this had been said by the doorkeeper, I then thought:
"What use are ministers, mature in policy, learning, and age,
before whom one sits unhappily, with speech and body constrained?
A man of similar age and character, open-handed, possessed of some means,

children.text: vyasanī ca svatantraś ca so 'smākam adhunā suhṛt ||
children.translated_text: given to vice and independent: he is now our friend.

children.text: tasmād dyūtasabhām eva yāmi draṣṭuṃ punarvasum
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall go straight to the gambling hall to see Punarvasu>."
Having decided this and taken leave of him, I went to the assembly of gamblers.
The hall was crowded with gamblers intent on play,
like a lake with flocks of herons greedy for the taste of bait.
There, while two dice-cheats were playing dice with one another,
a die fell on its edge, uncertain between a <s>pada</s> and a five.

children.text: pañcako 'yaṃ padaṃ nedaṃ padam etan na pañcakaḥ
children.translated_text: "This is a five, not a <s>pada</s>; this is a <s>pada</s>, not a five";
so a quarrel arose between the two, each seeking victory over the other.
One of the two said, "Let a neutral judge be asked."
The other too replied, "As you wish, so be it."

children.text: athaikaḥ puruṣaḥ prāṃśuḥ pṛṣṭas tābhyām anāgaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then a certain tall, uncouth man was asked by the two:
"Which of the two do you see clearly, the <s>pada</s> or the five?"
Then one of them, raising his hand, said loudly:

children.text: dīrghatvād eṣa nirbuddhir ato 'nyaḥ pṛcchyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Because this man is tall, he is witless; therefore let another be asked."

children.text: tataḥ pṛṣṭo 'paro hrasvaḥ so 'pi tena nivāritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then another man, a short one, was asked; he too was rejected by that man:

children.text: nedṛśāḥ praśnam arhanti bahudoṣā hi khaṭvakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Such people do not deserve the question, for short fellows have many faults."

children.text: atha māṃ dṛṣṭavantau tau pṛṣṭavantau ca sādaram
children.translated_text: Then the two saw me and asked me respectfully:

children.text: sādho yadi na doṣo 'sti tato nau chinddhi saṃśayam ||
children.translated_text: "Good sir, if there is no fault in you, then settle our doubt.

children.text: tvaṃ na dīrgho na ca hrasvas tasmāt prājño na duṣṭadhīḥ
children.translated_text: You are not tall and not short; therefore you are wise and not of corrupted judgment.
So, because you are of middle measure, take the place of a mediator."
And I thought, "Hard is the decision of a doubtful matter among rogues,
especially among gamblers greedy for another's money.
Yet knowledge of an art must certainly be displayed by one who knows the art;
for knowledge that is not made manifest is useless, like a miser's wealth.
And the art of gambling is not displayed anywhere except among gamblers;

children.text: na hi prayuñjate prājñāḥ veśād anyatra vaiśikam ||
children.translated_text: wise men do not practice the courtesan's art anywhere except in a brothel.

children.text: dyūte jeṣyati yaś cātra sa me mitraṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And whoever wins here at dice will become my friend;
for they regard the gain of a wealthy friend as greater than the gain of a treasure."

children.text: ityādi bahu niścitya puras teṣāṃ savistaram
children.translated_text: Having determined many such things, I explained at length before them
the names and characteristics of dice, the <s>aṣṭāpada</s> board, the pieces, and the ground.
Then, upon that doubtful throw of the die that had fallen on its edge,
I placed finely ground brick powder on top of the die.
Then that brick powder which fell on the side of the <s>pada</s>
all fell to the ground, while what was on the five remained in place.

children.text: tatas tān uktavān asmi yo bhāgaḥ pañcakāṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then I said to them, "The part marked with five

children.text: tasyottānatvam utkṛṣṭaṃ kṣodas tatra yataḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is raised higher, since the powder has remained there.

children.text: etāvan mama vijñānam ity uktvāvasthite mayi
children.translated_text: This is the extent of my knowledge." When I had said this and stood there,

children.text: aho sādhv iti nirghoṣaḥ samantāt sahasotthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a sudden cry arose on every side: "Ah, well done!"
Then some there declared, "This man, skilled in dice,
would surely defeat even <s>Nala</s> and <s>Kuntīsuta</s> by far."
Others, angered, said to them, "<s>Nala</s> and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> were defeated;
this man conquers even the conquerors <s>Puṣkara</s> and <s>Saubala</s>."

children.text: iti praśasyamānaṃ māṃ tiryag dṛṣṭvā samatsaraḥ
children.translated_text: As I was being praised in this way, the defeated advocate of the <s>pada</s>

children.text: padavādī jito yo 'sāv asau mantharam uktavān ||
children.translated_text: looked sideways at me with envy and said slowly:
"Those who have no stake for gambling, why are they sitting here?

children.text: dyūtasthāne hi kiṃ kṛtyaṃ pravīṇaiḥ prāśnikair iti ||
children.translated_text: For what business do expert judges have in a gambling place?"

children.text: āsīc ca mama kasmān māṃ kaulaṭeyaḥ kṣipaty ayam
children.translated_text: And I thought, "Why does this son of an adulteress insult me,
when I possess a stake whose wager is the very essence of the three worlds?"

children.text: atha nikṣipya sakrodhaṃ yauṣmākaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: Then, angrily throwing your ornament down on the ground,

children.text: ehi dīvyāva mitreti tam ahaṃ dhūrtam uktavān ||
children.translated_text: I said to that cheat, "Come, friend, let us gamble."
And that ornament, with its thick radiance spreading out,
was seen by the cheats, their eyes wide with craving, like fire by moths.
Then that dice-cheat, deceived by anger and greed,

children.text: mayā saha sasaṃrambham akṣān ārabdho devitum ||
children.translated_text: impetuously began to play dice with me.

children.text: tena cāhaṃ tribhiḥ pātair anakṣakuśalaḥ kila
children.translated_text: And by him, with three throws, I, supposedly unskilled at dice,
was beaten out of three thousand by that greedy gambler with his lucky casts.

children.text: tatas tat sakṛd unmocya sahasratritayaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: Then, having recovered that three thousand all at once,

children.text: lakṣam ekena pātena jitaḥ sa kitavādhamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I won a lakh from that lowest of gamblers with a single throw.
His courage swelled from victory, yet he was afraid of defeat;

children.text: na virantuṃ na vā rantum asāv aśakad ākulaḥ ||
children.translated_text: bewildered, he could neither stop nor go on playing.

children.text: dīvya vā dehi vā lakṣaṃ saumyeti ca mayoditaḥ
children.translated_text: "Either play or pay the lakh, good sir," I said to him;

children.text: vailakṣyād ghaṭṭayann akṣān na kiṃcit pratipannavān ||
children.translated_text: but, rattling the dice in embarrassment, he made no decision.

children.text: etasminn antare bhṛtyaṃ svam avocat punarvasuḥ
children.translated_text: At that moment <s>Punarvasu</s> spoke to his own servant:

children.text: kitavo 'yam idaṃ lakṣam acalaṃ dāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "This man is a gambler; make him pay this fixed lakh."

children.text: māṃ cāyaṃ svaṃ gṛhaṃ nītvā harṣād ṛjutanūruhaḥ
children.translated_text: And he took me to his own house, his hairs bristling straight with joy,

children.text: tathā pūjitavān devaṃ haraṃ dattavaraṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: and honored me as one would honor the god <s>Hara</s>, the giver of boons.

children.text: māṃ cāvocad dhanaṃ yat tad bhavadbhiḥ kitavārjitam
children.translated_text: He said to me, "That money which you won from the gamblers

children.text: tad udgrāhyedam ānītaṃ lakṣaṃ te gṛhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: has been collected and brought here; take this lakh."

children.text: mayāpy uktam upānte yad draviṇaṃ tvatparigrahāt
children.translated_text: I too said, "The wealth near me that was obtained through your protection,

children.text: sādhitaṃ bhavatā yac ca tasya svāmī bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: and what was secured by you: you are the owner of it.

children.text: uktaṃ cānena yan nāma yuṣmābhiḥ svayam arjitam
children.translated_text: And he said, "What was won by you yourselves

children.text: svāmino yūyam evāsya dhanasyety atra kā kathā ||
children.translated_text: belongs to you alone; what more is there to say about this wealth?

children.text: yad apīdaṃ mayāvāptaṃ yuṣmatsvāmikam eva tat
children.translated_text: Even this which I obtained belongs to you.

children.text: adhigacchati yad dāso bhartur eva hi tad dhanam ||
children.translated_text: For whatever a servant acquires is certainly the master's wealth.

children.text: yac ca pṛcchāmi tan mahyaṃ prasāde sati kathyatām
children.translated_text: And if there is favor toward me, tell me what I ask:
for what reason have you come down to earth from heaven?

children.text: manye saty api devatve bhavadbhiḥ krīḍayāhṛtaiḥ
children.translated_text: I think that, though you are divine, being carried away by sport,
you have not fully practiced making yourselves into another form.
For who among human beings has ever seen such wealth

children.text: dṛṣṭāḥ kena manuṣyeṣu yādṛśo bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: of color, build, skill, and knowledge as yours?"

children.text: tena yat satyam ity ukte duḥkham āśitavān aham
children.translated_text: When he said, "This is the truth," I became distressed;
for excessive praise is a cause of pain far more than excessive blame.
The business I had explained to the gatekeeper when he questioned me

children.text: yan mayā kāryam ākhyātaṃ tad evāsmai niveditam ||
children.translated_text: at the entrances to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, that same thing I reported to him.
Then he said, "A wonder! If there is one elder than you,

children.text: tvādṛśasyāpi yo jyeṣṭhaḥ kīdṛśaḥ sa bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: who are elder among the worlds by your virtues, what sort of man will he be?

children.text: kiṃ vānena vimardena jyeṣṭhas tiṣṭhati yatra saḥ
children.translated_text: Or what is the use of this pressing? In the place where that elder stays,

children.text: sarvatīrthādhike deśe taṃ prāpayata mām iti ||
children.translated_text: a land surpassing all sacred fords, take me to him."
Then I took him and went to your presence,

children.text: yac cottaram atas tatra pratyakṣaṃ bhavatām api ||
children.translated_text: and what followed after that was directly seen by you as well.

children.text: iti kṣipram ayaṃ labdho mayā vaḥ paricārakaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus I quickly found this attendant for you.

children.text: na hiṃsanti na sarvatra śriyaḥ puṇyavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Fortunes do not harm the meritorious anywhere.

children.text: tatas tam uktavān asmi vipadas tena durlabhāḥ
children.translated_text: Then I said to him, "Misfortunes are hard to obtain for one
whose heart, <s>Gomukha</s>, is itself the fruit of good conduct.
But <s>Punarvasu</s> must be troubled merely because we have taken shelter here;

children.text: parānnaṃ hi vṛthābhuktaṃ duḥkhāyaiva satām iti ||
children.translated_text: for food belonging to another, eaten needlessly, brings only pain to good people."

children.text: evamādibhir ālāpair ardham ardhaṃ ca nidrayā
children.translated_text: With conversations such as these, and half the time with sleep,

children.text: nītavān asmi yāminyāḥ prātaś cāgāt punarvasuḥ ||
children.translated_text: I passed the night; and in the morning <s>Punarvasu</s> came.

children.text: taṃ ca vanditamatpādam avocad iti gomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: After he had bowed to my feet, <s>Gomukha</s> said this to him:
"Some skilled cook should be sought from somewhere.
Food in the house of anyone other than you is not eaten by the noble elder;
for well-conducted twice-born men turn away from another's cooking.
But this man, honored and propitiated with respect, has eaten what is yours;
for deference to being honored is the conduct of great men."

children.text: pratyākhyānavicittas tu tam āha sma punarvasuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Punarvasu</s>, bewildered by the refusal, said to him:

children.text: yady evaṃ jagadīśānāṃ kiṃ nāsti bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "If this is so, what is there that you, lords of the world, do not possess?"
Soon, when they had been brought, I saw before me two men
endowed with estimable virtues, whose appearance eclipsed the <s>Nāsatyas</s>.

children.text: tau ca māṃ ciram ālokya vadanaṃ ca parasparam
children.translated_text: The two looked for a long time at me and at each other's face,

children.text: prasārya sabhujān pādāñ jayety uktvā bhuvaṃ gatau ||
children.translated_text: then stretched out their arms and feet, cried "Victory!", and fell to the ground.
Called by me, they came forward; I touched their backs and welcomed them.

children.text: vanditvā punar abrūtāṃ brūta kiṃ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: After bowing again they said, "Tell us, what is to be done?"

children.text: tatas tau gomukhenoktau bhavantau kila ballavau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gomukha</s> said to the two, "You two are said to be cooks.

children.text: satyaṃ ced idam āryasya pākaḥ saṃsādhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: If that is true, let this noble one's meal be prepared."

children.text: tau ca prītau pratijñāya nikartya nakhamūrdhajān
children.translated_text: The two were pleased, promised it, cut their nails and hair,
bathed, wrapped turbans on their heads, and went to the kitchen.

children.text: athavā tiṣṭhati vyāsaḥ samāsaḥ śrūyatām ayam
children.translated_text: But let the full detail rest; let this summary be heard:
the entire procedure was set in motion by those two as if it were unprecedented.
In the amount of time in which another cook would set a pot on the fire,

children.text: tāvatyā velayā tābhyāṃ pāka eva samāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in that very span the cooking was finished by them.
Then, having completed my bath and the offerings to the deities and the fire,
I occupied the eating-place, with rows of Brahmins close by.

children.text: pañca tittirayaḥ pakvāś catvāraḥ kukkuṭā iti
children.translated_text: "Five partridges are cooked, and four chickens," so they praised the meal;

children.text: āhāro yaiḥ praśastas tair aśitaṃ prākṛtāśanam ||
children.translated_text: and by those men ordinary food was eaten.

children.text: āhāraṃ yadi severan sakṛt tam amṛtāśanam
children.translated_text: If they ate that food, that ambrosial meal, even once,
then they would become beings whose diet of nectar had been cast aside.
Then, when the meal was finished, I said in <s>Gomukha</s>'s ear,
"Let ten thousand be given to the two cooks, who have eaten their meal."

children.text: sa gatvā sahitas tābhyāṃ cirāc cāgatya kevalaḥ
children.translated_text: He went with the two of them and, after a long while, came back alone,
his pleasure indicated by a smile, and began to speak.

children.text: mayā yāv uditāv etau na yuvām etad arhatha
children.translated_text: "When I told these two, 'You two do not deserve only this;

children.text: avasthāsādṛśaṃ kiṃtu yat kiṃcid gṛhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: rather, take whatever is suitable to the occasion,'
then one of the two said, 'Since our lord is living in distress,

children.text: na yuktaṃ dhanam ādātum āvābhyām iti bhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: it is not proper for us to take money.'
The other, angry, said to him, 'Shame on you, with your more than pitiable mind,
you who pity the lord of wealth, the conqueror of the wealth of the three worlds!
By his favor thousands of great padmas will be securely established
for those who ride in aerial palaces; what distress can he have?

children.text: prayacchaty ayutaṃ yaś ca pākasyaikasya niṣkrayam
children.translated_text: If he gives ten thousand as the price of a single cooking,

children.text: duḥsthitas tādṛśo yasya susthitas tasya kīdṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then if such a man is distressed, what would he be like when prosperous?'

children.text: evamādi bruvann eva sa mālyam iva tad dhanam
children.translated_text: Saying such things, he held that money on his head for a moment,

children.text: dhārayitvā kṣaṇaṃ mūrdhnā prasthāya prāptavān gṛham ||
children.translated_text: as if it were a garland, and then set out and reached home."
Then, filled with keen curiosity, I asked him,

children.text: divyam aiśvaryam āgāmi kathaṃ veda bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: "How do you know of this divine sovereignty that is to come?"
Then he said, "The father of this very king <s>Brahmadatta</s>
was <s>Pañcayajña</s>, whose prosperity surpassed that of a hundred sacrifices.
A cook named <s>Devavān</s>, learned in medicine and the science of cooking,

children.text: dvitīya iva tasyātmā devavān iti ballavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and honest even in craftsmanship, was like a second self to him.
The king, having formed the thought, 'This body of mine depends on him,'
assigned to him a tenth part of his own kingdom.
The sons of that chief cook were named <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>;

children.text: īdṛśākāravijñānāv āvām eva ca viddhi tau ||
children.translated_text: know that we ourselves are those two, possessed of such form and knowledge.
Even when we were children, we two were instructed in the science of cooking and in medicine
as a family lore, through innate knowledge and practical application.

children.text: ekadā nau pitāvocat putrakau śṛṇutaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Once our father said to us, 'My two sons, listen to what is beneficial.
Misfortunes do not touch one who listens to the words of his teacher.
You two must study words, sentences, and means of knowledge,
various poems as well, and the whole group of arts beginning with painting.
At some time, when the lord has gone to a hostile region
to conquer what has not yet been conquered, he may desire amusement in discussions of sciences, poems, and stories.
Then, if you know that his assembly has no learned men nearby,
you two should entertain him with conversations on the sciences and the like.
Servants who are bold, quick-witted, and learned in many events
play with their masters by revealing the movements of their minds.
But there a man of one learning, though bold, is a poor fellow;
wearied by the turns of talk on his own learning, he waits for a long time.
One practiced in many branches of knowledge, with a mind free from confusion,
because he is free from the pain of doubt, is the supreme lord among happy people.
And with zeal you should study the marks of long life and sovereignty;
for servants should attend upon those who are long-lived and wealthy.'
By our father's command, all that was studied by us,

children.text: ramyāsvādaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca ko 'vamanyeta bheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: for who would disdain a medicine that is both pleasant in taste and wholesome?
Therefore he will become the universal emperor of the circle of <s>Vidyādharas</s>,
and, in our opinion, he will be long-lived, like the thousand-rayed moon of <s>Jyaiṣṭha</s>.
For that reason, stretching out our limbs, we bowed to him;
for those bowed to by many do not deserve an ordinary salutation.
Many brahmins stay here, mere cocks of the pilgrimage-place;
we honor them only with a nod of the head.
Therefore, because with unattached eyes trained in every scripture

children.text: jyeṣṭhasya dṛṣṭam aiśvaryam ataḥ śraddhīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: we have seen the elder one's sovereignty, let it be believed.'

children.text: prajñaptikauśikasutapramukhair uktaṃ nandasya niścitataraṃ vacanāt tad āsīt
children.translated_text: What <s>Nanda</s> had said became still more certain from the words spoken by <s>Prajñapti</s>, <s>Kauśikasuta</s>, and the others,

children.text: bhāvaṃ hi saṃśayatamaḥpaṭalāpinaddham udbhāvayanty avitathā vacanapradīpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for true lamps of speech reveal an intention wrapped in the thick veil of the darkness of doubt.
Then, served by <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> in their own office,
I lived happily for a few days in <s>Punarvasu</s>'s house.
One day, standing on the top of the house and looking in all directions,
I saw a female ascetic, preceded by a company of disciples.

children.text: kavibhis tair anātmajñair buddhir āyāsyate vṛthā
children.translated_text: The intelligence of those poets, ignorant of the self, is spent in vain,
who shamelessly describe her color and bodily form.

children.text: sarvathā taṃ vidhātāraṃ dhig yat kiṃcanakāriṇam
children.translated_text: In every way, shame on that creator, that maker of random things,
by whom a wretched way of life, contrary to her form, was made for her.

children.text: sarvo hi viniyogārtham arthaḥ sarveṇa sṛjyate
children.translated_text: For every object is created by everyone for the sake of use;
who, after making a pot, has it broken to pieces with a clod?

children.text: dhātrā punar iyaṃ sṛṣṭā komaleva mṛṇālinī
children.translated_text: But this woman was created by the creator as tender as a lotus-fiber,

children.text: śoṣitā tuhineneti dhik tasya khalatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and then dried up by frost. Shame on his villainy!"

children.text: tatas tāṃ ciram ālokya nirnimiṣeṇa cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: Then, after gazing at her for a long time with unwinking eyes,
<s>Gomukha</s>, his eagerness stirred, asked <s>Punarvasu</s>,
"Good sir, with her movements slow from the weight of her thighs,

children.text: eṣā pravrajitā bhadra kva gacchati gatair iti ||
children.translated_text: where is this renunciant woman going along the adorned city roads?"
He replied, "This is <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>; she has undertaken the <s>ārhata dharma</s> (Jain religious path)."
and through freedom from passion she surpasses even the perfected ones, even the <s>Jinas</s>.
When this girl sees her childhood friend, the royal maiden, constantly
she comes from the maidens' inner apartments and goes to her own bed.
Having related this and other such things, he bowed to <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>:

children.text: ambike sahaśiṣyāyās te namo 'stu namo 'stv iti ||
children.translated_text: "Mother, together with your fellow pupils, homage to you, homage," he said.

children.text: taṃ ca pravrajitāvocad asaṃbhāṣyo bhavān iti
children.translated_text: And the nun said to him, "You are not to be spoken with."
When he said, "Why?" she replied, "Listen."
"Two Brahmins, who put the omniscient to shame with knowledge and make <s>Smara</s> forgotten by beauty,
named <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> and <s>Kaniṣṭha</s>, are staying in your house, they say.
And the pleasure born from seeing and speaking with them
is enjoyed by you in secret, like wealth by a miser.

children.text: suhṛtsādhāraṇaṃ yasya sukhaṃ sa paramaṃ sukhī
children.translated_text: The man whose happiness is shared with friends is supremely happy;
but the opposite man, from the effort of concealing happiness, is miserable.

children.text: suhṛdbhiḥ kupitais tasmād asaṃbhāṣyaḥ kṛto bhavān
children.translated_text: Therefore, because your friends are angry, you have been made one not to be spoken with.
Think of some effective means of bringing them here."
Then <s>Gomukha</s> said loudly:
"Before long <s>Punarvasu</s>, together with <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, came to the pavilion of the <s>Jina</s> temple."
There, after worshiping the <s>Arhat</s>, the <s>saṅgha</s> clothed in robes,

children.text: ṛṣidattāṃ ca tad datte viṣṭare samupāviśam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Ṛṣidattā</s> as well, I sat down on the seat given by her.
But <s>Gomukha</s>, with his arms hanging down and his armpits uncovered,
stood at the temple doorway and uttered a hymn to the <s>Jina</s>:

children.text: namo 'stu sarvasiddhebhyaḥ sādhubhyaś ca namo 'stu vaḥ
children.translated_text: "Homage to all perfected beings, and homage to you holy men;
homage to all the omniscient ones beginning with <s>Ṛṣabha</s>."

children.text: sādhu śrāvaka dhanyo 'si yaḥ sarvajñaṃ namasyasi
children.translated_text: "Good, lay follower; blessed are you, since you bow to the omniscient one";
saying much of this sort, the <s>Nirgranthas</s> praised <s>Gomukha</s> with delight.
Then he, firmly pressing <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>'s feet,

children.text: abravīt suprasannau me bhavantau bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: said, "May you both be very well pleased with me."

children.text: tayā tv asya prayuktāśīr asmākaṃ laghuśāsane
children.translated_text: But she pronounced a blessing on him:
"In our light discipline, may even a lay follower's practice be in agreement."
Then <s>Upananda</s> said, "Let a vīṇā concert begin;

children.text: eṣa saṃnihitaḥ saṃghaḥ sakalaḥ suhṛdām iti ||
children.translated_text: here the whole company of friends is assembled."
Another said, "When the skilled <s>Gaṅgarakṣita</s> has not arrived,
the assembly is soundless, like a lotus pond without swans.
Therefore, gentlemen, wait for the great chamberlain
<s>Gaṅgarakṣita</s>." Then <s>Gaṅgarakṣita</s> arrived.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nāgarair uktam āryajyeṣṭhasya vāsya vā
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the townsmen said, "Having looked carefully at noble <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> and at this man,

children.text: ākhyāta nipuṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā kataro rūpavān iti ||
children.translated_text: tell us which of the two is handsome."

children.text: āsīc ca mama yat satyaṃ satyam evāsmi rūpavān
children.translated_text: And I thought, "What is true is simply true: I am indeed handsome,
since my beauty is comparable to the beauty of <s>Gaṅgarakṣita</s>.
If even this man is honored by being compared with my beauty,
then he too must be accepted as a standard among handsome men."

children.text: vanditvā jinam agranthān ṛṣidattāṃ ca māṃ ca saḥ
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the <s>Jina</s>, the <s>Nirgranthas</s>, <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>, and me,
he sat down; and again <s>Upananda</s> spoke as before.
Then the nun said, "When the merchant <s>Priyadarśana</s> has not arrived,
this whole assembly is unpleasant to look at.

children.text: ataḥ pratīkṣyatāṃ śreṣṭhī kṣaṇam ity uditekṣayā
children.translated_text: Therefore let the merchant be waited for a moment." When she had said this with an expectant glance,

children.text: ayam āyāta ity ākhyan nāgarāḥ priyadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: the townsmen announced, "Here is <s>Priyadarśana</s> arrived."

children.text: āsīc ca mama taṃ dṛṣṭvā naivāyaṃ priyadarśanaḥ
children.translated_text: And seeing him I thought, "This is not <s>Priyadarśana</s> at all;
this is <s>Priyadarśanā</s>, adorned in a man's disguise.
By her feminine gait, posture, and voice
she has clearly revealed her own womanly beauty, which casts down the beauty of the three worlds."

children.text: sā tu vanditadevādiḥ sādaraṃ mām avandata
children.translated_text: After worshiping the deity and the others, she respectfully bowed to me;
I too returned the bow, saying, "Long may you live, fair lady."
Then I was looked at by <s>Gomukha</s> with eyes reddened by anger,

children.text: citraṃ nāgarakaiḥ kaiścil lajjitaiḥ kaiścid ambaram ||
children.translated_text: by some townsmen in amazement, by some in embarrassment, and by others looking at the sky.
<s>Ṛṣidattā</s>, with tearful, wide, trembling eyes,

children.text: sagomukham apaśyan mām ā śiraścaraṇaṃ ciram ||
children.translated_text: looked at me together with <s>Gomukha</s> from head to foot for a long time.

children.text: atha prapañcam ākṣeptum etaṃ sapadi gomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, in order to check this elaboration at once, <s>Gomukha</s>
addressed the circle of friends: "Let the concert be begun."

children.text: upanandas tataḥ pūrvaṃ tathā vīṇām avādayat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Upananda</s> first played the vīṇā

children.text: yathā vigatarāgād yair nirgranthair api mūrchitam ||
children.translated_text: in such a way that even the <s>Nirgranthas</s>, though free from passion, were entranced.

children.text: upanandāt tato nandaṃ nandād api punarvasum
children.translated_text: Then from <s>Upananda</s> the vīṇā went to <s>Nanda</s>, and from <s>Nanda</s> to <s>Punarvasu</s>;

children.text: punarvasor agād vīṇā kramāt taṃ gaṅgarakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: from <s>Punarvasu</s> it went in turn to <s>Gaṅgarakṣita</s>.
Among <s>Upananda</s> and the others, each later player,

children.text: parājayata dūreṇa pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ paraḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: by far defeated the previous one, though that previous one had surpassed <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>.
Then the vīṇā, reaching <s>Gomukha</s> in order from <s>Gaṅgarakṣita</s>,
went like <s>Sarasvatī</s> from a rich lord to a poor man.

children.text: gomukhas tu tato vīṇām avādayata līlayā
children.translated_text: But <s>Gomukha</s> then played the vīṇā with ease
in such a way that <s>Gaṅgarakṣita</s> was watched by the dejected townsmen.

children.text: gomukhāṅkāt tato vīṇā yāti sma priyadarśanam
children.translated_text: Then from <s>Gomukha</s>'s lap the vīṇā went to <s>Priyadarśana</s>,
like an adulterous woman going from her lover's lap to the handsome man she desires.
Then, when he played and sang in a superhuman way,
<s>Gomukha</s>, from embarrassment, formed the intention of fleeing.

children.text: kiṃtu nāradaśiṣyo 'yaṃ suto vā tumbaror iti
children.translated_text: "Is this man a pupil of <s>Nārada</s>, or the son of <s>Tumburu</s>?"

children.text: yat satyam aham apy āsam adbhutaśrutivismitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In truth, I too was astonished by the marvelous sound I heard.

children.text: muktavīṇe tatas tatra śanair māṃ gomukho 'bravīt
children.translated_text: Then, when the vīṇā had been set down, <s>Gomukha</s> slowly said to me,
"Now the turn for playing has come to you."

children.text: hasitvā tam athāvocam adyāpi hi śiśur bhavān
children.translated_text: Then I laughed and said to him, "Even now you are still a child,

children.text: yo māṃ yatra kvacit tucche pravartayati vastuni ||
children.translated_text: you who urge me on in some trifling matter anywhere at all.
And in the presence of naked ascetics and <s>Kirāṭas</s>,
what sort of reward would there be for a man like me playing the <s>vīṇā</s>?"
Hearing this, I was addressed by him, who had become angry:

children.text: campāyāṃ kīdṛśaṃ kāryam abhavad bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "What sort of business did you people have in <s>Campā</s>?"

children.text: tatas tam uktavān asmi śrūyatām yadi na śrutam
children.translated_text: Then I said to him, "Listen, if you have not heard it:

children.text: prāptir gandharvadattāyās tatra kāryam abhūd iti ||
children.translated_text: there our business was the attainment of <s>Gandharvadattā</s>."

children.text: athāyam avadat tatra devīprāptiḥ phalaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: Then he said, "If there the queen's attainment was the reward,
here too let the attainment of <s>Gomukha</s> be considered the highest reward.

children.text: yuṣmadanyo na māṃ kaścid vīṇayā jitavān iti
children.translated_text: No one other than you has ever defeated me with the <s>vīṇā</s>.

children.text: idaṃ me śreṣṭham āgamya śreṣṭhināpahṛtaṃ yaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: My supreme fame, when it came to this merchant, was stolen away by the merchant.
If this thief of our fame is not quickly restrained,

children.text: tyajāmy eṣa tataḥ prāṇān duḥkhabhārāturān iti ||
children.translated_text: then I shall give up my life, afflicted as it is by the burden of sorrow."

children.text: mama tv āsīd asaṃdigdhaṃ sarvam atropapadyate
children.translated_text: But for me there was no doubt: everything here was fitting.
For to proud men the breaking of pride is a torment greater than death.
What can be compared with the pain of a disputant drunk with knowledge of the meaning of the treatises,
when he has been defeated and abandoned by his beloved?

children.text: tasmād etad iha nyāyyam iti niścitya sādaram
children.translated_text: Therefore, having decided respectfully that this was proper here,
I began to tune the strings, which were badly out of order.
Then, with their eyes widened and their skin embraced by a line of horripilation,
each member of the assembly gazed at the faces of the others.
Then, when the strings had been touched by the tips of the branches of my hand,

children.text: hā hā kim idam ity uktvā pustanyastā ivābhavan ||
children.translated_text: they cried, "Ah! Ah! What is this?" and became as if drawn in a painting.

children.text: athaitasyām avasthāyāṃ mayā vīṇā ca saṃhṛtā
children.translated_text: Then, while they were in that state, I put away the <s>vīṇā</s>,
and by them, releasing long sighs, the world of the living was looked upon again.
Then at once the lotus of <s>Gomukha</s>'s face shone forth,
touched by the redness of joy, blooming, clear, and radiant.
Though defeated, the handsome <s>Priyadarśana</s>, his pride in defeating <s>Gomukha</s> now defeated,
spoke to me with joy, like a speaker who had conquered an unconquerable debater.
"The merchant has been defeated at the <s>vīṇā</s> by the elder, the conqueror of the world;

children.text: iti me prasthitā kīrtir ā payodhivasuṃdharām ||
children.translated_text: so my fame has gone forth as far as the ocean-bounded earth.

children.text: pūrṇā hi vasudhā śūdrair na ca tān veda kaścana
children.translated_text: The earth is full of <s>śūdras</s>, and no one knows them;
but spotless is the fame of <s>Śambūka</s>, whose head was cut off by <s>Rāghava</s>.
Moreover, from today onward I have offered my very self to you.
Accept me as a pupil who seeks instruction in playing the <s>vīṇā</s>."

children.text: asyām eva tu velāyām avocad gaṅgarakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: At that very moment <s>Gaṅgarakṣita</s> said:

children.text: ayam eva mamāpy arthaḥ saphalīkriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "This is my wish as well; let it be brought to fulfillment."
Then those two were told by <s>Gomukha</s>, "You both seek instruction,

children.text: anāyāsopadeśau ca yat tad evaṃ bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: and you can be taught without difficulty; since that is so, let it be so."

children.text: sa mayā śanakair uktaḥ kṣipram eva tvayānayoḥ
children.translated_text: He was then quietly told by me, "You have quickly accepted
the request of these two," after <s>Gomukha</s> had spoken.
The body of the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, his kingdom, his harem, his city,

children.text: yac cānyad api tat sarvaṃ gaṅgarakṣitarakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: and whatever else there is, all of it is guarded by <s>Gaṅgarakṣita</s>.

children.text: yasya ca svayam evāyaṃ dāsyām abhyanugacchati
children.translated_text: And for the man whose servitude this man himself undertakes,
all prosperities are in his hand, unmixed with misfortunes.
And because <s>Priyadarśana</s> is the chief merchant, master of every guild,

children.text: sa yasya kiṃkaras tasya kiṃkarā sakalā purī ||
children.translated_text: if he is someone's servant, the whole city is that man's servant.
With this reward in mind, I made a promise to these two;

children.text: na hy anālocyakartāraḥ kiṃkarā bhavatām iti ||
children.translated_text: for servants of yours are not people who act without deliberation."
After praising that joyous acuteness of his, and together with all my friends, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Upananda</s>, and the others,
I bowed to the community of those who practiced the vows of the <s>arhats</s>, and then went to <s>Punarvasu</s>'s house.
There, joined with friends such as <s>Nanda</s>, skilled in pleasing others,
whose feeling of friendship was unfeigned, I dwelt happily.
One day, at mealtime, <s>Gomukha</s> was not to be seen.

children.text: atha nītam anāhārair asmābhir api tad dinam ||
children.translated_text: Then that day was passed by us as well without food.
But he came back in the evening, his appearance not quite natural,
and, seeing me distressed by the thought that he was helpless, he spoke humbly:
"On the royal road, in a crush packed with a crowd of townspeople,
I saw a servant of <s>Hariśikha</s> himself, but he was hidden by the people.
Today, while searching for him, I passed the day;

children.text: kārye hi guruṇi vyagraṃ jighatsāpi na bādhate ||
children.translated_text: for when one is intent on an important matter, even hunger does not trouble one.
And he must certainly be sought out by me, in order to obtain news of my friend.

children.text: tasmān mā mām apaśyantaḥ kṛdhvaṃ duḥkhāsikām iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore do not, on failing to see me, make yourselves sit in sorrow."
I gave him permission, and after seven or eight days had quickly passed,
he returned, his gait slowed by intoxication and talking a great deal.
Then, seeing him, with my mind shaken by anger,
I stood silent for a moment and then spoke harsh words:

children.text: īdṛśas tādṛśaḥ prājñaḥ prekṣākārī ca gomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: "Such a one, so wise, so prudent a <s>Gomukha</s>!
Thus the speed of <s>Garuḍa</s> has been assigned to a lame horse.

children.text: pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇam ākhyāya samastāyāḥ puraḥ puraḥ
children.translated_text: Earlier you proclaimed the Brahmin before the whole city again and again;

children.text: adhunā madhunā mattaḥ kathaṃ paśyasi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: now, drunk with liquor, how can you show yourself to me?"

children.text: atha mām ayam āha sma na madaḥ pāramārthikaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he said to me, "This drunkenness is not real.

children.text: sadoṣaṃ tu vaco vaktuṃ mayāyaṃ kṛtrimaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I have made it artificial so that I may utter speech that is faulty.
For they say that faults of speech in a drunken man, such as harshness and falsehood,

children.text: dūṣayanti na vaktāram ato 'yaṃ kṛtrimo madaḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not taint the speaker; therefore this drunkenness is artificial."

children.text: tatas tam uktavān asmi saṃbhāvitaguṇasya te
children.translated_text: Then I said to him, "For you, whose qualities are esteemed,
is there perhaps even a faultless means of concealing my passion?"

children.text: athānenoktam astīti katham ity udite mayā
children.translated_text: Then he said, "There is." When I asked, "How?",
he began to explain it, his syllables slowed by shame.

children.text: śrūyatām ṛṣidattā me yatra netrapathaṃ gatā
children.translated_text: "Listen. From the day when <s>Ṛṣidattā</s> came within the path of my eyes,
from that day onward she became the object of my mind.
Then, recognizing the unrestrained condition of my heart, I thought:

children.text: kasmād aviṣaye cakṣuś cetasā me prasāritam ||
children.translated_text: 'Why have my eyes been stretched by my mind toward an improper object?
Because I knew the treatises on <s>dharma</s> (religious duty), wealth, and policy, and because of my place in assemblies of good men,

children.text: rāgādhīnaṃ na me cakṣuḥ pravṛttaṃ gaṇikāsv api ||
children.translated_text: my eye, ruled by passion, had not turned even toward courtesans.

children.text: nūnam eṣā parigrāhyā mama pravrajitā yataḥ
children.translated_text: Surely this renunciant woman is to be taken by me, since
my intention toward her has rushed forth like a hard-to-tame horse.
Therefore I shall first investigate the cause

children.text: jijñāsye tāvad ity enām agacchaṃ draṣṭum anv aham ||
children.translated_text: of this unwanted intention toward her.' Thus I went day after day to see her.
With entertainments of various kinds, and with stories of other countries and the like,

children.text: dvitrair eva dinais tasyā viśvāsam udapādayam ||
children.translated_text: in only two or three days I brought about her confidence.
One day, when conversation had begun, I was asked by <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>,

children.text: ke ke deśās tvayā dṛṣṭāḥ krāmatā pṛthivīm iti ||
children.translated_text: 'What countries have you seen while wandering over the earth?'
When I replied, 'I have formerly seen the country of <s>Vatsa</s>,

children.text: vatsadeśaḥ sa dṛṣṭaḥ prāṅ mameti kathite mayā ||
children.translated_text: where the city <s>Kauśāmbī</s> is prosperity itself in bodily form,'

children.text: tayoktam alam ālāpair aparais tava durbhagaiḥ
children.translated_text: she said, 'Enough of your other unlucky talk.
Let the story again concern only <s>Vatsa</s> and <s>Kauśāmbī</s>.
Now, do you know in <s>Kauśāmbī</s> one named <s>Gomukha</s>, whose appearance conquers <s>Manmatha</s>,

children.text: gomukhaṃ nāma niṣṇātaṃ savidyāsu kalāsv iti ||
children.translated_text: and who is accomplished in all branches of knowledge and arts?'
Then I thought, 'Shall I tell her about myself?

children.text: athavā dhig adhīraṃ mām evaṃ tāvad bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, shame on my impatience; for the moment let it be so.'

children.text: tato 'ham uktavān ārye jānāsīti kim ucyate
children.translated_text: Then I said, 'Noble lady, why do you ask, "Do you know him?"

children.text: ātmānaṃ ko na jānāti sa hi me paramaḥ suhṛt ||
children.translated_text: Who does not know himself? For he is my dearest friend.

children.text: athavā na viśeṣo 'sti sūkṣmo 'pi mama gomukhāt
children.translated_text: Or rather, there is not even a subtle difference between me and <s>Gomukha</s>.

children.text: tena māṃ paśyatā vyaktaṃ dṛṣṭo bhavati gomukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By seeing me, <s>Gomukha</s> has plainly been seen.'
Then, with the corner of her eye and with lashes dimmed by tears,

children.text: sānurāgeva dṛṣṭvā māṃ ciraṃ mantharam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: she looked at me for a long time, as if with affection, and slowly said:
'They say that <s>Gomukha</s>, by his beauty and by the charm of skill in the arts,
is like no one on earth except the son of the king of <s>Vatsa</s>.
And if he has your appearance and is refined by the whole web of your arts,
then <s>Gomukha</s> is like a prince of the <s>Vidyādharas</s>.
Whoever knows your appearance is altogether fortunate;
for even <s>Gandhaśaila</s> is praiseworthy when measured against <s>Sumeru</s>.'

children.text: ity uktvā cīvarāntena mukham āvṛtya nīcakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having said this, she covered her face with the edge of her robe,
and began to weep softly, her breasts heaving with longing.

children.text: ṛṣidattām athāvocam ārye kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Then I said to <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>, 'Noble lady, for what reason
do you weep at hearing of <s>Gomukha</s>, like a woman whose child has died?'

children.text: tayoktaṃ śrūyatām asti vidvān rājagṛhe vaṇik
children.translated_text: She said, 'Listen. In <s>Rājagṛha</s> there is a learned merchant,

children.text: padmo nāma dhanaṃ yasya padmasyeva mahānidheḥ ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Padma</s>, whose wealth is like that of <s>Padma</s>, the great treasure.
Clever in household conduct, dear to their husband, and devoted to their husband,

children.text: sumanā mahadinnā ca tasya bhārye babhūvatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumanā</s> and <s>Mahadinnā</s> were his two wives.
They had two sons bearing their mothers' names,

children.text: putrābhyāṃ dayite pitros tathā duhitarāv api ||
children.translated_text: dear to their parents because of those sons, and likewise two daughters.

children.text: tatra yā sumanā nāma tasyāḥ sumanasaḥ sutā
children.translated_text: Among them, the daughter of <s>Sumanā</s>, named <s>Sumanā</s> after her,
was married here in the city to the merchant <s>Kāliya</s>.

children.text: duhitā mahadinnāyā yā ca mātuḥ sanāmikā
children.translated_text: And the daughter of <s>Mahadinnā</s>, who had the same name as her mother,
was married to <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, the friend of the lords of <s>Cedi</s> and <s>Vatsa</s>.
From <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and <s>Mahadinnā</s>, they say, <s>Gomukha</s> was born,

children.text: na kutaścin na kasyāṃcit kaścij jagati yādṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: such that there is no one like him anywhere, born from any woman, in the world.
But I am the daughter of the virtuous <s>Mahadinna</s>;
even from the <s>Himālaya</s> rivers go forth to salty waters.
While still a child, I was promised by my elders to <s>Gomukha</s>;

children.text: kaṃ hi nāma na gacchanti kanyāpitror manorathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for to what do the hopes of a maiden's parents not go?

children.text: kāle kvacid atīte tu taṃ guṇair janavallabham
children.translated_text: But when some time had passed, wicked Time, like winter,
destroyed <s>Padma</s>, who was beloved by people for his qualities.
Then his family, deprived of that supporter,
came to the state of a house whose firm pillar has been uprooted.

children.text: vārāṇasyāṃ tataḥ pitrā svasuḥ sumanaso gṛhe
children.translated_text: After that, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, my father placed me in the house
of his sister <s>Sumanā</s>, and I was cherished by my father's sister like a daughter.

children.text: saṃtatādyaiḥ krameṇātha jvaraiḥ pañcabhir apy aham
children.translated_text: Then, afflicted in succession by all five fevers beginning with <s>saṃtata</s>,
I became blind and was given up by the physicians.
And here there was a compassionate female ascetic named <s>Śrutadharā</s>,
who had crossed the deep ocean of the scriptures of the Jain lord.
Expert in spells and medicines, she brought this about by her speech,

children.text: mām asāv acireṇaiva tasmād vyādher amocayat ||
children.translated_text: and very quickly freed me from that disease.

children.text: svasthāvasthāṃ ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā sumanā gṛham ānayat
children.translated_text: Seeing me restored to health, <s>Sumanā</s> brought me home;
then that same succession of fevers seized me again, as if in anger.
