children.text: tataḥ śrutadhārāyai mām arpayat sumanāḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sumanā</s> handed me over again to <s>Śrutadharā</s>,

children.text: sa ca yātaḥ punar vyādhir mantrāgadabhayād iva ||
children.translated_text: and the disease again departed, as if in fear of her spells and medicines.

children.text: śravaṇām avadad dainyād durmanāḥ sumanās tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sumanā</s>, downcast from misery, said to the nun:
"Let this girl live by taking ordination."

children.text: tathā cāgrāhayat sā mām arhatpravacanaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: And she caused me to accept the teaching of the <s>Arhats</s> in such a way
that the whole community of ascetics came to regard me as a pupil.'"
With the lamp of perfect knowledge, seeing the worthlessness of saṃsāra,
and the substantial value of nirvāṇa, <s>Śrutadharā</s> reached her final resolution.
Then, when she had completed that, the whole group of <s>śramaṇas</s> assembled

children.text: gaṇanīm akarod asmin vihāre mām anicchatīm ||
children.translated_text: and made me, against my will, a female leader in this monastery.

children.text: dhyānaṃ yad yat samāpadya devatālambanaṃ niśi
children.translated_text: Whatever meditation I entered at night, with a deity as its support,
there <s>Gomukha</s> forcibly presented himself as the object of concentration.

children.text: yadā yadā ca gośabdam adhīyānā vadāmy aham
children.translated_text: And whenever, in reciting, I uttered the word 'go',

children.text: mukhottarapadas tatra jāyate sa tadā tadā ||
children.translated_text: then each time he became there the one whose latter word was 'mukha'.

children.text: jalpantī mukhaśabdaṃ ca prayuñje yadi kevalam
children.translated_text: If, while speaking, I used only the word 'mukha',
it forcibly acquired there the word 'go' as its prior member.
Even grass and the like, when touched by <s>Gomukha</s>, seemed praiseworthy,
and, subject to this thought, I passed a long time.

children.text: tāvac ca na mayā tyaktā pratyāśā gomukhāśrayā
children.translated_text: Nor did I abandon my hope fixed on <s>Gomukha</s>
until another piece of news arrived, one that gave me despair.

children.text: campāsthasya prabhor mūlaṃ prasthitaḥ sabalaḥ kila
children.translated_text: It was said that <s>Gomukha</s>, with his troops and circle of friends, had set out
for the presence of his lord staying at <s>Campā</s>, and had been killed on the way by Pulindas.

children.text: yac cāsmi na mṛtā sadyaḥ śrutvā gomukhavaiśasam
children.translated_text: That I did not die at once on hearing of <s>Gomukha</s>'s slaughter
was the capacity of a mind still capable of reflection.

children.text: āsīc ca mama jīvantī jīvitasya mahat phalam
children.translated_text: And for me, while I lived, there was a great fruit of life:
I would hear the delightful story of <s>Gomukha</s>.

children.text: api cāparam apy asti jīvitālambanaṃ mama
children.translated_text: Besides, there was another support for my life:
that <s>Gomukha</s> had been killed by Śabaras only by mere rumor.
Therefore, when I heard the story connected with <s>Gomukha</s>, I wept,
even though it was more than nectar, because it was a cause of grief.

children.text: mama tv āsīd yathāheyaṃ sarvaṃ tad upapadyate
children.translated_text: But I thought: 'All this comes about just as it ought to be rejected;
how otherwise could servants of yours form a sinful intention?

children.text: svair iyaṃ gurubhir dattā madīyair api yārthitā
children.translated_text: This girl was given freely by her elders, and was also requested by my own people;

children.text: kumārī sānurāgā ca tasmān na tyāgam arhati ||
children.translated_text: she is a maiden and in love, and therefore she does not deserve abandonment. '
After determining at length this and much else as the reason for accepting her,
I employed this blameless means of taking her.
With tasty alms-food, obeisance, medical treatment,
massage, anointing, and other services, I quickly pleased the community.

children.text: vyagreṇa cātra vṛttānte dattaṃ vaḥ kṛtakottaram
children.translated_text: And, being occupied with this matter, I gave you a fabricated reply:
'Do not wait for me, for I am busy seeking news of a friend.'
Then I said to <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>, 'Let household followers skilled in their craft
provide cooks to prepare the food.
After honoring the <s>arhats</s> with perfumes, garments, garlands, and the like,

children.text: ṛṣibhyaḥ śramaṇābhyaś ca dātum icchāmi bhojanam ||
children.translated_text: I wish to give food to the sages and the <s>śramaṇas</s>.
The sin that is acquired by feeding thousands of false-view holders

children.text: tad ekam arhataṃ bhaktyā sadyaḥ pāpaṃ pramārjyate ||
children.translated_text: is immediately wiped away by devotedly feeding a single <s>arhat</s>.
Therefore, as many noble ones as are here, devoted to the teaching of the dear omniscient one,

children.text: saśrāvakagaṇān āryāṃs tāṃs tad āmantryatām iti ||
children.translated_text: let them be invited, together with their groups of lay followers.'

children.text: sarvathā sādhitaḥ sūdair āhāraḥ sa tathā yathā
children.translated_text: In every way the food was prepared by the cooks in such a manner
that even those who had conquered their tongues and mastered the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> were pleased.
Then, before <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>, I, with an artificial fever,
fell down, with my hair bristling high, trembling and yawning.

children.text: tādṛśī ca mayā vyaktā jvaritānukṛtiḥ kṛtā
children.translated_text: And I made such a clear imitation of a feverish man
that even the hard-to-feign burning heat was believed by her.

children.text: kim etad iti cāpṛcchat sā mām ujjvalasaṃbhramā
children.translated_text: 'What is this?' she asked me, bright with alarm,
and I too reported this, broken by the chattering of my teeth:
'Wasted by not eating for six nights, and seized by a fever caused by wind,
I am experiencing this condition of such a kind.'
Then, in her own sleeping quarters, crowded with the group of <s>śramaṇas</s>,
she, overcome with compassion, massaged me for a long time.

children.text: atha saṃghaṭṭayan dantān uktavān asmi tāṃ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, chattering my teeth, I said to her softly,
'Let this dwelling be cleared of the crowd.'
The nuns, given permission by <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>, went away,
and then, wishing to know her intention, I said this to her:
'Noble lady, even with fathers, brothers, and sons it is improper for women,

children.text: vratasthānāṃ viśeṣeṇa sthātuṃ saha rahaś ciram ||
children.translated_text: especially women established in vows, to remain together secretly for a long time.
And I am a rogue, a traveler, whose appearance may be suspected of impropriety,

children.text: pṛthagjanā janāś caite tena nirgamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and these people are ordinary folk; therefore go out.'

children.text: tayoktaṃ kṣaṇam apy ekam aśaktā svastham apy aham
children.translated_text: She said, 'Even if you were healthy, I could not bear to stay elsewhere

children.text: muktvā tvāṃ sthātum anyatra kiṃ punaḥ saṃtatajvaram ||
children.translated_text: leaving you for even a single moment; how much less when you have a continuous fever?
Even the mere supposition of someone like me being with someone like you is lovely;
even a branch of the kiṃśuka tree is praised when it is joined with spring.
Blessed too is the fever by which this body of yours is used;
even the kālakūṭa poison is praiseworthy when it has licked <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s throat.'
While she was saying such things, by that passion, fierce as a great seizure,
she was possessed, with the saintly state of her mind shaken.

children.text: mama tv āsīd iyaṃ cintā satyam āhuś cikitsakāḥ
children.translated_text: But I had this thought: 'Truly the physicians say

children.text: sarve saṃkrāmiṇo rogāḥ spṛśatāṃ prāṇinām iti ||
children.translated_text: that all diseases are contagious among living beings who touch one another.

children.text: madīyaḥ kṛtrimo 'py enaṃ yatra saṃkrāmati jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Since even this artificial fever of mine passes into her,

children.text: kathaṃ nāma na saṃkramet tatra yaḥ paramārthikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how indeed should that one not pass into her, the fever that is real?
For sweat, horripilation, tears, trembling, and yawning,
this retinue of fever, afflicts her body.
In every way, whatever sign is set forth in the treatises on love

children.text: lāvaṇyam iva gātreṣu tad asyāḥ prāsphurat sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: The grace of beauty shone clearly, as it were, upon her limbs.

children.text: tatas tām uktavān asmi dhik tvāṃ niṣkaruṇāśayām
children.translated_text: Then I said to her, "Fie on you, whose heart is without compassion,

children.text: śītajvarārtam aṅgair yā na pīḍayasi mām iti ||
children.translated_text: since, though I am afflicted by a cold fever, you do not press me with your limbs."

children.text: athāśliṣyaṃ tathā sā māṃ nādṛśyata yathā pṛthak
children.translated_text: Then she embraced me in such a way that she was not seen as separate from me,
like the moonlight at night's end within the faint reddish glow of dawn.
Then, by the treatment of that embrace, the two fierce fevers of us both,
the artificial and the genuine, went away in a moment.

children.text: yātāyām atha yāminyāṃ buddhvā vṛttāntam īdṛśam
children.translated_text: Then, when the night had passed and the community learned of such an event,

children.text: saṃghaḥ saṃhatya tāṃ svasmān nivāsān niravāsayat ||
children.translated_text: they gathered together and expelled her from their residences.
After that the merchant, delighted, had <s>Rṣidattā</s> mounted in a carriage with me
and brought her to his house, which was crowded with auspicious preparations.
There <s>Priyadarśana</s>, kind and good-hearted, with flowers at hand,
had the taking of our hands performed amid a company of delighted townspeople.

children.text: tad evam ṛṣidattā vaḥ saṃvṛttā paricārikā
children.translated_text: So in this way <s>Rṣidattā</s> became your attendant;

children.text: athavā kiṃ vikalpena svayam ālokyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: or rather, why speculate? Let her be seen by you yourselves."

children.text: tathāpi kathitaṃ tena naiva saṃśayam atyajam
children.translated_text: Even though he told the story in this way, I did not give up my doubt,
for such a chance coincidence is hard to believe all at once.
Having first sent garlands, ornaments, garments, and other things,

children.text: prasthāpya prāk tadārhāṇi tāṃ didṛkṣus tato 'gamam ||
children.translated_text: as well as household furnishings suited to her, I then went, wishing to see her.
And there I saw her adorned with bright, variegated cloth,
as if she were laughing at the beauty of a spring grove with its many flowers.
Even wooden images shine when they are ornamented in that way;
what need is there to speak of women like her, before whom maidens of the Asuras would be ashamed?

children.text: pravrajyāyāṃ punar yasyāḥ kāntir yāsīd akṛtrimā
children.translated_text: But of her whose splendor, even during renunciation, was natural,

children.text: durlabhāṇi kvacit tasyā vācakāny akṣarāṇy api ||
children.translated_text: words capable of expressing it are hard to find anywhere.
And to me the wearing of a heavy, solid mass of ornaments
seemed ill-suited both to a lovely form and to an ugly one.
For the charm of a lovely form, when covered by ornaments,

children.text: na śakyā sarvathā draṣṭuṃ janair lolekṣaṇair api ||
children.translated_text: cannot be seen completely even by people with restless eyes.

children.text: virūpasya tu vairūpyaṃ yat pracchādanam arhati
children.translated_text: But the ugliness of an ugly form, which ought to be concealed,
is proclaimed in the world by the loud drumbeat of lavish adornment.
Then <s>Rṣidattā</s> approached me as I sat upon the couch
and bowed, delighted though ashamed at having abandoned renunciation.

children.text: tatas tām uktavān asmi sakhyāḥ kiṃ kāryam āśiṣā
children.translated_text: Then I said to her, "What need has a friend of blessings?

children.text: sarāgaiva satī yā tvaṃ vītarāgagatiṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: For you, still full of passion, have entered the state of those free from passion.

children.text: mokṣaḥ kāruṇikair uktaḥ siddhair duḥkhakṣayaḥ kila
children.translated_text: The compassionate perfected ones call <s>mokṣa</s> the destruction of suffering;
since your unbearable suffering has been destroyed, you have in every way attained <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: sarvathā subhagatāmahoddhataḥ kiṃkaro bhavatu gomukhas tava
children.translated_text: Let <s>Gomukha</s>, greatly elated by your complete good fortune, become your servant;
for women whose husbands are visibly subdued delight their mothers and their female friends."
After making her embarrassment pass away with a string of crooked, playful speeches like these,

children.text: tām āmantrya svam āvāsam agacchaṃ sahagomukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I took leave of her and went to my own lodging together with <s>Gomukha</s>.
On another occasion, when I had come and been properly honored by her,
I saw <s>Priyadarśana</s>, who had come home from the market.

children.text: kañcukaṃ muñcatas tasya mayā dṛṣṭaḥ payodharaḥ
children.translated_text: As he was taking off his jacket, I saw a breast of his,
perfectly round like the moon seen between clouds.

children.text: āsīc ca mama yoṣaiṣā yatas tuṅgapayodharā
children.translated_text: And I thought, "This is a woman, since she has high breasts;
for the possession of breasts and long hair is the first sign of womanhood.

children.text: lokas tu yad imāṃ sarvaḥ pratipannaḥ pumān iti
children.translated_text: But the whole world has accepted this person as a man;
that is a mistaken cognition on its part, produced by some resemblance.
Or rather, why speculate? My eyes are not dimmed;

children.text: na hi dṛṣṭena dṛṣṭārthe draṣṭur bhavati saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for when the object has been seen in a matter of sight, the seer has no doubt.
As I was looking at <s>Priyadarśana</s> with unblinking eyes,
<s>Rṣidattā</s> saw me filled with many thoughts like these.
Then, with choked speech and eyes filled with tears of affection,
she said to <s>Priyadarśana</s>, "Compose yourself."

children.text: asāv api tam uddeśaṃ prakāśya jhagiti tviṣā
children.translated_text: That one too, lighting up that spot instantly with radiance,
entered the interior of the mansion like a streak of lightning entering a cloud.
Then I looked at <s>Rṣidattā</s> with eyes widened by anger,
for by her the merchant had been made to withdraw from the range of my sight.
Then I rose from that place, accompanied by <s>Gomukha</s>, who shared my anger born of desire,
and, reaching <s>Punarvasu</s>'s house, took refuge on a couch.
Then the succession of the stages of love, abandoning its proper order,
oppressed me all at once like an army in the tumult of battle.
Then, like a childish ordinary man who has only recently obtained prosperity,
I gave <s>Gomukha</s> an order in a harsh voice:
"Let my beloved <s>Priyadarśanā</s>, even if her husband has become a renouncer,
be brought quickly, without even having made her toilette."

children.text: sa tu mām abravīt trastaḥ kā nāma priyadarśanā
children.translated_text: But he said to me in alarm, "Who in the world is <s>Priyadarśanā</s>,

children.text: tyājitāḥ stha yayā sadyaś cetasaḥ sthiratām iti ||
children.translated_text: by whom you have suddenly been made to abandon firmness of mind?"

children.text: mayoktaṃ tava yaḥ syālaḥ puruṣaḥ priyadarśanaḥ
children.translated_text: I said, "The man <s>Priyadarśana</s>, who is your brother-in-law,
this very essence of the world is the woman <s>Priyadarśanā</s>.

children.text: yac ca vakṣyasi sarvasyāṃ vārāṇasyām ayaṃ pumān
children.translated_text: And if you will say, 'In all <s>Vārāṇasī</s> this person is a man;

children.text: bhavataḥ katham ekasya pramadeti tad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: how can she be a woman for you alone?' that point is answered as follows:
<s>Rṣidattā</s> was once determined by her to be detached from passion;

children.text: adhunā bhavataḥ kāntā jātety atra kim ucyate ||
children.translated_text: now she has become your beloved--what can be said about that?

children.text: gatānugatiko lokaḥ pravṛtto hi yathā tathā
children.translated_text: The world follows those who have gone before and proceeds in whatever way;

children.text: paramārthaṃ punar veda sahasraikaḥ pumān iti ||
children.translated_text: but one man in a thousand knows the highest truth."

children.text: tenoktaṃ janatāsiddhaṃ viruddham api na tyajet
children.translated_text: He said, "One should not abandon what is established by the people, even if it is contradictory."

children.text: kriyate chagalaḥ śvāpi saṃhatya bahubhir balāt ||
children.translated_text: Even a goat is forcibly made into a dog when many people join together.

children.text: tena yuṣmadvidhaiḥ prājñair na vācyaṃ sad apīdṛśam
children.translated_text: Therefore such a thing, even if true, should not be said by wise men like you;

children.text: aśraddheyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ pratyakṣam api yad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: what is unbelievable should not be spoken of, even if it is directly seen.

children.text: śrūyatāṃ ca kathā tāvad arthasyāsya prakāśikā
children.translated_text: Now listen to a story that clarifies this matter;
for the standard of proof was followed by those who knew proof even in an ancient age.
There was a Brahmin named <s>Kauśika</s>, learned in the <s>Veda</s> and the <s>Vedāṅgas</s>,
who was known in the world as <s>Satyakauśika</s> because he was vowed to truth.
Once, when he had gone to the <s>Jāhnavī</s> for bathing,
he saw, together with the circle of his pupils, a stone floating.
Then with great effort he instructed his pupils:

children.text: nāyam artho mahānarthaḥ prakāśyaḥ putrakair iti ||
children.translated_text: "My children, this matter, which would be a great calamity, must not be revealed."
Then one restless student among them, named <s>Piṅgala</s>,
talked in the market before a certain merchant.

children.text: śreṣṭhi kiṃ na śṛṇoṣy ekam āścaryaṃ kathayāmi te
children.translated_text: "Guildmaster, do you not hear? I will tell you one marvel:

children.text: tarantīṃ dṛṣṭavān asmi sopādhyāyaḥ śilām iti ||
children.translated_text: I saw a stone floating, together with my teacher."
Then a maid of the inner apartments had come to buy something.
Hearing this conversation, she reported it to the king's wife.

children.text: tayāpi kathitaṃ rājñe sa tāṃ pṛṣṭvā paraṃparām
children.translated_text: She too told the king; he questioned her about the chain of report,
summoned the student by whom it had been reported, and questioned <s>Satyakauśika</s>.

children.text: satyaṃ brūhīti no vācyaḥ satyavādivrato bhavān
children.translated_text: "You should not be told, 'Speak the truth,' for you are a man vowed to truth;

children.text: mithyā brūhīti no vācyaḥ kāmī mithyāvrato hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor should you be told, 'Speak falsely,' for a man who wants that is himself vowed to falsehood.

children.text: kiṃtu yat piṅgalenoktam etad yuktaṃ parīkṣitum
children.translated_text: But what <s>Piṅgala</s> has said ought to be examined,

children.text: pramadāt satyam apy ete vadanti baṭavo yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for student-boys sometimes speak the truth by accident.

children.text: saśiṣyaiḥ kila yuṣmābhis tarantī prekṣitā śilā
children.translated_text: A floating stone was supposedly seen by you together with your pupils.

children.text: kim etat satyam āhosvin mṛṣety ākhyāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Tell me whether this is true or false."

children.text: āsīc cāsya dhig etāṃ me ninditāṃ satyavāditām
children.translated_text: And he thought, "Shame on this condemned truthfulness of mine,

children.text: duḥśraddhānam aniṣṭaṃ ca yan mayā vācyam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: since such a hard-to-believe and unwelcome thing must be spoken by me.

children.text: na satyam api tad vācyaṃ yad uktam asukhāvaham
children.translated_text: Even the truth should not be spoken when its utterance brings unhappiness;
this maxim about truth is one that truth-speakers must not abandon.
Therefore, abandoning this truth, which is worse than a hundred lies,
I shall speak an untruth that is better than a hundred truthful statements."

children.text: athāvocat sa rājānaṃ rājan mithyā baṭor vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he said to the king, "O king, the boy's statement is false.

children.text: agniṃ paśyati yaḥ śītaṃ plavamānāṃ śilām asau ||
children.translated_text: The man who sees cold fire also sees a stone floating.
Who would believe the word of a boy, naturally unsteady in mind?
For the first comparison for restlessness is boys and monkeys."
Having convinced the king that the boy was bewildered, <s>Satyakauśika</s>,
angry at the speaker of contradiction, banished <s>Piṅgala</s>.
Thus, though questioned by the king, <s>Satyakauśika</s>, vowed to truth,
did not speak the truth that the world would hate.
But as for you, whose birth, character, and conduct are unknown,

children.text: viruddham idam īdṛk kaḥ śraddadhyād vadatām iti ||
children.translated_text: who would believe you when you say such a contradictory thing?"

children.text: sa mayokto bhavān eva duḥśraddhānasya bhāṣitā
children.translated_text: I said to him, "You yourself are the speaker of what is hard to believe,
since regarding this jewel among women you have the mistaken notion, 'It is a man.'
And what is the use of this babble? Soon I shall make the lovely <s>Priyadarśana</s>, that jewel among women,
my own, while people like you cry out."

children.text: evaṃ ca mama vṛttāntaṃ vijānann api gomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: And though <s>Gomukha</s> knew this condition of mine,
he summoned the royal physician and went to the physician.

children.text: sa mamālāpam ākarṇya kāyacchāyāṃ vilokya ca
children.translated_text: After hearing my speech and observing the color of my body,

children.text: pradhārya cāparair vaidyaiḥ śanakair idam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and after conferring with other physicians, he slowly said this:
"This is a mental disorder in him, caused by failure to obtain what he desires;

children.text: tenāsmai rucitaṃ yat tad āśu saṃpādyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore whatever pleases him should quickly be provided for him."
Then, after food had carefully been prepared by <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>,
<s>Gomukha</s> first fed me by the hand of <s>Punarvasu</s>.
That food, well prepared and tempting even to eaters of ambrosia,
made my limbs shake with aversion, like a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>.
Then, as I was gradually being fed by <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>,

children.text: saviṣādau karomi sma viṣādāv iva vairiṇau ||
children.translated_text: I made those two despondent, as if they were two enemies named Despair.
When their efforts proved fruitless, <s>Gomukha</s> brought <s>Priyadarśana</s>,
her steps slowed by bashfulness and her face bent downward.
Then, seated in the middle of the same couch as I,

children.text: grāsān agrāsayat ṣaḍ vā sapta vā gomukhājñayā ||
children.translated_text: she made me eat six or seven mouthfuls at <s>Gomukha</s>'s command.

children.text: ye tatpāṇisarojasaṅgasubhagā grāsā mayā svāditās taiḥ sadyas tanutām anīyata sa me saṃkalpajanmā jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: The mouthfuls made lovely by contact with the lotus of her hand were tasted by me; by them my fever born of imagination was at once reduced to thinness.

children.text: śailendrāḥ śuciśukrabhānudahanapluṣṭopalādhityakā mandair apy udabindubhir navatarair ujhanti saṃtaptatām ||
children.translated_text: Great mountains, with rocky slopes scorched by the pure bright fire of the sun, give up their heat even through gentle fresh drops of water.
Then, when the meal was finished, in the very presence of my friends,
I embraced <s>Priyadarśana</s>, my shame uprooted by love.
Then <s>Gomukha</s>, his face red with anger,
quickly drew <s>Priyadarśana</s> by the hand and went back to his own house.
When he returned, I said to him, my eyes widened with anger,

children.text: pāṇḍityāndhaka mitrāre mā sma tiṣṭhaḥ puro mama ||
children.translated_text: "You blind man of learning, enemy of your friend, do not stand before me.
If someone snatches a cup of wine from the hand of a thirsty drunkard,

children.text: yasya yas tasya kas tasmād arātir aparaḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: what other enemy could that man have, worse than him?"

children.text: ity uktaḥ sa viṣādena tyājitaś campakābhatām
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, he was made by sorrow to abandon his champaka-like color;
like the moon seized by <s>Rāhu</s>, he became dark as smoke.

children.text: taṃ ca dīrgham ahaḥśeṣam āyatāṃ ca vibhāvarīm
children.translated_text: And I used to pass that long remainder of the day and the extended night
with prolonged sitting and pacing about.
Surrounded mostly by a circle of friends, and having every means of distracting myself from what was hateful,
I searched for a way to obtain <s>Priyadarśanā</s>.
When matters had gone on in this way, two elders, wearing white turbans and jackets,

children.text: vismitau ciram ālokya sthavirau mām avocatām ||
children.translated_text: looked at me in astonishment for a long time and said to me:
"Brahmin, for some reason King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, lord of his subjects,

children.text: bhavantam icchati draṣṭum iṣṭaṃ ced gamyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: wishes to see you. If it pleases you, go."

children.text: idam ākarṇya yat satyam īṣad ākulamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this, to tell the truth, with my mind somewhat agitated,
I remembered the mind of <s>Gomukha</s>, clever in deliberation.

children.text: kiṃ gacchāni na gacchāni gacchataḥ kiṃ bhaved iti
children.translated_text: "Shall I go or shall I not go? If I go, what will happen?"

children.text: vitarkya kṣaṇam āsīn me saṃdehacchedanī matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After pondering for a moment, a judgment that cut through doubt arose in me:

children.text: yo bandhavyo 'thavā vadhyo na sa kañcukidūtakaḥ
children.translated_text: "A man who is to be bound or killed does not receive a mere chamberlain as envoy;
for he is surrounded by men holding chains and swords in their hands.

children.text: ye ca kecij janā yeṣāṃ viṣaye sukham āsate
children.translated_text: And whatever people live happily in the territory of kings,

children.text: rājñām ājñām avajñāya teṣāṃ jīvanti te katham ||
children.translated_text: how can they live if they disregard the kings' command?

children.text: amandaspandam etac ca kāṅkṣitām akṣi dakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: And this right eye of mine, throbbing strongly,

children.text: ākhyatīva priyāprāptiṃ mahyaṃ tad gamanaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: seems to announce to me the attainment of my beloved; therefore going is good for me."
Having thus made up my mind and gone out from the house, I saw outside a carriage
brought by the chamberlain, and I mounted it without fear.
Then, passing along the royal road, crowded and hemmed in by masses of townspeople,
I went to the palace gate, whose circle was adorned with auspicious designs.
After sitting there for a moment, with my name announced by <s>Gomukha</s>,
I entered the first court, greeted by the company of doorkeepers.

children.text: samṛddhiḥ srūyatāṃ tasyāḥ kṛtaṃ vā tatpraśaṃsayā
children.translated_text: Let its prosperity be heard of; or rather, what is the use of praising it?

children.text: ko hi varṇayituṃ śakto naro meror adhityakām ||
children.translated_text: What man is able to describe the upper slopes of <s>Meru</s>?
Passing beyond that and five other courts of still more outstanding beauty,
in the seventh I saw the great audience hall of the king.
It was attended by men who had crossed the ocean of texts beginning with the <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and <s>purāṇa</s>,
by those who knew the principles of the science of archery and the rest, and by men skilled in the arts.
In its form it bore the mutually opposed splendor of moon and sun,

children.text: sukhasevyaṃ durīkṣaṃ ca taptāṃśum iva haimanam ||
children.translated_text: easy to approach yet hard to gaze upon, like a winter sun.
Then, after offering a blessing to him, I mounted a golden-seated chair
appointed by the king and covered with unmarked cloth.

children.text: nṛpas tu māṃ ciraṃ dṛṣṭvā snehasnigdhāyatekṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But the king looked at me for a long time with wide eyes moist with affection,
and then glanced at his general named <s>Tārakarāja</s>.

children.text: sa tu mām abhitaḥ sthitvā kāryamātrasya vācakaḥ
children.translated_text: He, standing near me, speaking only of the matter at hand,
uttered a charming speech, its syllables clear and sweet:

children.text: āryajyeṣṭha manas tāvad avikṣiptaṃ kuru kṣaṇam
children.translated_text: "Noble elder, steady your mind for a moment.

children.text: rājā manmukhasaṃkrāntair vākyais tvām eṣa bhāṣate ||
children.translated_text: This king is addressing you with words that pass through my mouth.
This lineage of the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, white as the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>,

children.text: sā kim ākhyāyate tubhyaṃ prathitā pṛthivīva yā ||
children.translated_text: is it to be described to you, when it is as famous as the earth itself?
And the virtues of this King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, born in that lineage,

children.text: ye guṇās te 'pi te buddhāḥ śiśirāṃśor ivāṃśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are also known to you, like the rays of the moon.

children.text: asyāsīt kāliyo nāma śreṣṭhī prāṇapriyaḥ suhṛt
children.translated_text: He had a dear friend, dear as life, a merchant named <s>Kālīya</s>,
by whose fruitful riches even <s>Draviṇeśa</s> was put to shame.

children.text: antarvatyām asau patnyāṃ nītaḥ puṇyais tripiṣṭapam
children.translated_text: When his wife was pregnant, he was carried by his merits to <s>Tripiṣṭapa</s> heaven;

children.text: atha sā gṛhiṇī tasya kāle putraṃ vyajāyata ||
children.translated_text: then that wife of his, in due time, gave birth to a child.

children.text: tasmiñ jāte mahārājaḥ svātmajād api harṣade
children.translated_text: When it was born, the great king, more delighted than by the birth of his own child,
caused a splendid great festival to be held in the city, together with the inner palace.
That child, after all the rites had been performed, grew toward boyhood,
adorned in body and with all branches of knowledge and arts.

children.text: evaṃprāye ca vṛttānte dvāḥsthair vijñāpito nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: When events had gone on in this fashion, the king was informed by excited doorkeepers:

children.text: dvāre vaḥ kāliyaḥ śreṣṭhī tiṣṭhatīti sasaṃbhramaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Your merchant <s>Kālīya</s> is standing at the door.'
Then, while the king was filled with wonder, that man was admitted,

children.text: kas tvaṃ kasya kuto veti pṛṣṭaś cedam abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: and, when asked, 'Who are you, whose are you, and from where?', he said this:
'Your Majesty, I am the merchant <s>Kālīya</s>; by Your Majesty I was cherished, protected,

children.text: lālitaḥ pālitaś cāsaṃ śikṣitaś cākhilāḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and instructed in all the arts as though I were your own body.
Through my good conduct I was removed from the happiness born of your favor

children.text: cyāvayitvā divaṃ nīto na hi nāśo 'sti karmaṇām ||
children.translated_text: and taken to heaven; for there is no destruction of deeds.

children.text: athāsau bhavatāṃ dāsī durmanāḥ sumanāḥ sutām
children.translated_text: Then that slave-woman of yours, <s>Sumanā</s>, though downcast, brought her daughter,

children.text: jātāṃ putra iti khyātim anayal lobhadūṣitā ||
children.translated_text: who had been born, into the reputation of being a son, corrupted by greed.
Because of that falsehood of hers, I have fallen from the world of the gods;

children.text: bhāryayā hi kṛtaṃ karma patyāv api vipacyate ||
children.translated_text: for a deed done by a wife ripens also upon the husband.

children.text: kule ca kulaputrasya jāto jātismaraḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: And, reborn again as one who remembers his former birth in the family of a good man,
I bear this sort of form, censured by people.

children.text: asau ca yuvatir jātā kāntākārā ca dārikā
children.translated_text: And that girl has become a young woman, with the form of a beloved beauty;
let her be given to some handsome bridegroom.
As for me, I shall cast off this self, blamed for deformity of limb,
at <s>Prayāga</s>; send me away.'

children.text: evamādy uktavān ukto vismitena sa bhūbhṛtā
children.translated_text: When he had spoken words such as these, the astonished king said to him:

children.text: pūrvaṃ yad āvayor vṛttaṃ tat kiṃcit smaryatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Please remember something of what happened between us before.'

children.text: anenāpi vihasyoktaṃ yad yad devāya rocate
children.translated_text: He too, laughing, said, 'Whatever Your Majesty wishes,

children.text: asaṃdigdhaṃ suviśrabdhas tat tat pṛṣṭatu mām iti ||
children.translated_text: ask me that, without hesitation and with complete confidence.'

children.text: athādhyāya ciraṃ rājñā yad yat pṛṣṭaṃ cirantanam
children.translated_text: Then, after thinking for a long time, whatever ancient matter the king asked

children.text: aśeṣaṃ tat tad etena saviśeṣaṃ niveditam ||
children.translated_text: All of that was reported by him fully and with particular detail.
Then the king, saying, "This is utterly wonderful," and gaining confidence,

children.text: āhainaṃ dārikā kasmai jāmātre dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: said to him, "To what son-in-law should the girl be given?"
But he, with his syllables stumbling from satisfaction, said,

children.text: rocate yo varas tasyai tasmai sā dīyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "To whatever suitor is pleasing to her, let her be given to him."
Then, after she had been brought into the inner apartments together with <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>,
she, her body drawn in like a female tortoise through shame, was questioned by the company of queens:
"This man and that man, as sons-in-law, are adorned with family, beauty, and the like;

children.text: bhavatyai rocate neti mātar ākhyāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: tell us, dear lady, whether they are pleasing to you or not."
Then by her, whose cheeks and eyes had the hue of the dawn's rays,
her head was moved slowly, like a lotus in a windless place.
Then, when "<s>Āryajyeṣṭha</s>" was said, by her whose eyes and cheeks brightened,

children.text: svedārdrāṃśukayā prāgvan na tad vicalitaṃ śiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whose garment was wet with sweat, that head was not moved as before.

children.text: tad bhavān rūcitas tasyai nṛpāya ca yatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, since you are pleasing to her and to the king,
take the merchant's daughter's hand today itself.
Then I, as if having little desire, slowly from disregard,
with the frightened women of the inner apartments looking on, after a long time said this:

children.text: avanter aham āyātaḥ saha bhrātrā kanīyasā
children.translated_text: "I have come from <s>Avanti</s> with my younger brother
only for the study of the Veda, the śāstras, and the āgamas, not from a wish to obtain a woman.
But the command of a king is hard for city-dwellers to transgress,

children.text: yogakṣemārthibhir bhavyais tasmād evaṃ bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: for honorable people who seek safety and prosperity; therefore let it be so."
At that moment the circle of instruments sounded deeply,
with cymbals, tumultuous noise, and the sky roaring with echoes.

children.text: yaś ca saṃvatsareṇāpi duḥsaṃbhāro nṛpaiḥ paraiḥ
children.translated_text: And the wedding equipment which other kings could scarcely gather even in a year

children.text: vivāhārthaḥ sa saṃbhāro rājñā saṃbhāritaḥ kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: the king assembled in a moment.
Then the king, together with his inner apartments and his company of wives and friends,
had my noble hand-taking ceremony performed in the royal courtyard.

children.text: dattvā tataḥ śreṣṭhipadaṃ nagaryāṃ vittaṃ ca bhūmaṇḍalamūlyatulyam
children.translated_text: Then, giving me the office of chief merchant in the city and wealth equal in value to the circle of the earth,

children.text: samṛddhim anveṣya ca kāliyasya prāsthāpayan māṃ mudito narendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having sought out the fortune of <s>Kāliya</s>, the delighted king sent me away.

children.text: āsīc ca mama lokoktir iyaṃ mayy eva saṃprati
children.translated_text: And now this popular saying about me alone came to be:

children.text: vardhamāno yathā rājā śreṣṭhī jāta iti sthitā ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Vardhamāna</s>, though a king, has become a merchant."
Then, by <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Upananda</s>, and the others, whose love and wonder had grown,
and by <s>Priyadarśanā</s>, I, together with her, was regarded as one who had put <s>Śacīpati</s> to shame.

children.text: ahorātre tv atikrānte sa gomukham apaśyataḥ
children.translated_text: But when a day and night had passed and I did not see <s>Gomukha</s>,
my great festival seemed to me as if crowded with great misfortune.

children.text: āsīc ca me vilakṣasya vilakṣaṃ gomukhaṃ balāt
children.translated_text: And, embarrassed as I was, I thought, "Surely one of my clever friends
should by force bring embarrassed <s>Gomukha</s> here."
Then I saw him honoring the bowing city-dwellers,

children.text: adrākṣaṃ bhṛtyavargaṃ ca saṃcarantam itas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the body of servants moving here and there.

children.text: cintitaṃ ca mayā diṅ māṃ vilakṣakam akāraṇe
children.translated_text: And I thought, "Shame on me; I made myself embarrassed without cause.

children.text: balād ānāyayāmy enaṃ kiṃ duḥkhāsikayā mama ||
children.translated_text: I will have him brought by force; what use is this miserable sitting of mine?"
Then, after he had been brought by <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>,
he sat down and, smiling, spoke as if with a reproach:

children.text: kiṃ gomukhaḥ sakhā yasya prājñaṃmanyo na vidyate
children.translated_text: "Do the tasks to be accomplished by a man who has no friend <s>Gomukha</s>, who thinks himself wise,

children.text: tasya sādhyāni kāryāṇi na sidhyantīti so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: ever succeed?" So he said.
"For all living beings, the fruit is indeed made by what was done before,

children.text: na tu tatkāraṇair yogyair vinā sidhyati kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: but for no one does it come to pass without suitable causes.

children.text: yad apīdaṃ mahat kāryaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ kila sādhitam
children.translated_text: Even this great task which you are said to have accomplished
was accomplished by the skill of <s>Gomukha</s> alone, though he thinks himself wise.

children.text: prabhavaḥ prabhavanto hi doṣābhāse manāg api
children.translated_text: For powerful masters, even at the mere appearance of a fault,

children.text: bhṛtyān udvejayanty eva teṣāṃ kiṃ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: do make servants tremble; what can be done for them?"

children.text: kim asmin bhavatā kārye kṛtam ity udite mayā
children.translated_text: When I said, "What was done by you in this matter?"

children.text: ākhyātum ayam ārabdhaḥ śrūyatāṃ yan mayā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: he began to explain: "Listen to what I did.

children.text: asty ahaṃ bhartsitaḥ kruddhair yuṣmābhiḥ svagṛhaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: After I had been scolded by you in anger, I went to my own house;

children.text: tatra prāvṛtya mūrdhānaṃ patitvā śayano sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there I covered my head, fell onto the bed, and remained lying there.
Then I was questioned by <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>, whose voice was trembling and hurried with fear,

children.text: kim etad iti tasyaiva na mayā dattam uttaram ||
children.translated_text: "What is this?" But I gave her no answer.

children.text: sā yadā dṛḍhanibandhā pṛcchati sma punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When she, firmly insistent, kept asking again and again,
then I told her your entire affair.
Then, her cheeks wet with tears of joy, she asked respectfully,
"Could <s>Āryajyeṣṭha</s> be some son of the lord of <s>Vatsa</s>?"
After restraining her with oaths from revealing your affair,

children.text: āma subhrū sa evāyam iti tasyai nyavedayam ||
children.translated_text: I told her, "Yes, beautiful-browed one, this is he."
Then she said to me, "<s>Gomukha</s>, listen to her steadfast courage,"
and, as if both jealous and delighted, she told the story:

children.text: āsīt sumanasaḥ kāpi priyā vidyādharī sakhī
children.translated_text: "There was a certain dear Vidyādharī friend of <s>Sumanas</s>,
possessed of divine knowledge, swift as the wind, and named <s>Priyadarśanā</s>.

children.text: sā yadṛcchāgatā caināṃ prasaṅge kvacid abravīt
children.translated_text: She, having come by chance, once said to her in conversation,

children.text: tvaṃ mām āpadi kaṣṭāyāṃ vartamānā smarer iti ||
children.translated_text: "When you are in a hard calamity, remember me."
Then, when the merchant in time had been taken to the realm of <s>Vaivasvata</s>,
a daughter was born to the merchant's wife, like an oblation of ghee into the fire of grief.
For her, being sonless, this thought arose: "Who will be the guardian
of this very abundant wealth, the essence of our estate?"

children.text: uktā cāsmi purā sakhyā vyasane māṃ smarer iti
children.translated_text: "And I was once told by my friend, 'Remember me in misfortune.'
Then, as soon as she was merely thought of, <s>Priyadarśanā</s> appeared.
And seeing that girl, she smiled with an expression of surpassing delight.

children.text: avocat sakhi mā bhaiṣīr janayitvedṛśīṃ sutām ||
children.translated_text: She said, "Friend, do not be afraid because you have given birth to such a daughter.
She will be the beloved of the future lord of the vidyādharas,
his dearest beloved; therefore let rows of musical instruments resound.
Then he tied a glittering golden amulet containing herbs

children.text: kanyāyā hāṭakaṃ dṛṣṭvā kaṇṭhe gaṇḍakam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: to the maiden's neck, looked at it, and said:

children.text: prabhāvād oṣadher asyāḥ striyam enāṃ satīṃ janāḥ
children.translated_text: By the power of this herb, people will see this virtuous woman
as a woman, except for the future <s>cakravartin</s> (universal emperor).
For, because their merit is stainless and endless, all-knowing <s>cakravartins</s>

children.text: paśyanti hi yathābhūtam arthaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā ||
children.translated_text: see reality as it is with divine sight.

children.text: tena yaḥ striyam evaināṃ draṣṭā sa bhavati dhruvam
children.translated_text: Therefore whoever sees her precisely as a woman
will certainly be the <s>cakravartin</s>, her husband, and the overlord of all vidyādharas.

children.text: oṣadhir yā ca kaṇṭhe 'syāḥ sā nāmnā priyadarśanā
children.translated_text: And the herb on her neck is named <s>Priyadarśanā</s>;

children.text: idam eva ca nāmāsyāḥ praśastaṃ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: let this same auspicious name be given to her.
Accordingly, since this man, the foremost merchant of the city, is <s>Priyadarśana</s>,
this woman <s>Priyadarśanā</s> is fit for a lord of the vidyādharas.
Moreover, from what the <s>cakravartin</s> said in the riddle of the lute,

children.text: ciraṃ sundari jīveti tenaiva viditaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: "Live long, beautiful one," I knew by that very sign.

children.text: na hi śaktaḥ striyaṃ draṣṭum enām avanigocaraḥ
children.translated_text: For no earth-dwelling man is able to see this woman;

children.text: yas tu paśyati sma vyaktaṃ cakravartīty abhūn mama ||
children.translated_text: so when one did see her, it was clear to me that he was the <s>cakravartin</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ ca gomukha eveti tadaiva jñātavaty aham
children.translated_text: And I knew at that very time that you were <s>Gomukha</s>,

children.text: sarūpaḥ savayāś cānyo nāsti yac cakravartinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since there is no other man equal in form and age to the <s>cakravartin</s>.

children.text: rūpaṃ ca yuvarājasya tava cānāyitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: I also had a portrait of the crown prince and of you

children.text: kauśāmbītaḥ paṭe nyastaṃ tac ca niścayakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: brought from <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, painted on cloth, and that was the cause of certainty.
By these and other signs I recognized without mistake
that this man was the <s>cakravartin</s>; the last sign was his sight of her breasts.

children.text: yaḥ punar ghaṭanopāyaḥ kāryaḥ sa bhavatānayoḥ
children.translated_text: But the means by which these two are to be brought together

children.text: ghaṭane durghaṭasyāpi caturo hi bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: must be devised by you, for you are clever at joining even what is hard to join."

children.text: evamādi tataḥ śrutvā spṛhayāmi sma mṛtyave
children.translated_text: When I had heard all this, I longed for death,
because I had determined that there were three causes for dying.

children.text: mayā satyaṃ bruvad bhartā mithyā brūteti kheditaḥ
children.translated_text: By me my truth-speaking master had been distressed with the demand, "Speak falsely";

children.text: atra jīvati yas tasya mṛta evāmṛtopamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for one who lives in such a condition, life itself is like death.

children.text: pāṇḍityāndhasuhṛdvairi mā sma tiṣṭha puro mama
children.translated_text: "Blind with learning, enemy in the guise of a friend, do not stand before me";

children.text: iti yaḥ svāminādiṣṭas tasya mṛtyum arhotsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for one so commanded by his master, death deserves a festival.

children.text: na cāsti durghaṭasyāsya ghaṭane mama kauśalam
children.translated_text: And I had no skill for bringing about this impossible union;

children.text: tasmān maraṇam evāstu dhik prāṇān duḥsthitān iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore let there be death alone. Fie on lives so miserably placed!
So I went outside the city, desiring to find a means of death,
and heard in the sky the voice of someone whose form I could not see:
"Confused one, turn back from your blameworthy resolve to die;

children.text: na hi duḥkhakṣayopāyo mṛtyur iṣṭaḥ satām iti ||
children.translated_text: for the good do not regard death as a proper means for ending sorrow."
Then, my agitation loosened by that voice of a sky-roaming being,
I saw in front of me a man with a child set upon his shoulder.

children.text: asau ca dārakaḥ kuṇṭhaḥ khañjaḥ kubjaḥ pṛthūdaraḥ
children.translated_text: That child was dull, lame, hunchbacked, and pot-bellied,
and his father was cutting him down with harsh razors of speech:
"Die, son of a wanton woman, whose mother has been eaten by ghosts.

children.text: na vahāmi na puṣṇāmi bhavantaṃ niṣprayojanam ||
children.translated_text: I will not carry you, nor will I feed you, useless as you are.

children.text: eṣa tvāṃ gāḍham āveṣṭya grīvāṃ bhittvāthavā śiraḥ
children.translated_text: Now I will clasp you tightly and break your neck or your head,
and kill you. So go to the city of <s>Vaivasvata</s>."

children.text: tatas tena vihasyoktaṃ mā vākṣīr mā ca māṃ puṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the child laughed and said to him, "Do not carry me, and do not feed me.

children.text: etāvatā hi te kāryaṃ na madīyena mṛtyunā ||
children.translated_text: Your purpose is served by just that much, not by my death.

children.text: mayāpi kila kartavyaṃ mahat kāryaṃ mahātmanām
children.translated_text: I too, it seems, have a great task to perform for great men;

children.text: tad bhavān māṃ sahasreṇa vikrīṇītāṃ mahātmasu ||
children.translated_text: therefore sell me to great men for a thousand.

children.text: sahasraṃ yac ca tad dattaṃ paryāptaṃ jīvanaṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: And that thousand, once given, is enough to sustain life;

children.text: mā sma tasmād vinā kāryān mārayan māṃ bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore do not kill me, without any purpose."

children.text: mama tv āsīn mahātmānaḥ ke 'nye yuṣmaj jagattraye
children.translated_text: But I thought, "What great men are there in the three worlds other than you?
And what task could be greater than preserving your life?

children.text: sahasraṃ te na yat kiṃcit koṭyāpi yadi labhyate
children.translated_text: A thousand is nothing for you; if he can be obtained even for a crore,

children.text: tucchamūlyas tathāpy eṣa tṛṇamuṣṭisamā hi sā ||
children.translated_text: he is still cheaply priced, for that price is like a handful of grass."

children.text: tat tad ityādi niścitya gṛham ānāyya taṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having decided in this way, saying, "So be it, so be it," I brought him home,
and bought him for a thousand, as if buying a wish-jewel with a stone.
Then I said to <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>, "Whatever you remember

children.text: pracchannaṃ śreṣṭhino vṛttaṃ tāvan me kathyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: of the merchant's hidden conduct, please tell me that much.

children.text: kāliyena ca rājñā ca yad yat kāryaṃ rahaḥ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever was done secretly by <s>Kāliya</s> and the king

children.text: tat tat sumanase bhartrā kathitaṃ dhīracetase ||
children.translated_text: was told by the husband to wise-hearted <s>Sumanas</s>.

children.text: yac ca śrutadharā kāryaṃ rājñaḥ śrutavatī guru
children.translated_text: And whatever matter of the king the venerable <s>Śrutadharā</s> had heard,
that hard-to-disclose matter was disclosed by her to <s>Ṛṣidattā</s>.

children.text: tayā tayā ca tan mahyaṃ kubjāya kathitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: By her, and then by her, that was told to me, the hunchback;

children.text: kubjena brahmadattāya śeṣaṃ pratyakṣam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: by me, the hunchback, it was told to <s>Brahmadatta</s>, and the rest was directly witnessed.

children.text: tad yuṣmābhir yad ādiṣṭaṃ yad atra bhavatā kṛtam
children.translated_text: Therefore, tell what you ordered and what was done here by you:

children.text: tad ācakṣveti kāryaṃ tad etad atra mayā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: that was the task, and I have now carried it out in this matter."
After hearing from him such things, his conduct more wonderful than magic,

children.text: prāśaṃsaṃ caritaṃ tasya praśasyā hi guṇādhikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I praised it; for those rich in virtues are indeed worthy of praise.

children.text: kā vidyādharacakravartipadake tucchā ratir mādṛśaḥ suprāpaṃ dharaṇīcarair yad aparaiḥ krodhādivaśyair api
children.translated_text: What petty delight in the rank of vidyādhara-<s>cakravartin</s> could there be for one like me, when it is easily attained even by other earth-roaming men who are subject to anger and the rest...

children.text: prajñādhikkṛtadevadānavagurur yeṣāṃ suhṛd gomukhaḥ te yat piṣṭapasaptakāptivimukhās tatkarmaṇāṃ jṛmbhitam ||
children.translated_text: For those whose friend was <s>Gomukha</s>, a guru surpassing the teachers of gods and demons in wisdom, their turning away from obtaining the seven cakes of meal was the unfolding of their own deeds.
Thus, while I was staying in <s>Varanasi</s>, attended by my wife and friends,
the guilds of <s>Kasi</s>, with wares in their hands, came to wait upon me.
And I, knowing the whole course of events, addressed them:

children.text: ayam āryakaniṣṭho vaḥ śreṇiśreṣṭhī bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let this younger nobleman be your chief guild-master."

children.text: atha yāte kvacit kāle saudhe sapriyadarśanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after some time had passed, while I was on the palace with <s>Priyadarsana</s>,

children.text: sopāne tāram aśrauṣaṃ haṃsānām iva nisvanam ||
children.translated_text: I heard on the staircase a high, clear sound, as if of swans.

children.text: mama tv āsīn na haṃsānāṃ nūpurāṇām ayaṃ dhvaniḥ
children.translated_text: But I thought, "This is not the sound of swans; it is the sound of anklets,
because the movement is slow, step by step, and the succession is unbroken.
Nor does this fit the supposition that they are women of good family,

children.text: utsavābhyudayeṣv eva tā hi bibhrati bhūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: for such women wear ornaments only at the rise of festivals.
Therefore some sound of ornaments, proper to the feet of courtesans moving in the inner apartments,
is for some reason moving on the staircase."
And while I was reflecting in this way, with the clear jingling of their ornaments,
I saw young women wearing bright garments, with their youth fully risen.
Among them was one named <s>Kumudika</s>, moonlight to the eyes of the world;
bold, yet as if modest, she bowed to me and spoke:
"Noble elder, sharer in glory, your master's daughter,
the princess, after bowing respectfully, sends word to you.
For the sake of a vow I have worshipped the deities and Brahmins;

children.text: vaṇṭakas tasya yuṣmābhiḥ sadārair gṛhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: let the portion from it be accepted by you, together with your wives."

children.text: atha mahyaṃ susaṃskāraṃ sā samudraṃ samudgakam
children.translated_text: Then she brought before me a finely prepared casket with its contents,
and garments, flowers, perfumes, and delightful fragrances.
Then, taking out treasures that were the essence of the world, she showed me
two kinds of ornaments, suitable for men and for women.

children.text: mayoktaṃ dvayam apy etad arhati priyadarśanā
children.translated_text: I said, "<s>Priyadarsana</s> deserves both of these.

children.text: preṣitaṃ yoṣitā yat tad yoṣid eva yato 'rhati ||
children.translated_text: For what has been sent by a woman is fitting precisely for a woman."

children.text: idam ākarṇya tāḥ prekṣya vismitāḥ sasmitāś ca mām
children.translated_text: Hearing this, they looked at me in astonishment and with smiles;

children.text: tasyai dattvā ca tad dravyam agacchan kṛtavandanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, having given that property to her, they bowed and departed.
When I heard her say, "sharer in glory," I felt oppressed,

children.text: anabhyastaṃ hi yad yena tena tad vastu duḥsaham ||
children.translated_text: for whatever is unfamiliar to a person is hard for that person to endure.
Every man and every woman who addresses me
calls me "noble prince," except this man-like woman.

children.text: kiṃ cānyat kulakanyānāṃ keyam īdṛk svatantratā
children.translated_text: And further, what is this kind of independence among maidens of good family,
that such uninhibited dealings with the world occur together with men like us?
But a passionate woman, even while longing, my passionate dear,

children.text: na dhanāyaty api svāṅgaṃ kim aṅga dhanam adhruvam ||
children.translated_text: does not count even her own body as wealth; how much less unstable riches.

children.text: tad asyāḥ ko bhaved bhāvo mayīty etad vitarkayan
children.translated_text: So, as I was speculating, "What feeling toward me could she have?",
I was addressed in these words by <s>Gomukha</s>, whose face was gloomy:
"Noble prince, dealings with the world involving such women are dangerous
for men like you." Then I said to him, as if joking:

children.text: durantā vāthavā svantā na hīyaṃ prastutā mayā
children.translated_text: "Dangerous, or else ending well, this was not begun by me.

children.text: athavā saṃkaṭāt trātā mamāsty eva bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: And in any case I certainly have you as my rescuer from difficulty."
When that day and night had passed, <s>Kumudika</s> and the others
came and spoke these words, as if with bashful humility:
"Noble prince, the noble daughter, the princess, having bowed,
ashamed because of our fault, respectfully informs you with joined hands:
This transgression of proper conduct on our part should be forgiven,

children.text: mūḍhabhṛtyakṛtā doṣā na grāhyāḥ svāminām iti ||
children.translated_text: for faults committed by foolish servants should not be taken as belonging to their masters."

children.text: mayāpy uktaṃ na paśyāmi doṣam ācaritaṃ tayā
children.translated_text: I too said, "I see no fault committed by her.

children.text: asti cet kṣānta evāsau tathāpy ākhyāyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: And even if there is one, it is already forgiven; still, let it be explained."
Then <s>Kumudika</s> told me: "The king's daughter asked me,
'What sorts of conversation did you have with the noble elder?'
When I reported at the beginning, 'noble elder, sharer in glory,'
she, trembling as if jealous and distressed, said this:

children.text: ayi vairiṇi bhartāram evaṃ vadati kāṅganā
children.translated_text: 'Oh enemy, what woman addresses her husband in this way,

children.text: yathokto mandayā jyeṣṭho yaśobhāginn iti tvayā ||
children.translated_text: as you foolishly addressed the elder, saying, "sharer in glory"?

children.text: na ca tvadīyam evedaṃ vacaḥ saṃbhāvayaty asau
children.translated_text: And he will not suppose that this speech is yours alone,
for courtesans are known as bearers of messages from others.

children.text: yaḥ śreṣṭhiduhitur bhartā so 'smākam api dharmataḥ
children.translated_text: The man who is the merchant's daughter's husband is ours also by <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: priyadarśanayā sārdham abhinnaiva hi me tanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: for I and <s>Priyadarsana</s> are one undivided body.
Therefore he must be addressed by you as "noble prince,"

children.text: tathā vijñāpyatāṃ cedaṃ yathāvajñāṃ na manyate ||
children.translated_text: and this too must be reported in such a way that he does not think it contempt.
For our sake, this <s>Priyadarsana</s> should be told by me
that, after attending the festival of the vow, she will return in the evening.'

children.text: iti śrutvedam āsīn me ko 'nyaḥ paribhavaḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: On hearing this, I thought, "What greater insult could there be than this,

children.text: etasmād yad asāv āha bhāryā prasthāpyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: that she says my wife should be sent away?

children.text: yā vadhūs tātapādānāṃ mama bhāryā ca sā katham
children.translated_text: She is the daughter-in-law of my honored father, and how is she my wife,
if, like a common householder's woman, she goes to another's house?"

children.text: atha māṃ gomukho 'vocat kim asthāne viśaṅkayā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gomukha</s> said to me, "Why suspect something out of place?

children.text: nedaṃ paragṛhaṃ devyās tathā viditam eva vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is not another's house for the lady, as you indeed know.

children.text: maṅgalaṃ hi vivāhāntam asyās tatraiva kāritam
children.translated_text: The auspicious rite up to the marriage was performed for her there itself;

children.text: tac caitac ca gṛhaṃ tasmād abhinnaṃ dṛśyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: therefore let that house and this house be seen as no different."

children.text: tatas tadvacanān nyāyyād anujñātā satī mayā
children.translated_text: Then, because of that reasonable statement of his, she was permitted by me,
and <s>Priyadarsana</s> descended from the top of the palace together with them.
Then, standing on the palace terrace, with bright ivory ornaments...
I saw a carriage yoked with oxen on the royal road.
It was surrounded by countless aged royal chamberlains with canes in their hands,
and by crowds of people consisting mostly of women and eunuchs.

children.text: tac ca rājakulād dṛṣṭvā gacchatpravahaṇaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that carriage going from the royal palace,
I spent that day, hard to get through as a long imprisonment.

children.text: sūryo 'pi tad ahar manye bhagnākṣasyandano bhavet
children.translated_text: I think even the sun that day must have had the axle of his chariot broken,
or his horses cut down by Daityas, since he somehow managed to set.
Then, climbing up to the palace roof and watching the royal road,
I saw that same vehicle surrounded by a circle of lamps.
Descending from the top of the mansion,
I saw <s>Priyadarśanā</s> on the stairway, exhausted and companioned by the moonlight of the lamps.
Then, taking her by the hand, oppressed by intoxication and amorous excitement,
after a long while I brought her up to the bedchamber on the palace roof.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ ca tatra viśrāntāṃ tām āliṅgam asau ca mām
children.translated_text: When she had rested there for a moment, she embraced me and I embraced her;
then suddenly the fastening-cord of her girdle snapped.
Like a row of śarāṭi and kurara birds from sandbanks into a lotus-pond,
her jingling girdle then fell from her hips onto the bed.
Seeing it, shading the lamp with umbrella-like gleams from its broken jewels,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭā mayā tasyāḥ saṃprāptiṃ priyadarśanā ||
children.translated_text: I asked <s>Priyadarśanā</s> how she had obtained it.

children.text: bahu śrotavyam atrāsti krameṇa śrūyatām iti
children.translated_text: “There is much to hear about this; listen in order,” she said,

children.text: uktvā ruṣṭaiva tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sācaṣṭa sma kathām imām ||
children.translated_text: and, as if annoyed when she saw it, she told this story.
“At your command I had gone to the maidens’ inner apartments,

children.text: na ca tatra mayā dṛṣṭā mārgayantyā nṛpātmajā ||
children.translated_text: but while searching there I did not see the king’s daughter.

children.text: tataḥ parijanas tasyāḥ prāha māṃ rājadārikā
children.translated_text: Then her attendants said to me, “The royal maiden
is staying in the household garden; she should be sought there.”

children.text: praviśya ca mayā dṛṣṭā tasminn udyānapālikā
children.translated_text: Entering, I saw the garden-keeper in that garden,
wearing garlands and ornaments fashioned from spring flowers.

children.text: sā ca pṛṣṭā mayāvocad yo 'yaṃ saṃdhyāvadāruṇaḥ
children.translated_text: When I questioned her, she said, “In that aśoka grove, red like twilight,
the royal maiden is staying in seclusion.
Go by this path for the noble daughter, even though it is winding,
the one that passes fearlessly through the middle of the priyaṅgu thicket.
From afar avoid the grove of kurabakas
and the mādhavīs, mango trees, and aṅkolas.
There the bees roam about, and the trees are crowded like an army;

children.text: bhṛṅgadaṃśabhayāt kas taṃ nāpramattas tyajed iti ||
children.translated_text: who, unless careless, would not avoid that place for fear of bee-stings?”
Going by that way, I also saw kadambas and kuṭajas,
and mālatīs and saptaparṇas, their new leaves covered by clusters of blossoms.

children.text: mama tv āsīd aho śaktir dohadasya varīyasī
children.translated_text: But I thought, “Ah, the power of longing is very great,

children.text: anṛtāv api yenaite jṛmbhitāḥ pādapā iti ||
children.translated_text: since by it these trees have burst into bloom even out of season.”
Then, on the bank of a lotus-pond, on a stone slab gleaming like a Himalayan ridge,
thickly muddied with sandal paste, I saw her.
Even in this spring, where heat and cold were balanced, she seemed autumnal,
tormented at midday as if by a violent fever.
She was being fanned continually with palm-leaf fans and with breezes damp from sandal-water,
and being comforted with very gentle words.

children.text: atha tasyā mayā gatvā samīpaṃ vandanā kṛtā
children.translated_text: Then I went near her and made a salutation,

children.text: tayāpi kṣiptacetastvān na kiṃcid api bhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: but because her mind was distracted she said nothing at all.

children.text: tataḥ kumudikā tasyāḥ pādam ālambya niṣṭhuram
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kumudikā</s> grasped her foot firmly

children.text: pratibuddhām avocat tāṃ bhaginī dṛśyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: and, rousing her, said, “Sister, look.”
Then, taking <s>Kumudikā</s>’s hand, she rose and for a long time
embraced me with limbs hard to bear, like darkness, embers, and fire.

children.text: sukhāsīnāṃ ca mām āha bhartā te sukhabhāgini
children.translated_text: When I was comfortably seated, she said, “Fortunate one, is your husband
always well?” and such things; and I replied, “He is.”

children.text: punar āha sa te bhartā chāttratvād durjanaḥ kila
children.translated_text: Again she said, “Your husband, being a student, is surely a difficult man,

children.text: āhārādyair durārādhas tvayā tad iti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: hard for you to satisfy with food and the rest; so I think.”
I said, “Since he has prepared food brought to him with affection by <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>,
he does not need to be attended by me at all.”

children.text: punar uktaṃ tayā smitvā nedaṃ saṃbhāvyate tayoḥ
children.translated_text: She smiled and said again, “That is not to be expected of those two;
out of pride they are said to have given up a tenth share of a kingdom.
How could they possibly accept servitude to your husband,
a penniless traveler of unknown birth? The thing is hard to believe.”

children.text: mayoktaṃ sarvam asty etat kiṃtu tau divyacakṣuṣau
children.translated_text: I said, “All that is so; but those two possess divine sight.

children.text: yad evādiśataḥ kiṃcit tat tathaiva hi sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: Whatever they direct in any way, that very thing comes to pass.

children.text: jyeṣṭhasya ca guṇā jyeṣṭhās tābhyāṃ kasyeti mānuṣāḥ
children.translated_text: And the virtues of the eldest are the foremost; who among humans has such qualities as his?
For that reason the two accepted the state of servants to my husband.”
Hearing this story, <s>Bhagīrathayaśāḥ</s>, her eyes motionless,
was seized by horripilation and tears and embraced me forcefully.

children.text: evaṃ ca kṣaṇam āsīnām āha māṃ rājadārikā
children.translated_text: When I had sat thus for a moment, the royal maiden said to me,
“Your body is tired from the jolting of the carriage; let it be anointed.”

children.text: āstām āstām iti mayā anicchantyā yāvad ucyate
children.translated_text: While I, unwilling, was saying, “Let it be, let it be,”

children.text: tāvad balād balātailaṃ nyadhāt kumudikā mayi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kumudikā</s> forcibly applied bala-oil to me.
After signaling in every way to <s>Kumudikā</s> and the others by winking and such gestures,
under the pretext of anointing me, she uncovered my limbs and looked at them.
Seeing this mark, as though written by the branches of your hand,
on my body, the royal maiden said:
“Ah, friend, you are modest, a young guardian of family honor,
you tender-limbed girl who endured here this unbearable rough treatment.”

children.text: athavā tvaṃ parādhīnā bhartaiva tava nirdayaḥ
children.translated_text: Or rather, you are dependent on another; your husband himself is merciless,
by whose overpowering arrogance such unfairness has been done.
Who else could be more pitiless than he by whom you, soft as a blue lotus,
have been crushed like a lotus-bed by a great blind elephant?

children.text: matsaṃdeśaṃ ca vācyo 'sau kim asthāne kṛtam tvayā
children.translated_text: And he should be told this message from me: 'Why have you acted in an improper place?

children.text: na hi cūḍāmaṇiḥ pāde prabhavāmīti badhyate ||
children.translated_text: A crest-jewel is not fastened on the foot merely because it is capable of being there.'

children.text: idaṃ hi karkaśāḥ soḍhuṃ śaktā rājanyakanyakāḥ
children.translated_text: For royal maidens are able to endure this harsh thing,
but not merchants' daughters, whose limbs are soft as shade.

children.text: ityādi bahu jalpitvā sā mām udvartanādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: After chattering much in this and other ways, she honored me for a long time
with attentions beginning with rubbing and ending with food and drink.
For her this day, contracted to a moment, but for me stretched out to a year,
passed together with the sun because of the occasion of talking about you.
Then, unfastening this girdle from her own hips, which shone like the slope of a mountain,
she fastened it on my lighter hips.

children.text: bahur visraṃsamānāyāṃ granthir asyāṃ tayā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: When it kept slipping down again and again, she made knots in it
with lotus-fiber threads twined by her own hands, carefully.

children.text: tataḥ prasthāpitavatī mām ityādi vidhāya sā
children.translated_text: Then, after doing this and that, she sent me away,

children.text: mekhalā skhalitā ceyaṃ chittvā tat tantubandhanam ||
children.translated_text: and this girdle slipped down after breaking those thread-bonds.

children.text: iti tasyās tayā citre prapañce 'smin nivedite
children.translated_text: When this elaborate and wondrous account of hers had been reported by her,
I, touched by Love born of imagination, began to imagine.

children.text: tayā yad guru saṃdiṣṭam upalabdhaṃ ca yat tayā
children.translated_text: The important message that was sent by her, and what was obtained by her,
this alone is quite sufficient as a sign of attachment.

children.text: yat punar mekhalā baddhā niḥsarair bisatantubhiḥ
children.translated_text: But as for the girdle being tied with dry lotus-fibers,

children.text: satsv apy anyeṣu sūtreṣu tatredaṃ cintitaṃ tayā ||
children.translated_text: though other threads were available, this was what she had in mind there:
'From the agitation of a pitiless embrace this will come apart;
then this girdle, slipped loose, will fall on the bed.
And when he sees it, long as it is, perhaps

children.text: anayā prītim ādhāsyaty api kām iti ||
children.translated_text: he will take pleasure through it in the breadth of my hips.'
Even though each separate event had been plausibly arranged by her,
I set this conjecture aside, since I had understood what had to be done.
Then I said plainly, '<s>Bhagīrathayaśas</s> is dark-complexioned.'

children.text: kathaṃ vettheti sāpṛcchad athettham aham uktavān ||
children.translated_text: She asked, 'How do you know?' Then I spoke to her as follows:
'For fair women, experts describe a dark ornament; for dark women, one brighter than white;

children.text: śyāmānāṃ maṇḍanaṃ tajjñaiś citravarṇaṃ tu varṇitam ||
children.translated_text: but for dusky women they describe a variegated color as the adornment.
Since this girdle has the radiance of a garland of pārijāta flowers,
the young woman is certainly a royal maiden, dark like a blade of young dūrvā grass.

children.text: kiṃca nānyā tataḥ kācid darśanīyatamā yataḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, no other woman is more beautiful than she,
since the doctrine is that a dusky woman is the most beautiful of women.'

children.text: tayoktaṃ dhig dhig astv eṣāṃ ratnalakṣaṇakāriṇām
children.translated_text: She said, 'Fie, fie upon these makers of rules for the marks of jewels!

children.text: janaḥ pracchādanīyo 'pi khyāpito yaiḥ śaṭhair api ||
children.translated_text: Even a person who should have been concealed has been revealed by those rogues.
With such talk from her I sent along two watches of that night,
and the third with reflection on a means for gaining her.

children.text: mama tv āsīd iyaṃ cintā kiṃ mamopāyacintayā
children.translated_text: But this thought occurred to me: 'What need have I to think of means?

children.text: devatās tat kariṣyanti yena śāntir bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The deities will do that by which there will be relief.
What means did I contrive in obtaining <s>Vegavatī</s> and the others?

children.text: yathā tāḥ prāptavān asmi tathā rājasutām iti ||
children.translated_text: As I obtained them, so too I shall obtain the king's daughter.'
Then one evening <s>Kumudikā</s> came to me and said:
'After saluting you, <s>Bhagīrathayaśas</s> makes this request:
"The mangoes, mādhavī creepers, campakas, and other plants that I planted
have grown, their shoots bending under the weight of heavy clusters of buds.
Therefore tomorrow, having gone there, I shall perform
the marriage rite of the mādhavī creeper and the mango, and the worship of the others.
So, taking <s>Priyadarśanā</s> from the door of your house,

children.text: prātar eva prāyātāsmi tad eṣā mucyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: I shall set out early in the morning; therefore let her be released."'

children.text: atha tasyai pratijñāya gacchatv evaṃ bhavatv iti
children.translated_text: Then I promised her, 'Go; let it be so,'
and passed the night in distress, thinking, 'The princess must be seen.'
In the morning <s>Kumudikā</s> came and spoke in agitation:
'<s>Bhagīrathayaśas</s> has arrived; go, noble son,' she said to me.

children.text: atha tāṃ dṛṣṭavān asmi prasthāpya priyadarśanām
children.translated_text: Then, after sending off <s>Priyadarśanā</s>, I saw her
from the top of the palace, seated in a bright carriage standing at the door.

children.text: āstāṃ ca mama tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣaṇaṃ mānasacakṣuṣī
children.translated_text: When I saw her, my mind and eyes remained for a moment
as if sunk in deep sleep, with the vision born of imagination lost.
Wholly blessed are those gods, asuras, men, and serpents

children.text: asāv akālamṛtyur yair nārīrūpo na vīkṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by whom that untimely death in the form of a woman has not been seen.

children.text: tayā cānanam unnamya hṛṣṭaḥ saṃdṛṣṭavān aham
children.translated_text: And when she raised her face, I joyfully saw
my own self as <s>Sahasrākṣa</s>, bright with those many eyes and more.

children.text: māṃ ca maddayitāṃ nāsau saṃmānitavatī samam
children.translated_text: But she did not honor me and my beloved equally:

children.text: mayi dṛṣṭam adāt tasyāṃ gāḍha ṭhagrahārhaṇām ||
children.translated_text: after glancing at me, she gave my beloved a tight, grasping welcome.

children.text: atha svayānam āropya sā priyāṃ priyadarśanām
children.translated_text: Then she placed her dear <s>Priyadarśanā</s> in her own carriage,
and, guarded by a troop of chamberlains and others, went to the city park.

children.text: ahaṃ tu tad dinaṃ nītvā kṛcchrān mandiraniṣkuṭe
children.translated_text: I, however, after passing that day with difficulty in the garden of the house,
climbed to the palace roof out of desire to see the princess.
Then she, in a carriage whose speed was keen as the wind,
came to the door of my house, her face raised from afar.

children.text: sā ca māṃ tatra paśyantī saṃtataṃ priyadarśanām
children.translated_text: And seeing me there, while continually

children.text: gāḍhaṃ niṣpīḍayantī ca ciram aṅgaṃ nyapīḍayat ||
children.translated_text: pressing <s>Priyadarśanā</s> tightly, she pressed her body for a long time.

children.text: vandanāchadmanā paścān māyy ātmānaṃ nidhāya sā
children.translated_text: Afterwards, under the pretext of salutation, she placed herself upon me.
"After making an exchange of minds, she has set out for the palanquin," and so forth.

children.text: ārādhayāmi nṛpasūnukṛte nu gaurīṃ kiṃ khānayāmi caturais tvaritaṃ suruṅgām
children.translated_text: "Shall I propitiate <s>Gaurī</s> for the sake of the prince, or shall I have a tunnel quickly dug by clever men?"
With his mind exhausted by thinking over hundreds of expedients such as these, he passed the hard night without obtaining sleep.
